Keyboard focus shows a crosshair: the arrow keys move it 10 units, 40 with Shift, and its cell is announced when it changes; Enter or Space drops the pin there with the same fall, landing and sounds as a hold; Delete or Backspace removes the pin. Escape is left to the page.
- Under reduced motion nothing falls, bounces, lifts or glides: the hold's shadow only darkens, the pin fades in where it lands with the same thock and no whistle, a drag sets down where it is released, and the crosshair jumps.
- The town, its street names and its survey grid (columns A to T, rows 1 to 4, easting and northing to one decimal) are invented and drawn from a fixed hash, 1:1, so a narrower box shows less of the town, centred. dropPinPlace(point) returns the same cell, easting, northing and text the callout shows. A long press never selects text or opens the browser's menu; the map keeps touch-pan-y so the page scrolls past it, and the pin is touch-none so it drags.

### Node Wire (KQ-1109) — `node-wire`
Drag a wire from one node to the next.

A node editor whose cables are real cables: drag from an output jack and a Verlet rope pays out 1:1 under the finger, every compatible input shows its capture ring, and within the snap radius the plug is caught, flicks into the jack and seats with a jack snap; let go anywhere else and the cable reels back into its output. Nodes drag by their headers and glide on springs.glide, carrying the release velocity to where a light throw would rest, while their cables swing behind them on a fixed-step loop that runs only while something moves. Enter picks up a cable, Arrow keys choose among the inputs that take it, Enter plugs in and Escape lets it reel back; on a node's grip, Arrow keys move the node.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/node-wire`

Props:
- `nodes`: NodeWireNode[] — The node cards: { id, label, x, y, inputs?, outputs? }, with x and y as fractions (0 to 1) of the free space and ports as { id, label, type }. Ids contain no dots.
- `value / defaultValue`: NodeWireLink[] (default []) — The cables, each { from, to } written "node.port" from an output to an input. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (links: NodeWireLink[]) => void — Fires from the plug or unplug that changed the cables, with all of them. A plugged cable waits at its jack for a controlled host and reels back if the host does not take it.
- `canConnect`: (from: string, to: string) => boolean — An extra rule on top of matching types, given "node.port" of each end.
- `label`: string — The canvas's accessible name.
- `sag`: number (default 0.5) — Slack in each cable, 0 to 1: 0 is a straight wire, 1 hangs in a deep loop that lies on the canvas floor. In curve mode, the droop of the curve.
- `stiffness`: number (default 0.5) — 0 to 1: a limp string that swings long, up to a thick lead that arcs and settles fast (constraint passes, bending and damping). In curve mode, how hard the cable is pulled onto its curve.
- `snap`: number (default 24) — Capture radius around a compatible input, in px, 12 to 40, drawn as a ring while a cable is carried.
- `wire`: "rope" | "curve" (default "rope") — rope hangs free under gravity; curve springs the same cable onto the tidy editor curve that leaves each jack horizontally.
- `height`: number (default 200) — Canvas height in px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the cable's synthesised sounds: a slither while a cable or a wired node moves, a detent when a ring catches the plug, a jack snap when it seats, a pop when it comes out. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the canvas and blocks every drag, press and key.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the canvas's classes.

Notes:
- Every port and node grip is a real button with a one-string name that says what it is wired to. Enter or Space on an output picks up a cable and moves focus to the nearest input that takes it; Arrow keys move between those inputs with the plug gliding along, Enter plugs in, and Escape (or focus leaving the canvas) lets the cable reel back. Enter on a wired input unplugs it and carries it the same way; Delete unplugs it. Arrow keys on a grip move the node 8px, Shift 32px. Changes are announced in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion every cable is drawn straight onto its resting shape with no swing, a released node stays where it was dropped, a plug goes straight into its jack and a put-back cable disappears; rings, dimming, sounds and the wiring itself are unchanged.
- The loop runs on requestAnimationFrame only while something moves, stops once every cable is still, and never runs while the page is hidden. Only ports of the same type join; each input holds one plug, and plugging into a wired input pulls the old one out.

### Fling Sort (KQ-1110) — `fling-sort`
Throw it where it belongs.

A sorting tray you throw things into: grab the top chip of the inbox or of any bin and it lifts 1:1 under the finger; let go and it flies with the hand's speed on a real trajectory with gravity, air drag and spin, bouncing off rims, walls and the frame until it lands in the bin it reaches. The landing is heard, counted and reported on the frame the chip touches down with too little rebound to leave, then it docks into its pile on springs.glide carrying its landing speed, and the count rolls in on springs.snap. Number keys throw the focused box's top chip into that bin on a solved arc and 0 throws it back to the inbox.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/fling-sort`

Props:
- `items`: FlingSortItem[] — Everything to sort: { id, label, detail? }. Keep labels to a word; detail is a short second line such as an amount.
- `categories`: FlingSortCategory[] — The bins, in order: { id, label }. The first `bins` of them stand on the floor.
- `bins`: number (default 3) — How many of categories are open, 2 to 4. Items filed under a bin that is not shown sit in the inbox.
- `value / defaultValue`: Record<string, string> (default {}) — The filing, item id to category id; an item that is absent is in the inbox. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: Record<string, string>, change: { item: string; bin: string | null }) => void — Fires on the frame a throw is decided, with the whole filing and what changed (bin null: back to the inbox). A controlled chip docks wherever the host's value says once it settles, so a refused change flies home.
- `label`: string — The tray's accessible name.
- `gravity`: number (default 2000) — Downward pull in px/s², 800 to 3200: low values float long, lazy arcs; high ones drop the chip fast and short.
- `bounce`: number (default 0.4) — Restitution off the floor, rims and walls, 0 to 0.8: dead-stop landings at 0, lively rebounds near 0.8.
- `drag`: number (default 0.8) — Air drag per second, 0 to 3: at 0 a throw carries far, at 3 it dies in the air and drops short.
- `height`: number (default 200) — Tray height in px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the throw's synthesised sounds: a paper rustle on pickup, a whoosh by speed on release, a rim clang, a thunk on a bin landing and a thud on the floor. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the tray and blocks throws and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the tray's classes.

Notes:
- The inbox and every bin are buttons named by their contents ("Travel, 2 items, top: Taxi 24.80"). Number keys 1 to 4 throw the focused box's top chip into that bin on an arc that is flown through the same integrator and collisions as a real throw, so it lands where it was aimed; 0 or Backspace throws it back to the inbox. Each landing is announced politely.
- Under reduced motion nothing flies: a release or a key works the throw out at once through the same physics and the chip fades into its place, while counts, the landing sound and the announcement are unchanged. Dragging still follows the finger.
- The flight runs at a fixed 120Hz on requestAnimationFrame only while something is in the air, never while the page is hidden (hiding it lands every throw at once), and every throw stays inside the tray: its walls and ceiling bounce.

### Sling Send (KQ-1111) — `sling-send`
Pull it back; let it fly.

A composer whose send button is a slingshot: the draft rides as a bubble in the pouch of a rubber band, and pulling it back (and to one side to aim) stretches the band 1:1 with the finger, thinning and warming it as it goes, with a creak pitched by the stretch. Let go past a third of the way and the band fires as a real spring, the bubble leaves the pouch at that speed and flies out through the frame's own clipped edge while the band wobbles back on springs.recoil; a short pull snaps back on springs.snap carrying the release velocity, nothing sent. Enter in the text field sends with a full pull; on the bubble, Arrow keys pull and aim, Enter lets go and Escape lets the band down.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sling-send`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The draft. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires as the draft is typed, and with "" the moment the band fires.
- `onSend`: (message: string) => void — Fires the moment the band fires, with the message.
- `label`: string (default "Message") — The text field's accessible name.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Write a message") — Shown in the empty field and on the empty bubble.
- `stiffness`: number (default 0.5) — The band's spring, 0 to 1: a slack band pushes slowly and lobs the bubble, a stiff one fires it fast. It also sets the snap-back and the band's thickness.
- `maxStretch`: number (default 100) — How far the band pulls before it resists, in px, 60 to 140. The launch frame grows with it.
- `trajectory`: "straight" | "arc" | "guided" (default "arc") — How the bubble flies once it leaves the band: along the aim, under gravity so an angled shot curves, or turning upright so every shot leaves through the top.
- `trail`: boolean (default true) — A fading streak behind the bubble in flight.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the band's synthesised sounds: a creak pitched by the stretch while it moves, a twang when it fires, a whoosh as the bubble leaves, a slap when it snaps back. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the composer and disables the field and the bubble.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the frame's classes.

Notes:
- The field is a real textarea: Enter (not Shift, not while composing) sends with a full pull — the band draws back on its own, then fires exactly as a release does, same sounds — and Shift+Enter is a newline. The bubble is a button named with its message: Enter or Space sends with a full pull, Arrow Down and Up pull back or ease off by a tenth, Arrow Left and Right aim by 10°, Enter then lets go (short pulls are put back), and Escape lets the band down. Outcomes are announced politely.
- Under reduced motion the bubble still follows the finger and the band still stretches, but nothing travels on its own: Enter sends at once, a sent bubble fades where it was let go, a short pull jumps back to rest, the band returns without a wobble and there is no trail. Sounds and the send itself are unchanged.
- The flight runs on requestAnimationFrame only while the bubble is in the band or the air and ends at once if the page is hidden; the bubble always leaves through the frame's own clipped edge. onSend is where the message is actually sent.

### Snap Guides (KQ-1112) — `snap-guides`
Edges that find each other.

A small design canvas whose layers line themselves up: drag one and, within a few pixels, its edges and centre are pulled onto the edges and centres of the other layers and the artboard on a quick critically damped spring (the flick), with a guide drawn across both objects, a tick, and live labels measuring the gap to the nearest neighbour on each side. The layer is 1:1 under the finger when nothing pulls it, rubber-bands past the artboard's edge and glides back in carrying its release velocity. Arrow keys nudge the focused layer by 1 and Shift+Arrow by 10, with the same snapping and the same tick.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/snap-guides`

Props:

- `value / defaultValue`: Record<string, { x: number; y: number }> (default {}) — Where each layer sits, by id, in artboard px from the top-left corner. Controlled or uncontrolled; a layer with no entry starts at 0, 0.
- `onValueChange`: (value: SnapGuidesValue, change: { id: string; x: number; y: number; alignedWith: string[] }) => void — Fires from the release or the key that moved a layer, with every position and the labels of the layers the moved one now lines up with. A controlled layer waits for the host: a refused move glides back.
- `boardWidth`: number (default 400) — The artboard's width in artboard px. The artboard keeps its aspect ratio and scales to fit its box.
- `boardHeight`: number (default 200) — The artboard's height in artboard px.
- `label`: string (default "Artboard") — The artboard's accessible name.
- `snap`: number (default 6) — How close, in artboard px, a line must come before it pulls the layer into line, 2 to 16.
- `guides`: "edges" | "centres" | "both" (default "both") — Which lines snap and draw guides: left, right, top and bottom edges, the centres, or all of them.
- `distances`: boolean (default true) — Live measurement lines and labels from the moving layer to its nearest neighbour, or the artboard edge, on each side.
- `grid`: boolean (default false) — Shows an 8 px grid and, when no alignment is in reach, snaps the layer's corner to it, so it steps along the grid.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick when an edge finds another: higher for centres, lower for the artboard, softest for grid steps. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the artboard and stops every drag and nudge.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the artboard's classes.

Notes:
- Every layer is a native button in the tab order, named by its label and described by its position and the keys: arrow keys nudge it by 1 px and Shift+Arrow by 10, a nudge that lands within the snap distance of a line ahead of it finishes the move and ticks, and each move is announced ("Headline at 192, 24, in line with Photo."). Escape during a drag puts the layer back and is claimed.
- Under reduced motion snaps and returns land in one step with no spring, while the guides, the distance labels and the ticks still show and sound, because alignment is information.
- Layers are placed, not thrown: inside the artboard a release keeps the exact position; only a layer pulled past the edge glides back, carrying its release velocity.
- The artboard is a coordinate space: positions and sizes are artboard px whatever the rendered width, so values stay stable across screens.

### Meld Tags (KQ-1113) — `meld-tags`
Drop one on another; they merge.

Tags you group by hand with a liquid that does the grouping: drag one near another tag or group and a neck of liquid reaches out between them, drawn analytically as a metaball bridge from motion values each frame; let go and the neck draws it in on a spring that carries the release velocity, and it melds with a gloop while the row reflows on the glide. Drag a member out of its group and it stretches against the neck until it tears with a pop and snaps back as a droplet, the group closing the gap; an unseated member springs home on the recoil. The keyboard picks a tag up with Enter, chooses its new group with the arrows and drops it with the same sound.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/meld-tags`

Props:
- `tags`: { id: string; label: string }[] — Every tag, with its id and the label shown and spoken.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[][] (default every tag on its own) — The groups, in order, as arrays of tag ids; a tag on its own is a group of one. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string[][], change: { kind: "meld" | "free"; id: string; group: string[] }) => void — Fires from the drop or the key that changed the groups, with the new groups and what happened: the tag that moved and the group it is in now.
- `label`: string (default "Tags") — The set's accessible name.
- `goo`: number (default 0.5) — How thick the liquid runs, 0 to 1: a thicker neck, a longer stretch before a member tears free, and a slower, bouncier settle.
- `radius`: number (default 24) — The meld radius in px, 8 to 48: how near a dragged tag must come before the neck reaches out and a drop melds.
- `tint`: "mono" | "tint" (default "tint") — Groups in neutral ink, or each group in its own hue from the theme.
- `maxGroup`: number (default 4) — The most tags a group takes, 2 to 6. A full group grows no neck and shows a dashed ring instead.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A gloop when a tag melds (higher for bigger groups) and a pop when one tears free. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the set and stops every drag and pick-up.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the panel's classes.

Notes:
- Every tag is a native button in one roving tab stop (Left, Right, Home and End move focus), named by its label and its group ("Refunds, grouped with Billing"). Enter or Space picks it up; Left and Right choose another tag or group, or on its own for a member; Enter or Space drops it with the same gloop or pop; Escape puts it back and is claimed. Focus follows the tag to its new place, and every change is announced.
- Under reduced motion a drop lands in one step and the row reflows instantly; the neck is drawn only as a still connection while a target is in reach, and colours, counts, rings and sounds still answer.
- Tags in one group read as alternatives in the demo (a pill matches any of its tags); the component only keeps the groups, so the meaning is the host's to give.

### Corner PiP (KQ-1114) — `corner-pip`
Fling it; it finds a corner.

A floating player inside its own frame that you throw into a corner: it follows the finger 1:1 and rubber-bands past the edges, and on release its momentum is projected with a deceleration set by friction, the corner whose quadrant the projected centre lands in is where it goes, and a landing spring that takes the release velocity carries it there, overshooting more the more slippery it is. A throw off a side edge tucks it into a tab you pull or press to bring back. The grip is a button whose arrow keys move it corner to corner and into the edge, with the same flight, swish and soft thud.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/corner-pip`

Props:
- `player`: ReactNode — What plays inside the floating player. Its own controls work as usual; a drag that starts on them still moves the player.
- `children`: ReactNode — The screen behind the player: whatever the frame shows.
- `label`: string — The player's name: its accessible label, and the names of its grip ("Move …") and tab ("Show …").
- `value / defaultValue`: { corner: "top-left" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-right"; tucked: boolean } (default { corner: "bottom-right", tucked: false }) — Where the player sits: a corner, and whether it is tucked into that corner's side edge. Controlled or uncontrolled; a refused move flies back.
- `onValueChange`: (value: CornerPipValue) => void — Fires from the throw or the key that moved the player, with its new place.
- `friction`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly a throw dies, 0 to 1. Low friction coasts further and overshoots the corner; high friction needs a hard fling and settles flat.
- `inset`: number (default 12) — The corner margin in px, 0 to 24.
- `tuck`: boolean (default true) — A throw whose projection leaves through a side edge tucks the player into that edge, leaving a 22 px tab.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The player's width: 112, 144 or 176 px at 16:9, never more than 44% of the frame.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish on a fast throw (higher and louder the faster) and a soft thud on the frame it lands. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the frame and stops every drag and key.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the frame's classes; the frame is 2:1 unless an aspect class here says otherwise.

Notes:
- The player's grip is a button: Left and Right change column, Up and Down change row, pushing on through a side edge tucks it, and Enter or Space moves it clockwise to the next corner. While tucked, the player's contents are inert and the tab is a button that brings it back on click, Enter, Space or an inward arrow; focus moves to the tab when a key tucks it and back to the grip when a key brings it out. Every move is announced, and Escape during a drag puts it back.
- Under reduced motion the player still follows the finger, but a release or a key places it in one step with a short dip in opacity, and the thud still sounds.
- The player lives inside the frame and never uses fixed positioning, so it can sit in any panel, preview or card; its resting place is plain CSS, so the server markup is right at any width.

### Level Vial (KQ-1115) — `level-vial`
The bubble finds the value.

A two-sided slider drawn as a spirit level: dragging tilts the level 1:1 with the finger toward the end the value is heading for, and the bubble drifts after it through the liquid on a spring whose stiffness and damping are the viscosity, lagging, overshooting, stretching with its speed and flattening against the end of the vial. A release is projected from its velocity so a flick carries, and the level settles on the snap spring with the release velocity. It is a slider: arrows move a step, PageUp and PageDown go to the next graduation, Home and End to the extremes, each tilting the level and sending the bubble exactly as a drag does.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/level-vial`

- `min`: number (default -50) — The left extreme. The centre, halfway between min and max, is neutral.
- `max`: number (default 50) — The right extreme.
- `step`: number (default 1) — The value's resolution and what one arrow key moves, counted out from the centre.
- `label`: string — What the level sets: the slider's accessible name, shown above it.
- `format`: (value: number) => string — The reading beside the label and in the spoken value. Defaults to a signed offset from the centre.
- `ends`: [string, string] (default ["left", "right"]) — What the two sides are called in the spoken value, as in "L 20, left of centre."
- `viscosity`: number (default 0.4) — Thin spirit to thick oil, 0 to 1: how far the bubble lags, how much it overshoots and stretches, how far a flick carries, and the glug's pitch.
- `length`: number (default 360) — The level's length in px, 240 to 480; it shrinks to fit a narrower box. The ends always rise the same 10 px, so a longer level tilts less.
- `marks`: number (default 4) — Graduations on each side of the centre, 0 to 8, drawn across the glass and on the housing. PageUp and PageDown move to the next one.
- `tint`: "spirit" | "amber" | "cobalt" | "clear" (default "spirit") — The liquid's colour; the bubble and its rim follow it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a bubbly glug while the bubble moves, louder as it moves faster, pitched by the value and panned by its place. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the level, takes it out of the tab order and ignores drags and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The level is a horizontal role="slider" named by its label, with a sentence in aria-valuetext ("L 20, left of centre." or "Level, at the centre."): ArrowRight/ArrowUp move one step up, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown one step down, PageUp/PageDown to the next graduation (a tenth of the range with no marks), Home and End to the extremes. Each key tilts the level and sends the bubble exactly as a drag would, glug included.

- A drag is touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe over it still scrolls the page. A host changing value moves the bubble silently; only a gesture makes a sound.

### Curve Slider (KQ-1116) — `curve-slider`
A slider that follows any line.

A slider whose track is any line (an arc, a wave or a spiral): the thumb goes to the point on the path nearest the finger by projection onto the sampled path, the value is arc length so equal steps are equal distances however the line bends, and the fill traces the path behind the thumb. A press away from the thumb chases it on the flick spring and then follows 1:1, the ends rubber-band out along their tangents, and a release is projected along the path so a flick carries on round the curve, gliding to its step on the glide spring with the finger's speed. Arrows move a step, PageUp and PageDown go to the next mark, Home and End to the ends, and the thumb glides along the path each time, ticking at every mark it passes.

- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the gesture or key that changed it: once per step crossed while dragging, and once on release, tap or key.
- `min`: number (default 0) — The value at the start of the path.
- `max`: number (default 100) — The value at the end of the path.
- `step`: number (default 1) — The value's resolution and what one arrow key moves.
- `label`: string — What the slider sets: its accessible name, shown above the path.
- `format`: (value: number) => string — The reading beside the label and in the spoken value. Defaults to the number.
- `path`: "arc" | "wave" | "spiral" (default "arc") — The line the track follows: a 240° arc, one and a half periods of a wave, or a spiral of 1.75 turns winding outward. All three project, measure and rubber-band the same way.

- `fill`: boolean (default true) — Trace the path behind the thumb in the accent colour.
- `thickness`: number (default 6) — Track weight in px, 2 to 14; the thumb and beads grow with it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick softly on the frame the thumb crosses a mark (or an end), pitched by its place along the path and panned by where it is. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the slider, takes it out of the tab order and ignores drags and keys.

The thumb glides along the path and ticks at each mark it passes, exactly as a drag would. The focus ring is drawn round the thumb.

- Only the path and the thumb take a press: a press more than 26 drawing units from the line (the middle of an arc, the gaps of a wave) does nothing. On the spiral a drag keeps to the turn it is on rather than hopping to the next.

### Ruler Tape (KQ-1117) — `ruler-tape`
Throw the tape; it stops on a mark.

A length picker drawn as a tape measure: the tape is 1:1 under the finger beneath a fixed needle and rubber-bands past its hook and its cut end. Thrown, its landing is projected from the release speed with a rate set by friction and snapped to the nearest mark, then reached on a critically damped spring whose natural frequency is that friction's time constant, so the coast is an exponential slowdown that stops exactly on the mark; a throw off the end hits it on the snap spring instead, and a slow release catches on the nearest mark with the snap spring's small overshoot. A ratchet ticks as each mark passes the needle and a thunk lands when it stops. Arrows move a mark, PageUp and PageDown a numbered mark, Home and End to the ends, with the same ratchet and thunk.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ruler-tape`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default min) — The length under the needle, in unit. Controlled or uncontrolled; a value the host refuses slides back.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the gesture or key that changed it: per mark while dragging, and once with the landing mark on release, throw, tap or key.
- `min`: number (default 0) — Where the tape starts: its hook.
- `max`: number (default 300 (cm) or 120 (in)) — Where the tape ends.
- `step`: number (default 1 (cm) or 0.1 (in)) — The value of one mark; marks sit on whole multiples of it.
- `label`: string — What is being measured: the slider's accessible name, shown above the reading.
- `unit`: "cm" | "in" (default "cm") — The scale printed on the tape and the reading. Uncontrolled, switching it converts the value so the same length stays under the needle; controlled, the host converts.
- `friction`: number (default 0.4) — How soon a thrown tape stops, 0 to 1: at 0 it coasts like a light reel (a time constant near 400 ms), at 1 it stops like a heavy one (near 100 ms).
- `spacing`: number (default 10) — Pixels between marks, 6 to 16: a denser or looser tape, and how much value one flick covers.
- `majorEvery`: number (default 10) — Marks per numbered mark, 2 to 10, with a medium mark halfway when it is even. Numbers thin out rather than collide when majors are close. PageUp and PageDown move by one numbered mark.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A ratchet tick as each mark passes the needle (so its rate is the tape's speed; numbered marks tick lower and firmer) and a thunk when the tape comes to rest after a gesture. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the tape, takes it out of the tab order and ignores drags and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The tape window is a horizontal role="slider" named by its label, with a sentence in aria-valuetext ("140 centimetres, 1 metre 40." or "55.1 inches, 4 feet 7.1 inches."): ArrowRight/ArrowUp move one mark up, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown one down, PageUp/PageDown to the next or previous numbered mark, Home and End to the ends. The tape slides there, ratchets past each mark and thunks, exactly as a throw would.
- Under reduced motion the tape still follows the finger 1:1, but every settle, throw, tap and key jumps straight to its mark with no coast, while the reading and the sounds still answer.
- The drawing is rebuilt from one motion value each frame and only near the needle, so a tape of any length costs the same, and the server renders exactly what the browser does. It is touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe over it still scrolls the page.

### Fader Sweep (KQ-1118) — `fader-sweep`
Sweep across the faders in one stroke.

A bank of vertical faders joined by a smooth curve that you paint in one stroke: draw across the bank and every fader you pass takes the height where the stroke crossed it, the ones a fast stroke skips catching up on the flick spring, each playing a note pitched by its value so the sweep is heard as the shape it drew. Grab a knob instead and that one fader follows 1:1, rubber-bands past its ends and settles on the glide spring with the release velocity, while the brush's smoothing relaxes painted faders into a smooth contour behind the finger. Every fader is a vertical slider in one roving tab stop: Up and Down step it, Page keys, Home and End jump, Left and Right move between faders, and Shift with Left or Right carries the value along like a stroke.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/fader-sweep`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number[] (default all 0) — One value per band, each between -range and +range. Controlled or uncontrolled; an array of another length is resampled by relative position to the band count.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number[]) => void — Fires from the stroke, drag or key that changed the bank, with every band quantized to step. While a stroke is live the host's echoes are ignored; on release the faders settle on whatever the host says.
- `bands`: number (default 7) — How many faders, 2 to 10. The values are resampled to the new count so the shape survives, and the faders glide to it.
- `smoothing`: number (default 0.35) — How soft the paint brush is, 0 to 1. At 0 each fader keeps exactly the height the stroke gave it; higher, faders behind the finger relax toward their painted neighbours and untouched faders beyond the stroke feather toward it. The fader under the finger is never smoothed.
- `curve`: boolean (default true) — Draw the smooth response curve through the knobs, over a faint fill down to 0.
- `range`: number (default 12) — How far each fader reaches either side of 0. The scale labels follow it and values outside it are shown clamped.
- `step`: number (default 0.5) — The value's resolution and one arrow key's move.
- `label`: string (default "Equalizer") — The bank's accessible name.
- `labels`: string[] — One name per band, printed under it and used as its accessible name. Defaults to log-spaced frequencies from 63 Hz to 16 kHz.
- `format`: (value: number) => string — A band's spoken value, its aria-valuetext. Defaults to "Boosted by 3 decibels", "Cut by 1.5 decibels" or "Flat".
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a note per fader as the stroke catches it and as a moving fader crosses a scale step, pitched by value on a pentatonic scale and panned to its place. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the bank, takes it out of the tab order and ignores strokes.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- Each fader is a vertical role="slider" with a sentence in aria-valuetext, inside a role="group" with one roving tab stop: ArrowUp/ArrowDown step, PageUp/PageDown move a quarter of the range, Home/End go to the ends, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between faders, and Shift+ArrowLeft/ArrowRight carry the focused fader's value into the next through the same brush, spring and note as a stroke. Escape during a stroke puts the bank back.
- Under reduced motion the faders still follow the finger and the curve still redraws, but nothing springs: caught faders, settles and key steps land in one frame and the catch flash is a colour fade. The notes are unchanged.
- Press on a knob to move one fader; press anywhere else in the bank to paint. A drag that leaves its knob's column by a whole column becomes a paint stroke from there, and a pointer stroke is announced once on release.

### Stretch Slider (KQ-1119) — `stretch-slider`
Pull past the end; it pulls back.

A slider whose track is a rubber band: in range the thumb is 1:1 under the finger and snap points catch it with a quiet detent, but pull past either end and the thumb lifts the band off its peg and stretches it longer and thinner, keeping its area and necking where the finger pulls, with a creak that rises with the tension. Let go and it snaps back on a spring that takes the release velocity and rings as long as the elasticity allows, with a twang pitched by how far it was pulled; a throw that runs into an end is caught by the band the same way. Arrow keys step, Page keys jump between snap points, Home and End go to the ends, and a key that would go past an end plucks the band instead.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/stretch-slider`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default min) — The value, min to max. Controlled or uncontrolled; while a drag is live the host's echoes are ignored, and on release the thumb settles on whatever the host says.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the drag or key that changed the value, quantized to step.
- `min`: number (default 0) — The value at the left peg.
- `max`: number (default 100) — The value at the right peg.
- `step`: number (default 1) — The value's resolution and one arrow key's move.
- `label`: string — What the slider sets: its accessible name, shown over the band.
- `format`: (value: number) => string — The reading over the band, the captions under it and the spoken value. Defaults to the number itself.
- `elasticity`: number (default 0.5) — How rubbery the band is, 0 to 1: how far it gives for the same pull, and how it rings when let go, from one small overshoot to three or four bounces.
- `maxStretch`: number (default 40) — The furthest the band stretches past a peg, in px. Faint guides past each peg show the reach, and the track is inset by it so a stretch never leaves the box.
- `snapPoints`: number (default 3) — Equal divisions that carry magnetic detents and ticks under the band; PageUp and PageDown jump between them. 0 makes a plain precise slider.
- `thickness`: number (default 8) — The band's thickness at rest, in px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A creak while the band is stretched that rises with the tension, a twang on release pitched by the stretch, and a quiet detent on snap points. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the slider, takes it out of the tab order and ignores drags.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The band is a role="slider" with a sentence in aria-valuetext: ArrowRight/ArrowUp and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown step, PageUp/PageDown jump to the next snap point (a tenth of the range when there are none), Home/End go to the ends, and a key that would go past an end plucks the band with the same twang a pull past the end makes. Escape during a drag puts the thumb back.
- Under reduced motion the band still stretches and thins under the finger, but nothing rings: a release puts it back on the peg in one short tween, a key's pluck is an accent flash with the twang, and throws and key jumps land in one frame.
- The creak loop starts only when a drag leaves the pegs and stops when the thumb comes back into range, on release, on cancel, on window blur, on a hidden page and on unmount.

### Clip Trim (KQ-1120) — `clip-trim`
Trim the clip from either end.

A trimmer over a procedural waveform: drag either handle to trim and everything outside it dims while the in point, kept length and out point update frame by frame; drag the middle to slide the whole window. Handles follow the finger 1:1, rubber-band against the clip's ends and against each other at the minimum length, spring back on snap with the release velocity and can be thrown, and with beat snapping every beat of the drawn grid is a detent the handle jumps to on flick with a tick. Space or a tap on the middle previews the kept part with a real-time playhead that blips on every beat; start, kept part and end are three sliders whose arrow keys move a step or a beat, Page keys a second or four beats, and Home and End jump to their limits.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/clip-trim`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: { start: number; end: number } (default the whole clip) — The kept span in seconds from the clip's start. Controlled or uncontrolled; while a drag is live the host's echoes are ignored, and on release the handles settle on whatever the host says.
- `onValueChange`: (value: ClipTrimValue) => void — Fires from the drag or key that changed the span, on a beat or a step.
- `duration`: number (default 12) — The clip's length, in seconds.
- `bpm`: number (default 120) — The clip's tempo: the beat grid, the beat snaps, the preview's blips and the waveform's pulse.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds the procedural waveform; the same seed always draws the same clip.
- `label`: string (default "Clip") — The clip's name; the start, kept part and end sliders are named after it.
- `step`: number (default 0.1) — The span's resolution when not snapping to beats, and one arrow key's move.
- `format`: (seconds: number) => string — A time as printed under the strip. Defaults to m:ss.s.
- `onPreviewChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Fires when the preview starts and when it stops, however it stopped.
- `minLength`: number (default 1) — The shortest the kept span can be, in seconds. The handles rubber-band against it.
- `snapBeats`: boolean (default true) — Draw the beat grid and move the handles and the window in beats, each one a detent with a tick. Off, they move freely at step resolution.
- `handle`: "frame" | "bar" | "tab" (default "frame") — How the handles are drawn: a frame around the kept part with grips outside it, thin bars standing proud of the strip, or a hairline with a round tab under it.
- `density`: number (default 5) — The waveform's resolution in bars per second, from coarse blocks to fine texture.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick when a handle is grabbed, finds a beat or is stepped by a key, and a blip when the preview starts and on every beat it crosses. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the trimmer, takes it out of the tab order, ignores drags and stops a preview.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- Start, kept part and end are three role="slider" elements with sentences in aria-valuetext: ArrowLeft/ArrowDown and ArrowRight/ArrowUp move a step (a beat when snapping), PageUp/PageDown a second (four beats), Home/End jump to that slider's limits, Space starts or stops the preview and Escape stops it. A key that would pass a limit bumps against it. Escape during a drag puts the span back.
- Under reduced motion the handles still follow the finger, but beat snaps, spring-backs, throws and key moves land in one frame; the preview's playhead still runs because it is progress, and the ticks and blips are unchanged.
- The preview runs on one linear tween with no frame loop of its own, and stops on a drag, a value change, a hidden page, window blur, disable and unmount; preview starts and stops are announced politely.

### Mood Swipe (KQ-1121) — `mood-swipe`
Swipe the face from frown to grin.

A satisfaction input drawn as one face that you swipe from a frown to a grin: the mouth bends and opens, the eyes go from drooping half-moons to squinting crescents, the brows lift and the cheeks rise, all rebuilt each frame from one number on paths whose commands never change, so the morph is a real interpolation. It follows the finger 1:1, rubber-bands into a deeper frown or a wider grin past the ends, and a release is projected and lands on the nearest stop on the snap spring with its velocity (or coasts on the glide spring when snap is off), while a hum glides an octave with the mood and each stop rings a note. It is a slider: arrow keys step a stop, Page keys jump, Home and End reach frown and grin, with the same flight and sound.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mood-swipe`

Props:
- `label`: string — The question being answered: the slider's accessible name.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0.5) — The mood, 0 (frown) to 1 (grin). With snap on, a value between stops is shown and read at its nearest stop. Controlled or uncontrolled; a refused change flies back.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the swipe, tap or key that changed the mood, with the new value (a stop, or a score to 2 dp with snap off).
- `stops`: number (default 5) — How many detents from frown to grin, 2 to 9. The rail's dots, the words and the note scale follow.
- `labels`: readonly string[] — A word per stop, frown first. Used when there is exactly one per stop; otherwise built-in words (Awful, Poor, Okay, Good, Great for five).
- `face`: "filled" | "line" | "duo" (default "filled") — A solid tinted disc with dark features, an outline face in the tint, or a tinted wash with outline features.
- `colour`: "mood" | "accent" | "ink" (default "mood") — The tint: travels from danger through warn to success with the mood, or stays the accent, or stays ink.
- `snap`: boolean (default true) — Land on stops with one crisp overshoot. Off, the face coasts and rests wherever it stops, and the value is a continuous score.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A hum that glides an octave with the mood while the face moves, and a note on a rising scale at each stop it reaches. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the face, takes it out of the tab order and stops every swipe and key.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the outer wrapper.

Notes:
- The face is a role="slider" named by label, with aria-valuetext such as "Good, 4 of 5". Right and Up step a stop happier, Left and Down a stop sadder (5% steps with snap off), PageUp and PageDown jump, Home and End reach the frown and the grin. A value set by pointer is also spoken once through a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion the face still follows the finger, but a release or a key sets it at its stop in one step, with no lean, no overshoot and no glide, while the note, the word and the value still change.
- A tap on the rail goes to the nearest stop; a tap on the face nudges one stop toward the side tapped. The swipe claims only horizontal travel, so a vertical scroll that starts on the face still scrolls the page.

### Day Strip (KQ-1122) — `day-strip`
Flick through the week.

A horizontal strip of days you throw under a still centre lens. It follows the finger 1:1 and rubber-bands past the first and last day; on release the throw is projected with a deceleration set by friction to the day it would rest on, and the strip decays onto exactly that day with the throw's own momentum, then the lens catches it with a small swell on the recoil spring. The lens magnifies as a fisheye, a tick sounds for every day that passes it (a ratchet that slows as the throw dies), and taps glide a day to the lens on the glide spring. It is a listbox: Left and Right move a day, PageUp and PageDown a week, Home and End the ends, with the same flight and sounds.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/day-strip`

Props:
- `start`: string — The first day on the strip, as an ISO date (2026-09-28). Dates are handled in UTC arithmetic, so the server and the browser draw the same days.
- `days`: number (default 35) — How many days the strip holds.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default today if it is on the strip, else start) — The ISO date under the lens. Controlled or uncontrolled; a refused change flies back.
- `onValueChange`: (day: string) => void — Fires from the throw, tap, key or wheel that chose a day, with its ISO date — at release, before the strip has landed.
- `events`: Readonly<Record<string, number>> — Event counts by ISO date: up to three dots are drawn under a day, and the count shows in the header and the day's accessible name.
- `today`: string — The ISO date to mark as today: its date is drawn in the accent and its name says so.
- `label`: string (default "Day") — The strip's accessible name.
- `friction`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly a throw dies, 0 to 1: a light strip coasts through a couple of weeks from a hard flick, a heavy one stops in a few days.
- `lens`: number (default 1.3) — The lens's magnification, 1 to 1.6. The day under it swells and its neighbours part to make room; at 1 the frame marks the day and nothing swells. The strip grows taller to fit.
- `visible`: number (default 7) — How many days fit across the strip, 3 to 15.
- `dots`: boolean (default true) — Dots under days with events, and the event count in the header.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for every day that passes the lens, higher and louder the faster it goes, and a detent as a day lands. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the strip, takes it out of the tab order and stops every throw, tap, key and wheel.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the outer wrapper.

Notes:
- The strip is a role="listbox" with one tab stop and aria-activedescendant on the day under the lens; every day is an option named in full ("Tuesday 6 October 2026, today, 2 events"). Left and Right move a day, PageUp and PageDown a week, Home and End the first and last day, and Escape during a drag puts the strip back.
- Under reduced motion the strip still follows the finger, but a release, a tap or a key puts the chosen day under the lens in one step, with no coasting and no swell; the magnification, the header and the landing detent are unchanged.
- The swipe claims only horizontal travel (a vertical scroll that starts on the strip still scrolls the page), and a sideways trackpad swipe or shift-wheel scrolls the strip and settles on the nearest day when it stops.

### Slot Swipe (KQ-1123) — `slot-swipe`
Swipe it into the slot.

An inbox whose rows sit between a mail slot and a drawer. Swipe a row toward the slot and the slit opens to meet it while the row feeds in edgewise, clipped at the slit and squashed thinner the deeper it goes; past the threshold (or thrown past it, by projection) it runs in on the snap spring with its release velocity and the slot shuts on the recoil spring with a thwup. Swipe toward the drawer and the drawer slides out with a clock that winds and ticks as you pull; the row drops in, the clock spins round to the snooze hour and the drawer shuts. A short swipe springs back, Delete and S do the same as the swipes with the same frames and sounds, and Undo brings the last row back out of wherever it went.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/slot-swipe`

Props:
- `items`: { id: string; from: string; subject: string; time?: string }[] — Every row that can appear.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default every item, in order) — The ids still in the inbox, in order. Controlled or uncontrolled; a row the host keeps after a swipe comes back out of the slot or drawer.
- `onValueChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the swipe, key or Undo that changed the list, with the ids left — at the commit, while the row is still going in.
- `onAction`: (id: string, action: "archive" | "snooze") => void — Fires with what happened to a row: into the slot (archive) or into the drawer (snooze).
- `onOpen`: (id: string) => void — A row pressed without a swipe, or Enter or Space on it.
- `label`: string (default "Inbox") — The list's name, shown in the header with the count.
- `snoozeHour`: number (default 9) — The hour the drawer's clock spins to, 0 to 23; also the time in the announcement and the header.
- `threshold`: number (default 0.35) — How far a row must go, or be thrown, as a share of its lane (0.2 to 0.6) before it commits. The slot and drawer are fully open, and light up, at this point.
- `side`: "right" | "left" (default "right") — Which end of each lane the slot is on; the drawer takes the other.
- `squash`: number (default 0.5) — How much a row squeezes to fit the slot or the drawer, 0 to 1: up to 60% thinner, and a little longer along the swipe.
- `undo`: boolean (default true) — An Undo button in the header after each swipe, which brings the row back out of where it went.
- `empty`: ReactNode (default "Inbox zero") — Shown when nothing is left.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A detent as a row arms, paper as it feeds into the slot and a thwup as the slot shuts; the drawer's clock ticks as it winds and spins, and the drawer shuts with a clack. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the rows and stops every swipe, key and Undo.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the outer wrapper.

Notes:
- Rows are buttons in a role="list" with one tab stop: Up and Down (and Home and End) move between them, Delete or Backspace sends the focused row into the slot, S into the drawer, and Enter or Space opens it. Focus moves to the next row (or Undo) as a row leaves, what happened is spoken once through a polite live region, and Escape during a drag puts the row back.
- Under reduced motion the row still follows the finger and the slot and drawer still open with it, but a commit fades the row out in place and closes its lane in one step, the clock's hands jump to the snooze hour, and every sound and announcement is unchanged.
- The swipe claims only horizontal travel, so a vertical scroll that starts on a row still scrolls the page; every lane clips its own row, so nothing draws outside the list.

Tap through; swipe to the next person.

A stories viewer on a real CSS 3D cube inside its own phone-shaped screen: a tap on the right steps forward and on the left steps back, a held press pauses, and the bars fill and advance on their own. - `bars`: "split" | "single" | "ring" (default "split") — How progress is drawn: a bar per story, one bar notched at each story, or arcs around the avatar in the header.

- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for every story a tap, key or open starts, climbing the scale, and a whoosh when a swipe, key or tap turns the cube (a low one when it closes). Automatic advances are silent. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

Notes:

The header's Pause and Close are real buttons, and each tap zone is a button a screen reader can press. New stories, pauses and closing are announced.

- The bars run only while the viewer is open, on screen and in a visible tab, and not while it is held, dragged or turning. On touch the viewer takes sideways and downward swipes while a finger moving up still scrolls the page.

### Filter Swipe (KQ-1125) — `filter-swipe`
Swipe across; the next look slides over.

A photo whose look changes as you swipe across it: the boundary between the current look and the incoming one sits under the finger 1:1 with the incoming look's name riding it, and a release that carries or throws it past the threshold runs on to the far edge on the glide spring with the release velocity, while a short one slides back. - `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the photo and ignores swipes, dots and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the frame's classes; the frame is w-full at 4:3 unless an aspect class here says otherwise.

Notes:
- The looks are a radio group of dots inside the frame with a roving tab stop: Arrow Right and Down choose the next look, Arrow Left and Up the previous one, Home and End the first and last, and a click on a dot chooses it. Each slides the look in from the side a swipe would bring it, with the same swish and click, and the chosen look is announced.
- Under reduced motion the boundary never travels and the picture never rubber-bands: a drag fades the incoming look over the whole photo in proportion, with its name centred, and a release, key or dot cross-fades.
- The frame takes horizontal swipes and leaves vertical ones to the page (touch-action pan-y), so it can sit in a scrolling feed.

### Gesture Player (KQ-1126) — `gesture-player`
Swipe the picture to seek.

A player whose picture is the control: a sideways swipe seeks 1:1 with a time bubble riding the bar that shows where you are and how far you have jumped, and its release is projected and glides on the glide spring with the release velocity. Swipes up and down set volume on the right half and brightness on the left, a side meter filling and stretching a little past either end before it snaps back, and a double tap on a side skips with a ripple that adds up as you keep tapping. The host draws the picture from a motion value of the time, so a scrub moves the scene at frame rate without a render, and the focusable picture takes Space, the arrows and Shift with them along the same paths, with a tick per second scrubbed and a click per skip.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/gesture-player`

Props:
- `children`: (time: MotionValue<number>) => ReactNode — The picture, drawn from the playback time in seconds. Bind it with useTransform so a scrub moves the scene every frame without a render.
- `label`: string — The clip's title: the player's accessible name.
- `duration`: number — Length of the clip, in seconds.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — Position in seconds. A new value from the host seeks there; the player reports every seek and skip, and each whole second as it plays.
- `onValueChange`: (seconds: number) => void — Fires with the landing of every seek and skip, and with each whole second passed while playing.
- `playing / defaultPlaying`: boolean (default false) — Whether it plays. Playback runs only while the page is visible and nothing is being scrubbed, and stops at the end.
- `onPlayingChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Fires from the tap, key or button that played or paused, and with false at the end.
- `volume / defaultVolume`: number (default 0.7) — Volume, 0 to 1. Reported as a swipe moves it; after the release the meter settles on the host's value, so a refused change springs back.
- `onVolumeChange`: (volume: number) => void — Fires as a vertical swipe or an arrow key changes the volume.
- `brightness / defaultBrightness`: number (default 0.6) — Brightness, 0 to 1, applied as a CSS brightness from 0.4 to 1.4: 0.6 shows the picture as drawn.
- `onBrightnessChange`: (brightness: number) => void — Fires as a vertical swipe on the left half or Shift with an arrow key changes the brightness.
- `sensitivity`: number (default 1) — How far a swipe goes, 0.5 to 2: a swipe across the picture seeks sensitivity × 90 seconds, and one of 80% of its height sweeps a level from end to end at 1.
- `zones`: boolean (default true) — A brightness half on the left and a volume half on the right, the active half washed while it is set. Off, a vertical swipe anywhere sets the volume.
- `skip`: number (default 10) — Seconds a double tap or an arrow key skips, 5 to 15. Further taps on the same side while the ripple is up add another skip each.
- `hints`: boolean (default true) — Faint glyphs over the paused, idle picture showing what it answers to: the skips on the sides and the levels at the top.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for every whole second a seek crosses (a ratchet at most every 35 ms, pitched and panned by position), a tick per tenth of a level, and a click per skip. Playback is silent. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the player, holds playback, and ignores taps, swipes and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the player's classes; it is w-full at 16:9 unless an aspect class here says otherwise.

Notes:
- The picture is a focusable group: Space or K plays and pauses, Left and Right (or J and L) skip, Shift with Left or Right seeks one second, Home and End jump to the start and end, Up and Down set the volume and, with zones, Shift with Up or Down sets the brightness. Each shows the gesture's bubble, meter or ripple and makes its sound. A real Play button sits in the bar, and settled results are announced.
- Under reduced motion the bubble, meter and ripple appear and fade without travelling or swelling, a released seek or a skip lands at once, and levels settle without springing; the scrub still follows the finger and the readout still counts.
- The picture takes both axes (touch-action none), as a full-bleed player does; a middle tap plays at once, while a lone tap on a side waits a moment for a second tap.

### Hang Label (KQ-1127) — `hang-label`
The label lifts and hangs on the edge.

A text field whose label lifts off the placeholder on the glide spring, flipping up on a hinge along its top edge as it travels, and lands on the field's top edge where it hangs and swings on an underdamped pendulum spring whose first swing peaks at the swing angle; the outline style cuts a notch in the border under it with a mask, so the field sits on any background. An error shakes the tag on a keyframe tween and a character budget fills as a thread under the field on glide. Tabbing into the field lifts and hangs the label exactly as a click does, and everything else, typing, selection, IME composition, paste and autofill, is the browser's own input.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/hang-label`

Props:
- `label`: string — What the field is for: the visible label (the hanging tag is the real label element) and the input's accessible name.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The text. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires with the new text on every edit: typing, paste, composition and autofill.
- `error`: string | null — What is wrong, in a sentence. Shown under the field in a polite live region, sets aria-invalid, and shakes the label when it arrives or changes.
- `shakeKey`: string | number — Change it to shake the label again with the same error, e.g. a form's submit count.
- `hint`: string — Helper text under the field, replaced by the error while one shows.
- `maxLength`: number — The character budget, also the input's native maxlength.
- `swing`: number (default 5) — How far the tag swings when it lands on the edge, in degrees, 0 to 10. A long label swings less, so its rising corner never leaves the component's box.
- `stiffness`: number (default 220) — The pendulum's spring stiffness, 60 to 600: low is a slow, lazy sway, high a quick, tight wobble.
- `style`: "outline" | "filled" | "line" (default "outline") — A framed field with a notch cut under the tag, a filled field whose tag reads as a raised tab, or an underline.
- `budget`: boolean (default true) — Show the budget as a thread filling under the field, cobalt, then warn in the last 20%, with a count. Needs maxLength.
- `type`: "text" | "email" | "tel" | "url" | "password" | "search" (default "text") — The input's type.
- `name`: string — The input's name, for forms.
- `autoComplete`: string — The input's autocomplete hint. Autofill lifts the label, even before the page has had a key.
- `inputMode`: "none" | "text" | "tel" | "url" | "email" | "numeric" | "decimal" | "search" — The on-screen keyboard to offer.
- `placeholder`: string — Shown inside the field only once the label has lifted out of the way.
- `required`: boolean — The input's native required.
- `onFocus`: (event: React.FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void — The input's focus event.
- `onBlur`: (event: React.FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void — The input's blur event, e.g. to validate on leaving the field.
- `ref`: React.Ref<HTMLInputElement> — The input element, e.g. to focus the field when a submit is refused.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a tick on the frame the tag lands (only while the field has focus), a shrug with the error shake, and a detent on the key that fills the budget. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the field and disables the input; the label stays where the text puts it.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- A real <input> named by a real <label for>: Tab into the field and the label lifts, flips and hangs with the same tick a click gives; typing, selection, IME composition, paste and autofill are native. The field's own frame is the focus indicator (a 2px ring-coloured border, or a 2px rule), deliberately not an outline ring, which would run through the hanging tag. The error and hint are linked with aria-describedby, and the budget is spoken only at thresholds ("6 characters left.", "No characters left.").
- Under reduced motion the label cross-fades between the placeholder spot and the edge with no travel, flip, swing or shake, while the notch, the colours, the error message and the budget thread still answer.
- Pass the form's submit count as shakeKey (and focus the field through ref) so each refused submit shakes the label again on the edge where it hangs.

### Roll Search (KQ-1128) — `roll-search`
The lens rolls open into a field.

A search that lives as a round lens at the right end of its slot: pressed, or with / typed anywhere on the page, the lens rolls to the left end like a wheel on the snap spring while the field unrolls behind it like a strip of carpet, one motion value driving the pill's width, the lens's place and its turn, so the wheel never slips and always lands upright. Results drop in below on snap in a cascade, in a panel whose height is measured and glides, with the query lit in each; Escape rolls it back up on glide. The input is a real combobox: arrows move through the results, Enter picks one, Escape rolls it up and returns focus to the lens.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/roll-search`

- `label`: string — What is being searched, as "Search docs": the lens button's name and the input's visible label, which heads the results panel.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Search") — The input's placeholder.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The query. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (query: string) => void — Fires with the new query on every edit, and with "" when the search rolls up.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default false) — Whether the field is rolled open. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host change rolls it silently.

- `filter`: (item: RollSearchItem, query: string) => boolean — Whether an item answers a query. Defaults to every word of the query appearing in its label, meta or keywords.
- `limit`: number (default 4) — The most results shown at once; the panel says "4 of 9" when there are more.
- `shortcut`: string | null (default "/") — The key that opens it from anywhere on the page, shown as a small key cap beside the lens; null for none. It never fires while typing in a field, with a modifier, during composition, or behind a dialog.
- `width`: number (default 320) — How far the field unrolls, in px, 200 to 400. It shrinks to fit a narrower box.
- `roll`: boolean (default true) — The lens turns as it travels, like a wheel, rocking slightly against the end; off, it slides.
- `results`: "list" | "cards" (default "list") — Compact rows with a page glyph and the meta at the end, or small cards in two columns.
- `highlight`: boolean (default true) — Light every occurrence of the query's words in each result.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a whir while the lens rolls, its gain and pitch following the lens's speed (a swish when it slides), and a tick as each arriving result lands. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

Notes:

Open, the input is a role="combobox" with aria-activedescendant over a listbox: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active result, Enter picks it (the first when none is active), Escape rolls it back up wherever focus is inside the component and returns focus to the lens. Leaving an empty search rolls it up too, and the result count is spoken politely once typing pauses.
- Under reduced motion nothing rolls or drops: the slot cross-fades between closed and open, results fade in place and the panel height changes on a short tween; the result ticks still mark arrivals.
- The results panel sits in the flow under the field and its height is measured, so give the component room below it, or place it where the page can grow.

### Sift Filter (KQ-1129) — `sift-filter`
Type; what doesn't match falls away.

A filter field over a two-column set of cards: as you type, every card that stops matching drops off the bottom under constant acceleration with a slight spin, while the matches close ranks on the glide spring, and the set's floor waits for the last faller to pass through it before it glides up to fit. Deleting back or clearing brings the fallen up from below the floor on the snap spring, their spin unwinding, in a stagger that stays inside the choreography budget. The field is a real input: Escape clears it with the same rise as deleting, fallen cards leave the tab order and the accessibility tree at once, and IME composition filters on what was committed.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sift-filter`

- `placeholder`: string (default "Type to filter") — The input's placeholder.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The query. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (query: string) => void — Fires with the new query on every edit, and with "" when cleared.
- `filter`: (item: SiftFilterItem, query: string) => boolean — Whether a card answers a query. Defaults to every word of the query appearing in its title, meta or tags.
- `onSelect`: (item: SiftFilterItem) => void — Makes each card a button, and fires with the card pressed.
- `gravity`: number (default 2750) — How hard cards fall, in px/s², 1000 to 6000: a fall of d px takes √(2d/g). Also how hard the fallen are thrown back up.
- `spin`: number (default 14) — How far a card turns on its way down, in degrees, 0 to 40. Each card falls its own way, the same way every time.
- `stagger`: number (default 35) — The gap between one card leaving (or returning) and the next, in ms, 0 to 100, tightened so a whole cascade stays within 600ms.
- `highlight`: boolean (default true) — Light the query's words in each card's title and meta.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a patter, a soft plip as each card passes through the floor (pitched per card, panned by column), and a rise when an edit brings cards back. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the field and the clear button, and makes cards plain.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- A real <input> with a visible <label for>; Escape clears it (and only claims the key when there is text to clear), as does the Clear filter button, with the same rise and sound as deleting. The set is a list; fallen cards are aria-hidden and inert from the moment they start to fall, and "3 of 10 match." is spoken politely once typing pauses.
- Under reduced motion nothing falls, spins or travels: cards that stop matching fade out in place, survivors dip and reappear in their new slots, returning cards fade in, and the floor changes height on a short tween; the count, the spoken summary and the patter still answer.
- Cards are a fixed 64px tall in two percentage columns, so the set's height is known before anything is measured and it renders the same on the server; titles and metas truncate with their full text in a tooltip.

### Plain Date (KQ-1130) — `plain-date`
Type it the way you say it.

A date field you type in words: it reads today, tomorrow, next fri 3pm, in 2 weeks or oct 23 against a now you pass, lights the words it used, slides the date out of the end of the phrase as a chip on the snap spring, and lights the day in a mini calendar whose light hops on snap and whose page turns on glide when the month changes. A phrase with two readings offers both chips; ArrowDown and ArrowUp choose, Enter or a click sets, Escape puts back the last set phrase. It is a real input with the combobox pattern, so typing, selection, IME, paste and undo stay native.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/plain-date`

Props:
- `label`: string — What the date is for. Shown above the field and tied to it by id.
- `now`: Date — The moment phrases are read against. Required. Pass a fixed moment or one taken in an effect, never new Date() during render.
- `value / defaultValue`: Date | null (default null) — The committed date. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host that sets a date the field did not report sees it written back as a phrase the field reads ("fri 23 oct 3:00pm").
- `onValueChange`: (value: Date | null, detail: { hasTime: boolean }) => void — Fires from the Enter, chip click or blur that committed it, with whether a time was given. null when the field is cleared and Enter pressed.
- `defaultText`: string — The phrase the field starts with, read but not committed.
- `placeholder`: string (default "tomorrow 9am") — The field's placeholder.
- `weekStart`: "mon" | "sun" | "sat" (default "mon") — The calendar's first column, each day's chime on the scale, and where "this week" ends, which decides whether next <weekday> has two readings.
- `format`: "short" | "long" | "iso" | "relative" (default "short") — How the chip writes the date: Fri 23 Oct, Friday 23 October, 2026-10-23 with a 24-hour time, or In 10 days with the date underneath.
- `calendar`: boolean (default true) — Show the mini calendar beside the field.
- `strict`: boolean (default false) — Read only the exact grammar and guess nothing: no short forms or prefixes, no bare hours, unknown words stop the parse, and a phrase with two readings has none chosen until you pick.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A soft chime when the chosen date changes, pitched by weekday and panned by its calendar column, and a click when it is set. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the field and its chips and dims the calendar.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The grammar: today, tomorrow, in <n> days or weeks, <weekday>, this <weekday>, next <weekday>, <month> <day> [<year>] or <day> <month> [<year>], and a time anywhere (3pm, 3:30pm, 15:00, noon); "at", "on", "the", "of" are filler. next <weekday> has two readings while that day is still ahead this week. The input is a combobox whose options are the reading chips: ArrowDown and ArrowUp choose, Enter commits (and is left alone when the chosen date is already set, so a form can submit), Escape restores the last committed phrase undoably, and blur commits an unambiguous reading. Readings are announced once typing settles.
- Under reduced motion the chips and the calendar light fade in place instead of travelling, the month changes with a cross-fade and the check appears without drawing; every reading, highlight, ring and chime still happens.
- Nothing reads the clock during render: every date is local-time arithmetic on the now you pass, so server and browser render the same markup.

### Calc Field (KQ-1131) — `calc-field`
Type the sum; the answer keeps up.

An amount field that takes arithmetic: type 1240/3, 12*4+3 or 15% and the answer rides in a bubble just past the last character, kept up with on the snap spring, its digits rolling up as the answer grows and down as it shrinks. Enter or leaving the field commits: the sum folds away, or down into a receipt, on the exit tween while the answer folds down into place on snap; a character that can never be arithmetic is refused with a soft shake. The parser is a small recursive descent with no eval, and the input stays native, so typing, IME, paste and undo work, and undo brings a committed sum back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/calc-field`

Props:
- `label`: string — What the amount is. Shown above the field and tied to it by id.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The committed amount, already rounded. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host that sets an amount the field did not report sees it written into the field.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number | null) => void — Fires from the Enter or blur that committed it, with the rounded amount; null when the field is emptied and committed.
- `defaultText`: string — A sum the field starts with, worked out but not committed.
- `percentOf`: number — What a bare percentage is a share of: with 1240, 15% is 186. Without it a bare percentage is its fraction.
- `placeholder`: string (default "0.00" at the field's precision) — The field's placeholder.
- `precision`: number (default 2) — Decimals in the answer and the committed amount, 0 to 3 — the range currencies use.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — An ISO currency code whose symbol sits before the field and in the bubble, or "none" for a plain number.
- `expression`: boolean (default true) — Write the sum out under the field while you type (× ÷ −, and which way it was rounded when it was), fold it down into a receipt on commit, and make the receipt a button that brings the sum back. Off, the sum folds away with nothing kept.
- `rounding`: "half-up" | "half-even" | "up" | "down" (default "half-up") — How the answer is brought to precision, on its decimal digits (1.005 is 1.01 half up). "up" and "down" are away from and toward zero. A rounded answer shows ≈, and the tape names the mode.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick as the answer changes, pitched by its size and panned by the bubble's place, a click on commit, and a quiet shrug with each shake. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the field and the receipt.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- Arithmetic: + − × ÷ (also * / x), brackets, unary signs, decimals, thousands commas and %, where a + b% adds b% of a and a bare b% is b% of percentOf. Enter commits and is claimed only when there is something to commit, so a form still submits on a second Enter; blur commits too; Escape restores the last committed text; undo after a commit brings the sum back. An unfinished sum keeps its last answer, dimmed. The answer is in the input's description and announced once typing settles, never per keystroke.
- Under reduced motion the bubble moves without travel, digits cross-fade instead of rolling, the commit is a cross-fade and a failed commit turns the border danger instead of shaking; the answer, receipt and sounds still arrive.
- The parser never throws and never evaluates code: anything it cannot work out comes back as a sentence ("Two operators in a row", "Can’t divide by zero") shown under the field and set as aria-invalid.
