### Ratio Morph (KQ-1133) — `ratio-morph`
Pick a shape; the picture reframes.

An aspect-ratio picker that reframes a picture: choosing a shape glides the frame's width and height to the new ratio on the glide spring, with four corner brackets riding its corners, while the picture is re-laid every frame so its focal point stays as near the centre as its edges allow. Pressing the stage brings the focal reticle to the finger 1:1 (it swells on flick) while a ghost of the whole picture fades in round the frame; past the picture's edge the reticle rubber-bands, and on release the throw is projected and the picture glides to re-centre on the new point. The chips are a radiogroup whose arrows choose and whose Home and End jump; the stage takes arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps) to move the focal point with the same glide and sounds.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ratio-morph`

Props:
- `ratios`: "social" | "photo" | "screen" | string[] (default "social") — The shapes offered, in chip order: social is 1:1, 4:5, 16:9 and 9:16; photo is 3:2, 4:3, 1:1 and 2:3; screen is 16:9, 16:10, 21:9 and 4:3. Or your own list of "w:h" strings. RATIO_MORPH_SETS exports the named sets.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first of ratios) — The chosen ratio, as "w:h". A value that is not in the list shows the first ratio.
- `onValueChange`: (ratio: string) => void — Fires from the press or key that chose a new ratio. In controlled mode the frame morphs once the host passes the new value back.
- `focalPoint / defaultFocalPoint`: { x: number; y: number } (default { x: 0.5, y: 0.5 }) — The point the frame keeps in view as it changes shape, as fractions of the picture's width and height.
- `onFocalPointChange`: (point: { x: number; y: number }) => void — Fires once per drag release, tap or arrow key, with the new point rounded to three places.
- `brackets`: number (default 16) — The corner brackets' arm length in px, 6 to 40: short ticks to nearly closed corners.
- `focal`: boolean (default true) — Marks the focal point with a reticle on the picture.
- `grid`: boolean (default false) — Rule-of-thirds lines inside the frame that ride the morph; faint at rest, brighter while the picture is held.
- `picture`: ReactNode (default a procedural harbour at dusk) — What is framed. It is laid out in a box of pictureRatio and scaled, so pass something that fills its box, such as an img with object-cover.
- `pictureRatio`: number (default 1.5) — The picture's own width over its height.
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows, read with the stage's instructions. Defaults to a description of the built-in harbour.
- `label`: string (default "Aspect ratio") — The ratio chips' accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A detent when a ratio is chosen and a click on the frame the morph lands, both pitched by the shape; a detent when a drag meets the picture's edge and a click on release. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the picker and blocks the chips, drags, taps and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the wrapper that holds the stage and the chips.

Notes:
- The chips are a role=radiogroup of radios with one tab stop: any arrow moves and chooses (wrapping), Home and End jump, and each is named as a shape ("4 by 5, portrait"). The stage is a focusable role=application ("picture frame") described by the alt text and its instructions; arrows move the focal point 5%, Shift+arrows 20%, and a polite live region says the new point once per move.
- Under reduced motion the frame changes shape at once and its brackets fade in at the new corners; the picture re-lays at once. A drag still follows the finger 1:1 but lands without a projected glide, and keys jump. The reticle, grid, ghost fade and sounds are unchanged.
- The stage is touch-action: none, since the drag is two-dimensional. Its width is measured, so the frame is as large as the column allows; the server and the first client render use a 320px stage, then it resizes without a morph or a sound.

### Seat Map (KQ-1134) — `seat-map`
Pick your seats; the row makes room.

A seating chart for one booking: pressing a free seat flips it over on its centre line to its chosen face on the snap spring, with a clack as it lands flat, and the row makes room as its neighbours in the block are kicked aside by a velocity whose target is their own place, so each sways away and back on snap. While picks remain, the free seats beside yours light as together suggestions; taken seats are hatched, and the total rolls digit by digit on glide with a tick. It is a multi-select grid with one tab stop: arrows roam seat by seat over the aisles, Home, End, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End, PageUp and PageDown jump, and Space or Enter picks with the same flip and sounds.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/seat-map`

Props:
- `rows`: number (default 5) — Rows of seats, 1 to 12, lettered from the stage back with I and O skipped. More rows make smaller seats (at most 22px) so the grid stays within about 172px.
- `columns`: number (default 12) — Seats in each row, 4 to 16, numbered from the left.
- `aisles`: number (default 2) — Aisles splitting each row, 0 to 3. Two make the classic short-long-short blocks; otherwise the blocks are even with any spare seats in the middle.
- `tiers`: boolean (default true) — Prices the rows in three bands (front, centre and rear by thirds, the centre taking the remainder), each with its own tint and named in the readout.
- `maxPicks`: number (default 4) — The most seats one booking may hold, 1 to 12. At the limit the other free seats dim and a press is refused with a shrug.
- `taken`: string[] (default []) — Seats already sold, by id (row letter and seat number, "C7"). seatMapId(rowIndex, seatNumber) builds an id the way the map does.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The chosen seats' ids in the order they were chosen. Ids that are off the map or taken are ignored.
- `onValueChange`: (seats: string[]) => void — Fires from the press or key that chose or released a seat. A seat flips only once the value that is shown includes it.
- `price`: number (default 36) — Every seat's price when tiers is off.
- `tierPrices`: [number, number, number] (default [48, 36, 24]) — Front, centre and rear prices when tiers is on.
- `format`: (amount: number) => string (default US dollars) — How prices and the total are printed. The total's digits roll; any other characters stay put.
- `label`: string (default "Seats") — The grid's accessible name.
- `stageLabel`: string (default "Stage") — Printed under the curve at the top of the map.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A clack as a seat lands flat, pitched up with each seat you hold and panned by its column; a softer one as a released seat lands back; a tick as the total rolls; a quiet shrug for a refused seat. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the map and blocks picks; no seat takes focus.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the wrapper, whose max width is set from the seat size so the footer lines up with the grid.

Notes:
- The map is role=grid with aria-multiselectable; each row has a rowheader letter, and each seat is a gridcell with aria-selected (aria-disabled when taken) and a one-string name such as "Row C, seat 7, centre, $36.00, suggested". One seat is the tab stop. Arrows move a seat at a time, stepping over aisles; Home and End go to the row's ends, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the corners, PageUp and PageDown to the first and last rows; Space or Enter picks or releases. A polite live region says each change once, from the value actually shown.
- Under reduced motion seats cross-fade from their free face to their chosen face instead of flipping, nothing sways, and the total swaps in place. Suggestions, dimming, sounds and announcements are unchanged.
- The footer reads out the seat under the pointer or focus (its band and price, or that it is taken or yours), else the suggestions or your seats. Seats are touch-manipulation, so the page still scrolls from the map.

### Tool Dock (KQ-1135) — `tool-dock`
Pick a tool; its options unfold beside it.

The tool rail of a drawing canvas and the canvas it drives: the active tool sits on an indicator that slides to each new choice on the snap spring with a tick pitched up the rail, and a tool with variants unfolds its options beside it with a swish — a panel revealed from the rail's edge whose entries step out on snap, or a drawer that glides open inside the rail on glide. Single-letter shortcuts switch tools while focus or the pointer is on the dock (never while typing), the key of the active tool cycles its variants, and the canvas shows the tool's own cursor, drawn 1:1 under the pointer and popping to each new shape on snap. The rail is a toolbar of pressed buttons with one tab stop: arrows move, Space or Enter choose, and the arrow toward the options opens them as a menu of radio items with focus inside.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tool-dock`

Props:
- `tools`: { id: string; label: string; glyph?: ToolDockGlyph; icon?: ReactNode; cursor?: ReactNode; key?: string; variants?: { id: string; label: string; glyph?: ToolDockGlyph; icon?: ReactNode; cursor?: ReactNode; key?: string }[] }[] — The rail, top to bottom (or left to right). A tool with variants shows the last one used; key is a single letter. Built-in glyphs, each with a cursor: move, hand, frame, rect, ellipse, line, polygon, pen, pencil, brush, text, eraser, comment.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first tool (its first variant)) — The active tool's id, or the active variant's id for a tool that has them.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the press, key or shortcut that changed the tool.
- `orientation`: "vertical" | "horizontal" (default "vertical") — A rail down the canvas's left, or centred along its foot.
- `shortcuts`: boolean (default true) — Single-letter keys switch tools and each button shows its letter (and names it in aria-keyshortcuts). Keys act while focus is in the dock, or while the pointer is over it and nothing else has focus; never in a field or with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt, and a handled key is claimed.
- `flyout`: "side" | "tray" (default "side") — A tool's options float in a panel beside the rail (over the canvas, placed inside the component's box), or open as a drawer inside the rail that pushes the tools after it.
- `labels`: boolean (default false) — A label under each icon; the rail widens to fit. Off, the name is still each button's accessible name.
- `children`: ReactNode — What is on the canvas, laid out inside it (position it absolutely to fill).
- `canvasHeight`: number (default 400) — The canvas's height in px.
- `label`: string (default "Tools") — The rail's accessible name.
- `canvasLabel`: string (default "Canvas") — The canvas's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick on every tool or variant change, pitched up the rail on a pentatonic scale and panned to the button; a swish as options unfold and a lower, quieter one as they fold. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the dock, disables its buttons and stops the shortcuts; the system cursor comes back over the canvas.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the wrapper that holds the rail and the canvas.

Notes:
- The rail is role=toolbar (with aria-orientation) of buttons with aria-pressed and one tab stop: arrows along the rail move focus, Home and End jump, Space or Enter choose. A tool with variants has aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded; Space, Enter or the arrow toward the options (Right on a vertical rail, Up on a horizontal one) opens them as a role=menu of menuitemradio with focus on the checked one. There arrows move, Space or Enter choose and fold back to the tool, Escape or the arrow back folds without choosing, and focus leaving folds them. A shortcut's change is announced once in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion the indicator moves at once, options fade in and out with no reveal or step (a tray opens at full height), and the canvas cursor still follows the pointer but parks at once and swaps its shape with a fade. Sounds are unchanged.
- The canvas hides the system cursor and draws the tool's own with its hotspot under the pointer, parking it at the centre when the pointer leaves so a keyboard or touch user still sees the tool change; a tap moves it to the finger. A press anywhere outside the rail and its options folds them.

### Lasso Grid (KQ-1136) — `lasso-grid`
Draw around what you want.

A file grid with rubber-band selection: drag anywhere and a box (or, with Alt or mode="lasso", a freehand loop) follows the pointer 1:1, lighting every tile it catches and squeezing it a little on the snap spring while the band holds it. Let go and the band contracts onto what it caught on the same snap spring, one crisp overshoot like a rubber band let go around a bundle, while a count badge glides after the selection's corner on the glide spring. Arrow keys move and select in two dimensions, Shift+Arrow draws the same band from the keyboard and snaps it tight when Shift is released, Space toggles, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all and Escape clears.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/lasso-grid`

Props:
- `items`: LassoGridItem[] — The files, in reading order: id, name (the label and accessible name) and an optional kind — folder, image, doc, sheet, audio or video — that picks the glyph.
- `label`: string — The grid's accessible name.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The selected ids, controlled or uncontrolled. A controlled grid shows the host's answer after each band, tap or key.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string[]) => void — Fires once per band (on release), per tap and per key, with the new selection in item order.
- `mode`: "box" | "lasso" (default "box") — The band's shape: a rectangle, or a freehand loop that tightens into a box on release. Alt held as a drag starts draws the other one.
- `hit`: "touch" | "contain" (default "touch") — Whether a tile is caught as soon as the band touches it, or only once the band encloses it.
- `badge`: boolean (default true) — A count badge that rides the top-right corner of the selection, gliding after it as it changes, its figure rolling.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick per tile as the band catches it, climbing a pentatonic step each time, and a tock on release. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the grid and blocks selection; arrow keys still move focus.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- It is a multi-select listbox of options with roving focus: Arrow keys move in two dimensions and select the tile they land on, Ctrl/Cmd+Arrow moves focus only, Space toggles a tile, Shift+Arrow grows a box from the anchor tile — drawn on screen like the pointer's band — and releasing Shift snaps it tight with the tock, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all, and Escape clears a selection or cancels a band in flight (with nothing selected it is left for the page).
- A plain band replaces the selection, Shift adds to it and Cmd or Ctrl toggles against it; a click selects one tile, Shift+click a block from the anchor, Cmd/Ctrl+click toggles one. On touch there are no modifiers, so a tap toggles a tile and a band adds.
- Under reduced motion the band still draws under the pointer and fades on release instead of tightening, tiles do not squeeze and the badge moves without gliding; every tile still lights and every sound still plays.
- The grid takes touch-action: none so a band can be drawn with a finger; keep it a modest block on long mobile pages.

### Brush Select (KQ-1137) — `brush-select`
Paint across to pick many.

Filter chips you select by painting: a click toggles one chip, but press on a chip and drag and the press becomes a brush — the first chip flips, and every chip the stroke passes takes its new state (or flips, in toggle mode), once per stroke. The paint wipes across each chip from the side the brush came in on an enter tween, each chip dips under the bristles on an impulse given to the snap spring, and its check draws on the flick; the stroke reports once, on release. Space toggles the focused chip, Shift+Arrow carries its state onto the next chip with the same wipe and tick, and Shift+Home/End or Cmd/Ctrl+A paint a whole run on one staggered beat.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/brush-select`

Props:
- `items`: BrushSelectItem[] — The chips, in order: id and label.
- `label`: string — The chip set's accessible name.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The selected ids, controlled or uncontrolled. During a stroke the chips show its draft; a controlled set then shows the host's answer.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string[]) => void — Fires once on the release of a stroke, on a tap and on each key, with the new selection in item order.
- `mode`: "set" | "toggle" (default "set") — Paint the first chip's new state onto every chip the stroke passes, or flip each one.
- `layout`: "wrap" | "grid" (default "wrap") — Pills of their natural width in wrapping rows, or equal rounded cells in a grid.
- `check`: boolean (default true) — A round indicator on every chip that fills and draws a check when the chip turns on. Off, colour alone carries the state.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick per chip the brush passes, climbing a pentatonic scale through the stroke (falling when the paint takes chips off). Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the chips and blocks taps, strokes and keys that change them; arrow keys still move focus.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- It is a multi-select listbox of options with roving focus: Left/Right move along the chips, Up/Down to the nearest chip in the row above or below, Home/End to the ends. Space or Enter toggles the focused chip; Shift+Arrow then carries its state onto each chip it moves to (or flips it, in toggle mode) with the next tick of the scale, Shift+Home/End paints to the end, and Cmd/Ctrl+A paints every chip on, or off when all are on.
- A stroke is sampled every few pixels along its path, so a quick flick across a row still paints every chip it crosses; Escape during a stroke takes it back.
- Under reduced motion the on face cross-fades instead of wiping, the check appears whole and nothing dips; the painting, the ticks and the result are unchanged.
- The chip set takes touch-action: none so a finger can paint across it; keep it to a modest block on long mobile pages.

### Zone Map (KQ-1138) — `zone-map`
Tap the regions you cover.

A stylised map of invented regions, drawn procedurally and identically on server and browser, with a list beside it that keeps the selection in words. Hover or keyboard focus lifts a region above a flat shadow on the snap spring; a click selects it with a fill that floods out from the click point to the coast on an enter tween timed to its reach and an outline that draws both ways round from the nearest vertex, and a second click drains it back into the point you tapped, while list rows arrive and make room on the glide spring. Arrow keys move to the nearest region in that direction, Home and End to the first and last, and Space or Enter toggles with the same flood, from the region's centre, and the same tock.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/zone-map`

Props:
- `label`: string — The map's accessible name.
- `names`: string[] (default nine invented names) — Region names in map order, top-left first. They are also the ids in value; regions beyond the list are called Region 8, Region 9 and so on.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The selected region names in the order they were picked, controlled or uncontrolled. Names not on the current map are ignored.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string[]) => void — Fires from the click, key or remove button that changed the selection, with the new list.
- `regions`: number (default 7) — How many regions the island is cut into. The same count and seed always draw the same map.
- `lift`: number (default 4) — How far hover and keyboard focus lift a region, in map units (the map is 200 wide). 0 leaves only the tint.
- `flood`: boolean (default true) — The fill floods out from the click point with a swish; off, it fades in whole and silently.
- `palette`: "tide" | "ember" | "moss" | "ink" (default "tide") — The two theme colours every selected region's shade is mixed from: accent and signal, warn and danger, success and warn, or ink and ink-3.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Another map for the same count.
- `listLabel`: string (default "Covered") — The heading over the list beside the map, and the list's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tock on every select (lower and softer on a deselect) and a swish riding the flood. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the map, stops the lift and blocks changes from clicks, keys and the remove buttons.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The map is a multi-select listbox of regions with roving focus: arrow keys move to the nearest region in that direction, Home and End to the first and last, and Space or Enter adds or removes the focused one. The keyboard-focused region lifts like a hovered one and is ringed along its own edge. Each list row has a Remove button named for its region; removing a row moves focus to the row that takes its place.
- Every coordinate is built with arithmetic alone from constant directions and a seeded integer generator, never trigonometry, so the server's markup and the browser's first render match to the last digit.
- Under reduced motion nothing lifts, floods or draws: the raised region is tinted, the fill and outline fade in whole and list rows cross-fade; the selection, the list and every sound are unchanged.
- The component is a row — the map and a 120px list that scrolls inside the map's height — so give it at least about 300px of width.

### Pattern Lock (KQ-1139) — `pattern-lock`
Draw the path through the dots.

A pattern pad whose line's live end is 1:1 under the finger and snaps through every dot its path crosses, taking any free dot lying straight between two it joins; each caught dot pops on a flick up and a springs.snap back and plays the next note of a rising pentatonic phrase, so the pattern is also a melody. A refused pattern shakes and fades after the clear delay, and an accepted one locks with a ripple that runs along the path in the order it was drawn, with a chord. Arrow keys move between the dots, Space or a number key adds one, Backspace takes the last back, Enter finishes as a lift does and Escape clears.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pattern-lock`

Props:
- `label`: string — The pad's accessible name, e.g. "Unlock pattern".
- `value / defaultValue`: number[] (default []) — The pattern as dot numbers from 1 (reading order), in drawing order. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (pattern: number[]) => void — Fires from the catch that added a dot, the key that removed one, and the clear, with the whole pattern.
- `onComplete`: (pattern: number[]) => boolean | void | Promise<boolean | void> — Asked when a pattern of at least minLength dots is finished. Return true to accept it (ripple and chord), false to refuse it (shake and buzz), nothing to record it neutrally, or a promise of one of those while the pad waits.
- `minLength`: number (default 4) — Shorter patterns are refused before onComplete is asked.
- `grid`: 3 | 4 | "3" | "4" (default "3") — Dots per side: a 3 × 3 or a 4 × 4 pad. Changing it clears the pattern.
- `path`: boolean (default true) — Draw the line and keep caught dots lit. Off is the private mode: each catch only flashes and pops, the melody is the only trail, and success ripples from the centre so nothing of the pattern shows.
- `line`: number (default 4) — The line's weight in px, 2 to 10.
- `clearDelay`: number (default 800) — How long a wrong, short or recorded pattern stays on the pad before it fades, in ms.
- `size`: number (default 216) — The pad's side in px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a rising note for each dot, a chord when accepted and a buzz when refused. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the pad and blocks drawing and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the pad's classes.

Notes:
- Every dot is a real button with roving focus: Arrow keys move between dots, Home and End jump, Space adds the focused dot and number keys 1 to 9 add a dot by number (with the same skip rule, pop and note), Backspace removes the last dot, Enter finishes exactly as lifting the finger does, and Escape clears (it is left for the page when the pad is empty). Keyboard additions and every verdict are announced in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion the line still follows the finger, but no dot pops, nothing shakes and no ring travels: a refused pattern turns danger and fades, an accepted one turns success with its rings filled in place; notes, chord, buzz and verdicts are unchanged.
- onComplete may be async: the pad holds the pattern (aria-busy) until the promise settles, and a new press before then wins. With nothing returned the pattern is recorded and fades after clearDelay, which is the first step of setting a new pattern.

### Stroke Command (KQ-1140) — `stroke-command`
Draw a shape; it runs the command.

A gesture pad that runs a command when you draw its shape: a small unistroke matcher resamples the stroke, turns it to its indicative angle, scales it into a square and searches the leftover rotation against a check, a circle, an arrow and a zigzag. A match morphs the stroke you drew, point for point, into the clean shape laid over it on springs.glide, and the command's label lands on springs.recoil with its own chime; a stroke that is no shape shrugs and fades. The command chips are a real toolbar: Arrow keys move along it, and Enter or Space makes the pad draw that shape itself, through the same matcher, morph and sound.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/stroke-command`

Props:
- `commands`: { shape: StrokeShape; label: string }[] — The commands in chip order, each bound to "check", "circle", "arrow" or "zigzag". Only these shapes are recognised; a shape bound twice keeps its first command.
- `onCommand`: (run: { shape, label, score, via }) => void — Fires from the release (or the chip) that ran a command, with the match score from 0 to 1 and how it was run: "stroke", "keyboard" or "pointer".
- `onMiss`: (best: { shape, score } | null, threshold: number) => void — Fires when a stroke matched no command, with the nearest upright shape (or null for a line or a scribble too short to judge) and the score it needed.
- `label`: string — The accessible name of the whole control; the toolbar is named after it.
- `tolerance`: number (default 0.5) — How forgiving the matcher is, 0 (strict: a score of 0.92 needed) to 1 (loose: 0.74).
- `trail`: boolean (default true) — Show the ink while drawing. Off, only the pen tip moves, and the stroke appears as it is judged.
- `width`: number (default 4) — The ink's weight in px, 2 to 10.
- `templates`: "ghost" | "off" (default "ghost") — ghost fits the leading template faintly under the stroke while you draw, solid once it would match, and warms its chip; off shows nothing until release.
- `height`: number (default 176) — The pad's height in px; it fills the available width.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pencil scratch that follows the pen's speed, a chime for a match (a different step of one chord per command) and a shrug for a miss. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the pad and the chips and blocks drawing and commands.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The chips are a role="toolbar" with one tab stop: Arrow keys (and Home and End) move between commands, and Enter or Space makes the pad trace that shape and run it through the same matcher, morph, chime and onCommand. The pad itself is a pointer surface hidden from assistive technology; results are announced in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion drawing still follows the pen, but nothing is traced, morphed or shrugged: the clean shape and the label cross-fade in, an unmatched stroke simply fades, and every sound, callback and announcement is the same.
- Check, arrow and zigzag are recognised only upright (within 50°); circles in either direction and zigzags from either end both count. A straight stroke or one shorter than 24px is never a command.

### Guess Line (KQ-1141) — `guess-line`
Draw what you think; then see.

A line chart whose latest stretch is hidden: the reader draws what they think comes next across the shaded band, the pen steadied by the smoothing and the drawn line bending through it 1:1 between points, and letting go with every point guessed reveals the truth. The real line continues from the anchor under a clip whose edge sweeps across the band, the gap between guess and truth shades as it passes, a hum follows the real value under the sweep, and on landing the score rolls up on springs.recoil. Every hidden point is also a slider: Up and Down set it, Left and Right move between points carrying the guess on, Enter reveals and Escape clears.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/guess-line`

Props:
- `series`: Record<string, GuessLineSeries> — The charts on offer, by key. Each is { title, caption?, unit?, decimals?, hide?, step?, points: { label, value }[] }; hide is how many of the latest points are hidden (a third by default).
- `dataset`: string — Which of series is shown; the first key by default. Switching clears the guess.
- `value / defaultValue`: (number | null)[] (default []) — The guess, one value per hidden point, oldest first, null where nothing is drawn yet. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (guess: (number | null)[]) => void — Fires from the move, tap or key that changed the guess (while drawing, once a point moves by half a step), and from the reset.
- `onReveal`: (result: { score, guess, truth }) => void — Fires when the real line has finished drawing in, with the score from 0 to 100 and both sets of values.
- `smoothing`: number (default 0.5) — 0 to 1: how much the pen is steadied and the guess rounded into a curve. 0 is a raw pen and a straight polyline.
- `reveal`: number (default 1200) — How long the real line takes to sweep in, in ms.
- `score`: boolean (default true) — Show and announce the score. Off, the gap still shades, without a number.
- `height`: number (default 160) — The plot's height in px; the chart fills the available width.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pencil scratch that follows the pen, a tick per keyboard step, and the reveal: a swish and then a hum whose pitch follows the real line under the sweep. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the chart and blocks drawing and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- Each hidden point is a role="slider" on the plot with one tab stop for the set: Up and Down change the guess by one step (Page Up and Page Down by five), Left and Right move between points and moving right onto an empty point carries the guess on, Home and End jump, Enter reveals the real line with the same sweep and sound, and Escape clears the guess. Values read as "52k", "not guessed yet", or after the reveal "guessed 52k, actual 61k"; the reveal and the score are announced in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion the pen still draws, but the real line and the shaded gap fade in rather than sweep, the score appears without rolling, and the hum that follows the sweep is left out; the swish, the guess, the score and every callback are unchanged.
- The plot is one SVG stretched to the width with non-scaling strokes, so it reads the same at 320px and 720px; the reveal is a clip rectangle, never a dash offset. A new press on the plot, the Guess again button or Escape starts over.

### Loop Lift (KQ-1142) — `loop-lift`
Circle it to lift it out.

Draw a loop around part of a picture and the loop closes and smooths on one glide spring — the gap between the pen's end and its start grows shut while the wobble relaxes through a Fourier low-pass — then exactly that part lifts out: a copy of the picture clipped by the loop rises on the snap spring with a geometric glow, a shadow and a caption naming what it caught, while the rest dims. Escape, a tap or a new loop drops it back on glide. The things in the picture are a listbox: the arrow keys walk them, and Enter draws the loop around the chosen one with the same marker squeak, close and lift.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/loop-lift`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The picture. It is drawn twice: once as itself, and once as the lifted copy, which is aria-hidden and inert.
- `label`: string — The accessible name of the list of things in the picture.
- `regions`: { id: string; label: string; x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }[] — The things in the picture, as fractions (0 to 1) of its box: what a loop can catch, what the caption names and what the keyboard walks.
- `value / defaultValue`: { points: [number, number][]; regions: string[]; area: number } | null (default null) — The lifted selection: the closed, smoothed loop as fractions of the picture, the ids of the regions it encloses, and the enclosed share of the picture. null when nothing is lifted.
- `onValueChange`: (value: LoopLiftValue | null) => void — Fires from the loop, tap or key that changed the selection. Controlled, the piece lifts when the value comes back; a refused selection's outline fades.
- `smoothing`: number (default 0.5) — How much the loop relaxes when it closes, 0 to 1: the harmonics kept run from 14 (every wobble of the hand survives) down to 1 (an ellipse).
- `lift`: number (default 12) — How high the lifted piece rises, in px, 0 to 24: its offset, its scale and how far its shadow falls. 0 is a flat highlight.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — Strength and reach of the halo around the lifted piece, 0 to 1, drawn as layered strokes of the loop rather than a blur.
- `dim`: number (default 0.5) — How dark the rest of the picture goes while a piece is lifted, 0 to 0.8.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the marker's squeak (following the pen's speed), the tick as the loop closes, the lift's shimmer (higher for a smaller piece) and the drop. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Blocks drawing and takes the things in the picture out of the tab order.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the frame's classes.

Notes:
- The regions are a listbox with roving focus: the arrow keys and Home and End move between them, each one's focus ring outlines it, Enter or Space draws the loop around it (the same close, lift and sounds as a drawn loop) or drops it if it is already lifted, and Escape drops whatever is lifted — Escape is only claimed when there is something to drop.
- Under reduced motion the stroke still follows the pen, the loop snaps to its smoothed shape without the morph, and the piece is picked out by outline, glow and dim alone, with no rise, scale or shadow; the caption and the announcement are unchanged.
- Because the picture is rendered twice, avoid ids inside it (an SVG gradient with an id would be duplicated); the lifted copy is clipped with a polygon, so any picture that lays out the same at the same width works.
- A polite status line speaks what was lifted and how much of the picture it is, and when it is dropped.

### Measure Line (KQ-1143) — `measure-line`
Drag across; it reads the distance.

A plan you measure by dragging: the finger draws a dimension line with end bars, a ruler of ticks and a live length label in real units that stays upright at any angle, hopping over the line on the snap spring when it swings through vertical. The end follows 1:1, catches corners and the ends of other lines, rubber-bands past the sheet and springs back on snap with the release velocity, and every tick the length crosses ratchets. The keyboard walks a cursor corner to corner, Enter anchors a line, the arrows carry its end on the flick spring with the same ratchet, and after any line the arrows adjust its last point.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/measure-line`

Props:
- `width`: number — The sheet's width in drawing units (millimetres on paper, say). Lines and corners are in these units.
- `height`: number — The sheet's height in drawing units.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The plan: SVG elements in drawing units, drawn over a scale grid and under the lines.
- `corners`: [number, number][] (default []) — Points the ends snap to — wall corners, door jambs — in drawing units. The ends of lines already drawn are snap points too.
- `label`: string — The plan's accessible name.
- `value / defaultValue`: { id: string; a: [number, number]; b: [number, number] }[] (default []) — The lines, each from a to b in drawing units.
- `onValueChange`: (lines: MeasureLineSegment[]) => void — Fires from the drag, key or tap that changed the lines. Controlled, a refused change puts the live end back where the host says it is.
- `units`: "m" | "cm" | "ft" (default "m") — How lengths read ("3.42 m", "342 cm", "11′ 3″"), and the spacing of the ticks and the grid.
- `snap`: boolean (default true) — Ends catch corners and the ends of other lines within 14px, with a catch ring and a snap; the keyboard cursor jumps corner to corner.
- `scale`: number (default 50) — The drawing's scale, 1:n: one drawing unit is n real ones. The same line reads longer at 1:100, and ticks and grid re-space.
- `keep`: boolean (default true) — Keep every line (six at most, the oldest goes first), or let each new line replace the last.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the ratchet (a detent per tick crossed, rising with the length, louder on long ticks) and the snap as an end catches. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Blocks drawing and removing, and takes the plan out of the tab order.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the wrapper's classes.

Notes:
- The plan is a focusable application: the arrow keys walk a cursor between corners (or one tick at a time, Shift for a long tick), Enter anchors a line and the arrows carry its end, Enter finishes and the next Enter starts from there; after any line, drawn or typed, the arrows adjust its last point. Escape stops adjusting or discards an empty line and is only claimed then; Backspace removes the newest line. A tap on a kept line's label removes that line.
- Under reduced motion drawing stays 1:1, and the label's hop, the snap ring's pop, the spring back from past the edge and keyboard moves become jumps; the ratchet and snap sounds and every number are unchanged.
- A polite status line speaks each line's length as it is drawn or adjusted and each removal, and the lines are also listed for assistive technology outside the drawing surface.
- formatMeasure(mm, units) and measureLength(line, scale) are exported so a host can print totals in the same format.

### Scratch Card (KQ-1144) — `scratch-card`
Scratch it; see what's under.

A reward under scratch-off foil: the pointer scrapes the foil away with a ragged brush while flakes of the foil that actually came off tumble and fall, and the scrape's sound follows the brush's speed. Once enough is cleared a glint crosses the card, the rest of the foil crumbles behind its front, and the reward settles on the recoil spring with a chime. The foil is a canvas that reads its colours from its own computed style and repaints when the theme changes; before the reveal it is a real button, and Enter or Space sweeps the same brush across the card with the same sound.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/scratch-card`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The reward under the foil. It is inert and hidden from assistive technology until revealed, so it cannot be read or tabbed to through the foil.
- `label`: string — What is under the foil, e.g. "Weekly reward". The foil button is named "Scratch to reveal: {label}" and the revealed reward is a group with this name.
- `revealed / defaultRevealed`: boolean (default false) — Whether the foil is gone. Setting it back to false lays fresh foil over the reward before the next frame is painted.
- `onRevealedChange`: (revealed: boolean) => void — Fires with true from the scratch or sweep that cleared enough foil. Controlled, the foil dissolves when the host answers.
- `onProgress`: (cleared: number) => void — The share of foil cleared, 0 to 1 (two decimals), each time it moves by a whole percent.
- `brush`: number (default 18) — Brush radius in px, 10 to 34: a wider brush clears more per stroke and throws more flakes.
- `autoReveal`: number (default 60) — The percentage cleared, 40 to 80, at which the rest of the foil dissolves by itself.
- `flakes`: boolean (default true) — Flakes of the foil that comes off tumble and fall out of the card. The frame loop runs only while flakes are falling, on screen, in a visible page.
- `foil`: "silver" | "gold" (default "silver") — The foil's colours, mixed from the theme's ink or warning hue, and the chime's pitch (gold rings a fourth higher).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the scrape (noise whose pitch and level follow the brush's speed), a paper crinkle for a single dab, and the reveal's chime and shimmer. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the foil button: nothing scratches.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the card's classes.

Notes:
- Before the reveal the foil is a native button: Space or Enter, or a click from assistive technology, sweeps the brush across the card in rows with the same scrape, flakes and reveal. Once revealed the button leaves, the reward becomes reachable, focus that was on the foil moves to the reward, and a polite status line says it was revealed.
- Under reduced motion scratching still works, but there are no flakes, no glint and no settle: at the threshold the rest of the foil fades on a short tween, the keyboard reveals at once, and the chime still plays.
- The foil paints on a canvas at the device pixel ratio capped at 2, with its colours read from the canvas's own computed style, so it follows a light or dark stage; the scratches are replayed after a resize or a theme change, and coverage is counted on a coarse grid rather than by reading pixels back.
- The card clips to its rounded box; give the reward its own size (an aspect ratio or a height), since the foil covers exactly what the children lay out.

### Jog Shuttle (KQ-1145) — `jog-shuttle`
Turn to step; twist the ring to fly.

An edit deck's transport control: a jog wheel that turns 1:1 under the finger and steps the playhead one frame per detent, inside a spring-loaded shuttle ring whose twist sets a speed that doubles zone by zone up to shuttleMax. Let go spinning, the wheel is a flywheel: its landing is projected from the release spin, snapped to a detent and reached on a critically damped spring with the same time constant, so it slows exponentially and stops on a detent, stepping and ticking as it goes; let go of the ring and the playhead stops while the ring swings home on the return spring with the release's spin. Arrows jog a frame (Shift ten, PageUp and PageDown a second) by turning the wheel through the same detents, and J, K and L shuttle reverse, stop and forward, faster each press, with the ring twisting and holding to show it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/jog-shuttle`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default min) — The playhead, in frames. Controlled or uncontrolled; a frame the host refuses is not where the next step starts.
- `onValueChange`: (frame: number) => void — Fires from the jog detent, the shuttle frame or the key that moved the playhead.
- `onSpeedChange`: (speed: number) => void — Fires when the shuttle speed changes, from the twist or key that changed it: signed (negative in reverse), 0 when stopped.
- `min`: number (default 0) — The first frame.
- `max`: number (default 1439) — The last frame.
- `fps`: number (default 24) — Frames per second: the timecode, how far PageUp and PageDown jump, and the shuttle's rate (a 4× shuttle runs 4 × fps frames a second).
- `label`: string — What is being scrubbed: the control's accessible name, shown over the timecode.
- `detents`: number (default 24) — Detents per revolution of the jog wheel, 12 to 48. One detent is one frame, so fewer detents are further apart under the finger.
- `inertia`: number (default 0.5) — How far the jog wheel coasts when let go spinning, 0 to 1: at 0 it stops dead in the nearest detent, at 1 it runs on like a heavy flywheel.
- `shuttleMax`: number (default 16) — The shuttle's top speed. The ring's travel is split into zones that double from 1× up to it (16 gives 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16×), marked on the collar.
- `spring`: number (default 0.5) — The ring's return spring, 0 to 1: soft swings past centre and back, firm goes straight home. Key twists move the ring on the same spring.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A detent tick per frame jogged (a clack at either end), a click as the ring enters each zone, and a whir while shuttling whose pitch rises with the speed. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the control, stops any shuttle, takes both parts out of the tab order and ignores drags and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The root is a group named by the label holding two sliders. Jog: ArrowRight/ArrowUp a frame forward, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown back, Shift for ten, PageUp/PageDown a second, Home and End to the first and last frame, its value text a sentence ("1 minute 12 seconds and 5 frames, frame 1733"). Shuttle: arrows one zone toward forward or reverse, Home and End to full reverse and full forward. On both, L shuttles forward and J in reverse (again: faster), K stops and Space toggles, with the ring twisting and holding at that zone.
- Under reduced motion the wheel and ring still follow the finger 1:1, but a released wheel settles in its detent at once with no coast, key jogs jump the wheel in one step, and the ring snaps home; the playhead still shuttles and the readout, collar arc and sounds still answer.
- The shuttle's frame loop exists only while the speed is not zero, stops when the page is hidden, and stops at either end of the clip. Turning the jog wheel cancels a shuttle first. Both parts are touch-none, since a rotary drag is two-dimensional.

### Thumb Wheel (KQ-1146) — `thumb-wheel`
Roll the edge to set it.

A value set by rolling a knurled wheel seen edge-on in a slot: the knurl scrolls 1:1 under the finger, its ridges bunching toward the top and bottom as the cylinder turns away, while the value sits beside it level with a fixed notch and a gauge shows where the wheel is between its stops. Rolled past a stop it rubber-bands; flicked, its landing is projected at a rate set by friction, snapped to a step when detents are on, and reached on a critically damped spring with that time constant, so it slows exponentially and stops on the step, while a throw past a stop hits it on the snap spring. Arrows step, PageUp and PageDown move ten steps and Home and End go to the stops, rolling the wheel there through the same fine ratchet; the scroll wheel rolls it as it would scroll content.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/thumb-wheel`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default min) — The value the wheel is set to. Controlled or uncontrolled; a value the host refuses rolls back.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the roll, flick, scroll, tap or key that changed it: per step while rolling, and once with the value it lands on.
- `min`: number (default 0) — The bottom stop.
- `max`: number (default 100) — The top stop.
- `step`: number (default 1) — One detent's worth of value, and what a key or a tap moves it by.
- `label`: string — What the wheel sets: the slider's accessible name, shown over the value.
- `unit`: string — Printed after the value and read in its value text, as in "%" or "dB".
- `knurl`: "fine" | "coarse" | "diamond" (default "fine") — The pattern cut in the wheel's edge: fine straight ridges, coarse ones twice as far apart, or a diamond crosshatch drawn as the two helices a real knurl leaves.
- `friction`: number (default 0.4) — How soon a flicked wheel stops, 0 to 1: at 0 it coasts a long way, at 1 it stops almost at once.
- `detents`: boolean (default true) — Click and settle on whole steps. Off, the wheel rolls freely and stops wherever it coasts, and the value shows one more decimal; keys and taps still land on whole steps.
- `range`: number (default 1.5) — How far the wheel turns from one stop to the other, in turns, 0.5 to 3: short is quick and coarse, long is slow and fine. The gauge shows one mark per quarter turn.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A fine ratchet tick per step as the wheel rolls (per ridge, softer, with detents off), rising with the value, and a clack when it meets a stop. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the wheel, takes it out of the tab order and ignores drags, scrolls and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The housing is a vertical role="slider" named by its label, with the value and unit in aria-valuetext ("60%"): ArrowUp/ArrowRight one step up, ArrowDown/ArrowLeft one down, PageUp/PageDown ten steps, Home and End to the stops. The wheel rolls there and ratchets past every step, as a drag would. A tap above the notch steps up, below it steps down.
- Under reduced motion the wheel still follows the finger 1:1, but every settle, flick, scroll and key jumps straight to its value with no coast or spring, while the reading, the gauge and the ratchet still answer.
- The scroll wheel is claimed only while the wheel can still move that way, so a scroll that reaches a stop carries on to the page. The drag is touch-pan-x, so a horizontal swipe over the wheel still pans. The reading reserves the width of its widest value, so rolling from 99 to 100 never moves the layout.

### Rotary Dial (KQ-1147) — `rotary-dial`
Drag to the stop; it winds back.

A number input drawn as a telephone rotary dial: put a finger in a hole and drag it clockwise to the finger stop, and the wheel turns 1:1 with the pointer, ratcheting as it winds and giving only a few degrees at rest and at the stop. Let go at the stop and it winds back at the constant speed a governor holds, a linear run at returnSpeed pulses a second rather than a spring, ticking once per pulse while the next slot counts them up; it knocks against its rest stop on a stiff, loose spring and the digit lands with a flick. The holes are real buttons in one tab stop: arrows move round the dial, Enter or Space dials the focused hole, number keys dial directly (queued while it is busy), Backspace removes a digit and Escape clears.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/rotary-dial`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The number dialled so far, digits only; anything longer than digits is cut. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires with the whole number when a digit lands, on Backspace and on clear.
- `onComplete`: (value: string) => void — Fires when the digit that fills the last slot lands.
- `label`: string — What is being dialled: the dial's accessible name.
- `returnSpeed`: number (default 10) — How fast the wheel winds back, in pulses per second (30° each), 6 to 20: the pace of the pulse ticks and of the counting slot.
- `finish`: "bakelite" | "chrome" (default "bakelite") — A glossy black wheel over a cream plate with black digits, or a spun-metal wheel over a black plate with white digits. Physical colours mixed from black, white and the theme's ink, so the dial reads the same on a light or dark page.
- `digits`: number (default 7) — How many digits the number has, 3 to 10: the slot count. When every slot is full the holes stop engaging and number keys are ignored.
- `display`: boolean (default true) — Show the number above the dial in slots, with a clear button and a polite live region. Off, only the dial renders and the host shows and announces the number.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A ratchet tick every 10° as the wheel winds, rising as it goes, a clack at the finger stop, a tick per pulse on the way back and a knock when it comes to rest. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the dial, disables its holes and the clear button, and ignores drags and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The dial is a group named by its label; its ten holes are buttons named by their digit in one tab stop. ArrowRight/ArrowDown move to the next hole round the dial, ArrowLeft/ArrowUp back, Home to 1 and End to 0; Enter or Space dials the focused hole and number keys dial directly, with the same wind, pulses and sounds as a finger. Backspace removes the last digit, Escape clears the number (and is left alone when there is nothing to clear).
- Under reduced motion a finger still turns the wheel 1:1, but a released, tapped or typed wheel is shown at rest at once while the governed return runs unseen, so the pulses still tick, the slot still counts up and the digit lands on the same beat.
- Releasing short of the stop winds the wheel back silently and dials nothing. Digits typed while the wheel is busy queue, up to the free slots, and dial in turn. The live region speaks the number the host accepted: "5 5 5 0, 4 of 7 digits."

### Straighten Dial (KQ-1148) — `straighten-dial`
Level the horizon.

A photo editor's straighten control: a degree ruler under the picture scrolls 1:1 under the finger and turns the picture about its centre, while a thirds grid fades in for as long as it turns and the crop scales, frame by frame from the same angle, just enough to keep the corners covered. Zero is magnetic: the ruler holds at exactly 0 inside the magnet and catches up at double rate beyond it, the ends rubber-band, and a flick coasts to its projected landing on a critically damped spring while a slow release stays put; rubber-banded releases and keys move on the glide spring. Arrows turn a degree (Shift a tenth), PageUp and PageDown five, Home and End to the ends, with the same ticks and the same snap at zero.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/straighten-dial`

- `children`: React.ReactNode — The picture to straighten. It fills the frame and turns inside it.
- `aspect`: number (default 2) — The frame's width over its height. The crop scale is worked out from it.
- `label`: string (default "Straighten") — The ruler's accessible name, shown left of the reading.

- `grid`: boolean (default true) — Fade a thirds grid over the picture while it turns, and away again once it stops.
- `magnet`: number (default 1.5) — How wide the sticky zone around zero is, 0 to 3 degrees, drawn on the ruler. Inside it the ruler holds at exactly 0; 0 makes zero an ordinary degree.
- `crop`: boolean (default true) — Scale the picture by the least amount that keeps the frame covered as it turns. Off, it turns at its own size and the empty corners show a checkerboard.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A fine tick as each degree passes the needle, pitched up the further it is from level, and a snap as zero does. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

ArrowRight/ArrowUp turn a degree clockwise, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown back, Shift+Arrow a tenth, PageUp/PageDown five, Home and End to the ends; keys chain from where the last one aimed and are caught by the magnet only on the way in, so they can always step back out. A Reset button turns back to level the same way.
- Under reduced motion the ruler and picture still follow the finger 1:1 and the crop still scales with the angle, but releases, keys and the reset land at once with no coast or spring; the grid still fades in and out.
- The ruler is touch-pan-y, so the page still scrolls vertically over it. The picture and the ruler strip are both clipped to the component's own box however far it turns.

### Vinyl Scrub (KQ-1149) — `vinyl-scrub`
Spin the record to scrub the track.

A turntable as a track's playhead: at 33⅓ the platter turns 200° a second and one second of the track is exactly that much groove, so while it plays the record spins and the time runs, and turned by hand the time follows the hand, backwards too, with a scratch whose pitch follows the hand's speed. A finger brakes the record under it as hard as grip says, a drag turns it 1:1 about the spindle, and a release keeps the hand's spin while the motor pulls it back to speed on a time constant set by inertia, with a whir; the tonearm's stylus is solved onto the groove for the time and glides to a new groove on the glide spring after a needle drop. An arrow key is a hand on the record, holding it and scrubbing a second of groove per press on the glide spring, and letting go on key-up.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/vinyl-scrub`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The playhead in seconds, in tenths. Controlled or uncontrolled; a time the host sets by itself is a needle drop.
- `onValueChange`: (seconds: number) => void — Fires from the play clock, the scrub or the key that moved the playhead, at tenth-of-a-second steps.
- `duration`: number — The track's length in seconds. The stylus runs from the outer groove at 0 to the inner one here.
- `playing / defaultPlaying`: boolean (default false) — Whether the motor is on. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onPlayingChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Fires from start/stop, Space or K, and when the track runs out.
- `onScrubChange`: (scrubbing: boolean) => void — True while a hand, or a held arrow key, is on the record; false when it lets go. Pause real audio output while it is true.
- `label`: string — What is on the deck. The control's accessible name.
- `rpm`: 33 | 45 | "33" | "45" (default "33") — Platter speed: 33⅓ turns 200° a second, 45 turns 270°. It sets how fast the record spins and how much of the track one turn scrubs, and is lit on the deck and printed on the label.
- `grip`: number (default 0.6) — How hard a finger stops a spinning record, 0 to 1: at 1 it stops dead under the hand, at 0 it slides about 50° before it stops.
- `inertia`: number (default 0.4) — How heavy the platter is, 0 to 1: how long it takes to come back to speed or to rest (60 ms to 900 ms), and so how far a flick carries.
- `tonearm`: boolean (default true) — Show the tonearm tracking the groove. Off, a thin ring around the platter fills with the position instead.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A scratch while a hand is on the record, pitched by its angular speed and silent when still, and a whir while the motor spins it up or down after a gesture. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the deck, takes it out of the tab order, lets go of any hand and ignores drags and keys.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the deck's classes.

Notes:
- The deck is a group named by the label. The record is a slider ("Position") whose value text reads "42 seconds of 3 minutes 24 seconds, stopped". ArrowRight/ArrowUp scrub a second forward and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown a second back (Shift five): the key holds the record, turns it on the glide spring with the same scratch, keeps scrubbing on repeat and lets go on key-up so the platter spins back up. PageUp and PageDown drop the needle ten seconds on or back, Home and End at either end, and Space or K start and stop; start/stop is also a real Play/Pause button.
- Under reduced motion the record does not spin while it plays, and a release or a key lands at once with no coast or spin-up; the time still counts, the tonearm still tracks it, and the sounds still answer.
- One frame loop drives the deck, and it runs only while the record is turning, held or playing, and only while the deck is on screen and the page is visible; coming back, the time catches up. Nothing sounds on mount, at the end-of-track stop, or when the host changes the state by itself.

### Angle Pick (KQ-1150) — `angle-pick`
Set a direction by turning it.

An angle input for a design tool: a dial whose handle sits under the finger as it turns, a field that takes typed degrees, and a live gradient, shadow or arrow that follows the handle through every spring. Pressed away from the handle, it swings there the short way on the snap spring; dragged, it catches up on the flick spring and then holds 1:1; with Shift it jumps between snap marks on flick like detents; a real spin coasts to its projected landing on a critically damped spring, ticking past the marks, while a slow release stays put. Arrows turn a degree, Shift+Arrow and PageUp/PageDown to the next mark, Home and End to the ends, and the field's own arrows do the same.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/angle-pick`

- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The angle in whole degrees, clockwise from the top: 0 to 359, or −90 to 90 at range 180. Controlled or uncontrolled; a value the host refuses is turned back to.
- `onValueChange`: (degrees: number) => void — Fires from the drag, tap, key, throw or typed entry that changed the angle.
- `label`: string (default "Angle") — What the angle sets: the group's and dial's name, shown over the preview (the field is "<label> in degrees").
- `snap`: number (default 15) — The Shift step and the PageUp/PageDown step in degrees, 5 to 45. The ring's marks and the ticks fall on it.
- `preview`: "gradient" | "shadow" | "arrow" (default "gradient") — What follows the dial: a gradient whose bright end is where the handle points, a card whose shadow falls that way, or an arrow over a small compass.
- `readout`: boolean (default true) — Show the live angle in the dial's hub, counting through every spring. Off, the hub is a small cap.
- `range`: 360 | 180 | "360" | "180" (default "360") — A full turn, 0 to 359 and wrapping, or a half turn, −90 to 90 with 0 at the top, that rubber-bands past either end.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick at every snap mark the handle passes, pitched up with the angle and a touch louder at 0°. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the control, takes the dial out of the tab order, disables the field and ignores drags.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The root is a group named by the label. The dial is a slider whose value text names the direction ("135 degrees, south-east"): ArrowRight/ArrowUp turn a degree clockwise, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown back, Shift+Arrow and PageUp/PageDown to the next snap mark that way, Home and End to the ends. The field commits on Enter or blur (360 wraps, 180 clamps) and turns the handle the short way; Escape restores it and is claimed so a surrounding dialog does not also close; its ArrowUp/ArrowDown step like the dial's.
- Under reduced motion the handle still follows the finger 1:1, but taps, keys, typed values and the spring back from the ends jump straight to the value with one tick, and nothing coasts; the preview and readout still follow.
- The dial is touch-none, since a rotary drag is two-dimensional, and captures the pointer only after 4px, so a tap is a tap.

### Paper Slip (KQ-1151) — `paper-slip`
Printed, torn off, read.

Notices print out of a till printer as slips of paper: a new slip's lane opens a print line at a time, pushing the older slips up while the housing chatters, and its loose end curls toward you before relaxing on the drift spring. Pull a slip down and its body strains against the perforation with rubber-band give while seeded fibres stretch and snap one by one; past the tear the last fibres spring apart on the recoil spring, the body flutters out on the exit ease and the older slips drop into its place on glide, while a short pull springs back on snap. Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/paper-slip`

- `label`: string (default "Notifications") — The list's accessible name, printed on the printer.

- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Slips can be read but not torn.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is 416px tall by default and a height class resizes it.

Notes:

Every stub carries a Tear button for assistive technology, and focus moves to the neighbouring slip at the tear.
- Reduced motion: a print fades the slip in at rest with no chatter, the curl is still, and a tear fades the body out instead of fluttering; the paper still follows a pulling finger, and every sound and announcement is unchanged.
- Controlled: onDismiss fires at the tear. Remove the notice and the slip finishes falling; keep it and the slip is printed back where it stood. New notices are announced politely (alerts assertively) once, and removals once the host has removed them.

A one-time-code field drawn as a pin-tumbler lock: each digit raises its spring-loaded pin stack on snap to a height set by the digit, the coil compressing above it, and a paste raises them left to right on a cascade. When check accepts the code every split glides onto the shear line and the plug turns a quarter on snap with a clunk, folding the key pins away; a refused code jiggles the pins on a tween and drops them on recoil so they bounce as they land. The cells are real inputs in one tab stop: digits type in and advance, Backspace and Delete remove, arrows and Home/End move, and paste or one-time-code autofill fills them all.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tumbler-code`

Props:
- `label`: string — What the code is for: the visible label and the name of the group of cells.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — Controlled or initial code: digits only, never longer than length.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires from the key, paste or refusal that changed the code, with the new digits.
- `length`: number (default 6) — How many digits, and so how many pins the cylinder has, 4 to 8.
- `brass`: "brass" | "nickel" | "black" (default "brass") — The metal of the housing, the plug and the face. The pins stay nickel over brass so the split always reads.
- `verify`: boolean (default true) — Check the code when its last digit lands and turn or refuse the lock. Needs check; off, the field only collects the code.
- `check`: (code: string) => boolean | Promise<boolean> — The host's verifier. A promise holds the plug in a test turn until it settles; a rejected one leaves the pins where they are.
- `onComplete`: (code: string) => void — Fires from the key or paste that filled the last cell, with the whole code.
- `onResult`: (accepted: boolean, code: string) => void — Fires once check has answered, before the lock turns or the pins drop.
- `name`: string — The form field name; a hidden input carries the code under it.
- `hint`: string — Helper text under the cells, wired to every cell with aria-describedby.
- `error`: string | null — What is wrong, from the host: shown under the cells, marked on them with aria-invalid, and announced once.
- `wrongText`: string (default "That code didn't turn the lock. Try again.") — What a refused code says.
- `required`: boolean (default false) — Marks every cell required, so a form will not submit with an empty one.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play each pin's click, the plug's clunk and the refusal's shrug. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on; sounds only ever answer the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the field and dims it.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:
- Each digit is a native input named "Digit n of N" inside a labelled group, with one tab stop on the next cell to fill: digits type straight in and advance, Backspace clears the digit before or under the caret, Delete clears in place, Left/Right move and Home/End jump, and a paste (or the platform's one-time-code autofill on the first cell) fills from the start.
- Under reduced motion the pins take their digit heights, alignment and rest at once with no springs, no jiggle and no sweep, and the plug's open state is a swap; the words under the cells and the polite status ("Checking the code.", "Code accepted. The lock is open.", the refusal) are unchanged.
- Controlled use reports every change from the key, paste or refusal that made it and then follows the host; a code the host sets itself moves the pins in silence and is not checked.

Every rule shoots a bolt.

### Swatch Mixer (KQ-1164) — `swatch-mixer`
Mix the colour you want.

A colour input you fill by mixing paint: a pigment dragged off its pot follows the pointer 1:1 and, let go over the well, sinks in with a ripple while the well lands on the recoil spring; a tap hops a blob in along a short arc. The colour is the parts-weighted average of the pigments in OKLab and it does not swap: the new pigment curls in as a streak, stir lines sweep round, and the paint travels from the old mix to the new one over a stir whose length is `swirl`, while the dish's rim, a ring of one segment per pigment, re-divides on the glide spring and a segment dragged out of the dish takes that pigment away. Each pot is a slider: Left and Right move between pigments, Up, Enter and Space add a part, Down takes one away, Delete or Home take the pigment out and End fills it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/swatch-mixer`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The colour in the well as `#rrggbb`, or an empty string for an empty well. Controlled or uncontrolled; a value the host sets is shown exactly, with the nearest recipe the palette can make on the rim.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires from the drop, key or press that changed the mix, with the new colour.
- `label`: string — The field's visible label and the accessible name of its group.
- `name`: string — Form field name; the colour rides a hidden input inside a surrounding form.
- `hint`: string — Guidance under the well, wired to the field with aria-describedby.
- `error`: string — An error from the host, shown under the well and announced once.
- `required`: boolean (default false) — Marks the field required; once the visitor empties the well it says so unless the host passes its own error.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Stops every drag, key and press, and dims the field.
- `pigments`: number (default 4) — How many pigment pots the palette offers, 3 to 6: the primaries, then white, black and a green.
- `swirl`: number (default 0.6) — How much the well swirls as a part mixes in, 0 to 1: at 0 the colour simply cross-fades, at 1 the stir lasts about 1.4 s and the streak makes more than a full turn.
- `readout`: "hex" | "oklch" (default "hex") — The format of the readout beside the label and of the recent mixes' names.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A plip as a part lands, pitched by the pigment's lightness, and a gloop as one is pulled out. Only ever in answer to the visitor.
- `className`: string — Classes for the field's root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the palette is one tab stop. Left and Right move between pigments; Up, Enter and Space add a part (the same hop and drop as a tap); Down takes one away; Delete, Backspace or Home take the pigment out, the same end state as dragging its rim segment out of the dish; End fills it to eight parts. Recent mixes are a toolbar reached with Tab, where Left, Right, Home and End move and Enter restores.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels, swirls or bounces. A dropped blob vanishes where it was let go, a tap adds the part without the hop, and there is no streak, stir or landing; the rim still re-divides and the paint still cross-fades to the new mix in oklab, because the mix is the value.
- The settled mix is announced once in a polite live region and kept in the recent strip after it has stood still for 700 ms; a value the palette cannot make exactly is kept as given, and the rim shows the closest recipe.

- `onReject`: (rejections: { name: string; reason: string }[]) => void — The files that bounced off a drop or pick, with the reason for each.

- `onValueChange`: (slug: string) => void — Fires from the keystroke, press or offer that changed the slug, including a title keystroke while it is linked.
