- `scatter`: number (default 0.6) — How far from home, and how turned, the tipped-out pieces lie, 0 (just above their slots) to 1 (anywhere in the tray, up to 28°).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a snap as a piece placed by hand is pulled in and a click as it locks. The automatic assembly is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The puzzle still assembles itself; pieces cannot be moved.
- `className`: string — Sizes the tray; the default is aspect-[4/3] w-full.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the loose pieces are one roving group — Left and Right move through them in reading order, Up and Down by row, Home and End jump — and Enter or Space places the focused piece, the same end state as dragging it home, with focus moving on to the next loose piece and to the picture after the last.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels or bounces — pieces fade in where they lie, each placement is an instant move into its slot, and the last piece waits there at half strength until ready; dragging still follows the pointer directly.
- The tray's rim is exactly the tabs' reach, so pieces lying about and their focus rings stay inside the box; the cut is clipped with objectBoundingBox clip paths, so it renders the same on the server and at any size.

### Etch Reveal (KQ-1210) — `etch-reveal`
Drawn with two knobs.

An image placeholder that is a drawing toy: while the picture loads, one continuous line traced from its own contours runs across a powder screen at a steady mechanical pace, the left knob turning with the stylus's x and the right with its y, and when the line is done and the picture is ready the powder fades into the picture on the enter ease. Turning either knob — dragged round its centre, or by arrow keys, since both are real sliders — draws by hand while the tracing waits, and a turned knob settles on springs.snap. Dragging the frame side to side shakes the toy, rubber-banded within its own padding and settling on springs.snap with the release velocity, and every stroke knocks powder back over the line until the screen is clear; the Shake plate does the same from the keyboard.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/etch-reveal`

Props:
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows. Always its accessible name: the picture's role="img" label, or the img's own alt for src.
- `src`: string — The picture's address. Without it, children is the picture.
- `children`: ReactNode — The finished picture when there is no src: an inline SVG or an image, sized to fill the box.
- `ready`: boolean — Controlled: the picture may show. Uncontrolled, it is ready once the picture exists (a src has loaded or failed) and the line has been drawn.
- `progress`: number — 0 to 1, while not ready: how far the effect may come, for a determinate load.
- `onReady`: () => void — Fires once per load, when the effect has resolved and the picture is whole.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the stylus draws by itself, 0.5 to 2.
- `frame`: "red" | "teal" | "ink" (default "red") — The toy's colour, a fixed pigment in either theme.
- `line`: number (default 2) — The stylus's line, 1 to 3 px.
- `ratio`: number (default 2) — The screen's width over its height.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the stylus scraping while the visitor turns a knob, and the powder rushing while they shake. Every loop stops on release, key up or blur; the automatic drawing is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The toy still draws and resolves; knobs and shaking are off.
- `className`: string — Sizes the toy; the default is w-full.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the knobs are sliders named Across and Up and down — arrow keys turn them a step (Shift for five), Page keys ten percent, Home and End run to the stops, and a held key draws a continuous line; the Shake plate is a button that shakes the screen clear, the same end state as dragging the frame side to side.
- Reduced motion: the traced line appears in six still steps with no running stylus, the knobs jump to their angles and the frame never moves; each reversal of a drag still fades the drawing, the Shake plate fades it at once, and the picture resolves with a short fade.
- The line is traced from the picture's own pixels (an inline SVG is read with its computed colours); before the picture shows, shaking clears the traced line too and the toy traces it again, and after it shows, shaking clears only what the visitor drew over it.

### Sun Arc (KQ-1211) — `sun-arc`
Where the day has got to.

A daylight widget: the sun rides a sine arch from first to last light over a horizon whose sky, ground, glow and stars take the hour's colours, with the daylight left read beside it. Press anywhere in the sky and the sun comes to the finger on the flick spring, follows it 1:1 along the arch and rubber-bands past dawn and dusk; a release projects the throw and the sun glides to the landing on the glide spring with the release velocity, ticking once per hour crossed. The rail under the panel lines up with the arch and is a real slider: arrow keys step the time, Page keys an hour, Home and End jump to first and last light, and Escape or the Now pill brings the sun back to the present.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sun-arc`

Props:
- `sunrise`: number — Sunrise, in minutes after local midnight (06:14 is 374).
- `sunset`: number — Sunset, in minutes after local midnight.
- `dawn`: number (default sunrise - 30) — First light, in minutes after midnight: where the arc's left tail ends.
- `dusk`: number (default sunset + 30) — Last light, in minutes after midnight: where the arc's right tail ends.
- `now`: Date | number — The live moment the sun follows while the value is null. Pass it, with timeZone, to render on the server; without it the widget keeps its own clock after hydration.
- `timeZone`: string — The IANA time zone now is read in, e.g. "UTC". Defaults to the runtime's own.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The time shown, in minutes after midnight; null follows now.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number | null) => void — Fires from the drag, tap, key or Now press that changed the time shown (null when it returns to now).
- `step`: number (default 5) — Minutes per arrow key, and the grid a scrub lands on.
- `clock`: "12" | "24" (default "24") — Print every time in 24-hour (06:14) or 12-hour (6:14 am) form.
- `sky`: boolean (default true) — Paint the sky, ground, horizon glow and stars with the hour. Off leaves a quiet panel on the card surface.
- `marks`: boolean (default true) — Show the dawn and dusk marks with their times, and a dot on the arc for every whole hour.
- `label`: string (default "Daylight") — The widget's name: the group's and the slider's accessible name, shown over the reading when there is room.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick once per whole hour the visitor scrubs past, pitched by the sun's height, and brighter at sunrise and sunset.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the day but takes no drag or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the widget's root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the rail is a slider from first to last light — Left/Right (and Down/Up) step `step` minutes, Page Up/Down an hour, Home and End jump to dawn and dusk, and Escape returns to now (handled only when scrubbed). The sky's drag mirrors it for pointers, and the Now pill is a real button.
- Reduced motion: the sun never glides — a throw lands where it was let go and keys jump — while the sky, the reading and the stars still change with the time, because they are the information. The drag itself stays 1:1.
- Pass now and timeZone for server rendering; sunrise, sunset, dawn and dusk are wall-clock minutes in that zone. While live, sunrise, sunset and last light are announced once each as the clock reaches them.

### Moon Phase (KQ-1212) — `moon-phase`
Tonight's moon, and the next.

A moon widget whose lit part is computed from the date — the elongation with its six largest periodic terms — and drawn as the bright limb closed by the terminator's half ellipse, with the phase's name, the share lit and the next full and new moon beside it. A drag across the moon moves through the nights with the terminator travelling under the finger (its own width is a week), and a release projects the throw and glides to the nearest whole night on the glide spring with the release velocity, ticking once per night; the Full and New rows glide the moon to their nights, and seen from the south the whole moon turns over on glide. The night tile is a slider: arrow keys step a night, Page keys a week, Home and End the reach, and Escape or the Tonight pill returns to tonight.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/moon-phase`

Props:
- `now`: Date | number — Tonight: the moment the scrub counts from. Pass it, with timeZone, to render on the server; without it the widget keeps its own clock after hydration.
- `timeZone`: string — The IANA time zone the dates are written in, e.g. "UTC". Defaults to the runtime's own.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The night shown, in whole days from now (0 is tonight).
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the drag, key or button that changed the night shown.
- `range`: number (default 60) — How far the scrub reaches each way, in days.
- `hemisphere`: "north" | "south" (default "north") — Which way up the moon is seen: south turns it over (the light on the other side, the seas upside down) and flips the drag so the shadow still follows the finger.
- `detail`: boolean (default true) — Draw the near side's seas, a few craters with rays and the limb's shading. Off: a flat, graphic moon.
- `glow`: number (default 0.5) — The halo's size and strength, 0 to 1; it also follows how much of the moon is lit.
- `label`: string (default "Moon") — The widget's accessible name; the slider is named after it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick once per night the visitor scrubs past, pitched by how much is lit, and distinctly at full and new.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the night but takes no drag, keys or buttons.
- `className`: string — Classes for the widget's root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the night tile is a slider — Left/Right (and Down/Up) step a night, Page Up/Down a week, Home and End go to the ends of range, and Escape returns to tonight (handled only when away). The Full moon, New moon and Tonight controls are buttons with full names.
- Reduced motion: nothing glides or turns over — a key, a throw, a row or the hemisphere swaps straight to its night or view — while the drag still moves the terminator under the finger and the share lit, the name and the dates still update.
- The module also exports moonOn(date), which returns the phase's name, the share lit and whether the moon is waxing, for text elsewhere in a product.

### Egg Timer (KQ-1213) — `egg-timer`
Twist to set, and it rings.

A mechanical kitchen timer, face on: drag round the dial and it turns 1:1 with the hand and ratchets, lingering on each minute's detent and clicking across to the next, rubber-bands past zero and the top of the scale, and lands on the nearest detent on the snap spring when let go, which starts it. While it runs the dial turns back to zero, stepping once a second on the flick spring as the escapement lever rocks on snap (or sweeping silently with ticking off), a red band shrinks toward the pointer, and at zero the shell rattles about its feet on a keyframed tween while the bell rings; a tap pauses and resumes. The dial is a slider in minutes: arrows add or take a minute, Page keys five, Home clears and End sets the whole scale, a held key holds the count like a hand on the dial, and Space or Enter pauses.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/egg-timer`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — Seconds left.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires with the seconds left: on each detent while setting, on each key step, and once a second while running (while on screen; it catches up on return).
- `running / defaultRunning`: boolean (default false) — Whether it is counting down.
- `onRunningChange`: (running: boolean) => void — Fires from the release, key, tap or ring that started or stopped it.
- `onRing`: () => void — Fires when the count reaches zero and the bell rings.
- `max`: number (default 60) — The scale in minutes, 15 to 60: the graduations, the numbers (every 5, or every 10 past 30) and the size of each ratchet step.
- `shell`: "pear" | "lemon" | "mint" (default "lemon") — The shell's colour, at a fixed lightness so it reads the same in either theme.
- `ticking`: boolean (default true) — Step once a second with the escapement rocking (and a quiet tick-tock, with sound); off, the dial sweeps back smoothly and silently.
- `label`: string (default "Timer") — What is being timed: shown over the reading and used in the dial's name ("Eggs timer").
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Detents while setting, a tick a second while running and the bell's chime — only once someone has set it (a visitor's turn, key, tap or button, or a host change after mount).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Keeps counting, but takes no drag, keys or button.
- `className`: string — Classes for the timer's root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the dial is a slider in whole minutes — Up/Right add a minute (to the next whole minute), Down/Left take one, Page Up/Down five, Home clears and End sets the whole scale; a held key holds the count and letting go starts it, as letting go of the dial does. Space or Enter pauses and resumes, and the Pause/Start button does the same.
- Reduced motion: nothing springs, rocks or rattles — the dial jumps to each detent and each second, and the ring is the marks flaring — while the drag still turns the dial under the hand, the band and the reading still count down, and the chime still plays.
- The count runs from a deadline, so it keeps real time behind a hidden page or off screen; its once-a-second steps and reports rest there and catch up on return, and the bell is its own timeout so onRing fires on time.

### Plant Care (KQ-1214) — `plant-care`
It droops when it's thirsty.

A plant-care widget whose plant shows how thirsty it is: as the days since watering pass, a fern's fronds flatten until their tips hang over the rim, a monstera's stalks bend and its split leaves hang, a cactus thins and lets its arms sag, the green drains toward straw and the soil dries and cracks, all rebuilt each frame from analytic curves. Pressing Water brings a can in over the pot and tips it on the snap spring, a seeded shower falls in real arcs and splashes while a wet patch spreads, and when the last drops land the leaves spring back up centre first on a staggered snap; a pointer brushed through the plant flicks the leaves it crosses, crisply when watered and loosely when thirsty. The Water button is the whole keyboard path, and the next watering day is named from `now`.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/plant-care`

Props:
- `days / defaultDays`: number (default 5) — Days since the plant was last watered: its thirst, and so its pose, its colour and the soil.
- `onDaysChange`: (days: number) => void — Fires from the Water press with 0.
- `plant`: "fern" | "monstera" | "cactus" (default "fern") — Which plant is drawn: arching fronds, split leaves on stalks, or a column with two arms that flowers when well watered. It also sets the default interval.
- `pot`: "clay" | "stone" | "glaze" (default "clay") — The pot's finish: terracotta, speckled stone, or a deep blue glaze over a bare clay foot.
- `name`: string (default "Fern", "Monstera" or "Cactus") — The plant's name: the widget's title and its accessible name.
- `interval`: number (default 4 / 7 / 10 by plant) — Days between waterings. Thirst is days over interval: droop starts at a third of it and is complete at 1.4 times it.
- `now`: number | Date — The current moment. With it the next watering day is named ("Next Sun 11 Oct"); without it, counted ("Next in 3 days").
- `utcOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC used to read `now` as a calendar day, so server and client agree.
- `waterLabel`: string (default "Water") — The button's text.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — After a Water press: the pour loop while water leaves the can, and a plip as the first, middle and last drops land, rising as the soil fills. Brushing and host changes are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The button is disabled, brushing does nothing, and a watering in progress finishes at once.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, a container up to max-w-xs.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Water is a real button — Enter or Space waters the plant through the same choreography as a press, and it is aria-disabled (focus stays) until the watering ends. Brushing the leaves is decoration and changes no state. A polite live region says "Sill fern watered. Next watering Sunday 11 October." or, when the host changes the days, how long since watering and when it is due.
- Reduced motion: no can travel, flying drops, sway or springs — the can fades in already tipped over a still shower, the soil darkens, the can fades out and the leaves swap to their new pose while the green returns; the pour and plips still answer the press.
- Controlled: onDaysChange(0) fires from the press; the leaves perk up to whatever days the host holds when the water lands, so a host that refuses the watering keeps its plant thirsty. Pass `now` (and `utcOffset`) for a named next day that renders the same on the server.

### Bin Day (KQ-1215) — `bin-day`
Which one goes out tonight.

A collection-day widget: two to four wheelie bins stand in a row by the house and the one due this collection has been rolled to the kerb, with its name, when it goes out and the bin after it in the header. - `onDayChange`: (day: BinDayWeekday) => void — Fires from the week strip with the chosen weekday.
- `done / defaultDone`: boolean (default false) — This collection's bin has been dealt with: it stands back in the row. Uncontrolled, it is kept for that collection's date only, so the next bin rolls out once the date passes.

- `bins`: number (default 3) — How many bins take turns, one per collection, 2 to 4: Rubbish, Recycling, Garden, Food.
- `colours`: "council" | "pastel" | "mono" (default "council") — Strong civic pigments, soft pastels, or greys told apart by the signs on their fronts. Fixed pigments, the same in either theme.
- `names`: string[] — Names for the bins, in rotation order.
- `offset`: number (default 0) — Shifts which bin a week starts the rotation on (weeks start on Monday).
- `utcOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC used to read `now` as a calendar day.
- `label`: string (default "Bin day") — The widget's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A thud when a bin the visitor sent lands at the kerb, a tick when it arrives back in the row, a lighter tick per day stepped on the strip. Host changes are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Done, the strip and the drag do nothing.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, a container up to max-w-xs.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Done and Undo are a real button ("Mark Recycling done", "Undo: Recycling back out") and reach the same end states as dragging the bin; the week strip is a radiogroup with roving focus, where arrows move and choose, and Home and End jump to the first and last day. A polite live region speaks a sentence frozen at each change, such as "Recycling done. Next: Garden, Thursday 15 October."
- Reduced motion: nothing tips, rolls, rocks or opens — a bin swaps between its row slot and the kerb at once and the pill swaps days, while the header, chip and tags still change; a drag still follows the finger and lands at once.
- The scene is a role="img" with a sentence of where every bin stands. Only the due bin is draggable (touch-pan-x, so a vertical drag on it never scrolls the page); a tap on it rattles its lid.

### Commute Line (KQ-1216) — `commute-line`
Where the train is now.

A transit widget: the line's pill and direction, a delay badge whose figure rolls on the snap spring, a line diagram of stops with the train on it, and the chosen stop's arrival time. The train's position comes from the timetable, `now` and the delay (or a live `position`), with a dwell at each stop and a cosine pull-away and braking between them; each report moves the shown train there — at the pace steady reports set, so it reads as one continuous glide, or on the drift spring with its own velocity for a first or irregular report — and a jump back to the start is a fade, never a reverse. A window of stops follows the train and the chosen stop on glide and can be dragged sideways; each stop the train reaches pulses; the stops are a radio group where a tap or the arrow keys choose one and an ETA flag hops there on snap.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/commute-line`

- `now`: number | Date — The current moment. Each new value is a report: the train moves to where the timetable and delay put it.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — How late the train is running, in minutes: the badge (on time, late, very late from 6), every ETA, and where the train is.
- `position`: number — A reported position from a live feed, as a fractional stop index (2.4 is 40% of the way from the third stop to the fourth). Overrides the timetable's.
- `stops`: number (default 6) — How many stops the diagram shows at once, 2 to 8. Labels drop to two rows when the spacing is too small for one.
- `line`: "red" | "green" | "blue" (default "blue") — The line's colour, a fixed pigment that reads in either theme, and its default name.
- `label`: string (default "Blue line") — The line's name: its pill and the widget's accessible name.
- `direction`: string — Where the train is heading, shown beside the pill, e.g. "to Harbour".
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the next stop ahead of the train) — The chosen stop's id: its ETA flag and the footer.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from a tap or a key that chose a stop.
- `utcOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC for the clock times shown, so the server and the page agree.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A chime when the visitor chooses a stop, higher the sooner the train gets there and low for a stop it has left. Reports and arrivals are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The train still moves; stops cannot be chosen and the line cannot be dragged.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, a container up to max-w-[40rem].

Notes:
- Keyboard: the stops are a radiogroup with roving focus — arrows choose the next or previous stop, Home and End the first and last, and the window slides to keep the choice in view, which is also the keyboard path for dragging the line. Each radio is named with its ETA ("Fieldline, in 10 minutes, 08:57"). A polite live region speaks a sentence frozen at each change that matters: a choice, a delay change, the train arriving at the chosen stop.
- Reduced motion: the train, the window and the flag jump to each report, the arrival pulse is a flash without growth, and the badge swaps; every time, fill and position still updates.
- The host owns the clock: pass a fixed `now` for the first render and advance it in an effect (and pause that while off screen), so the server and the page render the same train.

### Wind Sock (KQ-1219) — `wind-sock`
Which way, and how hard.

A wind widget: an airfield windsock on a mast in the middle of a compass rose painted on the grass, built from six hoops projected from 3D so it points the way the wind blows in depth as well as across, with its shadow falling downwind on the rose. It hangs at calm and fills toward level by fifteen knots on the glide spring, its five stripes light one by one with the Beaufort bands and turn red from a near gale, and while it is on screen it flaps with a ripple and a seeded wander that grow with gust. Dragging on the rose moves the wind marker 1:1 and the sock swings after it on a hunting vane spring; arrow keys turn the preview 5°, Page keys 45°, Home faces north, and Escape or Live returns to the real wind.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/wind-sock`

Props:
- `speed`: number — Wind speed in knots: how full the sock is, which stripes are lit, how fast it flaps and the reading.
- `direction`: number — The bearing the wind blows from, in degrees (270 is a westerly). The sock points the other way.
- `gust`: number (default 0.35) — How gusty it is, 0 to 1: how hard the sock wanders and swells, and the reading's steady, gusty or very gusty.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The previewed bearing the sock is shown in, or null for the live wind.
- `onValueChange`: (bearing: number | null) => void — Fires from the drag, tap, key or Live press that changed the preview.
- `label`: string (default "Wind") — The widget's name, used in the slider's name and the band announcements.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A whoosh as the visitor swings the sock (on a drag at most every 45° and 220 ms, a tap, a key, and the return to live), pitched up with the wind. The flapping itself is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Keeps showing the wind, but takes no drag, tap or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the tile.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the picture is a slider in degrees — Right/Up turn the preview 5° clockwise, Left/Down 5° anticlockwise, Page Up/Down 45°, Home faces north; Escape returns to the live wind and is handled (with preventDefault) only while previewing. The Live button does the same.
- Reduced motion: nothing flaps or hunts — the sock is drawn still and turns and fills on short tweens — while the stripes, the reading and the preview marker still change.
- The flap loop runs only while the sock is on screen, the page is visible and the wind is above calm; a change of Beaufort band is announced once in a polite live region.

### Parking Meter (KQ-1220) — `parking-meter`
Time left on the meter.

A parking meter widget: in the classic style a needle sweeps down a cream dial through the time left, in the digital style seven-segment digits and a ten-bar graph show it, and both read one motion value. Tapping the meter or its button drops a coin into the slot on an accelerating tween as it turns edge-on, it clacks as it lands, and the needle kicks up to the new time on the recoil spring, overshooting against its stop pin and ticking past each mark; a full meter bounces the coin back out. In the last minutes the window's rim pulses and the red flag peeks over the sill, popping up on recoil at expiry; the add button is the keyboard's way in, and the time left is announced at the thresholds and after every coin.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/parking-meter`

Props:
- `now`: Date | number — The moment it is. Pass it, with timeZone, to render on the server; without it the meter keeps its own clock after hydration.
- `timeZone`: string — The IANA time zone times are shown in, e.g. "UTC". Defaults to the runtime's own.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The moment the meter is paid until, in ms. Null or past is expired.
- `onValueChange`: (paidUntil: number) => void — Fires as each coin lands, with the new paid-until moment.
- `max`: number (default 120) — The longest stay, in minutes: the dial's scale and marks, and the cap a coin cannot pass.
- `coin`: number (default 20) — Minutes one coin buys: the slot plate, the button and how far the needle kicks.
- `style`: "classic" | "digital" (default "classic") — An enamel dome with a needle dial, or a charcoal digital head with an LCD of segment digits and bars.
- `warnAt`: number (default 10) — Minutes left at which the window starts to pulse, the flag to peek and the reading turns the warning colour.
- `label`: string (default "Parking") — What is parked, shown over the reading and used in its announcements.
- `onRefuse`: () => void — A coin refused because the meter is already at max.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — The coin's clack (a low one when refused) and a tick for each mark the needle passes on its kick, only after a visitor's tap or press. Time passing is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Keeps counting down, but takes no coins.
- `className`: string — Classes for the tile.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the Add button is a real button — Enter or Space drops one coin, exactly as a tap on the meter drawing does (the drawing is a pointer convenience and hidden from assistive technology). The time left is a meter (aria-valuetext "23 minutes left").
- Reduced motion: the coin fades in at the slot instead of falling, the needle and digits move on a short tween with no kick, the flag fades in rather than rising and the rim is a steady amber or red; the reading, the flag and the announcements are unchanged.
- A polite live region speaks warnAt minutes left, one minute left and expiry once each as time passes, and every coin ("Added 20 minutes. 32 minutes left, paid until 14:52.") or refusal.

### Tear Pass (KQ-1221) — `tear-pass`
Tear here to board.

A boarding pass whose stub tears off along a real perforation: dragging down the stub runs the tear 1:1 with the finger while the torn part peels out about the tear front, and the fibres in each bridge stretch across the gap and snap back as tufts that quiver on the recoil spring. A throw that would finish the tear completes it on the glide spring with the release velocity, the free stub lands a little out and turned on recoil and turns over on glide to show its boarding code, and gate and seat roll to new values in split-flap tiles. The stub is a real button: Enter or Space tears it from the top with the same fibres and sounds, and then turns it over and back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tear-pass`

Props:
- `carrier`: string — Who flies it, printed in the pass's header.
- `flight`: string — The flight number, e.g. "WL 214".
- `passenger`: string — The passenger's name.
- `from`: { code: string; city: string } — Where it leaves from: the code printed large and the city under it.
- `to`: { code: string; city: string } — Where it goes.
- `date`: string — The date as printed, e.g. "07 Oct".
- `boards`: string — The boarding time as printed, e.g. "08:15".
- `gate`: string — Printed in split-flap tiles; a new value rolls them and is announced once.
- `seat`: string — Printed in split-flap tiles; a new value rolls them and is announced once.
- `zone`: string — Boarding group, printed under the seat.
- `code`: string — The booking reference, drawn as a seeded two-dimensional code on the stub's back.
- `torn / defaultTorn`: boolean (default false) — Whether the stub has been torn off. A host that sets it false gets a whole pass back; one that sets it true gets the same tear, silently.
- `onTornChange`: (torn: boolean) => void — Fires from the drag or key that freed the stub, with true.
- `perforation`: "round" | "slot" (default "round") — Round punched holes or slots along the tear; slots break with a lower snap.
- `paper`: "white" | "sky" | "sand" (default "white") — The card stock and its inks, fixed pigments that read the same in either theme.
- `flip`: boolean (default true) — The torn stub turns over in 3D to show its code; off, it cross-fades flat.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A paper crinkle for each bridge that lets go, a snap when the stub comes free, and a soft paper turn — only for the visitor's own tear and presses.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the pass but takes no drag or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the stub is a button — Enter or Space tears it from the top on a timed sweep that reaches the same end state as the drag (same fibres, same sounds); once it is free the same button turns it to the code and back. A tap on a whole stub only tugs at the seam; it never tears.
- Reduced motion: nothing shears, flies or turns — the drag still runs a hairline down the seam with the finger, the free stub stands a few pixels apart at once, the code cross-fades in, and the flap tiles swap characters at once.
- The stub drags vertically, so it carries touch-pan-x; the pass is a container and steps its type down and its fields to two rows under 440px, about 292×160 in a phone card and 560×187 in a wide one.

### Mail Postcard (KQ-1222) — `mail-postcard`
Flip it, stamp it, send it.

A postcard that turns over on the glide spring with perspective — pressed, swiped 1:1 with the finger and projected on release, or from its Turn over button — and the first time its back comes round the message writes itself, a pen nib running the measured text quick inside words, lifting at spaces and pausing at punctuation. Send lands the postmark on the recoil spring with a thud while the card gives under the blow, then slides the card off into the post on the exit ease and leaves a Posted slip. Turn over and Send are real buttons and focus follows the card to the slip and back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mail-postcard`

Props:
- `message`: string — What is written on the back — a postcard's worth, about 160 characters.
- `to`: { name: string; lines: string[] } — The address: the name names the card, and up to two more ruled lines.
- `from`: string — Signed under the message.
- `place`: string — The town on the postmark.
- `date`: string — The date on the postmark and the Posted slip, e.g. "07 Oct 26".
- `picture`: ReactNode — The picture side: an image or an illustration that fills it.
- `caption`: string — Printed on the picture side, e.g. "Greetings from Coldbrook".
- `side / defaultSide`: "front" | "back" (default "front") — Which side faces up.
- `onSideChange`: (side: "front" | "back") => void — Fires from the swipe, press or button that turned the card.
- `sent / defaultSent`: boolean (default false) — Whether the card has been posted. Setting it back to false brings a fresh card in from the left.
- `onSentChange`: (sent: boolean) => void — Fires from the Send press, with true.
- `hand`: boolean (default true) — The message is handwritten and writes itself behind a pen nib; off, it is printed in the house sans at once.
- `stamp`: "round" | "wave" (default "round") — A circular date stamp with cancel bars, or a machine postmark's wavy lines.
- `paper`: "cream" | "white" | "kraft" (default "cream") — The card stock and its inks, fixed pigments that read the same in either theme.
- `sendLabel`: string (default "Send") — The Send button's text.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A paper turn, the postmark's thud and the posting's paper — only for the visitor's own presses and swipes.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the card but takes no swipe or presses.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Turn over and Send are real buttons (the card's own press and swipe mirror Turn over). While it posts they stay focusable but inert, and focus moves to the Posted slip when the card has gone, then back to Turn over when a card returns.
- Reduced motion: the sides cross-fade, the message is there whole with no pen, the postmark fades in at rest and the card fades out and back in — every state still changes.
- The handwriting is measured on an untransformed hidden copy with Range rects, so the 3D turn never skews it; the side not showing is aria-hidden, and the message is real text from the start.

### Wax Seal (KQ-1223) — `wax-seal`
Break the seal to read.

A letter folded into panels and closed with a wax seal. Holding the seal makes the wax give on the flick spring while seeded cracks spread from the exact point pressed, drawn to the length the hold has reached; let go early and they close, hold for the full time and it snaps along the flap's edge, chips fly, and each panel unfolds about its crease on the glide spring with perspective while the sheet glides to stay centred. Reseal folds it back, pours a drop of wax that spreads with a wobble on the recoil spring and presses the monogram in; the seal is a real button that Enter or Space cracks to the end, and Escape stops.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/wax-seal`

Props:
- `to`: string — Who the letter is for: written on the outside and in the greeting.
- `from`: string — Who sealed it: the monogram pressed into the wax and the signature.
- `date`: string — Written on the outside and at the head of the letter.
- `message`: string — The letter itself, written across the panels and their creases.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default false) — Whether the seal is broken and the letter open. A host that changes it gets the same motion, silently.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the hold or key that broke the seal (true) and from Reseal (false).
- `hold`: number (default 800) — How long the seal must be held before it breaks, in ms (400–1500): the cracks spread over exactly this long.
- `wax`: "crimson" | "navy" | "forest" (default "crimson") — The wax's pigment, the same in either theme; it also tunes the snap.
- `folds`: number (default 3) — Panels the letter is folded into: 2 (one flap, a wider packet that leaves a wax remnant in the margin) or 3 (two flaps).
- `resealLabel`: string (default "Reseal") — The Reseal button's text.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — The snap of the wax, a paper sound for each fold and a soft press when it is sealed again — only for the visitor's own hold and presses.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the letter but takes no hold or presses.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the seal is a button named Break the seal — Enter or Space starts the same cracking, which runs to the end on its own, and Escape during it stops it (handled with preventDefault). Focus moves into the open letter, a document region, and back to the new seal button after Reseal.
- Reduced motion: the cracks still draw with the hold, because progress is information, but nothing flies, gives or unfolds — the packet and the open letter cross-fade, and fresh wax fades in whole.
- The letter's text is in the DOM only while it is open: sealed, only the outside (recipient and date) is readable. Pointer holds capture nothing and are released anywhere on the page; leaving the window lets the cracks close.

### Library Card (KQ-1224) — `library-card`
Stamped every time.

A library book's date-due card in its pocket, with a wooden date stamp and an ink pad beside it. The card follows a drag up out of its pocket 1:1, rubber-bands at the ends and commits where the throw was heading on the glide spring; a press on the stamp lifts it on snap, glides it over the next empty row while it turns to that row's seeded crooked angle, strikes on an accelerating tween with a thud and inks the date, then sets it back down on recoil. Every strike thins the ink, so each impression is fainter and patchier until the pad re-inks it, and the card, the stamp and the pad are real buttons, so Enter or Space slides the card, stamps the next row and re-inks.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/library-card`

Props:
- `title`: string — The book's title, printed at the head of the card.
- `author`: string — Who wrote it, printed under the title.
- `callNumber`: string — The shelf mark, printed beside the author in mono.
- `library`: string (default "Public Library") — The library's name, printed on the pocket; its initials are pressed into the cover as a seal.
- `due`: string — What the stamp is set to print next, e.g. "14 OCT 2026". Shown under the stamp.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The dates stamped so far, oldest first. Only as many as there are rows are shown.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string[]) => void — Fires from the strike that inked a row, with every date now on the card.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default false) — Whether the card is out of its pocket. Stamping a tucked card slides it out first.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the drag, tap or key that slid the card out or in.
- `rows`: number (default 6) — How many rows the card is ruled into, 4 to 10. They share the card's height, so fewer rows print larger dates.
- `ink`: "violet" | "red" | "black" (default "violet") — The colour of the pad, the stamp's rubber and every impression.
- `crooked`: number (default 3) — How far a stamp may land off square, in degrees, 0 to 6. Each row's angle and offset are seeded by the row and its date.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A thud for every strike (lighter as the ink runs dry), soft dabs on the pad, and a paper rustle as the card slides.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the card but takes no drags, taps or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the desk's root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the card's head is a button (aria-expanded) that slides it out or in; the stamp is a button named for what it will do ("Stamp 14 OCT 2026 in row 3") and described by its ink level; the pad is a button that re-inks. Enter or Space on each reaches the same end as the drag, and presses made mid-flight are queued, not lost.
- Reduced motion: nothing flies, lifts or bounces — the card jumps between in and out (a drag still follows the finger), a stamping fades the date in where it lands while the stamp dims at home, and re-inking fades the rim back to full. Ink still runs out and every change is still spoken.
- Every change is spoken once in a polite live region: the date and row stamped (with a warning when the stamp is running dry), the card sliding out or in, a re-ink, and a full card. The crooked angles are seeded, so the server and the browser draw the same card.

### Stat Card (KQ-1225) — `stat-card`
A profile you can collect.

A profile printed as a collectible card, edged in foil the colour of its rarity: the rim is a conic gradient that turns with the light and carries a glint where the light strikes it, and a mouse over the card tilts it toward the pointer in perspective on springs with glide's constants, so the glint runs round the rim as the pointer circles. Its numbers are odometers that roll up on the drift spring in a cascade the first time it is seen and whenever the front comes back round; dragging sideways turns it over 1:1, a release lands on the nearest face on the glide spring with the throw's velocity, and a raised level sweeps a shine across the face while the badge lands on recoil. The flip button on each face is a real toggle that Enter or Space presses, and focus follows it to the other side.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/stat-card`

Props:
- `name`: string — Whose card it is: the heading, the monogram and the group's accessible name.
- `role`: string — What they do, under the name and on the type line.
- `team`: string — Where they do it, on the type line.
- `level`: number — Their level, in the corner badge. Raising it plays the level-up; lowering it only rolls the number down.
- `stats`: { label: string; value: number; max?: number }[] — The numbers on the front, as rolling odometers; a stat with a max also gets a bar that fills with it.
- `bio`: string — A few sentences for the back.
- `facts`: { label: string; value: string }[] — Short facts listed on the back.
- `number`: string — The card's number in its set, e.g. "042/300", in the footer.
- `since`: string — The year they joined, in the footer.
- `avatar`: ReactNode — A picture for the portrait window. Without it, a monogram on a contour pattern seeded by the name.
- `flipped / defaultFlipped`: boolean (default false) — Whether the back (the bio) is showing.
- `onFlippedChange`: (flipped: boolean) => void — Fires from the drag, tap or key that turned the card over. A controlled host that refuses gets the card turned back.
- `rarity`: "common" | "rare" | "epic" (default "rare") — The foil on the rim and the colours of the portrait, bars and gem: matte silver, cobalt, or an iridescent run of hues with sparkles that flare as the glint passes.
- `tilt`: number (default 10) — How far the card leans toward the pointer, in degrees, 0 to 20. At 0 it stays flat and only the glint follows.
- `roll`: boolean (default true) — Roll the numbers up from zero when the front is revealed. Off shows them still.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A pop as a flipped face lands; a shimmer and a pop for a level-up the visitor caused (a level pushed from elsewhere is silent).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the card but takes no tilt, drags, taps or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the card's root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: each face has a flip button (aria-pressed, "Show the bio"); Enter or Space turns the card and focus moves to the same button on the side now showing. The face turned away is inert. Drags and taps on the card are pointer mirrors of the button.
- Reduced motion: the card stays flat and never turns — the faces cross-fade (a drag past 40px still flips) — the numbers and bars show their values at once, and a level-up swaps the number and pulses the badge's ring, without the sweep.
- The stats are a description list whose values are real text for assistive technology (the rolling digits are hidden from it), and a polite live region says which side is showing and the new level, once each.

### Wristband (KQ-1226) — `wristband`
Snap it on, it's yours.

An event wristband drawn as 36 flat slices on a cylinder in CSS 3D, each with an outer and an inner face, so it can lie flat and then curl round into a real loop with the inside of the far side showing. Worn, a tap or Enter lifts it toward the reader on snap while three rings ripple out from its print with a chime, a drag turns it on the wrist and it swings back on glide, and the Unsnap button pops the clasp and lets it fall open.

- `onSnappedChange`: (snapped: boolean) => void — Fires from the drag, tap or key whose clasp caught, or from Unsnap.

- `fabric`: "woven" | "silicone" | "paper" (default "woven") — What the band is made of: woven twill with stitched edges and a soft curl, glossy silicone with a travelling highlight and a lively curl, or paper with fibres, die-cut slits and a crisp curl. Each has its own height.
- `tier`: "ga" | "vip" | "crew" (default "vip") — The ticket tier: the band's colour (cobalt, gold, red), the word printed on it, the default access and the chime's pitch.
- `wrap`: number (default 0.6) — How much depth the band shows, 0 to 1: worn, 0 is straight on and nearly flat and 1 looks down into the loop with strong perspective; off, it is how much of the wrist's curve the band keeps as it rests.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A snap as the clasp catches (lower as it opens) and a chime on a scan, pitched by tier. Only ever in answer to the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the band but takes no drags, taps or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the band is one real button whose name says what a press does — "Put on the wristband: VIP, Teo Bramhall" or "Scan the wristband: …" — so Enter or Space wraps it on or scans it; Unsnap is a real button shown while it is worn, and focus returns to the band after it. Drags are pointer mirrors of the button.
- Reduced motion: nothing curls, lifts or ripples outward — the flat and worn bands cross-fade, the print still runs on (a clip, not a movement), and a scan shows one ring fading in place while the print panel glows. A drag still follows the finger and lands where it commits.
- The band's length follows its measured width (between 260 and 600px), and the view only tips down into the loop as it closes, so a half-wrapped band never rises out of its box. A polite live region says when the band goes on or off and each scan.

### Punch Card (KQ-1228) — `punch-card`
Nine punches, one free.

- `reward`: string (default "One free drink") — What a full card is worth.
- `member`: string — The holder's name, printed at the foot of the card.
- `number`: string — The card's number, printed on the band.
- `code`: string — The redeem code on the back. Defaults to a deterministic code from the brand, the member and the cycle.
- `label`: string — The card's accessible name. Defaults to "{brand} loyalty card".
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — How many spots are punched, 0 to holes; controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the press that punched a spot, or from Redeem with 0.
- `onRedeem`: () => void — Fires when the reward is redeemed.
- `holes`: number (default 9) — How many punches earn the reward, 6 to 12; the grid re-lays out in two rows.
- `shape`: "round" | "star" | "heart" (default "round") — The printed spot, the hole and the chad.
- `chad`: boolean (default true) — A paper chad pops out of each hole and falls away. Off: a clean cut.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A click at each cut, rising in pitch across the card, a pop as the reward lights, and a click on Redeem.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The card can be read but not punched or redeemed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the Punch button lies over the spots; Space or Enter dimples on key down and cuts on release, exactly as a press does, and once the card is full it reads "Card full. Turn over to redeem". When the card turns, focus moves to the arriving face's button (Redeem, or the Punch button again after a redeem). The count is a role="meter" with aria-valuetext such as "6 of 9 punched, 3 to go", and each punch is announced politely.
- Reduced motion: no dimple travel, jolt, chad flight, ring or turn — the chad fades in its hole and the faces cross-fade — while the hole, the count, the reward's colour and every sound still arrive.
- Controlled: onValueChange reports the press; a host that raises value animates the punches without sound, and a host that sets 0 while the redeem side is up turns the card back to a fresh front.

### Award Seal (KQ-1229) — `award-seal`

### Booth Strip (KQ-1230) — `booth-strip`

A photo booth's panel and the strip it prints: for each shot the readout counts down, the reflector charges and fires a white wash over the booth, and the strip feeds out of the slot by one frame on a tween stepped into roller lines, newest shot nearest the slot. - `flash`: boolean (default true) — The booth flashes white on each shot (never more than once a second). Off: only the reflector lights.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A shutter snap on each shot and the print feed's whir while the strip feeds, only during a strip the visitor started.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The strip can be looked at but not taken, shaken or enlarged.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the shutter is a button; the frames are one tab stop where Up and Down move between shots in their visual order, Home and End jump, Enter or Space enlarges, and Left and Right shake the strip (each a kick that dries it a step). ### Pocket Phone (KQ-1231) — `pocket-phone`

A phone frame that holds any screen and leans toward the pointer under a sheet of glass glare on the glide spring. - `power / defaultPower`: boolean (default true) — Whether the console is switched on; the content is inert while it is off.
- `onPowerChange`: (power: boolean) => void — Fires from the power switch with the state asked for.
- `onPress`: (button: PocketConsoleButton) => void — A key went down (pointer, keyboard or assistive technology) while the console is on.
- `onRelease`: (button: PocketConsoleButton) => void — A key came back up.
- `keyMap`: Partial<Record<PocketConsoleButton, string>> (default { up: "ArrowUp", …, a: "a", b: "b", start: "Enter", select: "Shift" }) — The key each button sends into the screen. Escape is never sent.
- `shell`: "grey" | "teal" | "clear" (default "grey") — The plastic: warm grey, teal, or a smoked clear shell that shows the board inside.
- `grid`: number (default 0.5) — How strongly the LCD's pixel grid shows, 0 to 1.
- `backlight`: number (default 0.8) — How lit the LCD is, 0 (unlit, under a dark film) to 1 (glowing).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Each key clicks going down and, quieter, coming up. Nothing plays on its own.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Keys take no presses and anything held is let go.
- `className`: string — Classes for the 5:8 root; size it by width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the d-pad is one Tab stop of four buttons with a roving tabindex; from any console control the arrow keys press the d-pad and the A and B keys press A and B for as long as they are held, Enter or Space hold the focused key, and an arrow on the d-pad moves focus to that arm. The power switch is a role=switch.
- Reduced motion: no cap travels and the d-pad does not rock — a pressed key darkens at once — and the power light holds steady; every press still reaches the content and clicks.
- Each press is dispatched as a KeyboardEvent at the element focused inside the screen, or at the content's first element, so an ordinary onKeyDown on the content's root hears it; the console never handles the events it sends.

### Viewfinder (KQ-1238) — `viewfinder`
Frame it, focus, shoot.

A camera viewfinder over any scene with a two-stage shutter: holding it sinks the cap to its first stage on flick and racks the lens to the focus point's subject on the recoil spring, hunting through sharp twice before the brackets close on snap and turn green. Letting go fires — two curtains meet and part on a tween, and the frame, with the blur, exposure and roll it was taken with, shrinks out of the finder on snap and arcs into the corner slot on glide; released before the lock, the photo is soft. The nine focus points are a radiogroup the arrow keys move through, re-metering the scene and changing the shutter speed, and Space or Enter held on the shutter is the half-press, released the shot, with Escape to cancel.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/viewfinder`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The scene: any content, framed 3:2 in a size container.
- `label`: string (default "Camera") — The camera's accessible name.
- `point / defaultPoint`: number (default 4) — The focus point, 0 to 8, row by row from the top left.
- `onPointChange`: (point: number) => void — Fires from a tap on the scene or an arrow key with the point chosen.
- `onShoot`: (shot: ViewfinderShot) => void — Fires as the shutter falls, with the photo's count, point and whether focus had locked.
- `grid`: "thirds" | "cross" | "none" (default "thirds") — The framing grid.
- `level`: boolean (default true) — Show the electronic level, which turns green when the frame is level.
- `focus`: number (default 0.5) — Depth of field, 0 (deep, f/11) to 1 (shallow, f/1.4): how soft the scene starts, how far the lens hunts, and the aperture and shutter speed read out.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — The half-press detent, the focus beep and the shutter's two curtains. Nothing plays on its own.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Takes no presses; a half-press held is cancelled.
- `className`: string — Classes for the 2:1 root; size it by width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the focus points are a role=radiogroup with a roving tabindex — arrow keys move in two dimensions and Home/End jump; on the Shutter, Space or Enter held is the half-press and releasing takes the photo, Escape cancels a half-press (handled with preventDefault) and losing focus cancels it too. An assistive-technology click focuses first and then shoots.
- Reduced motion: no hunting, rolling or flying — focus eases in on a short tween, the brackets turn green without closing, the curtains become one dim, and the photo appears in its slot; the lock, the count and the readout still change.
- A polite live region says Focused. on each lock and Photo 3, sharp. or Photo 3, soft. on each shot. The photo in the slot is a copy of the scene, inert and hidden from assistive technology.

### Ink Reader (KQ-1239) — `ink-reader`
Pages that refresh like paper.

An e-reader that lays any long text out in pages exactly as wide as its screen, measured, so a narrower reader has more pages; every turn is an e-ink refresh rather than a slide — the new page shows inverted, snaps to white and clears in three grey steps, or with a fast refresh draws at once and leaves the old page as a ghost that clears the same way, and a full flash never repeats within half a second. A swipe, a tap, the chin's keys (which press on flick and return on snap) or the keyboard turn the page, and the front-light slider follows the finger 1:1 and settles on snap, bringing the paper up from the room's own light and tinting it cool to amber while the ink stays black. On the focused page the arrow, Page and Space keys turn and Home and End jump; the slider takes arrows, Page keys, Home and End.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ink-reader`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The text: any long content, laid out in pages the size of the screen.
- `label`: string (default "E-reader") — The reader's accessible name.
- `title`: string — The book or chapter, shown at the top of the screen.
- `page / defaultPage`: number (default 1) — The page shown, from 1.
- `onPageChange`: (page: number) => void — Fires from a swipe, a tap, a key or a page key with the page asked for.
- `onPageCountChange`: (count: number) => void — Fires when the text has been laid out, and again whenever a new size changes its page count.
- `light`: number (default 0.5) — The front light, 0 (off) to 1. The slider starts here and follows a new value.
- `onLightChange`: (light: number) => void — Fires from the slider with the new level.
- `warmth`: number (default 0.3) — The light's colour, 0 (cool white) to 1 (amber).
- `refresh`: "full" | "fast" (default "full") — A full flash (inverted, then clean) or a fast draw that leaves a ghost of the last page.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A page turn's paper crinkle, a little higher going forward. Nothing plays at either end or on its own.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Takes no turns and no light changes.
- `className`: string — Classes for the 5:7 root; size it by width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the page is a focusable region named Page 3 of 12 — Right, Down, Page Down and Space turn forward, Left, Up, Page Up and Shift+Space turn back, Home and End go to the first and last page; Previous page and Next page are real buttons; the front light is a role=slider in percent.
- Reduced motion: no inversion flash and no ghost — the new page appears under a paper wash that fades on a short tween — and the keys darken instead of travelling; the page number and the light still change.
- The whole text stays in the DOM, so a screen reader reads it whatever page is shown, and a polite live region says Page 4 of 12. (or Last page.) at each turn. Inside the screen every token is redrawn in grey ink, so content styled with tokens reads as print.

### Stand Monitor (KQ-1240) — `stand-monitor`

A desktop display on a height-adjustable stand: dragging the screen lifts the panel on its column 1:1 under the finger, rubber-banding at the stops, and a heavy counterbalanced arm coasts it to where the throw would stop on the glide spring with the release velocity; dragging its top edge tilts it back in 3D on a friction hinge that holds where it is left and snaps to the nearest degree. The turn button pivots it to portrait on glide while the stand lifts it clear of the desk, the pivot height worked out each frame from the turned panel's reach, and once it settles the picture re-orients upright in a container the new shape; a cable hanging from its back swings at every move on a soft underdamped spring. The screen and its top edge are sliders for height and tilt that take arrow, Page, Home and End keys, and the turn button is a toggle.

- `sound`: boolean (default false) — The hinge creaks while the panel is dragged or turning, with the speed of the hand; the loop always stops.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Takes no drags, keys or turns.
- `className`: string — Classes for the 16:9 root; size it by width.

Notes:

### Loom Field (KQ-1241) — `loom-field`
A weave that ripples under the hand.

A background of woven cloth, warp and weft interlaced thread by thread in a plain, twill or basket weave, with your content on top; a hovering hand is a light touch and a press goes in deep, opening an eye in the weave as the warps part sideways and the wefts up and down. Every crossing is a spring held straight along its thread by tension, so the threads lag the finger, a flick runs a ripple down them, and a lifted hand lets the eye close with two small overshoots near the recoil spring's damping, while the press itself eases in over a blink and out over the base duration. A transparent button behind the content is the keyboard's way in: arrow keys move the hand and Space or Enter held presses into the cloth.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/loom-field`

- `press`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the hand presses, 0 to 1: how wide the threads part (0.7 to 3.2 thread pitches) and how deep the dent's shade reads.
- `thread`: "indigo" | "rust" | "moss" (default "indigo") — The warp's dye, a fixed pigment; the weft is the same dye washed into the page, so it follows the theme.
- `label`: string (default "Woven cloth") — The accessible name of the cloth's keyboard surface.

- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The cloth is drawn and holds still; the hand is ignored and touch scrolling is left to the page.
- `className`: string — Sizes the box; the default is h-full w-full, so it fills its container.

Notes:
- Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content, after it in tab order, named by label and described by a hint. Focused from the keyboard the hand rests at the centre as a light touch with a ring; arrow keys move it 16 px (Shift: 48), Space or Enter held presses in and releasing lets go, and a click from assistive technology presses for a moment. A polite status says Pressed into the cloth once per press.

### Ink Marble (KQ-1242) — `ink-marble`
Comb the ink.

A background of marbled paper still on the bath, bands of ink floating on the size with your content on top; a drag pulls a comb through the ink, its tines standing across the stroke, and the ink near each tine is carried along, so a stroke across the bands feathers them into chevrons and a second one back makes a nonpareil. A polite status says Combed across the paper after a pass.
- Reduced motion: no drift and no continuous relaxing; combing still redraws as the hand moves and a keyboard pass is applied at once. The ink settles in still steps, the marks halving 1.6 s after the last stroke and every 1.6 s after, with no motion between steps.

A background that is a garden pond seen from above, koi gliding in loose schools under a gently rippling surface while lily pads drift on it, with your content on top; the pointer is a hand over the water, whose shadow makes nearby koi edge away and whose stillness draws the bolder ones back to mill around it. ### Quilt Grid (KQ-1247) — `quilt-grid`
A patchwork that re-stitches.

A backdrop sewn from twelve classic quilt blocks — half-square triangles, pinwheels, flying geese, log cabins, Ohio stars — in printed fabrics with seams and running stitches, drawn in SVG and re-coloured by the theme. Waves re-stitch it from the pointer: ring by ring on a cascade delay, each block either turns a quarter turn on the snap spring or trades places with its outward neighbour on the glide spring, lifting with a soft shadow mid-move and landing flat, while a click re-stitches with a wave where half the blocks swap and a gentle ambient wave starts somewhere every few seconds. - `children`: React.ReactNode — What sits on the quilt — a hero, a heading — in a layer above it. Presses on its own controls never start a wave.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which fills its container (h-full w-full); set its size and radius here.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the quilt's role="application" surface; arrow keys move a stitched marker and turn the blocks round it (the same wave a pointer starts entering that block), Home and End jump along the row, Enter or Space re-stitch from it, and a polite live region announces each re-stitch once.

- Ambient waves run only while the quilt is on screen in a visible page and nobody is pointing at it; touch uses touch-action: pan-y, so a sideways slide sends waves and a vertical one scrolls the page.

### Cloud Chamber (KQ-1248) — `cloud-chamber`

### Follow Knot (KQ-1251) — `follow-knot`
The plus ties itself into a check.

A follow button whose plus is one rope: pressed, its free end sweeps round on a tween into a loop that crosses over the standing part, and the loop cinches into a knot at the vertex of a check on the snap spring, thrown hard enough by tension that its one overshoot reads as the knot pulling past tight. The label slides from Follow to Following on snap inside a slot as wide as the longest word, and the follower figure rolls one on, units first; hovering or keyboard-focusing a followed button loosens and turns the knot and offers Unfollow in danger ink, and a press unties it rope-first before the words and figure follow. It is a button with aria-pressed and a constant name, Space and Enter press it, and under reduced motion the rope swaps between plus and check with a short fade while the digits change in place.

- `label`: string (default "Follow") — The word before following, and the start of the accessible name.

- `releaseLabel`: string (default "Unfollow") — The word while a followed button is hovered or keyboard-focused: what a press will do.
- `target`: string — Who or what is followed, appended to the accessible name ("Follow Fieldline Journal").
- `count`: number — Followers without this viewer; the button adds one while followed. Omit to hide the figure.
- `formatCount`: (count: number) => string (default en-US grouping) — How the figure is written; digits roll, other characters swap.
- `describeCount`: (count: number) => string (default "1,300 followers") — The figure as spoken, read as the button's description.
- `tension`: number (default 0.5) — How hard the knot is pulled, 0 to 1: a loose eye that settles softly, or a hard bead that snaps past tight.
- `untieAngle`: number (default 8) — How far the knot turns as it loosens under a hover, in degrees.

- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Not pressable, drawn at half strength.
- `className`: string — Classes for the button.

Notes:

- `now`: Date | number — The current time. Pass it from your clock so server and client agree; without it a press reads the clock when it happens.
- `minutes`: number (default 60) — How long a tap focuses for, in minutes.
- `step`: number (default 30) — What one hold step or arrow key adds, in minutes; steps land on this grid (15:07 to 15:30).
- `maxMinutes`: number (default 480) — The furthest a hold can push the end, in minutes from now.
- `holdDelay`: number (default 450) — How long a press must be held before it starts extending, in ms.
- `holdInterval`: number (default 420) — Time between steps while held, in ms.
- `stars`: number (default 5) — How many stars come out around the eclipse, 0 to 8.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — Strength of the light, 0 to 1: the sun's bloom, the corona and its breathing.
- `label`: string (default "Do not disturb") — The button's accessible name and its words while off.
- `focusLabel`: string (default "Focusing until") — The words before the end time while on.
- `format`: (date: Date) => string (default 24-hour "15:00" in timeZone) — How the end time is written.
- `timeZone`: string (default "UTC") — The IANA time zone the default format writes in.
- `compact`: boolean (default false) — Icon only; the name stays and the end time moves to the description and title.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Pill height 32, 40 or 48px with a 24, 30 or 36px sky.
- `sun`: string (default oklch(from var(--warn) 0.84 0.13 h)) — The sun, the corona and the bloom, any CSS colour.
- `night`: string (default oklch(from var(--accent) 0.27 0.07 h)) — The night the face turns while focusing, any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A chime at totality (lower when it ends) and a rising tick per hold step or arrow key. Only after the visitor acts.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Greys the toggle out and ignores presses, holds and keys.
- `className`: string — Extra classes for the root, which wraps the button.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Space and Enter toggle it (on at the default length); the Up and Right arrows add a step (turning it on when off) and Down and Left take one away, never before the next step after now. A held press does the same with the pointer: past holdDelay it adds a step every holdInterval and letting go sets the time.
- Pass now from your own clock (a ticking state or a server timestamp) so the label renders the same on server and client. The toggle never turns itself off: when now passes until, set pressed to false from that clock.
- Controlled hosts get onPressedChange and onUntilChange from the gesture; a hold shows its draft time while held and commits once, on release, so the host hears one change rather than every step. A refused change slides the moon back away.
- A polite status speaks each committed change ("Focusing until 15:30", "Do not disturb off"); the end time and the hold hint are the button's description, and the name stays constant while aria-pressed carries the state.
- The corona's breathing runs only while focusing, on screen and in a visible tab. Under reduced motion the moon fades in over the sun and nothing slides, breathes or rolls; the night face, the label and the time still change.

### Launch Pad (KQ-1261) — `launch-pad`
Three, two, one — shipped.

A deploy button with a launch pad in its left cap: a press arms a countdown ring that drains one segment per second, linearly, while the label's digit rolls on springs.snap, and a second press or Escape aborts. At zero the rocket squats and climbs out through the roof on an accelerating exit ease with exhaust billowing along the floor, the label lifts off after it, and a progress line runs while the onLaunch promise is pending; a resolve drops a flag into the pad on springs.recoil and unfurls it on springs.snap, a reject brings the rocket back nose-down on springs.glide and shakes the button with the error and a retry. Enter and Space press it, Escape aborts the count, and every change is spoken once in a polite live region.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/launch-pad`

Props:

- `state`: "idle" | "countdown" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled state. Omit it and the countdown and the promise drive the pad.
- `onStateChange`: (state: LaunchPadState, error?: unknown) => void — Every change of state — a press, the count reaching zero, the promise settling, a hold running out — with the rejection on error. A controlled pad waits for the host to apply it.
- `onAbort`: () => void — A press or Escape during the countdown called the launch off.
- `countdown`: number (default 3) — Seconds counted down before lift-off, 0 to 9; each is one segment of the ring. 0 launches on the press.
- `thrust`: number (default 0.6) — How hard it launches, 0 to 1: a quicker climb, a longer flame, more exhaust.
- `shake`: number (default 6) — How far a failure shakes the button, in px. 0 keeps it still.
- `progress`: number — Known progress of the deploy, 0 to 1. Omit it for an estimate that approaches 92% and never claims the finish.
- `eta`: number (default 2400) — How long a deploy usually takes, in ms; paces the estimated progress line.
- `label`: string (default "Deploy") — The idle label.
- `abortLabel`: string (default "Abort") — Shown before the seconds while counting down, when a press aborts.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Deploying") — The label while the deploy is in flight.
- `version`: string (default "v2.4.1") — The version that goes live, read out in the success label.
- `successLabel`: string (default "Live · {version}") — The label once live.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Checks failed") — What failed, shown before the retry. A rejection's own message replaces it and truncates with a title.
- `retryLabel`: string (default "Retry") — The word after the error that says a press tries again.
- `successHold`: number (default 2600) — How long Live holds before the pad resets, in ms; 0 keeps it. Counts only while the page is visible.
- `errorHold`: number (default 0) — How long a failure holds before the pad resets, in ms; 0 keeps it until retried.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 36, 44 or 52px tall; the rocket, flag and ring scale with it.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--primary)") — The button's face while idle, counting and in flight.
- `flame`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.8 c h)") — The exhaust flame's colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the countdown ticks, the lift-off, the landing chime and the failure buzz — only for a launch the visitor started.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Takes the button out of use.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer wrapper.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Enter or Space presses through the native click; during the countdown a second press or Escape aborts (Escape is handled with preventDefault). In flight and while Live, the button stays focusable but is aria-disabled, and pending is aria-busy.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels or bounces — the ring still drains because it is the time left, the digit swaps, the rocket fades out and back, the progress line still fills, the flag and the tilted rocket appear in place, and the button never shakes; colours still change.
- Controlled use: pass state and apply what onStateChange reports. The pad calls onLaunch at zero and reports pending, then success or error when the promise settles; a host that refuses a change simply leaves the pad where it is.
- The countdown is an abort window, so it pauses while the page is hidden instead of launching behind the visitor's back; the success and error holds pause too.
