### Bin Lid (KQ-1264) — `bin-lid`
Thrown away, with a window to fish it out.

A delete button whose bin lid lifts on its hinge on the snap spring when the pointer or keyboard focus arrives; pressing folds the label into a paper sheet that is lobbed into the bin on a true ballistic arc and tumbles out of sight behind its front wall, the lid falls shut on an accelerating tween, and the bin squashes and recovers on snap while dust puffs from both ends of the lid. The button's corners then glide into an undo pill and a ring round the bin drains linearly over the undo window; undo, by a press or Escape, flies the paper back out along the same arc and unfolds it into the label, and when the ring empties onDelete fires, with a spinning ring while its promise is pending and the paper thrown back out with a shake if it fails. It is a native button whose Enter and Space press through the native click, its width never changes, and a polite live region speaks each change once.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/bin-lid`

Props:
- `onDelete`: () => void | Promise<unknown> — Fires once the undo window runs out. Return a promise and the button shows the deletion pending until it settles, then Deleted or the error.
- `onUndo`: () => void — The visitor fished it back out, with a press or Escape, before the window ran out.
- `state`: "idle" | "armed" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled state. Every move the button wants to make goes through onStateChange and waits for this; the choreography follows the shown state, so a host's change plays it too.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "armed" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each state the button moves to, from the press, the timer or the promise that caused it.
- `window`: number (default 5000) — How long the undo window stays open, in ms: the time the ring takes to drain. It pauses while the page is hidden.
- `arc`: number (default 0.6) — How high the paper is lobbed into the bin and how much it tumbles, 0 to 1. The apex is kept inside the component's frame.
- `puff`: number (default 0.6) — How much dust the slammed lid pushes out of its ends, 0 to 1: count, reach and size. 0 slams clean.
- `label`: string (default "Delete") — The text at rest.
- `undoLabel`: string (default "Undo") — The text while the undo window is open.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Deleting") — The text while onDelete is settling.
- `successLabel`: string (default "Deleted") — The text once it is gone.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Retry") — The text after onDelete failed; a press throws it away again.
- `itemName`: string — What is being thrown away. Joins the accessible name ("Delete Q3 forecast draft") and the spoken sentences.
- `successHold`: number (default 1800) — How long Deleted holds before the button is ready again, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 2600) — How long the error holds before the button rests again, in ms.
- `iconOnly`: boolean (default false) — The bin alone in a square button (a circle as the undo pill) that keeps its accessible name.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px tall; the bin, the paper and the dust scale with it.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--danger)") — The destructive colour for the text, outline, bin and ring. Any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the paper as it is thrown, the thud of the lid and the pop as it comes back out, only in answer to a press or key. No audio context exists unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims and disables the button.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes (the button and the 12 px frame its lob and dust stay inside).

Notes:
- A native button named by its current label (with itemName at rest): Enter or Space presses it through the native click, a press during the undo window restores, Escape restores too (handled where focus is, with preventDefault), and presses are ignored while pending or after success. A polite live region speaks one sentence per change: moved to the bin with the window in seconds, restored, deleting, deleted, or not deleted.
- Under reduced motion nothing flies, swings, squashes or puffs and the corners do not morph: the labels cross-fade, the ring still drains because the window is information, pending shows a still dashed ring, and an error changes the outline colour instead of shaking.
- onDelete only runs when the window has run out, so an undo never needs a server round trip; return a promise to keep the button pending until the deletion is confirmed, and a rejection brings the item back with Retry.
- Every label is stacked in one grid cell, so the button keeps the width of the longest through every state and nothing beside it moves.
- The undo countdown and the success and error holds pause while the page is hidden, and nothing animates at rest.

### Upload Orbit (KQ-1265) — `upload-orbit`
The file circles until it lands.

An upload button over a real file input whose files orbit it while they go up: chosen or dropped files become dots that pop into a waiting line on the top edge on the snap spring, step out on the glide spring, and then sit round the button's perimeter at their progress, walked by arc length so one lap is the whole file, chasing each reported value on a critically damped spring while a softer spring drags a fading comet tail behind them. A finished dot completes its lap and hops into the count in the label, where the badge recoils on the recoil spring and the digit rolls on snap; a failed dot leaves along its tangent, falls and fades red while a red counter appears on the badge. Click, Enter or Space opens the system picker and files can be dropped anywhere on it; Escape cancels what is in flight, and after a batch with failures a press queues them again.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/upload-orbit`

Props:
- `onUpload`: (file: File, progress: (share: number) => void, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<unknown> — Uploads one file: report progress from 0 to 1 as it goes and settle the promise when it is done or failed. Called for at most queue files at once; the signal aborts on Escape or unmount.
- `files`: UploadOrbitFile[] — Controlled list of files ({ id, name, size?, progress, status: "queued" | "uploading" | "done" | "error", error? }). The button reports every list it wants through onFilesChange and draws this one.
- `onFilesChange`: (files: UploadOrbitFile[]) => void — Every new list: files added, progress, completions, failures, retries.
- `onSelect`: (files: File[]) => void — The files the visitor chose or dropped that passed accept and maxSize.
- `accept`: string — What the picker offers and a drop accepts, as for a file input ("image/*,.pdf"). Refused files fall off at once and cannot be retried.
- `multiple`: boolean (default true) — Take several files at a time; off, only the first of a drop is taken.
- `maxSize`: number — The largest file accepted, in bytes. Larger ones fall off at once.
- `tail`: number (default 0.6) — How far each dot's comet tail trails it while it moves, 0 to 1, capped at 35% of the lap. 0 draws no tail.
- `speed`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly a dot runs to its reported progress, 0 to 1: a lazy glide that smooths a chunky connection, or a tight follow that dashes.
- `queue`: number (default 2) — How many files fly at once, 1 to 4; the rest wait in line as smaller dots.
- `label`: string (default "Upload") — The text at rest.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Uploading") — The text while files are queued, in flight or landing.
- `successLabel`: string (default "Uploaded") — The text once a batch has landed.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Retry") — The text after a batch with failures that can be retried; a press queues them again.
- `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled button state. Without it, the state follows the files: pending until the last finished dot has landed.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each state the button moves to, from the change that caused it.
- `successHold`: number (default 1600) — How long Uploaded holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 4000) — How long Retry holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px tall; the dots, their spacing and the orbit scale with it.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The orbit's colour: dots, tails and the lit track. Any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pop for the drop or pick and a rising plip as each dot takes its place, only in answer to the visitor. Landings and failures are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the button and refuses picks and drops.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes (the button and the 12 px frame its orbit stays inside).
- `ref`: React.Ref<UploadOrbitHandle> — An imperative handle: add(files) queues files as if dropped, open() opens the picker, cancel() stops everything in flight, retry() queues the failed files again.

Notes:
- The button is the keyboard path to the same end state as a drop: Enter or Space opens the native picker (the input itself is hidden and out of the tab order), Escape cancels everything queued or in flight while it is busy, and after a batch with failures a press retries them. The button is described by a sentence with the counts, aria-busy while pending.
- A polite live region speaks per arrival, never per progress tick: files added, each file uploaded with its place in the batch, each failure with its reason, and cancellations.
- Under reduced motion there is no glide, tail, hop or fall: queued dots sit at their slots, a flying dot jumps to each reported progress, a finished one fades into the badge (the count still moves) and a failed one turns red and fades in place.
- Uncontrolled, onUpload runs the uploads with at most queue in flight and gets an AbortSignal for cancels and unmounts; controlled, pass files and onFilesChange and the button draws your list, starting any queued files you added on the next frame.
- The count in the label moves only when a dot lands, and the button stays pending until the last finished dot has landed, so the words never run ahead of the picture.

### Publish Press (KQ-1266) — `publish-press`
A roller inks it live.

A publish button drawn as a sheet of paper, printed by a roller: a press sets an inked roller down at the start of the label, it bobs in place on a mirrored tween while the action is pending, and on success it rolls across the label on a symmetric move tween, inking the new word behind it through a clip that follows its track while the old label smears into a dragged, skewed band that dries away; the roller is a cylinder seen face on whose ribs turn at distance over radius, so a bigger drum turns slower. The ink is printed through a halftone screen whose dots grow with the ink load and starts wet and solid, drying back to its screen over the success hold; with a schedule set, a date stamp hovers while pending and slams down on the recoil spring instead, and pressing a published or scheduled button lifts the ink off in four strips on the exit ease in a cascade. It is a native button: Enter or Space presses it, Escape cancels while pending, and a failure leaves Retry.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/publish-press`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: "draft" | "published" | "scheduled" (default "draft") — The document's status, controlled or initial. A controlled press reports through onValueChange and prints once the host answers.
- `onValueChange`: (value: "draft" | "published" | "scheduled") => void — Each status the document moves to, once its action has succeeded.
- `onPublish`: (at: Date | null, signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Publishes now (at is null) or schedules for at. Return a promise and the roller bobs until it settles; the signal aborts on Escape.
- `onUnpublish`: (signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Takes a published or scheduled document back to draft.
- `schedule`: Date | number | null — When set, a press schedules for this moment and stamps the date instead of rolling; the draft label becomes scheduleLabel.
- `formatDate`: (date: Date) => string (default UTC "Oct 9 · 09:00") — How the stamped date reads. The default prints "Oct 9 · 09:00" from UTC parts so server and browser agree; pass your own for the reader's zone.
- `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled action state. Every move goes through onStateChange and waits for this.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each action state, from the press, the answer or the timer that caused it.
- `ink`: number (default 0.7) — How much ink the roller carries, 0 to 1: a pale, speckled halftone print or a dense, solid one.
- `roller`: number (default 0.5) — How big and heavy the roller is, 0 to 1: a quick small brayer or a slow wide drum whose ribs turn slower.
- `smudge`: number (default 0.5) — How much the old label smears as the roller drags over it, 0 to 1: the band's width, drag, skew and strength. 0 wipes clean.
- `label`: string (default "Publish") — The text on a draft.
- `scheduleLabel`: string (default "Schedule") — The text on a draft when schedule is set.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Publishing") — The text while publishing.
- `publishedLabel`: string (default "Published") — The word the roller inks.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Retry") — The text after an action failed; a press tries it again.
- `inkColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The ink: the printed word, the stamp and the roller. Any CSS colour.
- `successHold`: number (default 1400) — How long fresh ink stays wet before it dries and the button rests, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 2600) — How long the error holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px tall; the roller and the strips scale with it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the thock of the roller setting down and the stamp landing, and the swish of the roll and the peel, only within the press's own beat. No audio context exists unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims and disables the button.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- A native button named by what it shows (Publish, Publishing, Published, Scheduled for the date, Retry) and described by what a press will do: Enter or Space presses it, a press on a published or scheduled document unpublishes it, Escape cancels a pending action (handled where focus is, with preventDefault), and a polite live region speaks each change once.
- Under reduced motion nothing rolls, bobs, drops, smears or peels: the roller stands still at the start of the label while pending, the ink and the stamp fade in dry, and they fade out as one when unpublished. Labels, value and timings are unchanged.
- The label only changes once the action succeeds: pending keeps the old words with the roller waiting on them, and a refusal lifts the roller away and leaves Retry, so the button never claims something the server has not done.
- Every face, the stamped date included, is stacked in one grid cell, so the button keeps one width through every state; everything it draws stays inside the button.
- The bob runs only while pending and pauses on a hidden page, and the wet-ink and error holds pause there too; at rest nothing animates.

### Refresh Wind (KQ-1267) — `refresh-wind`
Wind it up, let it spin.

A refresh button you wind like a clock spring: drag around it, or press and hold, and the arrow turns back with the finger while its stroke coils into a tightening spiral and a ring of notches lights and ticks with the tension; let go and a per-frame integrator whips it forward from rest on the spring, then lets it coast on the stored energy against friction and air drag while the refresh runs, settling to a steady cruise if the work outlasts the energy and, once it has answered, decaying exactly onto the nearest upright. A plain press does one turn, and on success the Updated 2 min ago stamp rolls to just now on the snap spring while the notches flash and fade. It is a native button: Enter and Space refresh, Shift+Enter winds a full turn (again for another) and lets go, and Escape cancels a refresh in flight.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/refresh-wind`

Props:
- `onRefresh`: (signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Runs the refresh. Return a promise and the arrow keeps turning until it settles; the signal aborts on Escape.
- `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled action state. Every move goes through onStateChange and waits for this.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each action state, from the press, the answer or the timer that caused it.
- `updatedAt / defaultUpdatedAt`: Date | number | null (default null) — The time of the last successful refresh, controlled or initial. The stamp is written from it.
- `onUpdatedAtChange`: (updatedAt: Date) => void — The moment of each successful refresh: the now prop's value, or the clock when none is given.
- `now`: Date | number (default a clock started on mount) — The time the stamp is read against. Pass it for a relative stamp that renders on the server; without it the phrase arrives after mount and a shared 30-second clock keeps it current while the page is visible.
- `onWind`: (turns: number) => void — Fires when a wind is let go, with the turns of spring it stored.
- `friction`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly the released spin slows, 0 to 1: 0 coasts for seconds, 1 stops within a turn or two.
- `wind`: number (default 2) — Turns of spring the button holds: how far a full wind goes back, how tight the coil gets and how long the spin runs.
- `stamp`: "relative" | "clock" | "off" (default "relative") — The stamp beside the button: Updated 2 min ago, Updated 09:40, or none (an icon-only button whose stamp is its accessible description).
- `formatStamp`: (updatedAt: Date, now: Date) => string (default relative, or a UTC clock) — Writes the stamp from the last refresh and the current time; pass one for the reader's own time zone or language.
- `label`: string (default "Refresh") — The button's accessible name.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Refreshing") — The name and the stamp while refreshing.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Couldn't refresh") — The stamp after a failed refresh; a press retries.
- `emptyLabel`: string (default "Not updated yet") — The stamp before the first refresh.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The coil and the tension notches. Any CSS colour.
- `successHold`: number (default 1400) — How long the success flash holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 2600) — How long a failure holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px across; the coil and the notch ring scale with it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a tick for every notch the wind lights and the whir of the spin while it spends the spring's energy. No audio context exists unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the button and lets go of any wind without firing it.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- A native button named by its label and described by the stamp and the gesture: Enter and Space refresh with one turn, Shift+Enter winds a full turn (press it again during the wind for another, up to wind) and lets go, and Escape cancels a refresh in flight (handled where focus is, with preventDefault). A polite live region speaks Refreshing, the new stamp, a failure or a cancel once each.
- The wind is a real drag through the shared gesture kit: it follows the pointer's angle round the button 1:1, rubber-bands past empty and past full, and takes the pointer only after a few pixels, so a plain press is still a click. The button is touch-action none, since the wind is two-dimensional.
- Under reduced motion nothing spins or whips: the coil and the notches still show the tension while winding, the arrow stays upright, a refresh in flight shows the notch ring steady at half strength, and the stamp swaps by cross-fade.
- The spin is integrated per frame only while it moves and stops at rest; the whir only spends the energy the visitor wound in and fades as the spin falls to cruising speed. A host that sets state to pending on its own gets the cruise without a sound.
- The stamp's width is the widest of its phrases stacked in one cell, so the row never shifts when it rolls to just now or to the error. Pass now for server rendering; the default clock is shared by every instance and pauses on a hidden page.

### Gate Button (KQ-1268) — `gate-button`
Locked until the form is ready.

A submit button that shows its own readiness: a padlock at its left wears a segmented arc, one segment per requirement, and each requirement the form meets is drawn along the arc on the flick spring. When the last is met the shackle pops open, lifting on the recoil spring and swinging about its long leg on snap, and the button warms as an accent bloom grows out of the padlock across the face on glide; pressed, the padlock gives way to three dots bouncing in a wave while the request runs, then the dots run together and a check draws on flick as the label rolls to Sent. Locked, it stays focusable: hover or keyboard focus lists what is missing, Enter or Space is refused with a rattle and the first missing item flagged, and Escape closes the list or cancels a send.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/gate-button`

Props:
- `requirements`: { id: string; label: string; met: boolean }[] (default defaultRequirements) — What the form needs before it can be sent; one arc segment each. With none, the button is ready.
- `onSubmit`: (signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Sends the form. Return a promise and the dots bounce until it settles; the signal aborts on Escape.
- `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled action state. Every move goes through onStateChange and waits for this.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each action state, from the press, the answer or the timer that caused it.
- `onLockedPress`: (missing: { id: string; label: string; met: boolean }[]) => void — A press while locked, with what is still missing: scroll to the first field, flag it.
- `segments`: "arc" | "ring" | "pips" (default "arc") — How the padlock wears the requirements: an arc open at the foot, a closed ring, or one pip each.
- `warm`: number (default 0.7) — How strongly the button warms once it is ready, 0 to 1: an accent outline at 0, a solid accent fill with light text at 1.
- `hint`: "list" | "next" | "off" (default "list") — What hovering or focusing the locked button shows: every requirement ticked or not, only the next one missing, or nothing (the description still names them).
- `hintTitle`: string (default "Still needed") — The list's heading, also used in the spoken description.
- `hintSide`: "top" | "bottom" (default "top") — Which side of the button the hint opens on.
- `hintAlign`: "start" | "center" | "end" (default "end") — Which edge of the button the hint lines up with; end suits a form footer's right-hand button.
- `label`: string (default "Submit request") — The button's text.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Sending") — The text while sending.
- `successLabel`: string (default "Sent") — The text once sent.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Retry") — The text after a failed send; a press tries again.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent)") — The met segments and the warm fill. Any CSS colour.
- `successHold`: number (default 1600) — How long Sent holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 2600) — How long the error holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px tall; the padlock scales with it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click for each requirement the visitor meets, the shackle's snap, a dull click on a refused press and a chime when sent. Requirements met by the host alone are silent. No audio context exists unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims and disables the button; no hint opens.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- Locked is aria-disabled, never disabled, so the button stays in the tab order, its hint opens on keyboard focus as well as hover, and its description says what is missing (Locked. Still needed: Team chosen, Data policy accepted.) whether or not the hint is shown.
- A refused press rattles the padlock, keeps the hint open for a couple of seconds (for touch, which cannot hover), flags the first missing item and calls onLockedPress with the missing list, so the form can scroll to or highlight the field. A polite live region speaks progress, Ready to submit, Sending, Sent, a failure and a cancel once each.
- Escape is handled where focus is, with preventDefault: it cancels a send in flight (the signal aborts) or closes an open hint.
- Under reduced motion nothing lifts, swings, rattles or bounces: the shackle swaps open, the warm fill fades in, the segments fill quickly, the pending dots pulse in opacity and the check appears whole.
- Every label is stacked in one cell, so the button keeps its width from Submit request to Sending, Sent and Retry; the bloom, dots and check are all drawn inside the button. The hint is an overlay anchored to the button by hintSide and hintAlign.

### Rewind Undo (KQ-1269) — `rewind-undo`
Spool back through what you did.

Undo and redo as a tape deck: the Undo button carries a reel holding the applied history, the Redo button a reel holding what has been rewound, and the tape between them reads out each step. A press rewinds one step as both reels turn the same way on a spring as heavy as the spool, each by the tape's length over its own radius so a nearly empty reel visibly spins faster, while the undone action's name is pulled out onto the tape on the snap spring and struck through on flick; holding scrubs back with steps that come faster and faster, the reels spinning up and the names flicking past, and Redo slides in on glide once there is something to redo. Both are native buttons in a named group: Enter or Space steps and, held, scrubs exactly as a held pointer does, Escape cancels a step the host is still applying, and optional shortcuts bind Cmd or Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd+Z or Ctrl+Y outside text fields.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/rewind-undo`

Props:
- `history`: { id: string; label: string }[] (default defaultHistory) — Everything done so far, oldest first: the tape. Each label names its step on the tape and in the buttons' names.
- `index / defaultIndex`: number (default history.length) — How many steps of history are applied, controlled or initial.
- `onIndexChange`: (index: number) => void — Each new position, from the press, the hold or the shortcut that moved it.
- `onUndo`: (step: { id: string; label: string }, signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Undoes one step. Return a promise and the step waits on it (the reels tug, the name is faint) and commits once it settles; the signal aborts on Escape.
- `onRedo`: (step: { id: string; label: string }, signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Redoes one step, the same way.
- `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled action state. Every move goes through onStateChange and waits for this.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each action state, from the press, the answer or the timer that caused it.
- `steps`: number (default 6) — Steps one turn of a half-full reel holds, 3 to 12; also the reel's spokes. Fewer means bigger turns per press.
- `spool`: number (default 0.5) — Reel weight, 0 to 1: a light reel snaps to each step, a heavy one carries past and settles back.
- `hold`: number (default 0.5) — How hard a held press speeds up the scrub, 0 to 1: 0 keeps a steady pace, 1 races to the end.
- `holdDelay`: number (default 380) — How long a press is held before it starts to scrub, in ms.
- `shortcuts`: boolean (default false) — Bind Cmd or Ctrl+Z to undo and Shift+Cmd+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo, from anywhere on the page outside inputs, text areas and editable content.
- `undoLabel`: string (default "Undo") — The Undo button's word; its accessible name adds the step it would undo.
- `redoLabel`: string (default "Redo") — The Redo button's word; its accessible name adds the step it would redo.
- `readoutLabels`: { undid?: string; redid?: string; last?: string; empty?: string; failed?: string } (default { undid: "Undid", redid: "Redid", last: "Last", empty: "Nothing to undo", failed: "Failed" }) — The words on the tape between the reels.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The tape on the reels. Any CSS colour.
- `successHold`: number (default 2200) — How long a step's name stays on the tape before it rests on the last step, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 2600) — How long a failure holds before it rests, in ms.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px tall; the reels scale with it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click per step pitched by its place in history, a dull click at either end, and the reels' whir while a hold scrubs. No audio context exists unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims and disables both buttons and the shortcuts.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the group's classes.

Notes:
- A role=group named History holding two native buttons named Undo and Redo plus the step they would take (Undo Removed column). Enter or Space steps on key-down and, held, scrubs exactly as a held pointer does; a pointer steps on release, so a scroll that merely starts on the button never undoes. Undo at the start stays focusable as aria-disabled, and Redo, while there is nothing to redo, is inert and out of the tab order; if it leaves while focused, focus moves to Undo.
- A polite live region speaks each committed step once (Undid Removed column.), a whole scrub once on release (Undid 5 steps. Last: Renamed sheet.), a step in progress, a failure and a cancel, never once per scrubbed step.
- Under reduced motion the reels do not turn and Redo does not slide: the tape on each reel changes at once, names cross-fade, the strike appears whole, and a held press still scrubs at the same pace.
- When the tape is too narrow for its longest line the buttons drop their words and keep their names, with hysteresis so the switch never flickers; the tape truncates a long name with a title. The deck keeps one width as Redo comes and goes, since its slot is part of the deck.
- With shortcuts on, keystrokes in text fields are left alone so native text undo still works there; a host that keeps its own undo bindings should leave shortcuts off and drive index instead, and the reels and tape follow its changes the same way.

### Plug In (KQ-1270) — `plug-in`
Connected, with a spark.

A connect button with a plug on a cable: pressed, the plug lifts level and slides to the socket in the button's edge on the glide spring while its weighted cable first dips and then straightens, and while the connection is pending the plug works at the socket mouth in a seeded, uneven jiggle. When the integration answers, the plug seats on the snap spring with a clack, a seeded burst of sparks flies from the seam with a pop, the lamp lights and the label rolls to Connected; pressing again pulls the plug out on a tween and the cable recoils on the recoil spring's two bounces. The plug can be pushed in or pulled out by hand, following 1:1 and committing by where the throw would land, and the button is a native button in a group named for the integration: Enter and Space press it and Escape cancels a connection in flight.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/plug-in`

Props:
- `connected / defaultConnected`: boolean (default false) — Whether the integration is connected, controlled or initial. A controlled press reports through onConnectedChange and seats the plug once the host answers.
- `onConnectedChange`: (connected: boolean) => void — Each change, once its action has succeeded.
- `onConnect`: (signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Connects. Return a promise and the plug works at the socket until it settles; the signal aborts on Escape.
- `onDisconnect`: (signal: AbortSignal) => void | Promise<unknown> — Disconnects, the same way; the plug tugs at the socket while it waits.
- `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error" — Controlled action state. Every move goes through onStateChange and waits for this.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "pending" | "success" | "error") => void — Each action state, from the press, the answer or the timer that caused it.
- `slack`: number (default 0.5) — Spare cable, 0 to 1: a nearly taut line, or a deep loop that dips and swings when the plug moves.
- `spark`: number (default 0.6) — The contact's burst, 0 to 1: how many sparks and how far they fly. 0 is a clean connection.
- `jiggle`: number (default 0.5) — How hard the plug works at the socket while it connects, 0 to 1.
- `name`: string (default "Integration") — What is being connected: the group's accessible name.
- `icon`: ReactNode (default a block glyph) — The integration's mark on the tile the cable comes from, 16px.
- `label`: string (default "Connect") — The button's text while disconnected.
- `pendingLabel`: string (default "Connecting") — The text while connecting.
- `connectedLabel`: string (default "Connected") — The text once connected.
- `disconnectLabel`: string (default "Disconnect") — What a connected button shows, in danger ink, on hover or keyboard focus: what a press will do.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Retry") — The text after a failure; a press tries again.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--success)") — The live cable, the lamp and the connected face's tint. Any CSS colour.
- `successHold`: number (default 1400) — How long the contact holds as success before the button rests, in ms.
- `errorHold`: number (default 2600) — How long a failure holds before the button rests, in ms.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 32, 40 or 48 px tall; the tile, cable, plug and sparks scale with it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the clack of the plug seating and pulling out and the pop of the spark, only within a few seconds of the visitor's press or push. No audio context exists unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims and disables the button and the plug handle.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the group's classes.

Notes:
- A role=group named by name holding a native button named by its visible label and, when connected, described as Press to disconnect. Enter and Space press it; Escape cancels a connect or disconnect in flight (handled where focus is, with preventDefault). A polite live region speaks Connecting, Connected, Disconnected, a failure and a cancel once each.
- The plug handle is a decorative, aria-hidden drag through the shared gesture kit, touch-action pan-y so the page still scrolls: it follows the hand 1:1, rubber-bands at the rest and at the socket, and commits by projecting the release; a short or slow push springs back. The button reaches every state the hand can.
- Under reduced motion nothing slides, jiggles or recoils: the plug swaps between its rest, socket-mouth and seated poses, the cable takes its sag at once, and the contact is a still flash that fades; the lamp, label and live region still carry the state.
- The label never claims Connected before the host has answered, and a pointer still resting on the button after it connects does not preview Disconnect until it leaves and comes back. Every label is stacked in one cell, so the control keeps one width; the cable, plug and sparks are drawn inside its own box.
- The jiggle and the holds pause on a hidden page; at rest nothing animates.

The peeking card's strip is a real disclosure button that pins it up, Escape lowers it, Continue's name says where it goes, and focus follows the new front card.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/lesson-card`

Props:
- `course`: string (default "Pricing for Product Teams") — The course: the card's heading.
- `provider`: string (default "Fieldline Academy") — Who runs it, shown beside Continue.
- `lessons`: { id: string; title: string; minutes: number }[] (default defaultLessons) — The course's lessons, in order.
- `lesson / defaultLesson`: number (default 6) — Index of the current lesson; lessons.length means the course is complete. The ring shows lesson / lessons.length.
- `onLessonChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires from Continue (the next index) and Start again (0).
- `onContinue`: (lesson: { id: string; title: string; minutes: number }) => void — Fires from Continue with the lesson just finished.
- `activity`: boolean[] (default defaultActivity) — Days of activity, oldest first; the last is today. Continue marks today done.
- `ring`: "thin" | "thick" | "segmented" (default "thick") — The ring: one thin arc, one thick arc, or one segment per lesson filling in turn.
- `peek`: number (default 0.75) — How far the next lesson's card rises from behind on hover, 0 to 1.
- `streak`: number (default 14) — How many days dot along the bottom edge; 0 hides the streak.
- `continueLabel`: string (default "Continue") — The Continue button's text.
- `finishLabel`: string (default "Finish course") — Continue's text on the last lesson.
- `restartLabel`: string (default "Start again") — The button on the complete card.
- `nextLabel`: string (default "Up next") — Words on the card that peeks from behind.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Ring 48 / 60 / 72 px.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The ring, the active days and Continue, as any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish for the flip-through and a plip, pitched by the share, when the ring lands.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing continues or peeks.
- `className`: string — Classes for the card.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab reaches Continue, then the peeking card's strip; keyboard focus in the card raises the next card. Enter on the strip pins it up and Escape (caught wherever focus is in the card) lowers it. After Continue, focus moves to the new front card's button before the old card leaves.
- Only the front card is in the tab and reading order: the cards behind, and the one flipping away, are inert and hidden from assistive technology. The ring is a progressbar whose value is lessons done, and a polite live region speaks one sentence per lesson.
- Reduced motion: the deck re-stacks in place and the new card cross-fades in with no tip, rise or bounce; the ring still fills, on a short tween, and the percentage and streak still update.
- The ring fills the first time the card enters the viewport, so a card further down a page fills when it is reached rather than off screen.
- Control lesson to drive the card from your progress store; a host that moves it plays the same flip-through, and Start again calls onLessonChange(0).

### Pane Stack (KQ-1281) — `pane-stack`
Go deeper; the way back stays in view.

Nested navigation that keeps the way back in view: opening a row slides its pane in from the right on springs.glide, and the pane it covers is pushed and compresses into a narrow labelled tab along the left edge, its content clipped rather than squashed while the tab face takes over. One motion value is the stack's position, so every pane edge, the staircase of covered tabs and the fold of tabs that no longer fit (with a count) are functions of it; a tab, Escape or a 1:1 swipe of the open pane to the right goes back, the throw projected and carried on glide with its release velocity. Rows are a list with one tab stop (arrows move, Enter, Space or ArrowRight open, ArrowLeft goes back), the tabs are a nav with their own stop, and focus moves into each new pane and back onto the row you came from.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pane-stack`

Props:
- `root`: PaneStackNode (default defaultPaneTree) — The tree to navigate: each node has an id, title, optional description, meta, icon, content and children. defaultPaneTree is a Fieldline workspace seven levels deep.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the root's id) — The open pane's id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string, path: string[]) => void — Fires from the press, key or swipe that asked to open a pane, with its id and the ids from the root to it.
- `onSelect`: (id: string) => void — A row with nothing inside it (no children, no content) was chosen.
- `label`: string (default "Navigation") — The container's accessible name.
- `depth`: number (default 0.5) — How far covered panes recede, 0 to 1: tabs step in from top and bottom, shade toward the page and take the open pane's shadow. 0 is flat.
- `compress`: number (default 40) — Width of a covered pane's tab in px (28 to 64); from 36 up the tab shows its level's icon.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — Tempo of every slide, 0.5 to 1.5: the glide spring sped up or slowed down with its damping ratio kept.
- `minPaneWidth`: number (default 200) — The narrowest the open pane gets, in px; past it the oldest tabs fold under the first, which carries a count.
- `swipeBack`: boolean (default true) — Drag the open pane to the right to go back a level.
- `backLabel`: (title: string) => string (default (title) => `Back to ${title}`) — A tab's accessible name, from its pane's title.
- `emptyLabel`: string (default "Nothing in here yet") — What a pane with no content and no children says.
- `height`: number | string (default 440) — The container's height, in px or any CSS length.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Row height 36, 44 or 52 px; small rows drop the description line.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The trail back (the row you came from), the chosen row and the fold badge; any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish for each push and pop, a click for a tab, a chosen row and the swipe's half-way detent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Inert and dimmed: no presses, keys or swipes.
- `className`: string — Classes for the container.

Notes:
- Keyboard: rows are one tab stop (Up, Down, Home, End move; Enter, Space or ArrowRight open; ArrowLeft or Backspace go back); the tabs are a nav with their own stop (arrows walk them, Enter goes back to that level, ArrowRight past the last returns to the pane). Escape goes back a level and is left alone at the root, so a dialog around the stack can still close on it.
- Focus moves into each new pane as it arrives (its first row, else its heading) and back onto the row that led down when you return, but only when focus was already inside the stack.
- Rows open when their node has children or content; a node with neither is a leaf, and choosing it fires onSelect and marks it with aria-current.
- Controlled: pass value and onValueChange; a host that refuses the change keeps the stack where it is, and a host jump to a far branch slides in from the shared ancestor.
- Reduced motion jumps the stack and fades the arriving pane in; the swipe still follows the finger and drops to its result.
- Widths are CSS on the container's own width, so server markup is exact; the fold of extra tabs waits for the first measurement.

### Float Panel (KQ-1282) — `float-panel`
An inspector that docks where you leave it.

A floating inspector over a workspace: dragged by its title bar it follows 1:1, a magnet pulls it flush to an edge on springs.flick, pushed into a side it docks full height on springs.snap with the throw's velocity while the workspace glides aside, and carried into a corner it collapses into a pill that grows back into the panel when pressed. Its edges resize it 1:1 and a release springs to the nearest preset width on snap; with storageKey each key remembers its own place. The title bar is a button whose arrows nudge, Alt with an arrow docks, floats or collapses, Enter docks or floats and Escape collapses; the edge is a separator with arrow, Home and End keys.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/float-panel`

Props:
- `title`: string (default "Inspector") — The title bar's text, the pill's label and the panel's accessible name.
- `icon`: ReactNode (default a sliders icon) — 16px, drawn in currentColor, in the title bar and on the pill.
- `children`: ReactNode — The inspector's body; it scrolls when it is taller than the room.
- `workspace`: ReactNode (default a dotted canvas) — What the panel floats over; a docked panel takes room from it.
- `placement / defaultPlacement`: FloatPanelPlacement (default { mode: "float", x: 1, y: 0, width: 280 }) — Floating at shares of the free room ({ mode: "float", x, y, width }), docked to a side ({ mode: "dock", side, width }) or collapsed to a corner ({ mode: "pill", corner }); controlled or initial.
- `onPlacementChange`: (placement: FloatPanelPlacement) => void — Fires from the drag, key or button that moved, docked, collapsed or resized it.
- `storageKey`: string — Remember the placement under this key in local storage; each key keeps its own place, read the same way on the server and in the browser.
- `magnet`: number (default 24) — How close an edge has to come, in px, before the panel snaps flush to it; 0 turns the magnet off.
- `collapse`: number (default 64) — How close to a corner, in px, a drag has to come to collapse the panel into a pill there; 0 never collapses by drag.
- `widths`: number | number[] (default 3) — Preset widths a resize springs to: a count spread evenly between minWidth and maxWidth (0 resizes freely), or the widths in px.
- `minWidth`: number (default 220) — Narrowest the panel can be, in px.
- `maxWidth`: number (default 380) — Widest the panel can be, in px; the container caps it too.
- `nudge`: number (default 8) — How far one arrow key moves the panel, in px; Shift moves four times as far.
- `reserve`: boolean (default true) — A docked panel takes its room from the workspace instead of covering it, while at least 240 px of workspace remain.
- `badge`: ReactNode — Shown on the pill after the title: a count, a dot.
- `height`: number | string (default 440) — The container's height, in px or any CSS length.
- `label`: string (default "Workspace") — The workspace region's accessible name.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The dock and pill ghosts, the preset guides, the grip and the width readout; any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A snap when the magnet catches and when a width lands on a preset, a thock when it docks, collapses, expands or a pill lands.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Inert and dimmed: no drags, keys or buttons.
- `className`: string — Classes for the container.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the title bar is a button. Arrows nudge it with the same magnet (an arrow away from a dock lifts it off), Alt+Left and Alt+Right dock it, Alt+Up floats it, Alt+Down collapses it to the nearest bottom corner, and Enter or Space docks or floats it. Escape inside the panel collapses it and focus moves to the pill; Enter on the pill opens it and focus returns to the title bar; arrows move the pill between corners.
- The resize edge is a role="separator" with aria-valuenow in px: Left and Right step between presets (16 px when free), Home and End go to the minimum and maximum.
- Controlled: pass placement and onPlacementChange; the panel moves when the host's value changes and returns if the host refuses. Floating positions are shares of the room, so they survive the container being resized.
- With storageKey the placement and the place a pill reopens to are kept per key; a key change glides the panel to that key's place.
- Reduced motion jumps the panel to each place and cross-fades the pill and the body; drags still follow the finger and the magnet still catches.
- Give the workspace content that reflows: a docked panel narrows it on glide when reserve is on.

### Tab Strip (KQ-1283) — `tab-strip`
Open as many as you like.

A document tab strip whose tabs share one width that narrows as more open; the ones that no longer fit go into an overflow menu carrying their count, which rolls on springs.snap, and the active tab always stays in view. Every tab's slot and width are motion values on springs.glide, so a closing tab collapses while the rest are pulled left with no gap and a new tab grows out of the plus; a dragged tab lifts, leans into its speed and follows the finger 1:1 while its neighbours make room on the reorder spring. The panel cross-fades with a slide toward the side of the tab you moved to and its height glides to the new one; the tablist's arrows move and select, Shift with an arrow moves a tab, Delete closes one, and the overflow is a real menu button.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tab-strip`

Props:
- `tabs / defaultTabs`: TabStripTab[] (default defaultStripTabs) — The open tabs in order, controlled or initial: id, title, optional icon, content, dirty and pinned. defaultStripTabs is four Fernworks documents.
- `onTabsChange`: (tabs: TabStripTab[]) => void — Fires with the whole list after a close, a new tab or a reorder.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first tab's id) — The active tab's id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the press, key or menu choice that made a tab active, and when closing the active tab hands over to its neighbour.
- `onCreate`: () => TabStripTab | void (default an empty "Untitled n") — Makes the tab the plus opens; return nothing to open none.
- `onClose`: (id: string) => void — A tab was closed, by its button, Delete or the shortcut.
- `label`: string (default "Documents") — The tablist's accessible name.
- `width`: number (default 168) — How wide a tab is while there is room, in px; past that they all narrow together.
- `minWidth`: number (default 96) — Narrowest a tab gets before the ones that no longer fit go into the overflow menu, in px.
- `reorder`: "glide" | "snap" | "off" (default "glide") — How the other tabs make room for a dragged one: smoothly, with one crisp overshoot, or not at all (dragging off).
- `slide`: number (default 12) — How far the panel slides as it changes, in px, toward the side of the tab you moved to; 0 cross-fades in place.
- `maxTabs`: number (default 12) — The plus is disabled at this many open tabs.
- `closable`: boolean (default true) — Close buttons on tabs and Delete to close; pinned tabs never close.
- `shortcuts`: boolean (default false) — Ctrl or Cmd with W closes the active tab and with T opens one, where the browser passes those keys on.
- `newLabel`: string (default "New tab") — The plus button's accessible name.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Strip height 32, 36 or 40 px.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The active tab's rule and the unsaved dot; any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A click for each tab chosen (pitched by its slot) and each slot a dragged tab takes, a pop as a new tab grows and a lower one as a tab closes.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the tabs, the plus and the menu.
- `className`: string — Classes for the strip and its panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the tablist is one tab stop; Left and Right move and select (wrapping among the tabs in view), Home and End jump, Shift with an arrow moves the focused tab a slot, Delete or Backspace closes it and focus lands on the tab that takes over. The plus and the overflow menu button follow in the tab order; the menu opens on ArrowDown, Enter or Space, moves with arrows, chooses with Enter and closes on Escape with focus back on its button.
- Close buttons are siblings of their tab, never nested inside it, and are out of the tab order: Delete is the keyboard path. A tab with dirty shows a dot that turns into the close button on hover and is announced as unsaved.
- Controlled: pass tabs with onTabsChange and value with onValueChange. Closing the active tab reports the neighbour that takes over in the same press.
- The active tab is always in view: choosing a tab from the overflow menu brings it into the last slot and the tab it replaces collapses into the menu. While the menu is open the panel grows to hold it, so it never leaves the strip's box.
- Reduced motion changes places and sizes at once and cross-fades panels on opacity alone; a drag still follows the finger and drops into place.
- shortcuts only helps where the browser passes Ctrl or Cmd with W and T on (installed apps, embedded views); in an ordinary tab the browser keeps them.

### Bridge Menu (KQ-1284) — `bridge-menu`
The panel follows the pointer across.

A navigation bar with one mega-menu panel for every trigger: moving from one trigger to the next, the same panel slides across and resizes to the new content on springs.glide while that content crossfades in from the side the pointer came from, and a notch on the panel's edge and a pill behind the trigger move on springs.snap so they arrive first. A safe triangle from the last point on the open trigger to the panel's top edge (the bridge) holds the menu open while the pointer heads diagonally across other triggers, until it reaches the panel, leaves the triangle or rests, and bridge="show" draws it. The triggers are disclosure buttons in one tab stop: Left and Right move along the bar with the open panel following, Enter or Space opens, Down moves into the panel and Escape comes back to the trigger.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/bridge-menu`

Props:
- `items`: BridgeMenuItem[] (default defaultBridgeMenuItems) — The bar's items in order. An item with sections (and an optional feature card) or custom content has a panel; an item with only an href is a plain link in the bar.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default null) — The open menu's id, or null when closed, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the hover, press or key that opened, switched or closed a menu.
- `onSelect`: (link: BridgeMenuLink, itemId: string, event: React.MouseEvent) => void — A link in a panel (or a plain link in the bar) was chosen; the menu closes after it. Call event.preventDefault() to stay on the page.
- `label`: string (default "Main") — The navigation landmark's accessible name.
- `travel`: number (default 16) — How far the content slides in the direction of travel as it crossfades, in px. 0 is a plain crossfade.
- `bridge`: "off" | "on" | "show" (default "on") — The safe triangle that keeps a menu open while the pointer crosses other triggers on its way to the panel; show draws it as a translucent wedge.
- `delay`: number (default 120) — How long the pointer rests on a trigger before a closed menu opens, and inside the bridge before it gives way, in ms.
- `closeDelay`: number (default 260) — How long a menu stays open after the pointer leaves the bar and the panel, in ms.
- `align`: "center" | "start" (default "center") — The panel centred under its trigger, or starting at it; either way it is held inside the bar.
- `offset`: number (default 6) — The gap between the bar and the panel, in px.
- `notch`: boolean (default true) — Draw a notch on the panel's top edge pointing at the open trigger.
- `scrim`: boolean (default true) — Dim the page under the bar while a menu is open.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Bar height 32, 40 or 48px, with trigger text to match.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Any CSS colour for the open trigger's rule, the bridge and link icons on hover.
- `start`: React.ReactNode — Content before the triggers, such as a brand mark.
- `end`: React.ReactNode — Content at the bar's end, such as sign-in actions.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The page under the bar. With it, the panel floats over the page, its height is capped to the room there, and it never leaves the component's box.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish when a press or a key opens or closes a menu, and a tick when a key moves the panel between triggers or within it. Hover-driven changes are silent, so a pointer passing over the bar never starts audio.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the bar closed and ignores hovers, presses and keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root element.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the bar is one tab stop (Left and Right move with wrapping, Home and End jump, and while a menu is open the panel follows the focused trigger); Enter or Space toggles a menu, Down or Up opens it and moves focus to its first or last link, and Escape closes it, keeping focus on the trigger. Inside a panel, Up and Down walk the links, Left and Right move to the nearest link in the column beside, and Escape returns to the trigger.
- The panel follows its trigger in the document, so Tab from an open trigger walks straight into the panel; focus leaving the menu closes it, and focus inside a panel that is about to switch or close is moved to the trigger first so it is never dropped.
- Pass the page under the bar as children: the panel floats over it, the page dims while a menu is open, and the panel's height is capped to the room above the page's bottom, with a fade at its foot while its content scrolls.
- Under reduced motion the panel jumps to its trigger's place and size and content swaps by opacity alone; the bridge still holds, and bridge="show" still draws it.
- Touch never hovers: taps toggle menus and a tap on the page closes them. A press within 400ms of a hover opening the menu keeps it open instead of closing it.

### List Detail (KQ-1285) — `list-detail`
The row becomes the page.

A master list whose chosen row becomes the page: the row's avatar, title, subtitle and meta are measured and fly to their places in the detail header, scaling from the row's size to the header's, while the body streams in below a block at a time on springs.glide. Stacked, the row's own surface grows from its rectangle to fill the box on glide as the list fades beneath it, and Back runs the morph in reverse until the parts land on their row; side by side, the parts fly across between the panes while the previous header flies home as a ghost and a selection rule slides down the list on springs.snap, and with morph="arc" each part's x runs on snap and its y on glide so it travels a curve. The list is a listbox with one tab stop (arrows and Home or End move, Enter or Space choose), and stacked, focus moves to the detail's heading and Escape or Back returns it to the row.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/list-detail`

Props:
- `items`: ListDetailItem[] (default defaultListDetailItems) — The list in order: id, title, subtitle, meta, avatar (initials, tint, icon), badge and the detail's blocks (text, fields, list, actions). defaultListDetailItems is the seven-person Fernworks team.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default null) — The chosen item's id, or null for none, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the press, key or Back that changed the choice.
- `onAction`: (actionId: string, itemId: string) => void — An action button in the detail was pressed.
- `onLayoutChange`: (layout: "split" | "stack") => void — Fires when the layout moves between stacked and side by side, whether a resize or the split prop moved it, and once when first measured.
- `label`: string (default "People") — The list's name: its heading, the listbox's accessible name and the Back button's text.
- `morph`: "glide" | "arc" | "fade" (default "arc") — How the row's parts travel to the header: straight on glide, on a curve (x on snap, y on glide, cascaded), or not at all (a fade).
- `stream`: number (default 50) — The wait between one body block arriving and the next, in ms; the total is held under 600ms, and 0 brings the body in at once.
- `split`: "auto" | "stack" | "rail" (default "auto") — How list and detail share the box: side by side from 36rem of container width and stacked below it, always stacked, or always side by side with the list as a narrow rail of avatars (each named and titled).
- `listWidth`: number (default 280) — The list's width side by side, in px (at least 200); a rail is always 72px.
- `height`: number | string (default 480) — The component's height, in px or any CSS length; the list and the detail scroll inside it.
- `emptyLabel`: string (default "Choose someone to see their details.") — What the detail pane says side by side with nothing chosen.
- `renderDetail`: (item: ListDetailItem) => React.ReactNode — Replaces the block body with your own detail; the header still morphs.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Row height 48, 56 or 64px.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Any CSS colour for the selection rule and the chosen row's wash.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A click when a row is chosen, pitched by its place in the list, and a swish as the page opens or goes back.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Ignores choices and dims the component.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root element.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the list is a listbox with one tab stop (Up, Down, Home and End move; Enter or Space choose). Stacked, choosing moves focus to the detail's heading and Back, Escape or Alt+ArrowLeft return focus to the row once the list is live again; side by side, focus stays on the row and Escape inside the detail goes back to the chosen row. Every Escape it handles calls preventDefault.
- The static layout is container-query CSS (@container/list-detail), so the server render is already right at any width; a ResizeObserver tells the component which choreography to run and reports it through onLayoutChange. With split="rail" the list is a column of avatars at every width: the avatar flies to the header and the rest of the header fades in.
- Boxes are measured from the offset chain rather than the screen, so an interrupted flight never skews where the next one lands; a part flying home hides its row's own copy until it lands, so nothing doubles.
- Under reduced motion nothing flies or grows: the header and body fade in place in order, the list and detail cross-fade, and the selection rule jumps; the choice, focus moves and announcements are unchanged.
- A polite status region speaks each change once, frozen from the new value as it happens: "Showing Ines Okafor, Design lead." or "Back to People."

### Push Sheet (KQ-1286) — `push-sheet`
The page steps back to make room.

A bottom sheet that pushes its page back: as the sheet rises on springs.glide, the page behind scales down about its top centre, drops a few pixels, rounds its corners and dims like a card behind another in a stack, and a sheet opened from a sheet steps the one beneath it back the same way. Every layer's look is a function of how far the sheets above it have risen, so the grabber and title bar drag the top sheet 1:1 with everything behind following, rubber-banded past the top stop, and a release projects the throw to the nearest stop (half and full by default) carried on glide with its velocity, or sends the sheet away at its own speed. Each sheet is a modal dialog with focus moved in and trapped, Escape closes it and returns focus to its opener, and its grabber is a slider whose arrows move between stops.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/push-sheet`

Props:
- `sheets`: PushSheetItem[] — Every sheet that can open: id, title, description, content (a node or a function of the stack's controls) and optional snaps of its own.
- `children`: React.ReactNode | ((api: PushSheetApi) => React.ReactNode) — The page under the sheets. As a function it receives { open, close, snapTo, stack }.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The open sheets' ids, bottom first, controlled or initial (at most four).
- `onValueChange`: (stack: string[]) => void — Fires from the call, drag, key or button that opened or closed a sheet, with the new stack.
- `onSnapChange`: (id: string, snap: number) => void — A sheet came to rest on a stop after a drag, a key or snapTo, given as a share of its full height.
- `push`: number (default 0.6) — How far a covered layer steps back, 0 to 1: 0 only dims it; 1 shrinks it 6% per level, drops it 16px and rounds it fully.
- `snaps`: "half-full" | "full" | "thirds" | number[] (default "half-full") — Where a sheet stops: half and full height, full only, thirds, or your own shares of the full height.
- `dim`: number (default 0.35) — How dark a fully covered layer gets, 0 to 0.8; a second level darkens it by half again.
- `openAt`: "lowest" | "highest" (default "lowest") — Where a new sheet comes to rest.
- `inset`: number (default 28) — The gap above a sheet at full height, in px, where the layer behind peeks out.
- `width`: number (default 560) — A sheet's widest, in px; it is centred when the box is wider.
- `radius`: number (default 16) — The sheets' top corners and the pushed page's corners, in px.
- `dismissible`: boolean (default true) — Whether a drag down, Escape, a press on the page behind and ArrowDown at the lowest stop close the top sheet.
- `height`: number | string (default 520) — The box's height, in px or any CSS length; everything stays inside it.
- `backdrop`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--background) 45%, black)") — Any CSS colour shown behind the pushed page.
- `closeLabel`: string (default "Close") — The close button's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish as a sheet opens or is sent away, and a thock when it lands on a stop, louder for a harder throw and lower for a higher stop.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Ignores opens, drags and keys and dims the box.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root element.

Notes:
- Keyboard: each sheet is a modal dialog. Focus moves to its first control when it arrives, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the top sheet, Escape closes it (calling preventDefault) and focus returns to whatever opened it. The grabber is a vertical slider: Up and Page Up go to the next stop, Down and Page Down to the one below (from the lowest it closes the sheet when dismissible), Home and End jump, and Enter or Space toggle between the lowest and highest stops.
- Open and close sheets from inside the page or a sheet with the function form of children and content: (api) => <button onClick={() => api.open("send")} />. api.close(id) closes that sheet and everything above it.
- Focus reaching a control below a sheet's fold raises the sheet to its top stop, so a focused control is always on screen; the body also keeps room under its end equal to what is below the box, so its last line can always be scrolled into view.
- Under reduced motion sheets fade in at their stop and fade out, stops change on a short tween, and the page neither scales nor moves, but it still dims and rounds its corners, because what is covered is information.
- Controlled: a drag that sends a sheet away springs it back to its stop while asking the host; if the host takes the close, the exit carries on from there, and if it refuses, the sheet simply stays.

### Search Expand (KQ-1287) — `search-expand`
The search makes its own room.

An app header whose search icon grows into a field on the glide spring while the bar gives way to it frame by frame: the nav items nearest the field squeeze to their icons, then tuck into a More button that grows in with the first and squeezes on flick and snap as each lands, and the brand name steps aside before the last item goes — one motion value drives it all, and both rest states are rounded to whole items. The results panel then grows down out of the field itself on glide, its shell easing from a pill to a card with the matches rising in a cascade and a highlight that moves on snap, and Escape, a choice or blur unwinds it in reverse: the panel retracts on the exit ease before the field narrows and the items come back. The field is a combobox that `/` opens from anywhere, arrows move through results and Enter chooses; More is a menu button whose menu holds whatever is tucked.

- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the bar and disables the search, the nav and the shortcut.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root (a container-query box holding the bar and the page).

Notes:

Tab leaving the field closes it too, except into More and its menu.
