### Zoom Timeline (KQ-1288) — `zoom-timeline`
Years to minutes in one scroll.

A horizontal timeline with semantic zoom from years to minutes: Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel zooms about the pointer on the flick spring, a pinch zooms 1:1 about the fingers, and + and - step on glide, while each tick label fades in as the room around it grows (quarters before months, Mondays before days, every third hour before every hour) and the unit above becomes a row of context labels pinned to the left edge. Markers closer than the cluster radius merge into counted bubbles, and each member springs in and out on snap as you zoom, so a bubble visibly splits into its events; dragging pans 1:1 with rubber-banded ends, and a throw coasts on a critically damped spring whose time constant is the projection's, carrying the release velocity. Markers are one roving list: arrows step and pan to keep them in view, Enter selects an event or opens a bubble, Page Up and Page Down pan a screen.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/zoom-timeline`

Props:
- `events`: ZoomTimelineEvent[] (default defaultTimelineEvents) — The events to place: id, at (ms, an ISO string or a Date), title, detail and tone (default, success, warn or danger).
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default null) — The selected event. Its marker fills on flick and the readout row cross-fades to its title, time and detail.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the press or key that selected an event, or cleared it (Escape) with null.
- `onViewChange`: (view: ZoomTimelineView) => void — The view once a gesture, step or coast settles: start and end in ms, the axis unit, and how many events and bubbles are in view.
- `defaultCenter`: number | string | Date (default the middle of the events) — Where the view opens.
- `defaultUnit`: "year" | "month" | "day" | "hour" | "minute" (default the ladder's second unit) — The unit the view opens on.
- `levels`: "years-minutes" | "years-days" | "months-hours" | "days-minutes" (default "years-minutes") — The zoom ladder: how far out and in the view can go. Changing it re-frames the view on its opening unit.
- `cluster`: number (default 28) — How close markers get, in px, before they merge into a counted bubble (with 10% hysteresis); 0 never merges.
- `momentum`: number (default 0.6) — How far a throw coasts, 0 to 1: 0 stops almost under the finger, 1 glides a long way.
- `now`: number | string | Date — Draws a now line there. Passed in, never read from the clock, so the server and the browser agree.
- `utcOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes added to UTC for every label and readout, e.g. 60 for UTC+1.
- `label`: string (default "Timeline") — The timeline's accessible name.
- `formatTime`: (ms: number, unit: ZoomTimelineUnit) => string (default "14 Mar 2026 14:20") — The readout's and every accessible name's time; the default drops the time at midnight.
- `zoomControls`: boolean (default true) — Show the zoom out, unit and zoom in controls in the readout row.
- `height`: number (default 200) — Total height in px: a 36px readout row, the marker lane and a 52px axis with its context row.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Selection, bubbles and the now line. Any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick each time the axis changes unit during a visitor's zoom and softly as arrow keys step, and a whoosh for a fast throw or a zoom step. Nothing plays on its own.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the timeline and stops every gesture and control.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root (a rounded, clipped container-query box).

Notes:
- Keyboard: the markers (free events and bubbles, in time order) are one tab stop; Left and Right step between them and glide the view to keep them in sight, Home and End jump, + and - zoom about the focused marker, Enter or Space selects an event or opens a bubble (focus follows its first member once it has split out), Page Up and Page Down pan a screen, and Escape clears a selection with preventDefault.
- Only Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel (and a trackpad pinch) zooms, and a horizontal or Shift wheel pans; a plain vertical wheel is left to the page. The viewport is touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page while a horizontal one pans and two fingers pinch.
- Times are UTC (plus utcOffset) and labels are formatted by hand, never from the locale, so the server render and the hydrated page match; the server lays out the axis for 1600px and the browser corrects it once measured.
- Under reduced motion steps and pans jump, a throw stops under the finger and bubbles swap in place; labels still cross-fade by spacing because which labels are legible is information.
- Every per-frame value — ticks, labels, markers, bubbles — is a motion value; React re-renders only when a bubble forms or splits or the axis changes unit, and nothing runs while the view is still.

### Snap Board (KQ-1289) — `snap-board`
Drag a widget; the others make way.

A dashboard layout editor on a grid of columns and rows: a widget dragged by its header lifts on the flick spring and follows the finger 1:1, rubber-banding past the board's edges, and each time the cell under it changes a detent clicks, the ghost moves to the landing cell on snap and every widget in the way glides aside on glide. Let go, it flies to the ghost with the throw's own velocity and lands with a thock, and the layout is reported once; the corner resizes the same way, and push decides whether the others float back up, stay where they land or trade places. Every grip is a button: Space or Enter picks a widget up, arrows move it a cell (the widget snapping along with its ghost), Shift and arrows resize it, Enter drops and Escape puts everything back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/snap-board`

Props:
- `widgets`: SnapBoardWidget[] (default defaultBoardWidgets) — The widgets on the board: id, title, icon, content, and min and max size in cells. Content sits in a container-query box so it can lay itself out for the size it is given.
- `layout / defaultLayout`: SnapBoardItem[] (default defaultBoardLayout(columns)) — One item per widget: id, x and y of its top-left cell, w and h in cells. Anything wider than the columns or overlapping is clamped and settled.
- `onLayoutChange`: (layout: SnapBoardItem[]) => void — Fires from the drop, resize or key that changed the layout, with all of it. A drop that changes nothing is not reported.
- `onMove`: (id: string, moved: string[]) => void — A drop that changed the layout: the widget dropped and the ids of the others that made way.
- `onDragChange`: (drag: SnapBoardDrag | null) => void — A widget picked up by pointer or key, its landing cell (id, mode and item) each time it changes, and null when it is put down.
- `columns`: number (default 12) — The grid's columns. Column guides fade in under the widgets while one is held.
- `push`: "compact" | "free" | "swap" (default "compact") — How the others make way: pushed and floated back up into any gap, pushed and left where they land, or the widget under the drop trades places with the dragged one.
- `ghost`: "outline" | "tint" | "none" (default "outline") — The landing preview: a dashed accent outline, an accent wash with a solid edge, or nothing but the others making way.
- `rowHeight`: number (default 44) — One row's height, px.
- `gap`: number (default 8) — The space between cells, px.
- `maxHeight`: number | string — The tallest the board gets before it scrolls inside itself, px or any CSS length.
- `editable`: boolean (default true) — Off: no grips and no corners, a plain dashboard.
- `label`: string (default "Dashboard layout") — The board's accessible name.
- `moveLabel`: (title: string) => string (default (title) => `Move ${title}`) — Each grip's accessible name.
- `resizeLabel`: (title: string) => string (default (title) => `Resize ${title}`) — Each corner's accessible name.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The ghost, the picked-up ring, the column guides and the default widgets' charts. Any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A detent click at every cell the target crosses and a thock on every drop (louder for a longer flight). Nothing sounds when the host changes the layout.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the board and stops every drag, resize and key.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root (the labelled region that clips the board).

Notes:
- Keyboard: each widget's grip is a button (aria-pressed while held). Space or Enter picks it up; arrow keys move it a cell and the widget snaps along with its ghost while the others make way; Shift with arrows resizes (the corner button picks up in resize mode); Enter or Space drops; Escape puts everything back with preventDefault; Tab or blur drops it where it is. Each step is spoken once in a polite live region.
- A drag is tracked in the board's own frame, so the widget stays under the finger even if the board grows or the page scrolls; only the header and the corner are touch-none, so the widget bodies still scroll the page.
- With push="compact" a widget dragged down onto another by that one's height hops it above, so any order is reachable; "free" leaves gaps where you leave them; "swap" trades places with the widget under the drop when it fits.
- Under reduced motion nothing lifts, flies or glides: widgets and the ghost jump to their cells (the dragged one still follows the finger), the board's height jumps; the layout and every announcement are unchanged.
- Before the board is measured (and on the server) widgets are placed with the same geometry as CSS percentages, so the first paint is already the final layout.

### Collapse Header (KQ-1290) — `collapse-header`
The title docks as you scroll.

A scroll container with a large header whose title is one heading floating over the page: as you scroll it moves 1:1 with the page toward the toolbar, easing across to its docked place beside the back button (or centred) and down to toolbar size, while the cover parallaxes and fades behind it and the actions fold into the overflow button as they slide up to meet the bar. Past the threshold the title lets go of the scroll and docks by itself on the snap spring; docked, the header stays compact however you scroll until you come back to the very top, where it re-expands on glide. The scroll area is a focusable region, so arrow, Page, Home and End keys reach the same states, and the overflow button is a menu button whose menu holds the folded actions.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/collapse-header`

Props:
- `title`: string (default "Basin Road survey") — The heading that docks in the toolbar. Large it may wrap to two lines; docked it is always one clean line.
- `subtitle`: string — The line under the title; it scrolls away with the page.
- `eyebrow`: string — A small label above the title.
- `cover`: React.ReactNode (default a procedural ridge drawing) — Fills the cover; the default is drawn in the accent and mixed toward the page, so it reads in both themes.
- `actions`: CollapseHeaderAction[] (default defaultHeaderActions) — The row of actions under the title (id, label, icon); they fold into the overflow menu as they reach the toolbar.
- `onAction`: (id: string) => void — An action pressed, inline or from the overflow menu.
- `onBack`: () => void — The back button. Without it the button is still drawn, for the docked title to sit beside.
- `backLabel`: string (default "Back") — The back button's accessible name.
- `overflowLabel`: string (default "More actions") — The overflow button's and its menu's accessible name.
- `onDockChange`: (docked: boolean) => void — Fires from the scroll that docked the title (true) or re-expanded the header at the top (false).
- `parallax`: number (default 0.5) — How much slower than the page the cover moves, 0 to 1: 0 scrolls with the page, 1 stays put behind it.
- `dock`: "start" | "center" (default "start") — Where the title docks in the toolbar: beside the back button, or centred.
- `threshold`: number (default 0.6) — How far through its travel (0.3 to 1) the title lets go of the scroll and docks by itself on the snap spring; 1 never lets go early.
- `coverHeight`: number (default 168) — The cover's height in px; a fifth taller when the header is 560px wide or more.
- `height`: number | string (default 520) — The container's height, px or any CSS length. It scrolls inside itself.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The large title: 24, 28 or 34 px. It docks at 17 px.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The cover drawing and the docked toolbar's rule. Any CSS colour.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The page under the header.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish as the visitor's scroll docks the title (higher) and as it re-expands the header at the top (lower). Nothing else plays.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root (a rounded, clipped container-query box that carries data-state="expanded" or "docked").

Notes:
- The scroll area is a focusable region labelled by the title: arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, Space, Home and End scroll it, so docking (scroll down) and re-expanding (Home) have the same keyboard path as a finger. The toolbar comes first in the DOM, so Tab meets the back button before the page.
- The overflow button is inert until the actions have folded into it; it is a menu button (Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it) whose items move with arrows, Home and End, and Escape or Tab close it with focus back on the button. Focus on an action that folds moves to the overflow button, and back to the first action when they unfold.
- There is one h2 throughout: the floating title is the heading, and the one-line docked copy inside it is aria-hidden. A polite live region says "Title docked" and "Header expanded" once per change.
- Under reduced motion nothing flies or parallaxes: the title scrolls with the page and a docked copy cross-fades into the toolbar when the threshold is passed, the actions cross-fade as the overflow button fades in, and the cover only fades.
- Every per-frame value is a motion value read from the scroll; React hears only when the title docks or re-expands and when the actions finish folding, and nothing runs while the page is still.

### Answer Panel (KQ-1291) — `answer-panel`
Read it while it is still being written.

An AI answer you can read while it is written: thoughts arrive one at a time on snap, then the answer streams token by token behind a caret, its numbered citation pills scaling in on snap where each claim is made and lifting their source card on snap when hovered or focused. When the text is done the Thinking block collapses on glide into a one-line summary, the actions and follow-ups rise in a cascade, a pressed thumb lands on recoil, and Regenerate rewinds the text on the move ease before writing again. Tab reaches every pill, thumb and follow-up; focusing a pill opens its card, Enter opens the source and Escape closes the card.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/answer-panel`

Props:
- `question`: string (default defaultQuestion) — What was asked; names the panel.
- `answer`: string (default defaultAnswer) — The answer. Blank lines split paragraphs, "- " starts a bullet, and [n] cites sources[n - 1].
- `sources`: AnswerSource[] (default defaultSources) — The sources the answer can cite, in citation order: title, site, snippet, meta.
- `thoughts`: AnswerThought[] (default defaultThoughts) — The steps taken before writing, each with its duration in ms.
- `suggestions`: string[] (default defaultSuggestions) — Follow-up questions offered once the answer is done.
- `model`: string (default "Fernworks Model 3") — The model that wrote it, printed in the action row.
- `status / defaultStatus`: "thinking" | "streaming" | "done" | "error" (default — / "thinking") — The lifecycle. Controlled, the panel asks for the next status and waits for the host.
- `onStatusChange`: (status: AnswerStatus) => void — Fires when the panel moves on: thinking finished, text finished, or Regenerate pressed.
- `speed`: number (default 32) — Tokens per second the answer is written at; thoughts hold longer when it is slow.
- `citations`: "pill" | "number" | "none" (default "pill") — Citation markers as numbered pills, bare superscript numbers, or not at all.
- `followups`: "list" | "chips" | "none" (default "list") — Follow-ups as full-width rows, wrapping chips, or not at all.
- `feedback / defaultFeedback`: "up" | "down" | null (default — / null) — The visitor's rating of the answer.
- `onFeedbackChange`: (feedback: AnswerFeedback) => void — Fires from the thumb that changed it, and with null when Regenerate clears it.
- `onFeedbackReason`: (reason: string) => void — The reason picked after Not helpful.
- `reasons`: string[] (default ["Inaccurate", "Out of date", "Missed the question", "Too long"]) — Reasons offered after Not helpful.
- `onRegenerate`: () => void — Regenerate or Retry was pressed. Swap `answer` here; the old text rewinds first.
- `onFollowup`: (text: string) => void — A follow-up was chosen.
- `onSourceOpen`: (source: AnswerSource) => void — A citation or a listed source was opened.
- `onCopy`: (text: string) => void — Copy was pressed, with the plain text sent to the clipboard (markers out, sources listed after).
- `errorMessage`: string (default "The answer stopped partway.") — What the error line says.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the thumbs, the copy, the disclosure and the rewind. The stream itself is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the actions, feedback and follow-ups; the answer still reads.
- `className`: string — Give the panel a height (h-[32rem]) and its body scrolls inside it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the Thinking disclosure, each citation pill, the actions, thumbs, reasons and follow-ups. Focusing a pill opens its source card (described by it); Enter opens the source, Escape closes the card.
- Drive it live by controlling `status` and appending to `answer` as chunks arrive: the panel paces bursty chunks into a steady stream, and setting `status="done"` flushes the rest quickly. Uncontrolled, it plays `thoughts` and `answer` by itself.
- The body follows the caret only while the reader is at the bottom; scrolling up keeps their place and shows a Jump to latest pill.
- Reduced motion: tokens still arrive (without fades), the caret does not blink, cards and pills appear on opacity, lists open at once and Regenerate clears instantly before re-streaming.
- Pacing runs on requestAnimationFrame only while the panel is on screen and the page is visible; a polite status announces each phase once, never per token.

### Agent Run (KQ-1292) — `agent-run`
Watch the plan; approve the risky step.

An agent's run watched as it happens: steps move from pending to running to done or failed with live durations, nodes filling and ticking on flick, tool calls opening to a measured height on glide, and a time and cost meter whose digits run with the clock. A risky step halts the run behind an inline gate that glides open; holding Approve sweeps a linear fill, drains on the exit ease if let go early, and lands on recoil before the gate folds into a stamp. The timeline scrubs 1:1 and rubber-bands against its ends and any undecided gate, springing back on glide; arrow keys move the playhead and the plan, Space or Enter held approves.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/agent-run`

Props:
- `run`: AgentRunData (default defaultRun) — The run log: title, agent, model, budget in cents, and each step's title, tool, ms, cost, input, output, error and gate.
- `now`: number — Controlled clock in ms since the run started. The host owns time; scrubs and Replay ask through onNowChange.
- `defaultNow`: number (default 0) — Where the console's own clock starts.
- `onNowChange`: (ms: number) => void — A scrub, a seek, a key or Replay asked for a new time.
- `playing / defaultPlaying`: boolean (default — / true) — Whether the console's own clock runs. It also pauses by itself off screen and in a hidden tab.
- `onPlayingChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Play, Pause, Replay or the run reaching its end.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the console's clock runs, as a multiple of real time.
- `detail`: "compact" | "standard" | "full" (default "standard") — Titles only, a one-line call under each step, or every call opened.
- `approval`: "hold" | "click" | "auto" (default "hold") — Approve a gated step with a press and hold, a plain click, or let policy approve it without pausing.
- `holdMs`: number (default 700) — How long the approve button has to be held.
- `onDecision`: (stepId: string, decision: "approved" | "denied") => void — A gated step was approved or denied.
- `onStateChange`: (state: AgentRunState, step: AgentStep | null) => void — The run moved on (running, paused, waiting, finished, failed, stopped) from its own clock, a scrub, a decision or play and pause.
- `onReplay`: () => void — Replay was pressed: decisions clear and the clock rewinds to zero.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the run log is there yet: skeleton rows while loading, a Retry when it failed, and an empty plan says so.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry on the error state.
- `formatCost`: (cents: number) => string (default Intl US dollars) — How a cost in cents is shown in the meter and the log.
- `label`: string (default run.title) — The console's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the approval chime, scrub ticks and control clicks. The run playing on its own is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the controls, the gate and the timeline.
- `className`: string — Give the console a height (h-[34rem]) and the plan scrolls inside it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the plan is one tab stop; Up and Down move between steps, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens a step's call. The approve button charges while Space or Enter is held; assistive technology that clicks it gets a 'Press again' confirm instead.
- The timeline is a slider: arrows move the playhead a second, Shift with an arrow jumps step to step, Page keys five seconds, Home and End to the start and to the furthest point the run can reach.
- Drive it live by passing `now` (ms since start) and appending steps to `run`; a gated step with no decision holds the run until onDecision answers. Uncontrolled, it replays the log on its own clock.
- Reduced motion: the clock still runs and every state still changes; nothing spins, panels open at once, seeks and Replay jump, and the hold still fills because the fill is the feedback.
- Only step boundaries re-render: durations, meters and the playhead are motion values. The plan and the activity log scroll their own boxes, never the page.

### Prompt Dock (KQ-1293) — `prompt-dock`
Everything you need, around the box you type in.

A prompt box with its context around it: a tray of pinned files and snippets that collapses into a count as each chip's icon flies into a stack on glide, files dropped on the dock flying from the drop point into the tray (x on glide, y on snap, so the path bows), and an @ menu whose chosen row flies in the same way. A model pill opens in place into every model with a highlight sliding on snap, the token meter fills and warms toward the limit and bumps on recoil as it crosses 90% and the limit, and Send's arrow folds into a stop square on snap while a reply is written. The box is a real textarea and combobox: arrows walk the @ menu, Enter or Tab attaches, Escape closes it or stops a reply, and Backspace in an empty box removes the last chip.

- `models`: DockModel[] (default defaultModels) — The models the pill switches between: id, name, short name, note.

- `tray`: "open" | "count" | "auto" (default "open") — The tray starts open, starts collapsed into a count, or collapses itself while there is text in the box.
- `limit`: number (default 8000) — The context budget in tokens: the meter warms toward it and Send stops past it.
- `generating / defaultGenerating`: boolean (default — / false) — A reply is being written, so Send is Stop. Uncontrolled, Send turns it on and Stop off.
- `onGeneratingChange`: (generating: boolean) => void — Send or Stop changed it.

- `onStop`: () => void — Stop was pressed, or Escape while a reply is written.
- `onFilesAdd`: (files: File[]) => void — Files dropped on the dock or picked with Attach.
- `accept`: string — File types the Attach picker offers, as for an input's accept.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Ask anything, or type @ to add context") — The empty box's hint.
- `maxRows`: number (default 6) — How many lines the box grows to before it scrolls.
- `label`: string (default "Prompt") — The dock's and the box's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the chip landings, the switches, Stop and the send.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the box, the tray, the picker and Send.
- `className`: string — Classes for the dock's outer box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: type @ (or press the @ button) to open the menu; Up and Down move, Enter or Tab attaches, Escape closes. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, Escape stops a reply, and Backspace in an empty box removes the last chip.

- Drops and Attach report the raw files through onFilesAdd and add a chip each, with tokens estimated from size; give `context` and `onContextChange` to own the list.
- Reduced motion: nothing flies or slides; chips appear in their slots, the model label swaps, the send icon changes at once, nothing spins, and the token meter still fills and warms.
- The dock's height is measured and glides; every flyer flies inside the dock's own box.

### Thread View (KQ-1294) — `thread-view`
A conversation you can branch.

A complete assistant thread over a tree of messages: runs from one author share an avatar, each message's toolbar rises into place on snap, copy morphs into a check on flick and a reaction lands on recoil. Editing a sent message forks the thread, and the version switcher slides the message and every reply under it — the old branch out on the exit ease, the new one in on glide — while its counter rolls on snap and the edited bubble's measured height glides. Scrolled up, a pill counts the replies that land and glides the log to the newest on glide; End does the same, Enter sends or saves, Shift+Enter breaks a line and Escape cancels an edit.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/thread-view`

Props:
- `messages / defaultMessages`: ThreadMessage[] (default defaultThreadMessages) — Every version of every turn as one flat list: messages that share a parentId are versions of one turn. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onMessagesChange`: (messages: ThreadMessage[]) => void — Fires from the send, edit or reaction that changed the list, with the whole new list.
- `leaf / defaultLeaf`: string — Any message on the branch to show. The thread runs from the first turn through it, then on down the newest replies. Defaults to the newest version of every turn.
- `onLeafChange`: (leaf: string) => void — Fires when a version switch, a send or an edit moves the visible branch.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — How tightly the thread is set: type size, bubble padding, avatar size and the gap between runs.
- `branches`: boolean (default true) — Edits keep every version, with a switcher to move between them. Off: the data still forks, but an edit reads as a replacement.
- `toolbar`: "hover" | "always" | "off" (default "hover") — Each message's actions: a pill on hover, focus or tap, a row always shown, or none for a read-only transcript.
- `onSend`: (text: string, message: ThreadMessage) => void — A message was sent from the composer. It is already in the list; stream the reply in as a child of message.id.
- `onEdit`: (original: ThreadMessage, version: ThreadMessage) => void — A message was edited: version is the new sibling of original and the branch now shows it.
- `onCopy`: (text: string, messageId: string) => void — A message or one of its code blocks was copied to the clipboard.
- `onReact`: (messageId: string, reaction: "up" | "down" | null) => void — A reply was marked good or bad, or the mark was cleared.
- `onRetry`: (messageId: string) => void — Retry was pressed on a reply whose status is "error".
- `onReload`: () => void — Try again was pressed while status is "error".
- `now`: number | Date — The moment relative times count from. Defaults to the newest message's time, so the thread renders the same on the server and in the browser.
- `author`: string — The name new messages are sent under. Defaults to the newest user message's author, else "You".
- `title`: string (default "Basin export retries") — The thread's name in the header; also its accessible name unless label is given.
- `model`: string (default "Fernworks Model 3") — The model answering, shown in the header and the composer's placeholder.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the thread's data has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.
- `composer`: boolean (default true) — Show the composer: a textarea that grows to five lines, Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.
- `placeholder`: string — The composer's placeholder. Defaults to "Message" and the model's name.
- `suggestions`: string[] — Prompts offered while the thread is empty; pressing one fills the composer.
- `label`: string — The thread's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A pop for a send, a saved edit or a reaction; a tick for a version switch, a copy and the jump to the latest.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be sent, edited or reacted to.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab reaches each message's tools (the hover pill shows while focus is inside), Enter on Edit opens the editor, Enter saves and Escape cancels with focus back on Edit; the version switcher's Previous and Next say which version is shown; End in the focused log glides to the newest message.
- Streaming is the host's: append an assistant message with status "streaming", grow its text as tokens arrive and clear the status when done. The log stays on its floor while you are there, and the live region announces each finished reply once, never per token.
- Under reduced motion nothing travels: version swaps, arrivals, the toolbar and the pill cross-fade, the jump to the latest is instant and the caret holds still, while counts, checks and reactions still show.
- Lays out by its own width: a phone layout below 30rem (tools on tap, wider bubbles), and from 60rem a rail listing the visible turns, with fork counts, that glides the log to each one.
- Times are relative to now, never the clock, and new messages are stamped after the newest one — pass at yourself through onMessagesChange if you need wall-clock times.

### Usage Ledger (KQ-1295) — `usage-ledger`
Where the tokens went.

An AI usage panel built from daily records: each day is a column stacked by model, by kind or as one total that grows up from the baseline on glide, the whole period sweeping in inside 360ms, while the month's spend sweeps round a budget gauge on drift toward its projected month end. The daily alert is a line you drag: it follows the finger 1:1 with a magnetic pull onto round numbers, rubber-bands past the plot, re-colours every day above it to warn as it passes, and springs onto its value on snap with the release velocity. The plot is a slider over the days (arrows step, Home and End jump, Enter selects), the line's grip a slider over the threshold (arrows one step, Page keys four), and the period a radio group.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/usage-ledger`
