- `onThresholdChange`: (threshold: number) => void — Fires from the drag or key that moved the line, once for each round value it lands on.
- `stack`: "model" | "kind" | "total" (default "model") — What each day's column is split by: each model, input / output / cached, or one total. The legend follows.
- `range / defaultRange`: "7d" | "30d" | "90d" (default "30d") — The period shown: the last 7, 30 or 90 days up to now. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onRangeChange`: (range: "7d" | "30d" | "90d") => void — Fires from the period control with the new period.
- `thresholdStep`: number — The round number the line snaps to. Defaults to a nice twelfth of the axis (250k on a 3M axis).
- `models`: UsageModel[] (default defaultUsageModels) — The models billed: id, name, an optional colour, and a price per million input, output and cached tokens.
- `days`: UsageDay[] (default defaultUsageDays) — One record per day (date as YYYY-MM-DD), with tokens per model id. The default is ninety seeded days.
- `now`: number | Date — Today: where the period ends and the month's spend is counted to. Defaults to the last day in days.
- `budget`: number (default 330) — The monthly budget. The gauge shows the month's spend against it and where the month is heading.
- `onDaySelect`: (date: string) => void — Enter on the focused day, or a click on a column.
- `format`: (amount: number) => string — Money in the gauge and its caption. Defaults to US dollars in locale.
- `formatTokens`: (tokens: number) => string — Token counts on the axis, the grip, the readouts and the legend. Defaults to compact: 820k, 1.5M.
- `formatDate`: (date: string) => string — Day labels from a YYYY-MM-DD date. Defaults to "Sep 14".
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The locale of the default money format. Fixed, so the server and the browser print the same.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the usage has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed while status is "error".
- `title`: string (default "Usage") — The panel's heading; also its accessible name unless label is given.
- `label`: string — The panel's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A detent for each round value the line lands on, pitched by height; a tick for each day the keyboard steps and for a period change.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: the line, the days and the period cannot be moved.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall and scrolls inside itself; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the plot is a slider over the days — Left and Right step a day, Page keys a week, Home and End jump, Enter fires onDaySelect, Escape clears the readout; the alert grip is a vertical slider — Up and Down one round step, Page keys four, Home and End the ends; the period is a radio group on the arrow keys.
- The threshold reports once per round value it lands on, from the drag or key that moved it. A controlled host that refuses a value sees the line spring back to its own value on release.
- Under reduced motion the columns, the gauge and the sparklines appear drawn, and the line follows the finger without springs or rubber-band; it still snaps, and the days still change colour, because that is the information.
- Lays out by its own width: one column on a phone (scrolling inside its box), the gauge beside the chart from 40rem, and the legend as a third column from 68rem.
- Bars are pigment: each series takes a token's hue at a fixed lightness, so a model reads the same colour in light and dark. Pass a model colour as a CSS colour string to override it.

### Side by Side (KQ-1296) — `side-by-side`
Two models, one prompt, you decide.

Two models answer one prompt in parallel columns, each streaming at its own pace — its time to first token, then its token rate, scaled by speed — with a live clock, a progress hairline and a Done stamp that lands on flick. Once both finish, a highlighter sweeps across what each says that the other does not, in reading order within 600ms, and the stats tally beneath them with bars that grow on glide. The vote puck drags 1:1, rubber-bands past the ends and settles on snap at the stop the throw was heading for, the preferred column takes its hue as a badge lands on recoil, and the reason you pick moves into the summary on glide; the stops are a radio group on the arrow keys, and on a phone the answers become two tabs.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/side-by-side`

Props:
- `speed`: number (default 1) — Playback speed of both streams as a multiple of real time. The clocks and stats still read in the models' real time.
- `diff`: "phrases" | "sentences" | "off" (default "phrases") — What is marked once both finish: runs of two or more words the other answer never uses, whole sentences with under half their words in common, or nothing.
- `vote`: "pick" | "scale" (default "pick") — The vote bar: three stops (A better, tie, B better), or five with much better at each end.
- `prompt`: string (default defaultComparisonPrompt) — The prompt both models answered, shown above the columns.
- `answers`: [ComparisonAnswer, ComparisonAnswer] (default defaultComparisonAnswers) — The two answers: id, model, text, latencyMs and tokensPerSecond. Set an answer's status to drive its column yourself as text arrives; leave it unset and the column plays the text in at its own pace.
- `autoPlay`: boolean (default true) — Start streaming when the surface first scrolls into view. Off: both answers show complete, with their marks.
- `value / defaultValue`: ComparisonVote | null (default null) — The vote: choice ("a", "b" or "tie"), margin (1 or 2) and an optional reason. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (vote: ComparisonVote | null) => void — Fires from the drag, key or press that changed the vote or its reason.
- `reasons`: string[] — Why a winner won, offered after a vote for a side. Defaults to More accurate, Clearer, More concise, Safer advice.
- `onRerun`: () => void — Run again was pressed: both streams replay from the start and an uncontrolled vote clears.
- `onRetry`: (answerId: string) => void — Retry was pressed on a column whose answer has status "error".
- `onFinish`: (answerId: string, stats: ComparisonStats) => void — A column finished playing, with its first-token time, total time, token count and rate.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the run has data yet: skeleton columns while loading, a message with Run again on error.
- `labels`: { a: string; b: string } (default { a: "A", b: "B" }) — The two columns' short names, used on their badges, the stats and the vote stops.
- `label`: string (default "Model comparison") — The surface's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for each stop the puck crosses and each reason picked; a chime when a vote lands, pitched by side.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: no vote, no reason, no re-run.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the vote stops are a radio group — Left and Right move and vote, Home and End jump — enabled once both answers finish; reason chips are a second radio group; each answer's text box is focusable and scrolls with the arrow keys; on a phone the two answers are tabs on the arrow keys.
- The live region speaks each column's finish once and the number of marked differences once, never per token.
- Under reduced motion the text still streams (it is the data) but without the per-token fade, the highlights appear without the sweep, and the puck follows the finger without springs or rubber-band; the vote, the badge and the reason still land.
- Lays out by its own width: two tabs over one answer below 30rem (the whole surface scrolls), two columns with the stats and the vote beneath from 30rem, and a third column holding the stats and the vote from 64rem.
- Playback runs only while the surface is in view and the page is visible, and the clock carries on from where it stood when it resumes.

### Artifact Pane (KQ-1297) — `artifact-pane`
The thing it made, beside the chat.

A generated file beside the conversation that made it. Switching versions applies the diff in place: shared lines keep their element, dropped lines are struck and fold away on the exit ease, and new lines open on glide under a wash that sweeps across them in a cascade, on the Preview block by block and on the Code tab line by line, while the change count rolls on snap and the Preview / Code panels slide 16px on glide. Dock folds the pane into a chip in the thread: a ghost of its frame flies into the chip on glide, homing on its live box while the pane's column closes, and lands on recoil; the tabs and version pills take arrow keys, and Escape anywhere in the pane docks it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/artifact-pane`

Props:
- `versions`: "pills" | "stepper" | "timeline" (default "pills") — How the version history is offered: a segmented control whose indicator slides on snap, Previous and Next around a rolling readout, or a strip of dots under the header whose rail fills on glide.
- `diff`: "flash" | "hold" | "off" (default "flash") — What a version switch shows: marks that flash and fold away, marks that stay (with a Changes toggle) until cleared, or a plain swap.
- `dock`: "inline" | "pinned" (default "inline") — Where the docked pane lands: as a card inside the message that made the shown version, or on a bar pinned to the foot of the conversation.
- `artifact`: Artifact (default defaultArtifact) — The file and every version of it, oldest first: title, filename, kind ("document" renders its Markdown, "code" shows a preview node when a version has one) and versions with summary, time and source.
- `conversation`: ArtifactTurn[] (default defaultArtifactConversation) — The turns beside it. An assistant turn with a version id carries a chip that opens that version.
- `version / defaultVersion`: string (default the newest version) — The shown version's id. Uncontrolled, an appended version is followed when the reader was on the newest one.
- `onVersionChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the control, chip or arrow key that chose another version.
- `tab / defaultTab`: "preview" | "code" (default "preview") — The shown view. A code artifact whose version has no preview shows Code only.
- `onTabChange`: (tab: "preview" | "code") => void — Fires from the tab or arrow key that switched the view.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default true) — Whether the pane is open beside the conversation or docked into it as a chip. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host change flies the same way a press does.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the Dock button, the chip, a version chip or Escape, with the new state.
- `status`: "ready" | "writing" | "error" (default "ready") — A new version is being written (a badge, a running hairline and a typing row in the thread), or the last revision failed (a strip with Retry).
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after a failed revision.
- `onCopy`: (text: string, version: ArtifactVersion) => void — The shown version's source was copied to the clipboard.
- `onDownload`: (file: ArtifactFile) => void | false — The shown version is being saved, as { name, text, type }. Return false to save it yourself; otherwise the pane saves it through the browser.
- `now`: number | Date (default the newest version's time) — The moment relative times count from, so the surface renders the same on the server and in the browser.
- `label`: string — The surface's accessible name. Defaults to the artifact's title and "the conversation".
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish when the visitor docks or opens the pane, a click on copy, download, tabs and versions.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: versions, tabs, copy, download and dock do nothing; the panels still scroll.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the version chips, Copy, Download, Dock, the tabs and the version control; Left and Right (or Home and End) move the tabs and the version pills or dots with selection following focus; Escape anywhere in the pane docks it, and focus lands on the chip, then back on Dock when the chip opens it.
- Versions are whole sources: the pane computes a line diff between whatever was shown and whatever is chosen, so jumping from v1 to v4 shows the full change. Append a version to `artifact.versions` while `status` is "writing" and set `version` to it to play the new diff.
- Under reduced motion the diff marks still show, because they are information, but lines appear and leave without folding, panels cross-fade without travel, and docking cross-fades the pane and the chip with no flight.
- Lays out by its own width: under 40rem the conversation fills the box and the open pane covers it as a sheet; from 40rem the two sit side by side; from 60rem the thread widens, turns show their times and Copy and Download are labelled.
- Relative times count from `now`, never the clock. A Markdown document renders headings, paragraphs, "- " lists, **bold**, `code` and {template_variables} as chips.

### Voice Mode (KQ-1298) — `voice-mode`
Talk; watch it listen.

A voice call with an assistant, drawn around an orb that breathes with whoever is talking: one level, smoothed each frame with a fast attack and a slower release, ripples a blob, pushes a ring of dots or trails two rings, while the orb's resting size moves between listening, thinking and speaking on snap, shrinks away on glide when the call ends, and its pigment cross-fades with the state. The conversation plays from data at speaking pace, the caller's words arriving in light ink and firming as each line settles and every new line rising 8px on snap, and Interrupt halts the reply mid-word, tracked to the character. Mute, Interrupt and End are real buttons (Mute a toggle with aria-pressed), and each finished line is announced once, never per word.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/voice-mode`

Props:
- `orb`: "blob" | "rings" | "dots" (default "blob") — How the orb draws the voice: a closed curve rippling on three seeded harmonics, a disc with two rings trailing the level on slower smoothings, or 28 dots each pushed out on its own phase.
- `captions`: "transcript" | "live" | "off" (default "transcript") — What is shown of the words: the conversation as lines (beside the orb from 40rem), only the current utterance large under the orb, or nothing (lines are still announced).
- `level`: number (default 0.6) — How far the orb swells with the voice, 0 to 1. At 0 it stays round and only its colour changes.
- `turns`: VoiceTurn[] (default defaultVoiceTurns) — The conversation, { id, role: "user" | "assistant", text }, played in order at speaking pace. Append turns as they are transcribed and the call carries on from where it is.
- `live / defaultLive`: boolean (default true) — Whether the call is on. Turning it back on starts the conversation from the top.
- `onLiveChange`: (live: boolean) => void — Fires from End and Call again.
- `muted / defaultMuted`: boolean (default false) — The microphone is muted: the orb greys and stills, and the caller's turn waits until it is unmuted.
- `onMutedChange`: (muted: boolean) => void — Fires from the Mute button.
- `onInterrupt`: (turn: VoiceTurn, spoken: string) => void — The reply was cut off, with the part of it already said (empty when it was cut while thinking). Stop your speech output here.
- `onPhaseChange`: (phase: "connecting" | "listening" | "thinking" | "speaking" | "ended") => void — The call moved between listening, thinking, speaking and ended.
- `meter`: () => number — Reads the live input level, 0 to 1, each frame while listening, for example from an analyser on the microphone. Without it a seeded voice is simulated; nothing is ever recorded.
- `pace`: number (default 2.6) — Speaking pace in words a second. Longer words take longer and punctuation adds a breath.
- `agent`: string (default "Coldbrook Assist") — Who is on the other end: the header, the speaker names and the announcements.
- `status`: "ready" | "connecting" | "error" (default "ready") — The line is still connecting (a faint orb with a turning arc), or the microphone could not be reached (a message with Retry).
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after an error.
- `label`: string — The surface's accessible name. Defaults to "Voice call with" and the agent.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A blup when the visitor interrupts, a click on Mute, End and Call again. The call itself is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The controls do nothing; the call still plays.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Mute, Interrupt and End are buttons in that order; Interrupt is aria-disabled (never disabled) outside speaking and thinking, so focus is never dropped, and End becomes Call again in place with focus kept on it.
- The call plays only while the surface is on screen and the page is visible: the word timer, the clock and the orb's frame loop all stop otherwise, and stop for good when the call ends.
- Under reduced motion the orb keeps its round shape and size; the level shows as the strength of its halo and the state as its colour. Words still arrive and Interrupt still cuts them mid-word, because the conversation is information.
- To drive it from a real session, append each transcribed turn to `turns`, pass `meter` reading your microphone analyser, and stop your speech output in `onInterrupt`.
- Lays out by its own width: one column under 40rem; with the transcript, two columns from 40rem (orb and controls beside the lines), and from 60rem the speaker sits beside each line.

### Source Search (KQ-1299) — `source-search`
Choose what the answer stands on.

A retrieval surface where you choose what an answer is grounded on. The query scores the sources as you type: rows that stay glide to their new rank, new rows rise 8px on snap in a cascade, leaving rows fade on the exit ease, every relevance bar or ring eases to its score on glide, and facet counts roll on snap. Checking a result flies a ghost chip from its title into the tray, x on glide and y on a softer spring so it travels on a shallow curve while homing on its slot, landing on recoil as the tray's count and the Answer button's count roll; checkboxes are native with Up and Down between them, the tray's remove buttons are a roving toolbar where Delete removes, and Escape clears the query.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/source-search`

Props:
- `relevance`: "bar" | "ring" | "off" (default "bar") — How each result's score is shown: a bar that fills from the left, a ring gauge whose arc sweeps, or not at all (the rank still carries it).
- `facets`: "chips" | "rail" | "off" (default "chips") — How the filters are offered: toggle chips under the query, a column of checkboxes beside the results (chips below 40rem), or none. Within a group facets OR, across groups they AND.
- `tray`: "chips" | "stack" | "count" (default "chips") — How the chosen sources sit in the tray: numbered chips with titles, a fanned stack of small numbered cards that spreads on hover or focus, or one count with a dot per source.
- `sources`: SearchSource[] (default defaultSearchSources) — Everything that can be found: { id, title, site, snippet, kind: "doc" | "ticket" | "code" | "thread", space?, updated, relevance }.
- `query / defaultQuery`: string (default defaultSearchQuery) — The search text. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onQueryChange`: (query: string) => void — Fires on every keystroke in the query and when it is cleared.
- `onSearch`: (query: string) => void — Enter was pressed in the query: run your search here.
- `matching`: boolean (default true) — Score and filter sources against the query in the browser (relevance times the share of query words found, title words counting double). Turn off when the host searches and passes ranked results.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string[] (default []) — The ids in the tray, in tray order. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onSelectedChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the checkbox, the chip's remove button, Delete or Clear that changed the tray.
- `filters / defaultFilters`: string[] (default []) — Active facets as "kind:doc", "updated:week" | "updated:month" | "updated:older", "space:<name>".
- `onFiltersChange`: (filters: string[]) => void — Fires from the chip or checkbox that changed the filters.
- `max`: number (default 6) — The most sources the tray holds. When full, further checkboxes are aria-disabled and the tray says so.
- `onAnswer`: (sources: SearchSource[], query: string) => void — Answer was pressed, with the tray's sources in order and the query.
- `onOpen`: (source: SearchSource) => void — A result's title was pressed. Without it, titles are plain text.
- `status`: "ready" | "searching" | "error" (default "ready") — The host is searching (skeleton rows) or the search failed (a message with Retry).
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after a failed search.
- `now`: number | Date (default the newest source's time) — The moment "updated" times and the age facets count from, so results render the same everywhere.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Search docs, tickets and code") — The query's placeholder.
- `label`: string (default "Source search") — The surface's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick when the visitor checks, unchecks, filters or answers (rising with the tray's count), a pop when a flown chip lands.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be searched, filtered or chosen.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: ArrowDown in the query enters the results; Up and Down move between the native checkboxes and Space toggles; the tray's remove buttons are one tab stop with Left, Right, Home and End between them and Delete or Backspace to remove (focus moves to the next chip, then to Answer); Escape in a non-empty query clears it.
- Counts follow the landings: the tray's count and the Answer button's count change when a flown chip lands, not when the box is checked, so the number never runs ahead of what the reader sees.
- Under reduced motion nothing flies or slides: chips fade into the tray, rows re-rank and leave at once, scores are drawn at their values and skeletons hold still.
- With your own search, pass ranked `sources`, set `matching={false}`, drive `status` while it runs, and use `onSearch` for Enter; the tray keeps any chosen id that is still in `sources`.
- Lays out by its own width: under 40rem the facets are one scrolling chip row and the tray scrolls sideways above a full-width Answer; from 40rem the rail sits beside the results and tray chips wrap; from 60rem results show their updated time beside the score.

### Agent Inbox (KQ-1300) — `agent-inbox`
What your agents need you to look at.

A review queue for work agents have finished: each card carries the change (summary, area, a diff summary with its proportion bar, checks and risk) and two decisions. A card follows the finger 1:1 sideways while the decision it is heading for shows underneath and arms on snap past the threshold; the release is projected, so a flick commits and a short throw springs home on snap with its velocity, an approved card leaves on the exit ease while the cards under it close the gap on glide, and sending back opens a note on glide first. Checkboxes select several and a toolbar slides down over the header on snap, the header's counts roll on snap as the queue empties into an inbox-zero state whose check draws on flick and whose badge lands on recoil; the cards are a roving list where Up and Down move, A approves, R sends back, X selects, Enter opens the files and Escape closes a note.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/agent-inbox`

Props:
- `swipe`: "both" | "approve" | "off" (default "both") — What a sideways swipe does: right approves and left sends back, only right approves (left rubber-bands), or nothing (buttons and keys only).
- `batch`: boolean (default true) — Cards carry checkboxes, and a toolbar slides in to approve or send back several at once.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — How much each card says: one line with icon actions, a summary and the diff bar with labelled actions, or a two-line summary with every file and the risk spelled out.
- `tasks / defaultTasks`: InboxTask[] (default defaultInboxTasks) — Every task, waiting and decided: { id, title, agent, area, summary, files: { path, added, removed }[], checks?, risk?, at, status?, note?, decidedAt? }. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onTasksChange`: (tasks: InboxTask[]) => void — Fires from the swipe, button, key or undo that changed a task, with the whole new list.
- `onApprove`: (tasks: InboxTask[]) => void — Tasks were approved: one, or a batch.
- `onReturn`: (tasks: InboxTask[], note: string) => void — Tasks were sent back with this note.
- `onUndo`: (task: InboxTask) => void — A decision was undone; the task is waiting again.
- `threshold`: number (default 0.4) — How far a card must travel to commit, as a share of its width, 0.2 to 0.8. A flick that would carry it that far commits too.
- `notes`: string[] (default ["Add tests", "Smaller change", "Wrong place"]) — Quick notes offered when sending back; pressing one fills the note.
- `now`: number | Date (default the newest task's time) — The moment relative times count from, and the time decisions are stamped with.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — The queue is loading (skeleton cards) or failed to load (a message with Retry).
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after the queue failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Review queue") — The queue's name, shown in the header.
- `label`: string — The surface's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish for every decision the visitor makes (up for approve, down for send back), and a chime when their decision empties the queue.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be decided, selected or undone.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the cards are one tab stop with Up, Down, Home and End between them; A approves, R opens the send-back note (Enter sends it, Escape closes it and returns to the card), X or Space selects, and Enter opens the file list. Approve and Send back are also real buttons on every card, and the batch toolbar takes Left and Right.
- Focus never drops: when a card leaves, focus moves to the card that took its place, and to the inbox-zero heading when the queue empties.
- Under reduced motion a drag still follows the finger, because the visitor is moving it, but nothing else travels: cards fade out and back, the list closes at once, counts swap without rolling, the toolbar fades in place and the inbox-zero check is drawn.
- Sending back always needs a note: a left swipe springs the card home and opens the note rather than deciding on its own.
- Lays out by its own width: under 40rem the actions sit as a full-width row under each card and the header counts wrap; from 40rem the actions sit at the card's right; from 60rem a Reviewed column logs every decision with its note, with Undo on the newest.

### App Shell (KQ-1301) — `app-shell`
The frame every screen lives in.

The frame a product's screens live in: a sidebar whose width is one motion value on glide, so its labels tuck away row by row and leave a 56px icon rail with tooltips, its edge dragged 1:1 and committed by projection with the release velocity; below 640px it becomes a drawer that slides over a scrim on glide and can be pushed back out. A pill under the current row travels on snap, pages change by slide, fade or zoom with the last crumb cross-fading in the same beat, and search is a combobox over the pages. Arrow keys walk the sidebar, [ or Cmd/Ctrl+B folds it, 1–9 change page and / goes to search.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/app-shell`

Props:
- `pages`: AppShellPage[] (default defaultShellPages) — The destinations in sidebar order, each with its label, icon, optional badge and section, crumbs, heading, summary, search keywords and content.
- `page / defaultPage`: string (default the first page) — The current page's id. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onPageChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the row, crumb, shortcut or search result that chose a page.
- `collapsed / defaultCollapsed`: boolean (default open from 1024px, folded below) — The sidebar folded to its rail (or hidden without rail). Controlled or uncontrolled; left unset it follows the shell's width.
- `onCollapsedChange`: (collapsed: boolean) => void — Fires from the toggle, the edge drag, the edge's arrow keys or the shortcut, with the new fold.
- `rail`: boolean (default true) — Fold to a 56px icon rail whose labels become tooltips. Off: the sidebar slides away entirely and the content takes the width.
- `transition`: "slide" | "fade" | "zoom" (default "slide") — How the content changes page: rising 16px in the direction of travel through the nav, a cross-fade, or settling from 0.98 scale.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Row heights (28/32/36px), the top bar (44/48/56px), paddings and the heading size.
- `workspace`: AppShellWorkspace (default defaultShellWorkspace) — The product at the top of the sidebar: name, detail line and an optional 28px mark.
- `user`: AppShellUser (default defaultShellUser) — Who is signed in, at the foot of the sidebar.
- `navLabel`: string (default "Main") — The sidebar navigation's accessible name.
- `searchPlaceholder`: string (default "Search " + workspace name) — The search field's placeholder and accessible name.
- `onSearch`: (query: string) => void — Enter in search when no page matches, with the query.
- `shortcuts`: boolean (default true) — [ or Cmd/Ctrl+B folds the sidebar, 1–9 go to a page and / focuses search, while focus is in the shell or it is hovered with nothing focused; never while typing.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — The content area's state: a skeleton while loading, a message with Retry on error. The sidebar keeps working.
- `onRetry`: () => void — The error state's Retry button.
- `label`: string (default workspace name) — The shell's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish as the visitor folds or opens the sidebar or drawer, a click pitched by place as they choose a page.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height (h-full, h-dvh) to fill a screen.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the sidebar is one tab stop — Up and Down walk the pages, Home and End jump, Enter or Space open. The edge is a separator: Left folds, Right opens, Enter toggles. In the drawer Tab is trapped and Escape closes it, handing focus back to the menu button.
- Reduced motion: widths and the drawer change at once, pages cross-fade on opacity whatever transition says, the pill and tooltips appear in place; every change is still announced in the polite status.
- The shell arranges itself by its own measured width — drawer below 640px, rail from 640px, open from 1024px — and server-renders that arrangement with container queries, so the first paint already matches.
- Page content is yours: anything in a page's content renders in a scrolling region named by the page heading, and it reads --shell-row, --shell-pad and --shell-gap if it wants to follow density.
- Search finds pages by label, heading, summary and keywords; give a page the names of its records (ids, people, sites) as keywords and a search for one lands on the page that holds it, with focus on its heading.

### Command Center (KQ-1302) — `command-center`
Every action, one keystroke away.

A command palette that lives inside its frame: Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, pressed anywhere in the frame, lands it from 8px above on snap over a fading scrim, and it leaves on the exit ease. Commands are a tree — choosing one with sub-commands slides its page in on glide (or raises it over its parent like a sheet) while a chip with the parent's name pops into the field on snap and the list's measured height glides to the new page's; Backspace slides back. Fuzzy matching lights the letters it found across the whole tree, a pill follows the highlight on snap, Recent leads an empty field and a preview pane follows the highlight from 640px; the field is a combobox where arrows move, Enter runs or opens and Escape clears, then goes back, then closes.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/command-center`

Props:
- `commands`: CommandItem[] (default defaultCommands) — The command tree: each command has a label, group, icon, keywords, shortcut, hint, preview, placeholder and tone, and may hold children that open as a page of their own.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default false) — The palette is open. Controlled or uncontrolled; opening by default never takes focus.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the shortcut, trigger, Escape, scrim or run that opened or closed it.
- `recent / defaultRecent`: string[] (default defaultCommandRecent) — Ids of recently run commands, newest first. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onRecentChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires with the new list whenever a run changes it.
- `onRun`: (command: CommandItem, path: CommandItem[]) => void — A command was run, with the pages it was reached through.
- `nesting`: "slide" | "stack" | "flat" (default "slide") — How sub-commands open: a page sliding in from the side, a sheet rising over its receding parent, or no pages at all with every sub-command listed under its parent's heading.
- `preview`: boolean (default true) — A pane beside the list previews the highlighted command — its facts, a sentence, or the choices it opens — where the frame is 640px or wider.
- `fuzzy`: boolean (default true) — Letters match in order anywhere, scored for word starts and runs, and light up. Off: the query must appear as typed.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Search or run a command…") — The field's placeholder on the first page; each sub-page uses its command's own placeholder.
- `shortcut`: boolean (default true) — Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, pressed while focus is anywhere in the frame, opens and closes the palette; the key press is consumed there.
- `trigger`: boolean (default true) — Show the search trigger along the top of the frame.
- `triggerLabel`: string (default "Search or run a command") — The trigger's text.
- `maxRecent`: number (default 5) — How many recent commands are kept.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Commands still arriving show skeleton rows and a spinner in the field; a failed fetch shows a line with Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — The error state's Retry button.
- `label`: string (default "Command menu") — The palette's accessible name.
- `children`: ReactNode (default a Basinworks invoices screen) — The app behind the palette, inert while it is open.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick pitched down the list as the highlight moves, a swish as pages and the palette open and close. Typing is silent.
- `className`: string — Classes for the frame. It is 560px tall by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Up and Down move (wrapping), Page Up and Page Down jump five, Enter runs or opens, Tab or ArrowRight at the end of the text opens a command's page, Backspace or ArrowLeft in an empty field goes back, and Escape clears, then goes back, then closes — every key handled with preventDefault where focus is.
- Reduced motion: the palette, its pages and the preview cross-fade on opacity, the list's height and the pill jump, and the run flash and choice check still show.
- Give every command a stable id: recents are ids, and with nothing typed Recent leads with each command's path shown, so a deep command runs in one keystroke.
- Searching at the top level reaches the whole tree; a deep result shows its path with the matched letters lit in it and runs directly, without opening its pages.
- keepOpen commands behave as a choice among their siblings: running one leaves the palette open and moves the check to it, which suits settings like a theme.

### Swim Board (KQ-1303) — `swim-board`
Pick it up, carry it over.

A kanban board with swimlanes. A dragged card comes up into a carried copy 1:1 under the pointer, scaled on flick and leaning into its horizontal speed up to tilt degrees on a glide-tuned spring; the cell under it opens a gap of the card's exact height on glide while the cards below slide down, and on release it flies into the gap on snap with the release velocity and straightens as it lands. A move past a column's work-in-progress limit shakes its header on a five-beat tween and turns it warn (or is refused, the gap staying home), lanes group by priority or owner and fold on glide, and moving a card between lanes rewrites that field. Space picks a focused card up, arrows carry it a place or a column at a time, Enter drops and Escape puts it back, every step announced.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/swim-board`

Props:
- `cards / defaultCards`: SwimCard[] (default defaultSwimCards) — Every card in board order — a cell lists its cards in the order they appear here. Each has a title, column, priority, owner, and optional tag and points. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onCardsChange`: (cards: SwimCard[], move: SwimMove) => void — Fires from the drop that moved a card, with every card and the move (from and to as column, lane and index, and whether it came from the pointer or the keyboard).
- `columns`: SwimColumn[] (default defaultSwimColumns) — The columns left to right, each with an optional work-in-progress limit.
- `people`: SwimPerson[] (default defaultSwimPeople) — Everyone a card can belong to; owner lanes follow this order.
- `onMove`: (move: SwimMove) => void — A card was dropped somewhere new.
- `onCardOpen`: (id: string) => void — A card was tapped, clicked, or had Enter pressed on it while not picked up.
- `onLaneToggle`: (lane: string, collapsed: boolean) => void — A lane was folded or unfolded, with its new state.
- `tilt`: number (default 6) — How far a carried card leans into its travel, in degrees: its angle is the pointer's horizontal speed, clamped to this. 0 keeps it level.
- `limit`: "warn" | "block" | "off" (default "warn") — Work-in-progress limits: a move past one shakes the header and turns it warn, is refused with the card going home, or limits are hidden.
- `lanes`: "priority" | "owner" | "none" (default "priority") — What the rows group by. Moving a card between lanes rewrites that field on the card.
- `collapsedLanes / defaultCollapsedLanes`: string[] (default []) — Folded lanes by id. Controlled (with onLaneToggle) or uncontrolled.
- `title`: string (default "Sprint 14") — The board's heading.
- `subtitle`: string (default "Fernworks Field app") — A quieter line beside the heading, from 480px.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Skeleton cards while loading; a message with Retry on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — The error state's Retry button.
- `label`: string (default title) — The board's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A click as a card comes up or a lane folds, a thock pitched by column as it lands — duller when a drop is refused.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Cards can still be read and walked with the arrow keys, but not carried or opened.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; the lanes scroll inside it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the board is one tab stop for cards (plus each lane's fold button). Arrows walk between cards, Space picks the focused card up, arrows then carry it a place at a time (crossing into the next lane past either end) or a column at a time, Enter or Space drops it and Escape puts it back; every pick-up, step, refusal and drop is announced.
- Reduced motion: the carried card follows the pointer but never leans, the gap opens at once, landings and keyboard steps are instant and nothing shakes — the warn colour, Over limit, counts and announcements still show.
- On touch screens a card is carried by its grip (the six dots at its corner), so a finger anywhere else on a card scrolls the board; on a phone the columns scroll sideways and the column chips above jump to one, and holding a card near an edge scrolls the board under it.
- Controlled boards stay honest: the drop is reported with onCardsChange and the card flies to wherever the host's next cards put it — the new place if it accepted the move, home if it did not.
- Moving a card between lanes rewrites the field the lanes group by (priority or owner) in the cards you get back.

### Mail Inbox (KQ-1304) — `mail-inbox`
Triage with a flick.

An inbox built for triage: a row's face follows the finger 1:1 and reveals its action from the edge it leaves, archive on a green pigment and snooze on an amber one, arming with a pop on snap at the commit line; a release past it (or a throw, by projection) runs the row out on glide with its release velocity before its height closes, and a short one springs home on snap. Selecting a thread slides a batch toolbar down over the header on snap with a rolling count, opening one fades its unread dot and glides its messages open under the row (or into a reading pane when the inbox is wide), and every archive leaves an Undo toast that lands on recoil. j and k move, x selects, Enter opens, e archives, b snoozes, s stars, u toggles unread, z undoes and Escape backs out.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mail-inbox`

Props:
- `swipe`: "full" | "reveal" | "off" (default "full") — How a swipe commits: past 42% of the row, resting open on its action (a long swipe still commits), or not at all, leaving the hover tools and keys.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Row height and type size: single-line compact rows, cozy, or roomy with larger avatars.
- `preview`: number (default 1) — Lines of message preview under the subject, 0 to 2.
- `threads / defaultThreads`: MailThread[] (default defaultMailThreads) — Every thread in every folder, each a subject and its messages oldest first. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onThreadsChange`: (threads: MailThread[]) => void — Fires from the swipe, key or button that changed the threads, with all of them.
- `folder / defaultFolder`: "inbox" | "snoozed" | "archive" (default "inbox") — The folder on screen. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onFolderChange`: (folder: MailFolder) => void — Fires when a folder is chosen on the rail or the folder chips.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string[] (default []) — Selected thread ids. A selection brings in the batch toolbar.
- `onSelectedChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the checkbox, x, select-all or batch action that changed the selection.
- `open / defaultOpen`: string | null (default null) — The open thread: expanded under its row, or in the reading pane once the inbox is 68rem wide.
- `onOpenChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when a thread opens or closes.
- `swipeActions`: { right: MailAction | null; left: MailAction | null } (default { right: "archive", left: "snooze" }) — Which action each swipe direction runs; null leaves that direction rubber-banding. In the archive or snoozed folder the action that would send a thread where it is moves it back to the inbox.
- `now`: Date | number (default defaultMailNow) — The moment times are read against (09:12, Yesterday, Tue, 25 Sep). Never read from the clock during render.
- `zoneOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC that times are shown in, so the server and the browser draw the same inbox.
- `snoozeUntil`: (now: number) => number — When a snooze ends, from now. Defaults to the next day at 08:00.
- `account`: MailPerson — Whose inbox it is: shown on the rail, and their messages read as "me".
- `label`: string (default "Mail") — The inbox's accessible name.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholder rows; error offers Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed on the error state.
- `onArchive`: (ids: string[]) => void — Threads were sent to the archive, by swipe, key, hover tool or batch.
- `onSnooze`: (ids: string[], until: number) => void — Threads were snoozed, and until when.
- `onRestore`: (ids: string[]) => void — Threads were moved back to the inbox from the archive or a snooze.
- `onReadChange`: (ids: string[], unread: boolean) => void — Threads were marked read by opening them, or toggled with u or the mail tool.
- `onStarChange`: (id: string, starred: boolean) => void — A thread was starred or unstarred.
- `onReply`: (threadId: string) => void — Reply was pressed on an open thread.
- `onCompose`: () => void — Compose was pressed on the rail.
- `onUndo`: (ids: string[]) => void — The last archive or snooze was undone from the toast or with z.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pop when a swipe arms, a pick or a star lands, and a swish as rows leave. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Makes the whole inbox inert.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is 560px tall by default and lays out by its own width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the rows are one tab stop. j and k (or the arrows) move, Home and End jump, x selects, Enter or o opens, e archives, b snoozes, s stars, u toggles unread, z undoes, Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all, and Escape clears the selection, closes the open thread or a revealed row.
- Reduced motion: the row still follows the finger, but it fades rather than flies when it commits and every settle is a short tween; the toolbar, toast and pane cross-fade, and read state, counts and selections still change.
- Data: pass threads (with folder, unread, starred, labels, snoozedUntil) and keep them in your store through onThreadsChange; the specific callbacks (onArchive, onSnooze, onRestore, onReadChange) say what happened. A controlled host that keeps a thread where it was gets its row back.
- Layout follows the inbox's own width: one column with folder chips under 40rem, a rail with folders and label filters from 40rem, and a reading pane from 68rem.
- Times come from now and zoneOffset, never the machine's clock or locale, so the server and the browser render the same markup.
- Touch: rows are touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the list and a horizontal one throws the row.

### Week Planner (KQ-1305) — `week-planner`
Draw an event where it belongs.

A week drawn on its hours. Pressing empty time and dragging rubber-bands a block out of the pressed slot, its far edge 1:1 under the pointer with a snapped line and a live time label, ticking at every new slot; on release the edge springs onto the snapped time on snap with the pointer's velocity and the event thocks down with its title ready to type. Events drag across time and days and stretch from either edge the same way, landing on snap with the release velocity while a dashed placeholder shows the landing and overlapping events re-divide their columns on glide; a now line moves through today on drift. The grid is one tab stop with a slot cursor (arrows, Shift for a range, Enter to create), and each event moves with the arrows, stretches with Shift, renames with Enter and goes with Delete.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/week-planner`

Props:
- `snap`: number (default 15) — Minutes every drag, resize and cursor step snaps to; also the gutter's tick marks.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Height of an hour (40, 52 or 68px), with type and padding to match. A change glides every event to its new place.
- `now`: Date | number (default defaultWeekPlannerNow) — The current moment, which draws the now line and shades time already gone: a Date or epoch ms, or a number from 0 to 24 read as that hour of today (13.5 is 13:30).
- `events / defaultEvents`: WeekEvent[] (default defaultWeekEvents) — Events with epoch-ms start and end, a title, an optional calendar id and location. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onEventsChange`: (events: WeekEvent[]) => void — Fires from the drag, key or field that changed the events, with all of them.
- `calendars`: WeekCalendar[] (default defaultWeekCalendars) — The calendars events belong to, each with a label and a tint (a CSS colour token).
- `day / defaultDay`: Date | number (default today) — The focused day: its week is shown, and on a phone the day itself. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onDayChange`: (day: number) => void — Fires with the new day's midnight (epoch ms) from the arrows, the day strip, the headers or the keys.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string | null (default null) — The selected event, shown with a stronger tint and, from 68rem, in the details panel.
- `onSelectedChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when an event is picked, created or let go.
- `today`: Date | number (default the date of now) — The date marked as today; an hour-form now falls on it.
- `hours`: [number, number] (default [7, 21]) — The hours the grid draws. Events outside are clipped to them.
- `workHours`: [number, number] (default [9, 18]) — Working hours, drawn on the lighter ground; the keyboard cursor starts at their first hour when now is elsewhere.
- `weekStartsOn`: 0 | 1 (default 1) — 1 starts weeks on Monday, 0 on Sunday.
- `zoneOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC that times are drawn in, never the machine's own zone, so the server and the browser draw the same week.
- `defaultDuration`: number (default 30) — Minutes an event made with Enter or New lasts when no range is selected.
- `newTitle`: string (default "New event") — A new event's title, selected in its field so typing replaces it.
- `defaultCalendar`: string — The calendar new events join. Defaults to the first calendar.
- `onCreate`: (event: WeekEvent) => void — An event was drawn, made with Enter, or added with New.
- `onUpdate`: (event: WeekEvent, previous: WeekEvent) => void — An event moved, was resized, renamed or changed calendar.
- `onDelete`: (event: WeekEvent) => void — An event was removed with Delete, its close button or the details panel.
- `label`: string (default "Week") — The planner's accessible name.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading covers the hours with a note; error offers Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed on the error state.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a tick at every new slot a drag or key reaches and a thock when an event lands. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Makes the whole planner inert.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is 560px tall by default and lays out by its own width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop with a slot cursor. Up and Down move it a snap step, Left and Right a day, Page Up and Page Down an hour, Home and End the first and last slot, t jumps to now; Shift with Up or Down selects a range and Enter (or n) creates an event over it. Events are tab stops: Up and Down move them, Shift changes their end, Left and Right move a day, Enter or F2 renames, Delete removes, Escape returns to the grid.
- Reduced motion: drags still follow the pointer, but landings, column re-divisions, week changes and the now line move at once; the placeholder, the snapped label and every time readout still show.
- Times are absolute (epoch ms) and drawn in zoneOffset, never the machine's zone, so server and browser agree. now can be an hour of today, which keeps a fixed demo readable.
- Layout follows the planner's own width: one day with a day strip under 40rem, the whole week from 40rem (drags cross days), and a details panel with a title field, calendar radio group and duration stepper from 68rem.
- Touch: the hours scroll with touch-pan-y; a finger rests 300ms before it draws a new event or lifts one, so a swipe still scrolls.
- Overlapping events share their day side by side and widen into free columns; a controlled host that refuses a move gets the event back where it was.

### File Browser (KQ-1306) — `file-browser`
Lasso, drag, drop into folders.

A file manager you work with your hands: grid and list are the same items laid out twice, so the toggle morphs every tile into its row through motion's layout on the spring you choose, and folders slide in from the side you travel on that spring. Press empty space and drag to lasso (items join as the rectangle touches them, or only once inside); drag a selection and it lifts into a stack that follows the pointer, a folder's lid opens as the hover charges until it springs open with you still carrying, a drop on a folder shrinks the stack into it while it bumps on recoil, and a drop into the open folder lands the files on their measured places. Uploads run as rows whose progress glides and each turns into its tile when it resolves; the items are a multi-select listbox where arrows move, Shift extends, Enter opens, Backspace goes up, Ctrl or Cmd with X and V cut and paste, and Delete removes with Undo.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/file-browser`

Props:
- `view / defaultView`: "grid" | "list" (default "grid") — The layout. Changing view morphs every item into the other layout; the toggle also switches it and reports through onViewChange.
- `onViewChange`: (view: FileBrowserView) => void — Fires from the grid and list toggle with the new layout.
- `lasso`: "touch" | "contain" | "off" (default "touch") — How the lasso picks: items it touches, only items wholly inside it, or no lasso (empty space just clears).
- `spring`: "snap" | "glide" | "recoil" (default "glide") — The spring under the grid and list morph, the folder slide and every landing: crisp, settled or bouncy.
- `files / defaultFiles`: FileItem[] (default defaultFiles) — Every item in every folder as one flat list linked by parentId. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onFilesChange`: (files: FileItem[]) => void — Fires from the drop, paste, move, upload or delete that changed the items, with all of them.
- `folder / defaultFolder`: string (default rootId) — The open folder's id. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onFolderChange`: (folder: string) => void — Fires from a crumb, the tree, Enter, Backspace or a folder springing open under a drag.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string[] (default []) — Selected item ids. A selection brings in the selection bar with Move to and Delete.
- `onSelectedChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the press, lasso or key that changed the selection.
- `rootId`: string (default "root") — The id top-level items carry as parentId.
- `rootLabel`: string (default "Files") — The top level's name in the breadcrumb and the tree.
- `openDelay`: number (default 700) — How long, in ms, a dragged stack hovers a folder (a tile, a crumb or a tree row) before it springs open.
- `upload`: (file: File, progress: (fraction: number) => void, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<Partial<FileItem> | void> — Stores an uploaded file, reporting progress and honouring the signal; resolves with anything the stored item should carry. Without it a seeded local simulation runs, for demos.
- `accept`: string — File types uploads take, as an input's accept (".pdf,image/*"). Others are listed with the reason.
- `maxSize`: number (default 26214400) — The largest file an upload takes, in bytes (25 MB).
- `quota`: number (default 16106127360) — Storage shown on the meter under the tree, in bytes (15 GB).
- `now`: Date | number (default defaultFilesNow) — The moment modified dates are read against (Today, 09:12; 28 Sep). Never read from the clock during render.
- `zoneOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC that dates are shown in, so the server and the browser agree.
- `onOpen`: (item: FileItem) => void — A file was opened by double-click, Enter or Open in the details panel.
- `onMove`: (ids: string[], folderId: string) => void — Items moved into a folder by drop, paste or Move to (and back, by Undo).
- `onDelete`: (ids: string[]) => void — Items were removed, with everything inside a removed folder.
- `onUploadComplete`: (item: FileItem) => void — An upload resolved and landed as an item.
- `label`: string (default "Files") — The browser's accessible name.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholder tiles; error offers Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed on the error state.
- `ref`: React.Ref<FileBrowserHandle> — A handle whose upload(files) uploads into the open folder, as a drop or the picker would.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pop when a press selects, items join a lasso or a drop lands, and a swish on the view toggle, navigation and a folder springing open. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Makes the whole browser inert.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is 560px tall by default and lays out by its own width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the items are one tab stop in a multi-select listbox. Arrows move (two-dimensional in the grid), Shift extends, Ctrl or Cmd with an arrow moves without selecting, Space toggles, Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all, Enter opens, Backspace or Alt with Up goes up, Ctrl or Cmd with X then V cuts and pastes into the open folder, Delete removes, Escape clears. The tree, the layout toggle and the Move to menu each have their own arrow keys.
- Reduced motion: the layout swaps at once, folders cross-fade instead of sliding, and every flight (the stack home, into a folder, onto the grid) is a short fade; the lasso and the stack still follow the pointer and progress still fills.
- Uploads: pass upload to store files; report progress from 0 to 1 and honour the AbortSignal (Cancel aborts it). Resolve with the stored item's fields; its row turns into its tile when it lands. accept and maxSize refuse files with a reason, and a rejected promise offers Retry.
- Layout follows the browser's own width: one column with a Back button under 40rem, a folder tree with the storage meter and full breadcrumbs from 40rem, and a details panel from 68rem.
- Touch: the items scroll with touch-pan-y; a finger rests 350ms before it lassoes or lifts files, so a swipe still scrolls.
- Every move and delete leaves a toast with Undo; a folder can never be moved into itself or anything inside it.

### Review Thread (KQ-1307) — `review-thread`
Comments that know where they belong.

A draft under review with its discussions pinned in the margin at the height of the passages they are about: one layout pass places every card, the open one exactly on its passage, and when a card grows the cards beneath it glide out of its way. Hovering or focusing a passage or a card brightens the highlight and draws a leader along the passage's underline into the card, rebuilt each frame from the card's own position; replies land on snap, @-mentions complete from a list, and resolving folds the thread back into a one-line check with a dog-eared corner on glide while the check draws on flick. Up and Down walk the threads in reading order, Enter opens one, Escape closes the mention list and then the thread.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/review-thread`

Props:

- `threads / defaultThreads`: ReviewThreadData[] (default defaultReviewThreads) — The discussions, each anchored to a quote inside one block, with its comments and resolved state. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onThreadsChange`: (threads: ReviewThreadData[]) => void — Fires from the reply or the resolve that changed the list, with the whole new list.
- `people`: ReviewPerson[] (default defaultReviewPeople) — Everyone who can write here: comment authors and the @-mention list.
- `me`: string (default "mira") — The id of the person replying and resolving.
- `now`: Date | number (default defaultReviewNow) — The moment every comment is dated against; the component never reads the clock.
- `active / defaultActive`: string | null (default null) — The open thread, or null. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onActiveChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when a press, a key or a resolve opens or closes a thread.
- `onReply`: (threadId: string, comment: ReviewComment) => void — A reply was sent, with the comment as stored.
- `onResolve`: (threadId: string, resolved: boolean) => void — A thread was resolved (true) or reopened (false).
- `onMention`: (personId: string, threadId: string) => void — A sent reply mentioned someone.
- `onRetry`: () => void — The Retry button of the error state.
- `leaders`: "curve" | "elbow" | "off" (default "curve") — The line that joins a lit passage to its card: a curve, two rounded right angles, or none (the highlight still brightens).
- `resolve`: "fold" | "tuck" | "off" (default "fold") — What resolving does: fold the thread to a one-line check in place, fold it and tuck it out of the rail behind a Resolved toggle, or no resolving at all.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Type size, card padding, avatar size and how many lines of a closed thread show.
- `highlight`: string (default "var(--warn)") — The passages' highlight and leader colour, any CSS colour.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws the surface's skeleton; error offers Retry.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Reply, or @ to mention") — The reply composer's placeholder.
- `label`: string — The region's accessible name. Defaults to “Review of” and the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a tick on opening and moving between threads and a pop on replying and resolving. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Reads but does not reply, resolve or open.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. The root is h-[560px] by default; pass a height to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the thread cards are one roving tab stop. Up and Down walk them in reading order, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens one, Escape closes it; inside an open thread Tab reaches Resolve and the reply box, where Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks a line. Typing @ opens the mention list: Up and Down move, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes it without closing the thread.
- Reduced motion: cards jump to their places, the fold and the leader fade instead of moving or drawing, and scrolling to a passage is instant. Highlights, counts, the resolved check and the replies still appear.
- Layout follows the component's own width: under 600px the threads sit under their paragraphs with a notch pointing at the passage; from 600px they move into a margin rail; from 1040px a thread index joins on the left and a press there glides the draft to the passage.
- Anchors are quotes, not offsets: a thread points at the first occurrence of its quote inside its block, so an edit elsewhere in the draft never moves it. A quote that is no longer in the text keeps its thread, placed after the anchored ones.
- Every time is relative to `now`. Pass the current time from your app (a minute tick is plenty) and the “4 min ago” labels move with it; nothing reads the clock in render, so server and client match.

### Notice Center (KQ-1308) — `notice-center`
Everything that happened, sorted out.

A notification center whose groups stack into a deck: pressing one deals it out, each hidden row starting where its layer was and gliding down to its place on glide in a cascade while the group's measured height glides open, and Show less gathers them back on the exit ease. A row or a whole stack follows a sideways swipe 1:1, is thrown off on the exit ease when its projected rest passes 40% of its width (or snaps back on snap with the release velocity), and the rows under it close the gap on glide. Mark all read sends a band down the list that clears each unread row as it passes — the dot shrinks on flick — the tab pill slides on snap and times roll as `now` moves; arrows walk the rows, Enter opens, Right deals and Left gathers a stack, Delete dismisses.

- `onDismiss`: (ids: string[]) => void — Notices were dismissed by swipe, key or button: one, or a whole collapsed group.
- `onMarkAllRead`: (ids: string[]) => void — Mark all read cleared these notices.
- `onReadChange`: (id: string, read: boolean) => void — One notice was marked read or unread.

- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholder rows; error offers Retry.

- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish on dismiss and Mark all read and a pop on dealing, gathering and read changes. Off unless asked for.

Notes:

Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens a notice (or deals a stack), Right deals a stack and Left gathers it, Delete or Backspace dismisses with focus moving to the next row, and U toggles read. The tabs are a tablist: Left and Right switch them.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels. A stack's rows fade in place and its height changes at once, a dismissed row fades and its space closes, the band is skipped and every read state cross-fades together. Counts, dots and the read state still change.
- Layout follows the component's own width: under 600px a single column; from 600px a detail pane opens beside the list; from 1040px a Sources rail joins on the left and narrows the list to one source.
- Times are relative to `now` and days are UTC days, so server and client render the same labels. Advance `now` from your app (a minute tick is plenty) and the times roll over in place.
- A swipe commits only past 40% of the row's width, measured on where the throw would come to rest, so a lazy drag snaps back and a quick flick goes. Dismissing a collapsed stack dismisses the whole group.

### Member Roster (KQ-1310) — `member-roster`

The people in a workspace and what each can do. A role changes only after a confirm unfolds under the row to its measured height on glide and is accepted — in menu mode a chip whose label then rolls to the new role on snap, in segmented mode a thumb that slides on snap and waits dashed until the confirm — and the last owner can never be demoted or removed. Invites are typed or pasted as email chips that land one after another from 0.6 scale on snap, pending invites resend behind a cooldown bar that drains linearly, and removing someone folds the row away, tipping back about its top edge while its height runs to zero and the rows below close the gap. Choosing a different role unfolds a confirm whose button takes focus (arrow keys leave focus in the group while you choose); Escape cancels and returns focus to the role. In the invite field Enter, comma, semicolon or space turn text into chips, Left walks back through them, Backspace or Delete removes one, and Enter on an empty field sends.

### Data Grid (KQ-1311) — `data-grid`
A table that keeps up with you.

A data grid that keeps pace with the hand: rows arrive after a skeleton in a cascade on glide (row by row, on a diagonal wave of cells, or in one fade) and replay from the side you paged toward, a heading press morphs its sort glyph between a double chevron and an arrow on snap while the rows on the page glide to their new seats, and columns resize from a grip that follows the finger 1:1, rubber-bands past its limits and springs back on snap with the release velocity. Shift-click selects a range drawn as one band that stretches from the anchor on snap, editable cells open an editor that lifts out of the cell and land their new value on flick, and the header and first columns stay pinned while the body scrolls. It is a real role="grid" with one roving cell: arrows move, Page keys turn the page, Space selects, Shift with an arrow extends the range, Enter sorts a heading or edits a cell, and Shift with Left or Right resizes a column.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/data-grid`

The first is the row header and stays pinned.
- `rows / defaultRows`: DataGridRow[] (default defaultDataGridRows) — The records, each with an id and a field per column. Controlled or uncontrolled; the default is 42 seeded invoices.

- `onCellEdit`: (edit: DataGridEdit) => void | Promise<unknown> — Fires when an edit is committed, with the row, column, new value and previous value. Return a promise to show the cell saving; a rejection puts the old value back.
- `sort / defaultSort`: { columnId: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" } | null (default null) — The sort, or null for the rows' own order. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onSortChange`: (sort: DataGridSort | null) => void — Fires from the heading press or key that changed the sort: ascending, descending, then off.

- `onSelectedChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the click, Shift-click or key that changed the selection.
- `page / defaultPage`: number (default 0) — The page shown, from 0. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onPageChange`: (page: number) => void — Fires from the button or key that turned the page.
- `pageSize`: number (default 8) — Rows per page.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 360) — Tallest the body grows, in px, before it scrolls under its pinned header.
- `actions`: DataGridAction[] (default []) — Buttons offered in the footer while rows are selected: id, label, an optional 14px icon and tone.
- `onAction`: (actionId: string, rowIds: string[]) => void — One of the actions was pressed, with the selected row ids.
- `onColumnResize`: (columnId: string, width: number) => void — Fires when a column's width settles after a drag, a double-click fit or a key.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultDataGridNow) — Today, for relative dates such as "in 3d" and "5d ago".
- `itemLabel`: { one: string; other: string } (default { one: "row", other: "rows" }) — What one row is called in counts and announcements: "3 invoices selected".
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The locale for numbers and money.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — The currency for money columns.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the rows have arrived. Loading shows a skeleton of one page; going to ready plays the arrival.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the rows failed to load.
- `emptyLabel`: string (default "Nothing here yet") — What an empty grid says.
- `title`: string (default "Receivables") — The heading over the grid.
- `label`: string — The grid's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click for sorts, toggles, page turns and saves, and a tick per row joining a range and per 16px of resize.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Keeps the grid readable and navigable but refuses sorting, selecting, editing, resizing and paging.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: one cell is the tab stop. Arrows move, Home and End reach the row's ends, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the page's corners, Page Up and Page Down turn the page. On a heading Enter or Space sorts, Shift+Left or Shift+Right resizes by 16px and Shift+Enter fits the column to its contents (as a double-click on its grip does); in the body Space toggles the row, Shift+Up and Shift+Down extend the range from the anchor, Ctrl or Cmd+A selects the page, and Escape clears a selection.
- Editing: Enter, F2, a double-click or a typed character opens the editor on an editable cell (typing replaces the value). Enter and Tab commit, Escape cancels and hands focus back to the cell. validate returns the message shown under the editor; return a promise from onCellEdit to show the cell saving, and reject it to put the old value back.
- Sorting is an action, not a live view: the order is taken when a heading is pressed or rows come and go, so an edited row stays under the hand that edited it until the next sort.
- Reduced motion: rows and cells fade in without travel, reorders, bands and the page pill settle at once, the sort glyph swaps on a short tween and the editor appears without lifting. Selection, order, widths and saved values still change.
- On a narrow container the pinned column takes at most about half the width so the columns beside it can scroll; the footer turns its page numbers into a compact count.
- Columns and rows are plain data: pass format for custom cells, and keep the default exports (defaultDataGridColumns, defaultDataGridRows) as a template for your own.

### Funnel Flow (KQ-1313) — `funnel-flow`
See where they slip away.

A conversion funnel drawn as a flow: stages are bars as long as the people who reached them, ribbons carry the ones who went on, and from each stage a drop-off branch peels away and fades. A seeded pool of particles runs it, and at each stage a particle goes on only if its lane falls inside the share that converted, so the dots split exactly as the people did; pointing at a stage freezes its particles where they are while the rest keep flowing and the details swap in on snap, and the segment switch re-weights every stage and branch on glide while particles already in flight follow their lanes onto the new shapes. The stages are a list of buttons named with full sentences: arrows move between them and freeze each, Enter pins, Escape unpins, and the segment is a radio group.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/funnel-flow`

Props:
