- `segment / defaultSegment`: string (default the first segment) — Which of segments the flow is weighted by. A change glides every stage and branch to its new size. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onSegmentChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the segment switch with the new segment's id.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the particles run, as a multiple of 64px a second.
- `stages`: FunnelStage[] (default defaultFunnelStages) — The stages in order, each an id and a label.
- `segments`: FunnelSegment[] (default defaultFunnelSegments) — The segments: id, label, the people who reached each stage, and optionally the median hours from the stage before and the top reason people left at each stage.
- `stage / defaultStage`: string | null (default null) — The pinned stage: frozen, with its details shown, until it is unpinned. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onStageChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the press or key that pinned or unpinned a stage.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds the particles' lanes and pace, so the same page always draws the same flow.
- `format`: (count: number) => string — Formats a count of people. Defaults to grouped digits in locale.
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The locale for counts.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the numbers have arrived: loading shows the funnel's skeleton, error a retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the numbers failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Conversion") — The heading.
- `subtitle`: string — A quieter line under the heading, before the first stage's count.
- `label`: string — The funnel's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish when the segment changes and a plip when a stage is pinned or the keyboard moves to it, pitched by how many of its people the stage keeps. Particles never sound.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the flow but refuses segment changes and pins.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the stages are one tab stop. Arrow keys move between them, Home and End jump, and the stage with focus freezes and shows its details; Enter or Space pins it, Escape unpins. The segment switch is a radio group whose arrows select.
- The particles run only while the funnel is on screen and the page is visible; under reduced motion they never move, and each ribbon and branch holds a still, seeded scatter of dots in the same proportions while the numbers and the freeze still work.
- Bars are drawn relative to the segment's own first stage, so switching segments compares conversion, not size; the counts on each stage say how many people that is.
- Lays out by its own width: on a phone the funnel stands up, labels in a column on the left and losses peeling right; from 560px it lies on its side with the losses below; from about 1090px a table of stages sits beside it. At most 560px tall; it scrolls inside its own box below that.
- Every stage, count, median and reason is data: keep defaultFunnelStages and defaultFunnelSegments as templates for your own.

### Status Board (KQ-1314) — `status-board`
Ninety days, one glance.

A service status board built from records: each service's strip of days grows up out of the baseline in one wave on glide, sweeping across and down the board a cascade apart, every bar coloured by the worst incident that touched it. Point at a strip, scrub it, or step it with the arrow keys and a lens rides to the day on snap with a card of what happened; select an incident and every strip it touched stamps a ring over its days on snap while its updates open on glide. Beside it a seeded p95 latency line advances live from now, gliding left a step per sample and pausing while it is read, over a dot-matrix map whose troubled regions pulse only while the board is on screen.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/status-board`

Props:
- `days`: number (default 90) — Days of history each service shows, 7 to 90. Changing it regrows the strips and recomputes every uptime figure.
- `live`: boolean (default true) — The latency sparkline takes a new seeded sample every interval while the board is on screen. Off: a snapshot at now.
- `regions`: boolean | StatusRegion[] (default true) — The regions panel: true for defaultStatusRegions, your own list, or false to leave it out.
- `services`: StatusService[] (default defaultStatusServices) — One row each: id, name, current status, and minutes of downtime per day ending today.
- `incidents`: StatusIncident[] (default defaultStatusIncidents) — What went wrong or was planned: title, impact (minor, major, maintenance), services, start, end (omit while open) and updates.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultStatusNow) — The board's moment: today's bar, the update time, open incidents and the latency feed all run from it.
- `latency`: StatusSample[] — Your own p95 series, oldest first. Omit it for a seeded series that advances from now; pass it and you advance it.
- `latencyWindow`: number (default 40) — Samples across the sparkline.
- `latencyTarget`: number (default 300) — The p95 target in ms: a dashed line, and the reading turns warn above it.
- `interval`: number (default 2000) — Milliseconds between seeded samples while live.
- `incident / defaultIncident`: string | null (default null) — The selected incident: its days are ringed on every strip it touched and its updates are open. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onIncidentChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the click, key or bar that selected or cleared an incident.
- `region / defaultRegion`: string | null (default null) — The region whose latency the sparkline shows, or null for all regions. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onRegionChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the chip, arrow key or map marker that chose a region.
- `onDaySelect`: (serviceId: string, date: string) => void — Enter on a day, or a click on its bar, with the service id and the day as YYYY-MM-DD.
- `incidentLimit`: number (default 3) — Incidents listed before Show more; a desktop-wide board, with the room, lists three more.
- `formatDate`: (ms: number) => string — Day labels. Defaults to "Sep 24" in UTC, so the server and the browser print the same.
- `formatTime`: (ms: number) => string — Clock labels. Defaults to "14:32" in UTC; latency samples add seconds.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the status has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed while status is "error".
- `title`: string (default "System status") — The board's heading; also its accessible name unless label is given.
- `label`: string — The board's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for each day stepped by key or scrub and for a region choice, a low buzz when you select a major outage. The live feed is always silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: days and samples still read out, nothing can be selected and the feed holds still.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is at most 560px tall and scrolls inside itself; pass a max-height class to change that.

Notes:
- Keyboard: each strip is a slider over its days with one tab stop for the board — Left and Right step a day, Page keys a week, Home and End the oldest day and today, Up and Down the neighbouring service, Enter selects the day and its incident, Escape clears it. The sparkline is a slider over its samples, the regions a radio group.
- The seeded latency feed only runs while the board is on screen, the page is visible and nobody is reading the line; it pauses ("Paused") while pointed at or focused. Pass latency to drive it yourself — a new last sample glides in the same way.
- Bar colours come from incidents first (the worst impact that touched the service that day), then from downtime nobody filed. Every colour is pigment, the same in light and dark.
- Under reduced motion the bars stand at full height, the lens, card and line step without travel, and troubled regions wear a still halo; uptime, latency and selection still change.
- Lays out by its own width: stacked on a phone (scrolling inside its box), services with the timeline beside a latency and regions column from 40rem, and three columns from 68rem.

### Filter Builder (KQ-1315) — `filter-builder`
Say exactly which rows you mean.

A query builder over typed rows: rules of field, condition and value in nested All / Any groups, each with a rail down its left edge. Switching a group slides its thumb on snap, re-colours the rail and rolls every and between its rows to or on snap a cascade apart, so the change runs down the group; rules arrive from zero height on glide and leave on the exit ease while the gap closes on glide. Every change re-runs the query and the count rolls to its new figure a digit at a time on snap, chips above summarise the query and lead back to their rows, and the controls are native selects and inputs in groups and radio groups.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/filter-builder`

Props:
- `nesting`: number (default 2) — How deep groups may nest, 0 to 3. At 0 the query is a flat list of rules with no Add group and no inner rails.
- `chips`: boolean (default true) — A strip of chips above the builder summarising each top-level rule or group; a chip focuses its row and its × removes it.
- `count`: "rows" | "share" | "off" (default "rows") — The result readout: a rolling row count, the share with a meter that glides to it, or none.
- `value / defaultValue`: FilterGroup (default defaultFilterQuery) — The query: a root group of rules and nested groups. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (query: FilterGroup) => void — Fires from the control that changed the query, with the whole new query.
- `fields`: FilterField[] (default defaultFilterFields) — What can be filtered on: id, label, type (text, number, enum, date, boolean), enum options, number prefix and suffix.
- `rows`: FilterRow[] (default defaultFilterRows) — The records the count and preview are taken over. The default is 2,400 seeded transactions.
- `matches`: number — A count from your server; overrides counting rows.
- `total`: number — The total from your server. Defaults to rows.length.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultFilterNow) — Where "in the last N days" counts back from.
- `onApply`: (query: FilterGroup) => void — The footer's Show button, and Enter in a value. Without it there is no Show button.
- `applyLabel`: string (default "Show") — The Show button's verb; the count follows it.
- `maxRules`: number (default 12) — Rules allowed in the whole query; the Add buttons disable at the limit.
- `noun`: { one: string; other: string } (default { one: "row", other: "rows" }) — What a row is called in the count and its announcement.
- `formatCount`: (n: number) => string — Counts as text. Defaults to grouped digits in en-US, so the server and the browser print the same.
- `renderRow`: (row: FilterRow) => ReactNode — One row of the desktop preview. Defaults to the first text field, a few others as meta, and the first number on the right.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the count has arrived, for a server count: Counting… while loading, Count unavailable with Try again on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed while status is "error".
- `title`: string (default "Filters") — The builder's heading; also its accessible name unless label is given.
- `label`: string — The builder's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A click for each field, condition or match change, a pop for each rule or group added and a lower one for each removed. Typing is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: the query shows and nothing changes.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is at most 560px tall and its body scrolls between a fixed header and footer.

Notes:
- Keyboard: every rule is three native controls and a remove button in tab order; All / Any is a radio group on the arrow keys; Enter in a value applies. A new rule takes focus on its field the moment it arrives, and a removed one hands focus to its neighbour or to the group's Add button.
- Rules without a usable value are drawn dashed and left out of the count (a bad number is marked invalid); a group with nothing left in it lets every row through. matchFilter(query, row, fields, now) is exported to run the same logic on your side.
- The count is announced politely once typing settles (half a second); adding, removing and clearing are announced at once.
- Under reduced motion rows and chips fade without travel, digits swap instead of rolling and joiners swap without the flip; the count, the meter and focus still move.
- Lays out by its own width: rules on two lines on a phone, one line from 40rem, and a preview of the newest matching rows beside the builder from 68rem.

### Cohort Grid (KQ-1316) — `cohort-grid`
Who stayed, week by week.

A cohort retention triangle built from weekly cohorts: cells fill in on snap along the diagonals, the rows or the columns, the whole sweep inside 600ms, and a Users / Revenue switch slides its thumb on snap and recolours the grid in the same order. Pointing at a cell or stepping with the arrow keys lays a row band and a column band through it that ride between cells on snap, while the curve above, sharing the grid's week columns, morphs from the size-weighted average to that cohort on glide and carries on as a dashed projection past the weeks it has lived. It is a real grid with one tab stop: arrows walk the triangle, Home and End reach a row's ends, Enter pins a cohort and Escape lets it go.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cohort-grid`

Props:
- `cascade`: "diagonal" | "rows" | "columns" (default "diagonal") — The order the cells fill in and recolour in. Changing it replays the fill.
- `metric / defaultMetric`: "users" | "revenue" (default "users") — What the cells measure: users retained as a share of the cohort, or revenue as a share of week 0 (which can pass 100%). Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onMetricChange`: (metric: "users" | "revenue") => void — Fires from the switch or arrow key that changed the metric.
- `curve`: "area" | "line" | "off" (default "area") — The summary curve over the grid: filled, a line, or none.
- `cohorts`: Cohort[] (default defaultCohorts) — One per week of sign-ups, oldest first: id, start (YYYY-MM-DD), size, and users and revenue per week since.
- `weeks`: number — Week columns shown. Defaults to the longest cohort, at most 12.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultCohortNow) — Today: the week each cohort is living through is hatched in progress and left out of the averages.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string | null (default null) — The pinned cohort: the curve and the side panel hold it when the pointer leaves. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onSelectedChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from the click or key that pinned or unpinned a cohort.
- `onCellSelect`: (cohortId: string, week: number) => void — Enter on a cell, or a click on it.
- `onCrosshairChange`: (cell: { cohortId: string; week: number } | null) => void — The crosshair moved to a cell by pointer or key, or left the grid. Use it to link other views.
- `format`: (value: number, metric: "users" | "revenue") => string — A cell's value, a share (0.31 is 31%), as text. Defaults to a whole percent.
- `formatMoney`: (amount: number) => string — Money in the readouts and the side panel. Defaults to whole US dollars, en-US.
- `formatDate`: (iso: string) => string — Cohort labels. Defaults to "Aug 3", in UTC.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the cohorts have arrived: a skeleton triangle while loading, a message with Try again on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed while status is "error".
- `title`: string (default "Retention") — The grid's heading; also its accessible name unless label is given.
- `label`: string — The grid's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for each cell you step to or click, pitched by its value, and one for a metric switch.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: cells still read out; nothing pins and the metric is fixed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is at most 560px tall and scrolls inside itself.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the heatmap is a grid with one tab stop. Arrows walk the triangle (Down into a younger cohort lands on its last week), Home and End reach a row's ends, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the corners, Page Up and Page Down five cohorts, Enter or Space pins the cohort, Escape unpins it. Every cell is named in full: "Aug 3 cohort, week 4: 31%, 402 of 1,297 users".
- The week a cohort is still living through (from now) is hatched and left out of the averages and the curve, which projects it along the average's shape instead.
- Cells are pigment mixed into the card in oklab — cobalt for users, signal for revenue — so the ramp reads the same in light and dark; strong cells switch to light text.
- Under reduced motion the cells appear together, the recolour is a short fade with no sweep, and the bands and the curve jump to their place; values, the crosshair and the pinned cohort still change.
- Lays out by its own width: on a phone the grid scrolls sideways inside its box with the cohort column held, KPI tiles join from 40rem, and a side panel with the focused cohort and the key from 68rem.

### Activity Stream (KQ-1317) — `activity-stream`
Everything that just happened.

A live activity feed where new events gather behind an "N new" pill instead of shoving the list under the reader: the faces behind them land on the pill on recoil and the count rolls on snap. Pressing it scrolls the feed to its top on glide and releases them in a cascade while everything below glides down, each revealed line keeping a wash that fades over two seconds; switching the grouping between person, type and none glides every line to its new seat, and relative times tick on a timer set for the next boundary any line will cross. The list is a role="feed" of articles with one roving tab stop — Up and Down move between lines, Page keys between articles, Home and End to the ends, Enter opens — and the kind chips are toggle buttons.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/activity-stream`

Props:
- `rate`: number (default 12) — How many events arrive per minute from incoming while live; 0 stops arrivals. Sets how fast the pill fills.
- `group`: "actor" | "kind" | "none" (default "actor") — How the feed groups: consecutive events by one person, by one type, or one article per event. Changing it glides every line to its new seat.
- `pill`: "avatars" | "count" | "off" (default "avatars") — How new events wait: behind a pill of faces and a rolling count, behind a plain count, or not at all — they slide in at the top as they land.
- `events`: ActivityEvent[] (default defaultActivityEvents) — The history, in any order: id, actor, kind, action, target, detail and at (Date or ms). Ids added after mount wait behind the pill like arrivals.
- `incoming`: ActivityIncoming[] (default defaultActivityIncoming) — Events still to come (no time yet), released in order at rate and stamped with the stream's clock; the list loops with fresh ids.
- `actors`: ActivityActor[] (default defaultActivityActors) — Who can act: id, name, an optional role shown in group headers and an optional tint (any CSS colour) for the avatar.
- `kinds`: ActivityKind[] (default defaultActivityKinds) — What can happen: id, label, plural and an optional 16px icon. Each kind present becomes a filter chip with its count.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultActivityNow) — The time the stream starts from. Relative times are measured from it, never from the wall clock during render.
- `live`: boolean (default true) — The clock runs on from now in real time and incoming arrives. Off: the clock holds and nothing arrives.
- `filter / defaultFilter`: string[] (default []) — The kind ids shown; empty shows everything. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onFilterChange`: (kinds: string[]) => void — Fires from the chip that changed the filter, with the new kind ids.
- `onReveal`: (events: ActivityEvent[]) => void — The pill was pressed: fires with the events it brought into the feed, newest first.
- `onArrive`: (event: ActivityEvent) => void — An incoming event arrived, stamped with the stream's clock.
- `onOpen`: (event: ActivityEvent) => void — A line was pressed or opened with Enter.
- `groupWindow`: number (default 30) — Consecutive events further apart than this many minutes start a new group.
- `collapseAfter`: number (default 3) — Lines a group shows before a Show N more disclosure, whose height glides open to what its lines measure.
- `height`: number (default 560) — The panel's height in px; the feed scrolls inside it.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the history has arrived: loading shows a skeleton and marks the feed busy, error a retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the history failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Activity") — The panel's heading.
- `label`: string — The panel's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `emptyLabel`: string (default "No activity yet.") — What an empty feed says.
- `formatTime`: (at: Date) => string — The absolute time in a line's title. Defaults to a fixed, locale-free "30 Sep, 14:05 UTC".
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a plip for filter chips and Show more, and a pop when the pill reveals. Arrivals and ticks are always silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the feed but refuses filters, reveals and opens; arrivals keep gathering.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the feed has one tab stop. Up and Down move between lines and Show more buttons, Page Down and Page Up jump to the next or previous article, Home and End to the ends, Enter opens a line. The pill is a button named with its count; revealing from the keyboard moves focus to the newest revealed line.
- Feed it either way: let the component release a scripted incoming list at rate (looped with fresh ids), or set live={false} and append to events yourself — new ids wait behind the pill exactly like arrivals.
- Times come from now plus the stream's own running clock, so server and browser render the same markup; the clock pauses its updates while the page is hidden or the feed is off screen and catches up when it returns.
- A polite status speaks once when updates start waiting, once per reveal and once per filter change — never per arrival or clock tick.
- Reduced motion: the feed simply lists. Arrivals, reveals and regrouping swap in place, the count changes without rolling and the pill fades; the fresh wash still fades, because what is new is information.
- Lays out by its own width: chips in a scrolling row on a phone, a sidebar of kind filters and people from 640px, and an hourly histogram with each line's detail inline from about 1090px.

### Region Map (KQ-1318) — `region-map`
Pick a region; the map leans in.

A choropleth of invented regions with the numbers behind every colour. Picking a region leans the map toward it: the camera — centre and scale written into the SVG viewBox — glides on glide to frame it, the region lifts above its neighbours on snap with a flat shadow while the rest dim, and the side panel swaps the ranking for the region's numbers and trend, with Previous and Next travelling region to region by rank. The legend is a slider you scrub: a bracket follows the finger 1:1 and lights only the regions inside the band, then springs onto the class under it on snap with the throw's velocity. The map is a listbox where arrows move to the nearest region in that direction, Enter picks and Escape leans out; the legend takes arrows, Home, End and Escape.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/region-map`

Props:
- `zoom`: number (default 2.5) — How far the map leans in on a picked region, from 1 (it stays put and only highlights) to 4.
- `legend`: "steps" | "ramp" (default "steps") — Stepped classes or a continuous ramp — for the fills, the legend, and how a scrubbed band snaps (to a class, or wherever it is let go).
- `scheme`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "heat" | "diverging" (default "cobalt") — The colour scheme: one hue, a warm heat ramp, or a diverging pair around zero for changes. Fills are pigment mixed into the card colour, so both themes read.
- `regions`: RegionMapRegion[] (default defaultRegionMapRegions) — The regions as SVG paths in the map's viewBox: id, name, d, and an optional box ([x, y, width, height], measured from the path when omitted) and label point. The default is fourteen regions generated once from seeded points.
- `viewBox`: [number, number, number, number] (default defaultRegionMapViewBox) — The map's extent: what the camera shows when nothing is picked.
- `stats`: RegionMapStat[] (default defaultRegionMapStats) — What is measured: id, label, kind (count, money, percent as a fraction, or number), an optional unit word and signed for changes. Each becomes a metric option and a row in the details panel.
- `data`: RegionMapDatum[] (default defaultRegionMapData) — One datum per region: its values per stat id and optional trends (recent readings, oldest first) drawn in the details panel. Regions without a datum read as no data.
- `metric / defaultMetric`: string (default the first stat) — The stat id the map is coloured and ranked by. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onMetricChange`: (metric: string) => void — Fires from the metric switch with the new stat id. A band is cleared with it, since it was in the old metric's units.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default null) — The picked region the map leans toward, or null for the whole map. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host change moves the camera the same way a click does.
- `onValueChange`: (region: string | null) => void — Fires from the click, key or button that picked a region, or with null when the map leans out.
- `band / defaultBand`: [number, number] | null (default null) — The [low, high] values the legend highlights; regions outside it fade back. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onBandChange`: (band: [number, number] | null) => void — Fires when a scrub settles, a tap or key moves the band, or it is cleared.
- `steps`: number (default 5) — Classes in the stepped legend, 3 to 7, laid on round numbers that hold every value.
- `format`: (value: number, stat: RegionMapStat) => string — How a value reads in the tooltip, the panel and the spoken text. Defaults to the stat's kind in locale.
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The locale for numbers and money.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — The currency for money stats.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the numbers have arrived: loading shows a skeleton, error a retry over the map.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the numbers failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Regions") — The map's heading.
- `subtitle`: string — A quieter line under the heading.
- `label`: string — The map's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 580) — The tallest the surface grows, in px; it scrolls inside itself past that (the phone layout does).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish whenever the camera moves, panned to the region, and a plip as a scrubbed band crosses into a new class.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the map and its numbers but refuses picks, bands and metric changes.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the map is one tab stop (a listbox with an active region). Arrows move to the nearest region in that direction, Home and End to the first and last by rank, Enter or Space picks, Escape leans out — or, with nothing picked, clears the band. The legend is a slider: arrows move the band a class (or a tenth of a ramp), Page keys two, Home and End to the ends, Escape or Delete clears it. The ranking rows take Up, Down, Home and End.
- Bring your own geography: pass regions as SVG paths in your viewBox. Give each a box when you can; without one it is measured from the rendered path once, after mount.
- The default map is generated once from seeded points with arithmetic only — no trigonometry — so the server and every browser draw the same coast to the last digit.
- A polite status speaks once per pick, band and metric change, never while a scrub is moving.
- Reduced motion: the camera cuts instead of travelling, the picked region does not lift (its outline and the dimming still mark it), the panel swaps on opacity and the bracket jumps to its class. Colours, bands and numbers are unchanged.
- Lays out by its own width: stacked with the top five regions on a phone, map and a 15rem panel side by side from 640px, and a wider map with summary figures over a 20rem panel from about 1090px.

### Tree Map (KQ-1319) — `tree-map`
Zoom into where it adds up.

A spending treemap you zoom into with a real relayout. Every node has a rectangle in every view — squarified fresh for the plot's shape inside the focus, and the root's layout seen through the camera outside it — so a zoom glides each tile on glide from where it was to where it goes: the chosen category opens out to fill the plot while its children re-squarify into the new shape, siblings fly off past the edges and fade on the exit ease, and grandchildren grow out of their parent's old box; breadcrumbs reverse it. Labels are decided from each tile's final size and fade as they come and go, and a readout names the tile under the pointer. The tiles are buttons with one roving tab stop: arrows move to the nearest tile in that direction, Enter zooms in or selects a leaf, Backspace and Escape zoom out, and focus lands on the tile you came out of.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tree-map`

Props:
- `depth`: number (default 2) — How many levels the view draws below the node in focus, 1 to 3: 1 is flat tiles, 2 and 3 frame each tile with a header and nest its children inside.
- `labels`: "full" | "name" | "off" (default "full") — Tile labels: name, amount and share where they fit (fewer lines where they do not, none on slivers); the name alone; or none.
- `palette`: "category" | "size" | "change" (default "category") — How tiles are coloured: a hue per top-level category shaded by rank, one hue by share of the focus, or warm for spend that grew and green for spend that shrank.
- `data`: TreeMapNode (default defaultTreeMapData) — The tree: id, name, children, and on leaves a value and an optional previous value. A parent's amount is the sum of its children; color overrides the palette for a branch.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the root's id) — The id of the node the view is zoomed into. Controlled or uncontrolled; an id that is not a parent falls back to the root.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the tile, crumb or key that zoomed, with the new focus id.
- `onSelect`: (node: TreeMapNode, path: TreeMapNode[]) => void — A leaf was pressed or chosen with Enter, with the path from the root down to it.
- `format`: (value: number) => string — How an amount reads in tiles, the readout, the table and spoken names. Defaults to whole currency in locale.
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The locale for amounts and shares.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — The currency for amounts.
- `period`: string (default "Q3 2026") — The period the amounts cover, shown beside the total.
- `compareLabel`: string (default "last quarter") — What the change is measured against, in the readout and spoken names.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the numbers have arrived: loading shows a skeleton of blocks, error a retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the numbers failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Spend") — The heading.
- `label`: string — The accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish on every zoom (higher in, lower out) and a click for a leaf, a crumb or a keyboard move.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the spend but refuses zooms and selections.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the top-level tiles are one tab stop. Arrows move to the nearest tile in that direction, Home and End to the largest and smallest, Enter or Space zooms in (or selects a leaf), Backspace and Escape zoom out — Escape only when there is a level to leave. After a zoom, focus lands on the first tile, or on the tile you came out of.
- A press anywhere inside a top-level tile — on a nested tile too — acts on that tile, so depth 2 and 3 are previews of what a zoom will show.
- The layout is squarified with arithmetic only, from the plot's measured size: the server renders a 2:1 layout and the browser settles to its own shape at once, without animating.
- A polite status speaks each zoom and selection once; the readout under the plot is visual, and every tile carries its full reading in its name.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels — the new view cross-fades in over the old one, leaving tiles fading where they stood. Labels, colours and the readout are unchanged.
- Lays out by its own width: a 4:5 plot with crumbs that scroll on a phone, a 2:1 plot with the palette key from 640px, and a ranked table of the focus's children beside it from about 1090px.

### Chart Morph (KQ-1320) — `chart-morph`
One dataset, any shape.

A multi-series chart whose type is a shape the data takes, not a different drawing. Each series is one path rebuilt every frame from a few motion values — per point a flat top joined to the next by cubics that are either a notch to the floor or the curve between the points, plus a dot — so bars, line, area and dots are four settings of the same numbers, and a type change moves the points in a left-to-right sweep on glide: bars narrow and their notches rise into the curve, dots swell from the line or bars retract into them. The window, the y scale and each series' visibility glide too, gridlines riding the scale, and a cursor snaps to the nearest point on snap with a ring per series and a readout beside it. The type switch is a radio group, the legend toggle buttons, and the plot a slider: arrows step the cursor, Page keys three, Home and End to the ends, Escape clears it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/chart-morph`

Props:
- `type / defaultType`: "bar" | "line" | "area" | "dot" (default "bar") — The chart type. Changing it morphs the same points into the new shape in a left-to-right sweep. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onTypeChange`: (type: "bar" | "line" | "area" | "dot") => void — Fires from the type switch with the new type.
- `smooth`: number (default 0.5) — Curve tension for the line and the area, 0 (straight segments) to 1 (monotone curves that never overshoot a reading); bars round their corners by it.
- `points`: number (default 12) — How many of the latest readings are shown, from 2 to all of them. A change glides the window, so points slide in from the left or out past it.
- `series`: ChartMorphSeries[] (default defaultChartMorphSeries) — The series: id, label, values (one per label, oldest first) and an optional colour (any CSS colour; defaults to the house pigments).
- `labels`: string[] (default defaultChartMorphLabels) — One label per reading, oldest first, such as "Sep 2026". The axis shows the first word; the readout and spoken text the whole label.
- `hidden / defaultHidden`: string[] (default []) — Series ids toggled off in the legend. A hidden series flattens to the floor and fades while the others re-dodge. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onHiddenChange`: (hidden: string[]) => void — Fires from the legend with the new hidden ids. The last visible series refuses to hide.
- `onCursorChange`: (index: number | null) => void — The point under the cursor changed (an index into labels), or the cursor left.
- `wave`: number (default 0.5) — How far a type change sweeps across the points, 0 (all at once) to 1 (a full left-to-right wave).
- `format`: (value: number) => string — How a reading prints on the axis, the legend, the readout and in spoken text. Defaults to compact currency in locale.
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The locale for readings.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — The currency for readings.
- `title`: string (default "Volume") — The chart's heading.
- `subtitle`: string — A quieter line under the heading, before the latest total.
- `label`: string — The chart's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the readings have arrived: loading shows a skeleton of bars, error a retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the readings failed to load.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish on a type change, pitched by type, and a tick when the cursor reaches a new point or a series is toggled.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the chart but refuses type, series and cursor changes.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the type switch is a radio group (arrows move and select). The legend's series are toggle buttons. The plot is a slider over the visible points: Left and Right step the cursor (the first press lands on the latest point), Page Up and Page Down move three, Home and End jump to the ends, and Escape clears the cursor — only when there is one.
- Every type is the same geometry with different numbers, so a change in the middle of another carries on from the shapes on screen rather than restarting.
- The y scale rounds up to three to five even steps over the visible series in the window; hiding a series or changing points glides it, and each gridline keeps its value as it moves.
- The plot's aria-valuetext reads the cursor's label and every visible series' value; a polite status speaks type and series changes once.
- Reduced motion: types, windows, scales and series change at once behind a 150ms fade of the marks; the cursor and its readout jump. Every value still updates.
- Lays out by its own width: an icon-only type switch and a 200px plot on a phone, a labelled switch and a 300px plot from 640px, and a summary table of each series' total, average and change beside the plot from about 1090px.

### Setup Checklist (KQ-1321) — `setup-checklist`
Getting started, one step at a time.

An onboarding checklist whose steps open into their own inline action — a field, a choice or one button — on glide to a measured height, while the open step is lifted out as a raised card that travels between rows on glide, placed from the rows' own motion values so it tracks them exactly as they open and close. Finishing a step fills its disc on snap, draws its check on flick and fills the progress ring's share on glide; a beat later the next unfinished step slides into focus, and the last one lands the all-set state with seeded sparks and a check stamped on recoil before Dismiss folds the list into one line. The headers are an accordion: Up and Down move, Enter and Space open, Escape closes a step and returns focus to its header.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/setup-checklist`

Props:
- `steps`: SetupStep[] (default defaultSetupSteps) — The steps in order: title, description, minutes, optional flag and the inline action (button, field or choice) each opens into.
- `value / defaultValue`: SetupProgress (default {}) — Which steps are done or skipped, by id. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: SetupProgress) => void — Fires from the action, Skip or key that finished a step, with the whole new progress.
- `open / defaultOpen`: string | null (default the first unfinished step) — The open step, or null for none. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when a header press, a key or the advance after a finished step opens another.
- `dismissed / defaultDismissed`: boolean (default false) — Folds the checklist away into a one-line bar with a Show button. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onDismissedChange`: (dismissed: boolean) => void — Fires from Dismiss, Skip setup for now, and the bar's Show.
- `onAction`: (stepId: string, input?: string) => void | Promise<void> — Runs a step's action with the field's text or the chosen option's id. A returned promise holds the button pending; a rejection's message is shown on the step. Without it, actions finish at once.
- `onSkip`: (stepId: string) => void — An optional step was skipped. A skipped step counts as finished and can still be done later.
- `ring`: "arc" | "segments" | "ticks" (default "arc") — How progress is drawn: one round stroke, one arc per step, or a dial of forty ticks.
- `expand`: "lift" | "inline" (default "lift") — The open step as a raised card that travels between steps, or flush in the list with an accent bar that travels.
- `celebrate`: "burst" | "stamp" | "quiet" (default "burst") — The all-set moment: seeded sparks with a stamped check, the whole ring landing on recoil, or colour alone.
- `advance`: boolean (default true) — Finishing a step opens the next unfinished one and moves keyboard focus to it.
- `title`: string (default "Get started") — The heading and the region's accessible name.
- `subtitle`: string — The line under the heading.
- `doneTitle`: string (default "You're all set") — The heading once every step is finished.
- `doneBody`: string — The line under it.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholder rows; error offers Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — The Retry button of the error state.
- `label`: string — The region's accessible name, when it should differ from the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a plip as a step you finished checks off, rising with progress, and a chime when your action finishes the list. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the checklist but takes no presses or keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is content-sized; give it a height and it scrolls inside, bringing each newly opened step into view.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the step headers are an accordion. Up and Down move between them, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens and closes, Escape inside an open step closes it and returns focus to its header. Choice actions are a radiogroup: arrows select. After a step finishes, focus follows the advance to the next step's header, or to Dismiss when the list is done.
- Reduced motion: nothing glides or bounces. Bodies open at once, the lift moves at once, no sparks and no stamp, and the check appears whole — but the ring still takes its new share on a short tween and the count still changes, because progress is the information.
- Actions are yours: return a promise from onAction and the step's button holds a pending label at its own width until it settles; reject with an Error and its message is shown on the step as an alert. Email fields are checked before onAction is called.
- Layout follows the component's own width: under 640px the ring sits beside the title above the list; from 640px a summary column holds a large ring and Skip setup for now; from 960px an open step lays its description and its action side by side.
- Progress is controlled through value / onValueChange as a map of step id to "done" or "skipped", so it persists however your app stores onboarding state. Announcements are made from the value the host renders, so a host that refuses a change is never announced.

### Sign In (KQ-1322) — `sign-in`
In, by whichever way you like.

An authentication card: email first under generic single sign-on buttons, then a choice of method, a code or a password slides in from 16px on glide while the card's height glides to the new step and the step pips widen on snap. The code is one real input drawn as cells — a ring slides on snap to the cell the next digit lands in, digits land on snap, a paste fills them all, and a full code verifies itself under a travelling wave — while a refused field shakes on a symmetric tween, never a spring, and an accepted sign-in flies the button that finished it into the welcome's avatar on glide. Every step is a real form: Enter submits, Escape goes back a step, and focus moves to each step's first field as it arrives.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sign-in`

Props:
- `steps`: "choose" | "code" | "password" (default "choose") — What follows the email: a choice of method, straight to an emailed code, or straight to a password.
- `shake`: number (default 8) — How far a refused field shakes, in px; 0 for no shake.
- `cells`: number (default 6) — How many digits the sign-in code has, 4 to 8.
- `brand`: string (default "Fernworks") — The product's name, in the heading and the accessible name.
- `mark`: React.ReactNode — The product's mark, 32px. Defaults to the brand's initial on a tile.
- `providers`: SignInProvider[] (default defaultSignInProviders) — Single sign-on buttons above the email field, each with a label and an icon; an empty list hides them.
- `aside`: SignInAside | null (default defaultSignInAside) — The brand panel beside the form from 640px wide: heading, line, points, and a quote from 960px. Null for none.
- `email / defaultEmail`: string (default "") — The email address. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onEmailChange`: (email: string) => void — Fires as the email is typed.
- `step / defaultStep`: "email" | "method" | "code" | "password" | "welcome" (default "email") — The step on show. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onStepChange`: (step: SignInStep) => void — Fires from the press or key that moved the flow, before the new step shows.
- `onEmailSubmit`: (email: string) => void | Promise<void> — Checks the email before the next step; reject with an Error to refuse it with your message.
- `onSendCode`: (email: string) => void | Promise<void> — Sends the code and its link; called again by Resend.
- `onVerifyCode`: (email: string, code: string) => void | Promise<SignInAccount | void> — Checks a complete code. Reject to refuse it; resolve with the account to welcome it by name.
- `onVerifyPassword`: (email: string, password: string) => void | Promise<SignInAccount | void> — Checks a password, the same way.
- `onProvider`: (providerId: string) => void | Promise<SignInAccount | void> — Runs a single sign-on button, the same way.
- `onSuccess`: (account: SignInAccount) => void — Fires the moment a sign-in is accepted, with the account.
- `onForgotPassword`: (email: string) => void — The Forgot password link on the password step.
- `onCreateAccount`: () => void — The Create an account link under the email step.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click on presses, a buzz on a refusal and a chime as the welcome lands. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the card but takes no input.
- `label`: string — The group's accessible name. Defaults to "Sign in to" and the brand.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. The card is content-sized and lays itself out by its own width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: every step is a real form, so Tab moves through it and Enter submits. Escape goes back a step. Focus moves to each step's first control as it arrives — the email field, the first method, the code input, the password — and to the welcome heading at the end.
- The code is a single input with autocomplete="one-time-code" drawn as cells, so a paste (even "123-456"), an SMS autofill and Backspace all behave natively; a press on a filled cell selects that digit so the next one replaces it. A full code verifies itself.
- Reduced motion: panels cross-fade in place and the height changes at once, nothing shakes and nothing flies — the danger border and the message still say what was refused, and the welcome fades in with its avatar already in place.
- Every network step is your callback. Reject with an Error and its message is shown under the field as an alert; resolve a verifying callback with { name, email } and the welcome greets them by first name. The card never invents an account.
- Layout follows the component's own width: under 640px the card stands alone; from 640px a brand panel sits beside it; from 960px the panel widens and shows its quote.

What you get, and when you pay.

A paywall whose comparison shows what the chosen plan unlocks: those rows light in a cascade and their locks lift open on snap, and a plan change re-lights only the rows that changed while the chosen column's cells roll and, in the all-plans view, a band slides across to the new column on snap. Plan and billing are radiogroups with pills that slide on snap, every price rolls digit by digit, and the trial is drawn as a track from today to the first charge whose span sweeps in on glide, ticking off each day, with the reminder above it. The purchase button holds its width through pending, success and error — success stamps its check on recoil and turns the track and the unlocked rows green — and the plan and billing groups take arrow keys while the comparison is a real table.

- `onDismiss`: () => void — The Not now button in the corner. Hidden without it.
- `title`: string (default "Upgrade to keep your dashboards live") — The heading and the region's accessible name.
- `subtitle`: string — The line under it: why the wall is here.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholders; error offers Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — The Retry button of the error state.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click on plan and billing changes and a chime when your purchase lands. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the wall but takes no input.
- `label`: string — The region's accessible name, when it should differ from the title.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is h-[560px] by default; pass a height to change it — the columns scroll inside.

Notes:

Return a promise and the button holds Starting trial… at its own width, announced politely; reject with an Error and its message appears under the button, and a plan or billing change clears it. Or drive the button yourself through state and onStateChange.
- Layout follows the component's own width: under 640px one scrolling column with the price and the button in a footer; from 640px the summary (price, timeline, button) gets its own column; from 960px the plan switch becomes plan cards with prices.
- Dates on the timeline come from now, trialDays and reminderDays, printed as UTC days. Amounts go through format, so a different currency or locale is one function.

Cards, invoices and the next bill.

A billing settings panel built from data: the cards on file are a deck that sits in a pile and fans out like a hand, unfolds into wallet strips, or lies flat, every pose a glide from one function of the deck's measured width; Make default lifts the chosen card, slides it to the front on glide and the Default tag slides across to it on snap. - `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "comfortable" (default "regular") — Padding, invoice row height and how much each row says: one line, two, or two plus its description.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the billing data has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.

### Settings Form (KQ-1325) — `settings-form`
Change what you want; keep what you did.

A settings form built from typed sections that knows what you changed: a changed field grows an edge bar on snap with a bloom of accent washing into its row, and a save bar slides up on snap counting the changes, its digit rolling as fields change and come back. Discard plays every change backwards — text un-types and re-types, a switch's knob slides home, a choice's indicator slides back, a select's label rolls back down, a range's thumb glides home — newest edit first; Save waits on a promise, then confirms field by field with a check drawn on flick while the count rolls down, and fields the save refuses shake and keep their message. Enter and Ctrl/⌘+S save, Escape takes a changed text field back, every field has its Revert, and each control is native or a real widget.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/settings-form`

Props:
- `sections`: SettingsSection[] (default defaultSettingsSections) — The form: sections with a title, a line of help and fields — text (with prefix and validate), textarea, switch, choice, select or range — each with its own defaultValue.
- `value / defaultValue`: SettingsValues — The saved values, by field id: what the draft is compared against. Controlled or uncontrolled; fields left out use their own defaultValue (settingsValuesOf builds the full set).
- `defaultDraft`: SettingsValues — Edits to start from over the saved values — a draft restored from an earlier visit. They count as changes: the fields glow and the bar is up from the first render.
- `onValueChange`: (values: SettingsValues) => void — Fires when a save lands, with every saved value. Fields the save refused keep their old value.
- `onDraftChange`: (draft: SettingsValues, dirty: string[]) => void — Fires on every change to the draft — edits, reverts and each field a rewind brings back — with the ids that differ from what is saved.
- `onSave`: (changes: SettingsChange[], draft: SettingsValues) => void | { errors?: Record<string, string> } | Promise<…> — Save was pressed (or Ctrl/⌘+S, or Enter in a text field). A promise holds the bar in Saving; resolve with { errors } to refuse some fields with a message, reject to keep everything changed.
- `onDiscard`: (changes: SettingsChange[]) => void — Discard was pressed, with the changes being undone, in the order they will rewind.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How far and how bright a changed field's edge glows into its row, 0 to 1. 0 keeps only the edge bar.
- `bar`: "dock" | "float" | "inline" (default "dock") — Where the save bar lives: docked to the panel's bottom edge, a floating pill above it, or in the flow at the form's end.
- `rewind`: "sequence" | "together" | "instant" (default "sequence") — How Discard undoes: each field plays its change backwards newest edit first, all fields at once, or every value swaps back at once with only the glow fading.
- `rewindDuration`: number (default 520) — The longest one field's rewind may take, in ms. Short text rewinds faster.
- `confirmStagger`: number (default 110) — Time between fields confirming after a save, in ms.
- `savedHold`: number (default 1400) — How long "All changes saved" stays before the bar leaves, in ms.
- `title`: string (default "Settings") — The panel's heading; also its accessible name unless label is given. Focus lands here when the bar leaves with focus inside it.
- `description`: string — A line under the heading.
- `label`: string — The panel's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `saveLabel`: string (default "Save") — The Save button's text.
- `discardLabel`: string (default "Discard") — The Discard button's text.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the saved values have arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed while status is "error".
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Clicks for Save, Discard and Revert, a softer falling click as each rewound field lands, and a pop for each field a save you started confirms.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: every control is disabled and no bar appears.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall and scrolls inside itself, the dock and float bars sticky to its bottom; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: every control is native or a real widget — inputs, textarea, select, role="switch" buttons, a radiogroup with roving radios, a role="slider" with arrows, Page keys, Home and End. Enter in a text field and Ctrl/⌘+S save; Escape in a changed text field rewinds that field; each changed field has a Revert button named for it.
- The draft lives in the form; the saved values can be yours (value + onValueChange). onSave receives the changes and the whole draft; resolve with { errors: { slug: "That address is taken." } } and those fields shake, show the message and stay changed while the rest confirm.
- Validation runs per text field through validate(value); a field with a message cannot be saved — Save shakes it and moves focus there.
- Under reduced motion nothing travels: values swap back at once, the glow fades in and out, the bar fades in place, and fields still confirm one by one with a static check, because what was saved is the information.
- Lays out by its own width: label above control on a phone; label and help beside the control from 40rem; from 68rem a section nav with a changed count per section and a Changes panel listing each change with its own Revert.

Categories are a radiogroup on the arrow keys; "/" jumps to the search and Escape clears it.

- Keyboard: the thumbnails are a tablist (arrows, Home, End); the picture panel takes Left and Right to change picture, Enter to open the loupe, arrows (Shift for further) to move it and Escape to put it away. Colours and sizes are radio groups whose arrow keys move and choose.
- Pictures are render functions of { colour, size }, drawn again inside the loupe at its power, so vector art stays sharp; give a size a scale and the piece grows from its foot when it is chosen.
- Add to bag morphs into the stepper in the same box and focus moves to + as it arrives; − at one runs the morph backwards and returns focus to Add to bag.
- The docked bar watches the buy row against the component's own scroll box: cap the region's height (max-h) so it scrolls, or the bar never needs to show.
- Reduced motion: the glaze and the pictures cross-fade, sizes swap without growing, the loupe fades (it still follows the pointer), the price swaps digits; every choice is still shown and announced.
- Delivery dates come from estimate(postcode, now), counted from the now prop, so server and browser render the same words.

### Cart Drawer (KQ-1332) — `cart-drawer`
Everything in the bag, in one pull.

A bag that slides over the page it belongs to: the panel arrives from the right edge on glide over a fading scrim and can be pulled shut by its header, 1:1 with a rubber-banded overpull and a release or flick that closes on glide with the throw's velocity. Each line's face slides over a tray of actions — Save and Remove, or in full mode a pull right through that removes it — a removed line leaves on the exit ease while its height closes on glide and Undo keeps it for six seconds, steppers roll their counts on snap, and the totals roll, count or cross-fade as anything changes. A bar fills toward free delivery on glide with a van on its leading edge, and when the visitor carries the subtotal over the threshold the bar turns success, flecks spray from its end and the news lands on recoil; Escape closes a tray then the drawer, and every swipe has a button that does the same thing.

Notes:

### Order Tracker (KQ-1334) — `order-tracker`
Where it is, right now.

An order tracking surface where one progress value drives everything: the live dot rides the shipment's path between stages on glide as `now` advances, the path fills behind it through a sweeping clip, and on the map strip the van rides its route while the strip pans to keep it centred; reaching the door lands a check on recoil. Grab the dot and it scrubs the history 1:1 — fill, van and a time chip rewinding with it, ticking at every scan — then settles on the nearest scan with the release velocity, while the delivery window rolls digit by digit on snap and Change opens a measured disclosure on glide. The path is a slider: arrow keys step through the scans, Home goes to the first, End and Escape come back to now.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/order-tracker`

Props:
- `path`: "rail" | "road" | "arc" (default "road") — The progress track's shape: a straight rail, a winding road whose bends the stages ride, or one long arc.
- `eta`: "window" | "countdown" | "day" (default "window") — How the arrival reads: the delivery window, a countdown to it that rolls as `now` advances, or the weekday.
- `map`: "streets" | "dots" | "none" (default "streets") — The map strip: seeded streets, blocks, a river and parks; a dot grid with the route only; or no strip.
- `order`: OrderTrackerOrder (default defaultOrderTrackerOrder) — The order's number, store, carrier and tracking number, the map's origin, waypoint and destination labels, and the full address.

- `scans`: OrderScan[] (default defaultOrderScans) — Every carrier scan: time, text, the stage it belongs to, place, and a warn tone for hold-ups. Past scans are the marks the dot can stop on.
- `items`: OrderItem[] (default defaultOrderItems) — What is in the parcel: name, variant, quantity, unit price, a pigment and a thumbnail kind.
- `shipping`: number (default 0) — Shipping charged; 0 reads Free.
- `tax`: number — Tax charged. Defaults to 8% of the items.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultOrderTrackerNow) — The tracker's moment: where the dot sits between stages and what the countdown reads. Never read from the clock during render.
- `delivery / defaultDelivery`: OrderWindow — The delivery window (start and end, ms). Controlled or uncontrolled; defaults to the first of windows.
- `onDeliveryChange`: (window: OrderWindow) => void — Fires from the choice in Change with the new window. A controlled host that refuses it keeps the readout where it was.
- `windows`: OrderWindow[] (default defaultOrderWindows) — Windows the visitor may move delivery to. Empty hides Change.
- `onHelp`: () => void — Get help was pressed. Without it there is no Get help button.
- `onScanSelect`: (scanId: string | null) => void — A scan was previewed by drag, key or list (its id), or the preview went back to now (null).
- `format`: (amount: number) => string — Money. Defaults to Intl currency formatting in locale and currency.
- `formatTime`: (ms: number) => string — Times. Defaults to a 12-hour UTC clock, "2:40 PM", so server and browser agree.
- `formatDate`: (ms: number) => string — Dates. Defaults to "Thu, Oct 1" in UTC.
- `formatDay`: (ms: number) => string — The weekday the day view shows large. Defaults to "Thursday" in UTC.
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — Locale for the default money format.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — Currency for the default money format.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether tracking has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message and Try again on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after tracking failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Track order") — The surface's heading.
- `label`: string — The region's accessible name. Defaults to the title.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Ticks for each scan crossed while scrubbing or stepped with a key, a plip as the dot lands back at now, as a window is chosen and as the tracking number is copied. Nothing sounds on its own.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: the history cannot be scrubbed, the map not panned, the window not changed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which is at most 560px tall and scrolls inside itself.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the path is a slider — Left and Right step through past scans, Page keys move three, Home goes to the first, End and Escape return to now. The map strip pans with Left, Right, Home and End, and R recentres it. Change opens on click or Down; arrows move between windows and Enter chooses.
- Pass `now` and advance it yourself (a timer, a socket): the dot glides forward on its own spring. A stage counts as reached when `reached` is true or, if omitted, when its time has passed — set `reached: false` on the last stage until the carrier confirms delivery.
- Reduced motion: the dot, the van and the pan move without travel, the halo holds still, digits swap and the disclosure opens at once; the fill, the readout and the ETA still change because they are the information.
- Layout follows the container: one column at phone width (it scrolls inside its 560px box), map and scans beside the items from 40rem, three columns from 60rem.
- All times are formatted in UTC by default so the server render matches the browser's; pass formatTime, formatDate and formatDay for a local clock.

Pick three, save more.

A bundle builder where picking a product sends its bag flying into the next empty compartment — a thrown arc, a straight glide or a lift and a drop — and the landing is the event: the bag squashes and recovers on recoil, the box dips and the lid hops, and only then do the lid's savings and the totals roll on snap. ### Return Flow (KQ-1337) — `return-flow`
Send it back, easily.

A returns flow built from data that ends as paper in your hand: pick the items (each tick draws on flick), give each a reason as chips, rows or tiles, choose where the refund goes while its digits roll on snap, and the label feeds out of a printer slot in 3px steps like a stepper motor. - `state`: "idle" | "pending" | "ready" | "error" — Controlled label state. Ready prints the label; only a print the visitor started makes sound.
- `onStateChange`: (state: ReturnLabelState) => void — Fires as the label is requested, made or refused.
- `shippingLabel`: ReturnShippingLabel (default one made from the order, seeded) — The label to print: carrier, tracking, RMA, counter code and drop-by date (ms).
- `onTear`: () => void — The label was torn off, by a pull or by Tear off.
- `onDownload`: () => void — Download on a torn label. Without it there is no Download button.
- `onEmail`: () => void — Email it on a torn label. Without it there is no Email button.
- `onStartOver`: () => void — Start over was pressed: the selection and the label are cleared and the flow returns to its first page.
- `returnFee`: number (default 4.95) — The return fee, taken off the refund unless the method or a fault reason waives it.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultReturnNow) — The flow's moment: the days-left pill and the default drop-by date count from it, never the wall clock.
- `formatPrice`: (amount: number) => string (default US dollars) — Turns amounts into text everywhere they appear.
- `title`: string (default "Start a return") — The heading, and the region's name unless label is given.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the order has arrived: loading shows skeleton rows, error a message with Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the order failed to load.
- `label`: string — The region's accessible name, when the visible title is not enough.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Clicks for picks, reasons and steps, soft paper bursts as a visitor-started label feeds and a louder paper when it tears.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: everything shows, nothing can be changed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is at most 560px tall and scrolls inside itself.

Notes:
- Keyboard: items are checkboxes (Space toggles), reasons, methods and drop-offs are radiogroups (arrows move and choose, Home and End jump), Continue and Back move pages and focus lands on each new page's heading. Tear off reaches the torn label without a pull, and focus moves to its heading.
- Reduced motion: panels cross-fade in place, figures swap and ticks appear whole; the label fades in already printed and a press on it or on Tear off swaps to the torn state with its teeth showing.
- A Continue the page cannot take shakes once (a refusal never bounces), says why under the footer and focuses the first item or reason that needs attention.
- Pass onCreateLabel a promise to hold the button pending; resolve with your carrier's ReturnShippingLabel to print it. Without a label the component seeds one from the order id, so server and client print the same barcode.
- refundFor(order, selection, reasons, methods, dropoffs, fee) is exported, so a host can show the same refund the component does.
- The root is capped at 560px and scrolls inside itself; at 40rem it adds a Your return summary column, and at 68rem the step rail moves to a vertical list with a live line under each stop.

### Subscription Manager (KQ-1338) — `subscription-manager`
Skip, swap, or pause.

A subscription whose schedule is a row of dots you can push around: every upcoming delivery is a dot keyed by its place in the schedule, so skipping hollows it and slides the Next flag to the box that will ship on snap, a new cadence keeps the next box where it is and sends every later dot to its new day on glide, and a pause draws a hatched band across the days it covers. The strip of days drags 1:1, rubber-bands and coasts on glide with the throw's velocity (or turns month pages by direction), the cadence is chips or a detent slider that reshapes the dots live, and the next box swaps by dragging a coffee off the shelf onto a slot, both products flying from where they were on glide. - `label`: string — The region's accessible name, when the visible title is not enough.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Clicks for skips, detents, pick-ups and pauses; a swish when a swap lands or a cadence chip sends the dots travelling.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: the schedule and box still show, nothing changes.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is at most 560px tall and scrolls inside itself.

Notes:

On the shelf, Space or Enter picks a product up, the arrows choose a slot, Enter puts it there and Escape puts it back; in menu mode ArrowDown opens the list and Escape returns focus to Swap.
- Pick a date turns the calendar's days into a radiogroup (Left and Right a day, Up and Down a week); the hatched band previews the pause as you move and Enter picks the resume day.

### Music App (KQ-1343) — `music-app`

### Calendar App (KQ-1349) — `calendar-app`
Month, week, and the day ahead.

A complete calendar screen built around week-planner and meeting-card: a month grid and the week that morph into each other — the week you are in is a row of the month, so Week grows that row to fill the grid on glide while the other weeks fold away, then the planner cross-fades in over it, and Month runs it back — with a view switch whose pill travels on snap, months that slide in from 16px, a sidebar of mini month, calendars and the day ahead, and an event drawer that docks on glide, slides over or rises as a sheet you can pull down 1:1. Everything is read against `now`. The month is a real grid: arrows, Home, End and Page keys move the day, Enter steps into its events and Escape steps back out.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/calendar-app`

Props:
- `view / defaultView`: "month" | "week" (default "month") — The month, or the focused day's week; changing it runs the morph.
- `onViewChange`: (view: CalendarView) => void — Fires from the switch, a day's number or Show in week.
- `drawer`: "side" | "over" | "sheet" (default "side") — How the event drawer arrives: docked at the right (the calendar narrows), over the calendar above a scrim, or as a sheet from the bottom that pulls down. A phone always uses the sheet.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Month chips (two plain, three with times on wide grids, or three filled) and week-planner's hour height.
- `events / defaultEvents`: CalendarEvent[] (default defaultCalendarEvents) — Week-planner events with optional attendees, agenda and notes; an event with attendees opens as a meeting card.
- `onEventsChange`: (events: CalendarEvent[]) => void — Fires from the drag, edit, creation or deletion that changed the events, with all of them.
- `calendars`: WeekCalendar[] (default defaultCalendarCalendars) — The calendars events belong to, with their tints (CSS colours, never hex).
- `hidden / defaultHidden`: string[] (default []) — Calendar ids whose events are hidden everywhere.
- `onHiddenChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the calendar checkboxes.
- `day / defaultDay`: Date | number (default the day of `now`) — The focused day: the month and the week shown, and the day the agenda reads.
- `onDayChange`: (day: number) => void — Fires with the new day's midnight from the grid, the mini month, the arrows, Today or the planner.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string | null (default null) — The event in the drawer, or null for a closed drawer.
- `onSelectedChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires from a chip, an agenda row, a planner event, Close, Escape, the scrim or the pull.
- `now`: Date | number (default defaultCalendarNow) — The current moment: today, the now line, the agenda's Now and countdowns, and the meeting card's ring. Never read from the clock during render.
- `zoneOffset`: number (default 0) — Minutes east of UTC that dates and times are drawn in, so server and browser agree.
- `weekStartsOn`: 0 | 1 (default 1) — 1 starts weeks on Monday, 0 on Sunday.
- `onCreate`: (event: CalendarEvent) => void — An event was drawn or added in the week.
- `onDelete`: (event: CalendarEvent) => void — An event was deleted from the drawer or the week.
- `onJoinedChange`: (id: string, joined: boolean) => void — The viewer joined or left a meeting from its card.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholder chips; error offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed in the error state.
- `label`: string (default "Calendar") — The screen's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish for the morph, the drawer and the sidebar and a tick for each step of the day cursor; the composed pieces play their own. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be moved, made or deleted.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
- The month is one tab stop: arrows move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends, Page Up and Page Down change month, Enter steps into the day's events (Up and Down walk them, Enter opens one) and Escape steps back to the day. The view switch is a radio group; arrows flip it.
- The drawer is a dialog in over and sheet modes, trapping focus; focus moves to its heading and back to the chip, row or planner event that opened it, and Escape, Close and the scrim shut it. The sheet's handle pulls it down 1:1 and a release past 40% or a flick closes it.
- Under reduced motion the morph is a cross-fade with no rows growing, the drawers and sidebar fade in place and the sheet does not follow a drag, while every date, chip, count and countdown still changes.
- Hiding a calendar filters it from the month, the week, the mini month's dots and the agenda; week-planner's changes are merged back by id so the hidden events and any attendees or notes survive an edit.
- Below 640px the sidebar becomes a drawer, the month shows dots with the focused day's agenda under it, and the week is week-planner's one-day mode; from 1040px the sidebar is docked.

### Storefront (KQ-1350) — `storefront`
A shop that wants to be browsed.

A complete store home built around cart-drawer, product-grid and product-detail: the whole store is the bag's page, so the bag slides over it on glide and pulls shut; a hero, a category rail and product rails that scroll-snap and glide a page at a time; a category, a card or See all pushes product-grid's shelf in from the right on glide, and the hero pushes product-detail's page. Quick add throws a dot in the product's glaze to the bag on a true arc — x steady, y thrown up and falling — and when it lands the badge bumps on recoil, its count rolls and the button draws a check on flick. Rails take Left, Right, Home and End, pushed screens go back with Back, Alt+Left, Escape or a 1:1 swipe from their left edge that commits by projection.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/storefront`

Props:
- `rails`: number (default 2) — How many collections show as rails on the home, 1 to 3.
- `hero`: "banner" | "split" | "off" (default "banner") — The hero: a banner with the copy over the still life, a split with the copy beside it (a banner on a phone), or none, so the category rail leads.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Rail card widths (132, 160 or 196px; narrower on a phone) and how much each says — price only, a rating, or the rating and its glazes; also the shelf's density.
- `products`: ProductGridItem[] (default defaultProducts) — The catalogue, in product-grid's shape: categories come from it and every rail, tile and shelf reads it.
- `colors`: ProductGridColor[] (default defaultProductColors) — The glazes products come in, as pigments that read in both themes.
- `collections`: StoreCollection[] (default defaultStoreCollections) — The rails in order: a title, a line, product ids, and how See all sorts and filters the shelf.
- `featured`: ProductInfo (default defaultProduct) — The product the hero opens as a full product page; its glazes paint the hero's still life.
- `heroCopy`: StoreHero (default defaultStoreHero) — The hero's eyebrow, title, line and button words.
- `items / defaultItems`: CartLine[] (default []) — The lines in the bag, in cart-drawer's shape.
- `onItemsChange`: (items: CartLine[]) => void — Fires from the quick add, shelf, product page or bag that changed the lines, with all of them.
- `cartOpen / defaultCartOpen`: boolean (default false) — Whether the bag is open over the store.
- `onCartOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the Bag button and from the bag's close, Escape, scrim or pull.
- `screen / defaultScreen`: "home" | "product" | `category:${string}` | `collection:${string}` (default "home") — The screen on show: home, the featured product, or the shelf for a category or a collection.
- `onScreenChange`: (screen: StoreScreen) => void — Fires from a tile, a card, See all, the hero, Back, Alt+Left, Escape or the back-swipe.
- `onAdd`: (line: CartLine) => void — Something went in the bag from the store, with the line as it now stands.
- `onCheckout`: (items: CartLine[], total: number) => void | Promise<void> — Checkout was pressed in the bag; a promise holds its button pending.
- `now`: Date | number (default defaultStoreNow) — The moment the product page's delivery estimate counts from. Never read from the clock during render.
- `format`: (amount: number) => string (default euros, en-IE) — Money everywhere: rails, shelf, product page and bag.
- `storeName`: string (default "Fernworks Supply") — The store's name in the top bar.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws placeholder cards; error offers Try again. Passed on to the shelf.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed in the error state.
- `label`: string (default "Store") — The screen's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pop as a quick add lands and a category opens, and a swish for pushes, pops and the bag; the composed pieces play their own. Off unless asked for.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Browse only: nothing can be added or bought.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

Notes:
