- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The ink at the nib: fresh letters, a few em long.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "manual" (default "inView") — When a ghost pen writes the phrase once by itself, to show the piece; manual never does.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — The ghost pen writes once, or every time the container re-enters view.
- `delay`: number (default 300) — Wait before the ghost pen, ms.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The ghost pen has finished and the phrase has come to rest.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "rest" | "writing" | "gathered") => void — Fires as the phrase rests, is being written, or has gathered under the pen.
- `keyboard`: boolean (default true) — The container takes keyboard focus, and the arrow keys move a pen.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No writing: the phrase stays at rest.
- `className`: string — Classes for the container; give it a size (the trail is bounded to it) and the type the phrase scales from.

Notes:
- The trail is bounded to the container and drawn in an aria-hidden, pointer-events-none layer, so links and buttons inside stay fully usable; the system cursor is never hidden. Give the container a height — the phrase rests inside it.
- Keyboard: with keyboard on, the container is a focusable group named by the phrase. The arrow keys move a visible pen that writes the trail (Shift for 4em steps), Enter gathers the phrase under it, Escape sends it back to rest.
- Touch: a sideways drag writes the trail and lifting the finger gathers it; vertical swipes still scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y).
- Reduced motion: no letter travels. The phrase steps out of sight while the pointer moves and fades in as a neat line wherever it comes to rest; there is no ghost pen.
- Cost: frames run only while the pen is moving or letters are settling, on screen in a visible tab; at rest it costs nothing. Letter widths are measured once per phrase, size and font; the path is a fixed typed-array ring.

### Cipher Wheel (KQ-1373) — `cipher-wheel`
Each letter turns its dial until it reads.

A headline that decrypts on a row of rotary dials: every letter turns its own drum through the character set with a ratchet feel — each notch a springs.flick step, summed in closed form from one clock — and locks onto its letter on springs.snap with one clean overshoot and a hairline flash, the locks cascading left to right, at random or from the middle before the housings dissolve into plain type. Pressing the headline, or Enter or Space on it, turns the dials again from their own letters, and the pointer thumbs a resting dial that the detent pulls back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cipher-wheel`

Props:
- `text`: string — The headline. Read once by assistive technology, and copied as written.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "p" | "span" | "div" (default "span") — The element the headline renders as.
- `order`: "ltr" | "random" | "center" (default "ltr") — Which dial locks first: left to right, a seeded shuffle, or from the middle outward.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — Time scale of the whole run, 0.25 to 3: slow is chunky and every click legible, fast is brisk.
- `charset`: "alpha" | "digits" | "hex" | "symbols" (default "alpha") — The ring each dial turns through. A glyph outside it is added to its own ring.
- `characters`: string — A custom ring of characters, in the order they roll past; overrides charset.
- `duration`: number (default 900) — How long the first dial turns before it locks, ms at speed 1.
- `stagger`: number (default 70) — The gap between one lock and the next, ms at speed 1; a long headline's cascade is compressed to 1200ms.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the dials start, ms.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — What starts the dials. hover rests decrypted and turns again on hover or focus.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — With inView, decrypt only the first time it is seen.
- `active`: boolean — With manual: true decrypts, false returns to the scrambled rest.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A press, Enter or Space turns the dials again, and the pointer thumbs a resting dial.
- `housing`: boolean (default true) — Draw each dial's housing while it turns.
- `flashColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The hairline that flashes under a dial as it locks.
- `seed`: number (default 0) — Seeds the scrambled start and the random order.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick as each dial locks, for runs started by a press, Enter or Space. Off unless asked for.
- `onLock`: (locked: number, total: number) => void — A dial locked, or the dials were reset: how many are locked, of how many.
- `onComplete`: () => void — Every dial has locked and its housing has gone.
- `className`: string — Classes for the headline element; size, weight and colour are inherited by every dial.

Notes:
- Keyboard: with interactive on, the headline is focusable and Enter or Space turns the dials again; trigger="hover" also turns them when the headline takes focus. A drag that selects words never triggers a replay, and selection copies the real text.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels — each housing shows its scrambled glyph, which cross-fades to the true letter at its lock in the same order, with the same hairline flash; the pointer does not thumb the dials.
- Accessibility: the full headline is read once from an sr-only copy inside the element; the dial layer is aria-hidden. The hint for the keyboard path is referenced with aria-describedby, outside the heading so it never joins its name.
- Performance: one linear clock per run drives every dial through motion values — no per-letter animation objects, no React render per frame — and the clock pauses off screen and in a hidden tab. Settled, nothing runs.
- Size and colour inherit from the element (em-based), so the same dials work from a caption to a hero; the housings and the shading are drawn from currentColor, so both themes read.
- Sound, when on, ticks once per lock with the pitch rising along the cascade, and only for runs started by a press, Enter or Space; hovering, thumbing a dial and the automatic triggers stay silent.

### Word Bracket (KQ-1374) — `word-bracket`
A focus frame hops from word to word.

True-focus text: four corner brackets frame one sharp, full-ink word while the rest of the sentence sits blurred and dimmed, and on a timer the frame hops on like an inchworm — the leading edge leaves on springs.snap and bites the next word with one crisp overshoot, the trailing edge follows a beat later on springs.glide, and a hop to another line glides the whole frame. Hovering or tapping a word takes the frame there and holds the cycle; with the sentence focused, Left and Right move it a word, Home and End jump to the ends.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/word-bracket`

Props:
- `text`: string — The sentence. Read once by assistive technology, and copied as written.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "p" | "span" | "div" (default "p") — The element the sentence renders as.
- `interval`: number (default 1600) — How long the frame rests on each word, ms.
- `blur`: number (default 3) — How soft the words outside the frame are, px of blur.
- `dim`: number (default 0.4) — The opacity of the words outside the frame, 0 to 1.
- `frame`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The brackets' colour, any CSS colour.
- `lag`: number (default 0.5) — How far the frame's trailing edge lags its leading edge on a hop, 0 (rigid) to 1 (a long stretch).
- `cornerSize`: number (default 0.3) — Each bracket's arm, em.
- `thickness`: number (default 2) — Each bracket's stroke, px.
- `padding`: number (default 0.14) — Room between the word and its frame, em.
- `minLength`: number (default 1) — The shortest word, in letters, the cycle lands on; hover and keys reach any word.
- `index / defaultIndex`: number — The focused word as its index among the sentence's words, controlled or initial; defaults to the first word the cycle lands on.
- `onIndexChange`: (index: number) => void — The frame moved to a word: the cycle, the pointer or a key chose it. Also reported on arrival.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the frame where it is.
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — Wrap from the last word back to the first.
- `hoverControl`: boolean (default true) — Hovering a word, tapping it or the arrow keys take the frame; the cycle resumes after.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The cycle reached the last word (only without loop).
- `className`: string — Classes for the sentence element; size, weight and colour are inherited.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the sentence is focusable; Left/Up and Right/Down move the frame a word (skipping words shorter than minLength), Home and End jump to the ends, and the cycle waits while it has focus and resumes one interval after it leaves.
- Pointer: hovering a word takes the frame there and holds the cycle until the pointer leaves the sentence; on touch a tap focuses the tapped word and the cycle resumes after two intervals.
- Reduced motion: the frame does not travel or stretch — it fades out at one word and in at the next, and the words' sharpness changes with a short fade.
- Accessibility: the sentence is read once from an sr-only copy; the blurred word layer and the brackets are aria-hidden, and the visible words still select and copy as written.
- Performance: the cycle is a single timer that runs only while the sentence is on screen in a visible page and nothing holds it; the frame's four edges are motion values moved by transforms, and word boxes are re-measured only on resize and font load.
- Size and colour inherit from the element; pass any CSS colour (a token is best) to frame so the brackets read in both themes.

### Buoyant Line (KQ-1375) — `buoyant-line`
Letters rise into place as you scroll.

Scroll-float text: as the line scrolls up through its container's viewport, its letters float up from below their places left to right, each on its own share of the scroll and its own spring — from springs.snap toward springs.drift as the lag grows, with a bob at the surface — swaying, tinted and faded while submerged, and they sink back if you scroll up. Progress is read from the nearest scroll container, or set directly, and the element's bottom edge is the waterline; the keyboard path is the container's own scrolling.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/buoyant-line`

Props:
- `text`: string — The line. Read once by assistive technology, and copied as written.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "p" | "span" | "div" (default "p") — The element the line renders as.
- `rise`: number (default 1) — How deep the letters start below their places, em.
- `lag`: number (default 0.5) — How strung out the rise is, 0 (together, brisk) to 1 (one after another, slow to follow).
- `range`: number (default 0.5) — How much of the viewport's height the line scrolls through while its letters rise, 0.1 to 1.
- `start`: number (default 0.92) — Where the rise begins, as a fraction of the viewport's height from its top (1 is the bottom edge).
- `sway`: number (default 8) — How far a submerged letter tilts as it sways, degrees.
- `bob`: number (default 0.5) — How much the letters bob as they reach the surface, 0 (none) to 1.
- `tint`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The colour a submerged letter takes before it surfaces into ink.
- `fade`: boolean (default true) — Fade the letters with depth.
- `progress`: number — Drive the rise yourself, 0 to 1; overrides scrolling.
- `once`: boolean (default false) — Once every letter has surfaced, stay surfaced.
- `scrollContainer`: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> — The scroll container to read; defaults to the nearest scrollable ancestor, or the window.
- `onProgressChange`: (progress: number) => void — The line's progress through its rise, 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01, as it changes.
- `onComplete`: () => void — Every letter has surfaced (again).
- `className`: string — Classes for the line element; size, weight and colour are inherited.

Notes:
- Keyboard: there is no gesture of its own — the rise follows the scroll container, so make that container focusable (tabIndex 0 and a label) and the arrow, Page and Space keys drive it.
- Reduced motion: nothing rises, sways or bobs; the letters fade in place from faint to full ink in reading order, still tied to the scroll, because how far the reader has come is information.
- Accessibility: the line is read once from an sr-only copy; the letter layer is aria-hidden but its letters still select and copy as written.
- Performance: one passive scroll listener on the container does work only while the line is near view (an IntersectionObserver gates it, and a last reading lands as it leaves), every letter is a spring on a motion value with no React render per frame, and the springs settle and stop.
- The element's bottom edge is the waterline (a clip on that edge only): give the line a little room below it if its letters should be seen rising from further down.
- Colour and size inherit; tint takes any CSS colour, so a token keeps the water readable in both themes.

### Read Along (KQ-1376) — `read-along`
Words darken as you read them.

Scroll-reveal for long paragraphs: every word starts in faint ink and the words darken in reading order as the paragraph scrolls past the reading line, a long word taking longer than a short one, with the reading position gliding on springs.glide between scroll events so scrolling back reverses it just as smoothly. A soft underline draws itself through the word being read — its tail follows the word's start on glide, so between words it slides on like a finger under the line — or a caret marks the place; the keyboard path is the scroll container's own scrolling.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/read-along`

Props:
- `text`: string — The paragraph. It stays real text, read and copied in order.
- `as`: "p" | "div" | "span" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" (default "p") — The element the paragraph renders as.
- `faint`: number (default 0.2) — How faint unread words are, as opacity 0 to 1.
- `range`: number (default 0.5) — Where reading ends, as a share of the viewport's height below start: the paragraph is read once its bottom edge has risen to start − range. 0.1 to 1.
- `start`: number (default 0.85) — Where reading begins: the paragraph's top at this fraction of the viewport's height from its top.
- `cursor`: "underline" | "caret" | "none" (default "underline") — What marks the reading position: a soft underline drawn through the word, a caret, or nothing.
- `cursorColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The cursor's colour.
- `softness`: number (default 8) — How many characters the darkening front is spread over.
- `pace`: "length" | "even" (default "length") — Whether a long word takes longer to read (length) or every word the same (even).
- `smooth`: boolean (default true) — Glide the reading position between scroll events.
- `progress`: number — Drive the reading yourself, 0 to 1; overrides scrolling.
- `scrollContainer`: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> — The scroll container to read; defaults to the nearest scrollable ancestor, or the window.
- `onProgressChange`: (progress: number) => void — How far through the paragraph reading is, 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01, as it changes.
- `onWordChange`: (index: number) => void — The word being read changed: its index among the paragraph's words. Also reported on arrival.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The paragraph has been read to its end (again).
- `className`: string — Classes for the paragraph element; size, leading and colour are inherited.

Notes:
- Keyboard: reading follows the scroll container, so make that container focusable (tabIndex 0 and a label) and the arrow, Page and Space keys read the paragraph forward and back.
- Reduced motion: the reading position does not glide and the underline does not slide; words still darken with the scroll, because where the reader is is information.
- Accessibility: the words stay real text in order — there is no duplicate copy — so the paragraph reads and copies normally; the cursor is aria-hidden and faint ink never drops below the opacity you set.
- Performance: one passive scroll listener does work only while the paragraph is near view; one smoothed motion value drives every word's opacity and the cursor, and once the glide settles nothing runs. Word boxes are measured on resize and font load only.
- Progress runs from the paragraph's top reaching start until its bottom reaches start − range, so a long paragraph is read over more scrolling than a short one.
- Colours inherit; cursorColor takes any CSS colour, so a token keeps the underline readable in both themes.

### Char Cast (KQ-1377) — `char-cast`
Your headline cast in characters.

Your headline recast in characters: the real text is rasterised from its own layout and redrawn on a canvas as a grid of glyphs picked by a density ramp, with a slow value noise drifting through them, and it casts in on a seeded sweep where each cell's density follows the springs.snap step response — one step heavier, then settled. The pointer carries a soft light that trails the hand on springs.glide, inside which finer characters resolve the true letterforms; with the headline focused the arrow keys walk the light, and touch drags it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/char-cast`

Props:
- `text`: string — The headline. It stays real text — transparent over the characters — so it reads, selects and copies.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "p" | "span" | "div" (default "div") — The element the headline renders as.
- `cell`: number (default 6) — The character cell's width, px; rows are 1.4 times taller, as mono glyphs are.
- `ramp`: "fine" | "short" | "blocks" | "dots" (default "short") — The density ramp the coverage is cast through, light to dense.
- `characters`: string — A custom ramp, lightest first (start with a space); overrides ramp.
- `light`: number (default 72) — The radius of the light the pointer carries, px; 0 turns it off.
- `tint`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The colour the finer characters warm toward at the light's centre.
- `drift`: number (default 1) — How fast the noise drifts through the glyphs, 0 (still) to 2.
- `contrast`: number (default 1) — The coverage curve: above 1 thins the strokes, below 1 fattens them; 0.5 to 2.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "manual" (default "inView") — What casts the headline.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — With inView, cast only the first time it is seen.
- `active`: boolean — With manual: true casts the headline, false shows it as plain type.
- `duration`: number (default 700) — How long the cast takes to sweep across, ms.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer, a touch or the arrow keys carry the light.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Caps the canvas's device pixel ratio; never above 2.
- `seed`: number (default 0) — Seeds the noise and the cast's order.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The cast has settled.
- `className`: string — Classes for the headline element; its font, size, weight and colour are what get cast.

Notes:
- Keyboard: with interactive on, the headline is focusable; keyboard focus brings the light to the first letter, the arrow keys move it a few cells or a line at a time, Home and End jump along the line, and leaving puts it out. Touch drags it horizontally (vertical drags still scroll) and a tap leaves it a moment.
- Reduced motion: no drift, the cast is a single fade, and the light follows the pointer directly rather than trailing it on a spring.
- Accessibility: the headline is real text in the element — transparent once cast, so it reads, selects and copies — and the canvas is aria-hidden. Before the cast (and without script) it shows as plain type.
- Performance: the canvas draws only while the light moves or the cast runs, at about 12 frames a second while it only drifts (drift 0 stops it entirely), and never off screen or in a hidden tab. Rasterising happens on layout, font load and text changes only; the backing store follows ResizeObserver with its pixel ratio capped at 2, and a lost 2D context redraws when restored.
- Colour comes from the element's own text colour and tint, resolved on the element and re-read when the theme changes, so it reads in both themes. Use a heavy weight at display sizes: the bolder the strokes, the clearer the cast.

Your cursor scrambles what it touches.

Text you can brush: letters within a radius of the pointer turn to re-rolling noise, hot at the brush's core and cooling toward muted ink, and each returns to its letter a moment after the pointer last touched it — the core holding longer than the rim — so the cursor drags a tapering wake through the paragraph. ### Stamp Cycle (KQ-1379) — `stamp-cycle`
Each word is pressed in like a rubber stamp.

A rotating word that is stamped into its slot: the old impression lifts off on the exit ease while the slot's width springs to the new word on springs.glide, the stamp's shadow falls, and at contact the ink prints across the word from the edge the stamp rocked onto first while the slot squashes and recovers on springs.recoil and a ring of displaced ink spreads and settles to a residue. The ink carries the rubber's grain, so a firm press prints solid and a light one patchy and dry. The slot is a button: pressing lowers the stamp and letting go stamps the next word (holding prints firmer), and Enter or Space stamps through the native click.

- `interval`: number (default 2400) — Rest between automatic stamps, ms.
- `ink`: "cobalt" | "vermilion" | "moss" | "carbon" | string (default "cobalt") — A named token ink, or any CSS colour.
- `press`: number (default 0.6) — How firmly the stamp lands, 0 to 1: squash depth, ink coverage, ring size and fall speed.
- `texture`: number (default 0.5) — How much of the rubber's grain shows in the ink, 0 (flat) to 1.
- `tilt`: number (default 2.5) — The largest seeded tilt a word lands at, degrees.
- `frame`: "none" | "box" | "pill" (default "box") — A border printed around the word with the same ink and grain.
- `ring`: boolean (default true) — The spatter of displaced ink at contact and the residue it leaves.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the automatic cycle runs.
- `once`: boolean (default false) — One pass through the words, resting on the last.
- `delay`: number (default 500) — Wait after the trigger before the first stamp, ms.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the automatic cycle.
- `pauseOnHover`: boolean (default true) — Hover and keyboard focus hold the cycle so the word can be read.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The slot is a button: pressing it stamps the next word.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A thock when the visitor stamps, pitched by how firmly.
- `as`: "span" | "div" | "p" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "strong" | "em" (default "span") — The root element.
- `onComplete`: () => void — A once pass has stamped its last word.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; case and tracking carry into the slot.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the slot is a real button named by the current word; Enter or Space stamps the next word through the native click, and focus holds the automatic cycle so the word can be read.
- Reduced motion: no fall, squash or rock; the old word fades out, the new ink fades in at its seeded tilt with the residue already printed, and presses still stamp.
- Performance: there is no animation loop; one timeout per beat, armed only while the slot is on screen in a visible page and not held, and each stamp is a few springs and tweens that end.

- Ink is a token by default so it reads in both themes; pass any CSS colour to brand it. Only stamps the visitor makes are announced and heard.

### Datamosh Type (KQ-1380) — `datamosh-type`
A headline corrupted by compression.

A headline that fails the way compressed video fails: between bursts it is plain, selectable DOM text, and a burst swaps it for a canvas picture of the same glyphs that is corrupted frame by frame at a codec's frame rate — grid-aligned rows of macro-blocks slip sideways and drag a pixel run behind them, blocks freeze on the previous frame, drift to another block's pixels or quantise into a mosaic, and the two colour channels split apart behind the ink. Each burst ramps in, holds and decays on its own envelope rather than a spring, then a clean key frame puts the real text back in one frame. Bursts come on an interval while on screen, on pointer entry (clustered where the pointer came in), a tap, keyboard focus on the headline (a tab stop by default) or the link around it, and each change of burstKey.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/datamosh-type`

Props:
- `children`: string — The headline; it stays real, selectable text between bursts.
- `as`: "span" | "div" | "p" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" (default "span") — The root element.
- `intensity`: number (default 0.6) — How many artefacts a burst throws and how far they shift, 0 to 1.
- `burst`: number (default 520) — Length of one burst, ms.
- `split`: number (default 0.04) — How far apart the two colour channels drift, em.
- `block`: number (default 0.28) — The macro-block size, em.
- `smear`: number (default 0.5) — How often and how far a pixel run drags behind a slipped row, 0 to 1.
- `freeze`: number (default 0.5) — The share of corrupted blocks that hold a stale frame, 0 to 1.
- `fps`: number (default 24) — The codec's frame rate inside a burst, 8 to 60.
- `interval`: number (default 3600) — Rest between automatic bursts, ms; 0 turns them off.
- `channels`: [string, string] (default ["var(--danger)", "var(--accent-bright)"]) — The two channel colours, any CSS colour; tokens follow the theme.
- `hover`: boolean (default true) — Pointer entry, a tap and keyboard focus each fire a burst.
- `focusable`: boolean (default true) — A tab stop of its own, so the keyboard can fire a burst or, under reduced motion, clear the still frame; turn off inside a link or button, which is focused instead.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — When automatic bursts run; hover and manual turn the interval off.
- `once`: boolean (default false) — One automatic burst, then rest.
- `delay`: number (default 400) — Wait before the first automatic burst, ms.
- `burstKey`: string | number — Each change fires one burst: the host's own trigger.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds every burst's corruption, so a page breaks the same way each visit.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — No bursts at all; one under way ends clean.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The most device pixels per CSS pixel the canvas may use, capped at 2.
- `onBurstStart`: () => void — A burst began.
- `onComplete`: () => void — A burst ended on a clean key frame.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; the canvas copies its font and colour.

Notes:
- Accessibility: the DOM text is always the real text, read once and selectable; the canvas is aria-hidden and ignores the pointer. The headline is a tab stop by default and focusing it plays a burst; inside a link or button, set focusable={false} and the host's focus does the same.
- Reduced motion: one still corrupted frame stands in, drawn once and redrawn on resize, font load or theme change; hover or focus clears it to the clean text and leaving puts it back.
- Performance: nothing runs between bursts but one timeout, and only while on screen in a visible page; a burst redraws only on codec frames, reusing six offscreen buffers capped at device pixel ratio 2 and released on unmount.
- Theme changes are caught by a 1 ms colour transition on a hidden sentinel, so the canvas re-reads its ink and channel colours without reading the document; no 2D context simply means no corruption.
- Keep bursts short and infrequent for reading comfort (the defaults are 0.52 s every 3.6 s), and give the host a visible control, as the demo's Corrupt button does, when a burst should be on demand.

### Speed Banner (KQ-1381) — `speed-banner`
A marquee that answers how fast you scroll.

A marquee that answers the scroll: rows of repeated display type cruise in alternating directions, and the page's scroll velocity feeds one amount carried on springs.glide that runs the rows faster, leans each toward its own direction of travel and opens the letter spacing, the stretch anchored mid-row so the type elongates rather than slides. Scrolling up reverses every row through springs.drift, so the rows slow, stop and pull away the other way, and when scrolling stops everything eases back to the cruise. The banner is a focusable region: Space or Enter holds and releases it, Left and Right push it the way a scroll would, and Up, Down and the page keys scroll the page as usual.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/speed-banner`

Props:
- `text`: string | string[] — The items repeated along each row; a string is one item.
- `as`: "div" | "section" | "aside" | "header" | "footer" (default "div") — The root element.
- `rows`: number (default 2) — How many rows, 1 to 4; rows alternate direction and start on different items.
- `speed`: number (default 1.2) — The rows' calm drift, em per second, so it scales with the type.
- `skew`: number (default 10) — The largest lean at full scroll speed, degrees.
- `stretch`: number (default 0.06) — The most letter spacing opens at full scroll speed, em.
- `boost`: number (default 5) — How many times their base speed the rows reach at full scroll speed.
- `sensitivity`: number (default 2400) — The scroll speed that counts as full, px per second.
- `direction`: "left" | "right" (default "left") — The first row's direction; the next runs the other way.
- `flip`: boolean (default true) — Scrolling up reverses every row.
- `outline`: "none" | "alternate" | "all" (default "alternate") — Which rows are drawn in outline.
- `separator`: string (default "·") — Set between items.
- `fade`: boolean (default true) — Fade the ends of the rows.
- `gap`: number (default 0.1) — Space between rows, em.
- `label`: string (default "Banner") — The region's name for assistive technology.
- `paused / defaultPaused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the banner; the rows coast to a stop on the drift spring.
- `onPausedChange`: (paused: boolean) => void — Fires from the key press that held or released the banner.
- `onDirectionChange`: (direction: 1 | -1) => void — Scrolling flipped the rows: 1 their own way, -1 reversed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; type size, weight, case and tracking carry into the rows.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the banner is a focusable region; Space or Enter pauses and resumes it (announced politely), Left and Right push it backward or forward like a scroll, and the page's own scroll keys still scroll and still drive it.
- Reduced motion: the rows rest at staggered offsets with no drift, lean or stretch, and scrolling leaves them still; outline and fades stay so it still reads as a banner.
- Performance: one rAF loop runs only while the banner is on screen in a visible page, writing transforms and one CSS variable; when paused it stops as soon as the rows have coasted to rest. Scroll and wheel listeners are passive.
- It reads the velocity of whichever scroller holds it, including the window; over a banner where nothing scrolls, the wheel stands in for a scroll.
- Moving text can always be stopped: wire paused to a visible control as the demo does, and the items are read once from a hidden line while every row copy is hidden from assistive technology.

### Breath Type (KQ-1382) — `breath-type`
Letters inhale toward your cursor.

A word that breathes toward the pointer: letters within the radius open their tracking and grow along the inherited font's width, weight or optical size, while letters further away compress, and the line's width is conserved, so the space the near letters take is given up by the far ones and the word draws breath toward the cursor. The breath fills on springs.glide and empties on the slower springs.drift, its point trails the pointer on a critically damped spring, and on its trigger one breath passes along the line. Mouse hovers, touch presses and drags, and the keyboard breathes in at the middle on focus, walks the breath with Left and Right, jumps with Home and End and lets it go with Escape.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/breath-type`

Props:
- `children`: string — The text; it is read once and stays copyable.
- `as`: "span" | "div" | "p" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" (default "span") — The root element.
- `radius`: number (default 2.5) — How far the breath reaches from its point, em.
- `falloff`: "linear" | "smooth" | "sharp" (default "smooth") — The curve from the breath point out to the radius.
- `axis`: "width" | "weight" | "optical" (default "width") — What breathes besides the tracking; the font's own axis when it has one, a transform or stroke when not.
- `depth`: number (default 0.7) — How deep the breath is, 0 to 1.
- `spread`: number (default 0.1) — Extra tracking at the breath point, em.
- `lag`: number (default 0.35) — How far the breath trails the pointer, 0 (none) to 1.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the intro breath plays; hover means never, manual means on breathKey.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Play the intro breath only the first time it is seen; otherwise again each time it comes back into view.
- `delay`: number (default 250) — Wait before the intro breath, ms.
- `duration`: number (default 1800) — Length of the intro breath, ms.
- `breathKey`: string | number — Each change plays the intro breath: the host's own trigger.
- `breathing`: boolean (default false) — A slow resting breath while on screen and untouched.
- `focusable`: boolean (default true) — A tab stop with a keyboard path: arrows move the breath, Escape lets it go.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Ignore the pointer and the keys.
- `onBreathChange`: (index: number | null) => void — The letter at the breath point changed (grapheme index); null once exhaled.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The intro breath finished.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; the letters inherit its font, size and weight.

Notes:
- Keyboard: focusing the text breathes in at its middle; Left and Right walk the breath a letter at a time (mirrored in right-to-left text), Home and End jump to the ends, and Escape lets it go. Touch presses and drags along the line while vertical scrolling still works.
- Reduced motion: no intro or resting breath and nothing travels or scales; the pointer and keys still change the font's own axis (or ink weight when it has none) on a short tween.
- Variable fonts: the axes and their ranges are read from the inherited font's faces, so a self-hosted variable family whose faces declare weight or width ranges is used as is; a static font falls back to transforms and stroke.
- Layout never shifts: every letter keeps its rest width and the tracking is laid out as transforms whose sum is zero on each line, so the line's ends hold still.
- Performance: letter positions are measured on resize and font load only, and each frame of a moving breath is one pass over preallocated buffers; when the breath settles nothing runs.

### Tally Roll (KQ-1383) — `tally-roll`
Numbers that roll up like a meter.

A count-up figure built from mechanical digit wheels in little housings: every wheel runs its own ease-in-out drive and is coupled to it by a detent spring whose stiffness is a prop (damping ratio 0.62), so it lags a touch as it spins up and rocks into its detent as it lands; lower places spin extra turns and land first, and each higher place lands a stagger later, like carries arriving up a meter. The figure is laid out from Intl's own parts (number, currency, percent, or a hand-built compact form that server and browser agree on), a change mid-roll bends every wheel to the new figure without a jump, and fast wheels blur while leading zeros stay dim. The tally is a button: a press or Enter or Space spins the wheels forward to zero, as a tally's reset knob does, and counts again.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tally-roll`

Props:
- `value`: number — The figure the wheels roll to; a change mid-roll bends the roll.
- `from`: number (default 0) — Where the first roll starts.
- `format`: "number" | "currency" | "percent" | "compact" (default "number") — How the figure is written; compact is built by hand so server and browser agree.
- `decimals`: number (default 0 / 1) — Fraction digits: 0 for number and currency, 1 for percent and compact.
- `currency`: string (default "USD") — The ISO currency for the currency format.
- `locale`: string (default "en-US") — The formatting locale; digits are always Latin so they fit the wheels.
- `prefix`: string — Fixed text before the figure.
- `suffix`: string — Fixed text after the figure.
- `duration`: number (default 1600) — Until the highest place lands, ms.
- `stiffness`: number (default 420) — The detent spring each wheel is coupled to its drive by: low rocks, high clicks dead.
- `stagger`: number (default 90) — Each higher place lands this much after the one below it, ms.
- `revolutions`: number (default 2) — The most extra turns a lower wheel makes on a long roll.
- `housing`: boolean (default true) — Draw a window around each wheel.
- `dimZeros`: boolean (default true) — Dim the leading zero wheels, so 01,248 reads as 1,248.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the first roll runs; manual shows the figure and only rolls on change or press.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Roll only the first time it is seen; otherwise it counts again from `from` each time it comes back into view.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the first roll, ms.
- `replayOnPress`: boolean (default true) — The tally is a button: pressing resets the wheels and counts again.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Ticks as faces pass and as each wheel lands, only for rolls the visitor caused.
- `as`: "span" | "div" | "p" | "strong" | "h2" | "h3" (default "span") — The root element.
- `onRollStart`: () => void — A roll began.
- `onComplete`: () => void — Every wheel has landed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; the wheels inherit its size, weight and colour.

Notes:
- Accessibility: the formatted figure (with prefix and suffix) is read once and copies as plain text; as a button it is named by the figure and described as counting again on Enter or Space, and a changed figure is announced politely once it has landed.
- Reduced motion: the wheels change to their faces at once under a short cross-fade, with no spin, blur or rock; the figure is always right.
- Performance: one rAF loop runs only while a wheel is moving and stops the moment every wheel has settled exactly on its detent; off screen or in a hidden tab a roll lands at once.
- Server and client render the same wheels: formatting is Intl with Latin digits and a hand-built compact form, and the wheels start on `from` so a count-up never flashes the final figure first.
- Sound only answers the visitor: a press, or a value change that follows the visitor's own action (transient user activation); a roll that starts because the tally scrolled into view is silent.

### Glass Orb (KQ-1384) — `glass-orb`
A crystal sphere that holds its own weather.

A glass sphere on a table that holds its own weather, drawn in one WebGL2 pass: each pixel follows the view ray in through the front of the ball and out of the back, so the room behind comes back inverted and magnified, tinted where the glass is thick, with a window highlight, a caustic rim and a focused caustic in its shadow. Dragged, the orb follows the hand 1:1 along the table and off it; released, it rolls home on a spring between springs.glide and springs.recoil that takes the throw's velocity, and a lifted orb falls under gravity and lands with a small bounce, while the mist or snow inside is dragged after the glass and thrown up by the landing. Left and Right roll it, Up lifts and drops it, and Enter or Space shakes it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/glass-orb`

Props:
- `weather`: "clear" | "cloud" | "snow" | "storm" (default "snow") — What is inside the glass: nothing, a drifting mist, snow, or a dark storm with rain.
- `refraction`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the glass bends light, 0 to 1: a clear bubble at 0, a solid crystal that shows the room upside down at 1.
- `tint`: number (default 0.3) — How deeply the glass is coloured by glassColor, 0 to 1; the thick middle colours more than the rim.
- `glassColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The colour of the glass, any CSS colour, resolved on the element so it follows the theme.
- `weatherColor`: string (default "oklch(0.97 0.01 250)") — The colour of the snow and mist; a pigment, so it reads the same in both themes.
- `backdropText`: string — A word set large on the wall behind the orb; the glass shows it flipped and magnified.
- `size`: number (default 0.66) — The orb's diameter as a share of the box height, 0.4 to 0.9, never more than 72% of the width.
- `swirl`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly rolling, lifting and landing stir the weather, 0 to 1.
- `wobble`: number (default 0.5) — How much the orb rocks as it rolls home, from a glide at 0 to two visible rocks at 1.
- `drift`: number (default 0.3) — The slow circulation of the weather while nobody touches it, 0 to 1; 0 lets everything settle and the loop stop.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Drag, tap and keys move the orb.
- `alt`: string (default "A glass orb on a table") — Describes the scene for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seed for the weather's arrangement and the mist's grain.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the weather where it is.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish when the visitor rolls, lifts or shakes the orb.
- `onStir`: () => void — Fires when the visitor moves the orb: a drag, a tap or a key.
- `onSettle`: () => void — Fires when, after a stir, the orb is home and the weather has calmed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the scene box; set its height here (default h-56).

Notes:
- The orb is a real round button that moves with the drawn ball: Left and Right roll it, Up lifts and drops it, Enter or Space shakes it, and its focus ring is the orb's own outline. The scene is a group labelled by alt; the canvas is aria-hidden.
- One WebGL2 context and one draw per frame. The loop runs only while something moves (or, for mist and storm with drift above 0, at a rationed 30 fps), never off screen or in a hidden tab; snow stops it once the last flake has landed. The backing store caps its device pixel ratio at 2.
- The room is painted from tokens on the component's own element and repainted when the theme changes; without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still life of the same room and orb stands in.
- Under reduced motion nothing travels: the weather is a still, settled arrangement, and a key or a tap shows a new one.
- Give the box a height with className; the orb's size follows the height and never takes more than 72% of the width, so it fits a 258px phone plate.

### Live Wire Mark (KQ-1385) — `live-wire-mark`
Current crawls around your logo.

An electric outline for any SVG mark: the path is rendered as a faint wire and sampled into canvas points, and arcs of current crawl it both ways as jagged, tapering polylines re-kinked about thirty times a second, throwing forks that flicker and die over a glow that breathes underneath. Hover or keyboard focus charges it on springs.drift — more arcs, hotter, and sparks crackling off the corners past 0.6 — and a press discharges it in one flash on an exit tween, after which the charge climbs back on springs.drift from the point nearest the press. Enter or Space discharges it from the keyboard.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/live-wire-mark`

Props:
- `path`: string (default built-in hexagon-and-G mark) — The mark as SVG path data in viewBox units; any number of subpaths, with corners and open ends found for you.
- `viewBox`: string (default "0 0 100 100") — The viewBox the path is drawn in.
- `voltage`: number (default 0.5) — How hot the current runs, 0 to 1: the arcs' reach, speed and brightness.
- `arcs`: number (default 3) — How many arcs crawl the outline at rest; hover and focus add more.
- `glow`: number (default 0.5) — The glow breathing under the outline, 0 to 1.
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The current's colour; its hot core is mixed toward the foreground, so it is white-hot on dark and ink on light.
- `hoverBoost`: number (default 0.5) — How much hover or keyboard focus raises the voltage, as a share of what is left to full.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the arcs crawl, as a multiple of the house pace (0.25 to 3).
- `forks`: number (default 0.5) — How often an arc throws a fork off its side, 0 to 1.
- `sparks`: boolean (default true) — Corners crackle with sparks once the voltage passes 0.6, and burst on a discharge.
- `conductor`: boolean (default true) — Draw the outline itself as a faint wire.
- `thickness`: number (default 1.5) — The wire's stroke width, in CSS pixels.
- `label`: string (default "Electric mark") — The mark's accessible name.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A press discharges the mark and hover and focus charge it; off, it is an image.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the current still.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seed for where the arcs start and how they kink.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a buzz when the visitor discharges the mark.
- `onDischarge`: () => void — Fires when the visitor discharges the mark.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box; size it here (default size-40).

Notes:
- Interactive, the mark is a button named by label: hover and keyboard focus charge it, and a click, Enter or Space discharges it. With interactive off it is role="img" with the same label.
- The path is drawn inset by 14% of the box so arcs, forks and sparks always stay inside the canvas; size the box with className and the mark scales with it.
- Canvas 2D with fixed pools of arcs, forks and sparks, so nothing is allocated per frame. The loop runs only on screen in a visible tab and stops while paused; the wire is resampled only when the size or path changes, and the canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.
- Colours resolve on the element and re-resolve when the theme changes; a light core adds light on dark pages and a dark core is drawn over light ones, so it reads in both themes.
- Under reduced motion it is a still frame of the lit wire with frozen arcs; hover brightens it and a press darkens it for a beat, with no flicker or travel.

### Dither Curtain (KQ-1386) — `dither-curtain`
A veil of ordered dots draws back.

A veil of ordered dots over any content: where it is partly drawn back, cells switch on and off by a Bayer threshold, and the dots coarsen through nested grids toward the middle of the dissolving edge, so the content appears through a regular screen rather than a blur. The reveal is a tween across a ragged front (a dissolve is a clip, never a spring) and covering again is a shorter exit tween; while veiled, a mouse or pen pushes a dithered hole through it that trails the pointer and opens on springs.glide. With the hover trigger the reveal grows from the pointer, and keyboard focus anywhere inside lifts it the same way.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/dither-curtain`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The content behind the veil; it stays fully interactive and in the accessibility tree throughout.
- `matrix`: "2x2" | "4x4" | "8x8" (default "4x4") — The ordered-dither matrix: 2×2 is a coarse check, 8×8 a fine, even screen.
- `scale`: number (default 4) — The finest dot, in CSS pixels.
- `coarsen`: number (default 0.6) — How much the dots coarsen toward the middle of the dissolving edge, from one size at 0 to up to 8× scale at 1.
- `shape`: "square" | "round" (default "square") — Square cells, or round dots that grow until a full veil is solid.
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent)") — The veil's colour, resolved on the element so it follows the theme.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the veil draws back: on mount, when scrolled into view, on hover or keyboard focus, or when revealed turns true.
- `revealed`: boolean — For trigger="manual": true draws the veil back, false brings it over again.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Reveal only once; false lets the veil come back when the piece leaves the view (inView) or the pointer and focus leave (hover).
- `origin`: "left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom" | "center" | "pointer" (default "left" ("pointer" with the hover trigger)) — Where the dissolve starts.
- `duration`: number (default 900) — How long the reveal takes, ms; covering again takes 0.6× as long.
- `delay`: number (default 120) — Wait before a mount or in-view reveal, ms.
- `softness`: number (default 0.4) — How wide the dithered band at the edge is, 0 to 1.
- `ragged`: number (default 0.4) — How ragged the edge is, from a straight line at 0 to 1.
- `holeRadius`: number (default 64) — The radius of the hole a mouse or pen pushes through the veil, px; 0 turns it off.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer pushes a hole through the veil (mouse and pen only), and with the hover trigger the wrapper takes keyboard focus.
- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seed for the edge's raggedness.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onRevealChange`: (revealed: boolean) => void — Fires when a reveal or a re-cover completes, with whether the content is now revealed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the wrapper; give it the content's radius so the veil follows it.

Notes:
- The veil is decoration: its canvas is aria-hidden and takes no pointer events, so the children stay fully interactive and are read normally even while veiled. Use onRevealChange if a host wants to announce the state.
- With trigger="hover" the wrapper becomes a tab stop and keyboard focus anywhere inside lifts the veil from the focused element; a tap lifts it for touch-only visitors.
- Canvas 2D, one filled path per frame: solid and clear blocks are drawn or skipped whole and only the dissolving band is subdivided. Frames are drawn only while the progress, the hole or the size changes, never off screen, and nothing runs once it has settled.
- The server renders a solid veil in the same colour so the content never flashes before the canvas covers it; the colour re-resolves when the theme changes.
- Under reduced motion there is no travelling front and no hole: the solid veil cross-fades away, and back.

### Lantern Cursor (KQ-1387) — `lantern-cursor`
A warm pool of light follows you.

A dim room lit by a lantern the visitor carries: a canvas of night over any children with a feathered pool cut out of it and a faint warm spill past its edge, plus a disc of lamplight blended over what it lights. The lantern follows the pointer on a damped spring that slides from springs.flick through springs.glide to springs.drift by lag, leaning ahead along its travel and stretching with speed, while seeded noise makes the flame breathe; leaving sets it down at rest on springs.drift. Keyboard focus inside carries the light to the focused element and opens it to cover it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/lantern-cursor`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The scene the lantern lights; it stays fully interactive.
- `radius`: number (default 130) — The pool of light's radius, in CSS pixels.
- `warmth`: number (default 0.6) — The light's colour temperature, from a neutral white at 0 to candle amber at 1.
- `dim`: number (default 0.8) — How dark the room is outside the light, 0 to 1.
- `feather`: number (default 0.6) — How soft the pool's edge is, as a share of its radius.
- `lag`: number (default 0.5) — How far the lantern lags the hand: the flick spring at 0, glide at 0.5, drift at 1.
- `lean`: number (default 0.5) — How far the light swings ahead along its travel and stretches with speed, 0 to 1.
- `flicker`: number (default 0.4) — The flame's faint flicker in size and warmth; 0 holds it steady and lets the loop stop.
- `glow`: number (default 0.5) — The warmth the lamplight lays over what it lights, 0 to 1.
- `rest`: [number, number] (default [0.5, 0.45]) — Where the lantern is set down when the pointer leaves, as fractions of the box.
- `darkness`: string (default "oklch(0.16 0.025 262)") — The night's colour; fixed art by default, because night is night in either theme.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus inside carries the lantern to the focused element.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer carries the lantern (mouse and pen; touch gets the resting light).
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the flicker.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seed for the flicker.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.

Notes:
- The night and the lamplight are aria-hidden and never take pointer events, so every control in the children still clicks, focuses and reads as usual, and the system cursor is left alone.
- Keyboard visitors see what they are on: focus inside carries the light to the focused element and opens it to cover it, and it stays there when the pointer leaves. Touch-only visitors get the resting light.
- One canvas fill and one gradient cut per frame, with the lamplight moved by a composited transform. The loop runs while the lantern travels; the flicker keeps a half-rate loop only while on screen and visible, and flicker 0 or paused lets it stop. DPR is capped at 2.
- The lamplight screens over dark pages and multiplies over light ones, so it reads as added light in dark and as a warm tint on paper in light; the server renders the resting room in CSS so there is no flash.
- Under reduced motion there is no lag, lean or flicker: the pool sits exactly under the pointer and jumps to focus and back to rest.

### Scroll Unfold (KQ-1388) — `scroll-unfold`
Media that grows to fill the frame as you scroll.

A scroll-linked media card that grows to fill the frame: the section pins a stage in its nearest scroll container, and the distance scrolled, 1:1 and eased once by the house's symmetric move, opens the card's clip from its inset to full bleed while its corners flatten and the picture zooms out to meet it. The headline is split around the card and each half is pushed by the card's own edge, keeping a fixed gap as the words part and slide off the stage, while the caption rides the frame's bottom edge away and an overlay title rises over the last quarter; scrolling back folds it. Keyboard scrolling of the container (arrows, Page keys, Space) drives it exactly as the wheel does.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/scroll-unfold`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The media the card frames (an image, a video, an SVG); it fills the frame, so give it size-full object-cover.
- `headline`: string — The headline that splits around the card.
- `splitAt`: number (default half the words, rounded up) — How many words go before the card.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" (default "h2") — The headline's element.
- `caption`: ReactNode — A line under the card that slides away as it grows.
- `overlay`: ReactNode — A title laid over the full-bleed frame, rising in over the last quarter.
- `range`: number (default 400) — How far the reader scrolls to unfold it, px.
- `inset`: number (default 0.26) — The card's starting inset as a share of the stage width (0.05 to 0.45).
- `radius`: number (default 24) — The card's starting corner radius, px; it flattens to 0 at full bleed.
- `zoom`: number (default 0.12) — How much the media zooms out as the frame opens, 0 to 0.4.
- `pin`: boolean (default true) — Hold the stage in place (sticky) while it unfolds.
- `height`: number (default the scroll container's visible height) — The stage's height, px.
- `start`: number (default 0) — Scroll distance before the unfold begins, px.
- `smooth`: number (default 0) — Eases the scroll-linked progress on a spring, from 1:1 with the scroll at 0 to heavy at 1.
- `gap`: number (default 16) — The space between the headline and the card, px.
- `onStageChange`: (stage: "folded" | "unfolding" | "unfolded") => void — Fires when the piece passes between folded, unfolding and unfolded.
- `className`: string — Classes for the section.

Notes:
- It finds the nearest scrolling ancestor (or the window) and listens to its scroll passively, only while the section is within 200px of view; every visual is a clip-path, transform or opacity, and nothing loops.
- The headline is one real heading with both halves inside it, read once and in order; nothing takes focus, so keyboard scrolling of the container drives it exactly as a wheel does. Make a custom scroll container focusable so keyboard visitors can scroll it.
- On a wide stage the words sit either side of the card; when the side columns would be under 120px they stack above and below it, so it reads at 258px.
- Under reduced motion it is a still: the folded composition, unpinned, with no scroll linking.
- Pass height when the stage should not take the scroll container's full height, or when it renders before the container is measured.

### Drop Ripple (KQ-1389) — `drop-ripple`
Touch an image and it ripples like water.

Water over an image or generated pool tiles, simulated on the GPU: a height field on a ping-pong pair of framebuffers (half-float where possible, byte-encoded where not) takes the neighbours' average less the previous height each fixed step and damps it, and its reads clamp at the edges, so a ring meets the sides and comes back crossed with its own reflection before it smooths to glass. A press drops a cosine dimple, a drag leaves a wake, a passing mouse a faint trail and seeded rain can fall; the picture is refracted through the surface normals with a soft highlight on the crests. The surface is a button: Enter or Space drops at a marker the arrow keys move, which glides there on springs.snap.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/drop-ripple`

Props:
- `src`: string — An image to put under the water; without one, the water lies over generated pool tiles.
- `alt`: string (default "Water over pool tiles") — What the picture under the water shows, for assistive technology.
- `children`: ReactNode — Content laid over the water, such as a headline; it takes no pointer events, so drops land through it (give a control pointer-events-auto).
- `damping`: number (default 0.4) — How quickly the rings die away, from long-lived with many reflections at 0 to a quick settle at 1.
- `size`: number (default 16) — A drop's radius, in CSS pixels.
- `rain`: number (default 0) — Seeded rain on the surface, from none at 0 to about eight drops a second on a wide card at 1.
- `strength`: number (default 0.6) — How deep a drop dents the surface, 0 to 1.
- `refraction`: number (default 0.5) — How far the water bends the picture under it, 0 to 1.
- `specular`: number (default 0.5) — The soft highlight on the crests, 0 to 1.
- `wake`: number (default 0.25) — The faint wake a mouse leaves as it moves over the water, 0 to 1.
- `colors`: [string, string, string] (default pigments mixed from --accent and --signal with the background) — The generated tiles' deep water, shallow water and grout-and-lane colours, resolved on the element.
- `tile`: number (default 28) — The generated tiles' size, in CSS pixels.
- `resolution`: number (default 0.5) — The simulation's resolution as a share of the box, 0.25 to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Presses, drags, the mouse and the keyboard disturb the water; off, it is an image.
- `label`: string (default "Water surface") — The surface's accessible name.
- `seed`: number (default 9) — Seed for the tiles' tones and the rain.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the water where it is.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a plip for each drop the visitor makes (never for rain).
- `onDrop`: (x: number, y: number) => void — Fires when the visitor drops into the water, with the point as fractions of the box.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box; set its height here (default h-56).

Notes:
- The surface is a focusable button described by alt: Enter or Space drops at a marker shown only on keyboard focus, and the arrow keys move it (Shift for bigger steps). The overlay sits outside the button, so a headline stays readable as text.
- One WebGL2 context: a half-resolution simulation (two fixed steps a frame) and one render pass. The loop runs only while there is energy in the water or rain on it, never off screen or in a hidden tab, and it stops on a clean flat frame. DPR is capped at 2.
- Without float render targets the field is byte-encoded and still reflects and settles; without WebGL2, or after a lost context, the still picture stands in and each drop draws a CSS ring.
- The tile colours are pigments resolved from tokens on the element and re-resolved when the theme changes, so the pool reads in light and dark; pass src for a photograph instead.
- Under reduced motion there is no simulation or rain: a drop shows one still set of rings at that point that fades in place.

### Cloth Grid (KQ-1390) — `cloth-grid`
A mesh you can pull like fabric.

A rectangle of printed fabric that is a real Verlet cloth: pressed and pulled, the fabric under the fingers follows 1:1 and rises toward you with the snap spring's one overshoot, tenting up with radial folds and bunching ahead of the pull, lit from its own normals with a soft cast shadow. Let go and the release velocity carries on while every particle springs back to rest on a spring whose damping runs from the drift spring's ζ 1 down by ripple, so the cloth lies flat again through a few soft ripples; hung from a rod it sways from a passing pointer, pinned at two corners it falls into a drape. Focus shows a handle that moves on the glide spring: Arrow keys take hold and pull it, Enter or Space lets go (or plucks the cloth), Escape lets go.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cloth-grid`

Props:
- `src`: string — An image the cloth carries; it must be readable across origins (CORS). The woven print is used without it or when it fails to load.
- `pattern`: "check" | "ticking" | "towel" | "plain" (default "towel") — The woven print drawn when there is no image.
- `colors`: readonly [string, string, string] (default linen, indigo, madder pigments) — The print's ground, thread and accent colours, as CSS colours; the defaults are pigments that read the same in both themes.
- `caption`: string — Words woven into the print; they are part of the accessible name too.
- `label`: string (default "Fabric") — The cloth's accessible name.
- `stiffness`: number (default 0.55) — Silk (0) to canvas (1): how many folds form, how far the weave stretches and how firmly it returns.
- `resolution`: number (default 28) — Cells across the cloth's long side, 8 to 48: coarse cloth folds in facets, fine cloth in curves.
- `pin`: "sheet" | "banner" | "corners" (default "sheet") — How the cloth is held: lying flat, hanging from a rod, or pinned at its two top corners.
- `lift`: number (default 0.5) — How far a pinch raises the fabric toward you, 0 to 1.
- `grip`: number (default 0.35) — How much fabric a pinch takes, 0 (a single point) to 1 (a handful).
- `ripple`: number (default 0.5) — How many soft ripples the cloth leaves as it returns, 0 to 1.
- `gravity`: number (default 0.5) — The cloth's weight when it hangs (banner and corners), 0 to 1.
- `wind`: number (default 0.5) — How much a passing pointer pushes the cloth, 0 to 1.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.35) — The highlight along ridges, 0 (cotton) to 1 (silk).
- `shadow`: boolean (default true) — Lifted cloth casts a soft shadow.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio drawn, capped at 2.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the cloth where it is.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and the keyboard move the cloth; false leaves it still and out of the tab order.
- `onGrabChange`: (grabbing: boolean) => void — Fires when the cloth is taken hold of (true) and let go (false), by pointer or keys.
- `className`: string (default "aspect-[2/1] w-full") — Size the box here.

Notes:
- The surface is a role="application" named by label (and caption): focus shows a handle, Arrow keys take hold and pull it (Shift for longer pulls), Enter or Space lets go or plucks the cloth, and Escape lets go; a drag uses touch-action: none.
- One requestAnimationFrame loop runs only while the cloth moves or is held; it sleeps once every particle is still, never runs off screen or in a hidden tab, and caps the device pixel ratio at 2.
- WebGL2 draws the mesh (positions go up as a float texture each frame); with no WebGL2, or after a lost context, the flat print is shown as the still frame, and a restored context rebuilds itself.
- Under reduced motion a pull still poses the cloth under the hand, but nothing ripples or swings and a release lays it flat at once; banner and corners show their settled pose.
- Size it with className (it fills the box with a 14px margin so a pulled edge and the shadow have room); the default colours are fixed-lightness pigments, so the linen reads the same on light and dark pages.

### Murmuration (KQ-1391) — `murmuration`
A flock that wheels around your cursor.

A starling murmuration at dusk: a 3D boids flock seen in perspective, so the cloud folds over itself as it turns, with each bird darkening as it banks so waves of darkness roll through it. The pointer is a lure the flock wheels round, the lure trailing the hand on the drift spring's constants, and a click sends a hawk through whose fright passes bird to bird with a reaction delay, opening a hole that folds shut again. - `bird`: number (default 1.6) — A bird's size at middle depth, px.
- `scatter`: number (default 0.6) — How hard a passing hawk scatters the flock, 0 to 1.
- `color`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — The birds' ink.
- `sky`: boolean (default true) — Paint a dusk sky behind the flock.
- `horizon`: boolean (default true) — Paint a reed bed along the bottom.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — The flock's starting formation and the reeds.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the flock still.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and the keyboard lead the flock and send hawks; false leaves it to itself.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio drawn, capped at 2.

- `onHawk`: () => void — Fires when a hawk is sent: a click, a tap, Enter or Space.

- The flock is ambient: one loop runs while it is on screen in a visible tab and not paused, and stops off screen. Positions live in typed arrays allocated once for 2,400 birds, neighbours come from a spatial hash, and birds draw as six batched strokes.
- The sky is a separate static canvas drawn only on resize or theme change; its colours resolve from tokens on the element, so the dusk follows the page between light and dark.
- Under reduced motion the flock is one still frame flown from its seed; a hawk re-poses it with the hole it tore, and no loop runs.

### Halftone Wake (KQ-1392) — `halftone-wake`
An image surfaces through printed dots.

A single-ink halftone plate whose image surfaces in the pointer's wake: every dot rests at a faint fraction of its size, and the dots the hand passes grow on their own springs with the snap constants, popping just past full size before they settle, then recede from the trail's oldest end over linger seconds. ### Mosaic Flip (KQ-1393) — `mosaic-flip`
Images change hands tile by tile.

An image carousel whose change is a wave of turning tiles: each tile waits for the wave from the pointer, a corner, an edge or the centre, then turns 180° about the axis perpendicular to the wave's travel, so the tiles fall away from the origin like dominoes, on the snap spring with a slight lift and shadow mid-turn and each face darkening as it turns from the light.
