### Enter Stage (KQ-1395) — `enter-stage`
Content that takes its place with poise.

A wrapper that brings its direct children on stage in a cascade ranked by where they actually sit, so a grid arrives as one diagonal wave whose gaps open as it lands, all inside the 600 ms budget. Each preset carries its own spring: rise glides up, settle is set down on springs.snap with one overshoot, unfold swings down on a top hinge on springs.glide, and iris opens a clip while the piece drifts up to size; exits run in reverse on the exit ease and never spring. It adds no wrappers and no tab stops of its own — the children stay interactive in their own tab order, and tabbing into waiting content brings it on at once.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/enter-stage`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — What comes on stage. With scope "children" each direct child moves on its own.
- `as`: "div" | "section" | "article" | "ul" | "ol" | "header" | "footer" | "main" | "aside" | "nav" (default "div") — The element the stage renders — the only node it adds, so a list stays a list.
- `preset`: "rise" | "settle" | "unfold" | "iris" (default "rise") — How each piece arrives: rises, is set down, swings down on a top hinge, or opens through an iris.
- `stagger`: number (default 60) — Gap between neighbouring pieces, ms; the whole cascade is held to the 600 ms budget.
- `distance`: number (default 16) — How far the pieces travel, px — also the hinge angle of unfold and the zoom of iris.
- `scope`: "children" | "self" (default "children") — Move each direct child, or the stage as one piece.
- `curve`: "decelerate" | "accelerate" | "linear" (default "decelerate") — How the delays are spaced through the order: gaps that open as it lands, close up, or stay even.
- `origin`: "start" | "center" | "end" (default "start") — Where the wave starts; pieces are ranked by where they actually sit, so a grid enters as a diagonal.
- `trigger`: "inView" | "mount" | "manual" (default "inView") — What starts the entrance.
- `show`: boolean — False sends the pieces off with the exit choreography; with trigger "manual", true brings them on.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — True: the entrance plays once. False: leaving view plays the exit and coming back plays it again.
- `amount`: number (default 0.2) — Share of the stage that must be visible before an inView entrance starts, 0 to 1.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the first piece moves, ms.
- `spring`: "flick" | "snap" | "glide" | "drift" | "recoil" — Override the preset's spring from the calibration set (rise and unfold glide, settle snaps, iris drifts).
- `duration`: number (default 400) — Length of the tweened parts (opacity, the iris clip), ms.
- `exitOrder`: "reverse" | "same" (default "reverse") — Order of the exit: last in leaves first, or the entrance order again.
- `replayKey`: string | number — Change it to play the entrance again from the start.
- `onComplete`: (state: "entered" | "exited") => void — The entrance has landed, or the exit has finished.
- `className`: string — Classes for the stage element; lay out the grid or list here. Other HTML attributes (aria-label, id, style) pass through.

Notes:
- Keyboard and assistive tech: the stage adds no role and no tab stop, so the children keep theirs. Waiting content stays in the accessibility tree, and focus moving into it brings it on stage at once; an exited stage is inert.
- Reduced motion: no travel, scale, hinge or clip — each piece fades in on a cascade compressed to a quarter, and exits fade out on the exit ease. The content still arrives.
- Motion is written onto the direct children with inline styles and cleared when the entrance lands; a child that sets its own inline transform will have it replaced while it moves.
- Children added after the entrance (a list that grows) come on by themselves; keyed reorders are left alone.
- No loops: one IntersectionObserver until the entrance has run (kept only with once off), one MutationObserver for late arrivals, every animation stopped on unmount.

### Haze Fade (KQ-1396) — `haze-fade`
Content that clears like morning haze.

A fade-in wrapper whose content clears like haze lifting: three stacked backdrop-blur sheets, each masked a little ahead of the last, make a soft blur ramp that travels across on the move ease, while the content's own mask carries the fade and a brightness lift with it, so a headline sharpens letter by letter from one side to the other. As the front sets off the content rises a few pixels into place on springs.drift, and once clear the sheets and the mask are gone. The content is rendered once and stays selectable and interactive throughout; keyboard focus moving into hazed content clears it at once.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/haze-fade`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The content that clears. Rendered once, live and interactive throughout.
- `as`: "div" | "section" | "article" | "header" | "footer" | "aside" | "figure" | "blockquote" | "p" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" (default "div") — The element that wraps the content.
- `direction`: "right" | "left" | "up" | "down" (default "right") — Which way the clearing front travels.
- `haze`: number (default 0.6) — How thick the haze is, 0 to 1: blur, brightness lift and fade all scale with it.
- `duration`: number (default 1400) — How long the front takes to cross, ms.
- `softness`: number (default 0.4) — Width of the soft front as a share of the travel, 0 to 1.
- `blur`: number (default 14) — Blur at full haze, px.
- `brightness`: number (default 1.25) — Brightness at full haze: hazed ink glows a little, the way mist holds light.
- `fade`: number (default 0.7) — How far the hazed content fades toward the page at full haze, 0 to 1.
- `drift`: number (default 4) — How far the content rises into place as it clears, px; 0 keeps it still.
- `trigger`: "inView" | "mount" | "manual" (default "inView") — What starts the clearing.
- `play`: boolean (default false) — With trigger "manual": true clears, false lets the haze roll back in.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — True: clears once. False: leaving view brings the haze back for the next visit.
- `amount`: number (default 0.3) — Share of the content visible before an inView clearing starts, 0 to 1.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the front sets off, ms.
- `replayKey`: string | number — Change it to haze the content and clear it again.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The content is clear.
- `className`: string — Classes for the wrapper; lay out the content here. Other HTML attributes (aria-*, id, handlers) pass through.

Notes:
- Accessibility: the content is never duplicated or hidden from assistive tech, the haze sheets are aria-hidden and pointer-events none, and keyboard focus moving into hazed content clears it immediately.
- Reduced motion: no travelling front and no lift — the whole haze cross-fades away over 0.7 s, and the content still arrives.
- Theming: the fade is a mask on the content, not a tint, so hazed content fades toward whatever surface is really behind it, in either theme; the brightness lift is what makes it read as luminous mist.
- Performance: the backdrop filters exist only while hazed or clearing (about duration ms); once clear they are switched off and the mask removed. One IntersectionObserver until the trigger (kept only with once off).
- The heavier sheets thin out within their blur radius of the wrapper's edges so halos are never sliced off; content flush against an edge clears from a lighter blur.

### Arc Border (KQ-1397) — `arc-border`
A frame with lightning in its edge.

An electric frame around any children: a canvas draws a jagged current that hugs the content's rounded rectangle and re-strikes into a new shape several times a second, each strike a faint ghost strand, a glow pass, the coloured arc with a shadow halo and a hot core, while on a seeded schedule a bright bolt jumps across a corner and dies in 180 ms. Hover or focus inside charges it on springs.snap — the jag deepens, the glow swells, it strikes faster and jumps more — and the charge lets go on springs.drift so the hum lingers. The children stay fully interactive in their own tab order; the canvas never takes a pointer.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/arc-border`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — What the frame goes around. Fully interactive; the current never takes a click.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The current's colour: a preset, or any CSS colour (tokens resolve on the element, so they follow the theme).
- `coreColor`: string — The hot core down the middle of the arc. Defaults to the colour mixed toward white.
- `jitter`: number (default 0.5) — How far the edge jags, 0 (a nearly smooth live wire) to 1 (a ragged storm).
- `thickness`: number (default 1.5) — Width of the arc, px; the core is 40% of it.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How far the soft glow spreads, 0 to 1.
- `radius`: number (default 16) — Corner radius of the frame and the content box, px.
- `rate`: number (default 10) — How many times a second the arc re-strikes into a new shape at rest.
- `jumps`: number (default 0.5) — How often a bright jump leaps across a corner, 0 (never) to 1 (often).
- `surge`: number (default 0.7) — How far hover and focus inside lift the current, 0 to 1.
- `charged`: boolean (default false) — Hold the frame charged, as if hovered.
- `live`: "always" | "hover" (default "always") — "always" crackles whenever it is on screen; "hover" rests as one still strike until a visitor arrives.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the current still.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seed for the arc's shapes, so two frames on a page differ.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Highest device pixel ratio the canvas renders at (capped at 2).
- `onChargeChange`: (charged: boolean) => void — The frame charged or settled, from the hover or focus that caused it.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer box (the frame's gutter is its padding).
- `contentClassName`: string — Classes for the content box inside the frame — its surface and padding.

Notes:
- Accessibility: the canvas, rail and probes are aria-hidden and pointer-events none; the children keep their own roles and tab order, and keyboard focus inside charges the frame exactly as hover does.
- Reduced motion: one still strike that never re-forms and no corner jumps; hover and focus still brighten it, because charge is state.
- Performance: the loop runs only on screen, in a visible tab, unpaused and (with live="hover") while charged; between strikes a frame draws nothing. Buffers are typed arrays sized on resize, the backing store is capped at dpr (max 2), and everything is disposed on unmount.
- Fit: the gutter that holds the jag and its glow is the outer box's padding, computed from jitter, thickness, glow and surge, so the current never draws outside the component.
- Theming: the colour resolves on the component's own element and re-resolves when the theme changes; presets map to the accent, signal, warn and danger tokens.

### Moon Ring (KQ-1398) — `moon-ring`
Images circling like moons in orbit.

Images or generated tiles on a tipped elliptical orbit around a centre object: one phase value drives every moon's position, depth scale, far-side softening and z-order, so moons pass behind the planet and back in front of it, while the ring revolves on its own until a visitor touches it. A drag spins it 1:1 and a release projects the throw, snaps to the nearest moon and lands on springs.drift with the release velocity, so a flick coasts several moons round; a click brings a moon round the shortest way on springs.glide, with an optional whoosh. It is a radio group: the front moon is checked and holds the tab stop, arrow keys bring the neighbours round, and Home and End the first and last.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/moon-ring`

Props:
- `items`: { id: string; label: string; src?: string; alt?: string }[] — The moons. Short of count, generated tiles fill the ring.
- `count`: number (default 6) — How many moons circle, 3 to 12.
- `tilt`: number (default 20) — How far the orbit tips toward you, degrees: 0 is edge-on, 70 nearly overhead.
- `speed`: number (default 8) — Idle revolution, degrees per second; negative turns the other way, 0 holds still.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The moon at the front. Controlled rings do not drift.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number, reason: "drift" | "drag" | "press" | "key") => void — A new moon reached the front, with what brought it there.
- `lean`: number (default -8) — The orbit's lean in the picture, degrees.
- `depth`: number (default 0.45) — How much smaller the far side is, 0 to 0.8.
- `soften`: number (default 2) — Blur at the far side of the orbit, px.
- `shape`: "circle" | "rounded" (default "circle") — Moon shape.
- `moonSize`: number — Moon size, px. Fits the stage when left out.
- `height`: number | string (default "clamp(9rem, 30cqw, 12.5rem)") — Height of the stage.
- `center`: ReactNode — What the moons circle. A lit planet when left out.
- `caption`: boolean (default true) — Name the front moon under the ring.
- `label`: string (default "Orbit") — Accessible name of the ring.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A whoosh when a throw or a long trip brings a moon round.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the idle revolution.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No drag, no presses; the moons leave the tab order.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root (a size container for the stage).

Notes:
- Keyboard: one tab stop on the front moon (a radio group); Left/Up and Right/Down bring the neighbouring moon round and move focus with it, Home and End jump to the first and last, Space and Enter bring a focused moon round. Keyboard focus inside holds the revolution still.
- Reduced motion: no revolution and no travel — a press, key or release puts the chosen moon at the front at once; dragging still follows the finger, and depth, scale and softening stay as a still picture.
- Touch: the stage uses touch-pan-y, so a horizontal drag spins the ring and a vertical one scrolls the page; a tap on a moon brings it round.
- Performance: every pose is a useTransform of one phase value — no React state per frame. The revolution runs only uncontrolled, on screen, in a visible tab, unpaused and untouched, and eases back in a moment after the visitor leaves.
- Sound is off unless sound is set, and only ever answers a drag, press or key — never the idle revolution.

### Block Dissolve (KQ-1399) — `block-dissolve`
Swap images through a cascade of pixels.

A two-state transition for any two children: the first dissolves into the second block by block, each clipped by a path rebuilt every frame so even transparent content never shows through. The blocks come from a seeded quadtree and flip in a random, diagonal or pointer-led order with coarse blocks first and finer halves and quarters filling the holes, so the block size eases from coarse to fine as the dissolve finishes, and a faint glint rides the blocks that have just flipped; progress is one tween on the move ease and turns back over the same blocks if the pointer leaves early. With hover or press it is a single toggle button: Enter and Space swap it, touch taps swap it, and only the state on show is exposed to assistive technology.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/block-dissolve`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — Exactly two children: the first state, then the second. Any content — images, cards, charts.
- `value / defaultValue`: "first" | "second" (default "first") — Which state shows.
- `onValueChange`: (value: "first" | "second") => void — The state changed, from the hover, press or key that changed it.
- `trigger`: "hover" | "press" | "manual" (default "hover") — What swaps the states: hovering (keys and taps toggle), pressing, or only value.
- `block`: number (default 24) — Coarse block size, px; the run refines to halves and quarters of it.
- `order`: "random" | "diagonal" | "pointer" (default "pointer") — The order the blocks flip in: seeded scatter, a diagonal sweep, or outward from the pointer.
- `duration`: number (default 800) — How long the whole dissolve takes, ms.
- `levels`: 1 | 2 | 3 (default 3) — How many sizes the blocks refine through.
- `glint`: number (default 0.3) — Brightness of the glint on freshly flipped blocks, 0 to 1.
- `glintColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Colour of the glint.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seed for the block order and the coarse-to-fine split.
- `label`: string (default "Swap view") — Accessible name of the toggle, e.g. "Show the night view".
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No swapping; the toggle says it is unavailable.
- `onComplete`: (value: "first" | "second") => void — A dissolve finished on this state.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box — give it a size or an aspect ratio and a radius.

Notes:
- Keyboard: with hover or press the box is one tab stop, a toggle button with aria-pressed; Enter and Space swap the states (from the centre). Touch has no hover, so a tap swaps a hover dissolve.
- Reduced motion: no blocks — the two states cross-fade over 0.4 s, and the swap still happens.
- Accessibility: the state not on show is aria-hidden and inert, so screen readers and Tab only meet what is visible. Keep interactive controls out of the children when the box itself is the toggle.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest and neither child is clipped. During a dissolve one tween drives the clip paths; the blocks are built once per run into typed arrays.
- Fit: the box sizes to the larger child (both share one grid cell); give it an aspect ratio so the two states line up.

### Float Field (KQ-1401) — `float-field`

A few hundred soft motes rise through the box behind your content on a gentle seeded sway, in three depths from small far points to large out-of-focus discs. - `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Respond to the pointer, presses and keyboard focus.

### Logo Parade (KQ-1402) — `logo-parade`
A conveyor of marks that slows to look.

An endless conveyor of marks with edge fades, built in the DOM so every mark stays crisp and real. - `thickness`: number (default 2) — Bracket stroke width, in px.

### Halo Rings (KQ-1404) — `halo-rings`
Rings that ripple out from your cursor.

Rings of light ripple out from a source that trails the pointer, drawn in one WebGL2 pass under your content: each ring spreads, thins and fades, and because every ring is a short wave packet summed as a wave, offset rings that cross add and cancel into a fine lattice. The source follows the pointer on a damped spring blended between springs.glide and springs.drift by `lag`, so a sweep leaves a wake of crossing rings, and a press sends a bright ring that cuts through the rest. Keyboard focus moves the source to the focused control and Enter or Space on it sends the bright ring.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/halo-rings`

Props:
- `pulse`: number (default 1.2) — Rings sent per second while the pointer is in; three quarters of that at rest.
- `width`: number (default 8) — A new ring's width in px; it thins as it spreads.
- `colors`: "tide" | "dusk" | "ember" | "mono" | string[] (default "tide") — A named palette, or two CSS colours a ring travels between as it ages; resolved on the element so they follow the theme.
- `speed`: number (default 120) — How fast a ring spreads, in px per second.
- `reach`: number (default 300) — How far a ring travels before it has faded out, in px, never past the box's diagonal.
- `lag`: number (default 0.5) — How far the source trails the pointer, from springs.glide at 0 to springs.drift at 1.
- `interference`: number (default 0.6) — From plain glowing rings at 0 to wave packets whose crests add and cancel where they cross at 1.
- `intensity`: number (default 0.7) — How bright the rings are, 0 to 1.
- `origin`: [number, number] (default [0.5, 0.5]) — Where the source rests with nobody pointing, as x and y fractions of the box.
- `ambient`: boolean (default true) — Keep pulsing from origin while nobody points; off, the rings die away and the loop stops.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Follow the pointer and keyboard focus; a press sends a bright ring.
- `layer`: "under" | "over" (default "under") — Draw the rings under the content or over it.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the rings where they are.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onRing`: (point: { x: number; y: number }) => void — Fires when a press or a keyboard activation sends a bright ring, with its point in the box.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box; size it here.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content over (or under) the rings; it keeps every click, focus and key.

Notes:
- The rings are an aria-hidden canvas with pointer-events none; the wrapper only listens, so every control inside keeps its clicks, focus and keys. Keyboard visitors move the source by focusing a control and send the bright ring with Enter or Space.
- One WebGL2 context and one draw per frame, with up to 24 rings in a uniform array. The loop runs only while a ring is alive or the source is pulsing, on screen with the tab visible; resting, it draws every other frame, and with ambient off it stops once the last ring fades. The backing store caps its device pixel ratio at 2.
- Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, the same rings are stroked on a 2D canvas (without the interference); before the first frame a CSS still of soft rings stands in.
- Palettes resolve from tokens on the component's own element and re-resolve on a theme change; on a dark page the brightest crossings burn toward white, on a light one they stay pigment.
- Under reduced motion the rings are one still ripple around origin, and a press re-centres it instantly.

### Laser Sheet (KQ-1405) — `laser-sheet`
A beam that sweeps and scatters off the page.

A volumetric laser sheet in a hazy room, drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass behind your content: an emitter near the top fans a thin sheet of light down through drifting haze, the haze glows in proportion to the path each view ray travels inside the sheet (faint and textured while it faces you, a bright blade as it turns edge-on), dust glints only as it crosses the plane, and the sheet meets the floor in a crisp bright line with a spill of light around it. It sweeps back and forth on its own; the pointer steers it instead, the angle trailing on a damped spring blended between springs.glide and springs.drift by `lag`, and a press fires a pulse down the sheet that flares the line where it lands. Keyboard focus aims the sheet at the focused control and Enter or Space on it fires.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/laser-sheet`

Props:
- `haze`: number (default 0.55) — How thick the air is, 0 to 1: from clear air where only the floor line shows to a dense, glowing fan.
- `sweep`: number (default 0.35) — How fast the sheet sweeps on its own, from holding still at 0 to a pass every couple of seconds at 1.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The beam's colour: a named tone or any CSS colour, resolved on the element so it follows the theme.
- `spread`: number (default 32) — Half the fan's opening, in degrees.
- `range`: number (default 50) — How far the sheet swings either way, in degrees.
- `lag`: number (default 0.5) — How far the beam trails the pointer, from springs.glide at 0 to springs.drift at 1.
- `dust`: number (default 0.5) — How much dust glints in the sheet, 0 to 1.
- `glow`: number (default 0.7) — How bright the floor line and its spill are, 0 to 1.
- `grid`: boolean (default true) — Draw a faint perspective grid on the floor.
- `source`: [number, number] (default [0.5, 0.08]) — Where the emitter hangs, as x and y fractions of the box (y up to 0.5).
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Steer with the pointer and keyboard focus; a press fires a pulse down the sheet.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the beam where it is.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seed for the haze and the dust.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onFire`: () => void — Fires when a press or a keyboard activation fires a pulse.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box; size it and give it its background here.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content laid over the scene; it keeps every click, focus and key.

Notes:
- The scene is an aria-hidden canvas with pointer-events none behind your content; the wrapper only listens, so every control inside keeps its clicks, focus and keys. Keyboard visitors aim the sheet by focusing a control and fire it with Enter or Space.
- The room is the box's own background: give it one with className (a surface token) and the floor, grid and beam are worked out from it. On a dark room the light adds and burns toward white; on a pale one the beam is laid down as pigment, so both themes read.
- One WebGL2 context and one draw per frame. The loop runs only on screen with the tab visible and not paused; sweeping on its own it draws about 30 frames a second, every frame while steered or firing. The backing store caps its device pixel ratio at 2.
- Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still of the fan, its floor line and the emitter stands in; the same still shows before the first frame.
- Under reduced motion the scene is one still frame with the sheet at a fixed angle; presses and focus re-aim it instantly and never fire.

### Compass Field (KQ-1406) — `compass-field`
A field of needles turns to find you.

A staggered grid of compass needles on one canvas, each a damped rotational spring that turns to point at the pointer with a wobble set by its damping ratio, stiffening, lengthening and brightening as the pointer comes near. Every needle reads the pointer where it was distance / wave seconds ago, so a turn spreads outward from the hand like a ripple and the field swings home to north as a wave from wherever the pointer left; a seeded gust swings through it the first time it comes into view. Keyboard focus inside turns the needles toward the focused element, and a tap turns them for a moment.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/compass-field`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — Content laid over the field, such as a headline; it stays fully interactive.
- `density`: number (default 4) — How many needles stand in every 100 px, along each axis.
- `length`: number (default 0.7) — A needle's resting length, as a share of the space between needles.
- `damping`: number (default 0.45) — Each needle's damping ratio: low values ring and wobble, 1 settles dead-beat.
- `grow`: number (default 0.4) — How much longer needles grow as the pointer comes near, as a share of their length.
- `reach`: number (default 200) — The distance, in px, within which needles answer faster, lengthen and brighten.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How quickly the needles answer overall, as a multiple of the house stiffness.
- `wave`: number (default 900) — How fast a turn spreads outward from the pointer, in px per second; 0 turns every needle at once.
- `north`: number (default 0) — The bearing every needle rests at when the pointer is away, in degrees clockwise from up.
- `scatter`: number (default 6) — The seeded deviation from that bearing at rest, in degrees.
- `polarity`: "attract" | "repel" (default "attract") — Whether the north ends turn toward the pointer or away from it.
- `northColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The north half of every needle, any CSS colour, resolved on the element.
- `southColor`: string (default "var(--ink-3)") — The south half and the pivot, any CSS colour, resolved on the element.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — One gust through the field the first time it comes into view.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus inside turns the needles toward the focused element.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer (mouse and pen) turns the needles, and a tap turns them for a moment.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds every needle where it is and stops the loop.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seed for the resting scatter, each needle's own frequency and the gust.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `className`: string — Classes for the box; give it a height.
- `ref`: Ref<CompassFieldHandle> — Exposes swing(), which sends a silent, seeded gust through the field.

Notes:
- The canvas sits under the children, is aria-hidden and never takes a click, so everything laid over the field reads, focuses and clicks as usual; the system cursor is left alone.
- Keyboard visitors see the field answer them: focus inside turns every needle toward the focused element until focus leaves. A tap turns the field toward it for 1.2 s without touching scroll.
- Needles live in typed arrays and are drawn in six fills a frame. The loop runs only while a needle is still swinging or the pointer is moving, on screen and with the tab visible; a settled field costs nothing. DPR is capped at 2.
- Colours resolve on the element and re-resolve when the theme changes, so tokens work in light and dark; the server renders a faint dot grid of the pivots that hands over to the canvas on its first frame.
- Under reduced motion there is no spring, wobble, wave or gust: needles point straight at the pointer, still lengthen and brighten near it, and jump home on leave.

### Phantom Cursor (KQ-1407) — `phantom-cursor`
A shadow self that lags behind you.

A shadow self that follows the pointer inside its box: a soft form of rising smoke shaped like the pointer's own arrow (or a round wisp), drawn by one WebGL2 shader scissored to its own bounds. It trails on a 2D spring that slides from springs.glide to one softer than springs.drift, smearing along its travel, then stiffens up to five times and hurries in to condense under the cursor once the hand rests, and dissolves after an idle moment. Keyboard focus inside sends it to rest on the focused element's corner.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/phantom-cursor`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The surface the phantom haunts; it stays fully interactive.
- `lag`: number (default 0.6) — How far it lags the hand: 0 keeps close on the glide spring, 1 trails on a spring softer than drift.
- `size`: number (default 28) — The phantom's height, in CSS pixels.
- `smoke`: number (default 0.6) — How much of it is smoke: 0 is a soft silhouette, 1 a loose, drifting wisp.
- `shape`: "arrow" | "orb" (default "arrow") — A shadow of the pointer's own arrow, or a round wisp.
- `stretch`: number (default 0.6) — How far it smears behind itself along its travel, 0 to 1.
- `catchUp`: number (default 0.6) — How much faster it closes in once the hand rests, 0 (never hurries) to 1 (five times stiffer).
- `idle`: number (default 1400) — How long it lingers once caught up and still, in ms, before it dissolves; 0 never dissolves while the pointer is inside.
- `offset`: [number, number] (default [8, 10]) — Where it rests relative to the pointer, in CSS pixels; a shadow falls below and to the right.
- `color`: string (default "var(--ink)") — Its colour, any CSS colour, resolved on the element.
- `opacity`: number (default 0.45) — Its peak opacity, 0 to 1.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus inside sends the phantom to the focused element.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer (mouse and pen) summons it; touch gets the resting state.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the smoke's drift; the phantom still follows.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seed for the smoke.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.
- `ref`: Ref<PhantomCursorHandle> — Exposes appear(x?, y?), which shows the phantom resting at a point in the box (its centre when omitted) until it dissolves; ignored while the visitor's pointer is inside.

Notes:
- The canvas is aria-hidden and never takes a click, and the system cursor is never hidden, so the phantom is a companion rather than a replacement: the children read, focus and click as usual.
- Keyboard focus inside sends the phantom to the focused element's corner, where it dissolves after the idle time like it does for the pointer. Touch-only visitors get the resting state: no phantom.
- The shader runs only inside a scissor rect around the phantom and its smear, and the loop stops once it has dissolved, is off screen or the tab is hidden. DPR is capped at 2; program and buffers are disposed on unmount.
- Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a blurred DOM copy of the same shape takes over on the same physics, smearing along its travel with a composited transform.
- Under reduced motion there is no lag, smear or drift: a still, soft shadow sits exactly at the pointer and fades in and out.

### Edge Haze (KQ-1408) — `edge-haze`
Content that blurs softly into the edges.

A scroll area whose edges dissolve instead of cutting off: stacks of backdrop blurs, each twice the last and masked to begin a step further toward the edge, ramp the content smoothly from sharp to the full blur while a wash of the surface's own colour deepens toward the edge. Each edge's haze measures what it hides — the distance hidden beyond it over reach, followed on springs.glide — so the bottom haze recedes as the end comes near and lifts away on arrival while the top one gathers, and with nothing to scroll nothing is drawn. The viewport is a focusable region while it overflows, so arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Home and End scroll it natively.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/edge-haze`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The scrolling content.
- `strength`: number (default 10) — The blur at the very edge, in CSS pixels; it halves at each step inward.
- `height`: number (default 64) — How deep the haze reaches into the area at its fullest, in CSS pixels.
- `edges`: "both" | "top" | "bottom" (default "both") — Which edges haze over when content is hidden beyond them.
- `steps`: number (default 6) — How many blur layers build the ramp, 3 to 8.
- `fade`: number (default 0.5) — How far the content fades into the surface at the very edge as well as blurring, 0 (not at all) to 1 (gone at the edge).
- `reach`: number (default height × 1.5) — How many pixels of hidden content give the full haze.
- `tint`: string (default the first solid background behind the area) — The colour the content fades into at the edge, any CSS colour; read on the element and again when the theme changes.
- `maxHeight`: number | string — The scroll area's maximum height (a number is CSS pixels); or size the box with className.
- `label`: string (default "Scrollable content") — The scroll area's accessible name.
- `scrollPadding`: boolean (default true) — Keep keyboard-focused content and page steps clear of the haze.
- `onEdgesChange`: (edges: { top: boolean; bottom: boolean }) => void — Fires when content starts or stops being hidden beyond either edge, and once on the first measure.
- `viewportRef`: Ref<HTMLDivElement> — A ref to the scrolling element, for hosts that scroll it themselves.
- `viewportClassName`: string — Classes for the scrolling element.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.

Notes:
- The viewport is a role="region" with an accessible name and becomes a tab stop only while it overflows, so keyboard visitors scroll it with arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Space, Home and End; scroll padding equal to the haze keeps a focused item clear of the blur.
- No overflow, no cost: when the content fits, the blur layers are not rendered and the content carries no mask. There is no animation loop; a passive scroll listener writes two values and the springs run only while they settle.
- The fade is a wash of the surface's own colour that stands still over the edge while the content scrolls under it, so it can never lag a fast scroll; it reads the first solid background behind the area (or tint) and re-reads it when the theme changes. The scrollbar and the focus ring stay crisp, and the blur stops short of the scrollbar.
- Size the box with className (a height, or a grid row of minmax(0, 1fr)) or pass maxHeight; the haze stacks inherit the box's corner radius.
- Under reduced motion each edge's haze follows the scroll directly with no spring; it still shows, because it tells the reader there is more.

### Click Bloom (KQ-1409) — `click-bloom`
Every click blooms into petals.

A wrapper whose every click opens a small flower on one canvas: the petals unfold out of the press point on springs.snap's response with the pollen popping on springs.recoil's, then each lets go in its own moment, thrown outward by spread to fall under gravity through air that slows it, tumbling in 3D on two axes so it thins to an edge, shows its darker back and slips sideways as it turns, while a few heavier seeds burst out ahead. Rapid clicks layer blooms; keyboard clicks — Enter or Space on anything inside — bloom from the centre of what was activated.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/click-bloom`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — What blooms when clicked; it stays fully interactive.
- `petals`: number (default 7) — Petals in each bloom, 3 to 12.
- `spread`: number (default 1) — How far the petals are thrown when they let go, as a multiple of the house throw.
- `gravity`: number (default 700) — How hard petals and seeds fall, in px/s².
- `seeds`: number (default 4) — Seeds thrown with each bloom, 0 to 12; heavier and quicker than the petals.
- `size`: number (default 12) — A petal's length, in CSS pixels.
- `drag`: number (default 0.5) — Air resistance, 0 (petals drop like stones) to 1 (they float and drift).
- `tumble`: number (default 0.6) — How hard petals turn over as they fall, 0 to 1.
- `duration`: number (default 1400) — How long a bloom lives, in ms, before its last petal has faded.
- `colors`: string[] (default pigments of --accent, --signal and --warn) — The blooms' colours, any CSS colours resolved on the element; each bloom takes the next.
- `max`: number (default 8) — The most blooms in the air at once; the oldest retires early to make room.
- `trigger`: "press" | "click" (default "press") — Bloom on the press itself, or on the completed click; keyboard clicks bloom either way.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No blooms.
- `onBloom`: (point: { x: number; y: number }) => void — Fires with each bloom the visitor opens, at its point in the box's own pixels.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A soft pop with each bloom the visitor opens.
- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seed for every petal's throw, spin and lifetime.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.
- `ref`: Ref<ClickBloomHandle> — Exposes bloom(x?, y?), which opens a silent bloom at a point in the box (its centre when omitted).

Notes:
- The canvas is aria-hidden and never takes a click; every control inside keeps its own role and handlers, and the bloom is decoration on top of them.
- Keyboard visitors get the same bloom: a click with no pointer behind it (Enter or Space) opens from the centre of the activated element. Touch blooms on the tap, so a scroll that starts on the box never blooms.
- Particles live in a preallocated pool of typed arrays; nothing allocates per frame. The loop runs only while a petal is alive, on screen and with the tab visible, and stops with the last one. DPR is capped at 2.
- Colours default to pigments at fixed lightness, so a bloom reads the same in light and dark; blush and back tones are mixed in oklab and re-resolved when the theme changes.
- Sound is off unless asked for and only ever answers the visitor's press or key; bloom() from the ref is always silent.
- Under reduced motion a soft ring in the bloom's colour appears at the point and fades, with no petals and no travel.

### Lodestone (KQ-1410) — `lodestone`
Elements that lean toward your cursor.

A magnetic wrapper whose still outer box measures the pointer while an inner layer leans toward it once it comes within radius of the child's own edges: it follows strength of the pointer's offset — most when close — eased into a limit, and tilts in perspective so the nearest side rises toward it, on a follow spring between springs.glide and springs.snap integrated per frame. Past the field's edge the bond breaks and it snaps home on springs.recoil with the velocity it had; a press seats it on springs.flick, and keyboard focus holds it steady with a small lift on springs.snap while a drop shadow falls away from the pull.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/lodestone`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — What the lodestone pulls: a button, an icon, a card; it keeps its own role, focus and clicks.

- `strength`: number (default 0.35) — How much of the pointer's offset from the child's centre it follows, 0 to 1.
- `tilt`: number (default 8) — How far it tilts toward the pointer at most, in degrees.
- `limit`: number (default 12) — The most it travels, in CSS pixels; the pull eases into this cap.
- `lift`: number (default 3) — How far keyboard focus lifts it, in CSS pixels, while holding it steady.
- `shadow`: number (default 0.5) — The shadow that falls away from the pull and deepens with the lift, 0 to 1.
- `release`: "recoil" | "snap" | "glide" (default "recoil") — The spring it snaps home on when the pointer leaves the field.
- `axis`: "both" | "x" | "y" (default "both") — Which way it may travel.
- `pressable`: boolean (default true) — A press seats it: back toward the centre and down a little, until release.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer pulls it (mouse and pen; touch gets the resting state).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No pull, no tilt, no press; it rests.
- `onPullChange`: (pulled: boolean) => void — Fires when the pointer enters or leaves the field, with whether it is now pulled.
- `as`: "div" | "span" (default "div") — The wrapper's element: a div, or a span for inline use.
- `className`: string — Classes for the still outer box (its layout never moves).

Notes:
- The wrapper adds no role and no tab stop: the child keeps its semantics, focus and clicks, and because the moving layer is the child's own box, hit testing follows what the eye sees.
- Keyboard focus inside holds the child steady and lifts it slightly, so a focused control never drifts away from its focus ring; touch-only visitors get the resting state.
- One passive pointermove listener on the document is attached only while the wrapper is on screen and interactive; the spring loop runs only while the child is moving and stops when it settles.
- Give neighbouring lodestones room for limit on each side (20 px apart at the defaults) so two leaning toward the same pointer never touch.
- Under reduced motion nothing travels or tilts; keyboard focus shows as a shadow alone.

Strands that sway as you pass through.

A bed of kelp anchored along the bottom of its box, every strand a Verlet chain with a fixed root, buoyant toward the tip, held upright by a bending constraint set by stiffness and dragged toward the velocity of the water around it, so it sways as a slow swell rolls across the bed. ### Peel Label (KQ-1412) — `peel-label`
A label you can lift by its corner.

A paper label over any content whose fold is real geometry: the fold line is the perpendicular bisector of the corner and the tip under your finger, the face is clipped beyond it, and the corner's half is reflected across it — curled, liner-pale, shaded at the crease and casting a shadow that deepens as it lifts. Released short of halfway it falls back on a spring between springs.snap and springs.recoil that takes the throw, slapping flat and popping back to its dog-ear; past halfway the fold runs across the label on springs.glide and the sheet leaves, and putting it back rolls it on and lands it on springs.recoil. - `peeled / defaultPeeled`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether the label is off, controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onPeeledChange`: (peeled: boolean) => void — Fires from the release, key or press that took the label off or put it back.
- `onProgressChange`: (progress: number) => void — Fires as the visitor peels, with how far, 0 to 1 (two decimals).
- `handleLabel`: string (default "Peel the label") — The corner handle's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Holds the label down: no drag, no keys.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the paper's sounds: a crinkle when the corner is taken and as the adhesive lets go, a brighter one when it comes off, a soft one when it lands back.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box; the children size it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the corner is a role="slider" (0–100, with a spoken value). Right and Up peel a step and the label holds there; a step past the threshold lifts it off. Left and Down step back, Home or Escape lays it back (Escape is only taken when there is a peel to undo), End or Enter lifts it off, and Enter on a bared label puts it back. Moving focus away lets a held peel fall.
- While the label is on, the covered children are inert — they cannot be seen, so they cannot be focused; once it is off they are fully interactive. The face and the flap are aria-hidden presentation, so keep `label` free of controls and ids.
- Reduced motion: the drag still follows the hand, but nothing springs — a release puts the corner straight back, lifting off fades the label away, putting it back fades it in, and keyboard steps jump. The fold shading and the spoken progress still show.
- Performance: DOM and CSS only. The fold is four layers whose clip-path, transform and filter are written from one change handler on the tip's motion values — no loop, no canvas, no React render per frame, and nothing runs at rest.
- Colours are CSS strings applied directly, so they follow a theme switch with no work; the defaults are pigments of the accent at fixed lightness, so the label looks like the same physical sticker on a light or a dark page.

### Mosaic Trail (KQ-1413) — `mosaic-trail`
Your path in fading pixels.

A pointer trail laid in pixels: the box is a mosaic of square cells, and every cell along the pointer's path lights under a soft brush, holds for a beat, then fades while its colour walks from the head of the palette to the tail with its age, so a stroke is a comet that cools behind you. Brightness steps down through an ordered dither, so the tail dissolves pixel by pixel in a checker-and-cross pattern, and each tile that lights from dark pops in on its own spring with the springs.snap constants. A click sends an eight-ray pixel burst; keyboard focus inside runs a comet to the focused control on springs.glide and traces a pixel frame round it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mosaic-trail`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — Content laid over the mosaic. It stays fully interactive; the tiles never take a click.
- `cell`: number (default 14) — The side of one square cell, in px.
- `gap`: number (default 2) — The grout between lit tiles, in px.
- `fade`: number (default 900) — How long a tile takes to fade out once its hold is over, in ms.
- `hold`: number (default 140) — How long a tile stays at full brightness before it starts to fade, in ms.
- `colors`: "aurora" | "ember" | "ink" | readonly string[] (default "aurora") — The trail's colours from head to tail: a preset, or any CSS colours resolved on the element and mixed in oklab.
- `levels`: number (default 5) — How many brightness steps a tile fades through, 2 to 8.
- `dither`: boolean (default true) — Fade through an ordered dither, so tiles drop out in a pixel pattern rather than all together.
- `brush`: number (default 1) — The brush's radius in cells; a fast stroke paints a little wider.
- `round`: number (default 0.18) — How rounded each tile is, as a share of its side (0 to 0.5).
- `grid`: number (default 0.6) — How visible the resting grout grid is, 0 to 1.
- `intensity`: number (default 0.9) — The brightest a tile gets, 0 to 1.
- `burst`: number (default 6) — A click sends a pixel burst with rays this many cells long; 0 turns it off.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — One comet across the mosaic the first time it comes into view.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus inside draws a comet to the focused control and frames it in pixels.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer paints (mouse and pen); a tap sends a burst.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freezes the trail where it is.
- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seed for the dither offsets, the intro's path and the reduced-motion still.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when the first tile lights and when the last one has faded.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box. Give it a height; children are laid out inside it.

Notes:
- The canvas and the grout grid sit under the children, aria-hidden and without pointer events, so every child stays clickable and focusable; give the box a height and lay the content out inside it.
- Keyboard: focus moving onto a child (focus-visible) runs a comet from the last focused control to the new one and traces a pixel frame round it, so tabbing through a hero reads in the same pixels a mouse paints. Touch: a tap sends a burst and scrolling is untouched.
- Reduced motion: no moving trail, no pop and no burst. A still, seeded comet is laid across the mosaic with its dithered tail, the tile under the mouse lights in place, and a focused control gets a still pixel frame.
- Performance: lit tiles live in an active list of typed arrays, and the loop runs only while one is lit or popping, only on screen and in a visible tab, stopping itself when the last tile goes dark. The canvas caps DPR at min(dpr, 2) and resizes with a ResizeObserver.
- Colours resolve on the element (so a themed subtree's tokens are the ones read) and re-resolve on a theme change; a custom `colors` array can be any CSS colours, mixed evenly in oklab from head to tail.

### Cube Field (KQ-1414) — `cube-field`
A floor of cubes that rises to meet you.

A floor of cubes in true isometric fills the box behind its children, each cube shaded per face from tokens so it reads lit from the upper left in either theme. Every cube is a spring with the springs.snap, springs.glide or springs.drift constants toward a height that peaks under the pointer and falls away over a raised-cosine bell on the floor plane, so a hill follows the hand and settles back when it leaves; a click knocks the floor and a real lattice wave — each cube coupled to its four neighbours, short wavelengths damped — carries a glowing ring outward until a sponge at the edges drinks it. Rendered as CSS 3D cubes, or as canvas polygons past 260 cubes; keyboard focus inside raises the floor under the focused control.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cube-field`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — Content laid over the floor. It stays fully interactive; the cubes never take a click.
- `grid`: number (default 48) — A cube's edge on the floor, in px — the grid's pitch.
- `rise`: number (default 36) — How high the cubes under the pointer climb, in px.
- `falloff`: number (default 3.5) — How far the rise reaches, in cubes, fading to nothing along a raised-cosine bell.
- `base`: number (default 6) — Every cube's resting height, in px.
- `spring`: "snap" | "glide" | "drift" (default "snap") — The calibrated spring the cubes rise and settle on.
- `wave`: number (default 1) — Strength of the wave a click sends through the floor, 0 to 2; 0 turns it off.
- `waveSpeed`: number (default 1) — How fast the wave travels, as a multiple of 14 cubes a second (0.5 to 2).
- `topColor`: string (default "var(--card)") — The cubes' tops, any CSS colour.
- `sideColor`: string (default "var(--card)") — The colour the sides are shaded from, toward black in oklab.
- `glowColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The colour a risen top glows toward.
- `glow`: number (default 0.55) — How strongly a fully risen top glows, 0 to 1.
- `shade`: number (default 0.5) — How dark the sides are, 0 to 1: the left face takes half of it, the right face all of it.
- `renderer`: "auto" | "css" | "canvas" (default "auto") — CSS 3D cubes, canvas polygons, or CSS until the floor needs more than 260 cubes.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — One gentle wave from the centre the first time it comes into view.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus inside raises the floor under the focused control.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer raises the floor (mouse and pen); a click or a tap sends a wave.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds every cube where it is.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas renderer draws at (never above 2).
- `onWave`: () => void — Fires when a visitor sends a wave with a click or a tap.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box. Give it a height; children are laid out inside it.

Notes:
- The floor is aria-hidden and takes no pointer events — the pointer is read from the box — so the children stay fully interactive. Keyboard focus moving onto a child (focus-visible) raises the floor under it and sends a small wave; touch taps send a wave and scrolling is untouched.
- Reduced motion: the floor stays flat — no rise, no wave, no intro — and the tops under the pointer or the focused control brighten toward the glow colour instead, as an instant colour change with the same falloff.
- Performance: one simulation loop that runs only while some cube is moving, on screen and in a visible tab, and stops itself when the floor has settled. In CSS mode a frame writes only transforms and an opacity to the cubes that moved (compositor work, no layout); past 260 cubes, or with renderer="canvas", the same floor is drawn as polygons with DPR capped at min(dpr, 2).
- Colours: the CSS cubes read their tokens live, so a theme switch needs no work; the canvas resolves them on the element and re-resolves on a theme change, mixing the sides toward black in oklab exactly as the CSS does.
- Give the box a height (a hero band of 200–400 px reads best); `grid` sets the cube size, so larger boxes or smaller cubes move to the canvas renderer automatically.

### Molten Mark (KQ-1415) — `molten-mark`
Your logo poured in liquid metal.

An SVG mark or a word filled with liquid metal in one WebGL2 pass inside the shape's own mask: an exact distance transform rolls the edge like a meniscus, a slow churn of warped noise moves across the surface, and every pixel reflects a procedural studio tinted chrome, gold, copper or the accent, with a key light that follows the pointer on springs.glide and drifts home on springs.drift. The first time it is in view the metal pours into the empty mould from its foot, white-hot at the front and cooling to metal, and a click drops a ring ripple into the surface. It is an image to assistive technology, has nothing to focus, and shows a still metallic gradient without WebGL2.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/molten-mark`

Props:
- `path`: string (default a ring with a droplet in it) — The mark as SVG path data in viewBox units, filled with the nonzero rule.
- `viewBox`: string (default "0 0 100 100") — The viewBox the path is drawn in.
- `text`: string — A word to pour instead of the path, set in the inherited font at heavy weight.
- `label`: string (default text, or "Molten mark") — The mark's accessible name.
- `tint`: "chrome" | "gold" | "copper" | "accent" | string (default "chrome") — The metal: a preset (each a token pigment at a fixed lightness) or any CSS colour.
- `flow`: number (default 1) — How fast the surface churns, as a multiple of the house pace (0 to 3); 0 holds it still and stops the loop.
- `shine`: number (default 0.6) — Polish, 0 to 1: satin with soft broad highlights to a mirror with small hard ones.
- `bevel`: number (default 0.75) — How rounded the metal stands at its edges, 0.1 to 1: a flat pour with a rolled rim to a full pillow.
- `ripple`: number (default 0.5) — How deep the churning ripples run, 0 to 1.
- `heat`: number (default 1) — How hot the pour runs, 0 to 1: white-hot at the front and cooling through ember; 0 pours cold.
- `padding`: number (default 0.08) — Space around the mark, as a share of the box on each side (0 to 0.3).
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — Pour the metal in the first time the mark comes into view; off, it is cast already.
- `pourKey`: string | number — Change it to pour again.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The key light follows the pointer, and a click drops a ripple into the metal.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the surface still and stops the loop.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seed for the flow's pattern.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onPour`: () => void — Fires when a pour begins: on first view, or when pourKey changes.
- `onPoured`: () => void — Fires when the mark is cast: a pour has filled it and cooled, or, with no pour to run, the first time it is in view.
- `className`: string (default "h-40 w-full") — Classes for the box; give it a size.

Notes:
- The box is role="img" named by `label` (or the word); the canvas, mould and still are aria-hidden and nothing is focusable — the light and the ripple are decoration, so keyboard and touch visitors get the finished cast (a tap drops a ripple and moves the light there).
- Give the box a size: it uses size containment so a `text` word can be fitted with container units, and the GL mask is rasterised from the word's own computed font and position so the metal lands on the same pixels.
- Reduced motion: no pour, no churn, no ripple and no springs — one still frame of the finished metal, the light moving without easing, drawn on demand. Nothing loops.
- Performance: one fullscreen pass. The loop runs only while the flow is on and the mark is on screen in a visible tab, or while a pour, a ripple or the light is moving; flow={0} or paused stops it. DPR is capped at min(dpr, 2), and the mask and surface field are rebuilt once per resize, the field fitted to the mark's own box and stored as half-float so reflections run smooth.
- Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, the mark shows a still metallic gradient in its tint; a restored context rebuilds everything, and every GL object is disposed on unmount. The studio takes its brightness from the page background, so chrome reads silver on a light page and smoky on a dark one.

### Film Grain (KQ-1416) — `film-grain`
Analog grain that makes pixels feel printed.

Film grain over any section, built for cost: two seamless grain tiles per seed — fine noise plus clumped octaves blurred on the torus — are made once and shared, and each projected frame at the chosen frame rate only swaps which tile shows and jumps it to a seeded offset, so the compositor does the work and no WebGL context is used. Dark specks multiply and light specks screen, so the grain reads on light and dark pages alike, with optional gate weave, faint scratches, a vignette and a wavering lamp; the projector spins up from 4 fps the first time it is in view. Under the mouse, and around a control with keyboard focus, the grain clears in a soft patch that follows on springs.glide and fades in and out on tweens.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/film-grain`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The section under the grain. It stays fully interactive and selectable.
- `intensity`: number (default 0.5) — How strong the grain is, 0 to 1.
- `size`: number (default 1) — Grain size: 1 is fine 35mm stock, 3 coarse 16mm (0.5 to 3).
- `fps`: number (default 18) — The projector's frame rate: how many times a second the grain changes (1 to 30).
- `blend`: "dual" | "overlay" | "soft-light" (default "dual") — How the grain meets the page: dual darkens with dark specks and lightens with light ones, so it reads on light and dark; overlay and soft-light work the midtones only.
- `weave`: number (default 0) — Gate weave: how far the section drifts in the gate from frame to frame, in px (0 to 2).
- `scratches`: number (default 0.2) — How often faint scratches run down the frame, 0 to 1.
- `vignette`: number (default 0.3) — The darkening toward the corners, 0 to 1.
- `flicker`: number (default 0.2) — How much the lamp's brightness wavers from frame to frame, 0 to 1.
- `calm`: number (default 0.5) — How much the grain clears around the mouse and around a focused control, 0 to 1.
- `calmRadius`: number (default 140) — The radius of that clear patch, in px.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — Spin the projector up the first time the section comes into view.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The mouse and keyboard focus clear the grain around them.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds one frame of grain and stops the projector.
- `seed`: number (default 24) — Seed for the grain tiles and every flaw. Sections with the same seed share their tiles.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the grain is drawn for: one grain pixel per device pixel up to this (never above 2).
- `className`: string — Classes for the section box.

Notes:
- Every grain layer is aria-hidden with pointer-events none, so the section underneath stays selectable and interactive; the component isolates its own stacking context, so the blend modes only touch what is inside it. Give the box a border radius and the grain follows it.
- Keyboard: focus moving onto a control inside (focus-visible) clears the grain around it, so what is being pressed reads clean. Touch visitors get the grain at rest.
- Reduced motion: one still frame of grain and the vignette — no stepping, flicker, scratches, weave or start-up — and the clear patch moves without easing.
- Performance: zero cost off screen or in a hidden tab. While projecting, a frame is about ten opacity and transform writes on a timer at `fps` — no canvas, no WebGL, nothing painted per frame — and the tiles (about 5 ms to make) are cached per seed and shared by every section, so a page can carry many grained sections.
- `weave` moves the section itself by a fraction of a pixel, which softens text slightly between frames; keep it for imagery and posters, and leave it at 0 over body copy.

### Soft Shape (KQ-1417) — `soft-shape`
Shapes that blur into each other near you.

Flat pigment circles, rounded squares and rounded triangles drawn as signed-distance fields in one WebGL2 pass, joined by a smooth minimum whose reach grows near the pointer: as the pointer draws two shapes together (each leans in on springs.glide and drifts home on springs.drift) they flow into one mass through a neck and their colours blend across it, while their edges soften into a grained gradient near the pointer and stay crisp away from it. Pressing gathers the whole composition into one soft mass and releasing scatters it home on springs.recoil. Keyboard focus on a control inside draws the shapes to it, and Enter or Space on it pulses a gather.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/soft-shape`

- `softness`: number (default 28) — The widest the edges soften right under the pointer, in px; away from it they stay crisp.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "dusk" | "ember" | "moss" | readonly string[] (default "cobalt") — The pigment palette: a named set from the theme tokens, or your own CSS colours given to the shapes in turn.
- `count`: number (default 6) — How many shapes, 2 to 8.
- `scale`: number (default 1) — Shape size relative to the room each one has, 0.5 to 1.5.
- `roundness`: number (default 0.3) — Corner rounding of the squares and triangles, 0 (sharp) to 1 (pebble).
- `melt`: number (default 44) — How far apart two shapes start to flow together near the pointer, in px (the smooth minimum's reach).
- `radius`: number (default 160) — How far the pointer's pull and its soft focus reach, in px.
- `pull`: number (default 0.5) — How strongly nearby shapes lean toward the pointer, 0 to 1.
- `grain`: number (default 0.4) — A fine printed grain inside the soft edges, 0 to 1, so the blur never bands.
- `ambient`: boolean (default true) — With nobody pointing, a slow soft spot wanders the composition and the shapes bob.
- `gather`: boolean (default true) — Pressing gathers every shape into one soft mass; releasing scatters them home on springs.recoil.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Follow the pointer.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus on a control inside draws the shapes and the soft spot to it.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the composition still and stop the frame loop.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seed for the layout, the kinds, the colours and the tilts.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onGatherChange`: (gathered: boolean) => void — Fires when a press (or Enter/Space on a control inside) gathers the shapes, and again when they scatter.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box. Give it a height; children are laid out inside it.

Notes:

- Give the box a height (h-52, h-64, or a hero's own size). The composition is one zigzag row at 560 px and wider and two staggered rows below; the server renders the same shapes as an SVG still, which the canvas replaces on its first frame.
- Colours default to pigments built from the theme tokens at a fixed lightness, so the shapes read the same in light and dark; pass your own CSS colours to color, and they are re-read when the theme changes.
- Under reduced motion it is one still frame with a soft neck between the two closest shapes; the soft spot jumps to the pointer or the focused control and nothing travels or bounces.
- One fragment pass with at most eight shapes. The loop stops off screen, on a hidden tab, when paused and, with ambient off, once the springs settle; ambient-only frames run at 30 fps. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, the SVG still stays.

### Sight Lines (KQ-1418) — `sight-lines`
Hairlines that measure where you point.

A precision measuring overlay bounded to the container it wraps: four hairlines run in from the edges to the pointer, each with its length in a mono pill, over tick rulers that mark the pointer's coordinate, and the lines ease after the pointer on springs.glide while the crosshair cursor stays exactly under the hand. - `color`: "cobalt" | "redline" | "signal" | "ink" | string (default "cobalt") — The hairline tone: a named tone from the theme or any CSS colour.
- `targets`: string (default [data-measure] and interactive elements) — What the lines snap to, as a CSS selector; disabled controls never snap.

### Photo Scatter (KQ-1419) — `photo-scatter`
Pictures drop where your cursor travels.

An image trail of real-looking prints: as the pointer travels, the distance it covers is measured along its path and every few dozen px a print drops at that exact point, born lifted and landing with its scale on springs.recoil, its seeded tilt on springs.snap and its shadow drawing in tight on springs.glide. After its life each print fades and shrinks away on the exit ease, oldest first, and a press pins one to the table with a strip of tape until the next press. Keyboard focus travels too, dropping prints along the way to a focused control and landing them beside it, and Enter or Space pins one there.

- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seed for the tilts, the scatter and the shuffle.

Notes:
- The prints are an aria-hidden layer with pointer-events none, under the content by default, so links and buttons stay readable and clickable; a press on a control is left to the control and never pins.
- Tab moves the trail too: prints drop along the way to the focused control and land beside its group rather than on it, and Enter or Space pins one there, so keyboard visitors reach every state.
- Pass images as URLs or as your own nodes (an <img>, a gradient, an illustration); with none, it uses quiet plates tinted from the theme. Sizes cap through container units, so the server and the browser render the same resting stack.
- Under reduced motion a print appears in place with a short fade and leaves the same way; the trail, the pin and the order of leaving all still work.
- DOM only, transform and opacity on the compositor, at most max prints plus the pin; there is no frame loop, and each print's springs stop once it lands. On touch a sideways drag lays a trail (vertical scrolling is untouched) and a tap pins.

### Silk Ribbons (KQ-1420) — `silk-ribbons`
Ribbons that flow from your cursor.

Silk ribbons stream from the pointer on one Canvas 2D layer: each is a chain of 32 links whose head rides the pointer on a spring blended between springs.drift and springs.snap, with every link following the one ahead at its length and held smooth by a bending spring, and the ribbons differ in length, stiffness and drag so a sweep fans them out. When a link catches up its overtaking motion turns sideways, so as the pointer stops the ribbons overshoot, wind into loops and unwind, and a press whips an S-wave down each chain; each ribbon tapers and twists, darkening edge-on and shifting colour between its two faces like iridescent silk. With nobody pointing they fly a slow figure-eight, keyboard focus sends them to circle the focused control, and Enter or Space on it whips them there.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/silk-ribbons`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content laid over the ribbons, such as a headline. It keeps every click, focus and key.
- `count`: number (default 5) — How many ribbons stream from the pointer, 1 to 8.
- `length`: number (default 220) — A ribbon's length in px; each varies around it by variance, and none outgrows 1.6× the box's shorter side.
- `colors`: "opal" | "ember" | "tide" | "mono" | readonly string[] (default "opal") — The silk: a named palette from the theme tokens, or your own CSS colours the ribbons shift through along their length.
- `width`: number (default 11) — A ribbon's widest, just below the head, in px.
- `taper`: number (default 0.85) — How much a ribbon thins toward its tail, 0 (even) to 1 (a fine point).
- `stiffness`: number (default 0.5) — How tightly the heads follow and the silk holds its line, 0 (springs.drift, loose) to 1 (springs.snap, taut).
- `variance`: number (default 0.5) — How different the ribbons are from each other in length, stiffness and drag, 0 to 1.
- `curl`: number (default 0.5) — How much the ribbons wind into loops as they catch up, 0 to 1.
- `twist`: number (default 1.5) — Twists along each ribbon; where it turns edge-on it narrows and darkens.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.6) — A soft specular streak down faces turned to the light, 0 to 1.
- `spread`: number (default 12) — How wide the fan of heads is either side of the pointer, across its direction of travel, in px.
- `whip`: boolean (default true) — A press whips the ribbons, throwing a loop down each one.
- `ambient`: boolean (default true) — With nobody pointing, the ribbons fly a slow figure-eight through the box.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus on a control inside sends the ribbons to circle it.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Follow the pointer.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the ribbons still and stop the frame loop.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seed for every ribbon's length, spring, twist and colour.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `onWhip`: (point: { x: number; y: number }) => void — Fires when a press (or Enter/Space on a control inside) whips the ribbons, with the point in the box.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box. Give it a height; children are laid out inside it.

Notes:
- The canvas is aria-hidden with pointer-events none and sits under the children, so a headline stays readable and every button and link keeps its own clicks, focus and keys.
- Keyboard focus on a control sends the ribbons to circle it and Enter or Space on it whips them, so the keyboard reaches the same states as the pointer; on touch, a tap swoops them to the tap and a sideways drag leads them, while vertical scrolling is untouched.
- Colours default to pigments built from the theme tokens at a fixed lightness (mono follows the foreground), blended in OKLab into a lookup made once per palette, and they are re-read when the theme changes.
- Under reduced motion the ribbons are one still sweep, simulated from the seed and drawn once; nothing follows the pointer and no loop runs.
- Canvas 2D with typed arrays made once, so a frame allocates nothing. The loop stops off screen, on a hidden tab and when paused; ambient-only frames draw at 30 fps, and with ambient off it stops once the silk settles. DPR is capped at 2.

### Ink Splash (KQ-1421) — `ink-splash`
Your cursor stirs a pool of ink.

A pool of water under your content, simulated on the GPU as a real incompressible fluid (advection, vorticity confinement and a warm-started pressure solve every frame): the pointer drags a brush through it that pushes the water and lays pigment, so ink is shoved ahead, peels into curls, diffuses and fades. A click drops a splash — a zero-mean volume source pushes a ring of water out from the drop, its ink blooms with a pooled rim, satellite droplets patter down on a cascade stagger and a surface ripple runs out bending the ink — all inside 600 ms. Keyboard focus moving between controls inside draws a stroke of ink to the new one, and Enter or Space on a control drops a splash there.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ink-splash`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content floated on the pool, such as a headline. It keeps every click, focus and key.
- `viscosity`: number (default 0.3) — How thick the water is, 0 to 1: thin water coasts and curls, thick ink stops short and smooths.
- `fade`: number (default 6) — How long ink lingers before the water clears, in seconds (1 to 20).
- `colors`: "indigo" | "sumi" | "tide" | "ember" | readonly string[] (default "indigo") — The pigments: a named set from the theme tokens, or your own CSS colours. The brush walks through them, one per stroke and per splash.
- `curl`: number (default 0.5) — How strongly eddies are kept and sharpened, 0 to 1 (thick water damps them further).
- `radius`: number (default 22) — The brush's width, in px.
- `force`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the brush pushes the water, 0 to 1.
- `opacity`: number (default 0.85) — Coverage of the densest ink, 0 to 1.
- `splash`: boolean (default true) — A click (or Enter/Space on a control inside) drops a splash.
- `splashSize`: number (default 46) — The splash drop's radius, in px.
- `droplets`: number (default 7) — Satellite droplets that patter down around each splash, 0 to 12.
- `ambient`: boolean (default true) — With nobody stirring, a slow drip lands every few seconds so the pool stays alive.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer stirs the pool (mouse and pen; a tap drops a splash).
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus moving between controls inside draws a stroke of ink to the new one.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the water still and stop the frame loop.
- `resolution`: number (default 128) — The simulation grid's long side, 48 to 192 cells. Lower is cheaper and softer.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).
- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seed for the opening drop, the drips, the droplets, the grain and the still.
- `onSplash`: (splash: { x: number; y: number; source: "pointer" | "keyboard" | "ambient" }) => void — Fires when a drop lands, with where (px from the box's top-left) and why.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box. Give it a height; children are laid out inside it.

Notes:
- The canvas and its still are aria-hidden and never take the pointer, so buttons and links inside keep their own clicks, focus and keys. Focus moving between controls draws ink to the new one and Enter or Space on a control drops a splash, so the keyboard reaches the same states as the pointer.
- Give the box a height (h-52, h-60, or a hero's own size). Touch scrolls the page as usual — a tap drops a splash, a drag never stirs — so the pool is safe in a scrolling layout.
- Pigments default to the theme tokens at their own lightness and are re-read when the theme changes: deep ink with a darker pooled rim on a light page, a step brighter on a dark one. Pass your own CSS colours to colors.
- Under reduced motion there is no simulation: the server-rendered still swirl stays, and a click or Enter/Space crossfades a soft blot in at the point and lets it fade over the fade time.
- Needs WebGL2 with renderable half-float buffers; without them, or after a lost context, the still stays. The grid is capped at 192 cells and the dye at 512 texels; the loop stops off screen, on a hidden tab and when paused, drops to 30 fps when only the drip moves the water, and with ambient off stops once the water has settled and the ink has faded.

### Lava Blobs (KQ-1422) — `lava-blobs`
Blobs that merge and part like wax.

A tall column of warm liquid where wax rises and falls: each blob carries a temperature that the coil raises on the floor and the cap lowers at the top, buoyancy follows it, and touching blobs pull together, share heat and travel as one mass until their heat parts them. The wax is a metaball field drawn in one WebGL2 pass with soft light — wrap diffuse, a glossy specular, a rim and an inner glow that follows temperature — so blobs merge with smooth necks and pinch apart. The pointer adds its own blob that follows on springs.glide and swells in on springs.snap, drawing wax along; pressing grips nearby wax into one mass and releasing throws it with the pointer's velocity. - `size`: number (default 1) — Blob size relative to the column, 0.6 to 1.4.
- `heat`: number (default 0.5) — How hard the base heats the wax, 0 to 1: more heat keeps more of it aloft.

- `handSize`: number (default 30) — The pointer blob's radius, in px.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer adds its blob; a press grips nearby wax and a release throws it.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus on a control inside sends the pointer blob there; Enter or Space grips.

Notes:

- Made for a tall box (h-[420px] to a full-height hero). Blob size follows the column's width, clamped, so narrow and wide columns hold the same composition; the server renders that composition as lit discs, which the canvas replaces on its first frame.
- Wax is pigment — token hues at a fixed lightness — so it reads the same on light and dark pages; the liquid is the card colour washed with the palette's tint and is re-read when the theme changes. Pass your own [cool, hot, liquid] CSS colours to colors.
