- One fragment pass with at most eleven kernels. The loop runs at 30 fps while the wax only drifts and every frame while the hand is in play, and stops off screen, on a hidden tab and when paused. Without WebGL2 a Canvas 2D renderer draws the same field at a third of the resolution; a lost context brings the still back.

### Jelly Cursor (KQ-1423) — `jelly-cursor`
A cursor with a wobble of its own.

Inside its box the pointer becomes a ball of jelly: a soft-body ring of 40 points on damped springs, carried rigidly with the pointer so the cursor stays exact, drawn out into an area-keeping ellipse behind a fast move and set wobbling by a stop, with a damping ratio that `wobble` maps across springs.flick, springs.recoil and looser. Over a button or link it reaches for it side-first and wraps the child's own rounded box as a tint; leaving, the far side clings while the near side follows, until it lets go and snaps back into a ball. Keyboard focus on a child gets the same wrap and Enter or Space squashes it; any key returns the system cursor.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/jelly-cursor`

Props:

- `size`: number (default 28) — The jelly ball's diameter, in px.
- `wobble`: number (default 0.5) — How long it jiggles once it stops: 0 settles at once (flick), 0.5 bounces twice (recoil), 1 keeps on jiggling.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "mint" | "ember" | "ink" | string (default "cobalt") — Its colour: a named pigment from the theme tokens, or any CSS colour.
- `stretch`: number (default 0.6) — How far it draws out behind a fast pointer, 0 to 1.
- `squash`: number (default 0.5) — How deep a press squashes it, 0 to 1.
- `targets`: string (default "button, a[href], [role='button'], [data-jelly]") — Which children it wraps itself round, as a CSS selector.
- `padding`: number (default size × 0.22) — Room it leaves round a wrapped child, in px; a bigger jelly is puffier (6 at the default size).
- `stickiness`: number (default 0.5) — How far it clings to a child you leave before it lets go, 0 to 1.
- `tint`: number (default 0.16) — Its body's opacity while wrapped round a child, so the label reads through, 0 to 1.
- `restOn`: string (default "[data-jelly-rest]") — The child it rests on with no pointer inside, as a CSS selector; with none it hides.
- `hideCursor`: boolean (default true) — Hide the system cursor while the jelly leads (never over text fields, never after a key press).
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus on a child wraps the jelly round it; Enter or Space squashes it.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer leads the jelly (mouse and pen; a tap moves it to the tapped child).
- `onTargetChange`: (target: HTMLElement | null) => void — Fires when the child it is wrapped round changes, with that child or null.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.

Notes:
- The jelly is an aria-hidden SVG with pointer-events none, so every child keeps its own clicks, focus, keys and focus ring. The system cursor is hidden only inside the box, only for mouse and pen, never over inputs, textareas, selects or contenteditable, and it comes back on any key press and when the pointer leaves.
- Mark the child it should sit on at rest with data-jelly-rest (or pass restOn), so the box shows a designed first frame before anyone points. Add data-jelly to any extra element it should wrap.
- Keyboard focus on a child wraps the jelly round it as a second focus cue beside the ring, and Enter or Space squashes it the way a press does. On touch there is no follower: a tap moves the jelly to the tapped child.
- Under reduced motion it follows 1:1 as a plain disc with no stretch, wobble or squash, and wrapping changes its outline at once with the tint crossfading.
- Pure SVG, no canvas: one path of 40 points written straight to the DOM each frame, numbers rounded to 0.1 px. The loop runs only while the jelly moves or settles, and stops off screen and on a hidden tab.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/shape-swell`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content on top of the field: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.
- `spacing`: number (default 28) — Distance between shape centres, in px (12 to 80).
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the swell rolls, 0 (held) to 3.
- `shapes`: "mixed" | "round" | "plus" | "angular" (default "mixed") — Which shapes fill the grid: all four, circles, plus signs, or squares and triangles.
- `size`: number (default 0.5) — A shape's size at the crest, as a share of the spacing (0.2 to 0.8).
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default ["var(--accent-bright)", "color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent-bright) 40%, var(--signal))"]) — Crest fill colours, laid across the field along the swell, as CSS colours (1 to 3).
- `outline`: string (default "var(--ink-3)") — The trough outlines' colour, any CSS colour.
- `stroke`: number (default 1.25) — Outline width, in px.
- `turn`: number (default 90) — Degrees a shape turns as the crest lifts it (0 to 180): squares become diamonds, plus signs crosses.
- `wavelength`: number (default 320) — Distance between crests, in px.
- `angle`: number (default 35) — The heading the swell rolls along, in degrees; 0 runs left to right.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keyboard focus raise a crest of their own.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the pointer lifts the shapes near it, 0 to 1.
- `pulse`: boolean (default true) — A press on the field (not on a control) sends a ring crest out from it.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The swell rises out of quiet outlines the first time the field comes into view.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the swell still; the pointer can still lift shapes.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds which shape sits where and how each lags the swell.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when the pointer or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) raising its crest.
- `className`: string — Sizes and shapes the box; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

Notes:
- The canvas is transparent, so the field sits on whatever surface you give the box (bg-card, bg-background, an image). Only whole cells are drawn, centred, so the margins match on every side at any width.
- Keyboard: a control inside that gains keyboard focus raises the crest under it and sends a soft ring; blur lets it sink. The field is aria-hidden and never a focus stop or a click target.
- Reduced motion: a still field frozen mid-swell, a diagonal band of filled shapes across the outlines, with no intro and no rings; the pointer's crest is drawn directly under it.
- Cost: one fullscreen WebGL2 draw per frame (four distance-field taps a pixel), only on screen, in a visible tab and while something moves; paused or reduced motion stops once settled. DPR capped at dpr; context loss and missing WebGL2 fall back to a CSS grid of rings.
- Theming: fills and outlines are CSS colours resolved on the element, so tokens follow the theme and a theme switch repaints at once.

### Glass Drift (KQ-1428) — `glass-drift`
Shards of glass drift through soft colour.

Seeded glass shards floating in shallow 3D over a soft colour field, as a background with the content on top: each shard wanders, tilts and turns on its own and refracts the field behind it in WebGL2, magnified, shifted by its tilt and bent hard across a bevelled rim where the colours part a little, tinted toward glass, brighter as it turns edge-on, with a crisp rim lit on the side toward the light and a soft shadow beneath. The pointer parts the shards, each moving aside on springs.glide and drifting home on springs.drift, and a press puffs them outward with a little spin before the drift spring brings them back. It never takes focus; keyboard focus on a control inside parts the glass around it and puffs gently.

- `palette`: "lagoon" | "dawn" | "orchid" | "mono" | readonly string[] (default "lagoon") — A named palette, or your own CSS colours: the wash, then up to three blooms.
- `size`: number (default 0.5) — A shard's size, as a share of the box's shorter side (0.15 to 1).
- `depth`: number (default 0.5) — How far the shards tilt in depth, 0 (flat to you) to 1.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the colour and the glass drift, 0 (held) to 3.
- `tint`: number (default 0.35) — How much the glass tints what it shows, 0 (clear) to 1 (frosted).
- `edge`: number (default 0.7) — How bright the shards' edges catch the light, 0 to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keyboard focus part the shards.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How far the pointer pushes the shards aside, 0 to 1.
- `pulse`: boolean (default true) — A press on the glass (not on a control) puffs the shards outward from it.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The shards float up out of the colour the first time it comes into view.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the drift still; the pointer can still part the shards.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the cut of every shard and where it floats.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

Notes:

- Keyboard: a control inside that gains keyboard focus parts the glass around itself and sends a gentle puff; blur lets the shards drift home. The glass is aria-hidden and never a focus stop or a click target.
- Reduced motion: a still composition with every shard at its resting place and angle, no drift, intro or puff; the pointer parts the shards directly as it moves.
- Cost: the field renders at half resolution, then one blit and two small draws per shard (shadow and glass) from one preallocated vertex buffer; nothing runs off screen, in a hidden tab or when held and settled. ### Fiber Mist (KQ-1429) — `fiber-mist`
Soft fibres of light drifting in haze.

Hundreds of fine fibres drifting through haze as a background, with the content on top: each fibre is a streamline of a slowly turning curl-noise flow, traced from an anchor the flow itself carries, so they curve together and never knot, drawn in Canvas 2D as a fine core inside a faint halo that adds light where fibres cross in a dark haze and deepens like ink silk in a pale one. The pointer combs them, its path laid into the flow so nearby fibres align to it and relax back within about a second and a half, its place on springs.glide and its presence on springs.drift, and a press stirs them aside in a spiral. - `drift`: number (default 1) — How fast the flow carries the fibres, 0 (still) to 3.
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default ["var(--accent-bright)", "var(--signal)", "color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 70%, var(--accent-bright))"]) — Fibre colours, as CSS colours (up to four); each fibre takes one.
- `haze`: string (default "var(--background)") — The haze behind them, any CSS colour: dark haze makes the fibres glow, pale haze makes them ink.
- `length`: number (default 200) — A fibre's length, in px.
- `curl`: number (default 0.35) — How tightly the flow curls, 0 (long lazy sweeps) to 1 (tight eddies).
- `width`: number (default 0.9) — A fibre's core width, in px.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer combs the fibres, and keyboard focus draws them into a stream.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.7) — How firmly the pointer combs, 0 to 1.
- `pulse`: boolean (default true) — A press on the haze (not on a control) stirs the fibres aside in a spiral from it.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The fibres draw themselves out of the haze the first time it comes into view.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the flow still; the pointer can still comb it.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds where every fibre starts, its colour and the flow.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

- `className`: string — Sizes and shapes the box; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

Notes:
- The haze follows the page: on a dark background the fibres add light and glow brighter where they cross; on a light one they multiply and deepen there. Pass haze to set it explicitly.
- Keyboard: a control inside that gains keyboard focus draws the fibres into a level stream through it while it holds focus; blur lets them relax. The haze is aria-hidden and never a focus stop or a click target.
- Reduced motion: a still mist at a seeded moment, fibres at full length, no intro, drift or stirring; the pointer still combs the fibres directly as it moves, and leaving clears the comb.
- Cost: the flow is one noise sample per 22 px grid node per frame, fibres are traced through it with bilinear lookups and drawn in a few dozen batched strokes; every array is preallocated per size and count. Nothing runs off screen, in a hidden tab, or when held with the comb relaxed. DPR capped at dpr.
- Density is absolute: count stays the same as the box grows, so a phone card is denser and a wide hero airier; scale count with your box if you want the same look everywhere.

### Tube Glow (KQ-1430) — `tube-glow`
A colour field seen through an old tube.

A slowly shifting colour field seen through a curved picture tube, as a background with the content in front and perfectly crisp: domain-warped noise through a four-stop ramp, bowed by barrel distortion into a rounded picture that falls into a dark phosphor rim, laid with fine scanlines that close where the light is bright, an aperture grille, a slowly breathing bloom, a rolling sync bar and a soft reflection on the glass, all in two WebGL2 passes. ### Forge Flow (KQ-1431) — `forge-flow`
Molten metal moving under a cooling crust.

A background of molten metal moving under a cooling crust: a heat field carried along a swirling flow and coloured from ember red through molten orange to white heat, and wherever it cools a crust of dark plates closes over it, cracked along borders that glow with the heat beneath and re-heal as the metal moves, the glow breathing in patches. The hand is heat — the spot follows on springs.glide and warms on springs.drift, opening the crust into a bright pool and leaving a trail that crusts over behind it — and a press stokes it, the pool heaving open on springs.recoil; the first time it is seen the surface is poured molten, every current running hot, and cools into its crust on springs.drift. Keyboard focus on content inside it brings the heat to the focused element.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/forge-flow`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content above the metal: a hero, a heading, a call to action.
- `heat`: number (default 0.6) — The temperature, 0 to 1: how much melt shows and how bright the currents run.
- `crust`: number (default 0.55) — How much of the surface the cooling crust covers, 0 to 1, and how thick its plates read.
- `flow`: number (default 1) — How fast the metal flows, 0 to 2; 0 holds it still while the glow and the hand still work.
- `colors`: readonly string[] — Four CSS colours: crust, ember, molten, white heat. Defaults to a crust mixed from the page colour (near-black on dark, bronze on light) and three warm pigments.
- `scale`: number (default 1) — The size of the currents and the crust's plates, 0.5 to 2.
- `pulse`: number (default 0.5) — How strongly the heat glow breathes, 0 to 1.
- `direction`: number (default -18) — The heading of the flow in degrees: 0 runs rightward, positive turns clockwise.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The hand (and keyboard focus inside) heats the metal under it, and a press stokes it.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.7) — How hot the hand runs and how wide it opens the crust, 0 to 1.
- `radius`: number (default 90) — The size of the hand's heat, in CSS px.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Picks the surface: the same seed draws the same currents and plates.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the flow and the glow still; the hand still heats.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — Pour the surface molten and let it cool into its crust the first time it is seen.
- `dpr`: number (default 1.5) — The highest device pixel ratio the surface renders at, never above 2.
- `onIntroEnd`: () => void — Fires once the crust has set after the pour — at once when there is no pour (intro off, reduced motion, no WebGL2).

- `contentClassName`: string — Classes for the content layer above the metal.

Notes:
- The painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render above it untouched, keep their focus order, and a press on a button inside never stokes the metal.
- There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the heat glides to that element, as a hovering hand would. On touch a tap heats the spot for a moment and page scrolling is never taken.
- One WebGL2 fragment pass that renders only while on screen, in a visible page and moving; paused or reduced it draws on change only. The backing store is capped at dpr (and softened past about 1.4 million pixels) and follows ResizeObserver.
- A lost context or a browser without WebGL2 shows a static gradient in the same colours; a restored context repaints. Everything is disposed on unmount.
- Colours are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme or the colors prop changes. Under reduced motion it is a still frame with the crust set, and the hand's heat appears at once with no spring or trail.

- `intro`: boolean (default true) — Ink the higher contours in, lower to higher, the first time the sheet is seen; the lowlands are drawn from the start.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the lines are drawn at, never above 2.

- `contentClassName`: string — Classes for the content layer above the sheet.

Notes:
- The painted layers are aria-hidden and pointer-events-none, labels included (they are paint, not text); children render above them untouched, and a press on a button inside never heaves the hill.
- There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the hill rises under it, as it does under a hovering hand. On touch a press raises and heaves the hill under the finger; page scrolling stays with the page.
- Three height fields are surveyed once per size, seed and scale, then blended each frame, so the land breathes with no noise per frame; marching squares visit only the levels each cell spans, and the grid cell grows with the box so the cost stays bounded. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible page, and while the land breathes or the hill moves.
- Colours and the label font are read from the component's own element, re-read when the theme changes and when web fonts arrive. onSummitChange reports a settled summit once, not every frame, so it can drive a live region.
- Under reduced motion the sheet is still, the survey is drawn at once, and the hill stands under the hand immediately with its spot height.

### Pulse Tiles (KQ-1437) — `pulse-tiles`

The prism sways slowly about its angle of least deviation and the fan swings with it the way a real one does; the pointer turns the prism on the springs.drift constants, heavy and without overshoot, a press sends a pulse of light down the beam and out through the spectrum, and keyboard focus on a control inside turns the prism toward it and pulses.

Notes:
- The light is decoration: the canvas, its SVG stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never pulse the beam.

- In a dark theme the light adds to the surface; in a light theme the bands are laid as soft pigment and the beam as a pale warm line, so both read. Colours resolve on the element and are re-read when the theme changes.

### Pixel Bloom (KQ-1449) — `pixel-bloom`
Pixels that burst open where you touch.

A background of square pixels that bloom: a ring leaves the point you press at 300 px/s and every pixel it reaches turns over about the axis facing it, onto its colour on the springs.recoil constants and on home on springs.glide after a short hold, so each pixel spins once through its colour and the bloom travels out as a ragged ring with the field closing behind it (a long hold lets the pixels land, two small bounces on their stops, and fills the bloom in). Past the reach the ring only knocks pixels on springs.snap, so the bloom fades into the field. A resting pointer blooms where it rests, the pixel under a hovering pointer warms toward the colour, soft blooms open on their own every few seconds, and keyboard focus on a control inside blooms from that control.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pixel-bloom`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content on top of the field: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.
- `pixel`: number (default 10) — The pixel pitch in px, 4 to 32.
- `gap`: number (default 1) — Page showing between pixels, px.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast a bloom's ring travels, × 300 px/s, 0.25 to 3.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "violet" | string (default "cobalt") — The face a pixel turns over to: a named pigment or any CSS colour.
- `reach`: number (default 200) — How far a bloom turns pixels fully over, px; past it they only tilt.
- `hold`: number (default 90) — How long a turned pixel rests on its colour before turning home, ms: short makes a ring, long a disc.
- `shape`: "circle" | "diamond" | "square" (default "circle") — The ring's outline: round, a diamond or a square.
- `ambient`: number (default 4200) — A soft bloom opens on its own about this often, ms; 0 for never.
- `linger`: number (default 650) — A pointer resting this long blooms where it rests, ms; 0 for never.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Presses, a resting pointer and keyboard focus inside open blooms.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 1) — How hard a press blooms, 0 to 1: how far it reaches and how many pixels turn fully.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — No blooms of its own; the visitor's still open.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the field's tones, the ring's raggedness and where blooms open by themselves.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A pop for every bloom the visitor opens. Off unless asked for.
- `onBloom`: (bloom: { x: number; y: number; source: "press" | "linger" | "focus" | "ambient" }) => void — Fires when a bloom opens, with where it opened and what opened it.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- The field is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never bloom.
- Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus, a bloom opens from its centre — the same bloom a press makes. The background adds no tab stop of its own.
- Under reduced motion one bloom is held still mid-flight and nothing opens on its own; a press lights every pixel in reach at once, with no travelling ring and no turning, holds, and fades back by colour.
- Canvas 2D: the resting field is drawn once and each frame is one blit plus the pixels that are moving. The loop stops when they stop (pixels holding their colour wait on a single timer), nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page, and the backing store caps its pixel ratio at 2.
- Sound is off by default. With sound on, each bloom the visitor opens pops once — pitched by pixel size and panned to where it opened — and only after the page has had a click, tap or key; blooms that open on their own are silent.
- Colours resolve on the element and are re-read when the theme changes; the named colours are pigments at a fixed lightness, so a turned pixel reads the same on a light page and a dark one.

- `palette`: "cobalt" | "clay" | "sea" | "dusk" | readonly string[] (default "cobalt") — A named palette, or 2 to 8 CSS colours of your own, one per ribbon in turn.
- `width`: number (default 1.3) — A ribbon's width as a share of its spacing, 0.6 to 1.6: past 1 they overlap and fold over each other.
- `twist`: number (default 0.5) — How far the ribbons turn over along their length, 0 (flat) to 1 (turning right over).
- `angle`: number (default -8) — The tilt of the whole stack, degrees, −30 to 30.
- `speed`: number (default 0.5) — How fast the bends travel, 0 (still) to 2.
- `shadow`: number (default 0.5) — How dark a ribbon's shadow falls on the ones beneath it, 0 to 1.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.4) — A soft light along the flat of each ribbon, 0 to 1.
- `grain`: number (default 0.2) — A whisper of grain that also hides banding, 0 to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keyboard focus part the ribbons, and a press throws a fold along them.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How far the hand parts the ribbons and how hard a press folds them, 0 to 1.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the ribbons still; the hand still parts and folds them.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds every bend, twist and weave, so two folds never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when the pointer or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) parting the ribbons.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- The ribbons are decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never fold.
- Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the ribbons part around it and a softer fold leaves from it; blur lets go. The background adds no tab stop of its own.
- Under reduced motion one composed moment is held still — the ribbons bent and plaited, with no drift and no folds — and the hand parts them exactly where it is, with no easing travel.
- One WebGL2 pass. It draws thirty frames a second while it only drifts and every frame while the hand or a fold works; paused or at speed 0 it stops once they settle, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2 and resizes with its box.
- Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still frame of the palette stands in; the named palettes are pigments at a fixed lightness, and every colour resolves on the element and is re-read when the theme changes.

### Iris Watch (KQ-1451) — `iris-watch`
A vast iris that follows your every move.

A background that is one enormous iris seen close up — fibrous strands from the pupil to a darkening limbus, a warmer burst inside a zig-zag collarette, dark crypts, a deep pupil and a window of light on the cornea — that watches: the eye turns toward the pointer on a heavy, critically damped spring with the springs.drift ratio (its stiffness set by tracking), the iris sliding and foreshortening as the ball turns. The pupil breathes and narrows as the pointer comes near, a press flashes it small on a stiff spring before it opens again as the flash fades, it blinks now and then and glances about when nobody is near; keyboard focus on a control inside draws its gaze to that control.

- `glint`: number (default 0.6) — The window caught on the cornea, 0 to 1.
- `wander`: boolean (default true) — With nobody near, the eye glances about by itself.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keyboard focus inside draw its gaze, and a press flashes it.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How much the pointer's nearness narrows the pupil and how hard a press flashes it, 0 to 1.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — No breathing, wandering or blinking; it still follows the hand.

### Harp Strings (KQ-1452) — `harp-strings`
Lines that ring when you pluck them.

A background of horizontal strings that ring: each is a real fixed–fixed string solved by up to eight standing-wave modes, each turning at its own frequency and fading at its own rate, so a pluck is exact superposition and dies away the way a string does, treble strings shivering faster than bass ones and brightening toward their colour as they ring. A passing pointer catches the nearest string, bends it 1:1 round the hand and lets it go when the hand pushes through, so a slow pass drags each string before it twangs and a fast strum sweeps every one it crosses; a press grabs a string, the drag pulls it 1:1 with rubber-banding and the release plucks it with the hand's speed, and keyboard focus on a control inside strums the strings behind it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/harp-strings`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content on top of the strings: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.
- `strings`: number (default 24) — How many strings span the frame, 6 to 48.
- `damping`: number (default 0.35) — How quickly a plucked string falls quiet, 0 (rings about four seconds) to 1 (a muted third of a second).
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "brass" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — A ringing string's colour: a named token or any CSS colour.
- `tension`: number (default 0.5) — How tight the strings are, 0 (slack, slow and wide) to 1 (tight, a fast shiver).
- `scale`: "pentatonic" | "major" | "minor" | "chromatic" (default "pentatonic") — The notes the strings are tuned to, around C5 in the middle.
- `breeze`: number (default 0.35) — How much an idle breeze sets the strings shimmering, 0 to 1.
- `pluck`: number (default 0.6) — How hard a passing hand plucks, 0 to 1.
- `weight`: number (default 1.2) — A string's line weight, px; bass strings are drawn a little heavier.
- `inset`: number (default 20) — How far in from each side the strings are fixed, px.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A passing pointer, a press, a drag and keyboard focus inside pluck the strings.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — No breeze; plucked strings still ring.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the breeze.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Each pluck plays its string's note. Off unless asked for.
- `onPluck`: (pluck: { string: number; note: string; strength: number }) => void — Fires on every pluck, with the string, its note and how hard.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- The strings are decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never pluck.
- Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the strings behind it are strummed top to bottom, 28 ms apart — the ringing a hand passing across them makes. The background adds no tab stop of its own.
- Touch: a tap plucks the string under it and a sideways-and-down drag strums; the box keeps touch-action pan-y, so an upright swipe still scrolls the page — and a swipe the page takes never plucks, because a string is only grabbed once a press has become a drag.
- Under reduced motion the strings stay straight and nothing shimmers; a pluck shows as the string's colour rising at once and fading as it would have rung, and its note still plays when sound is on.
- Sound is off by default. With sound on, each pluck plays its string's note from the scale, louder for harder plucks and panned to where it was plucked; plucks from a passing pointer only sound once the page has had a click, tap or key, and the breeze is silent.
- Canvas 2D on typed arrays, nothing allocated per frame. With only the breeze it draws thirty frames a second; with the breeze at 0 or paused it stops once the strings are still, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.

### Sweep Scope (KQ-1453) — `sweep-scope`
A sweep that finds what is out there.

A background that is a radar scope: range rings with their numbers, faint spokes and ticks, and a beam that nods across the upper half from a centre on the bottom edge (or turns full circle from the middle), its afterglow exact — every half-degree of bearing remembers when the beam last crossed it — lighting ground clutter as it rakes it, while vessels drifting across show only where the beam last painted them, each paint fading into a dotted track. A press places a contact whose corner brackets close in on springs.snap; nothing shows there until the sweep finds it, when the blip lands on springs.recoil and a ping ring opens, and keyboard focus on a control inside places a contact at that control.

- `trail`: number (default 110) — How far behind the beam its afterglow reaches, degrees, 20 to 300.
- `persistence`: number (default 2600) — How long a contact glows after the beam paints it, ms.
- `contacts`: number (default 6) — How many vessels drift across the scope by themselves, 0 to 16.
- `clutter`: number (default 0.35) — Ground returns near the centre that the beam lights as it rakes them, 0 to 1.
- `grid`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the rings, spokes and ticks are drawn, 0 to 1.
- `labels`: boolean (default true) — Range numbers on the rings and bearings where the spokes leave the frame.
- `cursor`: boolean (default true) — A faint range ring and crosshair follow the pointer.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A press, and keyboard focus inside, places a contact for the sweep to find.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Stop the sweep: the scope holds its picture; placed contacts still mark.

- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

Notes:
- The scope is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never place a contact.
- Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus a contact is placed at its centre — the same contact a press places — and the sweep finds it on its next pass; blur takes the cursor away. The background adds no tab stop of its own.
- Under reduced motion the beam stands parked with its afterglow drawn as if it had just passed and every vessel at its last paint; a placed contact shows at once, lit, with its brackets closed and no ping, and onFind fires with onPlace.
- Canvas 2D: the face (rings, spokes, ticks, labels) is drawn once per size or theme; a frame is one blit, a third-resolution afterglow buffer from a precomputed bearing map, and a sprite per blip, with nothing allocated per frame. Paused, it stops once the last marker settles; nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page, and the canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.
- Bearings are degrees clockwise from straight up and ranges are in rings, so onPlace and onFind can feed a readout directly; labels drop away below 280 px wide, and the mono labels are redrawn once the page's fonts have loaded.

- Cost: one fullscreen WebGL2 pass at 0.75 render scale, sparks evaluated only near the ribbon, thirty frames a second while it only flows and every frame while the hand or a whip works; nothing off screen, in a hidden tab, or once paused or speed 0 has settled. DPR is capped at dpr. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still ribbon stands in and a restored context repaints.
- Theming: white-hot at the core on a dark page and a paler line in the ink on a pale one; colours resolve on the component's own element, so a theme switch repaints. Pass any CSS colour to color.

### Dust Motes (KQ-1458) — `dust-motes`
Dust drifting through a beam of light.

A background of dust hanging in still air, seen through a lens, with a beam of light crossing the room and the content on top: seeded flakes wander on slow currents, rise a little in the warm light and flash as they turn to it, while a thin-lens depth of field opens near and far motes into soft bokeh discs and keeps those at the focal plane crisp. The pointer leans the camera on springs.drift, so near motes slide further than far ones, and a press racks focus to the mote under the hand, the focal plane travelling to its depth on springs.glide while a thin focus mark closes on it on springs.snap. The hand is not reported through onActiveChange, since the camera never leans.

### Shutter Glow (KQ-1459) — `shutter-glow`
Blinds of gradient turning in the light.

### Grain Mesh (KQ-1460) — `grain-mesh`
A grainy gradient that shifts like a print.

A background printed rather than rendered, drawn in one WebGL2 pass with the content on top: a mesh gradient of four to six spot inks laid down drum by drum like a risograph, through a stochastic screen fixed to the paper so ink lands as grain where it is thin and solid where it is thick, each drum a little out of register on a stock with fibres and tooth. - `drift`: number (default 0.6) — How fast the points drift on their orbits, 0 (still) to 2.

- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.5) — How far the nearest ink leans toward a hovering hand, 0 to 1.

- `width`: number (default 0.4) — How broad each ray is, 0 (a fine blade) to 1 (a wide wedge).
- `intensity`: number (default 1) — How bright the light is, 0 to 1.5.
- `pulse`: number (default 0.5) — How much the rays breathe and ripple in length and brightness, 0 to 1.
- `halo`: number (default 0.35) — How bright the faint spectral ring around the burst is, 0 (none) to 1.
- `saturation`: number (default 0.8) — How rich the split colours are, 0 (grey fringes) to 1 (pure spectrum).
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The centre follows the hand, a press blooms the burst, and keyboard focus inside carries it to the control.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.7) — How far toward the hand the centre travels and how hard a press blooms, 0 to 1.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the turning and the pulse still; the hand still carries the centre.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds every ray's length, width, brightness and rhythm.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onBurst`: () => void — Fires when a press (or keyboard focus) blooms the burst.
- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when the pointer or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) carrying the centre.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- The canvas and its CSS stand-in are aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render above them and keep every click. A press on a control is the control's; only the bare background blooms.
- There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside carries the centre over it and blooms softly, and leaving returns it home.
- One fullscreen WebGL2 draw at half the capped pixel ratio; each pixel weighs only the ray under it and its two neighbours, with ray shapes hashed in the shader. 30 frames a second while it only turns, every frame while a spring settles, nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and nothing when paused and settled. Context loss shows the stand-in until the context returns.
- In the dark theme the light adds to the page; in the light theme it lays down as washes, the white of each ray only a faint warm shade and its split edges tinting the page. The page colour is read from the component's own element and re-read on theme change.
- Under reduced motion the burst is still at a seeded moment: the centre lands where the hand puts it at once, and a press shows the bloom's peak while it is held.

### Star Spiral (KQ-1466) — `star-spiral`
A galaxy turning slowly in the dark.

A background of a spiral galaxy built from density waves: every star rides its own closed orbit, the orbits bulging into lobes that twist with radius, so the arms stand where neighbouring orbits crowd while every star streams through them, the core turning faster than the rim. Young stars light only along the arm ridges, a bulge glows at the centre and dust rides each arm's leading edge, becoming the dark lane when the disk is seen edge on. A drag tilts the plane 1:1, rubber-banding past edge on, and on release it swings back on springs with the springs.drift constants taking the release velocity; a tap sends a ring of star formation out from the core on the enter easing as the core flares on a drift-spring impulse, and keyboard focus on a control inside tilts the plane toward it and sends a softer ring.

- `core`: number (default 0.6) — How bright the bulge glows, 0 to 1.
- `dust`: number (default 0.5) — How heavy the dust lanes along the arms are, 0 (none) to 1.
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The young stars' colour along the arms, any CSS colour.
- `coreColor`: string (default "var(--warn)") — The old stars' and the bulge's colour, any CSS colour.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A drag tilts the plane, a tap sends a ring of new stars out, and keyboard focus inside tilts toward the control.

- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when a drag or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) tilting the plane.

Notes:

- Canvas 2D with every orbit in typed arrays: a frame is a few trig calls per star and about a dozen batched fills, nothing allocated per frame. 30 frames a second while it turns, every frame while dragging, swinging back or ringing, nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and nothing when paused and settled.

- onTiltChange reports whole degrees only when they change, so a status line can follow a drag without rendering every frame.

### Dither Dunes (KQ-1467) — `dither-dunes`
Gradients printed in ordered dots.

### Relay Terminal (KQ-1468) — `relay-terminal`
A terminal screen humming with glyphs.

A background that is a terminal screen of mono glyphs holding real-looking console output, updating in bursts: lines re-roll and settle left to right, value fields tick, and now and then the screen feeds a line, scrolling up a row on the springs.glide constants while the new line types in behind a blinking cursor. Notes:

- The phosphor resolves on the element and is re-read when the theme changes: on a dark page it glows over a tinted tube, on a light page it is drawn as ink on a pale screen, so it reads in both.
- Glyphs come from an atlas built once per font, colour, theme and pixel ratio, one blit per cell a frame; block elements are drawn, not set in type, so meters join without seams. If the host's mono face is not monospaced the system's is used.
- Under reduced motion the screen is still with the newest lines a little brighter; the lamp lands where the hand is and a press lights the glyphs round it, fading back without anything travelling.
- Thirty frames a second while only the output runs, every frame while a tear springs, a ping travels, the screen scrolls or the hand moves; nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and paused stops the loop once the phosphor settles.

- The skein is decoration: the canvas, its SVG stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden. Your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact, and a press on one of your controls never pinches.
- Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus gathers the threads to it and plucks them once, the same swing a press and release gives. No tab stop of its own.
- Colours are pigment, not text colour: each palette hue is drawn at a fixed lightness per theme and the gap under each thread is the box's own colour, all re-read when the theme changes.
- Canvas 2D: two strokes per thread plus a few sheen arcs on its bends; every control point's spring lives in typed arrays sized once. The drift alone draws thirty frames a second, the hand and a release get every frame, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page.
- The server renders the same skein at a composed moment as an SVG traced with arithmetic-only noise, so it matches the browser to the digit.
- Under reduced motion the skein holds that composed moment, nothing gathers, and a press lights the bends round it where they lie.

### Oil Film (KQ-1474) — `oil-film`
The colour of light on oil.

A background of oil floating on a dark wet ground, its colour computed rather than painted: a WebGL2 shader builds the film's thickness from noise warped by noise and wound into spiral arms, then turns thickness into colour by thin-film interference summed across nine wavelengths, so the colours fall in a puddle's true order — dark where the film is thinnest, deep blue, magenta and gold, pearl where it lies thick. Moving the pointer stirs it with vortex pairs that carry the oil along the stroke and spread as they settle, and a press touches the film like a drop of solvent: a ring spreads on the springs.glide constants and the colours race outward round a dark eye that slowly heals. - `saturation`: number (default 0.7) — How much colour the light carries, 0 (pearl and grey) to 1 (full interference colour).

- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the hand stirs, 0 to 1.

- `images`: readonly string[] — Image URLs to show on the tiles, covering each one. Without them the tiles are generated prints.
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default five token-derived pigments) — The pigments the generated prints are made from, as CSS colours (2 to 6).
- `aspect`: number (default 1.3) — A tile's width over its height (0.5 to 2.5).
- `gap`: number (default 10) — Space between tiles and between rows, px (0 to 32).
- `radius`: number (default 8) — Tile corner radius, px (0 to 24).
- `variation`: number (default 0.5) — How differently the rows cruise, 0 (all alike) to 1.
- `fade`: number (default 0.5) — How far the wall fades into the page at its edges, 0 (hard edge) to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keyboard focus stir the rows, and rows can be grabbed.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How hard a sweep of the hand surges the rows near it, 0 to 1.
- `grab`: boolean (default true) — A sideways drag grabs the row under it and a release throws it.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the cruise; the hand can still stir and throw the rows.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the prints, the row speeds and where each row starts.
- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when the rows start (true) or stop (false) answering the hand: a surge, a grab or a throw coasting.
- `onFling`: (row: number, velocity: number) => void — Fires when a grabbed row is let go, with its row (0 at the top) and its throw, px/s.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- The wall is decoration: the plane, its tiles and any images (alt="") are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with focus and clicks intact. Presses on your controls never grab a row.
- Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus surges the rows behind it, the same answer a sweep of the hand gets. The wall has no tab stop of its own.
- On touch the wall takes sideways drags only (touch-action: pan-y), so the page still scrolls under a vertical swipe.
- Pass images for your own work; they load lazily and cover each tile. The generated prints use pigments mixed a tenth into the page, so they sit in both themes; give your own colors as any CSS colours.
- Under reduced motion the rows hold still; a drag still moves the row under the finger and it stays where it is let go, with no coast and no surge.
- Transform-only: one translate per row per frame, on screen in a visible page only, and the loop stops once a paused or speed-0 wall has settled.

### Shape Lattice (KQ-1481) — `shape-lattice`
A lattice of shapes that turn to face you.

A background lattice of small plates — squares, crosses or arrows — that turn in 3D to face the hand, with your content on top: plates under the hand look straight up at full size and those further off tip toward it, foreshortened down to slivers, so the lattice draws rings around whatever it is looking at. The turning travels — each plate faces where the hand was distance / waveSpeed seconds ago and arrives on its own spring with glide's stiffness softened by distance — while the hand's place follows on springs.glide and its presence on springs.drift. A press sends a ring of plates tumbling over in a full flip; with no hand near, a slow light wanders the lattice and the plates track it, and keyboard focus on a control inside brings the hand there with a softer ring.

- `color`: "ink" | "accent" | "signal" | "ember" | string (default "ink") — The plates' colour: a named token colour or any CSS colour.
- `size`: number (default 0.56) — A plate's size as a share of the spacing (0.2 to 0.95).

- `damping`: number (default 0.5) — How the plates arrive, 0 (wobbly) to 1 (no overshoot).
- `light`: number (default 0.6) — How much the plates catch the light as they turn, 0 (flat) to 1.
- `wander`: boolean (default true) — With no hand near, a slow light wanders the lattice and the plates track it.
- `flip`: boolean (default true) — A press on the lattice (or keyboard focus arriving inside) sends a ring of plates tumbling over.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keyboard focus are what the plates turn to face.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the wandering light still; the hand still turns the plates.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the wandering light's path.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

### Strip Shred (KQ-1484) — `strip-shred`
Deleted, one strip at a time.

A delete control with a shredder under the card: confirming makes the teeth bite on springs.flick, then the motor pulls the card into the mouth at a steady rate with a stick-slip judder while the teeth and the head shiver, and the card comes out underneath as strips that roll toward you as they hang, printed with the fragments of the card's own words that were in each column, before each lets go on a seeded beat and falls into the bin. Undo springs every strip back up on springs.snap in a cascade and feeds the card back out on springs.glide; the button cycles Delete, Confirm, Undo with a draining ring, Deleting and Deleted in one place, so Enter, Space, Escape and the Delete key all work without focus moving.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/strip-shred`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The card's content. The component draws the card's paper, border and padding around it.
- `label`: string (default "Delete") — The button's idle label and accessible name.
- `confirmLabel`: string (default "Confirm") — The label while it waits for a second press.
- `undoLabel`: string (default "Undo") — The label from the shred until the undo window closes.
- `deletingLabel`: string (default "Deleting") — The label while onDelete's promise is pending.
- `deletedLabel`: string (default "Deleted") — The label once the delete has landed.
- `shreddedLabel`: string (default "Shredded") — Printed in the dashed outline left where the card was.
- `onDelete`: () => void | Promise<unknown> — Called when the undo window closes. Return a promise to show the pending state; a rejection reassembles the card.
- `onUndo`: () => void — Called when the visitor undoes the shred.
- `deleted / defaultDeleted`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether the card has been deleted. A host setting it back to false reassembles the card; setting it true shreds it without a window.
- `onDeletedChange`: (deleted: boolean) => void — Fires with true when the delete lands.
- `onPhaseChange`: (phase: "idle" | "armed" | "shredding" | "undo" | "deleting" | "deleted" | "restoring") => void — Fires on every step of the cycle, from the press or timer that caused it.
- `strips`: number (default 10) — How many strips the cutters make, 3 to 24.
- `undo`: number (default 5000) — The undo window after the shred, in ms; 0 deletes as soon as the shred finishes.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — The motor's speed, 0.25 to 3: the feed, the slips and the fall all scale with it.
- `curl`: number (default 0.6) — How far the strips roll toward you as they hang, 0 to 1.
- `resistance`: number (default 0.5) — How hard the paper fights the cutters: the depth of the stick-slip judder, 0 to 1.
- `confirm`: boolean (default true) — Ask for a second press before shredding.
- `paper`: string (default "var(--card)") — The card's paper, any CSS colour; the strips are cut from it and their turned-over backs are mixed from it in oklab.
- `ink`: string (default "var(--ink-2)") — The colour of the word fragments printed on the strips.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Width cap, head, button and bin size.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the motor's scratch (stepping with each slip), the thud of the last strip and a softer one when an undo lands. Only ever in answer to a press or key.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is w-full up to its size's max width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the button is a real <button> whose name follows its visible label. Enter or Space arms it, again shreds, and during the shred or the window undoes. Escape disarms an armed button and undoes during the window (both preventDefault); blur also disarms. The Delete key with focus inside the card arms and confirms, except in text fields. Pending and deleted states are aria-disabled, never disabled, so focus is never dropped.
- A polite live region speaks each step once: "Shredding. Undo is open for 5 seconds.", "Restored.", "Deleted." and "Couldn't delete. Restored." when onDelete rejects. The shredded card is inert and hidden; the strips are aria-hidden SVG.
- Reduced motion: no bite, judder, shiver, fall or springs. The card crossfades out and a still frame of hanging strips (with their word fragments, gently curled at the tips) crossfades in, holds through the window and fades when the delete lands; undo crossfades back. The undo ring still drains.
- Performance: the strips, the card and the teeth are written from one paint per frame on motion's frame loop, driven by the feed and fall animations, and nothing runs at rest. The card's words are measured once per shred (Range client rects), and the card's size is tracked with a ResizeObserver.
- onDelete is only called when the undo window closes, so an undo never reaches the server; with undo={0} it is called as soon as the strips have fallen.

### Paper Ball (KQ-1485) — `paper-ball`
Crumple it, toss it, done.

A discard control you crumple and throw: holding the note folds a 6×6 mesh of the sheet inward along seeded creases into a lumpy paper ball, the facets that turn over going dark and the handwriting twisting with the paper, while letting go early springs it flat on springs.snap. A formed ball is tossed on a true ballistic arc into a wire basket, or dragged 1:1 and thrown with the release velocity into a small room whose floor, walls and the basket's rim lips it bounces off; a miss rolls to rest and glides home on springs.glide, and a ball that drops between the lips rocks the basket on springs.recoil. Space or Enter held crumples like a press, Delete crumples and tosses in one motion, and Escape smooths the sheet out.

- `crumple`: number (default 0.8) — How tight the ball is, 0 to 1: a loose wad (bigger, softer creases) to a small, hard, deeply creased ball.
- `arc`: number (default 0.5) — The toss's height, 0 to 1: a flat line drive to a high lob. The arc is solved so it always drops through the mouth.

- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The scene's max width: 260, 300 or 340px; its height follows the 5:3 scene.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a crinkle at every fifth of the hold, a crisp one on the toss and a thud on every landing, scaled by how hard it hits.

Once discarded it stays focusable, aria-disabled, named `discardedLabel`.
- Pointer: press and hold to crumple; release to toss, or keep the pointer down and drag the ball (touch-action: none) to throw it yourself. A polite live region says "Crumpled.", "Missed the basket." and "Discarded.".
- Reduced motion: the hold still charges, shown as creases and facet shading fading in on the flat sheet with a ring filling round it; a full hold crossfades the sheet to the ball, and a release crossfades it into the basket — no flight, no bounce, every release lands.
- Performance: one SVG. The note is redrawn from one function once per frame on motion's frame loop while it changes; the flight is a fixed-step integrator on that loop that runs only while the ball moves and stops when it lands or rests. The first frame (a flat note, or a ball in the basket) is server-rendered.
- Colours are CSS strings; the paper and ink default to pigments of the warn token at fixed lightness, the room and basket use surface and ink tokens, so it reads in both themes.

- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The box's max width (260, 300 or 340px); the card is 86% of it at 8:5, the rest is room for the lift.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish on every committed turn, pitched by the flip's speed and panned by where the card is.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Holds the card still and takes it out of the tab order.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the card is a focusable role="button" with aria-pressed (pressed = back showing), named by `label` and described by the visible face. Enter flips it on press, Space on release (as a native button), and Left/Right (or Up/Down for axis="x") flip it in that direction. The hidden face is aria-hidden and inert.
- Pointer: drag along the axis to turn it 1:1 (touch-action pan-y for the y axis, pan-x for x, so the page still scrolls the other way); a tap flips it. Pointer capture is only taken once the drag starts.
- Reduced motion: no rotation, lift, tilt or wobble — the faces crossfade on a short tween, and a drag past the threshold crossfades on release.
- Performance: CSS 3D transforms from motion values; the shading, sheen and shadow are derived with useTransform. Nothing runs at rest, and the angle is folded back to 0 or 180 after each landing.
- The box reserves room around the card (it is 86% of the width) so the lift and the perspective of a full turn stay inside the component's own box.

### Branch Out (KQ-1488) — `branch-out`
A menu that grows its options like branches.

A menu that grows its options like branches: opening grows a short stem out of the trigger, then a branch per option draws along a curve whose bend you set, nearest the centre line first and staggered, and as each arrives a bud swells at its end and the option opens out of it on springs.snap. Hovering or focusing an option thickens and tints its branch and grows a leaf at its middle, and closing retracts everything in reverse on the exit ease. It is a real menu button: arrows move a roving focus, Home and End jump, letters type ahead, Enter or Space chooses and Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/branch-out`

Props:

- `onSelect`: (id: string) => void — Called with the chosen option's id.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether the menu is open, controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the press, key or outside click that opened or closed it.
- `label`: string (default "Add") — The trigger's accessible name and the menu's; also shown beside the trigger while closed.
- `icon`: ReactNode (default a plus) — The trigger's icon; it turns 45° on springs.snap while open.
- `side`: "right" | "left" (default "right") — Which way the branches grow from the trigger.
- `spread`: number (default 0.5) — How wide the fan opens, 0 to 1: the options' spacing and the radius of the arc they sit on.
- `curve`: number (default 0.6) — How the branches bend, 0 to 1: straight twigs to S-shaped tendrils.
- `stagger`: number (default 60) — Time between one branch and the next as they grow, in ms; capped so the whole growth stays near 600ms.
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The trigger's fill and the colour a branch, bud and leaf take when their option is hot; any CSS colour.
- `branchColor`: string (default "var(--hairline-strong)") — The branches and buds at rest; any CSS colour.
- `closeOnSelect`: boolean (default true) — Close the menu (and return focus to the trigger) after an option is chosen.
- `showLabel`: boolean (default true) — Show `label` beside the trigger while closed; it gives way as the branches grow.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Max width (280, 320 or 360px), trigger and option height.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pop as each option buds (rising in pitch), a tick as focus moves and a lower tick on choose and close; only in answer to a press or key.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the trigger.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root box, whose height follows the item count and spread.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the trigger is a <button> with aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls. Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens it with the first option focused, ArrowUp with the last. In the menu, Up/Down move a roving tabindex, Home/End jump, typed letters jump to the next match, Enter/Space choose, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (preventDefault), and Tab closes and lets focus move on. Focus moves to an option only after the open menu has committed.
- While closed the menu stays mounted for its exit animation but is inert and aria-hidden, so nothing in it can be focused or read.
- Reduced motion: the branches appear whole and the options fade in together; closing fades them out. The trigger's icon swaps without turning.
- Performance: the branch geometry is computed once per item count, spread and curve, with no measurement — the option labels truncate (and are titled) in whatever width is left. Branches draw with motion's pathLength; nothing runs at rest.
- The component's box is the size of the open menu (its height follows the item count), so the branches never draw outside it; place it where that space is free.

### Think Thread (KQ-1491) — `think-thread`
A thought drawn as a wandering line.

A thinking indicator drawn by an invisible pencil: a single fine line travels a small box, curls into loops, turns hairpins and doubles back, with only its last stretch kept and fading toward the tail. When thinking ends the stroke is pulled taut — every point travels to its place on a straight line, pencil end first, on springs.glide — the straightened line rings once like a plucked string on springs.recoil, and the status word fades in at its end on springs.snap. It needs no keys: the state is spoken politely when thinking starts and when it ends.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/think-thread`

Props:
- `thinking`: boolean (default true) — Whether it is thinking. Turning false pulls the line taut and shows `doneLabel`; turning true sets the pencil off again from the line's end.
- `label`: string (default "Thinking") — The state while thinking, spoken politely when thinking starts.
- `doneLabel`: string (default "Done") — The status word that fades in once the line is straight, and is spoken.
- `pace`: number (default 1) — How fast the pencil travels, as a multiple of its natural pace.
- `wander`: number (default 0.5) — 0 draws gentle waves; 1 curls into loops and doubles back often.
- `color`: "ink" | "cobalt" | "signal" | "amber" | string (default "ink") — The line's colour: a named ink token or any CSS colour.
- `tail`: number (default 140) — How much of the path stays on the page, in px of travel.
- `strokeWidth`: number (default 1.25) — The line's weight, in px.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The box: 96×20, 136×28 or 184×40 px, and the word's size.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Picks the path; the same seed draws the same thought, on the server and in the browser.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the pencil where it is.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Caps the canvas's device pixel ratio (never above 2).
- `onSettled`: () => void — Fires when the line has gathered and the pluck has rung out.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is inline and grows to fill a stretched parent.

Notes:
- Accessibility: a polite sr-only status speaks `label` when thinking starts and `doneLabel` when it ends — never per frame. The canvas and the still drawing are aria-hidden, and the done word's width is reserved so nothing shifts when it appears.
- Reduced motion: no wandering — a still, seeded scribble (the same simulation run to a fixed point, drawn as SVG) stands in the box and crossfades to the straight line and the word.
- Performance: Canvas 2D with a ring buffer of typed arrays and no per-frame allocation; the backing store is DPR-capped and sized by a ResizeObserver. The loop runs only while thinking or gathering, on screen and on a visible page, and stops once the line is at rest.
- Server rendering: the server sends the seeded still frame (coordinates rounded), which is exactly the canvas's first frame, so the hand-off is seamless and hydration matches.
- Theming: named colours are ink tokens for strokes; the colour is resolved on the component's own node and re-read when it changes, so a theme flip repaints the line.

- `releaseLabel`: string (default "Release to cancel") — What the hint becomes once a release would cancel.

- `color`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The tape's colour.

- `label`: string (default "Notifications") — The region's accessible name.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Note height: 48, 56 or 64px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish as a note is thrown or keyed away (pitched by speed, panned by direction) and a pop as one seats back.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No flicks, keys or close buttons.
- `className`: string — Classes for the region, which is as tall as the fanned stack so nothing jumps on hover.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the region is a labelled <section> with an <ol role="list"> and one tab stop (roving tabindex). Keyboard focus fans the stack; ArrowUp and ArrowDown move between notes, Home and End jump, Enter opens, Delete or Backspace dismisses the focused note and Escape the top one (preventDefault). Focus moves to the note that takes a dismissed one's place.
- Each note's accessible name is one sentence (tone, title, body, time); arrivals are announced politely by title. The close button that appears on hover is for the mouse and is not a tab stop — Delete is its keyboard path.
- Touch: notes are touch-action: none so a flick never scrolls the page; on a touch screen the first tap fans the stack and a tap outside closes it.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels or spins — notes fade in and out where they stand, the fan swaps at once, a held note still follows the finger and a short throw returns without a spring.
- Performance: DOM only, motion values per note, DOM order never changes (new notes are appended and stacked with z-index). Nothing runs at rest.

### Slingshot (KQ-1496) — `slingshot`
Pull back to launch.

An action button held in an elastic band between the two pegs of a fork: pulling it back follows the hand 1:1 while the band's strands wrap its back in a pouch, thin and warm with the stretch, and a faint aim line reaches to the target, whose ring pops on springs.snap once the draw passes the threshold. Let go armed and the band fires the button home on a stiff underdamped spring that carries the release velocity; the frame it passes rest the icon leaves, flies along the aim line and settles into the target with two bounces, while a short pull just springs back on springs.snap. Enter launches with a full draw on springs.glide, Space held draws and fires on release, and Escape cancels a draw.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/slingshot`

Props:

- `icon`: ReactNode (default a horizontal paper plane) — The projectile: what flies out of the button into the target.

- `onLaunchedChange`: (launched: boolean) => void — Fires from the release or key that launched it, and from the uncontrolled reload.
- `onLaunch`: () => void — Fires once per launch, at the moment of release.
- `resetAfter`: number (default 1400) — Uncontrolled: how long the icon stays out before the slingshot reloads, in ms; 0 keeps it out.
- `tension`: number (default 0.5) — The band's stiffness, 0 to 1: thicker at rest, harder to draw past the limit, faster to fire.
- `pull`: number (default 72) — The longest draw in px; past it the band rubber-bands. A narrow box shortens it so the lane ahead keeps room.
- `distance`: number (default 140) — How far the icon flies to its target in px, clamped to the room ahead.
- `threshold`: number (default 0.35) — The share of the full draw that arms a launch; a shorter pull springs back.
- `aim`: number (default 14) — How far a shot can be angled up or down by pulling the other way, in degrees; 0 keeps it level.
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The projectile, the aim line and the target; any CSS colour.
- `bandColor`: string (default "var(--ink-3)") — The band at rest; any CSS colour.
- `tautColor`: string (default "var(--warn)") — The band at full stretch, mixed in oklab as it is drawn; any CSS colour.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Button height (32, 40 or 48px) and the rig's height (112, 132 or 152px).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the band's twang on release (pitch and level by the draw) and a whoosh as the icon leaves; only ever in answer to a drag or key.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the drag and the keys; the button stays in the tab order as aria-disabled.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which fills its width and centres the rig.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the button is a real <button> described by a hint. Enter launches with a full draw; Space held draws the band back and fires on release if it passed the threshold; Escape during a draw cancels it (handled and prevented); a click from assistive technology launches. While launched it stays focusable with aria-disabled, and a polite live region says when it is out and when it is ready again.
- Reduced motion: the drag still follows the hand, but release returns the button on a short tween, and the icon fades out of the button and into the target instead of flying; the ring still fills and the label still changes.
- Controlled use: set launched from onLaunchedChange and back to false when the work is done (a deploy, a send). A host that never takes the launch still sees the shot land, then the slingshot reloads.
- Performance: every per-frame number is a motion value; the band and aim are redrawn only while the button moves. Two ResizeObservers lay out the rig; nothing runs at rest.
- Layout: the rig fills its width and centres itself; the draw room and the flight are clamped to the width, so it works from 258px up. Height is fixed by size.

### Chime Bell (KQ-1497) — `chime-bell`
A bell that rings on, and rests off.

A notifications toggle drawn as a hand bell with a real pendulum inside: turning it on kicks the bell about its crown, and the bell and its clapper — two damped pendulums with different periods, integrated at 240 Hz — swing out of step, so the rim catches the clapper at the extremes in genuine collisions, each heard as a chime as loud as the impact, until the damping settles both to rest and the loop stops. Turning it off catches the bell on springs.snap, greys it in oklab and straps it still with a belt and a buckle that pops on springs.snap, two crossed straps, or tape over the mouth. It is a real toggle button with aria-pressed, so Space and Enter ring it or mute it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/chime-bell`

- `label`: string (default "Notifications") — What the bell turns on: its accessible name and the first line under it.
- `onLabel`: string (default "On") — The state line while on; it shares a cell with offLabel so the width never changes.
- `offLabel`: string (default "Muted") — The state line while off.
- `hideLabel`: boolean (default false) — Keep the label and state line for assistive technology only, leaving just the bell.
- `swing`: number (default 40) — How hard turning on kicks the bell: roughly its first swing in degrees. Below about 18° the clapper never reaches the rim.
- `damping`: number (default 0.4) — How fast the swing dies, 0 to 1: 0 rings for several strikes, 1 strikes once and settles.
- `strap`: "belt" | "cross" | "tape" (default "belt") — How the bell is held while off: a belt round the waist with a buckle, two crossed straps with a rivet, or tape over the mouth.
- `count`: number — Unread count on a badge (99+ past 99). A rise while on rings the bell silently at half swing; while off the bell strains against its strap.
- `color`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.8 0.12 h)") — The bell while on: a brass pigment at fixed lightness, so it reads the same in both themes. Any CSS colour.
- `mutedColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--ink-3) 0.74 0.01 h)") — The bell while off, mixed from the on colour in oklab. Any CSS colour.
- `strapColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.5 0.08 h)") — The strap's leather; the tape is a pale tint of it. Any CSS colour.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The bell at 40, 56 or 72px in a well of 60, 80 or 100px; a smaller bell rings higher.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a chime at each strike of the clapper, as loud as the impact and panned to the side it struck. Only rings that a press set going are heard.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button.
- `className`: string — Classes for the button.

Notes:
- Keyboard: a real <button aria-pressed>, named by label (with ", 3 new" when there is a count). Space and Enter toggle it through the native click; the visible state words are decorative and the pressed state is announced by the button itself.
- Reduced motion: nothing swings or draws. Turning on warms the colour and two sound arcs glow once beside the bell (with one chime if sound is on); turning off fades the strap in whole and greys the bell.
- Sound only answers a press: a host that turns it on, or a count that rises, rings the bell without a sound.
- Performance: the pendulum loop runs only while the bell carries energy, only on screen (IntersectionObserver) and only while the page is visible — otherwise the bell is put straight to rest. Angles are written as transform attributes on two groups, so no React state changes per frame.
- Theming: the bell, its muted state and the strap are pigments at fixed lightness derived from the status tokens, so the brass reads as brass on both a light and a dark page.

### Verdict Mark (KQ-1499) — `verdict-mark`
A mark that settles on the outcome.

A status mark drawn with one two-part stroke: while pending, an arc spins on the ring with its length breathing, and when the state changes that arc, still turning, flows point by point into a check, an exclamation or a cross, head first with its tail following, so the stroke draws itself into the outcome. The check draws on springs.flick, the exclamation's dot drops in on springs.recoil, the cross arrives on springs.snap and shakes once, and the colour moves with it in oklab while the ring turns from a hairline track into a tinted disc. Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/verdict-mark`

- `onSettle`: (state: "success" | "warning" | "error") => void — Fires once an outcome has finished settling: after the flick, the dot's drop or the shake.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | number (default "md") — 20, 32, 48 or 72px, or any number of px; the label's type size follows.
- `stroke`: number (default 3.5) — The stroke's weight in units of the mark's 48-unit box, 1 to 8.

- `colors`: Partial<Record<state, string>> (default accent, success, warn, danger) — The colour for each state, mixed in oklab as it changes. Any CSS colours.
- `speed`: number (default 1.1) — How fast the pending arc turns, in turns per second; its momentum carries into the gather.
- `ring`: boolean (default true) — Draw the ring: a hairline track while pending, a tinted ring and disc once settled.
- `shake`: number (default 3) — How far an error shakes, in units of the 48-unit box; 0 for none.

- `className`: string — Classes for the root, an inline-flex row.

It is not focusable and takes no keys. With announce off it is a named image instead, for marks that repeat down a list.
- Reduced motion: no spin, flow or shake. Pending is a still arc that breathes in opacity; outcomes cross-fade glyph to glyph, the colour still changes and onSettle still fires.
- Performance: the spin loop runs only while pending, on screen (IntersectionObserver) and in a visible tab; each change is one spring writing two path strings of 18 points, and nothing runs once settled.
- Pair it with the work it reports on: set state from your request's lifecycle and use onSettle to move on (close a dialog, show the next step) once the outcome has landed.

- Reduced motion: no neck, remnant or wobble; the drop fades out of one ring and into the next and the ring still takes the colour, because the selection is information.
