### Comet Knob (KQ-1503) — `comet-knob`
A dial that leaves light where it turns.

A rotary knob whose head leaves a comet of light along its track: a follower angle chases the head with an exponential lag, and the arc between them is drawn as a tapered tail whose gradient, glow and halo brighten with the gap, so the comet is as long and as bright as the knob is fast and drains into the head when it stops. Drag on the rim to turn it by angle 1:1 or on the face by distance, flick to coast on motion's inertia generator (started at the hand's speed, decaying by friction, landing on a detent and bouncing once off an end stop), and every detent passed ticks. Arrow keys step a detent on springs.snap so keys draw a comet too, Page keys move a tenth, Home and End jump, and the host's own changes glide on springs.glide.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/comet-knob`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default — / min) — The value, controlled or uncontrolled, from min to max.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the drag, coast or key that changed it, at every detent it passes.
- `onValueCommit`: (value: number) => void — Fires once the knob comes to rest after a gesture, a key or a rim tap: the value to act on.
- `min`: number (default 0) — The value at the start of the sweep.
- `max`: number (default 100) — The value at the end of the sweep.
- `step`: number (default 1) — The resolution when detents is 0.
- `detents`: number (default 12) — Notches across the whole range: the knob ticks at each, keys step by one and releases settle on the nearest. 0 turns smoothly by step.
- `tail`: number (default 0.5) — How long the comet is, 0 to 1: the follower's time constant, 50 to 320 ms behind the head.
- `friction`: number (default 0.4) — How quickly a flick coasts to a stop, 0 to 1: the inertia time constant, 700 to 120 ms.
- `sweep`: number (default 270) — Degrees of travel from min to max, centred on the top (60 to 340).
- `label`: string — The slider's accessible name, shown small under the reading.
- `format`: (value: number) => string (default the value, rounded) — The reading in the face and the spoken aria-valuetext; its longest output's width is reserved.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The comet, head, fill and lit detents: a preset tuned for both themes or any CSS colour.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The knob's box: 120, 152 or 184 px square.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick at every detent passed by hand, coast, key or rim tap, pitch rising with the value; never for the host's changes.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the knob and ignores pointer and keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the slider box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the knob is a focusable role="slider" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext from format. Arrow keys step one detent (or one step), PageUp and PageDown a tenth of the range, Home and End jump; each move runs on springs.snap, so the comet shows for keys too.
- Pointer: drag on the rim to turn by angle (the head stays under the finger) or on the face to turn by distance (up or right increases, about one and a half knobs for the sweep); a tap on the rim sets the value there; a flick coasts and lands on a detent; a press catches a coasting knob. The box is touch-none because the gesture is two-dimensional.
- Reduced motion: no comet, coast or spring travel; the head jumps to its detent with one brief halo, and the face still turns because the angle is the value.
- Performance: the comet's follower is a single requestAnimationFrame chain that runs only while the head moves or the tail is still draining, stops when settled, and is cut while the knob is off screen (IntersectionObserver) or the page is hidden. Geometry is SVG attributes in motion values, rounded to 2 dp.
- Theming: the track, face and knurl use tokens; the comet uses `color` (pigment presets look the same in light and dark).

### Wake Range (KQ-1504) — `wake-range`
A slider that leaves a wake.

A range slider seen from above like water: every frame the thumb moves it drops a wake sample, and each sample's wavefront spreads away from the channel and fades with age, so a moving thumb opens two V-lines behind it like a hull's wake that keep spreading and settle after it stops. The fill catches up on its own critically damped spring with foam showing between it and the thumb, the thumb follows a drag 1:1 and rubber-bands a few px past the ends, a press on the channel sends it there on springs.snap, and a release is projected and settles on the nearest step with the throw's velocity. Arrow keys step on springs.snap so keys leave a wake too, Page keys move a tenth, Home and End jump, and the host's own changes glide on springs.glide.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/wake-range`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default — / min) — The value, controlled or uncontrolled, from min to max.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the drag, press or key that changed it, at every step it passes.
- `onValueCommit`: (value: number) => void — Fires once the thumb comes to rest after a gesture or a key: the value to act on.
- `min`: number (default 0) — The value at the left end.
- `max`: number (default 100) — The value at the right end.
- `step`: number (default 1) — The resolution when steps is 0.
- `steps`: number (default 6) — Stops across the whole range, drawn as dots in the channel: the thumb ticks at each, keys step by one and releases settle on the nearest. 0 slides by step.
- `wake`: number (default 0.6) — How long and wide the wake runs, 0 to 1: a 0.3 s ripple close to the channel, or a 1.6 s wake spreading to the rail's edge.
- `fill`: boolean (default true) — Colour the channel from the start to the value; off leaves only the foam and the wake.
- `catchUp`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly the fill catches up with the thumb, 0 to 1: a lazy tide or a brisk one (a critically damped spring).
- `label`: string — The slider's accessible name, shown above the channel.
- `hideLabel`: boolean (default false) — Keep the label for assistive technology only.
- `format`: (value: number) => string (default the value, to the step's decimals) — The reading and the spoken aria-valuetext; its longest output's width is reserved.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The fill, foam, wake and thumb dot: a preset tuned for both themes or any CSS colour.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Rail height (room for the wake), channel and thumb size, and type.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick at every step the thumb passes by hand, press or key, pitch rising with the value; never for the host's changes.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the slider and ignores pointer and keys.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer column.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the thumb is a focusable role="slider" labelled by the visible label, with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext from format. Arrow keys move one step, PageUp and PageDown a tenth of the range, Home and End jump; each move runs on springs.snap and leaves a wake.
- Pointer: the rail is touch-pan-y, so a horizontal drag moves the thumb and a vertical one still scrolls the page. A press on the channel sends the thumb there and focuses it (without a keyboard ring); a drag that starts while it is still on its way chases the finger until it catches it.
- Reduced motion: no wake and no lag; the fill moves with the thumb and keys and presses move it on a short tween. Dragging stays 1:1.
- Performance: the wake and the fill's spring share one requestAnimationFrame chain that runs only while either is still moving, stops when both settle, and is cut while the slider is off screen or the page is hidden. Wake samples live in a preallocated ring buffer; track, fill and thumb are HTML positioned in percentages, so the server renders the resting frame.
- The wake is drawn inside the rail's own box (its height is the room above and below the channel) and the thumb's overshoot past an end is capped at 6 px, so nothing draws outside the component.

### Pin Slots (KQ-1505) — `pin-slots`
A code that drops into its slots.

A one-time-code field whose characters drop into their slots: one real, transparent input carries the code, and each new character falls from above on springs.recoil with two small landing bounces while its slot's border catches the colour, the next empty slot holds a glow that slides along on springs.snap, a paste fills every slot in one cascade and Backspace lifts the last character out on the exit ease. When the host accepts the code the slots slide together on springs.snap until the gaps close and lock into one success bar; a refusal shakes the row on a keyframe tween and typing again starts a fresh code. Typing, Backspace, paste and SMS autofill are the browser's own, with the caret held at the end.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pin-slots`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default — / "") — The code, controlled or uncontrolled; anything outside the charset is dropped and it is cut to length.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires from the typing, paste or Backspace that changed the code.
- `onComplete`: (code: string) => void — Fires once, from the keystroke or paste that fills the last slot.
- `length`: number (default 6) — How many slots (1 to 12).
- `mask`: boolean (default false) — Show each character as it lands, then cross-fade it into a dot.
- `maskDelay`: number (default 600) — How long a masked character stays readable, in ms.
- `state`: "idle" | "checking" | "success" | "error" (default "idle") — The host's verdict: checking dims the glyphs under a passing light, success locks the slots into one bar, error shakes them and turns them danger.
- `label`: string (default "Verification code") — The input's label, shown above the slots.
- `hideLabel`: boolean (default false) — Keep the label for assistive technology only.
- `hint`: string — A line under the slots while nothing has been decided.
- `successMessage`: string (default "Code accepted.") — Shown under the bar and announced when state is success.
- `errorMessage`: string (default "That code didn’t match. Try again.") — Shown under the slots and announced when state is error.
- `charset`: "numeric" | "alphanumeric" (default "numeric") — Digits only with a numeric keypad on phones, or letters and digits, upper-cased.
- `split`: number — Draw a separator after this many slots, as in 123–456; it folds away when the slots lock.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Slot size (largest width; narrow rows shrink below it) and glyph size.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The caret slot's glow, the caret and the landing flash: a preset tuned for both themes or any CSS colour.
- `name`: string — A form field name for the input.
- `autoFocus`: boolean (default false) — Focus the input on mount.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Tick as each typed or pasted character lands (rising along the row), chime when the slots lock, buzz on a refusal; only for a code the visitor typed.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the input and dims the slots.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer column.

Notes:
- One real <input autocomplete="one-time-code" inputmode="numeric"> sits transparently over the slots, so typing, Backspace, paste and SMS autofill behave natively; the caret is held at the end of the code (a select-all is kept, so a paste replaces). The slots themselves are aria-hidden.
- The input is labelled by `label`, described by the visible hint or message, aria-invalid on error, and aria-busy and read-only (never disabled, so focus stays) while checking. A polite live region speaks one sentence when the state changes.
- Drive `state` from your verification: set "checking" from onComplete, then "success" or "error". After an error, a new keystroke starts a fresh code; set the state back to idle from onValueChange when the code shortens.
- Reduced motion: characters fade in place and lift out as a fade, the caret glow jumps, the checking light does not run, and the bar and the danger state appear without sliding or shaking.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest except the caret's slow breathing while focused; the checking light runs only in that state. Sound and mask timers are cleared on unmount.

### Shy Label (KQ-1506) — `shy-label`
A label that steps aside as you type.

A text field whose label sits inside it and steps aside as you type: focus lifts it above the field on springs.glide with its letters hopping in a ripple from the caret's side, leaving a faint imprint inside, and as the text reaches the imprint each nearby letter hops up and away along a curved, tipping path on its own spring, shrinks and flies to its twin in the raised label, which hops on springs.flick and settles on springs.recoil as its letter regroups. Deleting brings the letters back down on springs.glide. Validation slides the message 4 px into place on glide over the hint while the border, label and an end icon popping in on snap take the state's colour; it is a real input with a real label, so the keyboard, selection and autofill are the browser's own.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/shy-label`

Props:
- `label`: string — The field's label: inside the field at rest, above it once there is focus or text. Its accessible text is a real <label for>.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default — / "") — The text, controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires on every edit with the new text.
- `hint`: string — A line under the field while there is no validation message.
- `state`: "default" | "success" | "error" (default "default") — The validation state: the border, raised label and an end icon take its colour, and message slides in under the field.
- `message`: string — Shown and announced under the field for success and error; the hint returns for default.
- `type`: "text" | "email" | "password" | "search" | "tel" | "url" (default "text") — The input's type; a password measures its dots for the caret.
- `name`: string — A form field name for the input.
- `autoComplete`: string — Passed to the input.
- `scatter`: number (default 0.6) — How lively the letters are as they step aside, 0 to 1: 0 just fades them, 1 sends them on high, tilting arcs.
- `reach`: number (default 20) — How far ahead of the caret, in px, a letter starts to step aside.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Field height (40, 48 or 56 px) and type size.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The focused border and raised label: a preset tuned for both themes or any CSS colour.
- `required`: boolean (default false) — Passed to the input.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the input and dims the field.
- `onFocus / onBlur`: (event: React.FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void — The input's focus handlers, e.g. to validate on blur.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer column.

Notes:
- It is a real <input> labelled by a real <label for>; the animated letters (the raised label and the imprint) are aria-hidden and the label's text is read once from an sr-only copy. aria-invalid is set on error, aria-describedby points at the visible hint or message, and a polite live region speaks the message once when the state changes.
- The component reserves the raised label's row above the field at all times, so focusing never shifts the layout; hint and messages share one grid cell under it for the same reason.
- Validate where it suits your form (on blur is kind) and pass the result through state and message; the label's letters only react to the caret.
- Reduced motion: the label cross-fades between inside and above, the imprint's letters fade as the caret passes with no hop or tilt, and the message fades in place.
- Performance: the caret's position is measured from a hidden mirror in the input's own events, and the letters are motion values; nothing runs at rest or between keystrokes.

### Lattice Wait (KQ-1507) — `lattice-wait`
A loader that weaves itself.

A loading indicator that weaves itself: a thread draws from dot to dot of a small lattice along a seeded walk that turns more than it runs straight, forming a pattern segment by segment, holding it, then unweaving from its tail, and each cycle starts where the last ended with the next seed, so the patterns never repeat but never vary between renders; the dot the thread reaches pops as it arrives. When the work is done the thread lets go, the dots glide one after another on springs.glide onto a check mark (or a cross) whose stroke draws through them on the enter ease, and they dissolve into it; back to loading the mark undraws and the dots glide home. The root is a role="status" whose text changes only with the status.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/lattice-wait`

Props:
- `status`: "loading" | "success" | "error" (default "loading") — Weaving while loading; collapsing into a check or a cross when done.
- `label`: string (default "Loading") — The status text while weaving.
- `successLabel`: string (default "Done") — The status text once it succeeds.
- `errorLabel`: string (default "Failed") — The status text if it fails.
- `showLabel`: boolean (default false) — Show the status text beside the lattice; otherwise it is for assistive technology only.
- `grid`: number (default 4) — Dots on each side of the lattice, 3 to 5.
- `pace`: number (default 1) — Weaving speed: 1 draws five threads a second.
- `hold`: number (default 420) — How long each finished pattern holds before it unweaves, in ms.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds the walks; the same seed weaves the same patterns on the server and in the browser.
- `color`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "ember" | "rose" | string (default "cobalt") — The thread and the lit dots: a preset tuned for both themes or any CSS colour.
- `successColor`: string (default "var(--success)") — The check's colour.
- `errorColor`: string (default "var(--danger)") — The cross's colour.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The lattice's box: 28, 44 or 64 px.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the weave still where it is.
- `onSettle`: (status: "loading" | "success" | "error") => void — Fires when the lattice has finished collapsing into its mark, or back into the weave.
- `className`: string — Classes for the status root.

Notes:
- Accessibility: the root is role="status" (polite) and its only text is the current label, so a screen reader hears "Syncing notes" and later "Notes synced" once each, never the weave. The drawing is aria-hidden; show the text with showLabel or keep it for assistive technology.
- Reduced motion: no weave and no glide; the first pattern is drawn still and the lattice breathes with a slow opacity pulse, and completion cross-fades to the mark.
- Performance: one requestAnimationFrame clock drives everything and runs only while the status is loading, the lattice is on screen (IntersectionObserver), the page is visible and it is not paused; a finished mark costs nothing. Walks are planned once per grid, seed and hold.
- Server render: the first frame shows a weave already three threads in, so a card never starts as an empty grid.

### Drag Number (KQ-1508) — `drag-number`
A number you scrub like a dial.

A numeric field you scrub by its label: a slow drag moves one step per few pixels, a fast one shifts up a gear to ×10 (×100 on long ranges) and snaps to that grid, while the digits roll on real odometer wheels that follow the value on springs.snap, carrying from 9 to 0 the way a counter does. A tick bar appears under the value as a tape beneath a fixed needle, moving 1:1 with the finger at every gear, zooming about the needle on springs.snap when the gear changes and rubber-banding past min and max before settling on springs.snap with the release velocity. It stays a real text input: type and Enter to commit, Escape to revert, ArrowUp and ArrowDown to step (Shift ×10, PageUp/PageDown ×10, Home and End to the ends), with the same tape gliding to each new value.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/drag-number`

Props:
- `label`: string — The field's name: shown on the left, and the handle you scrub.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default — / 0) — The value, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the scrub, key or typed entry that changed it, with the new value.
- `min`: number (default 0) — Lowest value; the tape ends here.
- `max`: number (default 100) — Highest value; the tape ends here.
- `step`: number (default 1) — The value's grid: one arrow key, one slow-scrub detent.
- `precision`: number (default 0) — Decimals shown and kept; never fewer than the step needs.
- `sensitivity`: number (default 1) — Scrub speed: one step per 6 / sensitivity px of a slow drag (also the tape's tick spacing).
- `accelerate`: boolean (default true) — Fast drags shift to coarser steps: ×10 above ~700 px/s, ×100 above ~1800 px/s on ranges of 1000 steps or more.
- `unit`: string (default "") — A short unit shown after the number, e.g. "%", "px", "°".
- `ruler`: boolean (default true) — Show the tick bar along the bottom of the field while scrubbing, stepping, or hovering the label.
- `valueText`: (value: number) => string — The spoken value (aria-valuetext). Defaults to the value and its unit.
- `onScrubChange`: (scrubbing: boolean, gear: number) => void — Fires when a scrub starts, changes gear (1, 10 or 100) and ends.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The needle and the grip while scrubbing; any CSS colour.
- `name`: string — The input's form name.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Field height 32, 36 or 44px, with matching type and tick sizes.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for each value the scrub or a key passes (lower in a coarse gear, and at an end); only in answer to the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the field and the scrub.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the field is a role="spinbutton" text input. ArrowUp/ArrowDown step (Shift ×10), PageUp/PageDown step ten, Home/End jump to min/max, typing replaces the selected value, Enter commits, Escape reverts a draft, blur commits. Text that is not a number shakes the field and reverts.
- Pointer: drag the label sideways (touch-action: pan-y); a tap on the label focuses the field without scrubbing. Hold Shift while dragging to force the ×10 gear. Pointer capture is only taken after 3px of travel.
- Reduced motion: the digits swap instead of rolling and gear changes jump instead of zooming; the tape still appears and still follows the finger 1:1, because it is the reading.
- Performance: no loops. The wheels and the tape are motion values derived from three springs and only compute while those move; the tape path is rebuilt only while it is visible.
- Layout: the number is right-aligned and its width is reserved from max(|min|, |max|) and the precision, so the field never shifts as the value changes. Colours are tokens; the accent is any CSS colour.

### Fuse Confirm (KQ-1509) — `fuse-confirm`
Light the fuse, or put it out.

A destructive button whose edge is a fuse: one press lights the spark at the tip of a little wick, and it burns once round the button in `time` seconds, consuming the cord to ash behind it under a thin trail of smoke while the face counts down on a digit wheel turned by springs.snap. When the spark gets back to the start the action fires with a small spray of streaks and a flash along the spent cord; pressing again, or Escape, stamps it out — the spark squashes flat under a puff of smoke and the cord is re-laid back to the wick on springs.glide. It is a native button (Enter and Space press it) whose face presses in on springs.flick, and a polite live region announces the lighting, the last seconds and the outcome.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/fuse-confirm`

Props:
- `label`: string — What the button does: its text and accessible name at rest.
- `cancelLabel`: string (default "Cancel") — The text while the fuse burns, beside the countdown.
- `firedLabel`: string (default "Done") — The text once the action has fired.
- `lit / defaultLit`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether the fuse is burning, controlled or lit on mount. A host that refuses a press gets its own state back.
- `onLitChange`: (lit: boolean) => void — Fires from the press that lit or put out the fuse, and with false when it fires.
- `onConfirm`: () => void — Called once, when the spark gets back to the start.
- `onCancel`: () => void — Called when the visitor puts a burning fuse out.
- `time`: number (default 4) — How long the fuse burns, in seconds: the spark's speed round the edge and the countdown.
- `spark`: number (default 0.6) — How fierce the spark is, 0 to 1: its glow, its rays, the smoke and the sizzle.
- `color`: "ember" | "ruby" | "gold" | "cobalt" | string (default "ember") — The fire's colour: a named pigment drawn from the theme's hues at a fixed lightness, or any CSS colour.
- `smoke`: boolean (default true) — Smoke rises from the spark as it burns, and puffs where it is stamped out.
- `resetAfter`: number (default 2200) — How long the fired state shows before a fresh fuse is laid, in ms; 0 keeps it until the host lights it again.
- `icon`: ReactNode — The icon beside the label at rest. Defaults to a bin.
- `remainingText`: (seconds: number) => string — The spoken countdown for the last three seconds. Defaults to "3 seconds left".
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Button height 32, 40 or 48px, with matching radius, type and wick.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A sizzle while it burns (rising as it nears the end) and a pop when it fires or is stamped out; only after the visitor's press.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button; a burning fuse is put out.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which adds a 12px frame round the button for the wick, smoke and spray (pass -m-3 to align the button itself).

Notes:
- Keyboard: a native button. Enter or Space lights the fuse and, while it burns, puts it out; Escape puts it out too (and is not passed on). The button's name is the visible text of its state, and it stays focusable but aria-disabled while the fired state shows.
- Announcements: a polite live region inside the component says "Fuse lit. Delete in 4 seconds.", the last three seconds, then the fired label or "Put out.".
- Timing: the fuse keeps its own clock. It pauses while the page is hidden, so the action never fires unseen, and keeps time while scrolled off screen, where a timer fires it and the drawing loop sleeps.
- Reduced motion: the cord still burns down with a steady glow at the burn point, because its length is the countdown; there is no travelling flicker, smoke or spray, stamping re-lays the cord with a fade, and the digits swap instead of rolling.
- Performance: one SVG overlay written from a single animation-frame loop that runs only while burning, re-laying, smoking or spraying, only on screen; nothing is allocated per frame (puffs and streaks are recycled). Geometry is rebuilt only when the button resizes.
- Theming: the cord and smoke use ink tokens; the fire is a pigment at a fixed lightness so it reads the same on light and dark pages.

### Ember Tip (KQ-1510) — `ember-tip`
Tooltips that warm up as you explore.

A tooltip group that warms up as you explore it: the first hover waits `delay` and the tip fades in slowly, rising into place on springs.drift, but while a tip is up the group warms, and moving to a neighbouring trigger slides the one shared bubble there on springs.glide — its size morphing to the new words as the old ones cross-fade out, its caret sliding to point at the new trigger, a slight stretch in the direction it travels. Leave and it cools over `warm`, so a quick return is shown almost at once; the warmth is visible as the bubble's border and an ember glow along the group's edge. Keyboard focus shows tips by the same rules, Escape dismisses them, and every trigger keeps its tip as an accessible description.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ember-tip`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The triggers, each wrapped in an EmberTipTrigger ({ content, children, id?, disabled? }), and any layout around them.
- `delay`: number (default 600) — How long a cold group waits before its first tip, in ms; a warm group waits delay × (1 − heat)².
- `warm`: number (default 1500) — How long the group stays warm after you leave, in ms (the heat drains linearly); 0 makes every visit cold.
- `placement`: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" (default "top") — Which side of its trigger the tip sits on; top and bottom tips are kept inside the group's width.
- `offset`: number (default 8) — The gap between trigger and tip, in px.
- `rise`: number (default 6) — How far a cold tip rises into place, in px; a warm one rises less.
- `closeDelay`: number (default 100) — Grace before a tip hides once the pointer leaves, in ms, so crossing the gap between triggers slides instead of hiding.
- `glow`: boolean (default true) — An ember glow rides the group's edge under the tip while the group is warm, and cools with it.
- `ember`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.76 0.16 calc(h - 22))") — The warmth's colour, any CSS colour; the default is a warm pigment from the theme's own hue.
- `arrow`: boolean (default true) — Draw a caret that points at the trigger and slides along the tip's edge.
- `maxWidth`: number (default 220) — The widest a tip grows before its text wraps, in px.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — The tip's type size and padding.
- `onOpenChange`: (triggerId: string | null) => void — A tip opened, with its trigger's id, or closed (null).
- `onWarmChange`: (warm: boolean) => void — The group warmed up (true) or has fully cooled (false).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows no tips at all.
- `className`: string — Classes for the group's root; any other div attributes (role, aria-label, onKeyDown…) pass through.

Notes:
- Structure: EmberTip renders one shared bubble for all its triggers. Wrap each control in <EmberTipTrigger content={…}>; the control must accept aria-describedby, which points at a hidden copy of the tip so its description is there whether or not the tip is showing.
- Keyboard and hover: tips show on mouse or pen hover and on keyboard focus (focus-visible), stay while the tip itself is hovered, and Escape dismisses the tip until the pointer or focus moves on (Escape is prevented so an enclosing dialog stays open). A mouse press on a trigger hides its tip. Touch never shows tips.
- Reduced motion: no rise, slide or stretch — the tip fades in place and jumps between triggers while the words cross-fade. The delays and the warmth still apply, and the glow and border still show the heat.
- Performance: no loops and two timers at most; a handful of motion values (anchor, size, lift, opacity, heat) and a trigger's box read only when its tip is requested.
- Theming: the bubble uses the popover tokens; the warmth is a pigment at a fixed lightness so it reads the same on light and dark pages.

### Slide Seal (KQ-1511) — `slide-seal`
Slide to seal the deal.

A slide-to-confirm strip whose handle is a seal stamp: it follows the finger 1:1 along the track and rubber-bands past the ends while the track's words dissolve letter by letter under it, and near the end a wax seal forms on the mark, growing from a dot to just wider than the handle as it closes on the threshold. Released past the threshold (or flicked so the throw would land past it) the handle slams onto the wax on springs.flick with the release velocity and presses it — squashing on springs.flick, the wax splatting out past its rim on springs.recoil — and its face becomes the seal with the monogram pressed in; released short, it springs home on springs.glide with the release velocity. The handle is a native button: Enter or Space runs the whole slide and presses the seal.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/slide-seal`

Props:
- `label`: string (default "Slide to seal") — The track's words and the handle's accessible name.
- `sealedLabel`: string (default "Sealed") — Shown once sealed, and the handle's name then.
- `sealed / defaultSealed`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether it is sealed, controlled or initial. Setting it back to false breaks the seal and the handle glides home; a host that refuses the seal gets its own state back.
- `onSealedChange`: (sealed: boolean) => void — Fires with true from the release or key that sealed it.
- `onConfirm`: () => void — Called once, when the seal is pressed.
- `onProgressChange`: (progress: number) => void — Fires while the handle is dragged with how far along the track it is, 0 to 1 (two decimals); 0 when it springs back, 1 when sealed.
- `threshold`: number (default 0.85) — Where a release commits, as a share of the travel (0.5 to 0.98); also where the wax finishes forming and the track's mark sits.
- `seal`: "crimson" | "forest" | "cobalt" | "amber" | string (default "crimson") — The wax: a named pigment from the theme's hues at a fixed lightness, or any CSS colour.
- `monogram`: string (default "") — One or two letters pressed into the wax; a check when empty.
- `icon`: ReactNode — The handle's icon before it is pressed. Defaults to a stamp.
- `wobble`: number (default 0.5) — How organic the wax's edge is, from a coin (0) to a splash (1).
- `squash`: number (default 0.5) — How deep the press squashes the handle and how far the wax spreads, 0 to 1.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Track height 48, 56 or 64px with a matching handle; the strip is w-full up to 420px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A thock when the seal is pressed, pitched by size; only after the visitor's drag or key.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the handle.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which keeps 6px round the track for the wax's overhang (pass -m-1.5 to align the track itself).

Notes:
- Keyboard: the handle is a native button named `label` and described by how to use it; Enter or Space runs the slide and presses the seal. Once sealed it stays focusable, aria-disabled and named `sealedLabel`, and a polite live region says it once.
- Pointer: drag the handle (touch-action: pan-y, so the page still scrolls vertically); a tap without a drag nudges it toward the seal as a hint. Pointer capture is only taken after 3px of travel, and a throw is projected, so a flick past the threshold seals.
- Reduced motion: the handle still follows the finger; the wax fades in where it would grow, a short release returns on a short tween, and the press is a cross-fade with no squash or splat.
- Performance: DOM plus one small SVG and no loops. The wax outline, its gloss, the text mask and the squash are motion values derived from the handle's position and two press springs, computed only while those move.
- Theming: the track uses surface and hairline tokens; the wax is a pigment at a fixed lightness with its shade and highlight mixed in oklab, so the seal looks the same on light and dark pages.

### Stretch Tabs (KQ-1512) — `stretch-tabs`
A segmented control with some give.

A segmented control whose pill is rubber: its two edges are separate springs, so choosing another segment sends the leading edge out first to land with a slight overshoot while the trailing edge holds for a beat and then lets go on a softer spring — the pill stretching toward the new segment, thinning as it stretches, and squashing against the track's ends instead of leaving them. The selected label colour is a copy of the labels clipped to the pill's exact shape, so it sweeps across each letter with the rubber edge; at elastic 0 the pill is one piece on springs.snap. The pill can be dragged 1:1 (its trailing edge following on a short spring) and a release projects the throw and snaps to the nearest segment with the release velocity; arrows move and wrap, Home and End jump, in tablist or radiogroup semantics with a roving tabindex.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/stretch-tabs`

Props:
- `items`: StretchTabsItem[] — The segments, in order: { value, label, ariaLabel?, controls?, disabled? }. `controls` is the id of the panel a tab shows.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default — / the first item) — The selected value, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires from the press, key or drag that changed it, with the new value.
- `label`: string — The control's accessible name.
- `segments`: number (default items.length) — How many of the items are shown, from the first; the pill keeps its place in segment units, so a change needs no measuring.
- `elastic`: number (default 0.5) — The rubber, 0 to 1: how long the trailing edge holds, how soft it catches up, how far the pill may stretch (1.5 to 2.6 segments), how much it thins, and how much the leading edge overshoots. 0 is one rigid piece on springs.snap.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Track height 32, 36 or 44px with 12, 13 or 14px labels.
- `semantics`: "tablist" | "radiogroup" (default "tablist") — Tabs that show panels (role tab, aria-selected, aria-controls) or a radio group that picks a value (role radio, aria-checked).
- `activation`: "auto" | "manual" (default "auto") — Arrow keys select as they move, or (tablist only) only move focus until Enter or Space.
- `draggable`: boolean (default true) — The pill can be dragged along the track; a drag that starts on another segment selects the segment it is released over.
- `pill`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — The pill's colour, any CSS colour.
- `pillText`: string (default "var(--background)") — The selected label's colour, on the pill.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick on every change and on every segment a drag crosses, pitched by position; only in answer to the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables every segment.
- `className`: string — Classes for the track; it is inline-grid sized by its widest label, so pass w-full to stretch it.

Notes:
- Keyboard: one tab stop (roving tabindex). ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (and Up/Down) move and wrap, skipping disabled items; Home and End jump to the ends. With activation="manual" (tablist) arrows move focus only and Enter or Space selects.
- Pointer: press a segment to select it; drag the pill (touch-action: pan-y) and it follows 1:1 with its trailing edge on a short spring, rubber-banding into the ends; a release projects the throw. Pointer capture is only taken after 4px.
- Reduced motion: the pill moves in one piece without stretch, thinning or overshoot — it jumps to the new segment with a short fade-in so the change is still seen; dragging still follows the finger.
- Server rendering: positions are segment units drawn with CSS calc() against the track, so the server renders the pill under the selected segment and nothing is measured at rest (one box read when a drag starts).
- Performance: two springs (the edges) and derived styles, only while they move; no loops. The selected label colour is a clipped copy of the labels, so text never re-renders mid-animation.

### Beat Like (KQ-1513) — `beat-like`
A like that keeps a heartbeat.

A like button whose heart beats: a press contracts it on a near-critical spring while the colour floods up from the tip, then relaxes it on an underdamped one that carries it past its size, and at the top of that relaxation a ring of small hearts is thrown outward while the count rolls up on springs.snap. Holding the heart makes it race — it beats on its own, quicker and bigger each time, while a ring around it fills — and letting go at full charge super-likes with a big beat and a double ring; while liked it keeps a quiet resting heartbeat. It is an aria-pressed button: Space and Enter behave like the pointer (a quick press toggles, a held one charges, Escape cancels the hold).

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/beat-like`

Props:
- `pressed / defaultPressed`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether the visitor has liked it, controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onPressedChange`: (pressed: boolean, kind: "like" | "super" | "unlike") => void — Fires from the press, key or hold that changed it, with the new state and how it was reached; a super-like over an existing like fires with pressed true.
- `count`: number (default 0) — Likes from everyone else; the visitor's own like is added while pressed.
- `format`: (count: number) => string (default grouped integer) — How the count is written; each digit rolls in its own column, other characters stand still.
- `label`: string (default "Like") — The button's accessible name; the count describes it.
- `burst`: number (default 8) — Small hearts thrown by a like, 0 to 24; a super-like throws twice as many in two rings.
- `beat`: number (default 72) — The heart rate in beats per minute: how fast a beat contracts and relaxes, the resting pulse, and where a held heart starts to race.
- `color`: "rose" | "amber" | "cobalt" | "mint" | string (default "rose") — The heart's colour: a named pigment that reads the same in both themes, or any CSS colour.
- `resting`: boolean (default true) — Keep a quiet lub-dub while liked, only while the button is on screen and the page is visible.
- `holdToSuper`: boolean (default true) — Holding the heart races it, and letting go at full charge super-likes; off, a hold is just a slow press.
- `superHold`: number (default 1200) — How long a hold takes to reach full charge, in ms.
- `onHoldChange`: (state: "idle" | "charging" | "full") => void — Fires as a hold starts charging, reaches full charge, and ends.
- `showCount`: boolean (default true) — Show the count beside the heart; off, the button is a round heart.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Pill height 32, 40 or 48px, with the heart and text scaled to match.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A pop as the hearts leave (two for a super-like), soft rising pops while charging and a low one on unlike; only in answer to the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root inline box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: it is a <button aria-pressed>. Space and Enter are handled as a press — released quickly they toggle, held they charge and a release at full charge super-likes — and Escape cancels a hold without changing anything. A click with no pointer or key behind it (assistive technology) toggles. A polite status announces Liked, Super liked or Like removed at the moment of change.
- The burst is drawn as the overflow of a heart-sized SVG, like a shadow: it paints about two heart-widths past the heart without adding to layout or scroll width. Leave that much clear space around the button, or lower `burst`.
- Reduced motion: nothing contracts, relaxes or flies — the colour fills and drains on a short tween, the ring of hearts appears still and fades in place, a hold shows only the ring filling, and there is no resting heartbeat.
- Performance: everything is SVG on motion values. The resting heartbeat is one short animation per beat scheduled by a timer that stops while the button is off screen (IntersectionObserver) or the page is hidden; an unliked, idle button runs nothing.
- Theming: the named colours are pigments taken from the theme's danger, warn, accent and success hues at a fixed lightness, so a filled heart looks the same on light and dark pages.

### Tick Spring (KQ-1514) — `tick-spring`
A checkbox with a spring in its step.

A checkbox whose tick is drawn by an elastic pen: a press squashes the box on its base on springs.flick and lets it go on springs.recoil, and checking draws the tick on a spring of your stiffness and bounce that runs past its end, so the long arm overshoots and springs back while the corner dips under the pen as it turns. The box floods with colour from its centre on springs.snap (or stays outlined while an ink tick swings past its corner), an indeterminate dash bends into the tick on the same spring instead of being erased, and an optional strike sweeps through the label on springs.glide, line by line. It is a native checkbox, so Tab reaches the box, Space toggles it and a form submits it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tick-spring`

Props:
- `checked / defaultChecked`: boolean | "indeterminate" (default — / false) — Ticked, clear, or indeterminate (a dash), controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onCheckedChange`: (checked: boolean) => void — Fires from the press or key that changed it; a press on a dash always ticks.
- `label`: ReactNode — The text beside the box, in a <label> that toggles the box.
- `description`: ReactNode — A quieter second line under the label, linked to the box with aria-describedby.
- `stroke`: number (default 2.25) — The pen's width in px.
- `stiffness`: number (default 520) — The pen's spring stiffness: higher draws faster and settles sooner.
- `bounce`: number (default 0.5) — How far the pen overshoots the end of the tick before it settles, 0 (lands dead) to 1.
- `strike`: boolean (default false) — Strike the label through once the tick lands, line by line when it wraps, and dim it.
- `appearance`: "fill" | "ink" (default "fill") — "fill" floods the box behind a light tick; "ink" keeps it outlined and draws the tick in colour, its long arm past the box's corner.
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The fill (or ink) colour; any CSS colour.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Box 16, 20 or 24px, with the label's line height to match so the box sits on the first line.
- `name`: string — Form field name, submitted while ticked.
- `value`: string (default "on") — The value submitted under `name`.
- `required`: boolean — Native required.
- `id`: string (default generated) — The box's id; the label points at it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick when the pen lands and a lower one when it retracts; only for the box the visitor pressed.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the box and dims the row.
- `className`: string — Classes for the row.

Notes:
- It is a real <input type="checkbox"> styled with appearance-none, so the focused element is the box itself and its focus ring is the box's. Tab reaches it, Space toggles it, the label toggles it, and indeterminate is set on the DOM node so it is announced as mixed.
- Indeterminate is controlled through `checked="indeterminate"`. A press on a dash reports `true`; a parent box over a group is the usual use — pass it `"indeterminate"` while only some children are ticked.
- Reduced motion: no squash, overshoot or corner dip — the tick and dash fade in whole, the fill fades, and the strike appears at once. The state always shows.
- Performance: the stroke is one SVG path rebuilt from motion values only while a spring runs (it can run past its end, which a dash offset cannot); nothing runs at rest and there are no observers.
- The ink appearance draws its tick past the box's corner as SVG overflow, which paints without adding to layout; leave a few px clear above and to the right.

### Heat Hold (KQ-1516) — `heat-hold`
Hold until it glows.

A hold-to-confirm button fired like a kiln: holding raises the heat, and one WebGL2 pass paints a front that climbs from the floor with its edge licked into tongues, the colour climbing the ramp from deep red through orange and yellow to white, a haze wavering above it and sparks rising through it, while a masked second copy of the label recolours as the heat passes through it. Let go early and it cools back down, quickest while hottest; reach the top and it fires — a white flare blooms from the middle, a glow spreads around the button and fades, the button kicks on springs.recoil and the kiln cools through the ramp. Space or Enter held heats it, Escape cancels, and a click with no pointer or key behind it fires at once.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/heat-hold`

Props:
- `onConfirm`: () => void — Fires once, the moment the heat reaches the top.
- `onHeatChange`: (state: "idle" | "heating" | "cooling" | "fired") => void — Fires as the button starts heating, starts cooling, fires, and comes back to rest.
- `label`: ReactNode (default "Hold to confirm") — What the button does; truncates in a narrow button.
- `doneLabel`: ReactNode (default "Confirmed") — Shown, with a check, once it has fired.
- `icon`: ReactNode (default a flame) — Before the label; 16px, drawn in currentColor.
- `hold`: number (default 1600) — How long a hold takes to bring it to full heat, in ms. Measured in real time, so a busy device fires on time.
- `cool`: number (default 900) — How long a full charge takes to cool back down when let go early, in ms; it cools fastest while hottest.
- `shimmer`: number (default 0.6) — How much the heat wavers, 0 to 1: the tongues on its front, the haze above it and the sparks in it. 0 is a calm level.
- `colors`: "kiln" | "forge" | "gas" | string[] (default "kiln") — The heat ramp, coldest first: a named ramp (red to white, copper to gold, blue flame to white) or 2 to 4 CSS colours.
- `glow`: number (default 0.7) — How far the glow blooms around the button when it fires, 0 to 1.
- `resetAfter`: number (default 1800) — How long it shows the fired state before it can be held again, in ms; 0 keeps it fired.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Height 40, 48 or 56px.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — The highest device pixel ratio the heat is drawn at (0.5 to 2).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A sizzle while heating, rising with the heat and stopped on release, and a flare on firing; only in answer to the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button and lets any hold go.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which the button fills; set its width here.

Notes:
- Keyboard: it is a real <button>. Space or Enter held heats it (key repeats are ignored), letting go cools it, Escape cancels a hold, and losing focus lets go. A click with no pointer or key behind it — assistive technology — fires it at once, because a hold cannot be asked of everyone. It is described by "Hold for 1.6 seconds", and a polite status announces Fired or Released early, not fired.
- Performance: one WebGL2 fragment pass over the button only, through registry/lib/glsl, with the device pixel ratio capped and the canvas resized by a ResizeObserver. The frame loop runs only while the button is heating, cooling, flaring or glowing; it stops at rest, off screen and in a hidden page, where a hold is let go and the sizzle stops.
- Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS gradient level in the same ramp stands in; the server renders that level too, so the first paint is the designed cold button.
- Reduced motion: the heat is a level with a straight, soft edge — no tongues, haze or sparks — the flare is a flash and the button does not kick. The label still heats and the hold still fires.
- Theming: the ramps are fixed pigments (heat colours do not change with the theme); the cold button uses the card surface and the label's heated copy picks dark or light ink against the ramp at the current heat, so it reads on both themes.

- `pleats`: number (default 12) — How many panels the sheet is folded into, 6 to 24.
- `density`: number (default 0.5) — How closely the points sit, 0 (a sparse lattice) to 1 (a fine one).
- `palette`: "prism" | "tide" | "ember" | "mono" (default "prism") — The spectrum the faces are tinted from, crease to crease.
- `colors`: string[] — Two or three CSS colours that replace the palette: one way, the creases, the other way.
- `rest`: number (default 0.5) — Where the sheet rests, 0 (closed) to 1 (fully open).
- `springBack`: boolean (default true) — Let go, the sheet eases back to rest; off, it stays where it is left.
- `crease`: number (default 0.6) — The folds' edge, 0 (rounded, like cloth) to 1 (knife-sharp creases).
- `tilt`: number (default 20) — How far the top of the fan leans away from the eye, degrees, 0 to 60.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How large and bright the points burn, 0 to 1.
- `sway`: number (default 0.4) — How much the fan breathes and shimmers while it rests, 0 (still) to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The hand opens and closes the sheet and the pointer leans it.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the breathing still; the hand still works.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds each point's shimmer, so two sheets never twinkle together.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Pleated sheet") — The sheet's accessible name.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: number) => void — Fires with the opening (0 to 1) the hand or the keys asked for, and with rest when it is let go.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The sheet is drawn and holds still; drag and keys are ignored.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the sheet is one role="slider" tab stop. Arrow Right/Up open it a tenth, Left/Down close it, Page Up/Down a quarter, Home closes and End opens; holding a key holds the fan and letting go eases it back to rest, the same end state as the drag. With springBack off it behaves as an ordinary slider.
- Give it a box with a height (it fills its parent): the fan is fitted to the box closed and fully open, so it never moves as it folds. The drag uses touch-action: pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page on touch.
- Colours are pigments taken at a fixed lightness per theme from the tokens you pass (any CSS colour works): glowing points added together on a dark page, ink dots laid over each other on a light one.
- Under reduced motion one still fold is drawn at rest: no entrance, breathing or lean. The drag and keys still set the opening directly, and a release returns to rest at once.
- One WebGL2 draw of up to ~8,000 points placed by the vertex shader, so a frame costs no JavaScript beyond a few uniforms. It draws only on screen and in a visible page, at 30 fps when only breathing, and stops when settled and still. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, an SVG still of the fold stands in.

### Limb Dawn (KQ-1519) — `limb-dawn`
A sunrise seen from orbit, behind your headline.

A sunrise seen from orbit behind your headline: the curved edge of the night side fills the lower frame under a hairline of atmosphere, and one progress value — autoplayed on mount or in view, tied to the scroll container, or driven by a prop — walks the dawn through its beats. - Colours come from tokens at a fixed lightness, so both themes read: deep space with stars on a dark page; on a light page the air tints the paper, the band is a crisp line and the sun is drawn by its warm halo.

### Ratio Loop (KQ-1520) — `ratio-loop`
A ribbon of light that reties itself into new figures.

A translucent ribbon tracing a closed harmonic figure in 3D — a Lissajous knot at the ratio a:b with its depth at a + b — turning slowly on its upright axis, drawn as one triangle strip whose width follows perspective and a seamless twist, so light adds and burns brighter wherever the ribbon crosses itself. Changing the ratio reties it without ever breaking: every sample travels from where it is to the new figure on springs.glide, the change starting at one point and running both ways round the loop while it loosens and pulls in, and a drag orbits it 1:1 with a throw that coasts on before the tilt drifts home on the drift constants. The ratio chips are a radio group whose arrow keys, Home and End step through the presets while the indicator snaps between them.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ratio-loop`

Props:
- `ratio / defaultRatio`: string (default "3:2") — The frequency ratio the ribbon traces, "a:b": controlled, or where it starts when uncontrolled.
- `onRatioChange`: (ratio: string) => void — Fires from the chip or key that asked for a new ratio, with that ratio.
- `ratios`: string[] (default ["2:1", "3:2", "4:3", "5:3", "5:4"]) — The preset ratios the chips and keys step through.
- `width`: number (default 10) — The ribbon's width, px, 2 to 24.
- `spin`: number (default 3) — How fast the figure turns on its axis, turns a minute, 0 (still) to 12.
- `twist`: number (default 0.5) — How often the ribbon twists edge-on along its length, 0 (flat) to 1.
- `tilt`: number (default 18) — The tilt of the turning axis toward the eye, degrees, -60 to 60.
- `momentum`: number (default 0.6) — How long a thrown orbit coasts, 0 (it stops at once) to 1 (it glides on).
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How bright the ribbon burns, 0 to 1.
- `colors`: [string, string] (default ["var(--accent-bright)", "var(--signal)"]) — The ribbon's two colours, round the loop and back.
- `showChips`: boolean (default true) — Show the ratio chips under the figure; without them the figure itself takes the keys.
- `label`: string (default "Harmonic figure") — The figure's accessible name.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Dragging orbits the figure.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the turning still; drags and ratio changes still work.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onOrbitChange`: (orbiting: boolean) => void — Fires when a drag starts orbiting the figure (true) and when its throw has run out (false).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The chips and the drag are ignored; the figure still turns.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes the whole piece: the figure fills what the chips leave.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the chips are a role="radiogroup" with roving tabindex — the checked chip is the tab stop, Arrow keys step through the presets (wrapping), Home and End jump, and focus follows the checked chip. With showChips off the figure itself is a role="slider" over the presets with the same keys. A polite live region says "Ratio 4 to 3" when it changes.
- Give the piece a height (className): the figure takes whatever the chips leave and fits itself inside. Without one it falls back to a 10rem figure. The orbit drag uses touch-action: none, so it owns the gesture on touch.
- On a dark page the ribbon is light that adds, so crossings burn brighter; on a light page it is pigment laid over pigment and crossings deepen. Colours are any CSS colours, taken at a fixed lightness per theme.
- Under reduced motion the figure does not turn and a throw does not coast; a new ratio dips the opacity for 150 ms and draws the new figure still. Dragging still turns it 1:1.
- Each frame builds 720 samples into one reused buffer and draws one strip; the loop runs only while it turns, coasts or reties, on screen and in a visible page — spin={0} or paused settles it. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, an SVG still of the same figure stands in.

### Fluted Tumbler (KQ-1524) — `fluted-tumbler`
Layered colour stirred behind fluted glass.

A heavy fluted tumbler of two to four coloured layers, drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: every flute is a small lens that resamples the liquid about its own centre, so the layers' boundaries break into repeating slivers with a faint colour fringe at the ribs. Drag in circles and the hand's angular velocity spins the liquid; overturning currents fold the layers into streaks and buoyancy separates them again by weight, while a sideways move tips the glass on springs.glide (heavy, no bounce) and sets the surface sloshing on a pendulum damped by the viscosity. The glass is a button: Left and Right stir, Shift with them tips it, Enter or Space gives a brisk stir.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/fluted-tumbler`

Props:
- `layers`: number (default 3) — How many layers of liquid are stacked, 2 to 4; they take the first colours of `colors`.
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default cherry, amber, cream, sage pigments) — The layers' colours, bottom to top, as CSS colours; pigment, so they read the same in either theme.
- `amounts`: readonly number[] (default [1, 1.1, 0.8, 0.6]) — Each layer's share of the liquid, bottom to top; only the ratios matter.
- `fill`: number (default 0.78) — How full the glass is, 0.3 to 0.95 of the space above its heavy base.
- `fluteCount`: number (default 20) — Flutes round the whole glass, 8 to 40; about half face you.
- `fluteDepth`: number (default 0.6) — How hard each flute bends what is behind it, 0 (flat glass) to 1 (each flute shows a small inverted sliver).
- `fringe`: number (default 0.5) — The colour fringe where the image jumps at a rib, 0 to 1.
- `viscosity`: number (default 0.4) — How thick the liquid is, 0 to 1: runny liquid swirls long and sloshes, syrup turns slowly and comes to rest quickly.
- `settle`: number (default 5) — Roughly how long the layers take to separate again by weight, in seconds.
- `tilt`: number (default 5) — The furthest a sideways move tips the glass, in degrees.
- `glassColor`: string (default "var(--ink-3)") — The glass's own tint, any CSS colour, resolved on the element so it follows the theme.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Drag, tap and keys stir the glass.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the liquid exactly where it is.
- `label`: string (default "A fluted tumbler of layered colour") — Names the glass for assistive technology.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pour while the liquid spins. Off unless asked for.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds where the overturning currents run, so two glasses never stir alike.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onStir`: () => void — Fires when the visitor starts stirring a settled glass: a drag, a tap or a key.
- `onSettle`: () => void — Fires once the stirred layers have separated again and the glass is still.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the glass but takes no stirring.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box; give it a height.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the glass is one button. Left and Right stir anticlockwise and clockwise (held keys keep stirring), Shift+Left/Right tips the glass, Enter or Space gives a brisk stir; a status line says when it is stirred and when it has settled.
- Reduced motion: the glass rests still. A stir swaps at once to a still of the stirred liquid, and the layers separate again in three still steps over `settle` seconds.
- Performance: one fragment pass and a 64 by 40 field texture updated only while the liquid moves; the frame loop stops once the glass is settled, off screen or in a hidden tab. DPR is capped at `dpr`; a lost context or a browser without WebGL2 shows the designed CSS still.
- The canvas is transparent: the glass, its shadow and the coloured light it throws sit on whatever surface holds it, in either theme. Give the box a height; the glass is sized from it.
- Sound is off by default; with `sound` the pour loop follows the spin and stops as the liquid slows, on release, when hidden and on unmount.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/fibre-lamp`

Props:
- `strandCount`: number (default 96) — How many fibres rise from the base, 24 to 200.
- `sway`: number (default 0.4) — How much the bundle breathes on its own and how far a breeze bends it, 0 to 1.
- `hueSpeed`: number (default 0.1) — How fast the colour wheel turns by itself, in colours a second; 0 holds a colour.
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default rose, amber, lime, teal, cobalt, violet) — The colour wheel, as CSS colours in order round it; pigment, so they read the same in either theme.
- `names`: readonly string[] (default ["Rose", "Amber", "Lime", "Teal", "Cobalt", "Violet"]) — A name for each colour of the wheel, for the lamp's accessible name and announcements.
- `travel`: number (default 1100) — How long a new colour takes to climb to the longest tips, in ms.
- `spread`: number (default 140) — The fan's angle, in degrees.
- `reach`: number (default 0.92) — The fibres' length, 0.4 to 1 of the room above the base.
- `glow`: number (default 0.7) — How bright the tips are and how far their halo spreads, 0 to 1.
- `breeze`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the pointer's breeze pushes the bundle, 0 to 1.
- `defaultIndex`: number (default 0) — The wheel's colour when the lamp first lights, as an index into `colors`.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer, keys and presses reach the lamp.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the bundle and the wheel still.
- `label`: string (default "Fibre lamp") — Names the lamp for assistive technology; the colour is added to it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Hum while a new colour climbs the fibres. Off unless asked for.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seeds how the fibres fan and sway, so two lamps never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onAdvance`: (index: number) => void — Fires when a press or a key advances the wheel, with the colour's index.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the lamp but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box; give it a height.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the lamp is one button named with its current colour. Space or Enter advances the wheel and announces the new colour; Left and Right send a gust from either side, the keyboard's breeze.
- Reduced motion: the fibres are still and the wheel holds its colour; an advance crossfades the whole bundle to the new colour over 240 ms instead of climbing.
- Performance: colours are precomputed into a lookup and cached gradient sprites, so a frame allocates nothing; the loop runs only while visible and while something moves, and stops when paused and settled. DPR is capped at `dpr`.
- Theming: on a dark page the tips add light; on a light page they are deepened so they still read as coloured beads. The unlit fibres take the page's ink.
- Sound is off by default; with `sound` each advance hums on a pentatonic step while the colour climbs, and the hum always stops after it reaches the tips.

### Moire Band (KQ-1526) — `moire-band`
Two ribbons of wire that shimmer where they cross.

Two ribbons of fine parallel wires drift and turn over across the box, drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass with optional content above, and wherever they overlap broad interference fringes bloom and slide far faster than the wires move. The fringes are computed, not aliased: each grating is a short Fourier series of its wire and their product is expanded into sum and difference terms, each filtered by its own frequency, so the moire survives at any scale. The pointer sets the twist on a curve that is fine near the middle (calm wide bands) and coarse at the ends (racing fringes), followed on springs.glide; the first sighting brings the twist in from wider on springs.drift. It is a slider: arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/moire-band`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content above the ribbons: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.
- `wireCount`: number (default 40) — Wires in each ribbon, 8 to 120.
- `spacing`: number (default 3.5) — Distance between neighbouring wires, in px; ribbons wider than 80% of the box tighten to fit.
- `twist`: number (default 6) — The twist between the two ribbons, in degrees, where the band starts; changing it moves the band there.
- `value`: number — The twist when you control it, in degrees; pair with `onValueChange`.
- `onValueChange`: (degrees: number) => void — Fires from the pointer or the keys that turned the twist, with the new twist in degrees.
- `maxTwist`: number (default 24) — The furthest the pointer or keys can turn the twist either way, in degrees.
- `drift`: number (default 0.35) — How restless the ribbons are, 0 (still) to 1.
- `roll`: number (default 0.5) — How far each ribbon turns over as it runs, 0 (flat) to 1 (edge-on at its narrowest).
- `wireWidth`: number (default 0.4) — A wire's width as a share of the spacing, 0.15 to 0.7.
- `tint`: string | readonly [string, string] (default ["var(--foreground)", "var(--accent-bright)"]) — The wires' colour, or one colour for each ribbon, as CSS colours.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keys turn the twist.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The first time the band comes into view, the twist arrives from wider so the fringes spread into calm bands.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the ribbons still; the twist still turns.
- `label`: string (default "Ribbon twist") — Names the twist control for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 2) — Seeds the ribbons' curves and turns, so two bands never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the band but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the band is a slider behind the content. ArrowRight/Up and ArrowLeft/Down turn the twist half a degree, Page Up and Page Down four, Home and End go to the limits; the reading says the twist and how the fringes look.
- Reduced motion: one crossing is frozen — no drift, no intro. Mouse hover does nothing; a drag and the keys still set the twist, drawn at once.
- Performance: one fragment pass of about ten cosines a pixel; the loop runs while the ribbons drift or the twist eases, only on screen and in a visible tab. DPR is capped at `dpr`; a lost context or no WebGL2 shows striped CSS bands.
- The canvas is transparent and the wires take `tint` (the page's ink and accent by default), so the band sits on any surface in either theme. Content above stays fully interactive; a press on it never moves the twist.

- Theming: the palettes mix tokens with the page, so the sky and the sea follow light and dark; pass `colors` to match a brand. Without WebGL2 a CSS still shows the sky, the horizon and the series as bars.

### Trace Current (KQ-1528) — `trace-current`
Light routed across a board of dots.

A grid of dim dots wired like a circuit board on one Canvas 2D layer, with content above: seeded walkers lay right-angled traces, and currents of light run along them dot to dot, lighting each dot and trace as they pass. Bring the pointer in and a walk along the traces makes every connected dot downhill toward it, so the currents reroute the way water finds the quickest way down and gather at the hand, falling back to their circuits when it leaves; a click sends one pulse out along every trace at once, the front walking each trace from its nearest point to the click. Nothing springs here — currents run at a steady rate and light fades exponentially — and the keyboard has a probe: arrows move it dot to dot, Enter or Space pulses from it, Escape lifts it.

- `hue`: number (default 260) — The light's hue, in degrees, at the theme's accent lightness.
- `currents`: number (default 22) — How many currents run at once, 4 to 80.
- `trail`: number (default 0.5) — How long a lit dot and trace keep glowing after a current passes, 0 to 1.
- `pull`: number (default 0.85) — How many of the currents answer the pointer, 0 (none) to 1 (all).
- `pulseSpeed`: number (default 520) — How fast a pulse's front runs along the traces, in px a second.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer reroutes the currents and a click sends a pulse.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the currents where they are.
- `label`: string (default "Circuit board") — Names the board for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 9) — Seeds the traces' layout, so two boards never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onPulse`: (origin: { x: number; y: number }) => void — Fires when a click or a key sends a pulse, with its origin in px from the board's top-left.
- `onRerouteChange`: (rerouting: boolean) => void — Fires when the currents start (true) or stop (false) rerouting toward the pointer or the probe.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the board but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the board's surface behind the content is one focus stop. Focusing it puts a probe at the centre; arrows move it dot to dot and the currents reroute to it, Enter or Space sends a pulse from it, Escape lifts it (and is handled, so it never closes a surrounding dialog).
- Reduced motion: a still board with a handful of currents caught mid-flight; the pointer or probe lights the routes that lead to it, and a pulse lights every trace at once and fades in still steps.
- Performance: the dim board is one cached image; lit traces and dots are grouped into eight brightness levels and stroked as one path each, from preallocated arrays. The loop stops off screen, in a hidden tab and when paused.

### Pocket Sky (KQ-1529) — `pocket-sky`
A small sky whose clouds drift where you push.

A small sky drawn in two WebGL2 passes with content above it: a few soft cumulus — clusters of puffs eroded by noise that travels with them — hang in a blue sky with the sun behind them, their bellies grey and their thin edges silver, and light shafts are walked toward the sun through every gap. Drag through it and your hand becomes wind: puffs near its path are dragged toward its velocity, those either side curl opposite ways, each stretches and thins with its speed and the clouds part so rays break through; then every puff gathers back into its cloud with springs.drift's damping ratio at the slower period `gather` sets. - `windDrag`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the hand's wind pulls the clouds along, 0 to 1.
- `timeOfDay`: "morning" | "day" | "evening" (default "day") — The light: a pale morning, a blue day or a warm evening.
- `sunX`: number (default 0.64) — Where the sun stands across the sky, 0 (left) to 1 (right).
- `rays`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly light shafts break through the gaps, 0 to 1.
- `drift`: number (default 0.3) — The sky's own breeze and the clouds' slow boil, 0 (still) to 1.
- `gather`: number (default 4) — About how long torn clouds take to gather themselves again, in seconds.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Dragging, taps and keys make wind.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the sky still; the hand's wind still moves it.
- `label`: string (default "Push the clouds") — Names the sky for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 6) — Seeds the clouds' shapes and places, so two skies never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onWindChange`: (blowing: boolean) => void — Fires when wind starts (true), from a drag, a tap or a key, and when the clouds have gathered again (false).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the sky but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-full w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the sky's surface behind the content is one focus stop; each arrow key sends a gust from the opposite side sweeping across the middle of the sky, announced, and the status says when the clouds have gathered again.
- Reduced motion: a still sky with no drift or boil; wind moves the clouds in one still step and they gather back in three still steps over `gather` seconds.
- Performance: the density pass runs at half the CSS resolution with at most 64 puffs, the lighting pass at DPR capped by `dpr`; the loop stops off screen, in a hidden tab, and when paused with the clouds gathered. A lost context or no WebGL2 shows a CSS still of the same sky.
- The sky is fixed art — a sky is blue in either theme — so put a translucent panel behind any text on it, as the demo does. Content above stays fully interactive; a press on it never makes wind.

- Cost: about 2,500–3,500 points at density 1, computed into preallocated arrays and drawn in eight batched fills; frames run only while on screen and in a visible tab, and stop when paused or reduced and settled. DPR is capped at dpr.
- Theming: colours resolve on the component's own element and repaint on a theme switch; a light page gets fuller, darker points and a fainter horizon haze so the sea reads in both themes.

### Dust Devil (KQ-1533) — `dust-devil`
A whirlwind of light that leans after your hand.

A tall funnel of fine light threads spiralling up from a floor in Canvas 2D, tight at the foot and loose at the crown, with dust circling its skirt: each thread winds round a spine of twenty nodes, spinning faster low down, drawn dim behind and bright in front, dense at the skirt and wispy at the crown. ### Star Geode (KQ-1534) — `star-geode`
A shell of stars that opens like a geode.

- `spin`: number (default 8) — The shell's slow turn, degrees per second, 0 to 60.
- `color`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — The stars and the seams.
- `crystal`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The crystal on the inner faces.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the turn and the twinkle; opening, closing and dragging still move.

- `className`: string — Sizes the box; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

### Tidal Pair (KQ-1535) — `tidal-pair`
Two galaxies on a close pass, scrubbed by hand.

Two small spiral galaxies on a slow, close pass, drawn in Canvas 2D points: a restricted three-body encounter in which two cores swing past each other on a bound orbit and every star of their prograde, tilted disks feels both, integrated with a fixed-step kick-drift-kick leapfrog, so the near sides are drawn into a bridge of stars and the far sides fling out into tidal tails that wrap and unwind. Checkpoints filled in the background make every moment exact, so a scrub shows the same sky every time, and the frame follows the pair as they part. It plays on its own at an unhurried pace and loops with a fade; drag sideways to scrub through time 1:1, and let go — a flick carries on and its pace eases back to playback. It is a slider through time: arrows step it, Space plays and pauses, Home and End jump.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tidal-pair`
