- `starCount`: number (default 1600) — How many stars the two disks hold between them, 200 to 3000.
- `colors`: readonly [string, string] (default ["var(--accent-bright)", "var(--warn)"]) — The primary's and the companion's stars.
- `duration`: number (default 26000) — How long the whole encounter takes to play, ms.
- `view`: number (default 30) — How far the orbit's plane is tilted from face-on, in degrees, 0 to 80.
- `closeness`: number (default 1) — How close they pass, as the closest distance over a disk's size, 0.6 (grazing) to 1.6 (wide).
- `playing / defaultPlaying`: boolean (default true) — Whether the encounter plays on by itself. Controlled or initial.
- `onPlayingChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Fires when Space or Enter starts or stops the playback, and when the arrow keys pause it to step.
- `defaultTime`: number (default 0.3) — Where in the encounter it starts, 0 (far apart) to 1 (tails unwound).
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — At the end, hold a moment, fade, and play again.
- `step`: number (default 0.025) — How far an arrow key steps through the encounter, as a share of it.
- `onScrub`: (time: number) => void — Fires as the hand or the keys move through time, with the time from 0 to 1.
- `onPhaseChange`: (phase: "approach" | "closest" | "bridge" | "tails") => void — Fires when the encounter passes into a new phase: approach, closest approach, the bridge forming, the tails unwinding.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the stars, so two encounters never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

- `className`: string — Sizes the box; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

Notes:
- Give the box a size; a wide one suits the pass best. A hairline timeline along the bottom shows where you are, with closest approach marked.
- Keyboard: it is a slider through time whose reading is spoken as millions of years either side of closest approach — arrows step it (and pause playback so the step holds), PageUp/PageDown four steps, Home/End jump, Space or Enter plays and pauses.

- Cost: about 1,600 stars feel two cores per step; checkpoints (positions and velocities every 50 steps) are filled a few milliseconds a frame while it is on screen, and any moment is at most 50 steps from one. Points are drawn in six batched fills; frames run only while on screen, in a visible tab and while playing, coasting or computing.
- Theming: the two colours resolve on the component's own element and repaint on a theme switch; on a dark page the stars and cores are drawn additively, on a light page as ink.

### Beach Scrawl (KQ-1536) — `beach-scrawl`
Write in the sand and let the tide take it.

A shoreline seen from above and drawn in characters — swell glyphs for the sea, sparse dots for dry sand, denser marks for wet — where an unseen hand writes a message in single-stroke capitals, hopping pen-up between strokes on the springs.flick constants, and waves run up on a decelerating ballistic curve to a reach that varies along the shore, spread a foam lace at the top of their run and drain away. Every water front that crosses a groove scours it and spreads it into its neighbours, so each wave leaves the writing softer until the tide has taken it and the hand writes again. Drag to press your own grooves into the sand; focus the beach and type, and the hand writes your letters at a caret (Backspace rakes the last one smooth, Enter smooths the line).

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/beach-scrawl`

Props:
- `message`: string (default "Low tide") — What the unseen hand writes, in single-stroke capitals (A–Z, 0–9, . - ' & +). Empty for none.
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — Write the message again once the tide has taken it.
- `waveRate`: number (default 7) — How often the tide comes, in waves a minute (1 to 30).
- `charSet`: "shore" | "dots" | "hatch" (default "shore") — The glyph vocabulary for sand, water and foam.
- `wetness`: number (default 0.5) — How far the swash runs up the beach and how long the sand stays dark, 0 to 1.
- `erosion`: number (default 0.5) — How much each wave takes from the writing, 0 (nothing) to 1 (about two waves).
- `writeSpeed`: number (default 2.5) — How fast the hand writes, in letters a second.
- `cell`: number | "auto" (default "auto") — Glyph size in px (6 to 18), or "auto": 10 on a wide beach down to 7 on a phone, so a long word still has enough cells to read.
- `brush`: number (default 7) — Width of a pressed stroke in px; the hand's stick narrows for small letters.
- `sandColor`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 45%, var(--ink-3))") — Sand ink, any CSS colour. Wet sand mixes it toward the sea; grooves toward the foreground.
- `seaColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Sea ink, any CSS colour.
- `foamColor`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent-bright) 30%, var(--foreground))") — Foam ink, any CSS colour.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Let the visitor write: drag to draw, type to write.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" (default "inView") — When the hand starts writing: at mount, or the first time the beach is on screen.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the tide and the hand where they are.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the sand, the waves and their reach.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onWritten`: (text: string) => void — Fires when the hand finishes writing the message, with the text it wrote.
- `onWashed`: () => void — Fires when the tide has taken every mark from the sand.
- `onWave`: (count: number) => void — Fires as each wave starts up the beach, with the count so far.
- `label`: string (default "Beach") — The beach's accessible name; what the sand reads is added to it.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the beach is one tab stop. Letters, digits and . - ' & + are written into the sand by the hand at a caret (shown while focused); Space advances, Backspace rakes the last letter smooth, Enter smooths the line. Escape is left to the page.
- Pointer and touch: a drag presses a groove 1:1 under the finger (segments between events are stamped, so fast strokes never dot) and a tap pokes a hole; the box is touch-action: none while interactive, so set interactive={false} where the page must scroll through it.
- The accessible name says what the sand reads ("Beach. The sand reads LOW TIDE."), and a polite live region announces "Written" and "Washed away" only — never per stroke or per wave.
- Under reduced motion the water is still, a single lace sits at the shore, writing appears at once, and the tide takes it one step per wave period by a short crossfade; nothing runs between steps.
- Canvas 2D from a glyph atlas with the device pixel ratio capped at 2; the loop runs only on screen in a visible page and stops when paused. Colours are text tokens resolved on the element and re-read when the theme changes.
- The tide waits for the hand to finish the message before the next wave, so the story is always written before it is taken; marks the waves cannot reach dry out and blow smooth after six waves.

A survey launch over a chart-recorder echogram drawn in glyph density: the launch rides the top edge after the pointer on springs.glide, pitching with its speed and bobbing on the swell, while the seabed scrolls beneath it, so the record painted under the keel is carried away behind it. At the ping rate a pulse arc descends and writes each depth's return into the column under the beam as it passes — surface clutter, water speckle, shoals as clouds of bright marks, the bed a bold band with a sub-bottom tail and a faint second echo — then the return climbs back. A click, Space or Enter pings at once with a brighter pulse and a highlighted column; it is a slider, so Left and Right steer the launch 2% a press, Page keys 10%, Home and End to the ends.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/echo-sounder`

Props:
- `depths`: readonly number[] (default defaultEchoSounderDepths) — Depths along the transect in metres; the line loops. The default is the Coldbrook basin: a shelf, a slope, a ridge, the deep floor and a channel.
- `shoals`: readonly { at: number; depth: number; size?: number; density?: number }[] (default defaultEchoSounderShoals) — Shoals along the transect: where (0 to 1), how deep (m), how tall (m, about four times as long) and how thick.
- `pingRate`: number (default 2) — Pings a second, 0.25 to 6.
- `gain`: number (default 0.6) — Return strength, 0 to 1: bolder bands, a longer sub-bottom tail, more clutter.
- `depthScale`: number (default 60) — Metres from the surface to the bottom edge, 10 to 400.
- `speed`: number (default 22) — How fast the launch is under way, px a second; 0 holds it over one spot.
- `units`: "m" | "ft" (default "m") — Units for the readout and the scale (depths are given in metres).
- `scale`: boolean (default true) — Show the depth scale on the right edge.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0.5) — The launch's place across the box, 0 to 1, controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires as the pointer or the keys steer the launch, with its new place.
- `colors`: { water?: string; bed?: string; shoal?: string; boat?: string } — The inks; text tokens by default (accent, foreground, signal, foreground), so both themes keep contrast.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer steers, a click pings, the keys steer and ping.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the launch and the record where they are.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A blup at each ping you ask for, pitched by depth, and a quieter one when its echo returns.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the clutter, the speckle and the fish.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onPing`: (depth: number, manual: boolean) => void — Fires with the depth under the keel (metres) as each ping's echo comes back, and whether the visitor asked for it.
- `label`: string (default "Echo sounder") — The sounder's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No steering and no pings from the visitor; the survey runs on.
- `className`: string (default "h-52 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- It is a slider (one tab stop) for the launch's place: Left/Right 2%, Page Up/Down 10%, Home/End to the ends, Space or Enter pings. aria-valuetext carries the depth under the keel, and a polite live region announces the depth after the visitor's own pings only.
- Sound answers the visitor only: automatic pings are silent; a ping you ask for plays a blup pitched by depth and a quieter one when the echo returns. Nothing plays unless sound is on.
- Touch keeps touch-action: pan-y: a sideways drag steers, a vertical one scrolls the page, a tap pings.
- Under reduced motion the record is a finished still survey across the width, the launch moves straight to where it is steered, and a ping glows the column under it while the readout updates; no loop runs between pings.
- The record is a ring buffer of typed-array columns drawn from a glyph atlas; steering writes the slider's value straight to the node, not through React state. The loop runs only on screen in a visible page and stops when paused; the device pixel ratio is capped at 2.

### Taffy Pull (KQ-1541) — `taffy-pull`
Pull a letter like taffy and let it snap home.

A display headline whose every letter can be grabbed and pulled like taffy: the part you hold follows the finger 1:1 while the letter's far side stays in its slot, so it stretches along the pull and thins into a neck (redrawn as a textured canvas mesh), rubber-banding past its reach while its neighbours are dragged a little after it on springs.snap. Let go and it snaps home on a spring of the given stiffness that takes the release velocity, while a wobble runs down the word letter by letter on the cascade; fling it hard, or pull far past the reach, and it tears free, arcs out under gravity, and is reeled back into its slot on springs.glide, landing with a recoil. Keyboard: Left and Right choose a letter, Up and Down tug it (Shift with Left or Right tugs sideways), holding the key pulls further and letting go lets it snap.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/taffy-pull`

Props:
- `text`: string (default "Pull me") — The headline. Every letter (grapheme) can be pulled; words never break mid-word.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "div" | "span" (default "h2") — The element the headline renders as.
- `stretch`: number (default 0.5) — How far a letter reaches before it resists (and, at 1.6× that, tears): 0 is 0.4 of a letter's height, 1 is 1.6.
- `stiffness`: number (default 420) — How hard a letter snaps home, as a spring stiffness (120 to 900).
- `thinning`: number (default 0.6) — How thin the neck gets as it stretches, 0 to 1.
- `wobble`: number (default 0.5) — How long a letter rings after the snap, 0 (dead) to 1 (ringing): the snap spring's damping ratio runs 0.9 to 0.18.
- `cling`: number (default 0.35) — How much the neighbours are dragged after a pulled letter, and how far the wobble carries down the word, 0 to 1.
- `tear`: boolean (default true) — A hard fling, or a pull far past the reach, tears the letter free; it arcs out and is reeled back.
- `tearSpeed`: number (default 1600) — Release speed that tears a letter free, px a second (with at least 40% of the reach pulled).
- `color`: string — Ink for the letters; inherits the text colour unless set.
- `onPull`: (index: number, amount: number) => void — Fires while a letter is pulled, with its index and how far toward the reach it is, 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01.
- `onSnap`: (index: number) => void — Fires when a pulled letter is let go and snaps home, or lands after a tear.
- `onTear`: (index: number) => void — Fires when a letter tears free.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A twang at the snap pitched by the stretch, a higher one at a tear, a low one at the landing.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Letters cannot be pulled; the headline is plain text.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Sizes the type (set the font size here, the letters inherit it) and places the headline; the box keeps 0.75em above and below for pulls.

Notes:
- The headline element carries the text once for assistive technology; the letter spans are aria-hidden. The pullable part is one tab stop (a group named by the headline, with a hint): Left/Right choose a letter (Home/End jump), Up/Down tug it, Shift with Left/Right tugs sideways, holding the key pulls further (past the limit it tears), releasing it lets go, and Escape lets go of a held letter. A polite live region names the chosen letter and announces tears.
- Letters are touch-action: none (a drag on a letter pulls it) while the rest of the box scrolls normally; a drag captures the pointer only after 3 px, so taps and text selection elsewhere behave.
- Idle cost is zero: no loop runs unless a letter is moving, and it stops once every spring is at rest. Rest letters are plain text with no transform; only a stretched letter is redrawn, as a 10×12 textured mesh rastered once per font and colour at the device ratio (capped at 2).
- Under reduced motion a pull still stretches under the finger (it is the visitor's own movement), but there is no wobble, neighbour drag or flight: a release or a tear crossfades the letter home over 150 ms.
- Pulls and flights stay inside the component's box; give it the room you want for them through its font size, since the padding is in em.

### Bulb Marquee (KQ-1542) — `bulb-marquee`
A headline spelled in theatre bulbs.

A headline spelled in an alphabet of theatre bulbs: every glyph is a set of centre-line strokes with bulbs dropped along them at an even pitch, each in a dark socket on a deep enamel face, with a frame of bulbs round the edge. On reveal a comet chases one lap of the frame, then the letters fill bulb by bulb in pen order, each filament following the step response of springs.recoil — a cold filament's inrush flashes past its rest brightness and settles — while its colour climbs from dull red through orange to the warm white set by warmth; at rest a slow chase keeps the frame alive. - `bulbSize`: number (default 1) — Bulb diameter, 0.6 to 1.4 times the house bulb; the spacing follows, so small bulbs make fine letters and big ones chunky letters.
- `chase`: number (default 4) — The resting frame's chase, steps per second, 0 to 10; 0 holds the frame steady.
- `warmth`: number (default 0.6) — Filament colour temperature, 0 (clear white) to 1 (deep amber).
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How far each bulb's halo spills, 0 to 1.
- `pattern`: "chase" | "alternate" (default "chase") — The frame at rest: a three-step chase, or odd and even bulbs taking turns.
- `frame`: boolean (default true) — Draw the border of bulbs round the sign face.
- `face`: string — The sign face, any CSS colour; a fixed enamel pigment by default so the sign reads the same in both themes.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — What lights the sign.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Light once, or go dark again when it leaves view or the hover ends.
- `play`: boolean (default false) — With trigger "manual": true lights the sign, false switches it off.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the frame's first lap, ms.

- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Hover sparkles a letter, a press relights the sign, and the keys do both.

Notes:

- Reduced motion: no lap, chase, sparkle or overshoot — every bulb fades up together on a short tween and the frame stays lit steady with every third bulb a little brighter.
- Performance: bulbs are deterministic SVG (the server renders the unlit sign); one loop writes pre-built palette strings only while a reveal, relight or sparkle runs, the resting chase is a timer plus CSS fades, and everything stops off screen and in hidden tabs.
- The alphabet covers A–Z, 0–9 and common punctuation; other characters fall back to a question mark. The text is read once from an sr-only copy and the bulbs are aria-hidden.
- Size it with font-size: the cap height is 0.78em and words wrap between themselves; the face and bulbs are fixed pigments, so it reads the same on light and dark pages.

### Reed Type (KQ-1543) — `reed-type`
Letters on stalks that sway as you pass.

Each letter stands on a slim stalk rising out of a waterline, the stalk drawn as one smooth arc and the letter riding its tip, turned about its own foot. Every reed is a damped angular oscillator joined to its neighbours by a coupling spring, with stiffness set between springs.drift and springs.snap, so a reed the pointer brushes bends away, whips back on a damped sway and pulls the next one a beat later; a fast drag released across the line sends a gust down all of it, and reeds that sank on a leave grow back up on springs.glide. A transparent button takes focus: keyboard focus sends a gentle ripple across, Enter or Space a strong one, and Left and Right a gust from either end.

- `stalk`: number (default 0.9) — Stalk length, em: tall reeds sway wider and slower.
- `stiffness`: number (default 0.5) — Spring rate of the stalks, 0 (limp, the drift calibration) to 1 (springy, the snap calibration).
- `damping`: number (default 0.3) — How quickly a sway dies, 0 (whippy, many swings) to 1 (composed, one).
- `coupling`: number (default 0.5) — How strongly a bent reed pulls its neighbours, 0 (alone) to 1 (a single mat).
- `radius`: number (default 1.4) — How far the pointer's reach extends, em.
- `strength`: number (default 0.6) — How hard a passing pointer pushes, 0 to 1.
- `maxBend`: number (default 38) — The largest bend a stalk takes, degrees; bends ease into it.
- `stalkColor`: string — The stalks' colour, any CSS colour; sage ink by default.
- `water`: boolean (default true) — Draw the waterline, the stalks' reflections and the ripples.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — What sends the arrival gust (and raises reeds that sank).
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Arrive once, or sink and rise again each time the line re-enters view or is hovered.
- `play`: boolean (default false) — With trigger "manual": true brings the reeds in, false sinks them.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the arrival, ms.
- `stagger`: number (default 45) — Gap between reeds rising, ms.
- `duration`: number (default 520) — Time scale of the rise, ms (the glide spring's ratio is kept).
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer, touch and the keys sway the reeds.
- `onSwayChange`: (swaying: boolean) => void — The reeds started swaying (true), or every reed has come to rest (false).
- `onComplete`: () => void — The arrival has settled.
- `className`: string — Size and type; stalks and bends are in em.

Notes:
- Keyboard: focusing the line by keyboard sends a gentle ripple across; Enter or Space sends a strong one, and Left and Right a gust from either end — the same travelling push a fast drag leaves behind.
- Touch: press and drag across the line to brush the reeds (touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical scrolling); a fast release sends a gust.
- Reduced motion: nothing sways or rises — the reeds stand straight and a colour wave along the stalks answers the pointer and the keys.
- Performance: one loop integrates every reed at fixed 1/240 s substeps and stops when they are all still (no idle cost); it halts off screen and in hidden tabs. Rest positions are measured on resize and font load.
- The line reads once from an sr-only copy; the reeds are aria-hidden. The root keeps 0.6em of sway room each side and clips to itself, so bends never spill out.

Letters slump like books, then stand straight again.

- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A press, a flick across the felt, Enter or Space throws again.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Clacks for the throws the visitor makes.
- `onThrow`: (index: number) => void — A throw began: the index of the word it will land on.
- `onComplete`: (index: number) => void — Every die is at rest: the index of the word showing.
- `className`: string — Size and layout; the dice shrink to fit a long word.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the felt is a native button — Enter or Space throws again onto the next word, the same as a press or a flick.
- Touch: a horizontal flick across the felt throws as hard as it was flicked (touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical scrolling); a tap throws at the tumble strength.
- Reduced motion: no tumbling — the dice fade into their slots face up, one after another, and the last one does not rock.
- Performance: one loop runs only during a throw, evaluating each die's analytic path and face shading, and stops when the last die is still; nothing runs at rest, off screen or in hidden tabs.
- The dice rest in their slots on the first frame (and on the server), so the word reads before the throw; the current word is the heading's text and the cubes are aria-hidden.

### Anagram Sort (KQ-1548) — `anagram-sort`
A jumble that sorts itself into your headline.

The headline arrives as a seeded anagram of itself — each word's letters jumbled, stray ones in a softer ink — and sorts itself back in beats: a letter hops over its neighbour on an arc whose height rides its horizontal springs.snap progress, so the spring's one overshoot lands it a hair past its slot and back, while the letter it crosses dips under and the letters between glide aside on springs.glide; each landing squashes on the baseline and a letter that reaches home develops to full ink. The method sets the rhythm — every out-of-order pair at once, one letter at a time leaping into place, or one sweep along the line — and a press, Enter or Space tosses the letters into a new jumble and sorts them again.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/anagram-sort`

Props:
- `text`: string — The headline. Letters only ever travel inside their own word.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "div" | "span" (default "h2") — The element rendered.
- `method`: "pairs" | "place" | "sweep" (default "pairs") — How the jumble sorts: every out-of-order neighbour pair on each beat, each slot's letter leaping into place one at a time, or one pass along the line hopping each letter back.
- `swapSpeed`: number (default 1) — Tempo of hops and beats, 0.5 to 2.5.
- `arcHeight`: number (default 0.55) — Peak height of a hop, em, 0 to 1. The same room is kept above the first line.
- `duration`: number (default 340) — Time scale of a hop's spring, ms; its damping ratio is kept.
- `stagger`: number (default 140) — Base gap between beats, ms at speed 1.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the sort starts, ms.
- `settle`: number (default 0.5) — How hard a letter lands — squash and overshoot, 0 to 1.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Which anagram the headline starts as.
- `color`: string (default "currentColor") — Ink of a letter in its place.
- `strayColor`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, currentColor 42%, transparent)") — Ink of a letter out of place.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — What starts the sort.
- `play`: boolean — Manual trigger: true sorts, false tosses the letters back into a jumble.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Sort once; false jumbles again when it leaves view or the hover ends.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A press, Enter or Space tosses the letters and sorts them again.
- `replayKey`: string | number — Any change tosses the letters into a new jumble and sorts them again.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick on every landing of a sort the visitor started, rising as letters reach home. Off unless asked for.
- `onProgress`: (home: number, total: number) => void — Letters in their place, out of the letters that move: on arrival and from every landing.
- `onComplete`: () => void — Every letter is home and settled.
- `className`: string — Size and type; hops and padding are in em.

Notes:
- Keyboard: interactive headlines are in the tab order; Enter or Space tosses the letters into a new jumble and sorts them again. Screen readers get the headline once, from a hidden copy, and the real words sit under the letters for selection and copy.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels. A sort jumps every letter home and develops the ink from stray to settled on a tween; a press shows the new jumble, then the same crossfade.
- The server renders the jumble, so the first paint is a legible anagram; the sort starts when the trigger fires and pauses off screen or in a hidden tab.
- Letters and digits move, punctuation stays put, and letters never leave their word, so line breaks never change while it sorts. Keep `arcHeight` in mind: the same room is reserved above the first line.
- Sound plays only for a sort the visitor started, one tick per landing, and only when `sound` is true.

### Caustic Type (KQ-1549) — `caustic-type`
Words on the floor of a pool, lit by moving water.

A paragraph laid in the floor of a clear pool: the words stay real DOM text while a WebGL2 canvas draws them as dark tiles in a pale plaster floor seen through moving water, and the light is computed, not painted — the floor's brightness is how hard refraction through a surface of nine seeded waves squeezes the light together, so it gathers into bright, wavering nets that slide across the words with a thin rainbow at their edges. Moving the pointer sends rings across the surface that sweep new nets over the paragraph and a press drops a pebble; resting lets the rings fade back to a slow shimmer. The pool is a focusable group: the arrow keys move a fingertip that stirs the water and Enter or Space drops a pebble.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/caustic-type`

Props:
- `text`: string — The paragraph laid in the pool's floor. Real text: it wraps, selects and reads.
- `as`: "p" | "div" | "h2" | "h3" | "blockquote" (default "p") — The element the text lives in.
- `depth`: number (default 0.5) — How deep the pool is, 0 to 1: deeper water focuses the light into finer nets, bends the words further and dims them.
- `caustics`: number (default 0.6) — Strength of the light nets, 0 (still water) to 1 (a lively surface).
- `tint`: "lagoon" | "glacier" | "peat" | "night" (default "lagoon") — The water: its colour, the floor, the letter tiles and the light.
- `waterColor`: string — Overrides the water colour, any CSS colour; the floor follows it.
- `lightColor`: string — Overrides the colour of the caustic light.
- `inkColor`: string — Overrides the colour of the letter tiles.
- `dispersion`: number (default 0.35) — Thin rainbow fringes along the light nets, 0 to 1.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the surface moves, 0.25 to 2.
- `tiles`: boolean (default true) — A faint grid of floor tiles under the words.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and the keyboard disturb the water.
- `pointerStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the pointer stirs, 0 to 1.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the water still.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seed for the wave directions and phases.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Device pixel ratio cap for the canvas.
- `label`: string (default "Pool") — Accessible name of the pool.
- `onStirChange`: (stirred: boolean) => void — The water was disturbed (true) or has calmed again (false).
- `className`: string — Size and type; the pool's padding and the light's scale are in em of the text.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the pool is a focusable group with a hint; the arrow keys move a fingertip (a faint ring on the surface) that stirs the water, Enter or Space drops a pebble. The paragraph itself is real text for screen readers, selection and copy.
- Reduced motion: a still pool — one frame of light nets at a fixed moment, no loop and no ripples.
- Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop, only on screen in a visible tab and not paused, drawing every other frame while the water is calm; the device pixel ratio is capped at `dpr` and the backing store follows a ResizeObserver.
- Robust: a lost WebGL context shows the designed CSS pool until it is restored, and without WebGL2 that pool — the floor through the water with soft pools of light — is what shows. It is also the server's first frame.
- The water is pigment, not theme: it reads the same on light and dark pages. Pass `waterColor`, `lightColor` or `inkColor` (any CSS colour, tokens included) to make it yours; they are re-read when the theme changes.

### Armillary Words (KQ-1550) — `armillary-words`
Lines of text engraved on turning brass rings.

An armillary sphere of thin metal bands drawn on a canvas with its own perspective, each band engraved round its outer face with one line and graduated in degrees on the rest, every segment of every band depth-sorted with the globe and polar rod so the rings cross properly. A drag spins the sphere 1:1 and a throw coasts down by its friction to a slow idle turn; tapping a ring, or picking or tabbing to its plate, swings it to face you — its orientation slerps on the springs.snap constants with one crisp overshoot to level, line centred toward you, a little forward — while the other rings slow on the springs.drift constants and dim. The sphere is a slider that Left and Right throw, and the plates are a toolbar of toggle buttons named by their lines; Escape lets the ring go.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/armillary-words`

Props:
- `lines`: string[] (default defaultArmillaryLines) — One line per ring, engraved round its band; cycled when there are more rings than lines.
- `ringCount`: number (default 4) — How many rings, 2 to 6.
- `tilt`: number (default 26) — Degrees between neighbouring rings' tilts, 0 to 45: a small tilt nests them, a large one opens the sphere.
- `finish`: "brass" | "bronze" | "steel" | "gilt" (default "brass") — The metal.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The ring facing you, or null.
- `onValueChange`: (ring: number | null) => void — From the tap, key or focus that turned a ring to face you or let it go.
- `spin`: number (default 9) — Idle turn, degrees a second; 0 holds the sphere still.
- `friction`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly a throw slows, 0 (coasts) to 1 (stops short).
- `view`: number (default 14) — How far above the sphere you look from, degrees.
- `caps`: boolean (default true) — Engrave the lines in capitals.
- `graduations`: boolean (default true) — Degree ticks on the rest of each band.
- `globe`: boolean (default true) — A small globe and the polar rod at the centre.
- `height`: number (default 196) — Height of the sphere's stage, px.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Device pixel ratio cap for the canvas.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the idle turn.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No dragging, tapping or keys.
- `label`: string (default "Armillary sphere") — Accessible name of the sphere.
- `className`: string — Width; the stage's height is `height`.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the sphere is a slider in the tab order — Left and Right throw it a step, Page Up and Page Down a quarter turn, Home back to the start. The ring plates beneath are a toolbar (one tab stop, arrows move): tabbing to a plate turns its ring to face you, Enter or Space toggles it, Escape lets it go. Each plate is named by its full line, so screen readers hear every line.
- Reduced motion: no idle turn, no coasting and no swing. A drag still turns the sphere 1:1 under the hand and stops on release; a chosen ring faces you at once and the others dim.
- Performance: the canvas loop runs only on screen in a visible tab and only while something moves — the idle turn, a throw, a swing; with `spin={0}` or `paused` it draws once and stops. Every buffer is allocated once; the device pixel ratio is capped at `dpr`.
- The metals are pigments, so the sphere reads the same on light and dark pages. Keep lines to about thirty characters: each is fitted to the front 150° of its band, and a longer line is engraved smaller.
- The server renders the ring outlines as a still, replaced by the canvas once it has drawn its first frame.

### Blade Type (KQ-1551) — `blade-type`
Slice the headline and watch it mend.

A headline cut from stiff card that a drag cuts like a blade: a bright streak follows the pointer and every letter it passes through splits exactly along the line where the blade entered and left it, the upper piece sliding down the cut on springs.glide with the blade's speed, then dropping and tipping a little on springs.recoil while the staying piece flinches on springs.flick. After the heal delay the pieces draw back together on springs.snap, one crisp overshoot as they meet, and the seam flashes and cools to a faint mark that fades away. Enter or Space makes one diagonal cut across the whole headline, a tap nicks the letter under it, and a silent diagonal cut on arrival shows what it does.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/blade-type`

Props:
- `text`: string — The headline.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "div" (default "h2") — The element rendered.
- `gravity`: number (default 0.5) — How far the cut pieces slide down the cut and drop, 0 to 1.
- `healDelay`: number (default 900) — How long the pieces stay apart before they draw back together, ms.
- `thickness`: number (default 2) — Depth of the card's cut edge, px.
- `ink`: string (default "currentColor") — Face colour of the card.
- `edgeColor`: string — Colour of the card's edge; defaults to the ink mixed toward the page.
- `seamColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.8 0.13 h)") — Colour of the blade's streak and the mended seam.
- `scar`: number (default 3200) — How long the faint mark stays after mending, ms; 0 leaves none.
- `angle`: number (default 14) — Slope of the keyboard's and the arrival's diagonal cut, degrees; flattened when needed so it crosses every line.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the arrival cut runs, to show what the headline does; manual never runs it.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Run the arrival cut once, or on every return to view.
- `delay`: number (default 350) — Wait before the arrival cut, ms.
- `replayKey`: string | number — Any change runs the diagonal cut.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Dragging, tapping and keys cut the headline.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing cuts.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish for each stroke the visitor makes, pitched by its speed. Off unless asked for.
- `onCut`: (letters: number) => void — A stroke finished: how many letters it split.
- `onHeal`: () => void — Every open cut has mended.
- `className`: string — Size and type; the slide and drop are in em.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the headline is in the tab order with a hint; Enter or Space makes one diagonal cut across it. Screen readers get the headline once, from a hidden copy.
- Touch: horizontal slashes cut and vertical swipes scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y); a tap nicks the letter under it. While interactive the headline is not selectable, because a drag is the blade.
- Reduced motion: nothing comes apart or moves. A cut draws its seam across the letters it crosses, which cools to the faint mark after the heal delay and fades away.
- No loop: every piece is a finite spring or tween on its own motion values, with clip polygons set once per cut; letter boxes are measured once per stroke.
- The card edge is a stacked text shadow in `edgeColor`; the default mixes the ink toward the page, so the edge reads on light and dark themes. The seam's gold is a pigment taken from the warn token.

### Crest Reader (KQ-1552) — `crest-reader`
A sea of lines, the one on the crest in focus.

A list read off the sea: the rows lie on a gently rolling surface in perspective, the current line riding the crest of a swell — lifted, standing up to face you, full size and sharp — while the lines to come lie ahead on the water, smaller, lying back and softer toward a hazy horizon, and the line just read sinks into the trough below, with a slow swell always passing through. The crest is one continuous value that the wheel and a drag move 1:1; a release projects the throw and settles on a line on springs.glide with its velocity, a tap carries a row to the crest and the arrow keys glide from line to line. - `height`: number (default 420) — The stage's height, px.
- `wheel`: boolean (default true) — The mouse wheel moves the crest; at either end it scrolls the page again.
- `align`: "center" | "start" (default "center") — Row alignment.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the swell still.

### Bunting Line (KQ-1553) — `bunting-line`
Your headline strung across as bunting.

A headline strung across the frame as bunting: each letter printed on a cloth flag sewn along a string that sags between two pegs, the string a real one — forty-eight nodes under the damped wave equation, fixed at the pegs — and every flag riding its slope on its own pair of damped oscillators for sway and swing, driven by the string's jolts and a breeze whose gusts run along the line so the flags flutter in turn. ### Optical Mix (KQ-1554) — `optical-mix`
Letters painted in dots that blend at a distance.

A headline painted in dabs of separate pure pigments laid in an ordered dither on a hex lattice, so no two touching dabs share a colour and from reading distance they fuse into one tone; the real text stays the element's own selectable text and the paint is sampled from its exact layout. Hovering opens a soft lens whose fisheye pushes the dabs apart and swells them, each pigment opening on the glide spring 45 ms after the last like light through a prism and closing on the slower drift spring, while idle dabs breathe and the line is painted on left to right on the snap spring. Keyboard focus sweeps the lens along the line; Left and Right move it word to word, Home and End jump, Enter sweeps again and Escape closes it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/optical-mix`

Props:
- `text`: string — The headline; it stays the element's real, selectable text.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "span" | "div" (default "h2") — The element that carries the text.
- `dotSize`: number (default 2.5) — Diameter of one dab, px on a 60 px line; dabs scale with the type.
- `palette`: "field" | "dusk" | "press" | "tide" (default "field") — The pigments the line is painted in, each set at one lightness so it fuses.
- `colors`: string[] — Any CSS colours, two to six; replaces palette.
- `density`: number (default 0.8) — How tightly the dabs pack, 0 (open weave) to 1 (just overlapping).
- `spread`: number (default 0.6) — How far the lens pulls the dabs apart, 0 (they only swell) to 1.
- `magnify`: number (default 2.2) — How much the dabs swell under the lens, 1 to 4.
- `lensRadius`: number (default 70) — The lens radius, px; held to about 1.3 times the font size.
- `twinkle`: number (default 0.5) — How much the dabs breathe while idle, 0 (still) to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and the keyboard can bring the lens.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" (default "inView") — When the dabs are painted on.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Paint on only the first time the line is seen.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before painting on, ms.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the idle breathing; the lens still works.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Twists the dither so two lines never share a pattern.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas pixel ratio, 1 to 2.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The dabs have all been painted on.
- `onLensChange`: (word: string | null) => void — The word under the lens, or null when it closes.
- `className`: string — Size, weight and alignment; the type is inherited.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the headline is one tab stop with a hint. Focus sweeps the lens along the line word by word; Left and Right move it, Home and End jump, Enter or Space sweeps again and Escape closes it. Each key move is announced politely.
- The real text is the element's own transparent text node, so it sizes the box (no layout shift), selects and copies as words (selected text shows in ink), and is read once by assistive technology; the canvas is aria-hidden.
- Reduced motion: no paint-on and no breathing; the dabs are painted still, the lens fades rather than springs and follows directly, and focus places it on the first word without a sweep.
- Performance: Canvas 2D, one path fill per pigment per frame from typed arrays. The loop runs only on screen in a visible tab while something changes; breathing alone draws at 30 fps and stops with twinkle={0} or paused. The lattice is rebuilt on resize, font load and theme change.
- The server renders the same pigments as a dotted fill clipped to the glyphs, which the paint-on wipes away, so the first frame is already the headline. Pigments sit at one fixed lightness each set, so the mix reads the same on light and dark pages.

Words rise off a warm cup and drift apart.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the cup is a real button in the tab order — Space or Enter blows the phrase away and brings the next, Left and Right blow it toward that side. The new phrase is announced only after a blow, never on the automatic cycle.
- Assistive technology reads the scene's label and every phrase once from a hidden line; the letters, their wisps, the steam canvas and the cup art are aria-hidden.
- Reduced motion: one phrase stands still and legible over a single drawn wisp of steam, with no loop running; a blow cross-fades to the next phrase.
- Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop drives a fixed pool of steam puffs (a cached soft sprite) and writes the letters' transforms straight to their nodes; it runs only on screen in a visible tab and stops while paused.
- Give it a height; the phrase's size comes from the className (em-based). Long phrases wrap on word boundaries.

### Word Hunt (KQ-1556) — `word-hunt`
A letter grid that rings the words that matter.

A word search: a wall of mono capitals with your words hidden in all eight directions by a seeded generator. A marker capsule hunts them one at a time, gliding to each word on the glide spring — centre, angle the short way round and length each on its own — drawing its outline round it and inking the letters in a cascade, then leaving the word tinted as it moves on. Drag across the grid to circle one yourself: the capsule follows the finger 1:1 held to the allowed directions and lands on whole cells on the snap spring, or fades if it caught nothing. The grid is one tab stop: arrow keys move the marker between found words, Home and End jump, Enter or Space circles the next hidden word.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/word-hunt`

Props:

- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The words found so far, controlled or initial.

- `onFind`: (word: string, by: "marker" | "visitor") => void — A word was found by the hunting marker or by the visitor.
- `gridSize`: number (default 14) — Columns in the grid, 6 to 24.
- `rows`: number (default about 0.42 of the columns, at least 5) — Rows override.
- `directions`: "all" | "straight" (default "all") — Hide words in all eight directions, or only reading right and down.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Where the words go and which letters fill the rest.
- `marker`: "cobalt" | "amber" | "rose" | "sage" | string (default "cobalt") — The pen: a named pigment or any CSS colour.
- `pace`: number (default 1) — How quickly the marker hunts, 0.5 to 2.
- `autoplay`: boolean (default true) — The marker hunts on its own while the grid is on screen.
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — Once every word is found, clear the tints and hunt again.
- `showList`: boolean (default true) — Show the word list beside (or under) the grid.
- `label`: string (default "Word search") — The puzzle's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No dragging and no keys; the marker still hunts.
- `className`: string — Give it a height; the grid scales to fit.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop (role application with a hint). Arrow keys move the marker between found words, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter or Space circles the next hidden word — the keyboard's way to find one yourself. Every find and move is announced politely.
- Pointer: press on a letter and drag across a word; the capsule follows 1:1 along the nearest allowed direction. The grid uses touch-action: none so a finger can drag in any direction; the word list and page around it still scroll.
- The hunt pauses while the pointer is over the grid or focus is in it, and only runs on screen in a visible tab; it is timers and springs only, no frame loop.
- Reduced motion: no glide or outline draw — the marker appears round each word with a short fade and the ink swaps in; the dragged capsule still follows the finger and settles without a spring.
- The grid is generated deterministically from words, size and seed, so the server and the browser render the same puzzle; the layout puts the list beside the grid from a 34rem container and under it below that.

### Formation Flight (KQ-1558) — `formation-flight`
Pictures that fly into formation on cue.

A flock of photo cards in CSS 3D holding a named formation — a tipped ring, a two-turn spiral, a globe or a grid — and turning slowly while it waits. Choosing a formation sends every card on its own cubic path through a curve the whole flock shares, departures from the flock's leading edge and arrivals packed tighter, so the flock stretches into a stream and tightens into the new shape; each card's roll comes from its real sideways acceleration on the path, so it banks into the turn and levels out as it lands. - `formations`: FormationName[] (default ["ring", "spiral", "globe", "grid"]) — Which formations the picker offers, in order.
- `cohesion`: number (default 0.6) — How tightly the flock holds together in flight, 0 (a loose stream) to 1 (one body).

- `className`: string — Give it a height; the flock scales with the smaller side.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the formation picker is a radiogroup with roving focus — arrows cycle the formations, Home and End jump. The flock is a listbox with aria-activedescendant: arrows move between cards and bring the active one forward with a focus ring, Enter or Space chooses it.
- Reduced motion: no flights and no idle turn — the cards fade out and back in at their new places, and a hovered or active card grows in place without travelling.
- Performance: CSS 3D on the compositor with transforms written straight to the card nodes; one requestAnimationFrame loop runs while flying, turning or settling a hover, only on screen in a visible tab, and stops when settled with spin={0} or paused.
- At rest the flock holds itself in the air: a loose flock (low cohesion) bobs out of line, every card rocks a little by bank, and in a turning ring or spiral the cards lean into the turn, so both knobs read before any flight.
- Every length is in container units (cqmin), so the server renders the first formation exactly and the flock scales with its box; cards facing away show the back of the print.

### Paternoster Cards (KQ-1560) — `paternoster-cards`
Cards riding an endless lift, one landing at a time.

Cards ride the open cabins of an endless lift: up the left shaft, over the top on the drive wheel's half circle (receding into the machine room so close cabins pass behind each other) and down the right, the loop longer than the frame so it never stops and never jumps. The chain runs by itself and crawls while a cabin is level with the landing; there the cabin's lamp warms and its card swings out on springs.snap while it travels and grows to full size on springs.glide, its detail printing in line by line, then tucks back on an exit tween as the cabin moves on. - `woodTone`: "oak" | "walnut" | "pine" (default "oak") — The crate's wood.
- `wheel`: boolean (default true) — The wheel flips sleeves once the visitor has rested on the crate or tabbed in, and lets the page scroll at either end.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the paper of the sleeves. Off unless asked for.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the frame, px.
- `label`: string (default "Record crate") — The crate's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Stops every gesture and key.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer frame.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the crate is one focusable group — Down/Right flip forward, Up/Left back, Home/End to the ends, Enter or Space pull or put back, Escape puts back; the revealed record and the pull are announced politely, and the plate under the crate prints the title and artist.
- Reduced motion: the stack re-poses at once, the record and plate cross-fade in, and the record does not turn.
- Performance: the flip and pull are motion values; the spin runs on a requestAnimationFrame loop only while a record is out, the crate is on screen and the tab is visible, spinning down and stopping otherwise.
- Sound: sleeves rustle as paper only after the visitor has clicked or pressed a key on the page — a wheel or scroll never starts audio.

### Yearbook Grid (KQ-1565) — `yearbook-grid`
Faces in a grid that open their row and column.

A yearbook page of drawn portraits where the face under the pointer or keyboard focus grows by widening its whole column and deepening its whole row: the grid's tracks are fractions driven by where the focus is — two motion values gliding cell to cell on springs.glide — and how open it is, so the page flexes like a table and every line stays in register instead of one picture bulging like a lens. Portraits are anchored at the foot, so a wider cell shows more shoulder and a taller one more room above the head, and where the open row and column cross the name and role print in left to right with a rule drawn under them. ### Shutter Spill (KQ-1566) — `shutter-spill`
A burst of frames spills across a light table.

A camera on a light table fires a burst of contact prints at `cadence` frames a second: each shot blinks the lens, throws a flash across the table, and sends a print out white, developing as it travels a loose spiral on springs.glide to a seeded resting place on a golden-angle spiral, where its angle lands on springs.snap. A click lifts a print into the middle on springs.glide while the others shuffle aside in a cascade, a double click gathers the set back into the lens, and a print slides 1:1 under the finger and coasts by projection. The prints are one roving tab stop: arrows step through them (carrying a held print along), Enter picks up, Escape puts down, Shift with an arrow slides one, and the camera button fires or gathers.

- `spread`: number (default 0.85) — How far across the table the spiral reaches, 0.3 to 1.
- `flash`: number (default 0.6) — Strength of each shot's flash, 0 (none) to 1.
- `swirl`: number (default 0.3) — How far each print curls round on its way out, in turns, 0 to 1.
- `tilt`: number (default 7) — The largest angle a print comes to rest at, degrees.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The picked-up print, controlled or initial.

- `spilled / defaultSpilled`: boolean (default false) — Whether the prints are out on the table, controlled or initial.

- `trigger`: "inView" | "mount" | "manual" (default "inView") — What fires the first burst: coming into view, mounting, or only the camera.

- Reduced motion: no travel or bounce; a burst fades the prints in at their places one by one at the same cadence, a pick cross-fades the print into the middle, and a gather fades them out while the counter still counts.
- Cost: nothing runs while idle; every motion is an animation started by an event and stopped on interrupt and unmount. One IntersectionObserver serves the inView trigger and is disconnected once it fires.

### Lens Turret (KQ-1568) — `lens-turret`
Spin the turret; each lens holds a picture.

A cine camera's lens turret: a machined plate of lenses, each holding a picture in its glass, with the lens in the gate projected large behind it, every picture weighted by how squarely its lens sits in the gate so a spin flickers through them like a projector. A drag turns it 1:1 through a notched detent field and a flick coasts on friction while the lenses smear, then a detent spring whose stiffness and damping come from detentStrength clicks the next lens into the gate carrying the coast's velocity, and the projection racks into focus on a tween. It is a slider: arrow keys turn it one lens at a time on the same detent spring, Home and End go to the first and last lens, and a click on a lens turns it in.

- `blur`: number (default 0.6) — How much the lenses smear when the turret spins, 0 to 1.
- `detentStrength`: number (default 0.6) — How notchy the drag feels and how firmly a lens clicks into the gate, 0 to 1.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The lens in the gate, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires from the drag, flick, click or key that brought a new lens to the gate.
- `friction`: number (default 0.5) — How soon a flick runs down, 0 (coasts) to 1 (stops short).
- `finish`: "black" | "chrome" | "brass" (default "black") — The turret's metal.
- `focalLengths`: string[] (default ["16", "25", "50", "75", "100", "135"]) — Focal lengths engraved on the barrels, in millimetres.
- `focusRack`: boolean (default true) — Rack the projection into focus after each landing.
- `caption`: boolean (default true) — Show the projected picture's caption.
- `turretSize`: number (default fitted) — The turret's diameter, px.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Detent clicks as lenses pass and land, after a visitor's action.
- `label`: string (default "Lens turret") — The turret's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No turning.
- `className`: string — Sizes the piece; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

Notes:
- Give the parent a height: the projection fills the box and the turret is fitted to its foot by width and height.
- Keyboard: the turret is a slider; Right/Up turn the next lens into the gate, Left/Down the previous, Home and End the first and last; the value text names the lens, its focal length and its picture.
- Reduced motion: the turret jumps lens to lens and the projection cross-fades; a drag still turns it under the finger and lands on the nearest lens without coasting or ghosts.
- Cost: no idle loop; rotation is one motion value read by the lenses, their two ghosts and the projection layers (transform and opacity only); a flick's run-down is a short rAF loop that hands over to a spring.

### Bokeh Orbit (KQ-1569) — `bokeh-orbit`
An orbit of pictures, in focus where you point.

Pictures ride a slow elliptical orbit seen from a little above, through a thin-lens model: each picture's circle of confusion is the aperture times its distance from the focal plane, so the picture at the plane is crisp and the rest melt, their lights blooming into soft-rimmed bokeh discs that grow with the blur. The pointer's height racks the focal plane on springs.glide, read off a distance scale, and a click spins the orbit open on springs.snap with the phase kicked on springs.drift before it draws back in on springs.drift. The scale is a vertical slider: arrows rack the focus, Page keys in larger steps, Home is infinity and End the nearest, Enter or Space spins the orbit open.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/bokeh-orbit`

- `radius`: number (default 0.85) — The orbit's size in the box, 0.4 to 1.
- `spin`: number (default 6) — The idle turn in degrees per second; negative turns the other way.
- `focus / defaultFocus`: number (default 0.5) — The focal plane, 0 (far) to 1 (near), controlled or initial.
- `onFocusChange`: (focus: number) => void — Fires as the pointer, the scale or a key racks the focus.

- `tilt`: number (default 22) — How far the orbit tips toward you, degrees.

- `pictureSize`: number (default fitted) — A picture's width at the front of the orbit, px.
- `scale`: boolean (default true) — Show the focus distance scale at the left edge.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the idle turn.
- `label`: string (default "Orbit of pictures") — The orbit's accessible name.

Notes:

- Keyboard: the distance scale is a vertical slider; Up/Right rack farther, Down/Left nearer, Page Up/Down in larger steps, Home to infinity, End to the nearest; Enter or Space spins the orbit open.

### Gate Rings (KQ-1571) — `gate-rings`

A small gyroscope of nested polished rings round a glowing core, drawn in Canvas 2D with real 3D: each ring tumbles about its own axle and is cut with a single gap at the axle's end, so when the axles line up the gaps sit one behind another and the core's beam passes clean out through them, whatever the tilts. ### Pause Bloom (KQ-1572) — `pause-bloom`
Rest the cursor and colour blooms beneath it.

A sheet of wet watercolour paper behind your content that the cursor paints only when it stops: rest the pointer and a drop of pigment falls at its tip and blooms into the paper as a stack of fractal-edged translucent layers, growing on a critically damped curve (the drift spring's character, stretched to growTime) that is quick at first and slows as the paper drinks it. Move on and the bloom coasts to a stop and dries where it lies — a tide line gathers at its rim and the pigment granulates into the paper's tooth — the next rest takes the next pigment, overlapping blooms mingle, and the paper slowly dries clean. Touch blooms on a long press; with the keyboard, arrows move the brush, Space or Enter held lets a drop bloom and Delete blots the paper.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pause-bloom`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content laid on the paper: a headline, a card, a call to action. It stays fully interactive.
- `palette`: "garden" | "harbour" | "ember" | "ink" (default "garden") — The pigments the drops step through, one per drop.
- `colors`: string[] — Two to eight CSS colours that replace palette.
- `bloomSize`: number (default 72) — How far a bloom spreads if you rest until it is done, px (16 to 200; held under 45% of the box).
- `dryTime`: number (default 12) — How long a dried bloom keeps its colour before the paper is clean, seconds (1 to 60).
- `restDelay`: number (default 260) — How long the pointer must rest before a drop falls, ms.
- `growTime`: number (default 1800) — How long a bloom takes to reach bloomSize while you rest, ms.
- `raggedness`: number (default 0.5) — How ragged a bloom's edge is, 0 (a soft round pool) to 1 (cauliflower).
- `edge`: number (default 0.5) — How dark the tide line gathers at a bloom's edge as it dries, 0 to 1.
- `granulation`: number (default 0.4) — How much the pigment settles into the paper's tooth as it dries, 0 to 1.
- `strength`: number (default 0.7) — How much pigment each drop carries, 0 (a tint) to 1 (a full wash).
- `maxBlooms`: number (default 24) — Blooms kept on the paper; past this the oldest dries clean at once.
- `defaultBlooms`: number (default 3) — Dried blooms already on the paper when it first shows, 0 to 6.
- `longPress`: number (default 380) — How long a finger must hold still on touch before a drop falls, ms.
- `paper`: string (default "var(--card)") — The paper's colour, any CSS colour; light paper mixes pigments like paint, dark paper like light.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Resting the pointer paints.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the paper as it is: nothing grows, dries or falls.
- `clearKey`: string | number — Any change blots the paper clean.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the bloom shapes and the paper's first blooms.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Wet paper") — The paper's accessible name, for the keyboard's way in.
- `onBloom`: (count: number, pigment: number) => void — A drop fell: how many so far, and which pigment of the palette it carried.
- `onClean`: () => void — The last bloom has dried clean.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing paints and the keyboard's way in is off.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the paper.

Notes:
- Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content is the paper's one tab stop. Arrow keys move the brush (Shift for longer steps), Space or Enter held lets a drop fall and bloom until you let go, Delete or Backspace blots the paper clean. A polite status says which pigment is blooming, and "Paper dry." once the visitor's painting has dried away.
- Pointer and touch: only a rest paints, so the page scrolls and clicks as usual; on touch a long press (longPress) blooms and any drift past a few pixels cancels it. Rests over links, buttons and fields inside the children never drop pigment, and the painted layer never takes a click.
- Under reduced motion no drop falls and nothing grows: a rest lays a dried bloom at its full size by a short crossfade, and drying clean is an opacity fade.
- Canvas 2D with the device pixel ratio capped at 2: the loop runs only while a drop falls, a bloom grows or dries, or the paper is drying clean (at twenty frames a second), and stops on its own once the paper is clean, off screen or in a hidden tab. Dried blooms are baked to their own small canvas once.
- Pigments are pigment colours at a fixed lightness from the token hues (light-dark keeps them readable on both themes); light paper multiplies them like paint, dark paper screens them, chosen from the paper's resolved lightness and re-read on theme change.

### Bevel Gauge (KQ-1573) — `bevel-gauge`

Put the pointer on the glass, or press it with a finger, and the tendrils nearest that angle swing over on springs.snap and converge onto one shared path, fusing into a single bright braided arc with a flare where it lands; a press gathers two more, and letting go lets them drift back into their wander on springs.drift. The globe is a round toggle button: Enter or Space touches the glass, the arrow keys move the finger round it and in or out, and Escape lets go.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/plasma-lamp`

Props:
- `tendrils`: number (default 9) — How many filaments wander from the core, 3 to 18.
- `hue`: number (default 300) — The plasma's hue in degrees: 270 is blue violet, 300 violet, 330 magenta.
- `flicker`: number (default 0.5) — How much the plasma crackles and stutters, 0 (smooth and steady) to 1.
- `gather`: number (default 3) — How many tendrils swing over to join the arc at your finger, 1 to 6 (a press adds two).
- `wander`: number (default 0.6) — How far the tendrils roam when left alone, 0 to 1.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast they roam, 0 to 2.
- `branches`: number (default 0.5) — How often a tendril forks near the glass, 0 to 1.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How much the plasma glows around its filaments, 0 to 1.
- `base`: boolean (default true) — Stand the globe on its pedestal.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and touch reach the glass.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the plasma still.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seeds where each tendril wanders.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Plasma lamp") — The lamp's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the lamp's hum while the glass is touched. Off unless asked for.
- `onTouchChange`: (touching: boolean) => void — The glass was touched or let go, by pointer, touch or key.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing reaches the glass and the button is disabled.
- `className`: string (default "size-56") — Sizes the lamp; the globe fits the box.

Notes:
- The globe is a real round button with aria-pressed: Enter or Space touches the glass and lets it go again, Left and Right move the finger 15° round the glass (Shift 45°), Up and Down move it in and out, and Escape lets go. A faint ring shows where a keyboard finger will land.
- A mouse touches the glass just by resting on it and a press gathers two more tendrils; a finger or pen touches by pressing and can drag round the glass, which is touch-action none so it never scrolls the page.
- The hum plays only with sound on, and only from a press, a key, or a hover once the page has had a press; it stops on release, on a hidden tab and on unmount.
- Canvas 2D with the glass and pedestal painted once per size; the plasma draws at about 30 fps alone and every frame while touched, and the loop stops off screen, on a hidden tab and when paused. Device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
- Under reduced motion the lamp holds one still frame with no wander or crackle; a touch redraws it with the arc already formed at the finger, and letting go redraws the still.
- The lamp is an object, so it looks the same on light and dark pages; hue tints everything that glows and the pedestal takes the theme's ink at a fixed lightness.

### Dart Cursor (KQ-1581) — `dart-cursor`
A paper dart that banks into every turn.

Inside its box the cursor is a folded paper dart seen from above, nose on the pointer: a small 3D model with dihedral wings and a keel, flat-shaded from an upper-left light, whose shadow falls further and softer the higher it flies. The nose points where it flies on springs.snap, it banks into each turn by the coordinated-turn angle on springs.snap, dips its nose as it slows on springs.glide and rides higher with speed on springs.drift; circle it fast and it loops the loop, and two hairlines from its wingtips trail behind and fade. A lifted finger or a pointer that leaves throws it on to glide, bank away from the edges and land; keyboard focus on a child flies it there along a banked curve, and Enter or Space on that child salutes with a loop.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/dart-cursor`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The area the dart flies in. Its buttons and links keep every click, focus and key.
- `size`: number (default 26) — The dart's length, px.
- `bank`: number (default 0.7) — How far it rolls into a turn, 0 (flat turns) to 1 (steep, knife-edge rolls).
- `trail`: number (default 1.2) — How long its wingtip trails last, seconds; 0 draws none.
- `color`: "paper" | "kraft" | "cobalt" | "ink" | string (default "paper") — The paper: a named tone from the theme, or any CSS colour.
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — Circle fast and it loops the loop.
- `glide`: boolean (default true) — A lifted finger or a pointer that leaves throws the dart on, to glide and land.
- `drag`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly a glide bleeds its speed, 0 (floaty) to 1 (heavy).
- `lift`: number (default 0.5) — How high speed carries it, 0 to 1: its shadow falls further below a fast dart.
- `restAt`: [number, number] (default [0.86, 0.72]) — Where it sits landed before anyone points, as fractions of the box.
- `restHeading`: number (default -150) — Which way it points while landed, degrees (0 is right, -90 up).
- `targets`: string (default "a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [role='button'], [tabindex]:not([tabindex='-1'])") — Children it flies to when they take keyboard focus, as a CSS selector.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus on a child flies the dart to it; Enter or Space there loops.
- `hideCursor`: boolean (default true) — Hide the system cursor while the dart leads (never over text fields, never after a key).
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and touch fly the dart.
- `onLoop`: () => void — It looped the loop.
- `onLand`: () => void — It touched down after a glide or a flight.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.

Notes:
- The dart, its shadow and its trails are aria-hidden and take no pointer events, so every child keeps its own clicks, keys and focus ring. The system cursor is hidden only inside the box, only for mouse and pen, never over inputs, textareas, selects or contenteditable, and it returns on any key press and on leave.
- Keyboard: when a child takes keyboard focus the dart flies to it along a banked curve and lands beside it pointing at it, a second focus cue beside the ring; Enter or Space on that child loops the loop.
- Touch: the dart follows the finger a little above it so it stays visible, and glides on when the finger lifts. The box keeps touch-action pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page (and simply throws the dart).
- Under reduced motion the dart follows 1:1 and points where it goes, with no bank, nose dip, altitude, loop or glide; the trails still fade, and keyboard focus places it beside the control at once.
- Five SVG polygons rewritten only when the pose changes (rounded to 0.1 px) and one composited transform per frame; the trails are a small canvas with the device pixel ratio capped at 2. The loop runs only while the dart moves, settles, glides, loops or a trail is fading, and stops off screen and on a hidden tab.

### Magpie Cursor (KQ-1582) — `magpie-cursor`
A cursor that collects the labels you pass.

A cursor that collects: point at anything marked data-magpie and its label lifts off the item as a small paper tag, starting at the item's own box and rising toward you, then flies to the head of a string of tags hanging off the cursor in 3D. Each tag follows the one in front on its own spring with the snap character, softer down the string by lag and further back by depth, tilting with its own speed; pointing at a label already held brings it to the front, and past maxTags the oldest lets go and falls away. A click deals the stack out where you stand in a shallow arc that lands on springs.recoil, holds for a beat so you can read it, then gathers up on springs.glide and clears; keyboard focus collects, Enter or Space drops, and Escape gathers the stack away.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/magpie-cursor`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The area the magpie works in. Mark anything collectable with attribute (default data-magpie).
- `depth`: number (default 22) — How far apart the tags hang in depth, px: 0 is a flat pile, 60 a long string into the page.
- `lag`: number (default 0.5) — How loosely the stack trails the cursor, 0 (tight) to 1 (loose and swinging).
- `maxTags`: number (default 5) — The most tags it carries, 1 to 8; past that the oldest lets go and falls away.
- `value / defaultValue`: string[] (default []) — The collected labels, newest first: controlled, or the labels it starts with.
- `onValueChange`: (labels: string[]) => void — Fires from the hover, focus, click or key that changed the stack, with the new labels.
- `attribute`: string (default "data-magpie") — The attribute that marks a collectable item; its value is the label, or the item's text when empty.
- `offset`: [number, number] (default [14, 18]) — Where the stack hangs from the pointer, px.
- `spread`: number (default 11) — How far the ends of a dropped arc tip, degrees.
- `hold`: number (default 1400) — How long a dropped arc rests before it gathers up, ms.
- `dropOnClick`: boolean (default true) — A click drops the stack where you stand.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus on a tagged item collects it; Enter or Space there drops the stack.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer collects.
- `onPick`: (label: string) => void — A label was picked up, or brought back to the front.
- `onDrop`: (labels: string[]) => void — The stack was dropped, with the labels it held, newest first.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.

Notes:
- Mark collectable items with data-magpie="Label" (or an empty data-magpie to use the item's text). The tags are aria-hidden decoration in a pointer-events none layer, so every item keeps its own role, clicks and focus ring, and the system cursor is never hidden.
- Keyboard: focusing a tagged item with the keyboard collects it and the stack hangs off that item; Enter or Space on it drops the stack there; Escape gathers the stack away and is not passed on. Each pick and drop is announced once in a polite live region.
- Touch has no hover: a tap on a tagged item collects it and a tap anywhere else drops the stack at that point.
- Use value and onValueChange to drive a comparison tray or filter from the collected labels; onDrop hands you the labels at the moment they are laid down.
- Under reduced motion the tags appear at their place with a short fade and move 1:1 with the pointer, with no swing, tilt, lift or bounce; the dropped arc appears in place, holds and fades.
- At most eight DOM tags moved by transform alone, written once a frame while anything still moves; the loop stops when the string settles, off screen and on a hidden tab.

### Board Tiles (KQ-1583) — `board-tiles`
Letter tiles laid down behind your cursor.

A board where the cursor's path spells a sentence in wooden letter tiles: as it travels, a tile drops into each grid cell it leaves (or, with grid off, one tile-pitch along the path itself, turned a little with it), falling from just above at a larger scale while its shadow tightens, and landing on a spring whose damping comes from bounce, from a dead set-down through the recoil spring's two bounces, with a wooden clack. Spaces leave gaps and the sentence repeats; after its life each tile flips face down on springs.snap and fades. A resting word holds the board until the first tile flips it away, and it drops back in on a cascade once your tiles are gone; the keyboard walks a caret across the cells laying a tile in each one it leaves, and Delete clears the board.

- `bounce`: number (default 0.5) — How much a tile bounces as it lands, 0 (sets down dead) to 1 (lively).
- `grid`: boolean (default true) — Snap tiles to a grid of cells; off, they are laid along the path itself, turned with it.
- `gap`: number (default 4) — The space between cells, px.
- `life`: number (default 2600) — How long a tile shows its letter before it flips face down, ms.
- `maxTiles`: number (default 48) — The most tiles on the board; past it the oldest flips early.
- `tone`: "maple" | "walnut" | "ash" | "cherry" (default "maple") — The wood.
- `uppercase`: boolean (default true) — Show the letters in capitals.
- `restText`: string (default the sentence's first word) — The word laid out at rest, before anyone moves; an empty string leaves the board empty.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and touch lay tiles.
- `clearKey`: string | number — Any change flips every tile on the board face down and clears it.
- `label`: string (default "Letter board") — The board's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a wooden clack as each tile lands. Off unless asked for.
- `onTile`: (letter: string, count: number) => void — A tile was laid, with its letter and how many so far.
- `onSentence`: (times: number) => void — The whole sentence was spelled, with how many times so far.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing is laid and the keyboard's way in is off.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the board.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the board is one tab stop with a dashed caret cell. Arrow keys walk the caret and lay the next tile in the cell it leaves, Enter or Space lays one where it stands and steps right, Delete or Backspace clears the board; each completed sentence is announced once, never each tile.
- The tiles are aria-hidden; the sentence itself is in the board once as screen-reader text. Letters are split by grapheme, so accented letters and symbols stay whole on one tile.
- Touch: drag across the board to lay tiles; the board is touch-action none so the drag lays tiles rather than scrolling.
- The clack plays only with sound on and only after the page has had a press or a key; moving a mouse over the board alone never starts audio.
- Under reduced motion tiles appear in place with a short fade and leave by fading, with no fall, bounce or flip; the resting word stays still.
- Tiles are DOM elements animated by transform and opacity alone, at most maxTiles at once; nothing runs at rest. Wood tones are fixed lightnesses of the theme's hues so the set looks the same on light and dark boards.

### Serpentine Pop (KQ-1584) — `serpentine-pop`
Paper streamers that uncurl from your cursor.

Paper streamers for any box: a moving pointer throws tight coils of coloured paper off the cursor, each popping out on the springs.recoil constants and flying on its throw while the strip pays out behind it, so the roll visibly unwinds in the air before the free paper flutters down, springing into ringlets from its curl memory and turning over to show its paler back. Physics steps at a fixed 120 Hz with no per-frame allocation, live streamers are capped at 70, and the canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.
