### Flipbook Path (KQ-1585) — `flipbook-path`
Leave frames behind, then sweep back to play them.

A surface that turns the pointer's path into a flipbook: moving over open space lays the next page of a drawn sequence every few pixels — a paper card with a binding edge and its frame number — set down on springs.snap and leaning into the direction it was laid in, so the path becomes a fanned deck. Sweep back over the trail and the page under the pointer lifts on springs.flick with its neighbours rising a little, so the drawing plays in order under the pointer at the speed of the sweep, forward or backward; left alone, the trail clears from its oldest page. The surface is one tab stop: the arrow keys move a pen that lays and plays exactly as the pointer does, and Backspace clears the trail.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/flipbook-path`

Props:
- `frames`: number (default 12) — Pages in one cycle of the drawing (4 to 24); laid pages loop through it.
- `sequence`: "bounce" | "flap" | "bloom" | "orbit" (default "bounce") — The built-in drawing: a ball with squash and stretch, a gull's wingbeat, a flower opening and closing, a moon passing in front of and behind its planet.
- `renderFrame`: (ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, progress: number, size: number) => void — Your own drawing for each page, into a square `size` CSS px wide at the origin; progress runs 0 to 1 across the cycle. Replaces sequence; pages are redrawn when the function's identity changes.
- `spacing`: number (default 30) — Travel between two laid pages, px (12 to 96).
- `frameSize`: number (default 56) — Width of a page, px (24 to 96); pages are 4:5 landscape.
- `fade`: number (default 2.5) — Seconds a trail left alone takes to clear, oldest page first.
- `hold`: number (default 700) — Milliseconds a trail waits, left alone, before it starts to clear.
- `lift`: number (default 1.5) — How far the page under the pointer rises, as a scale (1 to 2).
- `tilt`: number (default 0.5) — How far pages lean into the direction they were laid in, 0 to 1.
- `maxFrames`: number (default 36) — Most pages on the surface; past it the oldest fades.
- `resting`: boolean (default true) — Lay an S-curve of pages at rest (played once by an unseen hand on first view), and lay it again whenever the trail has cleared and the pointer has left.
- `paper`: string (default "var(--card)") — Page colour, any CSS colour.
- `ink`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — Drawing colour.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The drawings' one fill colour, and the lifted page's edge.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the pages where they are; nothing lays, lifts or fades.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds the pages' hand-laid jitter and the resting curve.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The surface ignores the pointer and the keys, leaves the tab order and lets touch scroll.
- `label`: string (default "Flipbook path") — The surface's accessible name.
- `onFrame`: (frame: number, of: number) => void — Fires when the page under the pointer (or the keyboard's pen) changes, with its frame (1-based) and the cycle length.
- `onTrail`: (count: number, resting: boolean) => void — Fires when the number of pages on the surface changes; resting is true when the component laid them itself.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the surface; pages stay inside it.

Notes:
- One tab stop (a group with a hint): the arrow keys move a pen by the spacing (Shift for three), which lays pages over open space and plays them over the trail, as the pointer does; Backspace or Delete clears the trail. A polite live region reads the frame under the keyboard's pen.
- Touch: drag to lay and to play. The surface is touch-action: none while enabled (it is a drawing surface), so give it a fixed height in a scrolling page; disabled gives scrolling back.
- Pages are rendered once into sprites per size, pixel ratio, colours and drawing; each page then costs two drawImage calls. The loop runs only while a page lands, lifts or fades, and stops on its own; off screen or in a hidden tab nothing runs.
- Under reduced motion pages appear with a 120 ms fade instead of a landing spring, the page under the pointer is raised at once without neighbours, and the resting trail is simply there — no unseen hand.
- Colours resolve from the component's own element (paper, ink and accent default to tokens) and re-read when the theme changes; pass renderFrame to draw your own sequence.

### Mica Drift (KQ-1587) — `mica-drift`
Flakes that flash as they catch the light.

Fine mica flakes suspended in a dark liquid, as a background with your content above: each flake is a thin plate that sinks slowly, drifts on a seeded current and rocks as it falls, lined up with the liquid's flow so neighbours face nearly the same way, and every frame its normal is checked against the half vector between the light and the eye — a broad sheen brightens a whole band of flakes and a tight lobe makes single faces flash with a four-point flare. The light rests far off at lightAngle; bring the pointer in and it comes close on the springs.drift constants, so the angle each flake needs changes across the field and a wave of glints follows the hand, and a click stirs a swirl that the liquid's viscosity takes back. - `shimmer`: number (default 0.8) — How bright a flake flashes, 0 to 1.
- `glintColor`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 22%, white)") — The flash's colour, any CSS colour.
- `flakeColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.72 0.045 h)") — The flakes' own dim colour (a pigment, the same in both themes).
- `liquid`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 16%, black)") — The liquid: fixed art, dark in both themes. Also the box's CSS background, so the server-rendered frame is already the liquid.
- `depth`: number (default 0.6) — How much depth the field has, 0 (flat) to 1: far flakes smaller, fainter and slower.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer carries the light, a click stirs, and the keyboard handle is present.
- `stir`: number (default 1) — Strength of a click's swirl, 0 to 2.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold every flake where it is; the loop stops.
- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seeds every flake.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Mica in liquid") — Name of the keyboard handle that turns the light.
- `onLightAngleChange`: (angle: number) => void — Fires when the keyboard turns the light, with its new angle in degrees.
- `className`: string — Sizes and shapes the box; the liquid fills it edge to edge.

Notes:
- The painted layer is aria-hidden. A full-size button sits beneath the content as the keyboard's handle: Left/Up and Right/Down turn the light by 15° (Shift 45°), Enter or Space stirs at the centre, and a polite live region says the new angle. Clicks on links and buttons in the content never stir.
- The loop runs only while the box is on screen and the tab is visible (or not at all when paused): flakes live in typed arrays, bodies are filled in five brightness batches, and only flakes with a visible flash get a pre-drawn sprite. Nothing is allocated per frame; the canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.
- Under reduced motion the flakes hold still and nothing swirls; the light still follows the pointer and the arrow keys, and each move relights the still field once.
- The liquid is dark in both themes by design, so put light text on it (text-primary-foreground reads in both); flake and flash colours resolve on the component's own element and re-read on theme change.

### Bow Ribbon (KQ-1588) — `bow-ribbon`
A message on a ribbon that ties itself in a bow.

A message printed on a satin ribbon that comes in from the left edge and ties itself into a bow: the ribbon slides along its own path like a strip pulled off a spool, twisting as it comes — its width is w·cos θ, the plain back shows where it turns over, and a sheen band runs along the satin as the turn meets the light — while a soft wave rolls along it and dies away. When the message has passed, the head of the ribbon runs on round the bow's track at the knot, so the end loops up into a right loop, a left loop and a tail; the knot wraps on with springs.flick, a second tail drops in, and the bow lands with a small bounce on springs.recoil. Everything is SVG in em units, so it sizes with the type and the server renders the tied still frame.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/bow-ribbon`

Props:
- `text`: string (default "Thank you for coming") — The message printed on the ribbon; graphemes are kept whole.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "div" | "span" (default "h2") — The element the message renders as.
- `ribbonWidth`: number (default 1.6) — The ribbon's width, in em of the type: 1.2 is snug, 2.4 generous.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the satin catches the light as it turns, 0 (matte) to 1.
- `bowSize`: number (default 1) — The bow's size relative to the ribbon, 0.6 to 1.6; the box grows to hold it.
- `color`: string (default "oklch(from var(--danger) 0.56 calc(c * 0.9) h)") — The satin's colour, any CSS colour; the default is a pigment that looks the same in both themes.
- `textColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--danger) 0.97 0.02 h)") — The printed message's colour.
- `twists`: number (default 2) — Full turns the ribbon makes as it comes in, 0 to 3.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the ribbon runs: on mount, when first on screen, on hover or keyboard focus, or only when replayKey changes.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Run once, or again each time it returns to view (inView) or is hovered.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before it starts, ms.
- `duration`: number (default 2400) — How long the ribbon takes to come in and tie, ms (900 to 6000); the bow's landing adds about half a second.
- `replayKey`: string | number — Change it to run the ribbon again.
- `onStart`: () => void — Fires when a run begins.
- `onComplete`: () => void — Fires when the bow has settled (at once under reduced motion).
- `className`: string — Sets the type size (the ribbon, bow and box are sized in em) and places it.

Notes:
- The message is read once, from an sr-only copy inside the heading; the drawn ribbon is aria-hidden. With trigger="hover" the heading is focusable and a keyboard focus replays it too; otherwise there is nothing to operate.
- The box reserves its final height in em from the first render, so nothing below moves while it plays; size the type so the band holds the message (the demo uses a container-relative clamp).
- One requestAnimationFrame loop runs only during a run (about the duration plus half a second); it pauses off screen or in a hidden tab and resumes where it stopped. At rest nothing runs: the still frame is plain HTML and SVG.
- Under reduced motion the tied ribbon is shown still — no slide, no twist, no bounce — and onComplete fires at once.
- Colours are CSS strings applied as styles, so tokens and the theme work directly; the defaults are pigments at a fixed lightness.

### Branch Draft (KQ-1589) — `branch-draft`
A headline weighing its next words out loud.

A headline that writes itself out loud: at each pause the candidate continuations fan down from the caret like cards hinged there, each opening on springs.snap a cascade apart, faint, with a small weight beside it. The weights flicker while it thinks, then converge — the strongest gains real typographic weight and full ink on springs.glide while the others thin, fade and drop away — and the chosen words swing up into the line and set in solid ink at their real place in the flow, so they wrap like text, before the caret moves on. With interactive, the arrow keys or the pointer pick a ghost, which gains the weight, and Tab, Enter or a click accepts it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/branch-draft`

Props:
- `steps`: { text: string; alternates?: string[]; weights?: number[] }[] (default a scripted three-step headline) — The headline: an opening, then each pause's chosen words and the alternates it weighs (weights seeded when left out, with text the strongest).
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "div" | "span" (default "h2") — The element the headline renders as.
- `candidates`: number (default 3) — How many continuations fan out at each pause, the chosen one included (2 to 5).
- `pace`: number (default 1) — Speed of the whole draft, 0.5 (deliberate) to 2 (brisk).
- `ghostOpacity`: number (default 0.45) — How faint a ghost continuation is before it is chosen, 0 to 1.
- `ghostColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The ghosts' colour, any CSS colour.
- `showWeights`: boolean (default true) — Show each ghost's weight beside it, flickering while it weighs.
- `fan`: number (default 3) — Degrees each ghost turns more than the one above it.
- `interactive`: boolean (default false) — Let the visitor choose: arrows or the pointer pick, Tab, Enter or a click accepts; a pick left alone is taken after a moment.
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — Write the headline again after hold; only while it is on screen.
- `hold`: number (default 2600) — How long the finished headline holds before it is written again, ms.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "manual" (default "inView") — When writing starts: on mount, when first on screen, or only when replayKey changes.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before writing starts, ms.
- `replayKey`: string | number — Change it to write the headline again from the start.
- `onStep`: (index: number, chosen: string) => void — Fires as each pause settles, with the step's index and the words chosen.
- `onComplete`: (text: string) => void — Fires when the headline is written, with its full text.
- `className`: string — Sets the type (size, weight) and places the headline; the ghosts and the committed words inherit it.

Notes:
- The headline is read once, from an sr-only copy of the finished words; the animated words, the ghosts and the caret are aria-hidden. With interactive, the box is one tab stop (a group with a hint): Up/Down or Left/Right choose the next words, Tab or Enter accepts them (Tab is taken only while words are on offer), and a polite live region reads the options when the fan opens and each choice.
- The final box is reserved from the first render by an invisible copy of the longest possible headline, plus room below the last line for the fan, so nothing below it moves while it writes.
- Ghost weight is real typographic weight: with a variable font (the default sans is one) it grows smoothly; with static weights it steps.
- Only timers and short motion tweens and springs run while it writes; a finished headline that does not loop is idle, and a looping one waits off screen or in a hidden tab before it writes again.
- Under reduced motion the ghosts appear stacked under the caret with a fade and do not swing; the weighing, the choice and the words still show, by opacity and weight.

### Melt Swap (KQ-1590) — `melt-swap`
One word melts and pours into the next.

A rotating word that swaps by melting: letters the next word does not share sag to the baseline and soften into glossy beads, the beads slide along the baseline and pool where the new letters stand, and the new letters rise out of the pools and firm up with a slight wobble, while letters the two words share keep their substance and glide across on the glide spring. The liquid is one SVG goo filter lit by `gloss`, its springs drawn from glide and recoil and thickened by `viscosity`, in a box reserved to the widest word so the line never shifts. It swaps on a timer, on hover or focus, or when a host sets `value`.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/melt-swap`

Props:
- `words`: readonly string[] (default ["melted", "tempered", "poured", "set"]) — The words it swaps between, in order.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The index of the word shown; a new value pours into that word.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires as a swap begins — from the timer, a hover or a host — with the new index.
- `interval`: number (default 2400) — Rest between automatic swaps in ms, before pace; 0 swaps only on hover or a new value.
- `viscosity`: number (default 0.5) — How thick the liquid is, 0 to 1: runny beads race and wobble, thick ones crawl and firm up composed.
- `gloss`: number (default 0.6) — How wet the molten letters look: matte to a bright highlight with shaded edges.
- `pace`: number (default 1) — Speed of the whole pour, 0.25 to 2; the rest between swaps scales with it.
- `stagger`: number (default 36) — Delay between letters starting to soften, in ms, from the middle of the change outward.
- `delay`: number (default 600) — Wait before the first swap once triggered, in ms.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — What starts the swaps: on mount, in view, one per hover or focus, or only a new value.
- `once`: boolean (default false) — Stop at the last word instead of wrapping round.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the current word; a swap under way finishes.
- `align`: "start" | "center" | "end" (default "center") — Where each word sits in the box reserved for the widest.
- `liquidColor`: string (default "currentColor") — The molten letters' colour; they cool to the text colour as they firm.
- `announce`: boolean (default false) — Announce each settled word politely to screen readers.
- `as`: React.ElementType (default "span") — The element to render.
- `onComplete`: (index: number) => void — Fires when a swap has settled, with the index now shown.
- `className`: string — Classes for the word's box; font size and colour inherit.

Notes:
- The word is real text at rest and its sr-only copy is the only one assistive tech reads; every animated letter is aria-hidden. Set `announce` when the swaps carry meaning a listener should hear.
- Size and colour inherit (blur, beads and lean are in em), so the same component works from a caption to a hero; the box is reserved to the widest word, so the surrounding line never moves.
- Nothing runs between swaps: the goo filter is applied only while a swap pours, the timer waits while the word is off screen or the page hidden, and one rAF loop runs per swap and stops when every letter rests.
- Under reduced motion the words cross-fade in place; the timer, `onValueChange` and `onComplete` still run.
- Letters two words share are matched in order first, so pairs like melted → tempered keep most of their letters and only the difference melts.

### Avatar Jar (KQ-1591) — `avatar-jar`
Faces poured into a jar you can tilt.

A glass jar of avatar pebbles that are real rigid discs: they pour in through the neck one by one, tumble, roll on each other and settle under gravity with a rattle. Drag the jar sideways and it turns 1:1 under the finger, rubber-banded past `tilt`, the turning frame sloshing the heap against the low side; on release the throw is projected and the jar glides to rest with the release velocity. Clicking a pebble lifts it out on the snap spring, upright and enlarged with its name card settling beside it on flick, and the heap closes the gap; clicking again drops it back through the mouth on glide to find a gap. Up and Down move between pebbles, Left and Right tilt, Enter lifts or drops, Escape drops.

- `onAngleChange`: (angle: number) => void — Fires when a drag or a key leaves the jar at a new tilt, with the angle it will rest at.
- `lifted / defaultLifted`: string | null (default null) — The id of the pebble lifted out of the jar.
- `onLiftedChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when a pebble is lifted out (its id) or dropped back (null).
- `tilt`: number (default 28) — How far the jar can tip either way, in degrees.
- `pebbleSize`: number (default 34) — A pebble's diameter in jar units (the jar is 200 wide inside).
- `glass`: "clear" | "sea" | "amber" | "smoke" (default "clear") — The glass's tint.
- `gravity`: number (default 1) — Gravity as a multiple of the house's.
- `bounce`: number (default 0.28) — How much a pebble bounces off glass and other pebbles, 0 to 0.8.
- `pour`: "inView" | "mount" | "none" (default "inView") — When the pebbles pour in; with none they start in a heap.
- `repourKey`: number (default 0) — Change it to pour every pebble in again from the top.
- `label`: string (default "Jar") — Names the jar for assistive technology.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Clack when pebbles the visitor moved hit the glass and each other.

- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freeze the pebbles where they are.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the jar but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-[30rem] w-full") — Sizes the jar's box; give it a height.

Notes:
- The pebbles are one roving tab stop: Up and Down move between them, Home and End jump, Left and Right tilt the jar 5° (Shift 15°), 0 rights it, Enter or Space lifts or drops the focused pebble, and Escape drops a lifted one. Lifts, drops and tilts are announced.
- The simulation runs only while something moves: it sleeps once the heap has been still for 0.4 s, wakes on input, and never runs off screen or in a hidden tab. Positions are written straight to transforms, never through React state.
- Under reduced motion nothing tumbles or pours: a tilt, a lift or a drop re-solves the heap at once and the result is shown still.
- Sound answers only the visitor's own commotion — impacts within 1.5 s of their drag, key, lift or drop — and only after the page has had a click or key press.
- Items without `src` get a drawn portrait seeded from their id; pass `src` for photos. The jar scales to fit its box, leaving room above the mouth for a lifted pebble and its card.

### Field Loupe (KQ-1592) — `field-loupe`
Magnify a photo and find its notes.

A photo inspected with a jeweller's loupe: a circle of it magnified `power` times inside a hairline brass rim follows the pointer on the flick spring, and annotated points are magnetic — come close and the loupe settles onto the note on the glide spring and holds until you pull clearly away, while a leader line draws out from the rim and a note card rises in beside it on flick. The wheel or a trackpad pinch (two fingers on the lens on touch) changes the magnification and hands the scroll back to the page at either end. Every note is a button, so Tab walks the loupe from note to note, + and - change the power and Escape closes the card.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/field-loupe`

Props:
- `notes`: readonly FieldLoupeNote[] (default defaultFieldLoupeNotes) — The annotated points: { id, x, y (fractions of the photo), title, body, tag? }.
- `src`: string — An image to inspect instead of the drawn workbench.
- `alt`: string — What the photo shows, for assistive technology.
- `aspectRatio`: number (default 1.6) — The photo's width divided by its height.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default the first note) — The id of the open note.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when a note opens or closes.
- `power`: number (default 2.5) — Magnification at rest; the wheel, a pinch or + and - change it from there.
- `minPower`: number (default 1.25) — The least the wheel or a pinch can magnify.
- `maxPower`: number (default 5) — The most the wheel or a pinch can magnify.
- `onPowerChange`: (power: number) => void — Fires when the wheel, a pinch or a key changes the magnification.
- `lensSize`: number (default 144) — The lens diameter in px, capped to fit small photos.
- `snap`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly notes pull the loupe, 0 (free) to 1 (a firm magnetic detent).
- `wheelZoom`: boolean (default true) — Let the wheel and a trackpad pinch change magnification over the photo.
- `markers`: boolean (default true) — Draw the hairline rings that mark each note.
- `rimColor`: string (default a brass pigment from --warn) — The rim and leader line, any CSS colour.
- `label`: string (default "Photo with notes") — Names the photo with its notes for assistive technology.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the photo without the loupe's input.
- `className`: string (default "w-full") — Sizes the component; the photo keeps its aspect ratio at this width.

Notes:
- Notes are real buttons in tab order, named "Note 2 of 5: …" and described by their card; focusing one moves the loupe there. + and - change the power, Escape closes the open card, and each change is announced politely.
- The drawn workbench is vector art, so magnifying it finds real detail; with `src` a raster shows its own pixels, so give it resolution to spare.
- No loop runs at rest: the lens position and power are motion values and the magnified copy is a transform derived from them. The lens is its own compositing layer, so moving it never repaints the photo underneath.
- The wheel only zooms between the limits and returns the scroll to the page at either end; on touch, a tap places the loupe and dragging the lens moves it while the photo still scrolls the page.
- On photos under 440 px wide the card sits under the photo, with the leader line dropping to its edge, and its height glides between notes. Under reduced motion the loupe jumps and the line and card appear without drawing or rising.

### Burning Glass (KQ-1593) — `burning-glass`
Focus the sun and burn through to the next image.

A frame of images you burn through with a magnifying glass: inside the frame the cursor is the glass, the picture under the lens a little darker and its light gathered into one bright point. Hold still and the spot browns, smokes and catches, then a hole spreads outward on its own along a ragged, glowing ember edge with a ring of char ahead of it until the next image is on top; move away early and only a scorch is left, fading slowly. Heat lives in a small WebGL2 field the CPU mirrors, so nothing is read back; the frame is a button, arrows move the glass and Enter burns from where it is.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/burning-glass`

Props:
- `images`: readonly BurningGlassImage[] (default defaultBurningGlassImages) — The images, { src, alt }, in the order they burn through; for WebGL they must be same-origin or CORS.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The index of the image on top.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires when a burn has gone all the way through, with the index now on top.
- `focus`: number (default 0.6) — How tightly the glass focuses the sun: a broad warm glow (0) to a hard pin-point that bites fast (1).
- `burnRate`: number (default 1) — How quickly a held spot catches and how fast the hole spreads, 0.25 to 2.
- `scorch`: number (default 0.5) — How dark the browning goes and how long a scorch lingers once you move away.
- `lensSize`: number (default 92) — The glass's diameter in px; it shrinks to fit short frames.
- `smoke`: number (default 0.6) — How much smoke rises from hot spots and burning edges.
- `emberColor`: string (default a warm pigment from --warn) — The glow along the burning edge, any CSS colour.
- `smokeColor`: string (default a grey from --ink-3) — The smoke, any CSS colour.
- `label`: string (default "Burn through to the next image") — The frame's accessible name.
- `onStageChange`: (stage: BurningGlassStage) => void — Fires as the held spot warms, browns, smokes and catches, and when it settles again.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Sizzle while the spot heats and burns, with a flare when it catches.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold everything where it is.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the image but takes no input.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the frame; give it a height.

Notes:
- The frame is a real button described by the current image's alt: Enter or Space burns from where the glass is (the centre by default), arrow keys move the glass (Shift for larger steps), and each burn-through announces the new image. The system cursor is hidden only inside the frame while a pointer is there.
- One WebGL2 context: the heat field runs at no more than 256 px wide (half-float when available) on a fixed 60 Hz step, and the loop runs only while the glass is over the frame, a hole is burning or a scorch is fading; it stops off screen and in hidden tabs. DPR is capped at 2 and context loss is handled.
- Without WebGL2 (or with a cross-origin image that cannot become a texture) the image is shown as a still and Enter cross-fades to the next. Under reduced motion there is no smoke or spreading flame: the spot still browns, and on catching the next image cross-fades in.
- Sound answers only the visitor and never starts before the page has had a click or key press: hovering alone stays silent, and the sizzle loop always stops when the glass leaves, the burn ends or the tab hides.
- The default scenes are drawn in code as SVG, so nothing is fetched; pass your own `images` with alts that describe them.

### Liquify Print (KQ-1594) — `liquify-print`
Push the picture around like wet paint.

A print you push around like wet paint: a drag smears the picture along the stroke through a WebGL2 displacement field, circling winds the paint into a small vortex, and fresh smears shine wet where the paint was worked. When the hand stops, the print relaxes back to itself on a critically damped ease over `relax` ms, as if the paint remembered its shape; smears made with Shift held are pinned in a second field and stay, and double click or Escape restores everything on the snap spring. The print is focusable: arrow keys smear from a brush at its centre, Shift pins, the bracket keys twist, P pins every smear and Escape restores.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/liquify-print`

Props:
- `src`: string — An image to smear instead of the drawn print; for WebGL it must be same-origin or CORS.
- `alt`: string — What the print shows, for assistive technology.
- `brush`: number (default 56) — The brush's radius in px.
- `relax`: number (default 2200) — How long the paint takes to remember its shape once you stop, in ms.
- `gloss`: number (default 0.55) — How wet a fresh smear looks: dry and matte (0) to a sheen that dries as it relaxes (1).
- `strength`: number (default 1) — How much paint a stroke carries, 0 to 1.5.
- `swirl`: number (default 0.6) — How much a circling stroke winds the paint into a vortex, 0 to 1.
- `pinned / defaultPinned`: boolean (default false) — Pin every smear so none relax.
- `onPinnedChange`: (pinned: boolean) => void — Fires when the pin is switched (the P key), with the new state.
- `onSmear`: (pinned: boolean) => void — Fires as a stroke starts, with whether it is pinned.
- `onRestore`: () => void — Fires when the print is restored by a double click, Escape or restoreKey.
- `onStateChange`: (state: LiquifyPrintState) => void — Fires as the print goes between rest, smearing, relaxing and holding.
- `restoreKey`: number (default 0) — Change it to restore the print from outside.
- `label`: string (default "Wet print") — Names the print for assistive technology.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the print but takes no input.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the print; give it a height.

Notes:
- The print is one focusable group described by its keys: arrows smear 24 px from a brush ring at the centre (Shift pins the smear), [ and ] twist the paint, P toggles pinning everything, and Escape restores — claimed (and prevented) only when something is smeared, so otherwise it still reaches a surrounding dialog. Restores and pin changes are announced.
- Two displacement fields — live over pinned — run at a quarter of the canvas, half-float when available; strokes are queued in a fixed buffer and applied once per frame. The loop runs only while smearing, relaxing or restoring and stops once the live field has settled; a pinned smear costs nothing.
- The surface takes `touch-action: none`, so a finger smears instead of scrolling; give it a modest height on phones. Holding Shift anywhere while it is mounted pauses relaxation.
- Under reduced motion smears still follow the hand, but nothing moves on its own: after `relax` the print cross-fades back, and restore is a cross-fade. Without WebGL2 (or with a cross-origin image) the print is shown as a still.
- The default poster is drawn in code as SVG, so nothing is fetched; fine lines and type make the smear easiest to read.

Paper lanterns drifting up into the night.

A night sky with paper lanterns rising through it and your content above: each is lit from inside, a warm glow through its paper and a halo added to the sky, and climbs from below the frame swaying on its own breeze and leaning into the sway, receding as it rises until it is a pinpoint of light. - `skyColor`: string (default the accent mixed toward black) — The sky, any CSS colour; the top is deepened and the horizon warmed from it.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — A click on the sky or Enter releases a lantern.
- `onRelease`: (wish: string | null) => void — Fires when a lantern is released, with the wish it carries.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold every lantern where it is.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds where the lanterns rise and how each one sways.
- `label`: string (default "Lantern sky") — Names the sky for assistive technology.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the sky; give it a height.

Notes:
- The canvas is decoration and hidden from assistive tech; the sky itself is one focusable group whose description says Enter releases a lantern, and each release (with its wish) is announced politely. Clicks on links, buttons and other controls in `children` keep their own behaviour.
- One Canvas 2D layer: each lantern's paper and wish is drawn once to a sprite and the halo is one shared sprite added with `lighter`, so a frame is a few dozen image draws. Nothing runs off screen or in a hidden tab, and the backing store is capped at the `dpr` you pass.
- Lanterns recede at a rate set by the sky's height, so they reach a pinpoint before the top whether the box is a 200 px banner or a full hero.
- Under reduced motion the lanterns hang still at seeded heights with a steady glow; a release adds a lantern where you clicked, fading in, and it hangs still too.
- The night is drawn from `skyColor` in both themes, so keep content above it light; the server renders a still of the same sky so the first paint is finished.

### Ring Shepherd (KQ-1596) — `ring-shepherd`
Ring dust parted by a moon you steer.

A close look down onto a planetary ring system in Canvas 2D: bands of fine dust bowed round a planet below the frame, dark gaps and thin ringlets between them, shearing past slowly as rings do seen from a moon's orbit. The pointer is a small moon on springs.snap that pushes every point of dust it passes out of a lane, and because each point then rings about its new orbit at the epicyclic frequency while the shear carries it along, both edges of the lane raise scalloped waves and bright crests that trail opposite ways and smooth out behind it as the lane closes. It is a slider for where the moon is: arrow keys steer it, Escape gives it back its own orbit, and with no pointer it circles the field on its own.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ring-shepherd`

Props:
- `ringDensity`: number (default 0.6) — How thickly the dust lies in the bands, 0.1 (a sparse scatter) to 1 (dense, opaque rings).
- `gapWidth`: number (default 0.4) — Width of the dark gaps between the bands, 0 (bands touching) to 1 (wide divisions).
- `wake`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the moon pushes and how long its wake rings, 0 (a light touch that heals at once) to 1 (a wide lane with long scallops).
- `bands`: number (default 6) — How many bands of dust cross the frame, 3 to 9.
- `color`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.88 0.03 h)") — The dust's colour: pale ice from the warn token's hue. Drawn as light on a dark page and as a darkened ink on a light one.
- `moonColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.8 0.05 h)") — The moon's colour, a pigment that reads on both themes; it is lit from the upper left.
- `moonSize`: number (default 6) — The moon's radius, px, 3 to 14. The lane it clears scales with it.
- `shear`: number (default 1) — How fast the rings shear past, 0 (held) to 2. The middle of the frame rides with the moon; dust inside and outside it drifts opposite ways.
- `curvature`: number (default 0.5) — How far the bands bow, as if the planet sat below the frame, 0 (straight) to 1.
- `autopilot`: boolean (default true) — With no pointer and no keys, the moon circles the field on its own.
- `step`: number (default 18) — Pixels per arrow key; Shift moves three times as far.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keys steer the moon.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No steering by pointer or key; the control leaves the tab order.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the shear and the moon's own orbit; steering still parts the dust.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the band layout and the dust's grain, so two ring systems never match.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Steer the moon") — The accessible name of the moon's control.
- `onBandChange`: (band: number | null) => void — The band under the moon (0 is the outermost), or null while it crosses a gap. Fires on change, and once when it first reads.
- `onSteerChange`: (steering: boolean) => void — The visitor took the moon (true) or gave it back to its own orbit (false).
- `className`: string — Sizes the box; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

Notes:
- Give the parent a height; a wide, shallow box suits it best. Band layout is in fractions of the height, so every band shows at any size.
- Keyboard: it is one vertical slider for where the moon is. Up and Down move it across the bands, Left and Right along the track (Shift for three times the step), PageUp and PageDown by four steps, Home and End to the outer and inner edge; Escape, or leaving the control, gives the moon back its own orbit. The value text names the band or gap it is in.
- Pointer: the moon follows a mouse while it is over the field and goes back to its orbit when it leaves. On touch a tap places the moon and a sideways drag steers it; an upright swipe still scrolls the page, and the moon returns to its orbit 1.4 s after the finger lifts.
- Reduced motion: the dust lies still and the moon parks in a gap; it goes straight to where the pointer or keys put it and the dust round it is parted at once into a clean clearing, with no travelling lane and no scallops.
- Cost: the dust is a lattice of up to 62,400 material points, one per texel of a small tone buffer, plus up to 2,200 glints, all in preallocated typed arrays and drawn with one putImageData and one batched path. Frames run only while on screen and in a visible tab; with paused or reduced motion the loop stops once everything settles. DPR is capped at dpr.
- Theming: on a dark page the dust is light and the wake's crests glow; on a light page it is inked in a darkened mix of color, like an engraving. Colours resolve on the component's own element and repaint on a theme switch.

### Rubber Belt (KQ-1597) — `rubber-belt`
A strip of pictures that stretches with your speed.

An endless strip of pictures riding a rubber belt: a ring of masses joined by damped springs, one picture driven and the rest following through the rubber, so the strip stretches behind and bunches ahead when it speeds up, and the trailing pictures catch up and bunch when it brakes. Each picture is drawn on its own stretch of belt, its width from the spacing either side and its height answering the other way, so it squashes and stretches with the belt's acceleration and relaxes back to true; a click pulls a picture to the centre on springs.snap with one elastic overshoot the rubber carries down the strip. It is a carousel: arrow keys pull the next picture in, Home and End the first and last, Enter picks the centred one, and a drag, a throw or the wheel drives the belt too.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/rubber-belt`

Props:
- `items`: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[] (default defaultBeltItems) — The pictures on the belt. Without a src the belt draws a landscape of its own; defaultBeltItems holds eight.
- `elasticity`: number (default 0.5) — How soft the rubber is, 0 (a stiff belt, almost rigid) to 1 (a soft one that stretches far and wobbles).
- `gap`: number (default 16) — Space between pictures at rest, px. The gaps stretch and bunch with the belt.
- `direction`: "left" | "right" | "still" (default "left") — Which way the belt drifts on its own; "still" holds it.
- `speed`: number (default 22) — The idle drift's speed, px/s.
- `squash`: number (default 0.6) — How much a picture's height answers its stretch, 0 (width only) to 1 (it keeps its area).
- `itemWidth`: number — Picture width, px. By default 30% of the belt's width, between 104 and 176.
- `aspect`: number (default 0.72) — Picture height as a share of its width.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — Index of the picture pulled to the centre. Controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires from the click, key, drag or wheel that pulls a new picture to the centre.
- `onSelect`: (index: number) => void — Fires when the centred picture is clicked or Enter is pressed on it.
- `onMotionChange`: (state: "drifting" | "held" | "pulling" | "resting") => void — What the belt is doing: drifting on its own, held by a hand or the wheel, pulling a picture in, or at rest.
- `resumeAfter`: number (default 2400) — Quiet time after a hand or key before the drift resumes, ms.
- `wheel`: boolean (default true) — The mouse wheel and trackpad drive the belt (either axis).
- `captions`: boolean (default true) — Show each picture's caption under it, unstretched.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the idle drift; hands and keys still move the belt.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No input at all, and no drift.
- `label`: string (default "Pictures") — The carousel's accessible name.
- `className`: string — Classes on the outer box, which is a size container for the default picture width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the centred picture is the one tab stop. Left and Right (or Up and Down) pull the previous or next picture to the centre and move focus with it, wrapping round the ring; Home and End go to the first and last; Enter or Space on the centred picture fires onSelect. Arriving by keyboard pulls your picture in wherever the drift had carried it.
- It is a real carousel: a region with aria-roledescription carousel, each picture a labelled slide ("3 of 8: Salt flats"), and a polite live region that names the picture a gesture brought in. The idle drift pauses while the belt is hovered or holds focus, and stays paused for resumeAfter after any input.
- Hand feel: a drag holds the grabbed picture 1:1 under the finger while the rest stretch and bunch behind it; a throw is projected and the picture nearest its landing is pulled in on springs.snap with the release speed. The wheel drives the belt while it spins and lands the nearest picture when it stops. A sideways finger drives it; an upright swipe still scrolls the page.
- Reduced motion: the belt is rigid and does not drift; pictures stay true, and a pull is a 240 ms tween with no overshoot.
- Cost: at most six copies of the items are simulated (copies are added only when the items cannot fill the ring, aria-hidden and inert) at 240 Hz in plain typed arrays; each frame writes only two transforms per picture, and the loop stops once the belt settles with no drift, off screen or in a hidden tab.
- Pictures without a src are drawn in code as small landscapes; pass src for real images (they are laid object-cover and never dragged as files).

### Hand Set (KQ-1598) — `hand-set`
Words set by hand, the spacing breathing as they land.

A paragraph composed word by word as if set by hand in a compositor's stick: the browser lays it out once at its final measure, so the box never shifts, and the copy waits as a faint proof while each word slides in at the end of the line on springs.snap. As a word lands the whole line re-spreads on the same spring — a justified line spreads what it has across the measure, so the gaps tighten with every word and open a little again when the line takes its true justification — and when the line is full it locks with a faint rule drawn in beneath it, its ink deepens, and the next begins. It has no keyboard stop of its own: the words are real, selectable text and the paragraph is read once from an unseen copy.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/hand-set`

Props:
- `children`: string — The paragraph, as a string. Wins over text.
- `text`: string — The paragraph, when it is not given as children. A short editor's note by default.
- `as`: "p" | "div" | "blockquote" (default "p") — The element that carries the paragraph.
- `measure`: number (default 46) — Line length, in ch; never wider than the box.
- `pace`: number (default 170) — Time between words, ms; a comma or a full stop holds the stick a little longer.
- `justify`: "full" | "left" | "center" (default "full") — How the lines are set: justified to the measure (the gaps breathe), ragged right (words simply land), or centred (the line re-centres on each word).
- `maxSpread`: number (default 1.6) — The widest a gap may open while a justified line is still short, em, so two words never sit at opposite ends.
- `jitter`: number (default 0.35) — How uneven the hand is, 0 (a metronome) to 1. Seeded from the text, so the same paragraph is always set by the same hand.
- `linePause`: number (default 320) — The pause after a line locks before the next begins, ms.
- `rules`: boolean (default true) — Draw a faint rule under each line as it locks.
- `ruleColor`: string (default "var(--hairline-strong)") — The rules' colour.
- `setColor`: string (default "var(--ink-3)") — The colour of words still in the stick; a locked line takes the paragraph's own colour.
- `proof`: number (default 0.24) — Opacity of the copy still waiting to be set, 0 (hidden) to 0.5. It is the designed first frame before the setting starts.
- `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "hover" | "manual" (default "inView") — What starts the setting.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Set once, or start again each time the paragraph re-enters view or is hovered.
- `play`: boolean (default false) — With trigger "manual": true sets the paragraph, false clears it back to the proof.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the first word, ms.
- `onLineSet`: (line: number, lines: number) => void — A line has locked: its index and how many lines there are.
- `onComplete`: () => void — The whole paragraph is set. Fires once per setting, and at once under reduced motion.
- `className`: string — Classes on the paragraph element; type size and colour inherit from here.

Notes:
- The paragraph is laid out by the browser at its final measure and alignment from the first paint, and the words move by transforms only, so it reserves its box and never shifts the page. Line breaks are the browser's, so words never break mid-word and the font, size and hyphenation settings you give it are honoured.
- Accessibility: the paragraph is read once from an sr-only copy and the visual words are aria-hidden; they are still real text, so selection and copy give the words. There is no focus stop. Use onLineSet if a host wants to narrate progress.
- Reduced motion: the set paragraph — every word in place, every rule drawn, final ink — and onComplete fires at once.
- Cost: no animation frame loop; each landing starts one snap spring per word in the current line, a timer schedules the next word, and everything stops while the tab is hidden and on unmount. ResizeObserver and font loading re-measure and re-pose what is already set.
- Set it in left-to-right scripts; the breathing is computed from the line's left edge.

### Off Register (KQ-1599) — `off-register`
Ink plates slip out of register where you point.

A headline printed on a sheet in up to four inks, each plate a real copy of the line stacked in register and blended like ink on paper, so it reads as one rich black until the pointer comes near; then every letter of every plate slips along that plate's own direction, leaving coloured edges and dark overprints where the plates cross, and register marks in the margins slip with them. Each letter of each plate is a mass on a spring: going out it rides springs.recoil, and the pointer's speed raises both the reach and a judder in the targets so a fast pass shakes the plates harder; coming home it rides a critically damped spring and eases back into register without a bounce. Keyboard focus slips the whole line once, left to right in a cascade, and Enter slips it again.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/off-register`

Props:
- `children`: string — The headline, as a string. Wins over text.
- `text`: string (default "Printed in four inks") — The headline, when it is not given as children.
- `as`: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "p" | "div" (default "h2") — The element that carries the headline.
- `plates`: number (default 4) — How many inks print the line, 2 to 4: key and magenta, then cyan, then yellow.
- `slip`: number (default 0.5) — How far the plates slip apart near the pointer, 0 (they hold) to 1.
- `paperTone`: "cream" | "white" | "kraft" | "slate" (default "cream") — The stock it is printed on, with its own inks; slate is a dark sheet printed in light inks blended as light.
- `inks`: string[] — The inks, key first, as CSS colours; overrides the paper's own set.
- `radius`: number (default 2.4) — How far from the pointer the plates feel it, em.
- `shake`: number (default 0.6) — How much the pointer's speed shakes the plates, 0 (speed adds nothing) to 1.
- `settle`: number (default 800) — How long the plates take to ease back into register, ms.
- `marks`: boolean (default true) — Draw register marks in the sheet's margins; they slip with the letters nearest them.
- `grain`: boolean (default true) — Give the paper a fine tooth.
- `focusSlip`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus slips the whole line once; Enter slips it again.
- `caption`: React.ReactNode — A small imprint line printed under the headline, in the key ink.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keys move the plates.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No slipping by pointer or key, and no focus stop.
- `onRegisterChange`: (inRegister: boolean, slip: number) => void — The plates left register (false) or came back into it (true), with the largest slip of that excursion, px.
- `className`: string — Classes on the sheet; set the headline's size, weight and alignment here.

Notes:
- The headline is the as element with an sr-only copy of the text; the plates are aria-hidden, and only the key plate takes the pointer and selection, so copying gives the words once. Letters are split by grapheme and words never break mid-word.
- Keyboard: one focus stop, an overlay button named "Slip the plates" that never takes the pointer. Arriving by keyboard slips the line once, left to right; Enter or Space slips it again. The focus ring is drawn inside the sheet.
- Reduced motion: no travel and no shake — while the sheet is pointed at or focused the plates step a hairline off register at once, and step back when the pointer leaves or focus moves on. onRegisterChange still reports.
- Cost: up to four plates of letters, each letter a spring in x, y and turn integrated at 120 Hz in one animation frame loop that runs only while something is out of register or the pointer is moving, and only while on screen in a visible tab. Transforms are written straight to the letter spans.
- The paper and inks are fixed pigments, so the sheet reads like a printed proof on either theme; pass inks to print in your own colours. Size the type from the sheet's className (an em-based radius and slip scale with it).

### Plumb Cursor (KQ-1600) — `plumb-cursor`
A weight that swings beneath your cursor.

A cursor effect bounded to its own box: a small brass plumb bob hangs from the pointer on a fine thread, a point mass under gravity on a thread that only pulls when taut, integrated at 240 Hz, so every movement swings it and it settles slowly to dead vertical — when a hairline drops from its tip to the floor — while fast circles pump it into an orbit round the pointer. A click pays out the reel and the bob falls freely to the end of its thread and bounces on the stretch before it is reeled back up on springs.glide; with no pointer it hangs from a nail, and the thread is handed to the pointer on springs.glide and carried back on springs.drift. Keyboard focus inside carries the thread over the focused control on springs.drift, and Enter drops it as a click does.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/plumb-cursor`

Props:
- `length`: number (default 84) — Thread length, px; kept to 70% of the box's height.
- `damping`: number (default 0.3) — How quickly a swing dies, 0 (it swings for ages) to 1 (it settles in one swing).
- `weight`: number (default 1) — The bob's weight, 0.5 to 2: a heavy bob is bigger, coasts longer against the air and stretches the thread further when it drops.
- `drop`: number (default 0.6) — How much thread a click pays out, as a share of the length, 0 to 1.5.
- `hold`: number (default 900) — How long the bob hangs at the end of its thread before it is reeled back, ms.
- `gravity`: number (default 1) — Gravity, as a multiple of the house value, 0.5 to 2: a slower or quicker swing.
- `color`: string (default "var(--ink-2)") — The thread's colour.
- `bobColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.78 0.12 h)") — The bob's metal, a pigment that reads on both themes: brass from the warn token's hue, shaded into a turned body.
- `restAt`: readonly [number, number] (default [0.9, 0.12]) — Where the nail sits that the bob hangs from with no pointer, as fractions of the box.
- `plumbLine`: boolean (default true) — Drop a hairline to the floor when the bob hangs dead vertical.
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus inside moves the thread over the focused control, and Enter or Space drops the bob.
- `touch`: boolean (default true) — On touch, the bob hangs from the finger while it is down and a quick tap drops it. Sets touch-action: none on the box.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The bob stays on its nail.
- `onStateChange`: (state: "resting" | "true" | "swinging" | "orbiting" | "dropped") => void — What the bob is doing: on its nail, hanging true, swinging, orbiting the pointer, or dropped to the end of its thread.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The content the bob hangs over; it stays fully interactive.
- `className`: string — Classes on the box the bob lives in; give it a size and, usually, overflow-clip and a radius.

Notes:
- It wraps content: the painted layer is an aria-hidden SVG with pointer-events none above the children, clipped to the box, so every control underneath keeps its own semantics, focus and clicks. The system cursor is never hidden.
- Keyboard: there is no extra focus stop. When a control inside takes keyboard focus the thread is carried over it and the bob swings across to hang above it, tip pointing at it; Enter or Space on it drops the bob as a click would; leaving the box returns the bob to its nail.
- Touch: the bob hangs from the finger while it is down and goes back to its nail when it lifts; a quick tap drops it. The box takes touch-action none for that; pass touch={false} where the page must scroll through it.
- Reduced motion: no swing and no bounce — the bob hangs dead vertical straight under the pointer, the nail or the focused control, and a click shows the thread at full length at once and back after hold.
- Cost: one SVG path and one group are rewritten per frame (rounded to hundredths), from a 240 Hz loop that runs only while the bob or the pivot moves, on screen, in a visible tab; it stops when the bob hangs true.

### River Script (KQ-1601) — `river-script`
Text that flows downstream, quick through the narrows.

A sentence floats down a winding river on a pale map, letter by letter along the centreline and turned to its heading, as an accordion: the spacing opens in the wide pools, where the letters drift across the stream on a slow eddy, and closes up tight in the narrows, while the sentence's speed follows continuity — slow through the pools, quick through the narrows — so one sentence breathes as it travels and loops from the mouth back to the source. Hovering the text eases the current to a stop on springs.drift and the line lies straight to be read; grabbing the river by a bank drags the nearest bend 1:1, re-splining the course live with the letters flowing along it, and a released bend settles on springs.snap with the release speed. Space holds and frees the current, and each bend is a vertical slider for the keyboard.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/river-script`

Props:
- `children`: string — The sentence, as a string. Wins over text.
- `text`: string — The sentence, when it is not given as children. A line about the river by default.
- `meander`: number (default 0.6) — How far the river winds, 0 (a straight canal) to 1 (deep bends).
- `flowSpeed`: number (default 38) — The current's speed through an average reach, px/s; quicker in the narrows, slower in the pools.
- `width`: number (default 30) — The river's width at an average reach, px.
- `narrows`: number (default 0.6) — How much the width swings between pools and narrows, 0 (even) to 1.
- `bends`: number (default 5) — How many bends the course passes through, 3 to 7; a narrow map draws fewer (about one per 130 px) so the text never kinks.
- `course / defaultCourse`: number[] (default all 0) — Offsets the visitor (or host) has added to each bend, -1 to 1 of the half height, negative north. Controlled or initial.
- `onCourseChange`: (course: number[]) => void — Fires from the drag or key that re-routed the river, with every bend's offset.
- `paused / defaultPaused`: boolean (default false) — Whether the current is held. Controlled or initial.
- `onPausedChange`: (paused: boolean) => void — Fires when Space holds or frees the current.
- `hoverToRead`: boolean (default true) — Hovering the text slows the current to a stop so it can be read.
- `waterColor`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent-bright) 18%, transparent)") — The water's colour.
- `bankColor`: string (default "var(--ink-3)") — The banks' and contour hints' ink.
- `places`: readonly [string, string] (default ["Fern Pool", "the Gauge"]) — Names for the widest pool and the tightest narrows, set beside the river where there is room (and left out where there is none).
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds the course and its pools, so two rivers never match.
- `height`: number (default 200) — The map's height, px. It fills its parent's width.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No dragging and no bend keys; the current still runs.
- `label`: string (default "River map") — The map's accessible name.
- `onFlowChange`: (state: "flowing" | "reading" | "paused") => void — The current's state: flowing, held by a hand over the text, or paused.
- `className`: string — Classes on the map; the text's size and colour inherit from here.

Notes:
- The sentence is read once from an sr-only copy; the map and its letters are aria-hidden. Letters are split by grapheme and laid in reading order, the last letter leading downstream.
- Keyboard: the map is one focus stop where Space holds and frees the current (announced politely). Each bend that fits the width is a vertical slider after it: Up and Down move it north and south (Shift for bigger steps), PageUp and PageDown by a quarter, Home and End to the south and north edges; the value text names the bend and how far it swings.
- Pointer: hovering the text eases the current to a stop and lets it go when you move off; a vertical drag anywhere on the map takes the nearest bend 1:1, rubber-banding past the edges and settling on springs.snap when released. On touch a vertical drag re-routes the river and a sideways swipe scrolls.
- Reduced motion: no current and no eddies — the sentence lies still across the widest pool with the same pool-and-narrows spacing, and a re-routed river carries it to its new course at once.
- Cost: the course, banks and arclength table are rebuilt only when the shape or size changes (or while a released bend settles); each frame writes one transform per letter. The loop runs only while flowing, on screen and in a visible tab, and stops when held or paused once the current has eased to rest.

### Notepad Flip (KQ-1602) — `notepad-flip`
Lines that flip over the spiral as you scroll.

A top-bound reporter's pad seen at an angle in real CSS 3D, one line of text per sheet: scroll over it and the top sheet peels up, turns over the binding with its lower half lagging on the air so the paper curls, throws a shadow down the next line and comes to rest on the turned pile above the spiral, its writing showing through from behind. Each sheet's angle is a spring toward the scroll — rising on springs.snap with one flap at the top of its arc, falling back on springs.glide with a soft landing — and a jump in the scroll is followed one sheet after another, so sheets go over and come back down in order. The pad is a native scroller and a vertical slider: Down and Up turn one sheet at a time, Page Down and Page Up two, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space turns the next.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/notepad-flip`

Props:
- `lines`: string[] — One line per sheet, the top sheet first.
- `label`: string (default "Notepad") — The pad's accessible name.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The index of the sheet showing, which is how many are turned.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires from the scroll, drag, tap or key that turned to a new sheet.
- `binding`: "spiral" | "wire" | "glue" (default "spiral") — How the sheets are bound along the top.
- `flipAngle`: number (default 190) — Where a turned sheet rests over the binding, degrees: under 180 the pile stands up, over 180 it leans away behind the pad.
- `paperTone`: "white" | "legal" | "steno" | "kraft" (default "legal") — The paper stock, with its ruling.
- `tilt`: number (default 24) — How far the pad lies back on the desk, degrees.
- `curl`: number (default 0.5) — How far a turning sheet's free half bends behind it, 0 to 1.
- `shadow`: number (default 0.6) — How dark a lifted sheet's shadow falls on the next line, 0 to 1.
- `step`: number (default 90) — Scroll distance that turns one sheet, px.
- `ruled`: boolean (default true) — Draw the blue rule under the words and the red margin line.
- `ink`: string (default a navy ballpoint) — The colour of the writing, any CSS colour.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Scrolling, dragging, tapping and the keys turn the sheets.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Paper sounds for the turns the visitor makes.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the pad as it is; nothing turns it.
- `className`: string — Size the pad with font-size: it is drawn in em.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the pad is a vertical slider — Down and Up turn one sheet, Page Down and Page Up two, Home and End jump, Enter or Space turns the next and from the last sheet starts again; the value reads “Sheet 2 of 5”.
- Scrolling: the pad is a real scroll region (step px per sheet, snapping to whole sheets), so wheel, trackpad and touch turn it and the page takes the scroll back at either end; a mouse drag scrubs 1:1 and a tap turns the next sheet.
- Reduced motion: no sheet travels or curls — the top sheet cross-fades away to the line beneath and the turned pile appears with a fade; the value and its announcements are unchanged.
- Performance: one loop springs every sheet and stops when they rest; it halts off screen and in hidden tabs. A line too long for its sheet is scaled to fit rather than wrapped.
- Theming: the paper, ruling and binding are fixed pigments that read the same in both themes; the lines are read once from an sr-only list and every painted sheet is aria-hidden.
- Sound: with sound on, a paper crinkle answers each sheet the visitor turns over the top; it stays silent until the page has had a click, tap or key press.

### Firefly Letters (KQ-1603) — `firefly-letters`
A headline of fireflies that scatter as you near.

A headline drawn by a few hundred fireflies on a dusk panel: the words are laid out for real, sampled into home spots, and a firefly hovers at each, glowing and flashing on its own rhythm — coupled oscillators, so a settled word slowly falls into step and its flashes ripple across it together. Bring the pointer near and the ones within reach flash once and burst away from it, blinking out as they coast into the dark; after a pause they come back one by one, nearest first, weaving in on a steering force that arrives softly, and each relights its spot with a swell timed like springs.drift until the word is whole. - `trigger`: "mount" | "inView" | "manual" (default "inView") — When they arrive and light the words.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Arrive once, or each time the headline comes back into view.
- `play`: boolean (default false) — With trigger "manual": true brings them in.

- The server renders the headline lit as a glowing word, so the first frame is finished before the fireflies arrive on the trigger.

### Break Shot (KQ-1604) — `break-shot`
Letters break like a rack of balls, then re-rack.

A headline racked as billiard balls on a small carom table, a lacquered ball for every letter with an ivory spot carrying it. The pointer is a cue ball: what it meets it hits as an equal mass would, with the pointer's speed and the force, and the balls run on real physics — elastic collisions, cushions that give back part of the speed, rolling resistance from the cloth — each one rolling so its letter turns over the top and comes back round. After the spread has lain still they are lifted and glide back to their slots along straight lines in reading order, a cascade apart on springs.glide, rolling upright so the letters land facing the reader. - `friction`: number (default 0.45) — How much the cloth slows the balls, 0 (slick, they run and bank) to 1 (heavy nap).

### Capillary Cursor (KQ-1606) — `capillary-cursor`
A drop of ink that fills whatever it touches.

Inside its own box the pointer is a single drop of ink, exactly at the pointer and drawn out a little along fast travel. Touch a button, link or field and the ink wicks along the control's real outline — its border box and its own four corner radii — from the point of contact in both directions, the fronts slowing as capillary flow does, then seeps inward from the wet edge at low strength until the control is filled in its exact shape, while the drop shrinks by the ink it gave; the drop's size eases on a rate as quick as springs.flick and the flood on a glide-like ease. Leave and the flood recedes and the outline drains back toward the exit point through a thread of ink that thins as it pulls and pinches off past its reach, and the drop swells again. Keyboard focus moves the ink from one control to the next, and the system cursor returns over text fields and on any key.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/capillary-cursor`

Props:
- `children`: ReactNode — The area the drop lives in; its buttons, links and fields keep every click, focus and key.
- `inkColor`: "cobalt" | "iron" | "sepia" | "carmine" | string (default "cobalt") — The ink: a named ink or any CSS colour.
- `wickSpeed`: number (default 520) — How fast the ink runs along an outline, px per second.
- `dotSize`: number (default 14) — The drop's diameter when it is full, px.
- `strength`: number (default 0.16) — How strongly the ink floods the inside of a control, 0 to 1.
- `lineWidth`: number (default 1.75) — The wicked outline's thickness, px.
- `flood`: boolean (default true) — Fill the inside of a control, not only its outline.
- `stretch`: number (default 0.5) — How far the drop draws out when it moves fast, 0 to 1.
- `cling`: number (default 0.5) — How far the draining thread stretches before it lets go, 0 to 1.
- `targets`: string (default "button, a[href], [role='button'], input, select, textarea, [data-ink]") — What the ink fills, as a CSS selector.
- `hideCursor`: boolean (default true) — The drop replaces the system cursor inside the box (never over text fields, never after a key).
- `followFocus`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus moves the ink to the focused control.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer leads the drop (mouse and pen; a tap inks the tapped control).
- `onTargetChange`: (target: HTMLElement | null) => void — The control holding the ink changed: that control, or null.
- `className`: string — Classes for the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: focus moves the ink — the focused control wicks from the side nearest the last one and the last drains toward it; any key press hands the pointer back its own cursor, and nothing new enters the tab order.
- Touch: there is no hover on glass, so a tap inks the tapped control from the tap point and the ink stays until the next tap.
- Reduced motion: the drop follows the pointer 1:1 at a constant size with no stretch, and a touched control's outline and flood fade in and out whole — no wicking, no thread.
- Performance: one loop runs only while ink is moving or the drop is changing; it halts off screen and in hidden tabs. Outlines are measured only for live stains (at most four), and the painted SVG layer never takes a click.
- Theming: the named inks are pigments that read in both themes (iron follows the theme's ink); pass any CSS colour or token. Mark custom targets with data-ink.

A paragraph of real text and a careful reader with a coloured pencil: when it comes into view the pencil marks it up mark by mark — an underline, a loop that overshoots its own start, a bracket in the gutter with a note, a phrase struck through — each built from the phrase's real line fragments so it sits on the words wherever they wrap. Every stroke is a ribbon whose width follows the hand's pressure, with a seeded wobble, and the pen travels it on a minimum-jerk profile timed from its length, lifting between strokes, while a small pencil rides the tip; notes are written line by line in a margin column, or as numbered footnotes when the container is narrow. - Theming: the named pencils are pigments that read on either theme (graphite follows the theme's ink); pass any CSS colour or token.

Arrows pan a column or a row, Page Up and Page Down a screen, Home returns to the start, and Enter or Space opens the picture nearest the centre, which is outlined while the wall has keyboard focus. The open picture is a modal dialog: focus moves to Close, Tab stays there, Escape closes and focus returns to the wall.
- Reduced motion: the wall still pans 1:1 under the hand, but there is no coast, lean or ripple, keys jump straight to their place and a picture fades in where it opens instead of growing from its tile.
- Performance: only the columns in view are rendered, and React re-renders only when one enters or leaves; per-frame positions are written straight to transforms by one loop that runs only while the wall moves and is on screen.
- The first frame is laid out in CSS with container query units, so it is composed and full at any width before the wall is measured. Screen readers also get a list of every picture with a button to open it.
- Pictures passed as `src` should be the size of a tile or larger; they are covered, not stretched, and the drawn defaults use tokens so the wall reads in both themes.

### Band Compare (KQ-1611) — `band-compare`
Several versions side by side, seams you drag.

Several versions of one picture side by side as bands across a single frame, in register, each labelled at its top. Drag any seam and it follows 1:1 while only the two bands either side give way, rubber-banding against a neighbour and landing on springs.glide with the release velocity; the grip lifts on springs.flick. Double-click a band or press its label and it widens to fill the frame as the seams sweep outward on glide, nearest first, and again sweeps them back to the shares they had. Seams are separators: Tab moves between them, arrows move them (Shift for larger steps), Home and End go to their limits, number keys widen a band and Escape shares it back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/band-compare`

Props:
- `items`: BandCompareItem[] (default defaultBandCompareItems) — The versions: { label, src?, alt?, filter?, art? }; the first `bands` are shown.
- `src`: string — The picture every version shares unless it brings its own; defaults to a drawn harbour.
- `alt`: string (default "A harbour at evening with boats and a lighthouse") — Describes the shared picture.
- `bands`: number (default 4) — How many versions share the frame, 2 to 6.
- `seamStyle`: "line" | "handle" | "gap" | "fold" (default "handle") — How the seams are drawn: a hairline, a hairline with a grip, a gutter between tiles, or folded strips.
- `labels`: "chip" | "rule" | "none" (default "chip") — How the bands are labelled; "none" keeps the labels for keyboard focus only.
- `value / defaultValue`: number[] (default equal shares) — The seam positions, left to right, as fractions of the frame; controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (seams: number[]) => void — Fires from the drag or key that moved a seam, with every seam.
- `expanded / defaultExpanded`: number | null (default null) — The band widened to fill the frame, or null; controlled or initial.
- `onExpandedChange`: (index: number | null) => void — Fires from the double-click, label or key that widened a band or shared it back.
- `minBand`: number (default 28) — The narrowest a band can be pushed, px.
- `step`: number (default 0.02) — How far an arrow key moves a seam, as a fraction of the frame; Shift moves five times as far.
- `label`: string (default "Versions") — The frame's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No drags, keys or widening; the frame dims.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the frame.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab runs label, seam, label… left to right. Each seam is a vertical separator with its value, limits and both bands' shares in its value text; arrows move it, Shift moves it five times as far, Home and End go to its limits. Labels are toggle buttons that widen their band, number keys do the same from anywhere inside, Escape shares the frame back, and a seam that hides while focused hands focus to the widened label.
- Reduced motion: seams jump to their places and a widened band fades in with no sweep; a drag still follows the hand and the grip does not lift.
- Performance: there is no loop. Each seam is one motion value; every clip path, label position and shade derives from them, so dragging re-renders nothing.
- Versions can be separate pictures (`src` per item) or one shared picture with a CSS `filter` per item; filters apply to the picture only, so labels and seams stay crisp.
- Theming: seams, grips and labels use card, background and hairline tokens with a hairline ring, so they read over light and dark pictures in both themes.

### Sand Furrow (KQ-1612) — `sand-furrow`
Plough through sand to find the picture beneath.

A picture buried under fine sand, the sand a heightfield simulated on a coarse grid and shaded per pixel in WebGL2 — directional light, grain, glints, short shadows cast into the furrow and damp edges where it thins. Drag to plough: a bowl-shaped plough cuts down toward the picture and heaps what it cuts onto a bank on each side, the banks round off at their angle of repose, and about a second later they slump back in at the settle pace until the sand lies smooth and the loop stops. Double-click, Enter or Space sweeps the tray clear with a broom front that carries a ridge off the edge; Backspace pours the sand back in; arrow keys plough from a marker.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sand-furrow`

Props:
- `src`: string — The buried picture (same origin or CORS-enabled); defaults to a drawn tile mosaic.
- `alt`: string (default "A tile mosaic of a fish among waves") — Describes the picture.
- `grainSize`: number (default 1.5) — Size of a grain of sand, 0.5 (silt) to 3 px (coarse).
- `settle`: number (default 0.45) — How quickly the banks slump back over the furrow, 0 (never) to 1.
- `plough`: number (default 24) — Width of the plough, 8 to 40 px.
- `depth`: number (default 0.9) — How much sand one pass moves, 0 to 1; 1 cuts down to the picture.
- `light`: number (default 135) — The direction the light comes from, in degrees (0 is from the right, 90 from above).
- `sandColor`: string (default "oklch(from var(--warn) 0.82 0.055 calc(h - 8))") — The sand's colour; a pigment, the same in both themes.
- `cleared / defaultCleared`: boolean (default false) — The sand swept clear; controlled or initial.
- `onClearedChange`: (cleared: boolean) => void — Fires from the double-click or key that swept the sand clear or poured it back.
- `onPlough`: (uncovered: number) => void — Fires after each stroke, and again once the banks have settled, with the share of the picture uncovered, 0 to 1.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish as the plough moves and as the sand is swept or poured.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Drag, double-click and the keys plough and sweep.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seeds the dunes and the grain.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Sand over a picture") — The tray's accessible name; the picture and how much of it shows are added.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the tray.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the tray is one tab stop and shows a plough marker on keyboard focus. Arrows plough from the marker, drawing the furrow along the move (Shift ploughs further); Enter or Space sweeps the sand clear and Backspace pours it back. A polite live region says how much is uncovered after each stroke, when it is covered again and when it is swept.
- Reduced motion: ploughing still cuts, but nothing slumps on its own; after a pause set by `settle` the sand fades back smooth, and sweeping and pouring are cross-fades.
- Performance: one WebGL2 pass. The heightfield is simulated in JavaScript on a 3 px grid and uploaded only on frames where it changed; the loop runs only while ploughing, sweeping, pouring or slumping, only on screen and with the page visible, and stops once the sand is still. Device pixel ratio is capped at 2, context loss is handled, and everything is released on unmount.
- Without WebGL2 (or with a picture from another origin that cannot be read) a drawn still shows the picture under sand with one shaded furrow, and the sweep cross-fades it away.
- Sound plays only when `sound` is on, only for the visitor's own strokes and keys: a swish every stretch of ploughing, pitched by speed and panned by position, and a longer one for the sweep and the pour.
