### Drum Plotter (KQ-1614) — `drum-plotter`
A live line drawn by a stylus on a turning drum.

A chart recorder whose graph paper is wrapped round a drum turning about a vertical axis, drawn as a real cylinder in Canvas 2D so the squares crowd into shade at both rims while the paper carries the inked trace left, away from a pen on a rail. The pen follows each reading on the snap spring's constants scaled by penResponse, so a step is drawn with one small overshoot; a series change lifts it on flick, glides the carriage to the new level while the ink changes to the next in the rack, and drops it on recoil, where a blot spreads into the paper. Hover reads the value under the pointer as the paper passes; the drum is a slider whose arrow keys move the same readout along the trace (Page Up and Down five seconds, Home the oldest ink, End the pen, Escape to hide it), and the legend is a radio group.

- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first series) — The series being plotted, by id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the legend press or key that picked a series.
- `reading`: number — Live mode: the pen follows this reading, in the series' units, instead of its samples.
- `sampleRate`: number (default 4) — Samples per second when playing a series' samples.
- `paperSpeed`: number (default 36) — How fast the paper travels across the front of the drum, px per second.
- `inkColor`: "red" | "blue" | "green" | "violet" | string (default "red") — The first ink in the rack, or any CSS colour; later series take the next inks.
- `gridStyle`: "graph" | "ruled" | "dots" | "plain" (default "graph") — The paper: fine graph paper, ruled lines, a dot grid or plain.
- `penResponse`: number (default 0.5) — How the pen answers a change, 0 (heavy and slow) to 1 (light and quick); 0.5 rides the snap spring.
- `penAt`: number (default 0.74) — Where the pen sits across the drum's face, 0.55 to 0.9 of its width.
- `lineWidth`: number (default 1.6) — Width of the inked line, px.
- `legend`: boolean (default true) — Show the series legend, with the live value in the active chip.
- `scale`: boolean (default true) — Show the value scale beside the drum.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Stop the drum; the readout still works.
- `onReadout`: (readout: { series: string; value: number; secondsAgo: number } | null) => void — Fires when the hovered or keyboard reading changes, and with null when it hides.
- `label`: string (default "Chart recorder") — The recorder's accessible name.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Highest device pixel ratio the drum is drawn at.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No legend, hover or keys; the drum keeps plotting.
- `className`: string — Sizes the recorder; it is 224px tall and full width by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the legend (a radio group; arrows pick a series) and then the drum, a slider over the history: Left and Right step half a second, Page Up and Page Down five seconds, Home the oldest ink, End the pen, and Escape hides the readout. aria-valuetext reads the series, value and how long ago.
- Reduced motion: the drum steps once a second instead of turning, the pen lands on each reading at once and a series change is an instant ink change with a gap; the record still grows and the readouts work the same.
- Performance: the frame loop runs only while the drum is on screen, the tab is visible and paused is false; the ink lives in preallocated typed arrays keyed by paper position, the canvas is capped at dpr and resized by ResizeObserver, and history is pre-filled on mount so the paper is never blank.
- Live data: pass reading and update it as values arrive (the pen interpolates on its spring); without it, each series' samples play back at sampleRate in a loop.
- Theming: ink, paper, grid and metal are pigments from tokens resolved on the element and re-read on a theme change, so the paper reads in both themes.

Every ring turns at its own slow pace, the pictures riding it upright; hovering or focusing a ring brakes it to a stop by constant friction while its band brightens and its year reads above the slice. A click brings a picture forward from its own rectangle on the glide spring to a framed view over the centre while the rings pause, and Escape, the close button or the scrim send it back with focus returned. Pictures share one roving tab stop: Left and Right move along a ring, Up and Down between years, Home the core and End the bark, Enter brings forward.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/year-rings`

Props:
- `items`: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string; year: number }[] (default 48 drawn pictures, 2020 to 2025) — The archive, any order: grouped into one ring per year, the oldest at the core.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The picture brought forward, by index into items, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number | null) => void — Fires from the press or key that brought a picture forward or sent it back.
- `ringGap`: number (default 1.4) — Space between rings, in picture widths (1.1 to 2).
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the rings turn, 0 (still) to 2.
- `grain`: number (default 0.7) — How much of the timber is drawn, 0 (a clean diagram) to 1 (rays, a check and every growth line).
- `alternate`: boolean (default true) — Neighbouring rings turn opposite ways.
- `brake`: boolean (default true) — Hovering or focusing a ring stops it.
- `wood`: "oak" | "cedar" | "ash" | "walnut" (default "oak") — The timber.
- `captions`: boolean (default true) — Show the year label above the slice.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold every ring still.
- `label`: string (default "Archive by year") — The archive's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No hovering, pressing or keys.
- `className`: string — Sizes the archive; it fills a 544px-tall box by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: one tab stop across every picture. Left and Right move along a ring, Up out to newer years and Down in to older (to the picture nearest in angle), Home the core and End the outer ring; Enter or Space brings a picture forward, its close button takes focus, and Escape sends it back with focus returned to the picture.
- Reduced motion: the rings stand still, hover and focus still show the year at once, and the forward view cross-fades instead of flying.
- Performance: one frame loop advances the ring angles, only while on screen, visible, not paused and with speed above zero; braked rings ease to zero and the loop stops when every ring is still. Each ring is one rotating layer whose pictures counter-rotate through a shared CSS variable.
- Each ring is a labelled group ("2023, 11 pictures") and each picture a button named with its caption, year and place in the ring.

### Burner Card (KQ-1620) — `burner-card`
A card with a gas flame breathing behind it.

A content card with a row of gas jets burning behind its top edge, drawn per pixel in WebGL2: a white-blue inner cone inside a taller translucent mantle for every port, a soft glow over the row and hot air above it that visibly wobbles the light. Hover, keyboard focus inside the card or a touch press turns the valve up on springs.snap, whose one overshoot is the roar before the taller, brighter flame settles, while the card's top edge catches the light; leaving turns it down on springs.drift to a low, steady flicker. The first time it is seen the burner lights from end to end, each jet popping alight as the front reaches it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/burner-card`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The card's content.
- `flameHeight`: number (default 26) — The resting flame's height above the card's edge in px; the roar reaches flameHeight × roar and the headroom above the card is kept for it.
- `hue`: number (default 255) — The flame's hue in degrees at fixed lightness: 255 town-gas blue, 200 cyan, 290 violet, 150 copper green.
- `flutter`: number (default 0.5) — How restless the flame is, 0 (steady) to 1 (nervous and dancing).
- `roar`: number (default 1.9) — How much taller the flame stands with the valve open, as a multiple of flameHeight, 1 to 3.
- `active`: boolean — Holds the valve open (true) or low (false) whatever the pointer does; leave undefined for hover and focus to drive it.
- `onActiveChange`: (active: boolean) => void — Fires when hover, focus or a touch opens or closes the valve, with the new state.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Hover, keyboard focus inside the card and a touch press open the valve.
- `jetSpacing`: number (default 14) — Distance between the burner's ports in px; smaller is a finer, denser row.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — The soft glow over the burner, 0 to 1.
- `shimmer`: number (default 0.5) — How much the hot air above the flame wobbles, 0 to 1.
- `ignite`: "inView" | "mount" | "none" (default "inView") — When the burner lights: the first time it is seen, at mount, or already lit.
- `focusable`: boolean (default false) — Makes the card itself a tab stop, for cards with nothing focusable inside; name it with label.
- `label`: string — Names the card when it is focusable.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the flicker still; the valve still opens and closes.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds each jet's own flicker.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's pixel ratio, at most 2; the soft flame never draws above 1.25.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root (width, margins).
- `cardClassName`: string — Classes for the card box (padding, background).

Notes:
- Keyboard focus anywhere inside the card (focus-visible) opens the valve and blur closes it, exactly like hover; with no focusable content, pass focusable and label to make the card its own tab stop. Touch opens it while pressed.
- The flame is one WebGL2 pass at a soft pixel ratio. It draws only while on screen and the tab is visible, at thirty frames a second while low and sixty while the valve moves, and stops when paused. Without WebGL2 a CSS flame stands in; a lost context is rebuilt.
- Under reduced motion there is no flicker, ignition or roar: a still flame is drawn, and redrawn tall and bright at once when the valve opens, so the state still shows.
- Colours come from hue at fixed lightness, composited so the flame reads as light on a dark page and as a saturated blue flame on a light one; the page's theme is re-read when it changes.
- The root reserves headroom above the card for the full roar (about flameHeight × roar + 16 px), so nothing is clipped and nothing draws outside the component's box.

### Curtain Count (KQ-1621) — `curtain-count`
Five ways to hold the stage while the page loads.

A full-frame loading screen over its own box in five variants driven by one progress value, which the readout follows on springs.glide: a counter whose odometer wheels rest on their digits and roll on the carry beside a filling rule, the brand word filling with colour from its baseline, five stacked bars filling over overlapping windows of the load, a split frame whose field inverts the giant percentage where its edge crosses, and a radial wipe with a clock hand riding its edge. All five end the same way: at 100 % the curtain holds a beat and says Ready, its seams crack open on springs.flick, and two halves, vertical slats or horizontal bands lift out of the box on the exit ease in a cascade while the page beneath settles from a hair's scale on springs.glide. - `variant`: "counter" | "word" | "bars" | "split" | "radial" | number (default "counter") — Which way to hold the stage, by name or by its place 1–5 in that order.
- `exitMotion`: "split" | "slats" | "shutter" (default "split") — How the frame leaves: two halves parting at the centre, vertical slats from the centre out, or horizontal bands from the top.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The fill colour, any CSS colour, taken at a lightness that reads on the curtain.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The page beneath, inert and marked busy until the curtain has gone.
- `brand`: string (default "Fieldline") — The brand on the curtain, and the word the word variant fills.
- `caption`: string (default "Loading the season") — A line of copy on the curtain; it reads Ready at 100 %.
- `stages`: readonly string[] (default ["Fonts", "Pictures", "Routes", "Data", "Scripts"]) — Labels for the bars variant's five bars.
- `label`: string (default `Loading ${brand}`) — Names the progress bar for assistive technology.
- `hold`: number (default 280) — How long the curtain holds at 100 % before it splits, in ms.
- `exitDuration`: number (default 680) — How long each part takes to lift away, in ms; the cascade adds to it.

Notes:
- Drive progress from your real loader; the readout smooths jumps on the glide spring, so a stalling request and a rush still read as one movement. A drop below 1 is a new run: the curtain fades back in and the count starts from there.
- Assistive technology hears one progress bar with the value from progress (not the smoothed readout) and, on reveal, a polite '{brand} loaded.'; the page beneath is inert and aria-busy until then, and no focus is taken.
- Under reduced motion the digits and fills change in place (the fill is the information) and at 100 % the curtain fades out instead of splitting.
- The curtain lives inside its box: it is a size container, never fixed or sized by the viewport, so wrap a page region or a full-height app shell. The parts exist only while they lift and leave through the top edge, clipped by the box.
- Nothing runs while it is settled: the readout and the exit are motion values on springs and tweens; at rest the curtain is a single sheet.

A picture that's sharp only where you look.

A picture drawn coarse in square blocks everywhere except where you look: under the pointer it sharpens in steps, a crisp centre and rings that each halve the block, chosen block by block so the ring edges step like a real change of resolution, every block the average of the picture beneath it. - `ring`: number (default 0.7) — Each ring's width as a share of the fovea, 0.2 to 2.

### Shop Light (KQ-1626) — `shop-light`
A strip light stutters on and lights what's under it.

A room in the dark with a fluorescent batten hanging over your content. On reveal the tube starts the way a cold tube does: its cathodes glow orange at both ends, it tries to strike in uneven, seeded flashes with dim swims between them, and it catches dimmer and cooler than it will be, settling to full on springs.drift while its colour warms to the chosen temperature and the content rises a nudge into the lit pool on springs.glide. The light is composited rather than tinted, so the wall and the content are multiplied by it and the pool dies into the dark below. The pull cord is a real switch that follows a downward drag 1:1 and springs back on springs.recoil with the drag's velocity; Space or Enter pulls it, and keyboard focus entering the content in the dark switches the light on.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/shop-light`

- `trigger`: "inView" | "mount" | "manual" (default "inView") — What switches the tube on by itself: coming into view, mounting, or nothing but the cord.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Light once and stay lit; false puts it out when it leaves the view and strikes it again on return.
- `delay`: number (default 250) — Pause before an automatic strike, in ms.
- `flicker`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the cold tube fights before it catches, 0 (strikes clean) to 1 (a long preheat and five or six failed strikes).
- `warmth`: number (default 0.55) — The settled light's colour, 0 (6500 K daylight) to 1 (2700 K warm white).
- `falloff`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly the light dies below the tube, 0 (a wash to the floor) to 1 (a tight pool under it).
- `tubeLength`: number (default 0.6) — The tube's length as a share of the width, 0.3 to 0.9.
- `hang`: number (default 22) — How far below the top edge the fixture hangs, in px.
- `ambient`: number (default 0.08) — How much of the room shows with the tube out, 0 (pitch dark) to 0.5.
- `surface`: "pegboard" | "plaster" | "slats" (default "pegboard") — The wall the content hangs on.

- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds the stutter: the same seed fails the same way.
- `label`: string (default "Shop light") — The switch's accessible name.
- `onSettle`: () => void — Fires when a strike has settled to a steady light.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Plays the cord's click and the tube's buzz on each flash, only for the visitor's own pull, key or focus.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the room but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-60 w-full") — Sizes the room.

Notes:
- The cord is a role=switch button with aria-checked: Space or Enter pulls it, a drag down past 9px pulls it, and the change is announced politely. Focus moving into the content while the room is dark switches the light on, so a focus ring is never drawn in the dark.
- Under reduced motion there is no preheat, stutter or rise: the light fades up over 240ms and out over 150ms, and the settled colour is used at once.
- The room is its own world: the wall is a fixed pigment and the content inside is scoped to the light theme's tokens, so it reads the same on light and dark pages. Style the content with ordinary tokens.
- Nothing runs once the tube has settled: a strike is a few keyframe tweens on motion values driving opacity, and the reveal is one IntersectionObserver.
- Sound never plays for an automatic reveal; with sound on, the visitor's own pull clicks and each flash of the strike buzzes.

### Shadow Box (KQ-1627) — `shadow-box`
A card built like a shadow box, deep inside.

A card built as a real box in CSS 3D: a framed window, inner walls running back to a sky panel, outside walls in the frame's colour, and layers of cut-paper scenery standing at their own depths. One side is open and the light falls in from it, so the walls are shaded by where they face, each layer's cut edge catches the light, and each casts a blurred shadow drawn on the layers behind it, which therefore moves with the surface it falls on as the box turns. The pointer tilts the box toward it on springs.glide and it drifts level on springs.drift when the pointer leaves. Keyboard focus starts a slow tour round the inside, arrow keys tilt it a quarter of the range and Home levels it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/shadow-box`

Props:
- `layers`: number | readonly ShadowBoxLayer[] (default 5) — How many cut-paper layers to generate, 2 to 7, or your own layers back to front: { path (0–100 SVG path), color, depth? }.
- `depth`: number (default 56) — How deep the box is, in px: longer shadows, more parallax.
- `light`: "top" | "left" | "right" (default "top") — The open side the light falls in from.
- `lightStrength`: number (default 0.7) — How strong that light is, 0 (flat, no shadows) to 1.
- `palette`: "dusk" | "fern" | "snow" | "ember" | readonly string[] (default "dusk") — A named paper set, or five CSS colours: sky top, sky low, moon, far ridge, near ridge.
- `tilt`: number (default 14) — The furthest the box tilts toward the pointer, in degrees.
- `perspective`: number (default 900) — The viewing distance, in px: smaller is a stronger perspective.
- `frame`: number (default 14) — The frame's width, in px.
- `frameColor`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 86%, var(--background))") — The frame's colour, any CSS colour; the outside walls are it, shaded.
- `glass`: boolean (default true) — A glass pane in the frame, its reflection sliding against the tilt.
- `title`: string (default "Night fern trail") — The piece's name, printed on the plaque and read first.
- `caption`: string (default "Cut paper, N layers") — A line read after the title.
- `href`: string — Makes the whole box a link.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Pointer, touch and keys tilt the box.
- `tour`: boolean (default true) — Keyboard focus starts a slow tour round the inside.
- `seed`: number (default 11) — Seeds the ridges, trees and stars.
- `label`: string — The accessible name, if it should say more than the title and caption.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the box at rest and takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "aspect-[5/4] w-full max-w-xs") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- The box is a focusable group (or a link with href) named by its title and caption, with aria-roledescription="shadow box". Keyboard focus starts the tour; arrow keys tilt it, Home levels it, and Escape levels it only when it is tilted, so otherwise Escape reaches the page.
- Under reduced motion the box rests at a fixed three-quarter view that shows its walls and depth; there is no pointer tilt or tour, and arrow keys set a new still view at once.
- Nothing runs at rest. The pointer retargets two springs, the tour's frame runs only while focused and on screen, and the scenery and its blurred shadows are rebuilt only when size, seed, layers or palette change.
- Paper colours are pigments, the same on light and dark pages; the frame defaults to ink on the page's tone, so it is near-black on a light page and gallery white on a dark one.
- The box sits in from its root by as far as its outside walls can swing, so a full tilt never paints outside the component; deeper boxes sit a little smaller.

### Droplet Swap (KQ-1628) — `droplet-swap`
A rolling drop carries the next image across.

A gallery whose transition is a drop of water. A drop rolls across the picture with the next one inside it, small and upside down as a ball lens shows it, its view sliding the other way as it moves, with a dark meniscus, a highlight, a cast shadow and a caustic, squashing along its path with speed and leaving a wet trail that dries. - `interval`: number (default 0) — ms between automatic swaps, 0 for none. Held while hovered, focused, hidden or off screen.
- `loop`: boolean (default true) — Wrap from the last picture to the first and back.
- `indicators`: boolean (default true) — Show a dot per picture to choose it.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion the bead rests still and a swap is a 240ms cross-fade; a drag still moves the drop under the finger and a long enough pull cross-fades the next picture in.
- Nothing runs at rest: the loop runs only while a drop rolls, is dragged or bursts, and the geometry is written to SVG attributes, never to React state per frame. Automatic swaps wait while the gallery is hovered, focused, hidden or off screen.

### Graph Horizon (KQ-1630) — `graph-horizon`
Graph paper rolling to the horizon, plotted as it comes.

A strip of graph paper running to a horizon in perspective, its minor and major lines rolling toward you, plotted as it comes: a pen per series rides a rail halfway out and swings to each value as the paper passes, so every series is drawn in its own lane as a curve on the paper. As each sample reaches the reading line near the bottom, the curve there lifts off the paper toward you on the settle of springs.snap, a quick rise, a held peak and the faintest dip, with its shadow left on the paper and its values printed beside it, then lays back down. - `format`: (value: number, series: GraphHorizonSeries) => string — How a reading is printed; by default one decimal and the series' unit.
- `playing / defaultPlaying`: boolean (default true) — Whether the paper is rolling, controlled or initial.
- `onPlayingChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Fires from the key or the step that started or stopped the roll.

### Snow Drive (KQ-1631) — `snow-drive`
Headlights into falling snow, the oldest warp.

Driving at night into falling snow, in Canvas 2D: every flake is a point in 3D falling at its own rate, swaying on its own phase, pushed by the wind and coming at you at the car's speed, and it is lit only by the headlights, so flakes appear out of the dark as they enter the beams and vanish at their edges, far ones points, near ones soft discs, each streaking from where it was one exposure ago. Reflector posts flash past on a snow-covered road, the beams glow in the snowy air, and a few flakes land on the windscreen and melt. - `boost`: number (default 2.8) — How much faster the car goes while held, 1 to 4 times the cruise.
- `wind`: number (default 0.25) — The crosswind, -1 (from the right) to 1 (from the left).

- `glass`: boolean (default true) — Let a few flakes land on the windscreen and melt.
- `speedometer`: boolean (default true) — Show the speed in the corner.

- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Pointer and keys drive.
- `onBoostChange`: (boosting: boolean) => void — Fires from the press or key that starts or ends a burst of speed.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content over the scene, in a layer of its own whose tokens are the dark theme's.
- `label`: string (default "Night drive in falling snow") — Names the scene for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds the snow.

### Harmonic Bands (KQ-1632) — `harmonic-bands`
Waves of colour you tune like a chord.

Layered strata of colour whose top edges are one travelling wave, the sum of a few harmonics of a fundamental, each tuned by a small vertical fader beneath; every band trails the one above by a phase lag, and dispersion decides whether the shape travels rigidly or keeps re-forming as each harmonic runs at its own speed. A change morphs the shape band by band on the glide spring, each lower band taking the new target a cascade step after the one above, while the palette slides with the spectrum from pale for a pure fundamental to deep when the upper harmonics lead. The faders follow a drag 1:1, rubber-band past either end and settle on snap with the release velocity, press on flick, and take the arrow, Page, Home and End keys.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/harmonic-bands`

Props:
- `harmonics`: number (default 4) — How many harmonics shape the wave, and so how many faders sit beneath it, 2 to 6.
- `palette`: "dusk" | "tide" | "ember" | "moss" | string[] (default "dusk") — The colours the bands are drawn from, pale to deep: a preset, or two to eight CSS colours of your own.
- `flow`: number (default 1) — How fast the waves travel across the frame, 0 (held still) to 2.
- `value / defaultValue`: number[] (default [1, 0.45, 0.2, 0.1, 0.06, 0.03]) — Each harmonic's level, 0 to 1, fundamental first; controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number[]) => void — Fires from the fader or key that changed a level, with every level.
- `bands`: number (default 5) — How many strata of colour are stacked, 3 to 8.
- `amplitude`: number (default 0.6) — How tall the crests stand, 0 (flat strata) to 1 (crests reaching the band above).
- `cycles`: number (default 1.25) — How many waves of the fundamental span the frame, 0.5 to 3.
- `dispersion`: number (default 0.4) — 0 moves the whole shape rigidly; 1 lets every harmonic run at its own deep-water speed, so the shape keeps re-forming.
- `lag`: number (default 0.35) — How far each lower band trails the one above, in phase and in the morph's cascade, 0 to 1.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.5) — The sheen on each crest and the shading toward each band's foot, 0 (flat pigment) to 1.
- `controls`: boolean (default true) — Show the row of faders beneath the bands. Off, it is a display driven by value.
- `label`: string (default "Harmonics") — The fader row's accessible name.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the waves still.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds each harmonic's starting phase.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The faders stop answering; they stay focusable and say so.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the panel.

Notes:
- Each fader is a vertical role="slider" with a spoken value ("Third harmonic, 20%"): Up or Right raises it 5 points, Down or Left lowers it, Shift moves 20, Page Up and Page Down 25, Home and End go to 0 and 100. The row is a group named by label.
- A drag follows the finger 1:1 over the fader's height, rubber-bands past either end and settles on the snap spring; the faders are touch-action pan-x, so a vertical drag never scrolls the page. A tap jumps to the tapped level.
- Canvas 2D: the loop runs only while the waves flow or a spring is still settling, only on screen and with the tab visible; with flow at 0 or paused a settled panel is one frame. Gradients are rebuilt only when the colours change, and the device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
- Under reduced motion the flow stops at its first frame and a new chord is drawn at once, colour and all; the fader fills move on a short tween.
- Palettes are pigment: each stop takes a token's hue at a fixed lightness, so the strata look the same on light and dark pages and follow your accent. Pass any CSS colours as palette to use your own.

### Tally Facets (KQ-1633) — `tally-facets`
Pick a value; every other count answers.

A faceted sidebar beside a results list where every value carries a live count and a slim count bar, counted disjunctively so a facet's own picks never zero its siblings. Picking a value flicks its check in on springs.flick and, in the same frame, every other facet's bars glide to their new lengths on springs.glide while their counts roll; values that would now return nothing dim and sink to the foot of their group on glide, and results leave on the exit ease while the rest close up and returning rows rise in a cascade. Arrow keys walk every value in the order you see it, Space toggles, and below a 560px container the facets fold into a modal sheet whose buttons carry the live result count.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tally-facets`

Props:
- `facets`: TallyFacet[] (default defaultTallyFacets) — The facets in order: { id, label, values?, badge? }. Values omitted are read from the rows, largest first; a badge facet shows as a pill on each result.
- `rows`: TallyRow[] (default defaultTallyRows) — The records counted and listed: { id, title, code, amount, at, facets } where facets maps facet id to value id.
- `value / defaultValue`: Record<string, string[]> (default — / {}) — Picked value ids by facet id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (selection) => void — Fires with the whole selection after every pick, clear or chip removal.
- `onChange`: (change: { facetId, valueId, selected, selection }) => void — Fires once per decision with the value that changed and whether it is now picked.
- `onClear`: () => void — Fires when Clear empties the selection.
- `onSaveView`: (selection) => void — Fires from Save view with the current selection; the button only shows when this is passed.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading stripes every bar and skeletons the results; error keeps the last counts, hatched, under a Retry banner.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after a failed refresh.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Facet row height (26, 30 or 36px) and type size.
- `barStyle`: "bar" | "line" | "fill" (default "bar") — How a count is drawn: a slim bar under the label, a hairline rule, or a wash behind the whole row.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Checks, bars, chips and the live count, any CSS colour.
- `sinkEmpty`: boolean (default true) — Values that would return nothing sink to the foot of their group.
- `now`: number (default defaultTallyNow) — Today in ms, for the "3d ago" on each result; never read from the clock during render.
- `formatAmount`: (amount: number) => string (default whole US dollars) — Formats each result's amount.
- `title`: string (default "Orders") — The heading over the results and the surface's accessible name.
- `itemLabel`: { one: string; other: string } (default { one: "order", other: "orders" }) — What one result is called, in counts and announcements.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px; the facets and the results scroll inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be picked, cleared or saved; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the facet list is one tab stop (roving tabindex). Up and Down walk every value in the order it is drawn, sunk values included, across groups; Home and End jump; Space or Enter toggles. Each value is a role="checkbox" named with its count ("North, 19 orders"), and empty values add "no matches" and aria-disabled. The result count is announced politely from the pick that changed it.
- Below a 560px container the sidebar folds into a sheet behind a Filters button that shows how many values are picked. The sheet is a modal dialog: focus moves in and is trapped, Escape closes it and returns focus to the button, and its footer button reads the live result count.
- Reduced motion: no glide, sink or rise — bars and counts jump to their new values, empty values dim and move instantly, the sheet fades in place and the loading stripes hold still. Counts and the result total still change, because they are the information.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. Bars are scaleX transforms and counts are motion values rendered as text, so a pick costs one React render and no per-frame renders. Sinking uses CSS order, so DOM order and keyboard focus never move under the visitor. The loading stripes run only while loading and on screen.
- Counting is disjunctive: values in one facet are OR'd, facets are AND'd, and a facet's counts ignore its own picks. Bars measure against each facet's unfiltered maximum, so they only shrink as filters narrow, with a hairline tick at the unfiltered length.

### Sieve Stack (KQ-1634) — `sieve-stack`
See exactly which filter is costing you rows.

Active filters stacked as layers above a work-order table, each applied to what survived the layers above it, so every bar shows exactly what its filter costs: the rows it lets through as a solid fill, the rows it removes as a shaded band, bare track for what earlier layers took. Switching a layer off collapses its band and the returning rows pour back down the stack, every layer beneath widening on springs.glide a stagger after the one above while the table admits them in a cascade; the switch thumb snaps on springs.snap. A grip drags a layer 1:1 with its neighbours sliding aside on glide and the release settling with the throw's velocity, and Alt+Arrow moves a layer from any of its controls while Delete removes it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sieve-stack`

Props:
- `filters / defaultFilters`: SieveFilter[] (default — / defaultSieveFilters) — The filters in the order they are applied, controlled or initial: { id, label, field, op, value, active? } with op is, not, in, gte, lte or within (days from now).
- `onFiltersChange`: (filters) => void — Fires with every filter after a switch, reorder or removal.
- `rows`: SieveRow[] (default defaultSieveRows) — The records the stack sieves: { id, ...fields }.
- `columns`: SieveColumn[] (default defaultSieveColumns) — The table's columns: { id, header, kind?: code | text | tag | due, hideBelow?: none | sm | md | lg, sub? }.
- `onToggle`: (id, active, filters) => void — Fires from the switch or key that turned a layer on or off.
- `onReorder`: (ids, filters) => void — Fires from the drop or Alt+Arrow that moved a layer, with the new order.
- `onRemove`: (id, filters) => void — Fires from the button or Delete key that removed a layer.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the rows have arrived; the stack keeps its shape in every state.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the rows failed to load.
- `bandStyle`: "hatch" | "tint" | "dashed" (default "hatch") — How the rows a layer removes are drawn: diagonal hatching, a flat wash, or a dashed outline.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Layer height (36, 44 or 52px; shorter on phones) and table row padding.
- `palette`: "ink" | "cobalt" | "ember" | "moss" (default "cobalt") — The hue of the surviving fill and the removed band; ember and moss are fixed-lightness pigments so they read the same in both themes.
- `pourStagger`: number (default 70) — Delay per layer, ms, as returning rows pour down the stack.
- `now`: number (default defaultSieveNow) — Today in ms, for due dates and the within operator.
- `title`: string (default "Work orders") — The heading over the stack and the surface's accessible name.
- `itemLabel`: { one: string; other: string } (default { one: "work order", other: "work orders" }) — What one row is called, in counts and announcements.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px; the table scrolls inside it under a sticky header.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No switching, moving or removing; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: every layer has a grip button, a role="switch" named with what it removes ("Priority high or urgent, removes 13, 10 work orders remain") and a remove button. Alt+ArrowUp/Down on any of them moves the layer and keeps focus on that control; ArrowUp/Down on the grip also move it; ArrowUp/Down on a switch walk to the neighbouring switch; Delete or Backspace removes the layer and focus lands on a neighbour. Every change is announced politely.
- Reduced motion: no pour cascade, no glide and no row rise — bands and fills reach their new widths in one short tween, rows appear in place, and a dragged layer still follows the finger but lands without a spring. The counts still change.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. Reorders are FLIPs on per-layer motion values (DOM order follows the visual order, focus is restored after the move), counts are motion values rendered as text, and a drag captures the pointer only after 4px so a tap on the grip is still a tap.
- Each layer is applied to what survived the layers above it, so its cost depends on its place: moving a layer re-divides every band. When nothing gets through, the table names the layer whose removal would admit the most rows and offers to switch it off.
- Below a 480px container every layer collapses to one line (grip, switch, label, surviving count) and its bar becomes the row's underlay; the table drops columns by each column's hideBelow and shows a column's sub field instead.

### Prose Filter (KQ-1635) — `prose-filter`
Type what you want; the sentence becomes filters.

One search line that reads a sentence against a typed schema and turns it into field, operator and value chips docked above a results table. A phrase docks when you type the space after it: a ghost of its words rises a step and fades where they stood while the chip starts over them, scaled to their width, and flies to its slot on springs.snap with one crisp overshoot; results close up on springs.glide and arrive in a cascade. Words with more than one reading keep a dotted, dashed or wavy underline, Tab walks them and opens a listbox of meanings under the word, Enter docks the chosen one, and Backspace at the start of the line pulls the last chip back into editable text.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/prose-filter`

Props:
- `schema`: ProseSchema (default defaultProseSchema) — What the line can read: { noun: { one, other, words }, fields } with enum (options with words, optional lead words), money, date (lead words, primary) and code fields.
- `rows`: ProseRow[] (default defaultProseRows) — The records the chips filter: { id, ...fields }.
- `defaultValue`: string (default "") — A sentence read on first render; its finished phrases dock straight away and doubtful words stay in the line.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Try: overdue invoices over 500 from Coldbrook") — The empty line's hint.
- `onQueryChange`: (query: ProseQuery) => void — Fires with { noun, clauses, text, unsure } on first render and whenever a chip docks, leaves, is pulled back or the line changes.
- `onApply`: (query: ProseQuery) => void — Fires from Enter or the apply button, after finished phrases have docked.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the results have arrived: loading shows skeleton rows, error a Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the results failed to load.
- `chipStyle`: "segment" | "soft" | "outline" (default "segment") — Chip look: field, operator and value in three tinted segments, one soft wash pill, or a hairline outline.
- `underlineStyle`: "dotted" | "dashed" | "wavy" (default "dotted") — The underline under words with more than one reading.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Chips, underlines, read-phrase washes and the live count, any CSS colour.
- `now`: number (default defaultProseNow) — Today in ms, for last month, this week, the last N days and month names (always the most recent one).
- `formatAmount`: (amount: number) => string (default whole US dollars) — Formats amounts in chips and rows.
- `maxRows`: number (default 40) — The most rows the table lists; it scrolls inside its box.
- `title`: string (default "Invoices") — The heading before the sentence names its noun; it takes the noun's name once it docks.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The line and the chips are inert; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the line is a real input with role="combobox". A phrase docks on the space after it, Enter docks what is finished and applies, Tab walks the doubtful words once each (opening a listbox of meanings, driven by aria-activedescendant) and then lets focus move on, ArrowUp/Down choose, Enter docks the meaning, Escape closes the list. Backspace at the start of the line pulls the last chip back to edit. Each chip is a button named "Remove Amount over $500"; dock and pull-back are announced politely.
- Reduced motion: no flight and no rising ghost — the chip fades in at its slot while the words leave the line, the meanings list fades without rising, rows appear in place. Underlines, chips and counts all still show.
- Typing, selection, IME, paste and undo stay native: the underlines and washes are painted on a mirror behind a transparent-background input, kept aligned with its scroll by a motion value. Nothing runs at rest; a dock is three short springs on one chip.
- Reading is deterministic and local: the schema's words, comparators (over, under, at least, between N and M), dates against now (UTC) and #numbers. Bare numbers, month names with two date fields, recent, big and large are doubtful and wait for a choice. A newer clause on the same field replaces the older one. readProse and proseMatches are exported for hosts that run the query themselves.
- When nothing matches, the table names the chip whose removal would admit the most rows and offers to remove it.

### Saved Lenses (KQ-1636) — `saved-lenses`
Switch views; only the filters that differ move.

A row of saved views over a chip bar and a results list where switching views is a shared-element move: chips the two views have in common are the same elements and keep their slots, arriving chips take the slots departing ones leave, the differing ones slide out on the exit ease and in on springs.snap a cascade apart, and later chips glide on springs.glide only when a replaced chip is a different width. The tab mark slides on snap. Removing a chip or adding one from Filter makes a draft whose tab earns a modified dot on snap while Save, Save as new and Revert slide in on glide; views are a tablist with arrows, Home and End, and digits 1 to 9 pick a view from anywhere in the surface.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/saved-lenses`

- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires with the new view id from the tab, arrow or digit that chose it.
- `onViewChange`: (view, previous) => void — Fires with the view switched to (including unsaved edits) and the one left.
- `onSaveView`: (view, { asNew }) => void — Fires from Save (asNew false) or Save as new (asNew true) with the saved view.
- `onRevert`: (viewId: string) => void — Fires from Revert with the view whose edits were dropped.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the active view's results have arrived; loading, empty and failed views each get a quiet panel.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed on a failed view.
- `tabStyle`: "underline" | "pill" | "boxed" (default "underline") — How the active tab is marked: an underline, a tinted pill, or a raised box; the mark slides between tabs.
- `chipStyle`: "soft" | "outline" | "solid" (default "soft") — Chip look: a soft wash, a hairline outline, or a solid fill.
- `cornerRadius`: number (default 8) — Corner radius of chips, tabs, the menu and buttons, px (0 to 16).
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The tab mark, chips and Save, any CSS colour.
- `now`: number (default defaultLensNow) — Today in ms, for due dates.
- `me`: string (default "Ines Park") — Whose queue this is: an assignee chip with this value reads "Me".
- `title`: string (default "Support queue") — The heading over the views and the surface's accessible name.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px; the results scroll inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Views, chips and actions are inert; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the views are a role="tablist" with one tab stop; Left and Right move and select, Home and End jump, and digits 1 to 9 select view n from anywhere in the surface except a text field. Each tab says when it is edited. Chips are buttons named "Remove Account is Fernworks" (Delete or Backspace also remove), Filter is a menu button whose role="menu" takes focus, walks with the arrows and closes on Escape back to the button. Switches, edits and saves are announced politely.
- Reduced motion: chips cross-fade in place (shared chips never move anyway), the tab mark and the modified dot appear without travel, rows fade in. Counts and contents still change.
- Performance: no loop. A switch is one layout pass: shared chips keep their keys, so they are the same DOM nodes and do not animate at all; the strip's fade edges are CSS variables driven by motion values from scroll, never React state per frame.
- Edits are drafts per view: switching away keeps a draft and its tab's dot, Save writes it back, Save as new names a copy (inline field, Enter saves, Escape cancels) and selects it, Revert drops it. A new value for a field replaces that field's chip in its slot.
- Narrow surfaces turn the tabs into a horizontally scrolling strip with a fade on whichever edge has more, and keep the chosen tab in view without scrolling the page.

### Brushed Windows (KQ-1637) — `brushed-windows`
Cut several time windows out of one busy month.

A density ribbon of a month of events above an event list, where dragging across the ribbon cuts a frosted window that follows the pointer 1:1 and you may cut as many as you need, overlapping cuts joining. On release the window's edges settle onto bin boundaries on springs.snap with the drag's velocity, its soft handles swell in on snap, a chip for it pops into the row below, and the list regroups on springs.glide with one heading per window while rows outside every window fold away. Handles resize and the body moves a window 1:1; touch starts a cut with a long press; the ribbon is a slider cursor whose Enter cuts a day, and a focused window moves with the arrows, resizes with Shift and goes with Delete.

- `onWindowsChange`: (windows) => void — Fires with every window, in time order and with ids, after a cut, move, resize, merge or removal.
- `now`: number (default defaultGaugeNow) — The end of the period in ms; the ribbon shows the days before it. Never read from the clock during render.
- `days`: number (default 30) — How many days the ribbon spans.
- `binSize`: number (default 6) — Hours per bin, 1 to 24: the ribbon's grain and the step windows snap to and keys move by.
- `frostLevel`: number (default 0.5) — How frosted a window's glass is, 0 (clear, tinted) to 1 (deep frost).
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Windows, the density inside them, chips and the live count, any CSS colour.
- `maxWindows`: number (default 6) — Most windows at once; a cut past it replaces the oldest.
- `rowsPerWindow`: number (default 5) — Rows shown under each window's heading before Show all.
- `longPressMs`: number (default 380) — How long a touch must hold before it starts a window, so a swipe still scrolls.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws a skeleton ribbon and rows; error keeps the ribbon's shape with a Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the events failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Gaugeworks events") — The heading over the ribbon and the surface's accessible name.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px; the list scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No cutting, moving or removing; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the ribbon is a role="slider" cursor over the period ("Sep 28, 06:00, 7 events"): Left and Right move a bin, Page Up and Page Down a day, Home and End jump, Enter or Space cuts a one-day window there and moves focus into it. A window is a focusable group: the arrows move it a bin, Shift with an arrow resizes its end, Alt and Shift its start, Delete or Backspace removes it and returns focus to the ribbon, Escape returns to the ribbon. Chips focus their window; their x removes it. Every change is announced politely.
- Touch: the ribbon uses touch-action pan-y, and a cut starts only after a long press (longPressMs), so a vertical swipe scrolls the page and a quick horizontal swipe does nothing; after the hold a seed window appears under the finger and the drag draws it out.
- Reduced motion: edges land on their bins without overshoot, handles appear, chips fade in and the list regroups without gliding. A window still follows the pointer during a cut: that is direct manipulation, not decoration.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. The ribbon's two paths are rebuilt only when the events, period or bin size change; window edges are motion values written 1:1 during a drag, so a drag causes no React render per frame; backdrop blur is limited to the window panes. The ribbon keeps its full width down to 316px, its labels thinning to one a week.
- A stretch of a day and a half with no events is drawn as a flat dashed calm line labelled quiet, rather than a gap, so a refit or an outage reads as information.

A filter tree of regions, crews and people with tri-state ticks and a summary that says the choice in words ("All of Coldbrook crew, 2 of Basinworks crew"). - `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be dragged, typed or saved; the editor dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the threshold handle is a role="slider" whose value text carries the would-have-alerted count. Up or Right nudge one step, Down or Left one step down, Shift with an arrow or Page Up and Page Down move ten, Home and End go to the axis ends. Comparison and duration are radiogroups (arrows), the channel is a native select, and the threshold is also a number field. Markers are one tab stop: arrows walk them, Enter opens a card with the fire time and peak, Escape closes it.
- Fires are worked out from the series, not stored: a breach is a run of readings past the line that fires once, duration minutes after it starts, if it is still past the line then; a gap in the data ends a run. The same function is exported as findTripwireFires, so a host can show the count elsewhere.
- Reduced motion: the line jumps to its value, markers fade in and out in place with no drop or lift, the count updates without rolling, and pills cross-fade. The recolouring past the line, the wash, the markers and the count still change, because they are the information.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. A drag writes one motion value that the handle, the clip rect and the wash read; React renders only when the stepped value changes. The chart is one stretched SVG with non-scaling strokes and the plot width is measured by a ResizeObserver bound to the node when it arrives.
- States: loading keeps the axes and the rule editable; a failed load keeps the draft under a Retry banner; a failed save says so inline and leaves the draft untouched. Below a 544px container the form drops under the chart and the body scrolls inside the editor.

### Heartbeat Ledger (KQ-1650) — `heartbeat-ledger`
Scheduled jobs that check in, and the ones that don't.

A monitor for scheduled jobs that check in: each row is a job, its owner, a strip of recent check-ins drawn as slim bars whose height is the run's length (on time, late, failed, and a hatched slot wherever a run never arrived) and its next deadline. A new check-in drops into the head of its strip on springs.recoil while the strip rolls one slot left on springs.glide; past its deadline a job wears a ring that runs down its grace on a linear tween between readings of the now prop, and if the grace runs out the row tips into a warning tint that sweeps in on glide while its dot turns into a warning glyph on springs.snap. It is a role="grid" with one roving cell: arrows move, P pauses, M mutes, Enter opens the last run, and Enter on a strip steps into it to pick an older run.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/heartbeat-ledger`

Props:

- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Row height and bar size.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — On-time ticks, grace rings and the clock, any CSS colour.
- `jobs`: HeartbeatJob[] (default defaultHeartbeatJobs) — The jobs: { id, name, schedule, every, grace, lastCheckIn?, owner, beats, typical? } with beats { id, at, status, duration } oldest first.
- `now`: number (default defaultHeartbeatNow) — The time every deadline is judged against, in ms; the host advances it and the clock is never read.
- `paused / defaultPaused`: string[] (default — / []) — Paused job ids, controlled or initial.
- `onPause`: (job: HeartbeatJob, paused: boolean) => void — Fires from the button or the P key, with whether the job is now paused.
- `muted / defaultMuted`: string[] (default — / []) — Muted job ids, controlled or initial.
- `onMute`: (job: HeartbeatJob, muted: boolean) => void — Fires from the button or the M key, with whether the job's alerts are now muted.
- `onOpenRun`: (job: HeartbeatJob, beat: HeartbeatBeat | null) => void — A run was opened: Enter or a press on the job, or a beat picked in its strip; null when the job has never run.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws skeleton rows with ghost strips; error shows its own state with Retry; an empty jobs list has its own state too.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after the check-ins failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Fernworks nightly") — The heading and the grid's accessible name.
- `formatTime`: (ms: number) => string (default HH:MM in UTC) — Formats the clock, deadlines and beat times.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px; rows scroll under the pinned header.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be paused, muted or opened; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: a role="grid" with one roving cell. Arrows move between cells and rows (hidden columns are skipped at narrow widths), Home and End go to the row's ends and Ctrl with Home or End to the corners. P pauses or resumes the focused job, M mutes it, Enter on the job opens its last run. Enter on a history strip steps into it: Left and Right pick a run (each is announced), Enter opens it, Escape steps back out.
- Time is a prop. The component never reads the clock: pass now and advance it (a second at a time is enough; the grace ring tweens between readings). Missed runs are derived, not stored: any gap between check-ins longer than every plus grace is drawn as a hatched slot, and a job past its grace grows a pending one at the head of its strip that keeps its place when the late check-in lands.
- Reduced motion: beats appear in place with a short fade and the strip re-seats without gliding, the ring and the warning tint jump to their state, and the warning glyph fades in. Every count, deadline and colour still changes.
- Performance: there is no loop of its own. Motion happens only when now or jobs change, the grace ring tweens only while the ledger is on screen, and strips are absolutely placed slots moved by transform. A lapse is announced once, politely, from the render that sees it.
- Helpers for hosts and tests: heartbeatRun, heartbeatBeats and heartbeatJobAt turn a seeded HeartbeatPlan into the beats it would have produced by a given time, which is how the demo replays a night.

Notes:

### Probe Relay (KQ-1652) — `probe-relay`
Check an endpoint from six stations at once.

A synthetic check runner: six stations sit on a ring round the endpoint, each joined to it by a path that bows the same way, and each holds its last latency for the active check with a slim bar against the budget. Run now sends a pulse from every station to the target at once on the move ease; while the results are out the paths turn dotted and march, and when they land a pulse returns to each station taking time in proportion to its latency, so the fastest hear back first, and each number lands at its station on springs.recoil, coloured against the budget, while its bar glides on springs.glide. Checks are a tablist, every station is its own tab stop with a details card, and R reruns the active check from anywhere inside.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/probe-relay`

Props:
- `pathCurve`: number (default 0.45) — How much the paths bow, from 0 (straight spokes) to 1 (deep curves).
- `pulseSpeed`: number (default 1) — Scales every travel time: 2 is twice as quick, 0.5 half.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Pulses, the target and the active check, any CSS colour.
- `stations`: ProbeStation[] (default defaultProbeStations) — The stations, drawn round the target from the top: { id, name, region, code }.
- `checks`: ProbeCheck[] (default defaultProbeChecks) — The checks: { id, name, method, path, host, budget, every, paused?, ranAt, results } with results { station, latency (null when failed), error? }.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default — / the first check) — The active check id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the tab, arrow or key that changed the active check.
- `onRun`: (check: ProbeCheck) => void — Run now or R was pressed. Answer by updating the check's ranAt and results; the pulses return when they change.
- `onPause`: (check: ProbeCheck, paused: boolean) => void — Pause or Resume was pressed, with the new paused state.
- `onEdit`: (check: ProbeCheck) => void — Edit was pressed.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading draws dotted paths and ghost checks; error shows its own state with Retry.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after the checks failed to load.
- `now`: number (default defaultProbeNow) — The time "ran 2m ago" is measured from, in ms; never read from the clock.
- `formatLatency`: (ms: number) => string (default "184 ms" or "1.2 s") — Formats every latency and the budget.
- `title`: string (default "Waylight API") — The heading and the surface's accessible name.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing runs, pauses or edits; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the checks are a role="tablist" with roving focus (arrows in either direction, Home and End) that activates as it moves; each station is its own tab stop, named with its latency against the budget or its error, and opens a details card that Escape closes, returning focus. R reruns the active check from anywhere inside the surface. A finished run is announced once: how many stations were within budget and which failed.
- Results are data: onRun only asks. The host runs the check and updates its ranAt and results; each station keeps its old number until its own pulse lands, so readings change in latency order. A host that never answers does not leave the run spinning: it gives up after twelve seconds.
- Reduced motion: no pulse travels. The paths are dotted but still while a run is out, numbers fade to their new value and bars set without gliding; colours and the announcement still say what happened.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. Pulses animate one motion value each for the length of a run and only while the surface is on screen (off screen the results land at once); the dotted march runs only while waiting. Geometry is measured with a ResizeObserver and every coordinate is rounded.
- Below a 544px container the ring becomes a list of stations with latency bars and a budget mark, and the checks become a horizontal tab row with an edge fade.

- `rota / defaultRota`: Rota (default — / defaultRota) — The rota, controlled or initial: { people: { id, name, color }[], layers: { id, label, shifts }[], overrides }.
- `onRotaChange`: (rota: Rota) => void — Fires from the override or swap that changed the rota, with the whole rota.
- `onOverride`: (override: RotaOverride) => void — An override was added: { id, layer, person, start, end }.
- `onSwap`: (a: RotaShift, b: RotaShift) => void — Two shifts traded people; a and b as they are after the swap.
- `onPage`: (person: RotaPerson, segment: RotaSegment) => void — Page was pressed (or P) for the person on the selected segment.
- `now`: number (default defaultRotaNow) — The current time in ms; the hand points at it. Never read from the clock.
- `weekStart`: number (default defaultRotaWeekStart) — Monday 00:00 of the week drawn, in ms.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string | null (default — / the primary segment at now) — The selected segment id, controlled or initial.
- `onSelectedChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the key or press that moved the selection.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the rota has loaded. Loading draws an empty dial; error adds a Retry banner.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after the rota failed to load.
- `team`: string (default "Gaugeworks platform") — The team, in the header and the grid's name.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the rota in px; its body scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be overridden, swapped or paged.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the dial (or the linear schedule) is a role="grid" with one tab stop and aria-activedescendant: rows are layers, cells are segments named in one sentence ("Primary, Ravi Okonjo, Wed 09:00–18:00, on call now"). Left and Right walk the week, Up and Down move to the same time on the next layer, Home and End jump, O opens the override form (a dialog whose Escape returns focus to the grid), S swaps with the next shift, P pages.
- Coverage is worked out, not stored: rotaSegments(layer, overrides, weekStart) is exported and returns each layer's week as contiguous shift, override and gap segments, with later overrides winning. Use it to show who is on call anywhere else in your app.
- Colours: each person carries a CSS colour for their wedges. They are filled shapes, so pass pigments that read in both themes (the defaults are token hues at a fixed lightness, e.g. oklch(from var(--signal) 0.8 0.11 h)); initials sit on them in dark ink.
- Reduced motion: the hand jumps to the hour, a new override fades in where it lands with no slide, and the selection is an outline with no lift. Colours, names and the now list still change.
- Performance: no timers in the component. The dial is static SVG with rounded coordinates; the hand is one motion value driving its endpoints, and the pulse on its tip plays once per change of now. Below a 480px container the dial is swapped for a linear schedule by container query, so there is no layout flash.

### Ghost Rows (KQ-1656) — `ghost-rows`
Hover a template and watch the table fill.

An empty table with three ways in — import a file, connect a source, or start from a template — whose templates preview themselves in place: pointing at one, or focusing it, re-heads the table with its columns and pours its sample rows in one by one, each dropping from 12px above on springs.snap a cascade apart and settling faint with dashed rules, and moving on drains them last row first on the exit ease. - Imports: the hidden file input and drops on the table both call onImport(file); the component never reads the file. Feed back progress through importState and, on failure, a plain-words error ("Row 14 has 9 columns; the header has 7") with Choose another file.
- Reduced motion: ghosts appear in place without the drop, drain without travel, and the solid wave is a single cross-fade; the ways in collapse without the glide. Rows, columns, counts and the progress value still change.

### Open Day (KQ-1657) — `open-day`

- `onDismiss`: (suggestion: DaySuggestion) => void — A suggestion was dismissed (its × or Delete).
- `onRemove`: (block: DayBlock) => void — A placed block was removed; its suggestion goes back beside the day.

Notes:

- Drag: the card is captured only after 4px, so a tap still places it at the next free hour. The held block is drawn in a layer over the whole surface, so it can leave the suggestion rail or row; the slot is snapped to the step and moved on to the next free time that fits. touch-action is pan-x in the phone row (so the row still scrolls) and pan-y beside the column.
- Reduced motion: no tuck, no drop and no stretch — a released or Enter-placed block fades in at its time, and the empty message changes size and place without travel. Times, the open count and the message's words still change.
- States: loading shows a skeleton column and cards; a rejected onPlace (or status="error") keeps the blocks on the day, dashed and marked unsaved in their names, under a Retry banner that calls onRetry and saves them again.
- Performance: no loops or timers at rest. A drag writes four motion values (position and size of the held block); React renders only when the snapped slot changes. Geometry is measured once at the start of a drag, not per frame.

### Offline Shelf (KQ-1659) — `offline-shelf`

Resolving means the server answered (flip status to "online"); rejecting — or returning nothing — counts as a failed attempt and the next wait comes from retryDelays. Each failure, each manual check and the reconnection are announced politely as one sentence; the seconds are never read out per tick.

A switch that differs from the workspace default carries a mark that pops in on springs.flick, and Reset to defaults runs every edited switch back as one diagonal run. It is a real grid with one roving tab stop — arrows, Home and End, Ctrl with Home or End, Space to toggle, Delete to reset — onChange and onReset fire per cell, and below 760px each event becomes a card of channel chips.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ping-matrix`

Props:
- `events`: PingMatrixEvent[] (default defaultPingMatrixEvents) — The rows, { id, label, description? }: what can happen.
- `channels`: PingMatrixChannel[] (default defaultPingMatrixChannels) — The columns, { id, label }: where it can reach you.
- `value / defaultValue`: Record<string, Record<string, boolean>> (default — / defaultPingMatrixValue) — On or off for every event and channel (value[eventId][channelId]), controlled or initial; the initial value also counts as saved.
- `onValueChange`: (value: PingMatrixValue) => void — Fires with every preference after each cell changes, run cells included.
- `defaults`: PingMatrixValue (default defaultPingMatrixDefaults) — The workspace's defaults; a cell that differs carries the edited mark and says what the default is.
- `onChange`: (eventId: string, channelId: string, on: boolean) => void — One cell changed — per cell, also as a column's run reaches it.
- `onReset`: (eventId: string, channelId: string) => void — One cell went back to the workspace default — per cell, from Delete or Reset to defaults.
- `onSave`: (value: PingMatrixValue) => void | Promise<unknown> — Save was pressed. Return a promise to show it saving; a rejection keeps the edits and says so.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" (default "ready") — Loading draws switch skeletons, makes the headings inert and marks the grid aria-busy.
- `switchStyle`: "pill" | "check" | "dot" (default "pill") — A track whose knob slides on snap, a box whose tick draws on flick, or a ring whose core grows on snap.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Row height and how much is said: 40, 52 or 64px rows; compact hides the descriptions.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The colour of a switch that is on, the edited marks and the column meters. Any CSS colour.
- `title`: string (default "Notifications") — The heading and the grid's accessible name.
- `workspace`: string (default "Basinworks") — Whose defaults these are, in the copy and the switches' names.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 548) — Tallest the surface grows before its body scrolls inside, px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be changed or saved; the surface dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop with roving focus across the channel headings and the switches. Arrows move, Home and End reach a row's ends, Ctrl or Cmd with Home or End the corners, Space or Enter toggles a switch or runs a column, and Delete or Backspace puts a switch back to the workspace default.
- Each cell is a role="switch" named like "Email for Mentions" — plus ", changed from the Basinworks default (off)" when it carries the mark. Column runs, resets and save results are announced politely as one sentence each; single toggles are left to the switch's own state.
- onChange and onReset fire per cell, in the order the run reaches them, so a host can save cell by cell; onValueChange gets the whole value after each one. A failed onSave keeps every edit and says so beside Save.
- Reduced motion: nothing tips; switches change in the same order with their colours, and marks fade. Performance: nothing runs at rest; a run is a few motion animations and timers, all stopped on unmount, and the skeletons breathe only while loading.
- Layout follows the container: from 47.5rem (760px) it is a table with a sticky heading row; below it each event becomes a card of channel chips in two columns from 34rem and one below that, and the headings become a chip bar.

### Hazard Shelf (KQ-1663) — `hazard-shelf`
Irreversible settings, with their consequences in full.

The irreversible end of a workspace's settings, where opening an action unrolls a caution-striped panel like a blind off a roll: its height runs to the measured size on springs.glide while a striped roll rides the leading edge, its stripes turning and its thickness thinning as it pays out, then each consequence count fills in from zero a cascade step apart. Typing the workspace name lights each matched letter with an underline drawn on springs.flick and a full match sweeps the confirm button's fill in on springs.snap; Escape, Cancel or opening another action rolls the panel up on the exit ease. Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/hazard-shelf`

- `onArchive`: () => void | Promise<unknown> — Fires after a confirmed archive; may return a promise.
- `onDelete`: () => void | Promise<unknown> — Fires after a confirmed delete; may return a promise.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the consequence counts have arrived. Loading shows placeholders and error offers Count again; nothing can be confirmed until they are in.

Notes:

An unarmed confirm stays focusable (aria-disabled) and sends focus back to the missing step.
- Reduced motion: the panel appears at its height with the roll still, counts show their final figures at once, matched letters and the armed fill change colour without drawing. Every state still shows.
- Callbacks fire only after confirmation. Return a promise to show the action pending; a rejection keeps the panel open and names what was not done, e.g. "Fernworks was not deleted. 412 documents, 18 members and 3 integrations are unchanged.", with the error's own message appended.
- Theming: stripes, the roll and the armed button take the tone token's hue at a fixed lightness, so a large band never turns to mud on a light page; sentences and icons keep the plain text tokens.
- Performance: no loop. Height, the roll and its stripe offset are motion values driven by one animation; counts are motion values rendered as text. The shelf scrolls inside its own box and brings an opening panel into view there, never the page.

### Chord Recorder (KQ-1664) — `chord-recorder`
Press the keys you want, and see what clashes.

A keyboard shortcut editor whose bindings become recording wells: every key pressed drops in as a keycap from above the rim on springs.snap, lit and pressed down while it is held, and the first key that is not a modifier completes the chord. A taken chord tints the well and nudges the row that owns it sideways on springs.snap, offering Swap, which trades the two bindings and drops both rows' keys in afresh. Enter starts recording, Escape cancels, Backspace clears, Up and Down walk the bindings, and modifier labels follow the platform.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/chord-recorder`

Props:
- `commands`: ChordCommand[] (default defaultChordCommands) — The commands, grouped by area: { id, label, area, binding, defaultBinding?, description? }. Bindings are platform-neutral strings such as "Mod+Shift+K" (Mod is Command on a Mac, Control elsewhere).
- `value / defaultValue`: Record<string, string | null> (default — / each command's binding) — Bindings by command id, controlled or initial; null is no shortcut.
- `onValueChange`: (bindings: Record<string, string | null>) => void — Fires with every binding after a record, clear, swap or reset.
- `onBind`: (id: string, binding: string | null) => void — A command got a new shortcut, or lost it (null).
- `onSwap`: (id: string, otherId: string, binding: string) => void — A clash was settled by swapping: id took binding and otherId took what id had.
- `onReset`: (id: string | null) => void — Reset was pressed for one command, or Reset all (null).
- `platform`: "auto" | "mac" | "other" (default "auto") — Which modifier labels to draw: glyphs on a Mac, words elsewhere. Auto reads the platform after mount, so server and first render agree.
- `defaultQuery`: string (default "") — Text in the search field at first.
- `requireModifier`: boolean (default true) — A chord needs Command, Control or Option/Alt unless it is a function key; a bare key is refused with a note.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the shortcuts have loaded; loading shows skeleton rows and error offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the shortcuts failed to load.
- `keycapStyle`: "raised" | "flat" | "outline" (default "raised") — Keycap look: a raised key with a lip, a flat tile, or a hairline outline.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Row height, keycap size and type size.
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "amber" | "graphite" | string (default "cobalt") — Lit keys, the recording well and search marks: a named token or any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click as each key lands, a lower one when a chord commits or clashes.
- `title`: string (default "Keyboard shortcuts") — The heading and the editor's accessible name.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the editor, px; the list scrolls inside under sticky area headings.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Bindings cannot be recorded, cleared or reset; the editor dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer editor.

Notes:
- Keyboard: every binding is a button named with its command and spoken chord. Enter starts recording; while recording, keys are captured (Escape cancels, Backspace or Delete alone clears, Tab leaves and cancels). Up and Down move between bindings, Home and End jump, and Backspace on a binding clears it. A clash moves focus to Swap as its notice arrives; Escape there cancels.
- Reduced motion: keycaps appear in the well without dropping, the clashing row tints instead of sliding aside, and the recording hint stops pulsing. Lit, warn and committed states still show.
- Bindings are stored platform-neutral ("Mod+Shift+K") and drawn per platform: ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ glyphs in Mac order on a Mac, Ctrl/Alt/Shift words elsewhere. Keys are read by physical code, so Option-modified characters and keyboard layouts never change what is recorded. formatChord(binding, mac) prints one for your own copy.
- Sound is off by default and only answers key presses: a click per landing keycap, pitched by its place in the chord.
- Performance: no loop; the list renders plain rows and only the recording well and the clashing row animate. Search filters by label, area, description and the keys themselves.

- Below 30rem the pinned list folds to one line (count, Next and a Show all toggle with aria-expanded) so it never covers more than a row of the form; choosing an item folds it again. Fields pair into two columns from 36rem.
- Nothing runs at rest: one ResizeObserver measures the list, the scroll is a single spring stopped by wheel, touch or unmount, and the rules are exported (checkMendField, findMendProblems) so a host can run the same checks on its server.

### Attendee Rows (KQ-1669) — `attendee-rows`

A registration form whose guests are rows you can add, remove and move.
