### Draft Keeper (KQ-1672) — `draft-keeper`
Your edits are saved, even when someone else edits too.

A long form that keeps itself: edits queue and are sent as one save a moment after your last keystroke, with an indicator that counts the time since; offline edits pile up with a count that rolls on springs.snap, a failed save keeps the queue and offers Retry, and Ctrl or Cmd+S saves at once. When someone else edits a field you have also changed, their avatar drops onto it on springs.recoil and the field splits along its width on springs.glide into yours and theirs, each with the words the other lacks marked; keeping one slides it into the whole field as the other folds away on the exit ease. Tab reaches the choice and the arrows move between its two buttons.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/draft-keeper`

Props:
- `values / defaultValues`: Record<string, string> (default — / defaultDraftValues) — The document, controlled or initial.
- `onValuesChange`: (values) => void — Fires from your edits, kept versions and clean remote edits, with the whole document.
- `fields`: DraftField[] (default defaultDraftFields) — The form: { id, label, kind: "text" | "textarea" | "select" | "date", options?, placeholder?, hint?, wide? }.
- `collaborators`: DraftCollaborator[] (default defaultDraftCollaborators) — Who else is in the document: { id, name, hue }.
- `incoming`: DraftRemoteEdit[] (default []) — Remote edits pushed by the host, { id, field, value, by, at, base? }; each new id is taken once. Yours differing from `base`, or a field you touched, makes a conflict.
- `me`: string (default "You") — Your name, for your avatar in the header.
- `online`: boolean (default true) — Offline, edits queue with a count; coming back sends the queue.
- `onSave`: (values, changed: string[]) => void | Promise<void> — Saves the queued changes. A promise shows Saving; a rejection keeps the queue and offers Retry.
- `onConflict`: (field, yours, theirs, by) => void — Someone else changed a field you had also changed; it has split into two versions.
- `onResolve`: (field, kept: "yours" | "theirs", value) => void — A version was kept.
- `autosaveMs`: number (default 1200) — Quiet time after your last keystroke before an autosave, in ms.
- `lastSaved`: number (default now − 12 s) — When the document was last saved, ms on the `now` clock.
- `now`: number (default defaultDraftNow) — The moment to count from, in ms; never read from the clock during render.
- `indicatorStyle`: "pill" | "dot" | "line" (default "pill") — The save indicator: a bordered pill, a quiet dot, or a line along the panel's top edge that fills while saving. Below 30rem each shrinks to its icon.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Field heights and the room between them.
- `tone`: "neutral" | "paper" | "slate" (default "neutral") — The surface temperature in both themes: plain card, warmed paper or cooled slate, for the panel, fields and version panes.
- `title`: string (default "Waylight 4.2 launch brief") — The form's heading and accessible name.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Panel height in px; the form scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be edited or saved.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer container.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Ctrl or Cmd+S anywhere in the form saves now (the browser's save dialog is prevented). A split field is a group named "Summary has two versions" holding two labelled regions and their Keep buttons; Tab reaches them and the arrows move between the two. If you were in the field when it split, focus moves to Keep yours; after a choice it returns to the field.
- The save indicator's spoken status changes only with its state (saved, saving, offline with the queue, failed with the queue), never per second; the visible time ticks once a second from a timer that runs only while the panel is on screen and the page is shown, slowing to every 15 s after a minute.
- Remote edits are taken in the render that brings them, so a conflict present at first load is drawn on the server too; onConflict and onValuesChange for remote edits are reported once each, after that render.
- Reduced motion: the versions cross-fade in and out with no split travel, avatars appear in place and the saving dot holds still; counts, marks and messages are unchanged.
- Avatars are pigment discs (oklch at a fixed lightness from each collaborator's hue), so they read the same in light and dark themes; the tone tints come from the theme's own surface tokens.

- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Padding, gaps and the title's size.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The caret, filled tokens, Create, the toast and the count's tint; text on it flips light or dark with its lightness.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the frame in px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be created.
- `className`: string — Classes for the frame.

Notes:
- Keyboard: focus starts in the title. @ # + ^ open their list inline (Down and Up move, Enter or Tab picks, Escape dismisses); each token is a button that opens a filter combobox (Enter picks, Escape or Tab closes and returns to the token), and Backspace on a filled token clears it. Enter creates, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter creates and stays.
- It is a modal dialog with the app behind inert: Tab wraps, Escape closes an open list first, then asks "Discard this task?" when text was typed (Escape again keeps writing). Focus returns to New task on close.
- The create is optimistic: the count rises at once and the toast flies; if onCreate rejects, the count rolls back and the draft returns with every field intact and the reason inline. Counts are labelled ("Riverside upgrade, 13 tasks") and every create, failure and discard is announced once.
- Reduced motion: nothing flies — the count updates with a tint, the form cross-fades to its reset state, and a failure fades the draft back.
- Below a 36rem container the sidebar folds into a strip of count chips along the top (the toast flies to those), the dialog fills the width and the tokens wrap to a second line. Nothing runs while the dialog is idle.

### Batch Runner (KQ-1683) — `batch-runner`
Run it on all 248, and see each one land.

A bulk-action dialog that confirms its scope as one small cell per item, then runs inside itself: a soft band glides down the grid a row at a time on springs.glide while each cell under it is stamped done on springs.flick, so every row reads as a ripple, and failures fill red with their reason and never bounce. Escape pauses after the item in flight, Stop leaves the rest untouched, and finishing folds the live counts into one plain sentence with the failures grouped by reason; Retry failed reruns only the red cells. The action is a roving radiogroup and the cells a role="grid" with one tab stop, arrows, Home/End and Page keys.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/batch-runner`

Props:
- `items`: BatchItem[] (default defaultBatchItems) — The selection, in reading order: { id, label, detail?, error?, recovers? } (error and recovers drive the built-in simulation only).
- `actions`: BatchAction[] (default defaultBatchActions) — The actions in the picker: { id, label, past, progressive, description, icon?, targetLabel?, targets? }.
- `action / defaultAction`: string (default — / first action) — The chosen action, controlled or initial.
- `onActionChange`: (action: string) => void — Fires from the press or key that picked another action.
- `run`: (item, { action, target, attempt }) => void | Promise<void> (default simulated) — The work for one item, called one at a time in reading order; a throw or rejection fails it with the error's message as its reason.
- `pace`: number (default 24) — Milliseconds per item for the built-in simulation; a retry takes at least 280ms per item so each can be seen.
- `autoStart`: boolean (default false) — Start the run by itself the first time the dialog scrolls into view.
- `itemLabel`: { one: string; other: string } (default { one: "conversation", other: "conversations" }) — What one item is called, in titles, counts and the summary.
- `source`: string (default "From Open · Coldbrook Support") — Where the selection came from, under the title.
- `onRun`: ({ action, target, ids }) => void — The primary press started the run.
- `onRetry`: (ids: string[]) => void — Retry failed was pressed, with the ids it reruns.
- `onCancel`: (progress: { done, failed, left }) => void — Cancel (before the run) or Stop (during it) was pressed.
- `onPauseChange`: (paused: boolean) => void — The run paused (Escape or Pause) or resumed.
- `onProgress`: (progress: { done, failed, left }) => void — Fires as each item lands, with counts across the whole selection.
- `onComplete`: (summary: BatchSummary) => void — A pass finished or stopped: totals, failures grouped by reason, and whether it was cancelled.
- `onClose`: () => void — Done was pressed, or Escape on the summary.
- `cellShape`: "square" | "round" | "bar" (default "square") — Rounded squares, dots, or tall tally bars that fold the selection into fewer, taller rows.
- `cellSize`: number (default 11) — The largest cell edge in px; cells shrink below it to keep the grid under maxGridHeight.
- `palette`: "cobalt" | "moss" | "graphite" | "dusk" (default "cobalt") — The done pigment, the row band and the progress line; failures stay red in every palette.
- `maxGridHeight`: number (default 200) — Tallest the grid may grow, px, before its cells shrink to fit.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows breathing placeholder cells and holds the primary; error offers Try again.
- `onReload`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the selection failed to load.
- `modal`: boolean (default false) — Trap Tab inside the dialog and set aria-modal; pass it when you render it in an overlay.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be started, paused or retried.
- `className`: string — Classes for the dialog panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the action picker is a radiogroup (arrows move and select); the grid holds one tab stop — arrows move between cells, Home/End to a row's ends, Ctrl+Home/End to the first and last, Page Up/Down by five rows — and each cell's name reads the item and its state. Escape cancels on the confirm step, pauses a run and closes the summary, always with preventDefault.
- The footer's two buttons keep their identity through every phase (Cancel/Archive → Stop/Pause → Stop here/Resume → Retry failed/Done), so focus never drops; nothing focused is ever disabled. Start, each quarter, pause, resume and the final sentence are announced politely — never per item.
- Reduced motion: cells change colour on a short tween with no stamp growth, the row band steps instead of gliding and the summary cross-fades; counts, the progress line and the sentence still update.
- Hand it your real work through run(item, context): items are processed one at a time in reading order, started from the press itself — never from an effect — and pause, stop and unmount halt the queue. The run is not tied to visibility; only autoStart waits for the dialog to be in view.
- Cells carry their look through data attributes styled once on the grid, so hundreds of items stay light in the markup and a tick re-renders one cell. One ResizeObserver fits the cell size to the width; render it inside your own overlay and pass modal to trap Tab.

### Wayfinding Dots (KQ-1693) — `wayfinding-dots`
Gentle marks on the features you haven't found.

Non-blocking hint dots that sit on the corners of the features nobody has opened yet, each breathing slowly from one shared clock with its own phase. Pressing a dot flicks it up on springs.flick, frames the feature on springs.snap and unfolds the tip out of the dot as a clip circle growing from its centre; closing folds it back and the dot flies on springs.glide along an arc into the corner counter, whose digit rolls on springs.snap and pill lands on springs.recoil. - `onDismissAll`: (ids: string[]) => void — Dismiss all was pressed, with the ids it found.
- `shown / defaultShown`: boolean (default — / true) — Whether the dots are showing, controlled or initial.
- `onShownChange`: (shown: boolean) => void — Fires from the hotkey or the eye button that showed or hid the dots.
- `hotkey`: string | null (default "h") — The key that shows and hides every dot while focus is inside the component and not in a text field; null turns it off.
- `dotStyle`: "beacon" | "halo" | "ring" | "pip" (default "beacon") — The mark: a ring that leaves the dot, a swelling glow, a breathing hollow ring, or a numbered badge.
- `breathSpeed`: number (default 1) — How fast the dots breathe, 0.25 to 2; 1 is one breath every 3.2 s.

Notes:

- Keyboard: dots are buttons after the interface in reading order. H toggles every dot unless focus is in a text field. The counter's eye and × buttons are the pointer twins of H and Dismiss all.
- Each found hint is announced once, politely ("Saved views found. 2 of 5."), and the layer's name carries the count.
- Reduced motion: nothing breathes or travels — each style rests at its fullest, tips and the sheet cross-fade in place, a found dot fades where it is and the count updates at once.
- Performance: one linear clock animation drives every breath, and only while the component is on screen, the tab is visible, hints are shown and at least one remains; per-frame values are motion values, never React renders.
- The pigment is the accent's hue at a fixed lightness (oklch from), so a token accent reads the same in light and dark themes; pass any CSS colour.

### Moving Day (KQ-1694) — `moving-day`
Bring everything over from your old tool.

The import step of moving into a new workspace: each category the old tool holds is a box with its count, and Start opens them in turn — the lid swings open on springs.snap, the count rolls up in tabular digits straight from a motion value, and the box's things leave it one by one, travelling into the new workspace's preview on springs.glide and landing on springs.recoil, before the box shuts with a tick drawn on springs.flick. A category too big to wait for keeps counting in the background behind a thin bar with a toast, and whatever could not move is listed with its reason for Retry. Start, Pause, Resume, Retry and Open are real buttons (the primary keeps focus as its label changes) and the source is a radiogroup the arrow keys move through.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/moving-day`

Props:
- `sources`: MovingDaySource[] (default defaultMovingDaySources) — The old tools to import from, { id, name, detail?, counts, blocked? }, each with a count per category and the items that cannot move.
- `categories`: MovingDayCategory[] (default defaultMovingDayCategories) — What moves, { id, label, unit, icon?, samples }, one box each in the order they open.
- `source / defaultSource`: string (default — / the first source) — The chosen source's id, controlled or initial.
- `onSourceChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the radio or arrow key that changed the source; only before the import starts.
- `workspace`: string (default "Fieldline") — The new workspace's name, in the preview, the copy and the open button.
- `onStart`: (sourceId: string) => void — Start was pressed.
- `onPause`: (sourceId: string) => void — Pause was pressed; the open box's count holds where it is.
- `onResume`: (sourceId: string) => void — Resume was pressed; the count continues from the same number.
- `onRetry`: (ids: string[]) => void — Retry was pressed, with the ids of the items it tries again. Retryable ones move; the rest keep their reasons.
- `onDone`: (summary: { moved: number; stayed: string[] }) => void — Every box has finished, background ones included.
- `onOpenWorkspace`: () => void — The open-workspace button was pressed (offered as soon as the visible pass is done).
- `pace`: number (default 2400) — Items per second the simulated import moves; each box takes between 0.9 and 2.4 s.
- `backgroundAbove`: number (default 5000) — A category with more items than this moves in the background after its first share, with a toast.
- `boxStyle`: "carton" | "crate" | "tote" (default "carton") — A carton whose flaps swing open, a slatted crate whose lid lifts and tilts, or a tote whose lid slides back.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Box size, row heights and spacing.
- `tone`: "kraft" | "slate" | "cobalt" | "mint" (default "kraft") — The boxes' pigment, a hue at a fixed lightness shaded toward black in oklab, so it reads in both themes.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the old tool's counts have arrived: loading draws skeleton boxes, error a message with Try again.
- `onReload`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the counts failed to load.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 560) — The tallest the step grows before its body scrolls, px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be started or chosen; the step dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer section.

Notes:
- The host owns the real transfer: wire onStart, onPause, onResume and onRetry to it. The component is the visible step and simulates progress at pace, so the counts and arrivals always tell a coherent story.
- Keyboard: the source is a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End) while nothing has started; Start, Pause, Resume and Open share one primary button that keeps focus as its label changes and is never disabled while focused (aria-disabled instead).
- Each box is a list item named by a sentence ("Files, 1,285 of 1,286 moved, 1 stayed behind"); the rolling digits are hidden from assistive technology and box starts, finishes, pauses and the background toast are announced once each.
- Reduced motion: lids cross-fade instead of swinging, things fade into their slots instead of travelling, the tick appears without its draw — the counts still count.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. During an import there is one linear count tween for the open box (and one per background box); it stops while the step is off screen or the tab is hidden and resumes from the same number. Arrival offsets are measured once per row, before paint.

### Practice Run (KQ-1695) — `practice-run`
Learn by doing the real thing, once.

A hands-on tutorial where each lesson is one small real task in a sandboxed copy of the interface: a working board whose cards drag 1:1 and glide into their lane on springs.glide, a comment box whose @ opens a real combobox of teammates, a job whose Labels menu opens on springs.snap. A coach line answers what the visitor actually does, one sentence at a time rising into place on springs.snap, and a finished task presses a quiet check stamp onto the sandbox on springs.recoil before the next lesson slides in on springs.glide. Every lesson has a keyboard path (Space picks a card up and the arrows carry it; arrows and Enter pick a person; arrows walk the menu) and a Skip, and progress is a value so a run resumes where it stopped.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/practice-run`

Props:
- `lessons`: PracticeLesson[] (default defaultPracticeLessons) — The lessons in order, each a move (board), mention (combobox) or label (menu) task with its own data and optional coach lines.
- `progress / defaultProgress`: Record<string, "done" | "skipped"> (default — / {}) — Each lesson's state, controlled or initial. The run opens on the first lesson that is neither done nor skipped.
- `onProgressChange`: (progress: PracticeProgress) => void — Fires from the finish, skip or restart that changed it, with the whole progress.
- `onComplete`: (lesson: PracticeLesson) => void — A lesson's task was done for real.
- `onSkip`: (lesson: PracticeLesson) => void — A lesson was skipped.
- `onFinish`: (progress: PracticeProgress) => void — Start working was pressed after the last lesson.
- `onRestart`: () => void — Practice again was pressed; progress is cleared.
- `coach`: string (default "Wren") — The coach's name, on its avatar, in the ticker and the caption.
- `coachStyle`: "bubble" | "ticker" | "margin" (default "bubble") — An avatar and a speech bubble, a single mono line over a progress hairline, or a note in the left margin pointing at the sandbox. Under 30rem it is always a caption docked at the foot of the sandbox.
- `stampStyle`: "seal" | "tick" | "ink" (default "seal") — The stamp a finished task gets: a round seal with its rim lettered, a tick drawn on flick in a rounded square, or a rubber-stamped DONE.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The stamp's ink, the lit lane, the step rail and the mention token. Any CSS colour, taken at a fixed lightness.
- `stampHold`: number (default 700) — How long the stamp rests before the next lesson slides in, ms.
- `workspace`: string (default "Fieldline") — The product being practised, in the copy.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" (default "ready") — Whether the lessons are ready; loading draws a still sandbox and the rail is inert.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 560) — The tallest the run grows before its body scrolls, px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be done or skipped; the run dims.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer section.

Notes:
- Keyboard: on the board, Space or Enter picks a card up, the arrow keys carry it lane to lane (focus follows it), Space puts it down and Escape puts it back. In the mention lesson @ opens a combobox (aria-activedescendant) that the arrows and Enter drive; in the label lesson the arrows open and walk a menu of checkbox items and Escape closes it. Skip and the step rail are buttons.
- The coach line is the one polite live region: each reaction is a single sentence frozen when it happens, and the stamp is announced as "Done: <lesson>". Focus moves into each new lesson's first control once it has arrived, when it was inside the run before.
- Pointer: cards follow the finger 1:1 after 4px of travel (touch-action none on the card only), settle into their new lane from where they were seen with the release velocity, and any card can be moved — the sandbox is real, and the coach says so.
- Reduced motion: cards change lanes in place, the stamp fades in at rest, lessons and coach lines cross-fade. Every state still shows.
- Nothing runs at rest; the only timer is the stamp's hold, cleared on unmount. Override any coach line per lesson with lesson.coach[event].

### Name Plate (KQ-1696) — `name-plate`
Name the workspace and hang its sign.

The workspace-creation step: as a name is typed its letters are set onto a plate that swings into the preview sidebar on a pendulum spring — slid along the rail on springs.glide, tilted, and falling through a few decaying swings to hang from its nail — while the address forms beneath the name with each new letter dropping in on springs.flick. - `plateStyle`: "enamel" | "brass" | "timber" (default "enamel") — An enamel sign in the colour with a cream inset rule, an engraved brass plate with screw heads and a colour inlay, or a timber board with a painted panel.

Notes:

Format is checked at once; availability after a 250 ms pause, through checkAddress or takenAddresses, and the message is announced only once the check has answered.

- Under 40rem the plate hangs in a band above the fields instead of in the sidebar; long names step their type down and wrap by whole words so the plate never spills.

### Goal Weave (KQ-1697) — `goal-weave`
Pick your goals; a plan assembles itself.

A goal-selection step whose plan assembles itself: choosing a goal draws a thread out of its card to each of its tasks — the curve split at a growing t on an enter tween, every point rounded — while the tasks arrive from 8px left on springs.glide in a cascade(), and removing a goal retracts its threads and pulls out only the tasks no other goal holds while shared ones stay. The goal cards are checkboxes that lift on springs.snap and follow the arrow keys; plan rows rove with Up and Down, Alt with Up or Down (or a drag of the grip, 1:1 with the release velocity handed to springs.glide) reorders them, and the threads follow every glide from a geometry loop that runs only while something moves.

- `cardStyle`: "tile" | "chip" | "row" (default "tile") — Two-column tiles with icon, title and detail; compact wrapping chips; or a list of rows with task counts.
- `threadStyle`: "thread" | "stitch" | "ribbon" (default "thread") — A fine 1.5px curve, a dashed stitch, or a soft 6px ribbon.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The first goal's tint (later goals turn its hue 48° each), the chosen cards and the primary button. Any CSS colour.
- `question`: string (default "What should Fernworks help with?") — The question over the goal cards; it also names the checkbox group.

- `maxHeight`: number (default 560) — The tallest the step grows before its body scrolls, px.

Notes:

- Performance: threads are SVG paths written straight to the DOM from a requestAnimationFrame loop that runs only while a weave, a reorder, a drag or a resize is in flight, and only while the step is on screen and the tab is visible.
- Reduced motion: threads fade instead of drawing, tasks fade into their slots, reorders and the drawer jump. The plan, counts and announcements are unchanged.
- Under 40rem the plan moves into a drawer under the goals; the threads give way to goal-coloured dots on each task, and a change made while it is closed rolls the count and shows a +n badge.

### Shortcut Drills (KQ-1698) — `shortcut-drills`
Learn the keys by pressing them.

A keyboard practice built from a list of actions and their keys: the screen names an action, you press its shortcut, and every key you press is mirrored on a small keyboard whose caps go down on springs.flick and come back on springs.snap. A correct chord bottoms out together and lights, the caps rise key first and modifiers after, and a bead lifts off the key and flies on an arc into the streak rail on springs.glide, landing on springs.recoil; a wrong one shakes nothing and gently shows the right chord with a breathing ring and a caption. The prompt is a focusable practice pad that takes real chords (Tab and Escape still leave), the board is a roving group of buttons where modifiers latch and a key commits, and the set ends on a summary where any drill can be repeated.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/shortcut-drills`

Props:
- `drills`: ShortcutDrill[] (default defaultShortcutDrills) — The shortcuts in order: { id, action, detail?, keys } where keys are Mod, Shift, Alt, Control, Meta plus one KeyboardEvent.code (Mod accepts ⌘ or Ctrl).
- `results / defaultResults`: Record<string, "clean" | "hinted" | "skipped"> (default — / {}) — Each drill's result by id, controlled or initial; a returning visitor's beads.
- `onResultsChange`: (results: ShortcutResults) => void — Fires from the press, tap or skip that changed a result, with every result.
- `onComplete`: (summary: { total, clean, hinted, skipped, results }) => void — A run reached the summary: the whole set, or a repeat of part of it.
- `onSkip`: (drill: ShortcutDrill, index: number) => void — Skip was pressed on a drill.
- `onAttempt`: (attempt: { drill, keys, correct }) => void — Every chord pressed or tapped while a drill was asked, right or wrong.
- `keyboardLayout`: "command" | "control" | "split" (default "command") — ⌘ ⌥ ⌃ legends, Ctrl and Alt legends, or the ⌘ board split in two halves.
- `keycapStyle`: "sculpted" | "flat" | "outline" (default "sculpted") — Tall caps with a skirt and real travel, low chiclets with a shadow, or line drawings that scale instead of travelling.
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "amber" | "graphite" | string (default "cobalt") — Lit caps, beads, the hint ring and the streak: a named accent or any CSS colour.
- `reveal`: "miss" | "always" (default "miss") — Show the chord after a wrong press, or from the start as a learn mode.
- `advanceDelay`: number (default 650) — Milliseconds between a correct press and the next drill.
- `tapThrough`: boolean (default true) — The caps answer taps: modifiers latch, a key commits the chord.
- `title`: string (default "Fieldline shortcuts") — The heading.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the drills have arrived: a skeleton while loading, a retry on error.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the drills failed to load.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick on every press, a brighter one when the bead lands.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Holds the pad, the board and the buttons.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface; give it a height to fix its frame.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the prompt is a role="application" pad, so screen readers pass keys through; every key but Tab and Escape is an attempt and is prevented while it has focus. Keep drills off chords the browser reserves (closing or opening tabs and windows). The board is one tab stop: arrows walk the caps, Enter or Space taps one.
- Reduced motion: caps change colour instead of travelling, the bead fades into its slot instead of flying, prompts cross-fade; every result, count and caption still updates at once.
- The board is drawn in key units and positioned in percentages with container-query legends, so it scales to any width (about 16px caps at a 316px card) and renders the same on the server. On a phone its caps grow taller.
- Letters match by what they type as well as where they sit, so a visitor on another letter layout answers by the legend; Mod accepts either ⌘ or Ctrl whatever the board shows.
- Nothing loops: the listening dot breathes only while the pad has focus, and timers and the bead flight are cleared on unmount.
- Theming: everything is drawn from tokens; accent sets --sd-accent and a fixed-lightness pigment for filled caps and beads, so both themes read.

- Accessibility: both painted copies of the report are aria-hidden; readers get the lens's name, the card's teaser as its description, and one polite announcement each time the lens settles on a new region.
- Reduced motion: the lens follows and stops where it is let go, with no coast, tilt, lift or bounce; the card moves with it and its text cross-fades.
- Performance: nothing loops — motion values run only while dragging or settling; region rectangles and sizes come from a ResizeObserver, and the blur is a static filter on a static layer.
- The report is painted twice (blurred, and sharp inside the lens's clip), so keep custom summaries to the shape of TeaserSummary; with no data pass summary={null} for a clearly labelled sample.
- Narrow containers (under 480px) swap the disc for a full-width band that moves on y with touch-action pan-x, and dock the card under or over it.

- Keyboard: Resend is a button with aria-disabled until its timer ends and its name carries the wait ("Resend link, available in 24 seconds"); the countdown itself is announced only when it reaches zero. Change email swaps in a labelled field (Enter sends, Escape cancels) and focus returns to Change email.
- A status change moves focus to the new heading only when focus was already inside (or nowhere), so a link noticed in the background never steals focus from the rest of the page.
- Timers never read the clock in render: they count on from now, schedule only the next tick that changes something, pause in a hidden tab and re-sync when it is shown. The glow loop stops off screen, in a hidden tab, at glowAmount 0 and in every state but waiting.
- Close the BroadcastChannel loop by posting from the page the link opens: new BroadcastChannel(name).postMessage({ type: "verified", name }).
- Reduced motion: the glow is a still halo and the envelope cross-fades to the welcome; nothing travels.

### Session Lapse (KQ-1714) — `session-lapse`
Still there? Stay signed in with a tap.

An idle-timeout guard for a page: before the session ends an alert dialog rises over it with a ring that drains linearly while the seconds in its middle count down, both read off one motion value. Stay signed in, Escape, or a press, key or scroll outside the dialog refills the ring on glide while it pops on snap and the seconds count back up, then the dialog leaves on the exit ease; letting it run out fades the page into a signed-out note that keeps the unsaved draft. - `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires when the warning appears or leaves, from whatever caused it.
- `watch`: "document" | "self" | "none" (default "document") — Whose activity keeps the session alive: the whole page, only this component's box, or nothing but the button.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the idle clock (a call, a video); it restarts when released, and a showing warning holds its time.
- `onExtend`: (via: "button" | "activity") => void — The session was extended, by the button or Escape, or by activity during the warning.
- `onSignOut`: () => void — Sign out was chosen from the warning.
- `onExpire`: () => void — The warning ran out and the session ended.
- `onSignIn`: () => void — Sign back in was pressed on the signed-out note.
- `draft`: { title: string; excerpt: string; words?: number } | null (default defaultSessionLapseDraft) — The unsaved work the signed-out note promises to keep; null for none.
- `appName`: string (default "Fernworks") — The product's name, in the warning's sentence and the announcements.
- `title`: string — The warning's title. Defaults by tone: "Still there?", "Are you still working?", "Signing out soon".
- `labels`: { stay?: string; signOut?: string; signIn?: string } (default Stay signed in · Sign out · Sign back in) — The three actions' words.
- `ringStyle`: "line" | "ticks" | "pie" (default "line") — How the countdown is drawn: a draining line, a tick per second, or a shrinking sector.
- `tone`: "calm" | "plain" | "urgent" (default "calm") — The ring's colour and the title's voice: cobalt, ink, or amber turning to danger for the last ten seconds.

- `className`: string — Classes for the outer wrapper.

Notes:
- Keyboard: focus moves to Stay signed in when the warning appears (unless the visitor is busy elsewhere on the page, or the warning is off screen); Tab wraps inside the dialog and Escape stays signed in. When the note arrives, focus goes to Sign back in if it was inside.
- Activity: before the warning any pointer, key or scroll activity in scope moves the clock on; once it shows only a press, a key or a scroll outside the dialog extends, so reaching for Sign out with the pointer never cancels the warning.
- Reduced motion: the ring still drains and the seconds still count, because the time left is information; the refill is a jump and the dialog and note only cross-fade.
- Performance: while the page is in use nothing ticks — one timeout marks when the warning is due; the drain runs only while the ring is on screen and the tab visible, and expiry is a single wall-clock timeout.
- The page stays mounted (inert and faded) behind the note, so the draft's state survives the sign-out and comes back on Sign back in.

### Cooling Lock (KQ-1716) — `cooling-lock`

A lockout panel for after repeated failed sign-ins: frost covers a ring round the lock and thaws clockwise from the top as the wait runs down, in six-armed flakes that shrink on snap and leave a slipping droplet as the front passes, bristling hoarfrost that shortens at the front, or a glaze that drains as one arc. - `appName`: string (default "Fieldline") — The product's name, in the sentences.
- `frostStyle`: "crystal" | "rime" | "glaze" (default "crystal") — The frost's material: six-armed flakes, bristling hoarfrost, or a smooth glaze of ice.

Notes:

- Reduced motion: the ring still thaws by the same front, because the time left is information; flakes fade without shrinking, droplets do not slide, and the copy cross-fades in place.
- Performance: the thaw and the once-a-second digits run only while the panel is on screen and the tab visible; the end is one wall-clock timeout, and a long lockout runs nothing at all.

A kanban board whose cards weather while they wait: every day still adds a faint patina — tarnish gathering at the edges first, then a mottled bloom from a seeded turbulence mask — mixed with the ink so it darkens on a light page and lifts like dust on a dark one, and a corner counter turns warn when a card goes stale and offers to nudge its owner. - `cardStyle`: "plain" | "raised" | "outline" (default "plain") — Cards drawn plain with a hairline, raised on a shadow, or as an outline over the column.
- `tone`: "copper" | "rust" | "dust" | "ink" (default "copper") — The patina's pigment; it follows the theme.
- `staleAfter`: number (default 7) — Days still before a card counts as stale: its counter warns and its owner can be nudged.
- `now`: number (default defaultPatinaNow) — Today, ms since the epoch.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the board's cards have arrived.
- `onRetry`: () => void — "Try again" was pressed after the board failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Basinworks facilities") — The heading.
- `height`: number (default 460) — The board's height in px; columns scroll inside it.
- `label`: string — The board's accessible name; defaults to the title.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Freezes the board: no drags, keys, edits or nudges.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer panel.

Notes:
- Keyboard: arrows walk the cards, Space lifts one and arrows carry it, Space or Enter drops it and Escape puts it back; Enter or F2 renames a resting card in place (Escape cancels), N nudges a stale card's owner, and Tab reaches the focused card's Nudge button.
- The patina is static markup — gradients and one shared set of four SVG turbulence filters per board — recomputed only when now, a card or a tweak changes; the polish is one tween per touched card, and nothing runs at rest.
- Patina colours are token pigments mixed with --ink, so they follow the theme with no theme reads; card names carry the age in words ("waiting 12 days, stale").
- A dropped card is polished after it lands, so the wipe is always seen; while the Stale filter sorts by age a moved card joins the end of its new column.
- Under reduced motion the patina fades instead of being wiped, nothing travels, and ages, stale marks and the filter order still show.

### Blocker Chains (KQ-1723) — `blocker-chains`
See what's stuck, and what it's stuck behind.

A kanban board whose blocked cards hang a thin chain to the card they wait on: quadratic catenaries drawn under the cards with a fixed length, so dragging a card pulls its chains taut and bringing it closer lets them droop. Moving a blocker into Done snaps its chains loose — the free end swings down from the waiting card as a damped pendulum and fades on the exit ease — while the freed card lifts on springs.snap with an unblocked glow and settles back on springs.glide, and every card that moved FLIPs to its place on glide. Cards share one roving tab stop: arrows move, Space lifts and drops, Escape puts back, B shows every chain, L links a blocker, and Tab reaches a card's chain chips where Enter jumps to the blocker as a bead runs along the chain and Delete unlinks.

- `onUnlink`: (blockedId: string, blockerId: string, reason: "done" | "removed") => void — Fires when a chain comes off: its blocker reached a done column, or Delete removed it.
- `showAll / defaultShowAll`: boolean (default — / false) — Every chain in full, rather than only the hovered or focused card's (the rest stay faint).
- `onShowAllChange`: (showAll: boolean) => void — Fires from the Chains switch or the B key.
- `chainStyle`: "links" | "thread" | "beads" (default "links") — How a chain is drawn: hollow interlocking links, one fine thread, or round beads.
- `cardStyle`: "raised" | "flat" | "outline" (default "raised") — Card surface: raised with a shadow, a flat tint, or an outline on the board colour.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Highlighted chains and shackles, the drop wash, the switch and link mode. Any CSS colour.
- `now`: number (default Date.UTC(2026, 9, 16, 9)) — The moment a card's `since` is read against for "blocked 3d", in ms. Never the wall clock.

- `subtitle`: string (default "Release board") — One line under the heading, followed by the card count.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the board has loaded: loading shows skeleton columns, error a message with Try again.
- `onReload`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the board failed to load.

Notes:
- Keyboard: cards share one tab stop. Arrows move between cards, Space lifts a card, arrows carry it across columns and positions, Space or Enter drops and Escape puts it back. L starts linking (arrows choose the blocker, Enter links), B toggles every chain, and Tab reaches the focused card's chain chips: Enter jumps to the blocker, Delete unlinks.
- Touch scrolls the board from a card's face; a card is carried by its grip and linked from its link handle, both touch-action: none.
- Reduced motion: chains still draw and still come off, but fade instead of swinging; cards jump to their places, the freed card glows without lifting, and the jump bead becomes a brief highlight of the chain.
- Performance: the chain layer is drawn by writing path data straight to the DOM in a requestAnimationFrame loop that runs only during a drag, a settle, a fall or a resize, then stops. Nothing runs while the board is still.
- Under 40rem of container width the columns stack and the chains become a "Blocked by" line on each card; summarizeBlockers(cards, columns) returns the blocked and loop counts the header shows.

### Stack Carry (KQ-1724) — `stack-carry`
Select several cards and move them as one.

A kanban board where a selection moves as one stack. Dragging any selected card gathers the others under the pointer into a fan whose spread is fanAngle: the grabbed card follows 1:1 and each card behind it follows on its own spring, softer the deeper it sits, so a fast throw strings the deck out and a pause gathers it, while a count badge lands on springs.recoil. Dropping deals the cards into the column in their original board order on springs.glide, cascade() apart, as their dashed home slots fold shut and the cards around them FLIP to make room; refused cards fly home, shake once and say why. Shift-click selects a run, Cmd or Ctrl-click or the check tab toggles, X toggles the focused card, M opens a move menu that deals the same way, Escape clears, and a long press starts selecting on touch.

Answer now or later with { failed: [{ id, reason }] } for any that could not move; the rest land in board order at index among the column's other cards. While a promise is pending the stack waits and its badge spins.
- `fanAngle`: number (default 7) — How far the carried stack fans, in degrees per card; 0 is a neat pile.
- `maxFan`: number (default 5) — Cards drawn in the carried stack; the badge counts the rest.
- `cardStyle`: "raised" | "flat" | "outline" (default "raised") — Card surface: raised with a shadow, a flat tint, or an outline on the board colour.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Selection border and check tab, the stack's badge, the drop wash and the Move button. Any CSS colour.

- `title`: string (default "Coldbrook Support") — The board's heading.
- `subtitle`: string (default "Tuesday queue") — One line under the heading, followed by the ticket count.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the board has loaded: loading shows skeleton columns, error a message with Try again.
- `onReload`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the board failed to load.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read-only: cards can be selected but nothing moves.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer container.

Notes:
- Keyboard: each column is a multi-select listbox and the board shares one tab stop. Arrows move, Shift with Up or Down extends the selection, X or Space toggles, Cmd or Ctrl+A selects the column, M opens the move menu (arrows, Home, End, Enter, Escape returns focus) and Escape clears the selection.

- Reduced motion: the stack is a tidy pile at the pointer with no trailing springs, and cards appear in their new places without flying; selection, counts and refusals are unchanged.
- Performance: nothing runs at rest. Per-card springs run only while carrying and dealing, and the edge auto-scroll frame loop only while a drag sits near the board's edge.

### Chart Recipe (KQ-1726) — `chart-recipe`

### Dry Run (KQ-1728) — `dry-run`
See what the migration would do before it does.

A data migration wizard — connect, map, rehearse, run — that shows what it would do before it writes. The rehearsal is a grey pass: one motion value walks the rows on the move ease and three counters (would create, would update, would skip) tick up as their rows pass, as figures, bars or a waffle of row batches whose cells pop as the head goes by; the real run repeats exactly the same seeded walk in colour over the grey ghost, and the actual counts land on springs.recoil beside their rehearsed figures and a delta chip. Panels swap by direction on springs.glide, the stepper's fill glides and its checks draw on springs.flick, and every step validates before Next, taking focus to whatever needs fixing.

- `onMappingChange`: (mapping) => void — Fires from the select that changed the mapping, with the whole mapping.
- `results`: DryRunResults (default defaultDryRunResults) — { rehearsal, run, skipped }: the counts each pass lands on and the rows left out.
- `step / defaultStep`: "connect" | "map" | "rehearse" | "run" (default — / "connect") — The current step, controlled or initial; opening later counts the earlier steps as passed.
- `onStepChange`: (step) => void — Fires from Next, Back or the stepper with the step asked for.
- `onConnect`: () => boolean | void — Fires when the connection is checked; return false to report the source unreadable.
- `onDryRun`: (mapping) => void — Fires when the rehearsal starts, with the mapping it rehearses.
- `onRun`: (mapping) => void — Fires when the real run starts, with the mapping it runs.
- `onPassEnd`: (pass: "rehearsal" | "run", counts) => void — Fires when a pass has walked every row, with that pass's counts.
- `onDownloadReport`: (report: DryRunReport) => void — Fires from Download report with source, target, mapping, both passes' counts and the skipped rows.
- `counterStyle`: "digits" | "bars" | "waffle" (default "digits") — Counters as tiles of figures, long bars, or one waffle of row batches.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Padding, type size and figure size.
- `tone`: "signal" | "cobalt" | "ember" | "moss" (default "signal") — The real run's colours (the rehearsal is always grey); pigments at fixed lightness.
- `passDuration`: number (default 2400) — How long each pass takes to walk the rows, in ms.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows placeholders; error explains and offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the source failed to load.

Notes:

Next validates the step and, when it cannot go on, says why under the step and moves focus to what needs fixing (the Check button, or the first bad select). Step changes move focus to the new step's heading; the stepper's earlier steps are buttons.
- Each pass is one motion value; every figure, bar and waffle cell derives from it, so nothing re-renders per frame and nothing runs once a pass has finished. The progressbar's value is written as it moves; the live region speaks once when a pass starts and once with the counts when it ends.
- The rehearsal and the run share one seeded order of rows, so the run visibly repeats the rehearsal's walk; cells that came out differently are ringed and each counter shows a delta chip. Changing the mapping after a rehearsal marks it stale and blocks the run until it is rehearsed again; the mapping locks once the run starts.
- Reduced motion: the pass still runs, in 600 ms with no cell pops, landings or panel travel; counts, fills and colours still change because they are the information.
- Colours: the rehearsal is a share of the foreground and the run's tones are pigments at fixed lightness, so both read the same in light and dark. Skipped rows are hatched as well as tinted. Below a 34rem container the counters stack and the stepper drops its labels.

- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Card padding and type size.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Rings, lights, the estimate's rules and Provision — any CSS colour.
- `rackUnits`: number (default 12) — The cabinet's height in rack units, 10 to 20.
- `format`: (amount: number) => string (default US dollars with cents) — Formats every amount; the estimate's digits roll whatever the format.

- `title`: string (default "New environment") — The wizard's heading.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows placeholder cards; error explains and offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the catalogue failed to load.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the surface in px; the step body scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be chosen or provisioned.

Add-ons are role="switch" buttons. Next validates (a size the new region does not offer sends you back to Size and says why), and step changes move focus to the new heading.

### Question Trail (KQ-1730) — `question-trail`
One question at a time, with your answers kept.

A conversational intake, one question at a time: each question is typed first, then its bubble rises a step from its tail corner on springs.snap, and the option you pick travels into place as your answer chip on springs.glide. Pressing an earlier chip rewinds — the later bubbles fold back up into it bottom-first in a cascade, heights closing on glide while their words lift away on the exit ease — and answering again replays the trail forward with every kept answer until a question has none, so a changed branch only asks what is new. Options are a roving group of buttons (arrows move, Enter sends, Escape keeps the old answer) and text questions are labelled fields that say what is wrong.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/question-trail`

Props:
- `questions`: QuestionTrailQuestion[] (default defaultQuestionTrailQuestions) — { id, prompt, short?, kind?, options?, placeholder?, optional?, next?, validate? } — next is an id, a map from answer to id (a branch), or null to end.
- `value / defaultValue`: Record<string, string> (default — / {}) — Answers by question id, controlled or initial; "" is a skipped optional question. The trail opens at the first unanswered one.
- `onValueChange`: (answers) => void — Fires from the press, Enter or Skip that changed an answer, with every answer kept.
- `onAnswer`: (questionId, value, answers) => void — Fires once per answer given.
- `onComplete`: (answers, path) => void — Fires when the last question on the path is answered, with the path's ids — again after a rewind that completes it.
- `onRewind`: (questionId) => void — Fires when an earlier answer is opened again.
- `onSave`: (saved: { answers, at }) => void — Fires from Save for later with the answers and the question waiting.
- `storageKey`: string — Writes a saved trail to this device's storage under this key and picks it up after mount.
- `bubbleStyle`: "soft" | "outline" | "plain" (default "soft") — Filled bubbles with a tail corner, hairline bubbles, or a plain transcript on a left rule.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Gaps, padding and type size.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Answer chips, the composer's focus, progress and the save mark — any CSS colour.
- `typingDelay`: number (default 420) — How long the host types before a new question arrives, in ms.
- `host`: string (default "Basinworks") — Who is asking; named to assistive tech before each question.
- `title`: string (default "Book a call-out") — The intake's heading.
- `closing`: string | (answers) => string (default a thank-you that repeats the phone number) — The host's last line once every question on the path is answered.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows placeholder bubbles; error explains and offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the questions failed to load.
- `height`: number (default 520) — Height of the surface in px; the trail scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be answered or changed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: each composer takes focus when its question arrives. Options are a group with one tab stop — arrows and Home/End move, Enter or Space sends. Text questions are labelled fields: Enter sends, errors are linked by aria-describedby. Every earlier answer is a button named "Change <short>: <answer>"; while changing one, Escape keeps it (and is not passed on).
- Answers off the current path are kept, not deleted: going back and choosing differently only asks the questions the new branch needs, and switching back replays the old ones with a "kept" mark. Questions reached through a branch say which answer led there.
- The trail scrolls its own box to keep the newest item in view and never scrolls the page. Announcements are one sentence per answer (with how many kept answers replayed and the next question), never per typing frame.
- Reduced motion: no typing dots, travel or scale — bubbles and chips fade in and out, folds collapse at once, and the replay still re-deals in order.
- With storageKey the trail is written on Save for later and picked up after mount, so server and client render the same first frame; onSave hands the same payload to a host that keeps drafts itself.

### Range Remarks (KQ-1736) — `range-remarks`
Comment on a span of lines, not just one.

A code review diff where comments cover spans of lines. Pressing in the comment gutter and dragging grows a bracket across the lines you mean — its live end under the pointer 1:1, the lines tinting as it passes them — and on release the end settles onto the last line's edge on springs.snap with the throw's velocity, then a comment box unfolds under the range, its measured height opening on springs.glide as it swings down from its top edge. Existing threads sit after their last line with their bracket in the gutter, brighten with their lines on hover or focus, carry suggested changes as mini diffs, and fold to a one-line summary on glide when resolved or outdated. The diff is a role="grid" with one roving line: Up and Down move, Shift with an arrow grows the same bracket a line at a time, Enter or C opens the box and Escape clears; long lines wrap below a 30rem container.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/range-remarks`

Props:
- `diff`: RangeDiff (default defaultRangeDiff) — The file: { path, lines: { kind: "context" | "add" | "del", text, old?, new? }[] }; missing line numbers are counted from the top.
- `threads / defaultThreads`: RangeThread[] (default — / defaultRangeThreads) — Threads as { id, start, end (line indexes), comments, resolved?, outdated?, suggestion? }, controlled or initial.
- `onThreadsChange`: (threads) => void — Fires with every thread after a comment, a reply or a resolve.
- `selection / defaultSelection / onSelectionChange`: { start, end } | null (default — / null) — The selected range of lines, controlled or initial, and the callback from the drag or key that changed it.
- `onComment`: (range, text, threadId?) => void — A comment was posted on a range — a new thread, or a reply when `threadId` is given.
- `onSuggest`: (range, suggestion, text) => void — A suggested change was posted on a range, with its replacement text and optional comment.
- `onResolve`: (threadId, resolved) => void — A thread was resolved (true) or reopened (false).
- `bracketStyle`: "bracket" | "bar" | "brace" (default "bracket") — A square bracket with caps, a solid rounded bar, or a curly brace whose nose points at the range's middle.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Line height (18/20/24px) and code type size.
- `editorTheme`: "plain" | "paper" | "night" (default "plain") — The page's own surfaces, a warm paper tint, or a dark editor in either page theme (the accent's hue at fixed lightness).
- `wrap`: "auto" | "always" | "never" (default "auto") — Wrap long lines below a 30rem container, always, or never (the diff scrolls sideways instead).
- `author`: string (default "Noor Haddad") — The name new comments are posted under.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultRangeNow) — The moment relative times count from, so server and browser render the same text.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows skeleton lines; error shows Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the diff failed to load.
- `height`: number (default 540) — The surface's height in px; the diff scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: threads can be read and expanded, nothing posted or resolved.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the diff is a grid with one roving line — Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Shift with Up or Down grows the range from its anchor (the bracket's keyboard path), Enter or C opens the comment box on it, Escape clears it (consumed); in a box, Cmd or Ctrl with Enter posts and Escape cancels back to the line.
- Pointer: the gutter strip between the line numbers and the code is the drag handle (touch-action pan-x, so a vertical drag on a phone grows the range instead of scrolling); a tap there comments on one line.
- Each line is named for assistive technology ("Line 12, added: const cap = 30_000") and marked aria-selected while in the range; every range, post and resolve is announced once.
- Reduced motion: the bracket and the comment box appear at rest — no settle, no swing — and threads fold instantly; ranges, tints and counts still change.
- Row geometry is measured after layout and on resize (ResizeObserver), never per frame, so wrapping lines and opening threads keep every bracket on its lines.

### Sign-off Round (KQ-1737) — `sign-off-round`
Every reviewer stamps it before it ships.

An approval round on a document: every reviewer's verdict lands as a stamp in its slot on the document's header, dropping from 1.4× and a little more turned onto its resting tilt on springs.recoil — the two small bounces of a hand stamp — while the header sinks 1.5px and springs back on springs.snap, a ring of ink spreads under it and the thock is heard at touch-down. Changes requested stamps in muted red whatever the accent and needs a comment; its stamp is a button that brings the comment into view. The progress rail fills a segment per verdict on springs.glide, and when the last stamp lands the round completes: the rail takes the outcome's colour and the chip rolls to Signed off or Changes requested. Reviewers are a list in tab order with Approve, Request changes and Remind as real buttons.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sign-off-round`

Props:

- `onReviewersChange`: (reviewers) => void — Fires with every reviewer after a verdict is recorded here.
- `viewer`: string | null (default "noor") — The reviewer the visitor is: only their row offers Approve and Request changes, the rest offer Remind. null records verdicts for anyone (a facilitator).
- `onApprove`: (reviewerId) => void — A reviewer approved.
- `onRequestChanges`: (reviewerId, comment) => void — A reviewer requested changes, with the required comment.
- `onRemind`: (reviewerId) => void — Remind was pressed for a reviewer who has not answered.
- `onComplete`: (outcome: "approved" | "changes") => void — The last verdict landed — from the press that made it, or once after the host's update that did.
- `stampStyle`: "round" | "rect" | "initial" (default "round") — A round seal with the verdict on an arc, a rectangular rubber stamp with the date, or a circled monogram with a verdict badge.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Stamp size (52/60/68px, smaller below a 30rem container), row padding and type.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--success)") — Approval ink, the rail and Approve — any CSS colour, taken at a fixed lightness so the ink reads in both themes. Changes requested stays muted red.
- `remindCooldownMs`: number (default 4000) — How long Remind rests (aria-disabled, reading Reminded) after a press, in ms.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultSignOffNow) — The moment relative times count from; new verdicts are dated with it.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows skeleton stamps, reviewers and text; error shows Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the round failed to load.
- `height`: number (default 540) — The surface's height in px; the document and reviewers scroll inside it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the thock of a stamp the visitor pressed, at touch-down (lower for changes requested).
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: verdicts show; nothing can be stamped or reminded.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: reviewers are a list in tab order; Approve, Request changes and Remind are real buttons. Request changes opens a labelled field that takes focus — Cmd or Ctrl with Enter sends, Escape closes it and returns focus to the button (consumed) — and Send stays focusable and explains itself until the field has text.
- Assistive technology: stamps are named ("Approved by Ines Marlow, 14 oct"); a changes stamp is a button that moves focus to its comment; the rail is a progressbar ("2 of 4 reviewers signed"); every verdict, reminder and the completion are announced once as whole sentences.
- Sound answers the visitor only: a verdict pressed here thocks at touch-down; verdicts that arrive from the host land silently.
- Reduced motion: stamps fade in at rest with no drop, sink or ink ring, the rail fills at once and chips swap; every verdict, count and the outcome still show.
- Each stamp's tilt and bare ink patches are seeded from the reviewer's id, so the same stamp looks the same on every render and in server markup.

### Duration Slots (KQ-1740) — `duration-slots`

The zone box is a role="combobox": typing filters, Up and Down move, Enter chooses, Escape closes and is handled where focus is.

- Pointer: a press grows the draft from the pressed quarter; a press-and-drag sets the end with the pointer instead. Edges are captured after 1px and rubber-band at the gap's bounds (a neighbouring booking, the now-line, the day's end). The gap stays mounted under its draft so the drag that creates it is never cut off.
- Time is minutes from midnight and the now-line follows the now prop: drive it from your own clock (the demo ticks a simulated minute only while the rail is on screen and the page visible).
- Reduced motion: the now-line jumps, the draft appears at full length, edges land without springs and a release retracts at once under a fading wash; every time and readout still changes.
- Out-of-service rooms are hatched across the day with their reason and have no cells to walk. Under 36rem each room becomes a card with its next free slots as chips that open the same draft with − and + on its end.

### Series Edit (KQ-1743) — `series-edit`

### Backward Plan (KQ-1745) — `backward-plan`
Set the deadline and the plan lays itself out behind it.

A deadline-first planner: every task is scheduled as late as it can be and drawn as a car on a timeline that ends at the deadline flag. Dragging the flag, or any unlocked car, pulls the train — each car's finish follows the start of the car after it through the springs.snap calibration, integrated per frame in one loop, so the pull travels back down the train and every car settles a beat after the one ahead; the release projects the throw to a whole day and the flag springs there with its velocity. Cars pushed before today turn amber, locked cars hold their dates and lean toward the pull before springing upright on springs.recoil, and the flag is a slider whose arrow keys move the deadline a day while Tab reaches every task.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/backward-plan`

- `dayWidth`: number (default 12) — Pixels per day on the board: the scale of the timeline (8 to 40).
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "moss" | "plum" | "slate" (default "cobalt") — The bars' pigment at a fixed lightness; tasks in the past are always amber.
- `tasks / defaultTasks`: PlanTask[] (default — / defaultPlanTasks) — Each { id, name, days, after?: id[], locked?, start? }; start is the first day of a locked task. Controlled or initial.
- `onTasksChange`: (tasks) => void — Fires with every task after a lock, a pinned move or a length change.
- `deadline / defaultDeadline`: number (default — / defaultPlanDeadline) — The handover day, ms at UTC midnight; controlled or initial.
- `onDeadlineChange`: (deadline) => void — Fires from the drag release or the key that moved the deadline, with the new day.
- `onTaskChange`: (task) => void — Fires when one task's pinned dates or length change.
- `onLock`: (task, locked) => void — Fires when a task is locked (to its current dates) or unlocked.
- `now`: number (default defaultPlanNow) — Today in ms; tasks that would start before it turn amber. Never read from the clock.
- `range`: [number, number] (default [10, 70]) — Earliest and latest deadline, in days after now.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows placeholder bars; error explains and offers Try again.

- `title`: string (default "Fieldline site handover") — The heading.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the surface in px; the board scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be moved or locked.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the deadline flag is a slider — Left and Right move it a day, Page Up and Page Down a week, Home and End to the range's ends — and the board scrolls to keep it in view. Tab then reaches each task's lock toggle and bar; on a bar, L locks it, Left and Right move a locked task a day, Shift with Left or Right changes its length.
- One rAF loop drives the whole train while something moves and stops when every car is within a thousandth of a day and still; it never runs while the board is off screen or the tab is hidden (cars jump to their places instead) and allocates nothing per frame. Bars and couplings are written through motion values; React renders only when the snapped day changes.
- Reduced motion: no train — every car jumps to its place when the deadline changes and locked cars do not lean; amber, dates, couplings and the summary still change.
- A task that would have to start before a task it needs has finished (behind a locked one) is ringed, its coupling breaks into a dashed danger line and the header says what it waits on — in words, never colour alone. Below a 40rem container the board becomes a list with start dates under a deadline stepper, and a deadline change rolls the dates a cascade step per car.
- Dates are whole UTC days and are formatted by hand, so the server and the browser draw the same plan.

### Webhook Replay (KQ-1746) — `webhook-replay`
See every delivery, and send a failed one again.

A webhook endpoint's delivery log where a failed delivery can be sent again. Replay sends a pulse along its row — a comet riding one motion value for 520 ms on the move ease, from the event name, under the columns, to the status chip — and if the answer is not back the head breathes at the chip until it is; then the chip flips about its horizontal axis, out on the exit ease and in on springs.snap with a soft success ring, or still failing, in on springs.flick to the new error code with the new response under the event. Rows open with Enter to the payload, headers and response at their measured height on springs.glide, Up and Down walk the rows, R replays, and the endpoint can be paused and its signing secret revealed or rotated.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/webhook-replay`

Props:
- `chipStyle`: "pill" | "tag" | "dot" (default "pill") — How each status code is drawn: a tinted pill, a square tag with a leading bar, or a dot and the bare code.
- `payloadTheme`: "plain" | "tinted" | "night" (default "tinted") — How payloads, headers and responses are coloured: one ink, tinted tokens, or a dark code panel in both themes.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Row height and type in the log.
- `endpoints`: WebhookEndpoint[] (default defaultWebhookEndpoints) — Each { id, name, url (no scheme), events, secret, paused? }.
- `deliveries / defaultDeliveries`: WebhookDelivery[] (default — / defaultWebhookDeliveries) — Most recent first: { id, endpoint, event, status, duration, attempt, at, payload, response?, replayAs? }; controlled or initial.
- `onDeliveriesChange`: (deliveries) => void — Fires with every delivery after a replay lands or a test event is sent.
- `endpoint / defaultEndpoint`: string (default — / the first) — The endpoint shown, by id; controlled or initial.
- `onEndpointChange`: (id) => void — Fires from the tab press or arrow key that chose another endpoint.
- `onReplay`: (delivery) => WebhookReplayResult | Promise<WebhookReplayResult> | void — Replay was pressed. Return { status, duration, body? } or a promise of it; return nothing and the delivery's replayAs answers. A rejected promise reads as no answer.
- `onPause`: (endpoint, paused) => void — Pause or Resume was pressed.
- `onRotateSecret`: (endpoint) => string | void — Rotate was confirmed. Return the new secret, or nothing for a generated one.
- `onSendTest`: (endpoint) => void — Send test event was pressed on an empty log; a test delivery is added and lands with its own pulse.
- `now`: number (default defaultWebhookNow) — The current time in ms; delivery times are read against it. Never read from the clock.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows placeholder rows; error explains and offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the log failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Webhooks") — The heading.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the surface in px; the log scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be replayed, paused or rotated.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: endpoints are a tablist and the filter a radio group. The log is an ordered list whose rows are disclosure buttons with one tab stop: Up and Down move between rows, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens the payload, headers and response (a tablist), R replays a failed row. Replay is also its own labelled button, kept focusable with aria-disabled while sending or paused, and its name says why.
- Status chips carry the code as text and the words in their title and in the row's accessible name ("504 Gateway timeout"); success and failure differ in colour and in words. One polite announcement when a replay starts and one with its result.
- The pulse is one motion value and three tail segments derived from it; the secret's scramble is one short tween; nothing runs at rest, and both stop on unmount. The pulse's route is measured from the row when the replay starts, so it follows the wide layout or the stacked one.
- Reduced motion: no pulse, flip or bloom; the chip dims while sending and cross-fades to its new code, panels open without growing and the secret swaps without scrambling. Codes, attempts and times still update.
- Secrets are masked until revealed with an explicit action, and signature headers stay masked. The night payload theme is a deliberately fixed dark panel; the other two use tokens and follow the theme.

### Sync Pairs (KQ-1747) — `sync-pairs`
Pair the fields and choose which way each flows.

A two-way field mapping between two apps whose fields face each other across a gutter of soft cables. Dragging from a field draws a live cable 1:1 under the pointer; plugged into a compatible field its sag drops in slack and swings taut on springs.recoil, two visible bounces of a rope catching. Pressing a cable's knot cycles its direction — right, left, both — and the arrowhead turns on springs.flick and slides along the curve to its new end on springs.glide, a second chevron sliding out for both ways; lossy flows draw the cable in warn and name what is lost, and types that do not convert refuse to pair. Each side is a listbox: Enter opens a partner list, D turns a pair, Delete unpairs, and narrow containers turn the cables into rows with direction chips.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sync-pairs`

Props:
- `cableStyle`: "soft" | "taut" | "dashed" (default "soft") — How a cable is drawn: a sagging cable with a soft under-stroke that swings on recoil, a nearly straight one that settles on snap, or a dotted lead.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Row height (36, 44 or 52px) and type; regular and roomy rows also name the partner.
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "moss" | "plum" | "ember" (default "cobalt") — The cables' and ports' pigment at a fixed lightness; lossy cables are always warn.
- `leftApp`: SyncApp (default defaultSyncLeftApp) — The app on the left: { name, initials }.
- `rightApp`: SyncApp (default defaultSyncRightApp) — The app on the right: { name, initials }.
- `leftFields`: SyncField[] (default defaultSyncLeftFields) — The left app's fields: { id, name, type } with type text, email, phone, number, money, date, datetime, picklist or boolean.
- `rightFields`: SyncField[] (default defaultSyncRightFields) — The right app's fields.
- `pairs / defaultPairs`: SyncPair[] (default — / defaultSyncPairs) — Each { left, right, direction: "right" | "left" | "both" }; one partner per field. Controlled or initial.
- `onPairsChange`: (pairs) => void — Fires with every pair after a pairing, an unpairing or a direction change.
- `onPair`: (pair) => void — Two fields were paired; any pair it replaced is reported through onUnpair first.
- `onUnpair`: (pair) => void — A pair was taken apart.
- `onDirectionChange`: (pair, direction) => void — A pair's direction was cycled; directions a type cannot flow in are skipped.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Loading shows placeholder rows; error explains and offers Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the fields failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Field sync") — The heading.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the surface in px; the board scrolls inside it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be paired, unpaired or turned.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: each side is a listbox with one tab stop — Up and Down move, Left and Right cross to the other side (to the partner when there is one). Enter or Space opens the partner list, a popover listbox that names what each type does to the values (converts, lossy and why, or doesn't convert); Enter pairs, Escape closes and returns focus. On a paired field or a knot, D turns the pair and Delete unpairs; knots are buttons in the tab order.
- Pointer: drag from a field to its partner, or tap one field and then another. A drag captures only after 4px, so a press is still a tap; dragging a plugged field's cable into empty space unpairs it, and a drop the types refuse flies back to its port.
- Every cable's sag, knot and chevrons are motion values driven by springs that stop when they settle; paths are rebuilt from them with useTransform, row positions are arithmetic and the gutter is measured once by a ResizeObserver — nothing runs at rest.
- Reduced motion: cables appear without swinging, chevrons jump to their ends and a refused drop simply disappears; the live cable still follows the pointer because it is the gesture. Lossy pairs are named in the knot's label, under narrow rows and in the footer, never by colour alone.
- Below a 36rem container the cables become rows with a direction chip that cycles, an unpair button, and an Add a pair form of two native selects.

### Quick Fix (KQ-1754) — `quick-fix`
Problems underlined, fixes one keystroke away.

A code editor panel built from code and diagnostics: every problem is underlined under its exact columns in its severity's colour, marked in the gutter and counted in the header. Applying a fix morphs the faulty token into its correction character by character — the common start and end stay, each changed slot rolls on springs.snap in a left-to-right cascade and slots that appear or vanish grow or shrink on springs.glide — while the squiggle unwinds, its coil straightening on glide before it retracts into its middle, and the count ticks down on snap. The text is a real textarea over a painted layer: F8 and Shift+F8 walk the problems, gliding the code into view and opening a peek under the line, Command or Control with period opens the fixes menu at the caret, and edits shift the problems after them.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/quick-fix`

Props:
- `squiggleStyle`: "wave" | "dots" | "line" (default "wave") — How a problem is underlined: a sine wave, a row of dots (they close into a rule as a fix unwinds them) or a straight rule.
- `editorTheme`: "paper" | "slate" | "mono" (default "paper") — The surface and syntax colour: the card with quiet hues, a sunk slate panel with stronger hues and a tinted gutter, or no syntax colour so only the squiggles carry colour.
- `fontScale`: number (default 1) — Code size as a multiple of 13px; line height, squiggle size and gutter follow.
- `code / defaultCode`: string (default — / defaultQuickFixCode) — The source text.

Tab leaves the editor as usual.
- The editor is a real textarea over a painted layer, so caret, selection, typing and native shortcuts all work; edits shift every problem after them and drop one whose range they touch, for the host to re-check.
- Under reduced motion the token cross-fades instead of rolling, the squiggle fades instead of unwinding, and the code jumps into view; counts, marks and the clean state still change.

### Screenshot Markup (KQ-1755) — `screenshot-markup`
Arrow it, box it, and blur what's private.

An image annotation editor: arrows, boxes, labels and redaction over a screenshot, every mark kept in the image's own pixels. Drawing an arrow, the shaft bows behind the hand — a curve whose control point trails the pointer on springs.glide — and on release it pulls taut while the head springs into place on springs.recoil with two visible bounces. The redact brush pixelates whatever passes under it: cells of a grid fill with the real mosaic of the image beneath, popping in as separate tiles on springs.flick, and when the stroke ends they settle — gaps closing and corners squaring on springs.snap in the order they were laid — into one solid mosaic. Tools have single keys, the canvas has a keyboard cursor so Enter, arrows and Enter draw any mark, [ and ] select marks, arrows nudge them and Delete removes them, and undo and redo walk a history.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/screenshot-markup`
