- `image`: MarkupImage (default defaultMarkupImage) — The screenshot as { width, height, alt, src?, content? }: a raster src, or SVG content drawn in the image's coordinates (the default Basinworks dashboard).
- `annotations / defaultAnnotations`: MarkupAnnotation[] (default — / defaultMarkupAnnotations) — Marks in image pixels: arrow { x1, y1, x2, y2 }, box { x, y, w, h }, text { x, y, text } and redact { size, cells: [column, row][] }.
- `onChange`: (annotations) => void — Fires with every mark after one is drawn, moved, nudged, edited, removed, undone or redone.
- `tool / defaultTool`: "select" | "arrow" | "box" | "text" | "redact" (default — / "arrow") — The active tool.
- `onToolChange`: (tool) => void — Fires from the button or single key (V, A, B, T, R) that picked a tool.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string | null (default — / null) — The selected mark's id.
- `onSelectedChange`: (id) => void — Fires when a click, a bracket key or a new mark changes the selection.

- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the screenshot has arrived: loading shows a ruled frame and a progress bar, error offers Try again.

- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the screenshot failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Basinworks · levels, 14 Oct") — The editor's heading.
- `cellSize`: number (default 16) — The redaction grid in image px: the size of each pixelated block.
- `height`: number (default 540) — The editor's tallest height in px; the image letterboxes inside.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Marks can be viewed but not drawn, moved, removed or exported.
- `className`: string — Classes for the editor's outer box.

Notes:
- The canvas is one focusable group with a keyboard cursor: arrows move it (Shift for larger steps), Enter starts a mark of the current tool there, arrows extend it and Enter ends it with the same landing as the pointer; [ and ] select marks, arrows nudge the selected one (Shift for ten pixels), Delete removes it and Escape cancels a mark or clears the selection, consumed only when it does something.
- Redaction is a real mosaic: an SVG pixelate filter (blur, sample, dilate) over a use-copy of the image, clipped to the brushed cells, so it works on drawn SVG and raster src images alike; the source pixels remain in the page, so export the flattened image server-side before sharing.
- Under reduced motion the arrow draws straight and its head appears in place, cells land as a solid mosaic, and moves are immediate; the pixelation and every count are unchanged.
- Nothing loops at rest: the trailing control point, the head's landing and the settle are finite springs, and the brush adds cells to state only when it crosses a new one.
- Arrow and box colours ride on plain groups through currentColor, so a changed accent re-colours marks that motion is animating.

### Schema Table (KQ-1756) — `schema-table`

A database schema editor where each field's name, type and options sit above its sample column, so a change of type is something you watch. A bug report that starts from the page it is about: Report a bug flashes the page (or closes a shutter on it, or lifts it toward you), then a copy of the page shrinks along a straight path into the form's thumbnail slot on springs.glide and drops into it on springs.recoil while the form's sections rise into place in cascade order. A drag on the thumbnail draws a highlight or an opaque redaction from the press point, the signed-in address is hidden on its own, environment rows can be removed and restored, and Send becomes its own progress bar that follows the host's progress on glide; a failed upload keeps every word, box and choice. Notes:

- Real screen capture is the host's job: pass what was on screen as `page` (an SVG or an element that fills a 16:10 box) and the areas to hide as `sensitiveAreas`. The capture is drawn, so it costs nothing until Report is pressed.

### Ease Check (KQ-1760) — `ease-check`
One quick question, right after the task.

A one-row question for right after a task, whose effort slider is a string between two pegs: pressing rests the finger on it, dragging moves the thumb 1:1 while dragging up or down bends the string under the thumb into two straight runs with a rounded apex, and letting go settles the thumb on its step on springs.snap and plucks the string, which rings through straight on a spring with springs.recoil's character (its stiffness set by the track and the tension) carrying the release velocity. A release, a tap or Enter sends the answer; low scores open a short why field on a measured glide, others say thanks and fold the question away, and a task is never asked twice. It is a real slider: arrows step and pluck lightly, Page keys move two, Home and End jump.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ease-check`

Props:
- `question`: string (default "How easy was that export?") — The question, asked right after the task; it also labels the slider.
- `taskId`: string (default "waylight-export-q3") — The finished task this asks about. Each task is asked once: answered or dismissed, it never returns.
- `stepCount`: number (default 7) — Points on the scale, 3 to 10: ticks, labels and keyboard steps.
- `labels`: string[] — One label per point, hardest first. Defaults to a preset for 3, 5 and 7 points, else the end labels and "n of N".
- `minLabel`: string (default "Very hard") — The hard end's label.
- `maxLabel`: string (default "Very easy") — The easy end's label.
- `lowThreshold`: number (default ⌊(stepCount − 1) / 2⌋) — Scores at or below this open the why field.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default — / null) — The score, 1 to stepCount, or null before an answer; controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the release, tap or key that chose a score.
- `onAnswer`: (score: number, taskId: string) => void — An answer was sent: on release, on a tap, or on Enter.
- `onComment`: (text: string, score: number, taskId: string) => void — The why field was sent, with the score it explains.
- `onDismiss`: (taskId: string) => void — The question was dismissed without an answer.
- `trackStyle`: "string" | "cord" | "beads" (default "string") — What the slider is made of: a fine string that rings fast, a thick cord that sways slowly, or beads on a thread, one per point.
- `tone`: "accent" | "score" | "ink" (default "accent") — The filled run and thumb: cobalt; a colour that warms from red at the hard end through amber to green; or ink.
- `tension`: number (default 0.5) — How taut the string is, 0 to 1: tighter rings faster and settles sooner.
- `whyPrompt`: string (default "What got in the way?") — The why field's prompt and label.
- `thanksMs`: number (default 1800) — How long the thanks shows before the question folds away, in ms.
- `persist`: boolean (default false) — Also remember asked tasks in localStorage, so they stay answered across visits.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The slider and buttons do nothing.
- `className`: string — Classes for the question's outer box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the slider is role="slider" labelled by the question, with aria-valuetext such as "5 of 7, fairly easy". Arrows step from the waiting middle thumb, Page Up and Page Down move two, Home and End jump, and Enter sends; after a key the line under the string says "Enter to send". In the why field Enter sends and Escape skips.
- Reduced motion: the string never bends or rings and the thumb moves to its step at once; the value, the fill, the why field and the thanks still change, and the fold is instant.
- Ask once: pass a stable `taskId` per finished task. Answered and dismissed task ids are remembered for the page's life (and in localStorage with `persist`), and a question for one of them renders nothing — so it is safe to mount it after every export.
- It fits one row at 316px: the question wraps to two short lines beside the slider, and the end labels appear from 30rem. Give it the width of the task's own surface.
- There is no loop: the string's spring runs only after a press or a key and stops when it settles, and the path is rebuilt from two motion values with every coordinate rounded.

### Point and Tell (KQ-1761) — `point-and-tell`
Point at the part of the page you mean.

Feedback that points: Point turns the page into targets, and hovering — or Tab, which cycles through the parts while point mode is on — finds the smallest part under the pointer while one fine measuring outline travels to its box on springs.snap, with its size in a tag and guides out to the page's edges. A click or Enter pins it: a crop of the page lifts off at the part's own box and flies into its slot in the form on springs.glide on one uniform scale while the outline flashes. Crops are the page drawn again and scaled, sensitive values are masked in every crop, Escape leaves point mode, and Send shows sending, sent and failed — a failure keeps the note and every pin.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/point-and-tell`

Props:
- `targets`: PointTarget[] (default defaultPointTargets) — The page's parts as { id, label, kind, rect: { x, y, w, h } in percent of a 16:10 page, text?, sensitive? }; each kind (header, nav, heading, field, select, button, chart, table, card, note, badge) draws itself.
- `pageLabel`: string (default "Fieldline · Equipment checkout") — Names the page in its frame's bar and the point-mode group.
- `form`: PointForm — The form's words: { heading, prompt, placeholder, sendLabel }, defaulting to Feedback, a one-line prompt, "What should we know?" and Send.
- `pointing / defaultPointing`: boolean (default — / false) — Whether point mode is on, controlled or initial.
- `onPointingChange`: (pointing: boolean) => void — Fires from the button, key or send that turned point mode on or off.
- `pins / defaultPins`: string[] (default — / []) — The pinned target ids in pin order, controlled or initial.
- `onPinsChange`: (pins: string[]) => void — Fires with every pin after one is added or removed.
- `onPoint`: (target: PointTarget) => void — A part of the page was pinned.
- `onSubmit`: (feedback: { message: string; targets: PointTarget[] }) => void | Promise<unknown> — Send was pressed. Return a promise to show sending; a rejection shows the failure and keeps the note and pins.
- `onCancel`: () => void — Cancel was pressed; pins and note are cleared.
- `outlineStyle`: "measure" | "dashed" | "corners" (default "measure") — The pointing outline: a fine box with corner ticks, guides and a size tag; a dashed box with the tag; or four corner brackets.
- `maskStyle`: "blur" | "bars" | "dots" (default "blur") — How sensitive values look in crops: blurred, covered by solid bars, or replaced by dots. The live page is untouched.
- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Outline, guides, pin numbers, the point-mode tint and Send — any CSS colour.
- `maxPins`: number (default 4) — The most parts that can be pinned at once.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 540) — Tallest the surface grows before it scrolls inside, in px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be pointed at, pinned or sent.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: Point is a toggle button. In point mode the parts are buttons over the drawn page in reading order; focus moves to the first, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through them (a loop until you leave), Enter or Space pins or unpins, and Escape leaves point mode from anywhere in the surface and returns focus to Point. Removing a pin moves focus to the next pin's remove button.
- Reduced motion: the outline jumps to each box and fades, a pin appears in its slot with a fade instead of flying, and the sent check is drawn at once; pins, masks and the send states all still show.
- Mark parts that show personal data `sensitive`: they read normally on the page and are masked in every crop and in the copy that flies, so a screenshot of the form never carries them.
- The page is drawn in container units from `targets`, so it scales to any width and each crop is the same page at 640px, scaled and clipped — exact, and free of images. Pass your own parts with percent rects to point at your own screen.
- Nothing runs while idle: hover hit-testing is the buttons themselves (smaller parts sit above larger ones), the outline moves only when the part under the pointer or focus changes, and the flying crop exists only during a pin.

### Theme Sorter (KQ-1762) — `theme-sorter`
Sort incoming feedback into themes that count.

A feedback inbox you sort by hand: a card lifts after 4px of travel and follows the pointer 1:1 as a copy above both columns, leaning with its speed, while the theme under it swells on springs.snap. Dropped on a theme it is squeezed in — narrowing on springs.glide and flattening 60ms behind on the same spring toward the theme's centre — the theme gulps on springs.recoil as its tally rolls up on snap, and once it is in the themes re-rank by count with a layout glide; dropped anywhere else it springs home with the release velocity. The inbox is one tab stop with roving focus: Up and Down move, T or Enter opens a theme menu with type-ahead and New theme, A or Delete archives, and a failed tag springs the card back into its slot with a note.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/theme-sorter`

Props:
- `items / defaultItems`: FeedbackItem[] (default — / defaultThemeSorterItems) — Feedback as { id, quote, customer, company, source: "email" | "call" | "survey" | "chat" | "review", plan, sentiment: "positive" | "neutral" | "negative", at, themeId?, archived? }, controlled or initial. Untagged, unarchived items wait in the inbox; tagged ones count toward their theme.
- `onItemsChange`: (items: FeedbackItem[]) => void — Fires with every item after a tag, an archive or a failed tag's revert.
- `themes / defaultThemes`: FeedbackTheme[] (default — / defaultThemeSorterThemes) — Themes as { id, name }, controlled or initial; shown most-counted first.
- `onThemesChange`: (themes: FeedbackTheme[]) => void — Fires with every theme after one is created.
- `onTag`: (itemId: string, themeId: string) => void | Promise<unknown> — An item was tagged by a drop or the theme menu. Return a promise; a rejection springs the item back into the inbox with a note and rolls the tally back.
- `onCreateTheme`: (theme: FeedbackTheme) => void — A theme was created from New theme; the item it was opened on is tagged into it.
- `onArchive`: (itemId: string) => void — An item was archived without a theme.
- `bucketStyle`: "tray" | "jar" | "row" (default "tray") — How a theme looks: a tray with its count, a share bar coloured by its sentiment mix and a percentage; a jar whose level rises with its count; or a compact row. Chips at narrow widths keep a hint of each.
- `density`: "compact" | "regular" | "roomy" (default "regular") — Card padding, quote size and gaps.
- `sentimentPalette`: "signal" | "duo" | "mono" (default "signal") — Sentiment colours: green, ink and red; cobalt, ink and amber; or ink alone, told apart by the dot, ring and diamond marks.
- `now`: number | Date (default defaultThemeSorterNow) — The moment ages count from, so the server and the browser print the same text.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" | "error" (default "ready") — Whether the items have arrived: loading shows skeleton cards and themes, error a line with Try again.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Try again was pressed after the items failed to load.
- `title`: string (default "Feedback inbox") — The inbox's heading and accessible name.
- `maxHeight`: number (default 540) — Tallest the surface grows before its columns scroll, in px.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be dragged, tagged, created or archived.
- `className`: string — Classes for the surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the inbox is one tab stop with roving focus — Up and Down move between quotes, Home and End jump. T or Enter opens a theme menu on the card (arrows move, a letter jumps to the theme it starts, Enter tags, Escape returns to the card, New theme… becomes a name field); A, Delete or Backspace archives. Focus moves to the next quote when one leaves, and to the inbox itself when the last one does.
- Reduced motion: nothing lifts, leans or squeezes — a tagged card fades out of the inbox, counts update, the themes re-order at once and a failed tag fades the card back; jar levels and share bars change without travel.
- Touch: the grip is the drag handle (touch-action none), so a finger anywhere else on a card still scrolls the inbox. The dragged copy lives above both columns, so it can cross from the scrolling inbox to the themes without being clipped.
- Themes re-rank only once a tag has landed, so the theme a card is flying into never moves out from under it; the re-rank is announced when the leader changes.
- Nothing runs while idle: a drag sets motion values only, theme bounds are read as the pointer moves, and every animation and pending timer is dropped on unmount.

### Macro Reply (KQ-1763) — `macro-reply`
Answer the ticket and set its fields in one move.

An agent's ticket view — the conversation, a customer sidebar with plan, fields and earlier tickets, and a reply box — where # opens the macros and picking one types its reply at a steady pace while every field it changes switches at its own moment: a wash sweeps the field, the old value rolls out and the new one rises on springs.snap, a set-by-macro dot pops on springs.flick, and a chip for the change lands in the reply's footer on snap, so nothing changes unseen even when the sidebar is a tab. Sent replies rise into the conversation on springs.glide. The reply is a combobox over the macro listbox (arrows, Enter or Tab to apply, Escape to close), any key finishes a typing macro, and Ctrl+Enter sends.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/macro-reply`

Props:
- `sidebarSide`: "left" | "right" (default "right") — Which side the customer sidebar sits on; at narrow widths, which side its tab sits on.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Type size, paddings and gaps.
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "jade" | "amber" | "mono" (default "cobalt") — The macro wash, typing hairline, change chips and Send.
- `ticket`: MacroTicket (default defaultMacroTicket) — Subject, number, channel, status, priority, tags and messages. Field changes from the host on the same ticket id flash like a macro's.
- `customer`: MacroCustomer (default defaultMacroCustomer) — The customer shown in the sidebar: name, email, plan, seats, since and earlier tickets.
- `macros`: MacroDef[] (default defaultMacros) — Each macro's name, reply text ({first}, {agent} and {number} are filled) and the fields it sets.
- `agent`: string (default "Theo") — The agent replying; fills {agent} and signs sent messages.
- `now`: number (default defaultMacroNow) — The moment relative times count from, ms. Never read from the clock.
- `status`: "ready" | "loading" (default "ready") — Loading draws skeletons in the same boxes.
- `onApplyMacro`: (macro: MacroDef) => void — A macro was applied, before it starts typing.
- `onSend`: (reply: { text, fields, macroId }) => void | Promise — The reply was sent with its fields. A promise holds Send; a rejection keeps the draft and offers Retry.
- `onStatusChange`: (status, source: "macro" | "field" | "reopen") => void — The ticket's status changed, and what changed it.
- `onFieldsChange`: (fields: { status, priority, tags }) => void — Any field changed, with all three.
- `typeSpeed`: number (default 90) — How fast a macro types, in characters a second.
- `flash`: number (default 640) — How long a changed field flashes, ms.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the surface, px; the conversation scrolls inside it.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Reply to {first}…  Type # for macros") — The reply box's placeholder.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Read only: nothing can be typed, applied or sent.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.
- `ref`: Ref<MacroReplyHandle> — applyMacro(id) applies a macro as if picked; focusReply() moves focus to the reply.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the reply textarea is a combobox over the macro listbox — # (or the Macros button) opens it, typing filters, Up and Down move, Enter or Tab applies, Escape closes. While a macro types the reply is read-only and busy, and any key finishes it at once. Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter sends.
- Each macro is announced once as a sentence when it lands ("Refund duplicate charge applied: status Pending, priority Low, tag refund added."); status and priority are native selects under a drawn face, so they keep every platform's own keyboard and picker.
- Below a 36rem container the sidebar becomes a tab with a badge counting unsent macro changes, and the change chips stay in the reply footer, so a narrow agent still sees everything a macro set.
- Typing is one linear tween that writes the draft only when the character count changes; nothing runs at rest, and timers stop on unmount or when the ticket id changes.
- Reduced motion: the macro text arrives in one step and the fields swap under a fading wash with no roll or sweep; every change is still shown and announced.
- Accent colours derive from the theme tokens (accent, success, warn, ink), so all four read in light and dark.

### Request Tracker (KQ-1764) — `request-tracker`
Where your request is, and whose turn it is.

A customer's own page for a support request: whose turn it is in words, a bead riding the stages from received to solved, the updates as headed articles and a reply box. Replying (Ctrl+Enter) lands your update at the top on glide and passes the turn back with an honest next-reply time, and a solved request asks for a rating in a radiogroup driven by the arrow keys.

- `accent`: "cobalt" | "jade" | "amber" | "mono" (default "cobalt") — The bead, the rail's fill, the turn and Send.

- `onReopen`: () => void — Reopen request was pressed on a solved request.
- `onRate`: (rating: "poor" | "okay" | "good" | "great") => void — A solved request was rated.
- `onRetry`: () => void — Retry was pressed after the updates failed to load.
- `company`: string (default "Basinworks") — Who is answering.

- `pulse`: boolean (default true) — Let the bead breathe while the request waits on you.
- `height`: number (default 540) — Height of the page, px; the updates scroll inside.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be sent, closed, reopened or rated.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the reply textarea follows the turn card in the tab order and is labelled by the question it answers; Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter sends, and when the box folds away focus moves to Add more detail. The rating is a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End), and the updates list is a focusable region so it scrolls from the keyboard.
- The stages are one ordered list with aria-current="step" and a completed, current or to do word per stage; the bead, line and dots are decoration. Turn changes are announced once as a sentence.
- The bead's breathing is the only loop and runs only while the request waits on the customer, the page is in view, the tab is visible, motion is allowed and pulse is on.
- Below a 40rem container it is one column with the reply box at the foot; above it, the turn card, reply box and request details move to a side column. Under 19rem the rail names only the current stage.
- Reduced motion: the bead and fill move in one step, the ring holds still at half strength and the reply box opens without travel; stage, turn and rating still change.

### Before You Send (KQ-1765) — `before-you-send`
Answers appear while you're still writing in.

A contact form that searches the help articles as the subject is typed and slides the matches up between the subject and the rest of the form: the panel's measured height opens on springs.glide, each answer rises 8px in cascade order and its relevance bar grows on glide a beat later, and a changing query re-ranks them in place on glide. Choosing one opens it in the panel, and This solved it folds the form down to a thank-you on glide — a ring landing on springs.recoil, a check drawn on springs.flick — instead of a ticket. The subject is a combobox: Down and Up walk the answers, Enter opens one, Escape hides them, and a failed search never blocks Send.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/before-you-send`

Props:
- `resultStyle`: "cards" | "rows" | "wash" (default "cards") — How the answers are drawn: a row of cards, hairline rows with a meter and percentage, or rows whose relevance is a wash behind the title.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Control heights, type and gaps.
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "jade" | "amber" | "mono" (default "cobalt") — Relevance bars, the active answer, Send and the thank-you ring.
- `articles`: HelpArticle[] (default defaultHelpArticles) — The help articles searched: title, summary, steps, topic, keywords, read time and href.
- `topics`: ContactTopic[] (default defaultContactTopics) — The topics offered as a radiogroup above the subject.
- `value / defaultValue`: ContactDraft / Partial<ContactDraft> (default — / { topic: "billing", email: "jun@coldbrook.studio" }) — The draft (topic, subject, details, email), controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (draft: ContactDraft) => void — Fires from every edit with the whole draft.
- `onSearch`: (query, topic) => ArticleMatch[] | Promise<ArticleMatch[]> | void — A settled search. Return matches to replace the built-in scoring; a rejection shows a quiet note and never blocks Send.
- `onSolved`: (article: HelpArticle, query: string) => void — This solved it was chosen: the form closes with a thank-you and nothing is sent.
- `onSend`: (draft: ContactDraft) => { reference? } | Promise<{ reference? }> | void — The form was sent after validation. A promise holds Send; resolve a reference to show it, reject to keep everything and offer Try again.
- `onOpenArticle`: (article: HelpArticle) => void — Full article was pressed in a preview.
- `company`: string (default "Fieldline") — Whose support this is.
- `responseTime`: string (default "within a day") — How soon a message is answered, in words.
- `maxResults`: number (default 3) — The most answers shown.
- `minRelevance`: number (default 0.25) — Answers below this relevance (0 to 1) are not shown.
- `searchDelay`: number (default 160) — Quiet time after typing before a search runs, ms.
- `height`: number (default 540) — The tallest the surface grows, px; past it the form scrolls inside.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be typed, chosen or sent.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the subject is a combobox over the answers' listbox — Down and Up move (Down also brings back answers hidden with Escape), Home and End jump, Enter opens the active answer instead of submitting, Escape hides them. A preview's heading takes focus; Escape or Back to answers returns to the subject.
- Each settled search is announced once, and only when what it found changed (a count, nothing, or an outage). Field errors use aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and the first invalid field takes focus on Send.
- The built-in ranking (also exported as scoreArticles) is deterministic, so server and browser agree; pass onSearch to rank on your own index. Stale answers are dropped by a sequence number, and a failing search only ever adds a quiet line.
- Below a 30rem container every result style collapses to titles with a thin bar; above 36rem the cards sit three across.
- Reduced motion: the panel opens at its height, answers and bars appear in place at their widths, and the thank-you cross-fades with its check already drawn.

### Callback Queue (KQ-1766) — `callback-queue`
Wait your turn, or ask us to call you back.

A live support queue with your place, an honest wait (a likely figure and a range from the line, the average chat and the agents on shift) and the agents on shift. When the queue moves, the person at the front goes into the desk on the exit ease, everyone behind glides one place forward on springs.glide, and your place and the estimate roll down digit by digit, the estimate a beat later. Call me back opens a picker — a number and a radiogroup of times — and booking turns your token into a time chip in its place, one element whose layout glides from circle to pill; your turn, leaving, closed hours and a full queue each say what happens next.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/callback-queue`

- `tokenStyle`: "dots" | "tickets" | "lane" (default "dots") — How the line is drawn: circles to the desk, numbered ticket stubs, or a lane you ride along.
- `density`: "compact" | "cozy" | "roomy" (default "cozy") — Token size, type and gaps.
- `accent`: "cobalt" | "jade" | "amber" | "mono" (default "cobalt") — Your token, the estimate and the primary button.
- `queue`: QueueSnapshot (default defaultQueue) — position (1 is next, 0 your turn), waiting, capacity, avgHandleSeconds, ticket and joinedAt. A lower position moves you forward.
- `agents`: QueueAgent[] (default defaultQueueAgents) — Who is on shift and whether each is free, on a chat or on a break.
- `now`: number (default defaultQueueNow) — The moment times count from, ms. Never read from the clock.
- `status`: "open" | "closed" | "full" | "loading" (default "open") — Open, closed for the day, full, or loading.
- `hours`: { open: number; close: number } (default { open: 480, close: 1200 }) — Opening hours in minutes after midnight (UTC); they set the closed message and the callback times.
- `callbackSlots`: CallbackSlot[] (default the next three half hours, or tomorrow morning when closed) — The times offered for a callback; at null means as soon as an agent is free.
- `defaultPhone`: string (default "07700 900418") — The number a callback goes to until it's changed.
- `company`: string (default "Coldbrook") — Whose queue this is.
- `onRequestCallback`: ({ phone, slot }) => void | Promise — A callback was booked. A promise holds the button; a rejection keeps the picker open with a message.
- `onCancelCallback`: () => void — A booked callback was cancelled; you're back in the line.
- `onLeave`: () => void — Leave queue was pressed.
- `onRejoin`: () => void — Rejoin was pressed after leaving.
- `onJoinChat`: () => void — Join chat was pressed when it was your turn.
- `maxTokens`: number (default 5) — The most people drawn ahead of you; the rest fold into a count.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing can be booked, left or joined.
- `className`: string — Classes for the outer surface.

Notes:
- Keyboard: every action is a button. Call me back opens a form whose number field takes focus; the times are a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End), Enter books, and Escape cancels back to Call me back. After booking, leaving or rejoining, focus moves to the new state's heading or button once it arrives.
- The line itself is decoration; one sentence carries it for assistive technology ("You're 4th in line, 3 people ahead. About 6 minutes, usually 4 to 8."), and each move is announced politely once, computed from the new place.
- The component runs no loop of its own: everything moves on a prop change or a press. Drive queue.position from your server, and pause your own polling while the page is hidden.
- The estimate is a figure and a range, never a promise: position × average chat ÷ agents on shift, widened to 0.8–1.3× and rounded to whole minutes.
- Reduced motion: tokens re-place without travel, digits cross-fade, and the token-to-chip swap is a cross-fade; position, estimate and states still update and are announced.

### Overage Forecast (KQ-1768) — `overage-forecast`
Where usage will land by the end of the month.

A metered-usage panel where each meter is a small chart: history up to today, the plan's allowance as a hairline, and a forecast cone fanning from today's reading to the period's end, its share above the allowance drawn in warn. When a meter is first seen the history draws across and the cone grows out of today on springs.glide, a beat apart per meter, and turning on planned load springs every cone's ends to their new values on the same spring so each fan widens and lifts while the overage and the projected bill roll to their new figures. - `clips`: ClipThreadClip[] (default defaultClips) — The thread, oldest first: { id, author, role?, at, duration, title?, scene?, transcript: { at, text }[], reactions?: { kind, count, mine?, marks? }[], replyTo?, processing? }.
- `selected / defaultSelected`: string (default — / the first ready clip) — The clip in the player, controlled or initial.

- `onReply`: (clipId) => void — "Reply with a clip" was pressed on the clip in the player.
- `onReact`: (clipId, kind, at, on) => void — A reaction ("agree" | "love" | "idea" | "question") was toggled at a moment of the clip, in seconds.

- `skip`: number (default 5) — Seconds the arrow keys skip on the frame and the track.

- `accent`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — Word capsule, playhead, fill, reaction markers, rings and the chosen card — any CSS colour; fills take its hue at a fixed lightness.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the frame is a play/pause button whose Left and Right skip; the track is a slider (arrows ±skip, Page keys twice that, Home, End, Space plays); the strip is a horizontal listbox (Left, Right, Home, End, Enter or Space to play a clip); transcript lines are buttons walked with Up and Down, and Enter jumps to a line. Space anywhere outside a control plays.
- Pointer: hovering a strip thumbnail skims its frames under the pointer; clicking any transcript word jumps to that word and plays.
- Reduced motion: the word capsule does not travel — the current word is marked by colour and an underline — frames swap without sliding and reactions do not pop; playback, the fill, skimming and the processing ring still work, because they are content and progress.
- Performance: the clock is one linear animation on a motion value that runs only while playing; frames, the fill and the readout read that value without rendering, and the active word is React state only when it changes.
- Clips are drawn, not loaded: pass a `scene` per clip ("flow", "settings", "empty", "pricing", "mobile") and the transcript's line times drive both the words and where the cursor points.

### Pendant Drop (KQ-1782) — `pendant-drop`
A drop of colour that leans toward your hand.

A single drop of coloured liquid hangs from the top edge of its frame on surface tension over a shallow pool, drawn in one WebGL2 pass of signed distances joined by a smooth minimum whose reach is the viscosity and shaded as glass. Bring the pointer near and the drop leans and stretches toward it on a spring set by the viscosity, its neck thinning to a thread as the colour pools into the leading lobe; pull far enough and a droplet pinches off while the rest recoils home on the recoil spring's constants and refills from the film, and the droplet falls, is met by the pool and reabsorbed with a mound that rebounds on the same constants and ripples running out along the surface. The frame is a button: the arrow keys lean the drop and Down stretches it, Enter, Space or a click lets a drop fall, and Escape lets it hang straight.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pendant-drop`

- `reach`: number (default 0.6) — How far away the drop notices your hand, 0 (only right beside it) to 1 (across the frame).
- `palette`: "iris" | "amber" | "lagoon" | "rose" | [string, string] (default "iris") — The liquid's colours, pale at the root to deep in the lobe: a preset, or two CSS colours of your own.
- `tension`: number (default 0.5) — How far the drop stretches before a droplet pinches off, 0 (lets go early) to 1 (holds on long).
- `size`: number (default 34) — The bulb's radius in px; it shrinks to fit a small frame.
- `anchor`: number (default 0.5) — Where along the top edge the drop hangs, 0 (left) to 1 (right).
- `gravity`: number (default 1) — How fast a droplet falls, 0.5 to 2.
- `gloss`: number (default 0.6) — The glassy highlights, rim light and caustic, 0 (matte) to 1.
- `pool`: boolean (default true) — Draw the pool along the bottom edge that droplets fall into. Off, they fall out of the frame.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and touch pull the drop. Keys still lean it.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the liquid still.
- `label`: string (default "Pendant drop") — The frame's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a plip as each droplet lands. Off unless asked for.
- `onDrip`: (count: number) => void — Fires as each droplet lets go, with how many have fallen.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing reaches the drop and the frame's button is disabled.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string (default "h-96 w-full") — Sizes the frame.

Notes:
- The whole frame is one button with a spoken hint: Left and Right lean the drop, Down stretches it until it lets go and Up eases it back, Shift leans twice as far, Enter, Space or a click drops one, and Escape lets it hang straight (it is only handled while the drop is leaning).
- A mouse pulls the drop just by coming near; a finger or pen presses and drags, and the frame is touch-action none so the pull never scrolls the page. Move away faster than the drop can follow and it lets go of you instead of dripping.
- One WebGL2 pass on a fullscreen triangle, drawn at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels with the device pixel ratio capped at 2. The loop runs only while something moves and only on screen with the tab visible; a resting drop is a single frame. Context loss is handled, and without WebGL2 a drawn still stays.
- Under reduced motion the drop hangs still and the pointer does not pull it; Enter or a tap shows a still of the moment after a drip for 600 ms and onDrip still reports.
- The canvas is transparent: put the frame on any surface. Palettes are pigment at a fixed lightness, so the liquid looks the same on light and dark pages; the shadow it casts takes the theme's ink.
- The plip plays only with sound on and only after the page has had a press, since a hover alone is not a user activation.

### Redshift Jump (KQ-1784) — `redshift-jump`
The sky crowds ahead and reddens behind as you jump.

A window onto a starfield drawn with real relativistic optics: press and hold, or hold Space or Enter, and the drive's rapidity climbs at constant thrust, so the stars bunch toward the direction of travel by aberration and shift blue, the rim thins and reddens, each star streaks by how fast it crosses the sky, and near top speed the visible sky collapses onto one bright ring where the Doppler factor is one. - The rising tones play only with sound on, and only from the press, key or click that drives the jump.

### Bistable Sea (KQ-1785) — `bistable-sea`
A rolling swell on a one-bit paper display.

A slim e-paper display showing an open-sea swell under a low sun, rendered at e-paper resolution as a real perspective ocean (four wave trains, sky Fresnel, a sun-glitter path, foam on steep crests, cloud bands) and error-diffused to pure ink and paper. It refreshes like e-paper rather than video: each step of the sea rolls down the panel in bands, changed pixels flipping through their inverse before they land and keeping a faint ghost of what they were, and every few partials a full refresh flashes inverse, blanks and lands clean. - `level`: number (default 0.5) — How much of the tank is water, 0.25 to 0.8.

- `followPointer`: boolean (default true) — A hovering mouse or pen sets the lamp's height; a finger taps it there.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the lamp lights the tank from behind, 0 to 1.
- `waterColor`: string (default a blue from the accent token (light-dark)) — The water, any CSS colour; it deepens toward the floor.
- `airColor`: string (default a pale or night tint of the accent token (light-dark)) — The backlit air above the water, any CSS colour.
- `lightColor`: string (default a near-white from the accent hue) — The lamp's light, any CSS colour.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the waves where they are.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the phase of the two wave trains.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Lamp height") — The lamp control's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The lamp does not move.
- `className`: string — Sizes the tank; it fills its parent by default.

Notes:
- The lamp knob on the right wall is the one control: role="slider" from −30 to 30 with a spoken value ("Lamp 8 degrees above level"); arrows step 2°, Page Up and Down 10°, Home and End jump to the ends. On touch, drag the rail or tap the tank at the height you want.
- The scene itself is decoration (aria-hidden); children render above it in their own layer and keep every click and focus.
- Under reduced motion the waves stand still at a designed phase and the lamp moves at once, without easing — the fringes still jump to their new place.
- One WebGL2 pass (seven wavelength samples) at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels, the device pixel ratio capped at 2; it runs only on screen, in a visible tab and while the waves roll or the lamp eases, at thirty frames a second when only the waves move. Context loss stops it and a restore rebuilds.
- Colours resolve on the element and re-read on a theme change; the light-dark defaults give a pale backlit tank on light pages and a night tank on dark ones. Without WebGL2 the server's gradient still — water, meniscus and a spectral edge on each crest — stays.

### Beadwork Loom (KQ-1788) — `beadwork-loom`
A picture woven in glass beads, moving with it.

A panel of glass seed beads woven on a loom — wooden beams, warp threads between every column — whose beads take their colour from a moving picture (a slow wave, a seascape with a low sun and rolling swell, a turning flower, or any image or video), so the beadwork plays like a soft low-resolution screen, every bead shaded as a little glass barrel with its own round highlight. Each bead is also a node on a spring lattice, home on the springs.recoil constants and linked to its four neighbours: a drag grabs the warp under the finger 1:1, and on release it springs back past home in two bounces while the ripple runs along the rows, the picture bending with the beads and every highlight rolling with its bead. - `onPlayingChange`: (playing: boolean) => void — Fires from the tap or key that played or paused the picture.

### Cyclone Jar (KQ-1789) — `cyclone-jar`
Swirl the jar and a funnel forms inside.

A tall glass jar of water and fine glitter, seen side-on and a little from above: drag in circles over it — the hand's travel around the jar's axis is torque, so circles spin it up and a scrub barely does — and a funnel forms down the middle, its depth following the spin on the springs.drift constants as it narrows, while the glitter, carried by a Rankine vortex and one closed secondary cell, spirals faster as it is drawn down toward the core and is thrown out under the surface. - Colours resolve on the element and re-read when they change; the water defaults to light-dark tints so the jar reads on both themes, and glitter keeps nearer its colour on light pages so shaded flakes never look like grit.

### Mercury Gate (KQ-1790) — `mercury-gate`
A liquid gate that shows where it leads.

Lines of light rise from the horizon, one per value.

A glowing horizon with thin filaments of light rising from it, one per value of a data series — a quiet equaliser drawn in light, each filament a hairline core with a soft glow, a bloom at its tip, a flare where it meets the horizon and a faint reflection on the wet ground below. - `reflection`: number (default 0.5) — How strongly they reflect on the ground below the horizon, 0 to 1.

### Ghosting LCD (KQ-1794) — `ghosting-lcd`
A slow screen that remembers where you moved.

A reflective monochrome LCD with visible pixel gaps that you draw on: the pointer lays a soft brush whose edges are dithered through a 4×4 Bayer matrix, and every pixel answers on the slow, smeary response of an old pocket screen — darkening on a quarter of `response` and clearing on all of it — so a quick stroke leaves a longer, fainter ghost than a slow one, and each lit pixel casts a faint shadow `depth` px onto the reflector. A press squeezes the crystal into a dark bloom whose radius rides springs.recoil out and back with two visible bounces as the glass flexes; Delete wipes the glass with a scan bar. It is a focusable screen: arrow keys draw with a blinking pen (Shift for a quicker stroke), Enter and Space press.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ghosting-lcd`

Props:
- `response`: number (default 600) — How long a pixel takes to clear once released, ms (80 to 2000): the slower it is, the longer the ghosts.
- `pixel`: number (default 6) — Pixel pitch in px (3 to 12).
- `tint`: "olive" | "grey" | "teal" | "sepia" (default "olive") — The panel's tint: the classic olive pocket screen, a calculator grey, a pager teal or a warm sepia.
- `colors`: { panel?: string; ink?: string } — Overrides of the tint, as CSS colours: the panel and the lit pixels.
- `gap`: number (default 0.16) — Share of the pitch left as a gap between pixels (0 to 0.4).
- `depth`: number (default 1.5) — How far, px, each lit pixel's shadow sits below and right of it on the reflector; 0 hides the shadows.
- `brush`: number (default 1.4) — Radius of the drawing brush, in pixels (0.6 to 4).
- `dither`: boolean (default true) — Ordered (Bayer) dither at the stroke's soft edges; off, the edge is a hard threshold.
- `bloom`: number (default 0.6) — How far a press spreads through the crystal, 0 to 1; 0 turns the press bloom off.
- `text`: string (default "") — A line of pixel text the device shows in its top-left corner (A–Z, 0–9, - . : / ! ? ' +); whole words only.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer, touch and keys draw.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freezes the screen's response.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onClear`: () => void — The screen was wiped (Delete or Backspace).
- `label`: string (default "Drawing screen") — The screen's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing draws; the screen keeps what it shows, leaves the tab order and says it is disabled.
- `className`: string (default "h-52 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the screen.

Notes:
- The screen is a focusable group (aria-roledescription "drawing screen") with a key hint: arrow keys draw with a pen that blinks (and ghosts) only while keyboard-focused, Shift draws four pixels a step, Enter and Space press, Delete and Backspace wipe; a polite live region confirms presses and wipes from the keyboard.
- Mouse and pen draw on hover; touch draws while the finger is down, so the screen sets touch-action: none. The system cursor stays (a crosshair inside the screen only).
- Under reduced motion the press bloom and the wipe fade in place instead of travelling; pixels still ghost away by opacity, because what you drew is the feedback.
- Only changing pixels are visited (an active list) and lit pixels are drawn in sixteen batched alpha levels; the glass, its unlit grid and the device text are a cached layer. The loop stops when nothing on the glass is changing and never runs off screen or in a hidden page.
- Tints are pigments at fixed lightness taken from theme hues, so the glass looks like the same physical screen on light and dark pages.

### Heading Glyphs (KQ-1795) — `heading-glyphs`
Your path, set in the characters that fit it.

A cursor trail set in monospaced type behind your content: every cell the pointer crosses takes the character that fits the stroke there — a dash, pipe or slash for its heading, a weight from dots to hashes for its speed — then cools down the ramp a character at a time while its ink walks from hot to cold, so a fast stroke lingers and a slow one is soon gone. A click stamps an asterisk whose eight rays reach out on springs.recoil, one cell past and back, and cool from the centre outward. Keyboard focus on any child draws a short underline stroke under it, and Enter or Space there stamps at its centre.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/heading-glyphs`

Props:
- `ramp`: "ascii" | "box" | "dots" (default "ascii") — The type the trail is set in: plain ASCII, box-drawing strokes, or braille dots.
- `fade`: number (default 1400) — How long a cell takes to cool through the whole ramp, ms (200 to 5000).
- `cell`: number (default 14) — Cell height in px (8 to 28); a cell is a monospaced character wide (about 0.62 of that) and the glyphs are set to fit.
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default ["var(--accent-bright)", "color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent-bright) 40%, var(--ink-2))", "var(--ink-3)"]) — Inks from hot to cold, as CSS colours, mixed in oklab into eight steps.
- `sensitivity`: number (default 1600) — Pointer speed, px/s, that reaches the heaviest weight of the ramp.
- `burst`: number (default 3) — Ray length of the asterisk a click stamps, in cells; 0 turns the stamp off.
- `focusStroke`: boolean (default true) — Draw a short underline stroke under a child that takes keyboard focus.
- `grid`: boolean (default true) — A faint dot lattice at rest, like an empty type case.
- `weight`: number (default 500) — Font weight of the glyphs.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The first time the box comes into view, a stroke sets itself across it — slow, fast, slow — to show the ramp; never under reduced motion.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer, clicks and keyboard focus draw.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds every glyph where it is.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onStamp`: (cell: { col: number; row: number }) => void — A stamp landed, with the cell it centred on.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content set above the type; it stays fully interactive.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the box.

Notes:
- The painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, under a z-10 content layer: children keep their own semantics, focus order and clicks, and the system cursor is never hidden.
- Keyboard visitors get the same marks: :focus-visible on any child draws an underline stroke under it, and Enter or Space on it stamps at its centre. Touch never draws a trail (it scrolls the page); a tap stamps.
- Under reduced motion each glyph keeps the character it was given and fades by opacity over `fade`; the stamp and the focus stroke appear whole and fade.
- Only lit cells are visited and every glyph is one image draw from an atlas of the ramp in eight inks; the loop stops when the last glyph is gone and never runs off screen or in a hidden page. The resting lattice is a cached layer.
- Inks are text tokens mixed in oklab and re-read on theme change. Every glyph is centred in its cell by its own ink, so box-drawing characters from a fallback face still sit on the stroke; braille dots are drawn rather than set, so the dots ramp looks the same on every platform.

### Sea Printout (KQ-1796) — `sea-printout`
A rolling sea printed one line at a time.

A strip of continuous-feed paper — sprocket holes punched down both margins, tear-off perforations, green-bar banding and a fold crease every page — rising out of a line printer as it prints a rolling sea in overstruck ASCII, one line per tick: each line is the next slice of three Stokes swells and a short chop, shaded by the slope facing the light with crests drawn as runs of tildes, the darkest tones struck twice a hair out of register. Each line arrives in a chain printer's scattered order and the paper ratchets up on springs.snap, one crisp overshoot per line; moving the pointer sideways sets the wind on springs.drift, leaning the swell and raising whitecaps. It is a real slider: arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Home and End set the wind.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sea-printout`

Props:
- `swell`: number (default 0.6) — Height of the swell, 0 (glassy) to 1 (a heavy roll).
- `feed`: number (default 4) — Lines printed per second (1 to 12).
- `ink`: number (default 0.6) — Ribbon density, 0 (pale and sparse) to 1 (heavy, with more overstrikes).
- `wind / defaultWind`: number (default 0) — The wind, -1 (blowing from the west) to 1 (from the east); controlled or uncontrolled.
- `onWindChange`: (wind: number) => void — Fires from the pointer or the key that changed the wind, in steps of 0.05.
- `chop`: number (default 0.6) — How choppy the wind makes the sea, 0 to 1: short waves, spray and whitecaps.
- `pageLines`: number (default 24) — Lines between the paper's fold creases (8 to 66).
- `bars`: boolean (default true) — Faint green-bar banding every three lines.
- `overstrike`: boolean (default true) — Overstruck pairs for the darkest tones.
- `size`: number (default 9) — Glyph size in px (7 to 13).
- `colors`: { paper?: string; ink?: string; bar?: string } — Paper, ribbon and bar colours, any CSS colours; pigments by default, the same in both themes.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and the keys set the wind.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — The printer stops (its lamp reads off line).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — The printer whirs while you work the wind.
- `seed`: number (default 2) — Seeds the sea and the hammers' small errors.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Wind over the printed sea") — The slider's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The wind holds and the slider says it is disabled; the printer keeps printing.
- `className`: string (default "h-96 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the printer.

Notes:
- The paper is a role="slider" from -100 to 100 with a spoken aria-valuetext ("Wind 40 from the east, a light chop"): Left/Right and Up/Down step 0.1 (Shift 0.25), Page Up/Down 0.25, Home and End the extremes, 0 calms it. Touch sets the wind with a sideways drag and keeps touch-action: pan-y for vertical scrolling.
- Sound is off by default; with `sound`, the whir loop runs only while the visitor works the wind (never before the page has had a click, tap or key press), lifts with each struck line and stops 600 ms after the last input, on unmount, or when sound is turned off.
- Under reduced motion the paper does not feed and no line is struck in order: the page is a still print for the current wind and reprints with a 240 ms crossfade once the wind rests.
- Between ticks nothing runs; each tick strikes and feeds and the loop stops when the paper settles. Every printed line is drawn once into a cached bitmap in a ring buffer, so a frame is a few dozen image draws. Nothing runs off screen, in a hidden page or paused; DPR is capped at 2.
- The sea is computed with arithmetic-only trigonometry, so the server prints the same first page the canvas continues from, character for character, with no hydration risk.

### Dendrite Reach (KQ-1797) — `dendrite-reach`
Tendrils that reach, touch and pass a signal.

Fluorescent nerve cells under a microscope: dendrites grow slowly out from each soma by branching, their tips carrying growth cones that feel about, and when a tip meets another cell's dendrite it either pulls back along its own path and turns away, or lunges the last pixels on springs.snap and forms a junction whose bouton blooms on springs.recoil. Cells fire at `pulse` Hz — the soma flashes and a front of light runs out along every branch — and at each junction the signal crosses after a synaptic delay, runs in to the partner's soma and fires it in turn. The pointer offers a cue that nearby tips grow toward and a click stimulates the nearest cell; as a focusable group, arrow keys move the cue, Enter stimulates and Escape clears the cue.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/dendrite-reach`

Props:
- `branching`: number (default 0.5) — How bushy the dendrites grow, 0 (long and sparse) to 1 (densely branched).
- `pulse`: number (default 0.3) — Spontaneous firings per cell per second (0 to 2); 0 leaves the cells quiet until stimulated.
- `stain`: "green" | "magenta" | "cyan" | "amber" | (string & {}) (default "green") — The fluorescent stain: a named one, or any CSS colour.
- `cells`: number (default 0) — How many cells (1 to 8); 0 picks one per ~190 px of width.
- `growth`: number (default 16) — How fast a growth cone advances, px/s (4 to 60).
- `reach`: number (default 1) — Length budget of each cell's tree, 0.4 to 2.
- `junctions`: number (default 0.6) — Chance that two meeting dendrites form a junction rather than pull apart, 0 to 1.
- `cue`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly tips grow toward the pointer's cue, 0 to 1.
- `cueRadius`: number (default 150) — How far the cue reaches, px.
- `background`: string (default "oklch(from var(--accent) 0.135 0.02 h)") — The field behind the cells, any CSS colour; dark in both themes, as fluorescence is.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and the keys offer a cue and stimulate.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds growth and signals where they are.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seeds the culture; a new seed grows a new one.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onFire`: (cell: number, cause: "spontaneous" | "signal" | "stimulus") => void — A cell fired, with its index and why: on its own, passed a signal across a junction, or stimulated by the visitor.
- `onJunctionsChange`: (count: number) => void — The number of junctions, reported from the start and on each new one.
- `label`: string (default "Neuron culture") — The culture's name; the group reads "<label>, N junctions".
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No cue, no stimulation; the culture grows on and says it is disabled.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes and shapes the field.

Notes:
- The field is a focusable group (aria-roledescription "micrograph") named with its junction count and a key hint: arrow keys move the cue (24 px, Shift 72 px), Enter or Space stimulates the cell nearest it, Escape clears it (and only then prevents the default). A polite live region speaks stimulated cells and new junctions, no more than one junction every 1.5 s.
- Mouse and pen offer the cue on hover; a tap places it and stimulates. Touch keeps touch-action: pan-y so the page still scrolls over the culture.
- Under reduced motion the culture is a still micrograph grown to completion in one go; stimulating a cell crossfades a glow over it and every cell it is joined to, with no travelling pulses and no growth.
- Trees are baked into a cached layer as they grow; only the last ~36 px of each live tip is redrawn per frame, and meetings are found through a spatial hash. Once growth is done and no signal is in flight the loop sleeps until the next scheduled firing; nothing runs off screen, hidden or paused, and a resize grows the culture again.
- Named stains are pigments at fixed lightness taken from theme hues and the field stays dark in both themes, as a fluorescence image does; onFire's cause lets a host narrate only the visitor's own stimulus.

### Torus Puzzle (KQ-1798) — `torus-puzzle`
Rows and columns of dots slide until it solves.

A square of glowing dots holding a simple picture whose rows and columns slide one cell at a time on springs.snap and wrap round the edges like a torus — the dot leaving one side is drawn again entering the other — while the moving line's track lifts behind it and its dots glow with its speed. On its own it scrambles itself and then solves back in a calm, deliberate sequence, the inverse of every step; drag any row or column and it follows 1:1, wraps as far as you pull and snaps to a whole step with the release velocity, and after a quiet spell it solves from wherever you left it. Solved, the lit dots swell and land on springs.recoil in a cascade from the centre. It is a real grid: arrow keys move between dots, wrapping at the edges, and Shift with an arrow slides the row or column.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/torus-puzzle`

Props:
- `grid`: number (default 6) — Dots per side (3 to 9).
- `pace`: number (default 600) — Milliseconds per autoplay step while solving; scrambling runs at 0.7 of it (200 to 1500).
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — Halo of the lit dots and their boost while moving, 0 (none) to 1.
- `pattern`: "ring" | "plus" | "diamond" | "arrow" | readonly boolean[] (default "ring") — The picture the lit dots make at home, or your own grid × grid cells, row by row.
- `scramble`: number (default 7) — Steps in each scramble (1 to 30).
- `autoplay`: boolean (default true) — Scrambles and solves itself while on screen.
- `resumeAfter`: number (default 5000) — Quiet time after your last move before autoplay solves from where you left it, ms.
- `colors`: { lit?: string; dim?: string; track?: string } — Colours, as CSS colours: lit dots, unlit dots and home rings, and the track behind a moving line.
- `onMove`: (move: { axis: "row" | "column"; index: number; by: number }) => void — Fires for every committed move — yours, a button's or autoplay's — with the shortest equivalent shift.
- `onSolvedChange`: (solved: boolean) => void — Whether the picture is home, reported from the start and on every change.
- `onDistanceChange`: (steps: number) => void — Steps from home, reported from the start and on every change.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Ticks as dots cross cells, for the visitor's own moves only.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No drag and no keys; autoplay still runs.
- `label`: string (default "Torus puzzle") — The grid's name; it reads "<label>, solved" or "<label>, N steps from home".
- `className`: string (default "w-52") — Sizes the square board.
- `ref`: React.Ref<{ solve: () => void; scramble: () => void }> — Imperative solve() and scramble(), played one step at a time; autoplay waits resumeAfter before taking over again.

Notes:
- The board is role="grid" with rows and gridcells ("Row 2, column 3, lit, out of place") and one roving tab stop: arrow keys move between dots and wrap at the edges, Home and End jump within a row (with Ctrl, the whole grid), Shift with an arrow slides the row or column one step with focus riding along. A polite live region speaks the visitor's own moves and "Solved"; autoplay is silent.
- Drag captures only after 4 px and picks its axis from the first travel; touch-action is none on the board because a line can move either way. Sound, when on, ticks only for the visitor's drags, keys and solve/scramble calls.
- Under reduced motion a step is an instant swap with a short flash of the moved line, and solved is a glow rather than a swell; autoplay keeps its pace because the state changes are the information.
- Nothing runs per frame outside a step: motion values per dot (keyed by dot id) carry every position, autoplay is a timer chain that stops off screen, in a hidden page and while the visitor plays, and everything is disposed on unmount.
- Every move is kept in a history that cancels inverse steps, so the puzzle always knows its way home; solving it yourself is noticed and clears the history.

- The hour scale is a role=slider with aria-valuetext such as "01:30, about 84 meteors an hour, radiant 41 degrees up"; the sky is a role=img whose label says the same. Drag is horizontal with touch-action: pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page.
- Under reduced motion the sky is a still long exposure: streaks fanning from the radiant, as many as a few minutes at that hour would bring, redrawn at once as the hour changes. No streak moves and the scale jumps without the glide.
- One second in the frame is a minute of the night, so a rate of 100 gives about one and a half meteors a second at the peak. showerReading(rate, hour) returns the same numbers the scale shows, for a status line or a caption.
- Canvas 2D: the sky, its stars, the galaxy band and the trees are drawn once per size and theme; meteors and trains are pre-rendered sprites under a transform from fixed pools. The loop runs only on screen and in a visible tab, at half rate while nothing is in the air.
- The night is fixed art, dark on light and dark pages alike; the tint and train colours are read from tokens on the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes.

### Tube Rack (KQ-1802) — `tube-rack`
Glass tubes of colour, each filled to its value.

A rack of glass test tubes, each filled to its value with glossy coloured liquid behind a front rail: a curved meniscus climbs the glass, a shine runs down the liquid and the glass has its own long glint. Every few seconds a slow wave runs along the rack and nudges each tube as it passes, so the surfaces tilt and rock back to level in turn on a damped oscillator. Pick a tube and drag on it: a target mark follows the finger 1:1 and the liquid pours to meet it, capped at a pour rate and settling on springs.glide's constants, with a thin stream falling from the mouth as it rises and bubbles climbing as it drains; each tube is a vertical slider under one tab stop, Left and Right move between tubes, Up and Down step, Page keys move a tenth, Home empties and End fills.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tube-rack`

Props:
- `values / defaultValues`: number[] (default defaultTubeValues) — One level per tube, from 0 to max, controlled or initial.
- `onValuesChange`: (values: number[]) => void — Fires from the drag or key that changed a level, with every level.
- `labels`: string[] (default defaultTubeLabels) — A short name under each tube; also each slider's accessible name.
- `max`: number (default 100) — The value of a full tube.
- `step`: number (default 1) — How far an arrow key moves a level; drags snap to it too.
- `palette`: "lab" | "berry" | "sea" | "amber" (default "lab") — The liquids' colours, cycled along the rack.
- `colors`: string[] — Liquid colours of your own, any CSS colours; overrides palette.
- `slosh`: number (default 0.5) — How far the surfaces tilt when the wave passes and how long they rock, 0 (still) to 1.
- `gloss`: number (default 0.6) — The glass's highlight and the liquid's shine, 0 (matte) to 1.
- `wavePeriod`: number (default 6500) — How often a slow wave runs along the rack, in ms.
- `pourSpeed`: number (default 0.5) — How fast liquid pours to a new level, 0 (a slow trickle) to 1 (a quick pour).
- `graduations`: boolean (default true) — Faint graduations at each quarter of the glass.
- `format`: (value: number) => string — Formats a value for its chip, its label and assistive technology; defaults to a rounded number.
- `onActiveChange`: (index: number | null) => void — Fires when a tube is picked by a press or by focus, or with null when focus leaves the rack.
- `label`: string (default "Tube rack") — The rack's accessible name.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the glug of the pour, rising as the tube fills, for the visitor's own changes; it stops when the pour does.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the levels but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-52 w-full") — Sizes the rack; tubes are laid out in pixels from the measured width.

Notes:
- The rack is a role=group of vertical role=slider tubes under one tab stop, each named by its label with aria-valuetext such as "P3: 62". Left and Right move focus between tubes; Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End change the focused level.
- The first press on a tube picks it; pressing a picked tube pours to that height, and a vertical drag sets the level 1:1 (touch-action: pan-x, so a sideways swipe still scrolls).
- Under reduced motion the surfaces stay level and a change is a 150 ms tween with no stream or bubbles; the value still changes in full.
- SVG redrawn by one loop that writes path data directly and runs only while a surface moves and the rack is on screen; the next wave waits on a timer, so a settled rack costs nothing between waves.
- Liquids are pigments mixed from tokens (oklch relative colours), so they read the same on light and dark pages; glass and rack follow the theme's ink and surfaces.

### Forecast Glow (KQ-1803) — `forecast-glow`
Scrub tonight's forecast and the sky answers.

A soft, heavily blurred aurora over dark hills and a still lake whose strength follows an hourly activity forecast: the glow is computed per pixel into a small buffer and left to the browser to scale and blur, a few slow curtains rising from behind the ridge, fading upward and mirrored dimmer in the water. The timeline beneath, one bar per hour coloured by its reading, is a slider through the night: a drag moves the playhead 1:1, a release projects the throw and glides to a quarter hour on springs.glide with the release velocity, and the sky follows on springs.drift's constants, growing brighter and taller and shifting from its quiet colour toward its peak colour while the hour and the reading ride the playhead above. Arrow keys step a quarter hour, Shift and the Page keys an hour, Home and End go to the first and last hour.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/forecast-glow`

Props:
