- `startHour`: number (default 18) — The clock hour of the first reading.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 5) — The position on the timeline in hours from the first reading, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the drag or key that moved the timeline, in quarter hours from the first reading.
- `intensity`: number (default 0.7) — How bright the glow can get, 0 to 1.
- `blur`: number (default 0.6) — How soft the glow is, 0 (soft) to 1 (a haze): the buffer's resolution and the blur radius.
- `palette`: "polar" | "violet" | "teal" | "mono" (default "polar") — The glow's colours from quiet to the peak.
- `colors`: [string, string, string] — Colours of your own: the base of a quiet glow, its middle, and the top at the peak; overrides palette.
- `maxReading`: number (default 9) — The top of the reading scale.
- `format`: (reading: number) => string — Formats a reading for the readout and assistive technology; defaults to "Kp 5.3".
- `describe`: (reading: number) => string — Names a reading; defaults to quiet, active, strong and storm.
- `drift`: number (default 0.5) — How fast the curtains drift, 0 (still) to 1.
- `reflection`: boolean (default true) — A lake under the hills that mirrors the glow.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the curtains still.
- `seed`: number (default 4) — Seeds the stars, the hills and the curtains.
- `label`: string (default "Forecast hour") — The timeline's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the forecast but the timeline takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-52 w-full") — Sizes the widget; the timeline takes 56px of it.

Notes:
- The timeline is a role=slider whose aria-valuetext reads the hour, the reading and its name ("23:00, Kp 5.7, strong"); the visual readout is hidden from assistive technology so nothing is said twice, and the sky is a role=img with the same sentence.
- Under reduced motion the curtains are still and the sky eases to each new reading over a few frames; the playhead jumps without the glide.
- The glow is a small ImageData buffer, roughly a sixth of the box, reused every frame and blurred by the compositor: the loop runs at about 30 frames a second while the curtains drift, only on screen and in a visible tab, and stops once a still sky has settled.
- forecastAt(forecast, hour) is exported: the same monotone interpolation the sky uses, for a status line or a chart beside it.
- The night is fixed art, dark on light and dark pages alike; the glow and bar colours are pigments read from tokens on the component's own element.

### Anaglyph Card (KQ-1804) — `anaglyph-card`
A red and cyan card whose depth shows as you tilt.

An image card split into two colour channels by a depth map: one WebGL2 pass samples the picture as a left and a right view, each shifted along the tilt by its depth with a short search so edges hold, and feeds them through the two filter colours, while whatever neither filter covers comes from the centred view so the picture at rest is exactly itself. Lean in with the pointer and the channels part in proportion to depth (the near reeds fringe the most, the far sky not at all) as near and far slide against each other and the card leans a few degrees under a soft glare, the tilt following on springs.glide's constants and returning on springs.drift's. A press toggles glasses mode, folding the split shut on springs.snap so only the parallax remains; it is a real toggle button, Enter or Space toggles, arrow keys hold a tilt, and Escape or Home levels the card.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/anaglyph-card`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The caption under the picture.
- `src`: string — A picture of your own (same origin, or served with CORS); defaults to a lake at dusk drawn in code.
- `depthSrc`: string — Its depth map, white near and black far. Without one, depth runs from far at the top to near at the bottom.
- `alt`: string (default "A lake below pine ridges at dusk") — What the picture shows, for assistive technology.
- `depth`: number (default 0.6) — How far the channels part at full tilt, 0 to 1.
- `tilt`: number (default 0.5) — How far the card leans toward the pointer, 0 (flat) to 1.
- `channels`: "red-cyan" | "red-blue" | "green-magenta" | "amber-blue" (default "red-cyan") — The two filter colours.
- `channelColors`: [string, string] — Two filter colours of your own, left eye then right; overrides channels.
- `parallax`: number (default 0.5) — How far near and far slide against each other as you tilt, 0 to 1.
- `convergence`: number (default 0.35) — The depth that stays put while the rest slides, 0 (far) to 1 (near).
- `pressed / defaultPressed`: boolean (default false) — Glasses mode, controlled or initial: the colours folded back into one, only the parallax left.
- `onPressedChange`: (pressed: boolean) => void — Fires from the press or key that toggled glasses mode, with the new state.
- `glare`: boolean (default true) — A soft glare that slides across the glass as it leans.
- `preview`: boolean (default true) — Lean once when the card first comes into view, so its depth shows before anyone touches it.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Glasses mode") — The toggle's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the picture but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "w-full max-w-72") — Sizes the card; the picture keeps 16:9 above the caption.

Notes:
- The picture is a native button with aria-pressed, named by label and described by the alt text and a hint. Arrow keys hold a tilt so the split can be seen without a pointer; Escape (handled, so a surrounding dialog stays open) and Home level the card.
- Mouse and pen tilt on hover; touch tilts with a horizontal drag (touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical scrolling) and a tap toggles glasses mode.
- Under reduced motion there is no lean and no glare travel; the split still follows the tilt, because it is the information, with a short fade instead of a spring, and the glasses fold is a fade too.
- One fullscreen-triangle pass drawn on demand: only while the tilt or the fold moves, and never off screen or in a hidden tab. Textures are uploaded once per size and theme; context loss shows the still picture and rebuilds on restore, and without WebGL2 the drawn picture stays as a still image.
- Filter colours are optics and stay pure on every page; the drawn scene's palette is mixed from tokens and re-read when the theme changes. A src image must be same-origin or served with CORS for the GPU to read it; otherwise the drawn scene stays.

### Condenser Coil (KQ-1805) — `condenser-coil`
Light poured through a run of glass coil.

A run of clear glass tubing coiled like a condenser, drawn in Canvas 2D, with liquid light flowing through it as segmented flow: seeded slugs parted by gas gaps, small bubbles swaying across the bore as they ride, and the light glowing brighter wherever the coil doubles back on itself (a fold weight found once per shape). The pointer warms the glass, quickening the flow and raising bubbles at the warm spot; a click sends one bright slug through the whole run that launches with a flick, flashes every crossing and leaves the outlet in a flare that blooms with the springs.recoil overshoot. The keyboard's way in is a button behind the content: Enter or Space sends a slug, arrow keys move a warm hand along the glass, Escape lifts it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/condenser-coil`

Props:
- `flow`: number (default 0.4) — How fast the liquid runs, 0 (a slow seep) to 1 (a brisk run); a sent slug runs faster with it too.
- `bubbles`: number (default 14) — How many small bubbles ride in the slugs, 0 to 40.
- `hue`: number (default 205) — The liquid light's hue, 0 to 360, held at a fixed lightness for each theme.
- `path`: string — The coil as an SVG path; it is fitted inside the box with its aspect kept. Defaults to a horizontal coil that fits the box.
- `viewBox`: string — The coordinate box `path` was drawn in, so the server can show it before the canvas paints.
- `turns`: number — Loops in the generated coil, 2 to 16. Defaults to about one for every 64 px of width.
- `tubeWidth`: number (default 10) — The tube's outer width, in px, 6 to 18.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How much brighter the light runs where the coil doubles back on itself, 0 to 1.
- `warmth`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the pointer warms the glass: the flow it adds and the bubbles it raises, 0 to 1.
- `warmColor`: string (default "oklch(0.76 0.14 55)") — The colour warm glass takes on, any CSS colour.
- `glassColor`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — The glass's colour, any CSS colour; resolved on the element so it follows the theme.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content above the coil: a caption, a heading, a call to action.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keys warm the glass and send slugs.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the liquid where it stands; a sent slug still runs.
- `label`: string (default "Glass condenser coil") — Names the coil for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seeds the slugs' lengths and where the bubbles ride.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onSend`: () => void — Fires when a bright slug is sent, from the click or key that sent it.
- `onArrive`: (count: number) => void — Fires when a bright slug leaves the outlet, with how many have run through.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the coil flowing but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the coil is one focus stop (a button behind your content). Enter or Space sends a bright slug; arrow keys move a warm hand along the glass (Shift moves three times as far); Escape lifts it. Pointer clicks and taps send a slug too, and up to six can run at once.
- Reduced motion: the train stands still mid-run and warmth shows in place; a send lights the whole run at once and fades over 600 ms, so the press is still answered.
- Performance: the glass is cached in two layers and only the liquid is drawn per frame; the loop runs only while the coil is on screen, the tab is visible and something moves, and stops when paused and settled. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at `dpr`.
- Theming: glass follows `glassColor` (the foreground token by default) and re-reads it when the theme changes; the liquid takes `hue` at a lightness tuned for each theme, glowing by adding light on dark pages and by deepening on light ones.
- Pass any SVG `path` to lay the tubing your own way; it is fitted inside the box with its aspect kept, and its own crossings glow. Give `viewBox` too if you want the server to show it before the canvas paints.

### Corner Tide (KQ-1806) — `corner-tide`
Soft squares rounding and squaring in a tide.

A centred grid of glowing tiles drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass, each a superellipse whose corner exponent rides a slow travelling field of two crossing waves, so bands of tiles soften toward circles and sharpen back toward squares while keeping their size, each lit from within by a round core and a halo summed over its neighbours. The pointer pushes its own rounded patch through the grid, following on springs.glide and swelling in on springs.drift; a click sends a squaring ripple outward and each tile it passes rings back with the springs.recoil damping ratio, its core flashing as it squares. The keyboard's way in is a button behind the content: arrow keys move the patch a tile at a time, Enter or Space sends a ripple from it, Escape lifts it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/corner-tide`

Props:
- `exponent`: number (default 6) — How square the squarest tiles get: the corner exponent at the tide's crest, 3 to 12.
- `minExponent`: number (default 2) — How round the roundest tiles get: the corner exponent in the trough, 1.2 to 4 (2 is a circle).
- `gap`: number (default 6) — The gap between tiles, in px, 2 to 16.
- `glow`: number (default 0.5) — How much light each tile holds and spills around it, 0 to 1.
- `cell`: number (default 30) — One tile and its gap, in px, 16 to 64.
- `colors`: readonly string[] (default ["var(--accent-bright)", "var(--signal)"]) — The tiles' colours, one to three CSS colours laid across the grid; resolved on the element so they follow the theme.
- `tide`: number (default 0.85) — How far the tide swings the corners, 0 (every tile still at the middle exponent) to 1.
- `speed`: number (default 0.35) — How fast the tide travels, 0 to 1.
- `patchRadius`: number (default 70) — The reach of the pointer's rounded patch, in px.
- `rippleSpeed`: number (default 520) — How fast a squaring ripple travels outward, in px per second.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content above the tiles: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keys push the patch and send ripples.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the tide where it is; the patch and ripples still answer.
- `label`: string (default "Tile grid") — Names the grid for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 4) — Seeds the tide's directions and phases, so two grids never swing alike.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onRipple`: (x: number, y: number) => void — Fires when a ripple is sent, with its origin in px from the box's top left.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the tide but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the grid is one focus stop (a button behind your content). On focus the patch lands on the middle tile; arrow keys move it a tile at a time, Enter or Space sends a ripple from it, Escape lifts it. A click or tap sends a ripple from where it lands.
- Reduced motion: the tide is frozen in one designed swing, the patch moves without easing, and a ripple squares the tiles near it at once and lets them ease back over half a second without travelling.
- Performance: one fragment pass with four superellipse lookups a pixel; the loop runs only while the grid is on screen, the tab is visible and the tide, the patch or a ripple is moving. Paused with nothing moving, it draws nothing.
- Theming: `colors` are resolved on the element and re-read when the theme changes; two colours meet through their oklch midpoint so the grid never greys in the middle. Halos add light on dark pages and soften to a tint on light ones.
- Content passed as children sits above the tiles and stays fully interactive; the tiles never take its clicks.

A ribbon of chalk pastel on dark, toothy paper.

### Colonnade Pass (KQ-1809) — `colonnade-pass`
Light and shadow strobing as you walk past columns.

A walk along a sunlit cloister, ray-cast per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: fluted columns down the left with a lawn court beyond, a coffered ceiling, a paved walk and a wall with arched doors, and the sun's light coming in between the columns to lay bars of light and shade across the floor and up the wall, each shadow's penumbra widening with the distance to the column that casts it, faint shafts in the air and the eye adjusting as you pass from sun to shade. You walk at `pace` (and with `scroll`, with the nearest scroll container), the near columns sweeping past while the far ones creep; the pointer moves the sun, across for its angle so the bars lean and up and down for its height so they lengthen, following on springs.glide, and the first sighting swings the sun in from the far side on springs.drift. It is a slider: arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End move the sun's angle, Up and Down its height.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/colonnade-pass`

Props:
- `columns`: number (default 6) — How closely the columns stand, 3 (wide bays, 7.2 m apart) to 12 (close set, 1.8 m apart).
- `sunAngle`: number (default 25) — The sun's angle along the walk where it starts, −60° to 60°; changing it moves the sun there. Positive puts the sun to the right, so the bars lean left.
- `pace`: number (default 1) — How fast you walk past the columns, in metres a second, 0 (standing) to 2.5.
- `value`: number — The sun's angle when you control it, in degrees; pair with `onValueChange`.
- `onValueChange`: (degrees: number) => void — Fires from the pointer or the keys that moved the sun, with its new angle in degrees.
- `sunHeight`: number (default 34) — The sun's height above the horizon where it starts, 12° to 65°; lower suns lay longer bars.
- `softness`: number (default 0.3) — How soft the shadows' edges are, 0 (a crisp noon sun) to 1 (thin cloud).
- `haze`: number (default 0.35) — How much the air inside the portico glows where the sun gets through, 0 to 1.
- `scroll`: boolean (default false) — Walk with the nearest scroll container as well as on your own.
- `stoneColor`: string (default "oklch(0.84 0.035 78)") — The stone's colour, any CSS colour. Pigment: daylight reads the same in either theme.
- `sunColor`: string (default "oklch(0.96 0.06 82)") — The sunlight's colour, any CSS colour.
- `skyColor`: string (default "oklch(0.84 0.06 235)") — The sky's colour, which also fills the shade, any CSS colour.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content above the scene: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The first time the colonnade is seen, the sun swings in from the far side and the bars sweep into place.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer and keys move the sun.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Stand still; the sun still answers.
- `label`: string (default "Sun angle") — Names the sun control for assistive technology.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the walk but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the sun is a slider and the scene's one focus stop. Left and Right move its angle 2°, Page Up and Down 10°, Home and End to the ends; Up and Down raise and lower it 3°. Its value text says which way the bars lean.
- The walk plays on its own: give people a way to stop it with `paused` (the demo's Stop walking button) when it sits beside reading. Under reduced motion you stand still between two columns, there is no intro and the sun moves at once.
- Performance: one fragment pass with eight haze samples a pixel. The loop runs only while the scene is on screen, the tab is visible and you are walking or the sun is easing; at pace 0 with the sun settled it draws nothing, and scroll walking redraws only on scroll.
- Theming: stone, sun and sky are pigments, so the picture of daylight is the same on light and dark pages; restyle it with `stoneColor`, `sunColor` and `skyColor`.
- No WebGL2, or a lost context: a CSS still of the walk stands in, with the wall striped by light and the floor's bars leaning with `sunAngle`.

### Smoke Tunnel (KQ-1810) — `smoke-tunnel`
Smoke lines streaming past a shape you can turn.

A wind tunnel's test section in Canvas 2D with threads of smoke streaming past a wing model: the flow is real potential flow around a Joukowski aerofoil with the Kutta circulation, solved in closed form, so the smoke divides at the stagnation point, hugs the upper surface and leaves the trailing edge smoothly, and puffs released together at the rake are drawn by the time smoke takes to reach each point, so the ones over the top race ahead. From the tip a tube of haze peels away with two filaments and dust spiralling through it, wound tighter the more lift the wing makes. Drag the wing (its leading edge follows the finger 1:1) or use the keys; release projects the throw and the model locks on with springs.snap, and past the stall angle the threads leave the surface and tumble on curl noise, eddies roll off the separation point and the model buffets. It is a slider: arrows step a degree, Page Up and Down five, Home and End go to the ends, and crossing the stall is announced.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/smoke-tunnel`

Props:
- `flow`: number (default 0.5) — The tunnel's speed, 0 (a slow drift) to 1 (a brisk run): the puffs, the dust and the turbulence.
- `angle`: number (default 6) — The wing's angle of attack where it starts, in degrees; changing it turns the wing there.
- `smoke`: number (default 0.6) — How much smoke the rake lets out, 0 (a few faint threads) to 1 (many dense ones).
- `value`: number — The wing's angle when you control it, in degrees; pair with `onValueChange`.
- `onValueChange`: (degrees: number) => void — Fires from the drag or the keys that turned the wing, with its new angle in degrees.
- `minAngle`: number (default -10) — The lowest angle the wing turns to, in degrees.
- `maxAngle`: number (default 26) — The highest angle the wing turns to, in degrees.
- `stallAngle`: number (default 14) — The angle past which the flow over the top lets go and the smoke tumbles, in degrees.
- `camber`: number (default 0.5) — How arched the wing's section is, 0 (symmetric) to 1.
- `thickness`: number (default 0.5) — How thick the wing's section is, 0 (thin) to 1 (thick).
- `vortex`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the tube of haze winds off the tip, 0 (none) to 1.
- `smokeColor`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — The smoke's colour, any CSS colour; resolved on the element so it follows the theme.
- `modelColor`: string (default "var(--ink-2)") — The model's colour, any CSS colour.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content above the tunnel: a caption, a heading, a call to action.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The drag and keys turn the wing.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Stop the smoke where it is; the wing still turns.
- `label`: string (default "Wing angle") — Names the wing's angle control for assistive technology.
- `seed`: number (default 8) — Seeds the turbulence and the dust, so two tunnels never tumble alike.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `onStallChange`: (stalled: boolean) => void — Fires when the flow stalls (true) or attaches again (false), from the drag or keys that caused it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the tunnel running but takes no input.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the wing's angle is a slider and the tunnel's one focus stop. Up and Right raise the nose a degree, Down and Left lower it, Page Up and Down move five, Home and End go to `minAngle` and `maxAngle`; its value text and a polite status say when the flow stalls and when it attaches again. Touch drags turn the wing vertically; horizontal swipes still scroll.
- Reduced motion: the threads stand steady with their puffs held in place, the tip's tube and its dust are still and there is no buffet; a stalled wing still shows its tumbled smoke, frozen at one moment, because the stall is information.
- Performance: the streamlines are re-traced only while the wing turns (a closed-form field, no simulation); otherwise each frame restrokes cached threads and stamps the puffs. The loop runs only while the tunnel is on screen, the tab is visible and the smoke flows or the wing settles; paused and settled it stops.
- Theming: smoke follows `smokeColor` (the foreground token) and the model `modelColor`, both re-read when the theme changes, so the tunnel is white smoke on a dark page and ink on a light one.
- Set `stallAngle`, `camber` and `thickness` to match the section you are showing; the flow pattern, the lift that winds the tip's tube and the puffs' race over the top all follow from them.

### Root Exchange (KQ-1811) — `root-exchange`
One hub feeding many, in pulses you can read.

A hub feeding a ring of nodes through fine, root-like paths: neighbours share a trunk that forks half way, each trunk as thick as the flow it carries, and pulses of light leave the hub along every route at that node's share of the total, so the busy ones visibly draw more. Hovering or tabbing to a node lights its route and shows its label, value and share in a tag that rises on springs.snap; a press reverses its flow, the route's direction springing through zero on springs.snap so pulses already in flight slow, stop and run home while the node kicks on springs.recoil and its chevron turns. Arrow keys walk the ring and Enter or Space reverses the focused node.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/root-exchange`

Props:
- `nodes`: { id: string; label: string; value: number }[] (default defaultRootNodes) — The nodes the hub feeds; each value's share of the total sets its pulse rate and its route's thickness.
- `hubLabel`: string (default "Hub") — What the hub is, for its accessible name and announcements.
- `format`: (value: number) => string (default en-US grouping) — Prints a node's value in its tag and accessible name.
- `reversed / defaultReversed`: string[] (default []) — Ids of the nodes whose flow runs back to the hub, controlled or initial.
- `onReversedChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from the press that reversed or restored a node, with the new ids.
- `onActiveChange`: (id: string | null) => void — Fires when hover or keyboard focus brings a node forward, or lets it go.
- `pulseRate`: number (default 4) — Pulses a second leaving the hub in all, shared out by value.
- `travel`: number (default 1800) — Time for a pulse to cross an average route, ms; every pulse moves at the same speed in pixels.
- `curve`: number (default 0.55) — How far the roots wander off a straight line, 0 (schematic) to 1 (gnarled).
- `rootlets`: number (default 0.5) — How many hair-fine side rootlets the routes shed, 0 to 1.
- `palette`: "cobalt" | "signal" | "amber" | "ink" (default "cobalt") — The colourway, from the theme's tokens.
- `colors`: { route?: string; pulse?: string; hub?: string } — CSS colours that replace parts of palette.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds where the nodes sit and how the roots wander.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freezes the pulses where they are.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the pulse canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Flow from the hub") — The node group's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nodes cannot be focused or reversed; the flow still runs.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the nodes are one tab stop with a roving focus. Arrow keys walk the ring in order, Home and End jump, Enter or Space reverses the focused node (aria-pressed), and the change is announced once from the press that caused it.
- The layout is measured from the box and seeded, so server and client draw the same roots; the pulses live on a Canvas 2D layer with a fixed pool and pre-sampled routes, nothing allocated per frame.
- The pulse loop runs only while the box is on screen, the page is visible, the piece is not paused and motion is allowed; the canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
- Under reduced motion each route carries still beads graded toward where it flows and a chevron, and a reversal flips them at once with no kick.
- Palettes are token colours (cobalt, signal, amber, ink) and read on light and dark pages; on a dark page the pulses add light, on a light one they stay the hue.

### Ice Cube (KQ-1812) — `ice-cube`
A melting cube that bends what it slides over.

A clear ice cube slides across a picture after the pointer on a per-frame glide spring, turning with the curve of its slide, and bends the picture per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: bevelled facets displace it, the top magnifies it through frosted cracks and a cloudy core, a cold highlight runs along the top edge and a pale shadow holds a bright caustic. Sliding melts it — it shrinks, rounds and softens and lays meltwater into a ping-pong field that bends the picture too before it dries — and a click drops a fresh cube that lands on springs.recoil with a splash. Keyboard focus on anything inside parks the cube on it, and a drop button that appears on focus takes Enter or Space.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ice-cube`

Props:
- `children`: React.ReactNode — Content laid over the picture: headlines, buttons, links. It stays fully interactive.
- `image`: { src?: string; alt?: string } — The picture under the cube, drawn cover-fit. Without a src, a cloth is drawn from the theme.
- `pattern`: "gingham" | "tiles" | "linen" (default "gingham") — The drawn cloth when there is no src.
- `melt`: number (default 0.4) — How fast it melts as it slides, 0 (never) to 1 (a few seconds of sliding).
- `facets`: number (default 0.7) — Facet sharpness, 0 (soft, rounded sides) to 1 (flat facets with hard folds).
- `trail`: number (default 0.5) — How much meltwater it leaves and how long the trail takes to dry, 0 to 1.
- `size`: number (default 68) — The fresh cube's edge, px; it never exceeds a third of the box's height.
- `refraction`: number (default 0.6) — How hard the ice and the water bend the picture, 0 to 1.
- `frost`: number (default 0.5) — Frosted cracks and the cloudy core inside the ice, 0 to 1.
- `tint`: string (default "oklch(from var(--accent-bright) 0.9 0.05 calc(h - 40))") — The colour of the ice, any CSS colour.
- `rest`: { x: number; y: number } (default { x: 0.74, y: 0.55 }) — Where the cube rests before anyone moves it, as fractions of the box.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The pointer moves the cube and a click drops a fresh one.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the cube and the water where they are.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A clack when a fresh cube lands or the cube hits the frame. Off unless asked for.
- `onDrop`: (count: number) => void — Fires when a fresh cube is dropped, with how many cubes there have been.
- `onMelt`: (left: number) => void — Fires as the cube melts, with how much of it is left (1 to 0.2) in 5% steps.
- `onMelted`: () => void — Fires when the cube has melted into a puddle.
- `dropLabel`: string (default "Drop a fresh cube") — The keyboard's drop button, shown on focus.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing moves the cube and the drop button is off.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the box.

Notes:
- Keyboard: focusing anything inside the box (Tab) parks the cube on it; after the children, a Drop a fresh cube button appears on focus and Enter or Space drops one where the cube is, announced once.
- The children sit above the picture and stay fully interactive; clicks on links and buttons never drop a cube, and touch follows only while the finger is down (touch-action pan-y keeps vertical scrolling).
- The draw loop runs only while something changes — the cube sliding, a landing, water drying — and only on screen on a visible page; at rest it stops. Water is a quarter-resolution field and the canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
- Without WebGL2, after a lost context, or with a cross-origin picture that has no CORS, the picture stays plain and a glassy drawn cube still slides and drops.
- Under reduced motion the cube rests still and refracting at rest, does not melt or leave water, and focus or a click moves it at once with no fall.
- The drawn cloth takes its colours from the theme, so it is light gingham on a light page and a dark one on a dark page; pass image.src for your own picture.

### Catseye Marble (KQ-1813) — `catseye-marble`
Roll a glass marble and watch its ribbon turn.

A glass marble in a felt tray, ray traced per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: the studio reflected by Fresnel with a highlight as sharp as gloss, three twisted vanes found by marching the refracted ray, the felt seen magnified and flipped through the far side, and on the felt a soft shadow holding a ribbon-tinted caustic. Drag it and it follows 1:1 with its orientation integrated as true rolling, so the ribbon turns the way a real marble's does; released, it coasts on rolling friction, bounces off the wall with a soft clack and settles. Arrow keys nudge it with the same physics and Home rolls it back on springs.glide.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/catseye-marble`

Props:
- `ribbon`: "ember" | "lagoon" | "moss" | "ink" (default "ember") — The ribbon's colourway.
- `colors`: string[] — Up to three CSS colours, one per vane, that replace ribbon.
- `gloss`: number (default 0.6) — How glossy the glass is: the reflection's strength and the highlight's sharpness, 0 to 1.
- `roll`: number (default 0.4) — Rolling friction, 0 (a slick table that lets it run) to 1 (felt that stops it quickly).
- `size`: number (default 64) — The marble's diameter, px; never more than 36% of the tray's shorter side.
- `twist`: number (default 0.5) — How far the vanes turn from one pole to the other, 0 (flat) to 1 (a turn and a half).
- `tint`: string (default "oklch(from var(--accent-bright) 0.95 0.02 calc(h - 50))") — The glass's colour, any CSS colour; the thicker the glass, the more it shows.
- `table`: string (default "color-mix(in oklab, var(--bg-2) 86%, var(--ink-3))") — The tray's felt, any CSS colour.
- `defaultPosition`: { x: number; y: number } (default { x: 0.42, y: 0.5 }) — Where the marble starts, as fractions of the tray.
- `resetKey`: string | number — Any change rolls the marble back to where it started.
- `onRoll`: () => void — Fires when the marble starts rolling from rest.
- `onRest`: (position: { x: number; y: number }) => void — Fires when the marble comes to rest, with where (fractions of the tray).
- `onBounce`: (speed: number) => void — Fires when the marble hits the tray's wall, with its speed into the wall, px/s.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Dragging and the keys roll it.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A soft clack off the tray's wall. Off unless asked for.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `label`: string (default "Glass marble") — The tray's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing rolls it.
- `className`: string (default "h-56 w-full") — Sizes the tray.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the tray is one button. Arrow keys nudge the marble (Shift harder) so it rolls, coasts and bounces like a throw; Home rolls it back; when it settles after a key the tray says Resting. once.
- Pointer and touch: drag anywhere to roll it 1:1 (the tray is touch-action none, so a finger rolls rather than scrolls); a tap on the glass flicks it away from the finger.
- It draws only while the marble moves and once on mount, resize and theme change; the loop stops at rest, off screen and on a hidden page. The canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
- Without WebGL2 or after a lost context, a drawn marble with gradients and a turning ribbon still drags, coasts and bounces.
- Under reduced motion a drag still rolls it 1:1 but it stops on release, the keys step it 24 px at once and Home places it back.
- The ribbon colours are fixed lightnesses of the theme's hues and the felt follows the theme's surface, so it reads on light and dark pages.

A dark mass that bends your headline into rings.

A black hole on a real headline: the browser lays out the words, each word is painted into a texture where it was set, and one WebGL2 pass lenses that picture through the point-lens equation, so the words behind the mass bend into arcs, a flipped image appears inside the Einstein radius and whatever is right behind becomes a ring round the shadow, swirled by spin, with a thin smoky accretion disc and a bright photon edge. Drag it and it follows 1:1 while its disc flares on springs.flick; release and it drifts back to rest on springs.drift carrying the throw. ### Desk Spike (KQ-1816) — `desk-spike`
Notes on a spike; tear off the top to read on.

A desk spike with notes impaled on it, seen at a three-quarter angle in real CSS 3D: a heavy base, a steel needle drawn from the top slip's hole to its point, and paper slips from data turned a little about it, each curled at a corner. - `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — How many slips are torn off the top, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the click or key that tore off, put back or refilled, with the new count.
- `onTear`: (slip: DeskSpikeSlip) => void — Fires when a slip is torn off, with the slip.
- `onRestore`: (slip: DeskSpikeSlip) => void — Fires when a slip goes back on the spike, with the slip.
- `curl`: number (default 0.5) — How far each slip's corner curls up, 0 to 1.
- `angle`: number (default 36) — How far the desk tips away from you, degrees, 20 to 50.
- `ink`: string (default "oklch(from var(--ink) 0.27 0.02 h)") — The print's colour, any CSS colour.
- `refill`: boolean (default true) — A click on the empty spike puts every slip back.
- `seed`: number (default 4) — Seeds each slip's turn, flight and torn hole.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A paper rip when a slip tears free, and a soft one when it lands. Off unless asked for.
- `label`: string (default "Note spike") — The spike's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Nothing tears.
- `className`: string (default "h-[34rem] w-full") — Sizes the scene.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the spike is one button named for the top slip. Space or Enter tears it off, Backspace puts the last one back, and on an empty spike Space or Enter refills it; each change is announced once with how many slips are left.
- The top slip's text is real text in an article; the slips beneath and the torn ones are hidden from assistive technology until they are on top.
- Pure DOM and CSS 3D transforms driven by one progress value per slip: nothing runs at rest, and every tear, put-back and refill finishes cleanly if it is interrupted.
- Under reduced motion there is no tug, flight or landing: slips fade out and back in, and the torn holes and the count still change.
- Paper and ink are fixed pigments of the theme's hues, so the notes read the same on light and dark pages; pass your own slips for tickets, messages or receipts.

### Flambe Pan (KQ-1817) — `flambe-pan`
Tip the pan and the flames flare off its edge.

A copper pan on a dark range, held by its handle: a drag follows the hand 1:1, up to tip the far lip toward the gas and sideways to slide it over the grate, and a release sets it back level on springs.glide with the throw's velocity. When the lip dips past the catch angle the spirit catches, a front of fire running across the sauce from the low lip, and additive tongues of flame flare up, leaning with the tilt and trailing the pan through the air while the room takes their light; a quick shake gusts them higher before they burn down to a few blue licks and go out. - `metal`: "copper" | "steel" | "iron" (default "copper") — The pan's metal.

- `trigger`: "inView" | "mount" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the pan tips itself once to show the flare (silently): first seen, at mount, or never.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the flare when the visitor catches the spirit or gusts it with a shake.
- `onFlameChange`: (state: "out" | "flaring" | "licks") => void — Fires when the flame catches, burns down to blue licks, or goes out.
- `label`: string (default "Flambé pan") — The scene's accessible name.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the flame still where it is; the pan can still be moved.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No tipping, tossing or shaking.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the flame's tongues.

Notes:

A polite live region says Flaring, Burning down to blue licks, and Out.

- Reduced motion: the pan follows the hand without springs and is set level at once; a catch shows a still, seeded flame that is redrawn smaller in calm steps as it burns down, and the room's light still comes up. Feedback stays, motion goes.
- Performance: one Canvas 2D layer at a capped pixel ratio, sprites pre-rendered once per hue, particles in preallocated typed arrays. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible tab and while something burns or moves; out and level, it stops.
- Sound only answers the visitor: the automatic first toss (trigger) is silent, and the flare plays only when sound is on and the visitor's own tip or shake caused it.
- The scene is drawn in fixed pigments (a dark range and copper), so it reads the same on light and dark pages.

### Mitre Joint (KQ-1818) — `mitre-joint`
Four lengths of frame meet at the corners.

A border for any content built like a picture frame: four lengths of moulding with mitred ends, each shaded across its own width by a flat, cove or gilt profile so a real seam shows where two meet. When first seen the lengths slide in from beyond their edges on springs.glide a stagger apart; as the last one seats the corners click, the frame settling on springs.flick with the seams flashing, and a crisp glow runs once round the bevel from the top-left corner both ways before it settles to a quiet sheen. Hover, or keyboard focus inside the content, lifts the frame on glide and turns the light toward the pointer, the lengths facing it brightening and a highlight sliding along the moulding.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mitre-joint`

Props:

- `bevel`: number (default 14) — The moulding's width in px, 6 to 28.
- `glow`: "gold" | "accent" | "frost" | "ember" | string (default "gold") — The light that runs along the bevel once the corners meet: a preset or any CSS colour.
- `color`: string (default by profile) — The moulding's colour: the page's ink (flat), walnut (cove) or gold leaf (gilt) unless set.
- `trigger`: "inView" | "mount" | "manual" (default "inView") — When the frame assembles: first seen, at mount, or only when assembled says so.
- `assembled`: boolean — Controls the frame: true slides the lengths in, false takes them apart. Undefined lets trigger decide.
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Assemble only the first time it is seen; false assembles again on every return.
- `delay`: number (default 0) — Wait before the first length moves, ms.
- `stagger`: number (default 60) — Time between the four lengths setting off, ms, 0 to 150.
- `onAssembled`: () => void — Fires when the last corner clicks home.
- `lift`: number (default 2) — How far hover or focus inside lifts the frame, px, 0 to 6 (the shadow stays inside the root).
- `highlight`: number (default 0.6) — Strength of the highlight that follows the pointer along the moulding, 0 to 1.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.5) — The quiet sheen the glow settles to, 0 to 1.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — Hover and focus lift the frame and move its light.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the click when the corners meet, only when the visitor's own action assembled it.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root (width, margins).
- `contentClassName`: string — Classes for the opening that holds the content (padding, background).

Notes:
- The frame is decoration: every painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, so links, buttons and fields inside keep their own semantics, tab order and clicks. Keyboard focus inside (focus-visible) lifts the frame like hover and parks the highlight on the edge nearest the focused element.
- Reduced motion: the frame fades in already assembled with no slide, settle or glow run, the sheen fades up instead, and nothing lifts; the light still turns toward the pointer because it is colour, not travel.
- Performance: four clipped divs and motion values, no canvas and no loop. The glow is an SVG drawn only while it runs, measured with a ResizeObserver; geometry is calc() on a CSS variable, so any size works.
- Sound only answers the visitor: an automatic assembly (in view, at mount) is silent; the click plays when sound is on and assembled flipped to true right after a click or key press.
- Themes: the flat profile mixes the page's ink tokens, so it inverts with the theme; cove and gilt are fixed pigments that read on both. Pass color to match a brand.

### Swatch Ladder (KQ-1819) — `swatch-ladder`
Colour strips in a slow wave; lift one to read.

A row of paint-chip strips, each a ladder of chips computed in OKLCH from the palest tint at the top to a shade as deep as you set at the foot, rising and falling in a slow wave that travels across the row. Pointing at a strip, or arrowing to it, lifts it clear on springs.snap with one crisp overshoot while its neighbours part on springs.glide, and the readout gives its name, code and the chip under the pointer in OKLCH with its light reflectance value; a click copies that chip as oklch() and a check pops onto it on springs.flick. It is a horizontal listbox: Left and Right move between paints, Up and Down step lighter and darker, Enter copies, Escape lowers the strip.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/swatch-ladder`

Props:
- `swatches`: { name, hue, chroma, code? }[] (default twelve invented paints) — The paints, one strip each; chips are computed in OKLCH from hue and chroma.
- `strips`: number (default 8) — How many strips stand in the row, 3 to 12 (never more than swatches).
- `steps`: number (default 7) — Chips on each strip, palest to deepest, 4 to 9.
- `wave`: number (default 0.5) — How far the strips rise and fall in the travelling wave, 0 (still) to 1.
- `period`: number (default 6) — Seconds for one swell to pass, 2 to 14.
- `shade`: number (default 0.6) — How deep the darkest chip goes: 0 keeps to pale tints, 1 runs almost to black.
- `lift`: number (default 16) — How far a strip lifts clear when it is read, px, 6 to 28.
- `height`: number (default 144) — Height of a strip, px.
- `value / defaultValue`: number | null (default null) — The strip being read, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (index: number | null) => void — Fires from the hover, touch or key that lifted or lowered a strip.
- `onCopy`: (color: string, info: { name, code?, step }) => void — Fires when a chip is copied, with its colour as oklch(L C H).
- `paper`: string (default a warm paper pigment) — The strips' card stock.
- `showReadout`: boolean (default true) — Show the line under the row that reads the lifted strip.
- `label`: string (default "Paint swatches") — The row's accessible name, also shown in the readout at rest.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the wave still.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No lifting or copying.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: one tab stop, a horizontal listbox with aria-activedescendant. Left and Right move between paints, Home and End jump, Up and Down step lighter and darker within the strip, Enter or Space copies the chip, Escape lowers the strip. Each option is labelled with its name, code, tint, oklch() value and LRV, and copies are announced politely.
- Copy uses the Clipboard API; where it is unavailable the readout and the announcement say so and show the value instead. onCopy fires either way with the colour string.
- Reduced motion: no travelling wave (the row holds a still, staggered arc) and the lift is an instant change; the ring, the readout and the copy check still answer.
- Performance: DOM only. One requestAnimationFrame loop writes a transform per strip; it runs only on screen, in a visible tab, and while the wave is live or a spring is moving. wave={0} or paused lets it stop once settled.
- The strips are physical card stock in a fixed paper pigment and the chips are absolute OKLCH colours, so the card reads the same on light and dark pages; the readout uses the page's ink tokens.

### Spiral Engraving (KQ-1820) — `spiral-engraving`
A picture cut as one spiral line that turns inward.

A round plate engraved with one continuous spiral line whose width swells where the picture is dark and thins to an unbroken hairline where it is light, drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass that samples the picture at each pixel's own position. As the plate turns the line flows inward like a vortex while the picture holds still within it; a drag round the plate turns it 1:1 and a release keeps the throw's spin, easing back to the resting turn over a time set by friction. The first time it is seen the line swells from a hairline into the picture as a front runs out from the spindle. Arrow keys flick it either way, Enter flings it and Home brakes it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/spiral-engraving`

Props:
- `pitch`: number (default 4) — Distance between neighbouring turns of the line, CSS px, 3 to 10.
- `contrast`: number (default 1.2) — How hard the picture's tones are pushed apart, 0.5 to 2.
- `spin`: number (default 20) — The resting spin in turns per minute, 0 to 60; the line flows by one pitch per turn.
- `subject`: "moon" | "peak" | "bloom" (default "moon") — The picture drawn in code when there is no src.
- `src`: string — An image URL to engrave (CORS-enabled); the subject stands in while it loads or if it cannot be read.
- `alt`: string (default by subject) — What the picture shows, for assistive technology.
- `ink`: string (default "var(--foreground)") — The line's colour. A light ink on dark paper prints a white-line engraving (the line swells in light tones).
- `paper`: string (default "var(--card)") — The plate's colour.
- `thin`: number (default 0.08) — The line's width in the lightest tones as a share of the pitch, 0 to 0.4; it never breaks.
- `bold`: number (default 0.9) — The line's width in the darkest tones as a share of the pitch, 0.5 to 1.
- `friction`: number (default 0.5) — How quickly a fling slows back to the resting spin: 0 coasts long, 1 stops short.
- `direction`: "inward" | "outward" (default "inward") — Which way the line flows as the plate turns.
- `reveal`: "inView" | "mount" | "none" (default "inView") — When the line swells from a hairline into the picture.
- `onSpinChange`: (state: "still" | "turning" | "flung") => void — Fires when the plate comes to rest, settles into its resting spin, or is flung faster.
- `label`: string (default "Spin the plate") — The plate's accessible name.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Hold the plate still; a drag still turns it.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No dragging or keys.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is square, so give it a width.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the plate is a role=button described by the picture's alt and a hint. Right and Up flick it with the spin, Left and Down against it, Enter or Space fling it, Home brakes it to its resting turn: the same end states as a drag. A polite live region says Flung, Turning or Still.
- Touch: the drag turns the plate round its centre in two dimensions, so the plate sets touch-action: none; a tap gives it a small flick.
- Reduced motion: no resting spin, no coasting and no cut animation; the picture is engraved at once and a drag (or a key, by a fixed step) still turns it, stopping where it is released.
- Performance: one WebGL2 pass at a capped pixel ratio; the tone map is drawn once per subject or image. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible tab and while the plate turns; spin 0 and settled draws nothing. Context loss stops the loop and rebuilds on restore; without WebGL2 the same line is drawn as a ribbon on a 2D canvas, redrawn only while dragged.
- Themes: ink and paper default to the page's foreground and card tokens, read from the component's own node and re-read when the theme changes; on a dark page the line becomes a white-line engraving rather than a negative.
- The server draws an even hairline spiral (the uncut plate), so the first paint is designed before WebGL starts.

### Text Bottle (KQ-1823) — `text-bottle`
A bottle of typed water you can tip.

A bottle typed on a fixed grid of monospace cells: its glass is one ring of edge glyphs that re-letters itself as it turns, and its water is a density ramp over a shallow-water simulation that conserves volume, so tipping it makes the water lag, run up the glass and slosh back. Dragging turns it 1:1 and a release projects the throw and lands on springs.glide with the release velocity; arrow keys tip it on springs.snap, whose one overshoot slops the water. Past the lip the water pours out of the neck in gulps as a ballistic stream of glyphs into a puddle, and stood upright it refills from a dripping tap.

- `viscosity`: number (default 0.35) — How thick the liquid is, 0 (water: quick waves, a fast glug) to 1 (syrup: slow, damped, a slow pour).
- `charset`: "ascii" | "blocks" | "dots" | "binary" (default "ascii") — The glyphs the water is typed in, light to heavy.
- `ramp`: string — A custom density ramp, light to heavy, starting with a space; overrides charset.
- `fill`: number (default 0.7) — How full the bottle starts and refills to, 0 to 1.
- `maxTilt`: number (default 135) — The furthest it tips either way, 30 to 170 degrees.
- `refill`: number (default 7000) — How long an upright bottle takes to refill from empty, ms; 0 never refills.
- `cellSize`: number (default 10) — The grid's font size in px; smaller is a finer, denser bottle.
- `waterColor`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The water, any CSS colour, drawn at fixed lightness so it reads on both themes.
- `glassColor`: string — The glass outline, any CSS colour; defaults to the ink at two thirds.
- `onStateChange`: (state: TextBottleState, level: number) => void — Fires when it starts or stops pouring, sloshing or refilling, or runs empty, with the level 0 to 1.
- `onLevelChange`: (level: number) => void — Fires as the level passes each 5% step while it pours or refills.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A glug loop while it pours, only after a tip by hand or key.
- `label`: string (default "Bottle of water") — The slider's accessible name.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Freezes the water: no waves, pouring or refilling; the bottle still turns.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No tipping by hand or key.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Sizes the piece; it fills a 448px-tall box by default.

Notes:
- It is a role="slider" for the angle: arrow keys tip it 10° (Shift 30°), PageUp/PageDown 45°, Home/End all the way, Enter or Space stand it upright. Its valuetext says the angle, the level and whether it is pouring or refilling, and a polite status says "Pouring.", "Empty." and "Full again." once each.
- Under reduced motion the bottle turns at once and the water stays dead level; a pour still drains the level, drawn as a still column of glyphs, and a refill still raises it — the level is information, the slosh is not.
- One Canvas 2D: per frame a few thousand signed-distance tests, a 60-column wave step at 240 Hz and glyphs drawn grouped by colour, with every buffer preallocated. The loop runs only while the bottle is on screen, the tab is visible and something moves, and stops once the water settles.
- The glug is a loop that starts only after a visitor's drag or key tips the bottle past its lip, follows the flow and the level, and stops when the pour ends, on unmount or when sound is turned off.
- Give it a tall box (360×560 or so): the bottle is sized so it still fits when tipped all the way, and the stream falls into the space below it. The server renders the upright bottle as SVG text; the canvas fades in over it.

### Folded Steel (KQ-1824) — `folded-steel`
Twist the billet and the pattern comes up.

A polished bar of pattern-welded steel drawn per pixel in WebGL2: every pixel works out which layer of the twisted, pressed billet it was ground from, so twisting brings up chevrons and roses and folding presses waves into ladder rungs, etched dark with a crystalline grain and lit by a brushed sheen that follows the pointer on springs.glide. Dragging twists and folds it 1:1 and a release projects the throw and glides there; arrow keys step on springs.snap. A double click or Enter quenches it: a cool temper flash runs out from the strike and the layers relax straight on springs.drift, and the first time it is seen the etch comes up along it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/folded-steel`

Props:
- `twist / defaultTwist`: number (default 0.75) — How far the billet is twisted, in turns along the bar, −3 to 3; controlled or the uncontrolled start.
- `onTwistChange`: (twist: number) => void — Fires from the drag release, key or quench that changed the twist, rounded to 0.05 turn.
- `fold / defaultFold`: number (default 0.2) — How deeply the layers are pressed into waves and ladder rungs, 0 to 1; controlled or the uncontrolled start.
- `onFoldChange`: (fold: number) => void — Fires from the drag release, key or quench that changed the fold, rounded to 0.05.
- `layers`: number (default 24) — How many layers were welded into the billet, 8 to 64.
- `etch`: number (default 0.6) — How deep the acid bit: 0 a polished blank, 1 dark sunk layers with a crystalline grain.
- `rungs`: number (default 7) — How many ladder rungs a full fold presses along the bar, 3 to 14.
- `sheen`: number (default 0.7) — The brushed sheen under the light, 0 to 1.
- `brightColor`: string — The nickel-bright layers, any CSS colour; defaults to a cool steel from the tokens.
- `darkColor`: string — The etched carbon layers, any CSS colour; defaults to a deep blued grey.
- `sheenColor`: string — The light's colour on the brushed surface; defaults to a cool white.
- `reveal`: "inView" | "mount" | "none" (default "inView") — When the etch first comes up: the first time it is seen, at mount, or already etched.
- `onQuench`: () => void — Fires when a double click or Enter quenches the bar to straight layers.
- `interactive`: boolean (default true) — The light follows the pointer and drags twist and fold.
- `label`: string (default "Pattern-welded steel bar") — The slider's accessible name.
- `seed`: number (default 7) — Seeds the hand-forged wobble in the layers.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No twisting, folding or quenching.
- `className`: string — Sizes the piece; the bar fills it less a small margin. 144px tall by default.

Notes:
- It is a role="slider" for the twist (−3 to 3 turns): ←/→ twist a quarter turn (Shift a whole one), PageUp/PageDown one turn, Home/End the limits, ↑/↓ fold by 10%, Enter quenches. The valuetext names the twist, the fold and the pattern they make; a quench is announced.
- Under reduced motion the etch is there at once, twist and fold changes land without a spring, the sheen jumps to the pointer and the quench has no flash — every state still shows.
- One WebGL2 fragment pass, drawn only when something changes (a spring, the light, the reveal or the quench) — there is no idle loop — and only while on screen with the tab visible. A lost context falls back to the CSS still and is rebuilt on restore; without WebGL2 the still bar (straight layers and a sheen) stays.
- foldedSteelPattern(twist, fold) is exported for a status line: it names the pattern a smith would see — straight, waves, ladder, twist or rose.
- Colours are resolved from the props on the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes; the metal keeps its own lightness so it reads on either page.

### Tilled Horizon (KQ-1825) — `tilled-horizon`
Wavy furrows running to a low, striped sun.

A two-tone print of a ploughed field at dusk: furrows run away from you as fine wavy ribbons over rolling hills toward a low sun striped by haze, each drawn near to far so a crest hides the furrow behind it, heavy where the slope turns from the sun and hairline where it faces it, with the furrows in line with the sun taking its ink. The field glides slowly toward you. The pointer, or keyboard focus moving onto a control laid over it, slides the sun along the horizon on the springs.drift constants and the light rolls across every hill with it.

- `palette`: "dusk" | "harvest" | "indigo" | "moss" (default "dusk") — The two inks the print is pulled in; the paper follows the page.
- `inkColor`: string — Overrides the land's ink, any CSS colour.
- `sunColor`: string — Overrides the sun's ink, any CSS colour.
- `paperColor`: string — Overrides the paper; defaults to the page's background, warmed.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the field glides toward you, 0 (still) to 3.
- `horizon`: number (default 0.42) — Where the horizon sits, as a share of the height from the top, 0.2 to 0.7.
- `sunSize`: number (default 0.24) — The sun's diameter as a share of the height, 0.08 to 0.5.
- `haze`: number (default 0.6) — How strongly the haze stripes the sun and the sky, 0 to 1.
- `sun / defaultSun`: number (default 0.62) — Where the sun sits along the horizon, 0 left to 1 right; controlled or the uncontrolled start.
- `onSunChange`: (sun: number) => void — Fires when the pointer, a key or focus moves the sun, rounded to 0.01.

- `label`: string (default "Sun position") — Names the sun slider when focusable.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Holds the field still; the sun still moves.
- `seed`: number (default 5) — Seeds the hills and the ridge.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Sizes the scene; 256px tall by default.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion the field is a still print and the sun moves to the pointer at once, without drifting.
- Canvas 2D: the furrows are batched into a few strokes by weight and fade, on an ink layer allocated only on resize, with the sun's glow laid source-atop. The loop runs only while on screen, the tab is visible and it is gliding or the sun is moving.
- The paper mixes from the page background and the inks are mixed toward the foreground, so the print reads on both themes; colours are re-read when the theme changes. The server renders a CSS still of the sun and a fan of furrows.

### Pulled Sugar (KQ-1826) — `pulled-sugar`
Glossy candy pulled and folded in slow loops.

A candy-pulling machine whose two arm pins orbit opposite ways round a fixed middle pin, with a rope of striped sugar looped over all three: a soft body of particles under gravity, carried by the pins' grip, that stretches plastically and necks thin where it is pulled and slowly gathers back. Every pass folds it over the middle pin, the stripes doubling along the rope from the fold until they read as satin, while a gloss highlight runs along the side of each span that faces a swaying light. Dragging an arm turns it 1:1 and the release sets the motor's speed, forwards or reversed, the flywheel easing to it on the springs.drift constants; arrow keys step the speed.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pulled-sugar`

Props:
- `speed / defaultSpeed`: number (default 18) — The motor's speed in turns a minute, negative runs it backwards; controlled or the uncontrolled start.
- `onSpeedChange`: (speed: number) => void — Fires from the throw, key or stop that changed the motor's speed, in whole turns a minute.
- `stretch`: number (default 0.5) — How readily the sugar stretches, 0 stiff to 1 soft with long sags and thin necks.
- `gloss`: number (default 0.6) — How glassy the candy is, 0 matte to 1 a sharp, bright highlight.
- `palette`: "berry" | "mint" | "honey" | "lilac" (default "berry") — The candy's three colours.
- `colors`: string[] — Three CSS colours for the stripes, overriding palette.
- `batch`: number (default 8) — Folds before a fresh batch drops on; 0 keeps pulling the same one.
- `maxSpeed`: number (default 60) — The fastest the motor turns either way, 10 to 90 turns a minute.
- `ropeWidth`: number (default 24) — The rope's thickness before it is pulled, in the machine's own units (it is drawn 280 wide).
- `onFold`: (folds: number, stripes: number) => void — Fires on every fold, and with 0 when a fresh batch starts, with the folds so far in this batch and the stripes across the rope.
- `label`: string (default "Candy puller speed") — The slider's accessible name.
- `paused`: boolean (default false) — Stops the machine and the candy where they are.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No dragging or keys.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds the stripes' order.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Sizes the piece; the machine scales to fit and centres. 224px tall by default.

Notes:
- It is a role="slider" for the motor speed: ←/→ (↓/↑) step 6 turns a minute (Shift 18), Home/End run it flat out backwards or forwards, Space stops and restarts it, Enter drops a fresh batch. The valuetext gives the direction, the speed and the stripes.
- Under reduced motion the arms do not turn and the candy hangs still on the pins; speed changes are still reported, and a fresh batch swaps in place.
- Canvas 2D with every buffer preallocated: a 120-particle rope at 120 Hz with ten constraint passes, drawn in fifteen chunks of stripe polygons. The loop runs only while on screen, the tab is visible and the motor turns or the rope is still moving; at rest it stops.
- Letting go of a still arm leaves the motor at its speed; a throw sets a new one, which is how a drag reverses it. Candy colours are pigments at fixed lightness from the tokens, so they read the same on both themes.

### Spin Art (KQ-1827) — `spin-art`
Spin the disc; paint throws itself into spirals.

A spin-art turntable: drag round the card and it turns 1:1, then coasts from the release velocity on bearing friction and air drag; tap to drip. A drip lands as a blot with a little splash and breaks into threads that run outward under the spin's centrifugal pull while, in the card's own frame, the Coriolis effect bends them back against it — loose petals at a slow spin, long tight spirals at a fast one — with a gloss on the wet paint that fades as it dries matte. Arrow keys spin it up, Enter drips, Space brakes and Escape clears.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/spin-art`

Props:
- `friction`: number (default 0.4) — How quickly the disc coasts down, 0 spinning on for many seconds to 1 stopping almost at once.
- `drips`: number (default 9) — The size of each drip, px of blot: small drips throw fine threads, big ones heavy ribbons.
- `palette`: "primary" | "sunset" | "sea" | "ink" (default "primary") — The paints, used in turn.
- `colors`: string[] — CSS colours to drip in turn, overriding palette.
- `defaultSpin`: number (default 0) — The speed the disc starts at, turns a minute; negative is anticlockwise.
- `onSpinChange`: (rpm: number) => void — Fires as the spin passes each 10 turns a minute and when it stops, from the hand, key or friction that changed it.
- `maxSpin`: number (default 360) — The fastest a throw or a key can spin it, 60 to 600 turns a minute.
- `runniness`: number (default 0.6) — How runny the paint is, 0 thick with short throws to 1 thin with long threads.
- `dryTime`: number (default 3000) — How long paint stays wet and glossy, and can still be flung, ms.
- `intro`: boolean (default true) — The first time it is seen the disc spins up and three drips land.
- `onDrip`: (count: number) => void — Fires after each drip lands, with the drips on the card.
- `onClear`: () => void — Fires when the card is cleared.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A whir while the disc turns, after you spin it.
- `label`: string (default "Spin-art turntable") — The slider's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No spinning, dripping or clearing.
- `seed`: number (default 4) — Seeds where keyboard drips land and how each one breaks up.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Sizes the piece; the disc fits inside and centres. 224px tall by default.

Notes:
- It is a role="slider" for the spin in turns a minute: ←/→ (↓/↑) add 30 either way (Shift 90), Home/End spin it flat out, Space brakes, Enter drips, Escape clears (it calls preventDefault so a surrounding dialog stays open). Drips and clears are announced.
- Under reduced motion the card does not visibly turn: each drip resolves straight to its finished spiral using the spin at that moment, and a clear is instant; the spin value still changes and is announced.
- Canvas 2D with one paint layer the size of the card, kept across resizes; rivulets come from a preallocated pool. The loop runs only while on screen and something moves — the spin, wet paint, a splash or a clear — and stops when the card is still and dry.
- The whir is a loop that answers only the visitor's own spin (a drag or a key), follows the speed, and stops when the disc stops, on unmount or when sound is turned off; the intro is silent.

A small LED badge hanging on a printed lanyard: behind a smoked lens a crisp grid of square LEDs runs rippling waves in four PWM steps, the messages scrolling in a 5×7 pixel face, or simple pictures wiped in column by column, and two buttons on its edge cycle the mode and the brightness, each press travelling in on springs.flick with a click. - Under reduced motion the badge hangs still (a drag does nothing, a push is acknowledged in the status) and the screen shows still pages that turn every 2.4 s on a timer instead of a loop; the buttons still change the screen.
- The LEDs are one Canvas 2D redrawn at thirty frames a second only while the badge is on screen, the tab is visible and the screen is not paused; the swing is motion values set from a fixed-step pendulum in the same loop, capped so the badge never swings out of its box.
- The badge's width follows its container (164–228px) and a narrow box shows fewer LEDs rather than smaller ones. The housing and the LEDs keep their own colours on both themes; the engraved marks beside the buttons use the ink token.

Swipe between slides and the stars streak sideways.

A slide pager over a quiet starfield: drag, swipe or press the arrows and the stars are thrown into sideways streaks that sweep into a warp point on the edge the slides travel toward, then shrink back to points as the new slide lands on springs.glide with the throw's velocity. - `density`: number (default 0.5) — How many stars fill the sky, 0 to 1.
- `tint`: string (default "var(--accent-bright)") — The colour a fast swipe tints the streaks, any CSS colour.

### Acrylic Pour (KQ-1830) — `acrylic-pour`
Tilt the canvas; poured colours drift into cells.

A small canvas of poured acrylic: dragging tips it in 3D 1:1 under the hand and the paint runs downhill in WebGL2, each colour at its own pace so the rings shear and stretch, while lacy cells of a lighter layer open where the film thins. Released, the canvas settles level on springs.drift with the throw's velocity and the paint stays where it ran; a tap pours a new seeded composition that floods out cup by cup over the old one. The canvas is focusable: the arrow keys tilt it gently while held and Enter or Space pours anew.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/acrylic-pour`

Props:
- `seed / defaultSeed`: number (default 1) — The composition (controlled / initial); a new seed pours a new one over the old.
- `onSeedChange`: (seed: number) => void — Fires from the tap or key that asked for a new pour.
- `cells`: number (default 0.55) — How much the lighter layer breaks through as lacy cells, 0 to 1.
- `tilt`: number (default 0.6) — How far a drag tips the canvas and how freely the paint runs, 0 to 1.
- `palette`: "tide" | "ember" | "moss" | "dusk" | string[] (default "tide") — The paints: a named set, or up to five CSS colours.
- `pours`: number (default 4) — How many cups were poured, 2 to 7.
- `viscosity`: number (default 0.5) — How thick the paint is: runny and far-flowing (0) to heavy and creeping (1).
- `gloss`: number (default 0.6) — How glossy the wet paint looks, 0 to 1.
- `base`: string (default titanium white) — The lighter layer that shows through the cells, any CSS colour.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a pour while the paint runs.
- `onFlowChange`: (flowing: boolean) => void — Fires when the paint starts and stops flowing.
- `label`: string (default "Acrylic pour") — Names the canvas for assistive technology.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Shows the pour but takes no input.
- `dpr`: number (default 2) — Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
- `className`: string — Sizes the component (default h-52 w-full); the canvas is the largest square inside.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the canvas is one tab stop; hold an arrow key to tilt it that way (two keys tilt diagonally), let go to level it, and press Enter or Space for a new composition, which is announced.
- Reduced motion: the canvas no longer tips in 3D and a new pour cross-fades instead of flooding; the paint still follows a drag, because that is direct manipulation.
- Performance: the flow is a 128×128 half-float map advected only while the canvas is tilted or a pour floods in, on screen and while the tab is visible; at rest the canvas is a single still frame. DPR is capped at `dpr`, context loss rebuilds it, and without WebGL2 a still pour is drawn in CSS from the same seed.
- Sound (`sound`): a pour loop follows the flow — louder and higher the steeper the tilt — and always stops when the paint settles; it never starts before the visitor has interacted with the page.
- Palettes are pigments taken from the theme tokens at fixed lightness, so a pour looks the same in light and dark themes; pass `palette` as five CSS colours for your own.

### Vantage Cube (KQ-1831) — `vantage-cube`
A cube of loose letters that reads from one angle.

A wireframe cube of loose letters floating at different depths that turns to follow the pointer on a spring set by `lag`: from most angles it is a scatter, but at each word's vantage its letters line up in perspective, one size on one baseline. Near a vantage the cube is drawn toward it and inside `snap` degrees it locks on springs.snap — the word brightens, a rule draws under it and a glint sweeps across it — and leaving the box drifts it home on springs.drift to lock again. It is a slider over the words: arrow keys turn the cube to the next or previous word on springs.glide, Home and End jump.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/vantage-cube`

Props:
- `words`: VantageCubeWord[] (default FIELD, LINE, DRIFT, NORTH) — The words hidden in the cube, each with the yaw and pitch (degrees) it reads from.
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The word the cube shows, by index (controlled / initial).
- `onValueChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires when a different word locks, from the pointer, a drag or a key.
- `density`: number (default 0.5) — How many loose letters fill the cube besides the words, 0 to 1.
- `depth`: number (default 0.6) — How far the letters are spread in depth, 0 (nearly flat) to 1 (the whole cube).
- `lag`: number (default 0.45) — How lazily the cube follows the pointer, 0 (at once) to 1 (slow and heavy).
- `snap`: number (default 7) — How close to a vantage, in degrees, the cube snaps to it and locks.
- `range`: number (default 50) — How far the cube turns toward the pointer at the box's edge, in degrees.
- `perspective`: number (default 3.2) — Viewing distance in cube widths; lower is a stronger wide-angle look.
- `glint`: boolean (default true) — Sweep a glint across a word when it locks.
- `edges`: boolean (default true) — Draw the cube's edges.
- `seed`: number (default 3) — Seeds where the letters float.
- `onLock`: (index: number) => void — Fires each time a word locks, including a return to the same word.
- `label`: string (default "Word cube") — The cube's accessible name.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — No following, dragging or keys.
- `className`: string — Sizes the cube's box; give it a height. Defaults to h-52 w-full.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the cube is a slider over its words — Left/Right (or Up/Down) turn to the previous or next word, Home and End jump — and the locked word is announced once; aria-valuetext always names the current word.
- Reduced motion: the cube holds still at the current word's vantage, ignores the pointer, and keys swap words with a short cross-fade instead of a turn.
- Performance: every letter's 3D place is a static transform computed once from the seed; only the cube's own rotation and a few CSS variables change per frame, and the spring loop stops as soon as the cube settles or leaves the screen.
- Choose vantages at least three `snap` widths apart and within `range` (pitch within 0.7 × range) so each is reachable by the pointer; loose letters are placed clear of every word's row so each word reads clean.
- The cube is sized from its box with container units, so it renders the same on the server and fits any height; touch and pen drag it 1:1 and a release locks to a vantage near where the throw would land.

### Pillow Print (KQ-1832) — `pillow-print`
A puffed vinyl card that dimples where you press.

An image card printed on an inflated vinyl pillow: a WebGL2 mesh bulges out, draws in at the middle of each edge and wrinkles where the welded seam gathers into the corners, under a softbox gloss that slides across the bulge as the pillow leans toward the pointer on the glide spring. Pressing pushes a soft dimple in under the finger on the snap spring, drawing the print into it while the rest puffs out to keep its air; letting go pops it back on an underdamped spring set by `stiffness`, overshooting into a little bump and wobbling level.
